aatrox-combo-basic.basis: The basic trade combo is Q1 → E to reposition → basic attack → W → Q2 → Q3. Use E immediately after pressing Q to reposition during the cast and land the blade's sweet spot.
aatrox-combo-basic.text: The basic trade combo is Q1 → E to reposition → basic attack → W → Q2 → Q3. Use E immediately after pressing Q to move during the cast and land the blade’s sweet spot.

aatrox-combo-ult.basis: The teamfight combo is R → Q1 → E → W → Q2 → Q3. R increases attack damage. R increases self-healing. R's duration can only be extended through takedowns. Since R has a short duration, use it just before engaging when you are sure you can force a fight.
aatrox-combo-ult.text: The teamfight combo is R → Q1 → E → W → Q2 → Q3. R increases attack damage and self-healing, so activate it just before engaging, once you are sure you can force a fight; its short duration extends only through takedowns.

aatrox-combo-w.basis: The W combo is Q1 → W → Q2 before the pull → Q3 immediately after the pull. W also reaches targets within Q1's knockup range. If Q1 misses, hold W to avoid wasting it. Land W immediately after Q1's knockup to limit the opponent's time to walk out of the chain area.
aatrox-combo-w.text: The W combo is Q1 → W → Q2 before the pull → Q3 immediately after it. W reaches any target close enough to be knocked up by Q1, so hold W if Q1 misses; when Q1 lands, use W immediately to give the opponent less time to walk out of the chain area.

aatrox-laning.basis: At levels 1–2, farm safely near your turret, even if you have to give up some CS. From level 3 onward, farm with Q. From level 3 onward, stick to short trades in lane. Use Q3 and W after the opponent has used their tools for fighting back. In losing matchups, Q's damage alone lets you trade, so choose health and regeneration over attack damage to sustain in lane.
aatrox-laning.text: At levels 1–2, farm safely near your turret, even if it means giving up some CS. From level 3 onward, farm with Q and take only short trades, saving Q3 and W until the opponent has used their tools to fight back. Q deals enough damage to trade without building attack damage, so in a losing matchup you can prioritize health and regeneration to stay in lane without giving up much damage.

aatrox-laning-q-timing.basis: Harass melee opponents with Q as they step forward to last-hit. Land Q's sweet spot during the opponent's basic attack windup to prevent them from dodging or fighting back. Wait for the opponent's last-hit animation before using Q instead of using it on cooldown.
aatrox-laning-q-timing.text: Against melee opponents, use Q as they step forward to last-hit. If its sweet spot lands during their basic attack windup, they cannot dodge or fight back, so wait for that moment instead of using Q on cooldown.

aatrox-phase.basis: Aatrox is often weak at levels 1–2, when Q has a long cooldown. From level 3 onward, with points invested in Q, Aatrox gains strong trading power. Aatrox reaches his peak in the mid game as he builds up ability haste and items. Aatrox often struggles against duelists in late-game 1v1s.
aatrox-phase.text: Aatrox is weak at levels 1–2 because Q has a long cooldown, but his trades become strong from level 3 onward as he invests points in Q. He peaks in the mid game as he builds ability haste and items, then struggles against duelists in late-game 1v1s.

aatrox-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent's healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. Buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
aatrox-situational-antiheal.text: If the opponent’s healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item to reduce it.

aatrox-situational-armor.basis: If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Cloth Armor or Bramble Vest first. If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps earlier. In matchups where you keep getting pushed back, switch to a build that prioritizes armor and health to survive.
aatrox-situational-armor.text: If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Cloth Armor or Bramble Vest first and get Plated Steelcaps earlier. If the matchup keeps pushing you back, switch to a build that prioritizes armor and health to survive.

aatrox-skill-e.basis: E can be used to move even while other abilities are in progress. Use E during Q's cast to adjust the position of its sweet spot. E's passive restores health based on damage dealt to champions. Use E to close in and land abilities, bringing the next passive empowered auto sooner. Avoid saving E solely for disengaging, so your abilities and empowered basic attacks keep cycling.
aatrox-skill-e.text: E can move Aatrox while other abilities are in progress, letting you adjust Q’s sweet spot during its cast. Its passive restores health from damage dealt to champions, so landing abilities sustains you; using E to close in and land them also reduces the passive cooldown, bringing your next empowered auto sooner. Saving E solely for disengaging slows that entire cycle.

aatrox-skill-passive.basis: The passive's empowered auto deals damage based on the target's maximum health. The passive's empowered auto restores health. Each ability hit reduces the passive cooldown. Save the empowered auto to pressure melee opponents instead of wasting it on minions.
aatrox-skill-passive.text: The passive’s empowered auto deals damage based on the target’s maximum health and restores health, while each ability hit reduces its cooldown. Its increased range lets you pressure melee opponents, so avoid wasting it on minions.

aatrox-skill-q-tip.basis: Q must hit with its sweet spot to deal full damage. Q knocks up opponents hit by its sweet spot. Prioritize landing Q1, which has the longest range of the three casts. Q2 and Q3 have visible windups, making them easy for opponents to dodge. Try to land the tip of every Q to reduce the passive cooldown as much as possible and keep empowered autos cycling.
aatrox-skill-q-tip.text: Q must hit with the blade’s sweet spot to deal full damage and knock up the target. Prioritize Q1, which has the longest range, since the visible windups of Q2 and Q3 make them easier to dodge. Aim for the sweet spot on every cast to reduce your passive cooldown as much as possible and keep empowered autos cycling.

aatrox-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use W to group opponents and try to hit multiple targets with Q's sweet spot. Avoid accepting 1v1 duels during teamfights. Engage once you and your allies have created a numbers advantage. Follow up allied immobilizing crowd control with Q to reliably land its sweet spot.
aatrox-teamfight.text: In teamfights, use W to group opponents and hit multiple targets with Q’s sweet spot. Avoid 1v1 duels and engage with your allies once you have a numbers advantage; following up their immobilizing crowd control with Q is the easiest way to land its sweet spot reliably.

ahri-combo-basic.basis: The basic combo is E → W → Q. Land E first to focus all three W flames on one target. Landing E first guarantees that the follow-up W and Q will hit.
ahri-combo-basic.text: The basic combo is E Charm → W Fox-Fire → Q Orb of Deception. Land Charm first: Fox-Fire prioritizes charmed champions, so all three flames will hit the same target, and the follow-up abilities are guaranteed to connect.

ahri-combo-q.basis: Q hits on both the outward and return paths. Q's orb returns toward Ahri after being thrown. To hit both parts of Q, throw it past the enemy, then immediately move in toward them. Q's return damage is true damage, so the enemy's magic resistance does not reduce it.
ahri-combo-q.text: Q Orb of Deception hits on its outward and return paths. Throw it past the enemy, then immediately move toward them so the orb hits both ways as it returns to Ahri. The return hit deals true damage, so magic resistance does not reduce it.

ahri-combo-ult.basis: R is a mobility ability that links your combo together. You can use other abilities while dashing with R.
ahri-combo-ult.text: R (Spirit Rush) is a mobility ability that links Ahri’s combo, and she can cast other abilities while dashing.

ahri-laning.basis: Use Q as your main poke tool in lane. Throw Q so it clips the enemy backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time. Save E unless you have a kill opportunity or are following up on a gank. When you run out of mana, stop poking and focus on farming.
ahri-laning.text: Use Q Orb of Deception as your main poke tool in lane, throwing it so it clips the enemy backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time. Save E Charm for a kill opportunity or a gank follow-up. When you run out of mana, stop poking and focus on farming.

ahri-laning-roam.basis: After unlocking R, push the lane and roam. Only enter another lane when both E and R are available. If either E or R is unavailable, farm instead of roaming. Ahri's roams depend on landing E.
ahri-laning-roam.text: After unlocking R Spirit Rush, push the lane before roaming. Enter another lane only when both E Charm and R are available; if either is down, farm instead. Ahri’s roams depend on landing Charm.

ahri-phase.basis: Ahri is weakest without R because she has no mobility ability available. Do not overextend in lane while R is on cooldown. From the mid game onward, as Ahri builds ability power, landing E gives her stronger single-target kill potential.
ahri-phase.text: Ahri is weakest without R Spirit Rush because she has no mobility ability available. Her first power spike comes at level 6; after that, avoid overextending in lane while R is on cooldown. From the mid game onward, as she builds ability power, landing E Charm gives her the potential to take out a single target.

ahri-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing offsets your combo damage, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
ahri-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing offsets a full combo’s damage, buy Morellonomicon to reduce that healing after completing one core item.

ahri-skill-e.basis: E only affects the first target it hits. Minions block E, preventing it from reaching enemies behind them. To hit an enemy behind minions with E, move around the side or use R to cross the minion line. Ahri's combat effectiveness drops sharply while E is unavailable. Do not waste E.
ahri-skill-e.text: E Charm affects only the first target it hits, so it cannot reach an enemy behind minions. Move around the side or use R Spirit Rush to cross the minion line before casting it. Ahri can do little for a while after E is spent, so do not throw it carelessly.

ahri-skill-passive.basis: P restores health each time you kill a set number of minions. Ahri's lane sustain effectively depends on P's healing. Keep up your CS so P's healing can support your trades. P heals more from champion takedowns than from minion kills. Champion takedowns restore R dashes.
ahri-skill-passive.text: P Essence Theft restores health each time you kill a set number of minions. Ahri’s lane sustain depends heavily on this healing, so keeping up your CS helps support your trades. Participating in a champion takedown heals you for more and restores R Spirit Rush dashes.

ahri-skill-r.basis: R lets you dash multiple times. Champion takedowns while R is active increase your remaining dashes. Champion takedowns while R is active extend its duration. Save at least one R dash to disengage. If you can secure a kill, use the extra R dash from the takedown to go after the next enemy.
ahri-skill-r.text: R Spirit Rush allows multiple dashes, and participating in a champion takedown while it is active increases the remaining dash count and extends its duration. Save at least one dash to get out instead of committing them all on the initial engage. If you can secure a kill, use the extra dash from the takedown to pursue the next enemy.

ahri-skill-w.basis: W deals greatly increased damage to low-health minions. Use W to last-hit minions and clear waves. Using W increases movement speed. Use W's movement speed boost to chase and disengage.
ahri-skill-w.text: W (Fox-Fire) deals greatly increased damage to low-health minions, making it useful for last-hitting and clearing waves. It also grants movement speed to help Ahri chase or disengage.

ahri-teamfight.basis: Ahri is classified as an assassin, but she is also strong in teamfights. Q is easier to land when enemies are grouped together. Use E to draw one enemy toward your allies so they can follow up. Poke with Q from outside the enemy's range without engaging head-on first. While poking, use E when you have an angle to land it.
ahri-teamfight.text: Ahri is classified as an assassin, but she is also strong in teamfights. Grouped enemies have a harder time dodging Q Orb of Deception, and E Charm can pull one of them toward your allies for a follow-up. Poke with Q from outside the enemy’s range, then cast E when you have an angle instead of engaging head-on first.

ahri-teamfight-cleanup.basis: As the fight winds down, use R to chase fleeing enemies. Use W for movement speed while chasing. Decide how far to chase by calculating how many R dashes takedowns will restore.
ahri-teamfight-cleanup.text: As the fight winds down, use R Spirit Rush to chase fleeing enemies and W Fox-Fire for movement speed. Account for the R dashes restored by each takedown when deciding how far you can chase without overcommitting.

akali-combo-allin.basis: Use the first R to get past the target and close in, chip away with Q and an empowered basic attack, then finish with the second R. The second R deals more damage the more health the target has lost. Save the second R until the end of the combo. Cast Q during the second R dash to land both hits at once.
akali-combo-allin.text: For a full engage, use the first R to dash past the target and close in, wear them down with Q and an empowered basic attack, then finish with the second R. Its damage increases with the health the target has lost, so save it for last; casting Q during the second dash lands both hits at once.

akali-combo-basic.basis: Land Q, step back across the ring, then finish the trade with an empowered basic attack. The empowered basic attack's extra range lets you attack from outside the enemy's retaliation range. Crossing the ring and returning to poke with an empowered basic attack costs no energy.
akali-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, land Q to create the ring, step back across its edge, then return with an empowered basic attack. Its extra range lets you strike from outside the enemy’s retaliation range, and this back-and-forth poke costs no energy.

akali-combo-passive-ring.basis: Akali's combos rely on moving around her passive ring. Hitting an ability creates a passive ring around the target. Cross the edge of the passive ring and return to use an empowered basic attack with twice the range. Practice quickly moving back and forth across the passive ring to keep dealing damage.
akali-combo-passive-ring.text: Akali’s combos revolve around her passive ring: hitting an ability creates one around the target, and crossing its edge before returning prepares an empowered basic attack with twice the range. Practice moving quickly back and forth across the ring to keep your damage flowing.

akali-combo-r-flash.basis: You can combine Flash with either R dash to extend its reach. Combine R with Flash to chase down a fleeing target from farther away.
akali-combo-r-flash.text: Flash can extend the range of either R dash. Combine them against a fleeing target to catch them from much farther away than expected.

akali-laning.basis: Statistically, Akali ranks near the bottom in CS. Even if you give up some farm, build a health advantage with max-range Q hits and empowered basic attacks. Once you have a health advantage, push the wave and move to another lane to build on it.
akali-laning.text: Akali ranks near the bottom in CS statistically, so giving up some farm to build a health advantage with max-range Q hits and empowered basic attacks is a normal way to play. Once you have that advantage, push the wave and move to another lane to turn it into a lead elsewhere.

akali-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Akali lacks the energy to trade effectively. Akali can start poking as she levels up Q. Kill opportunities open up as soon as you learn R at level 6. After completing one core ability power item, Akali can kill a backline target in one combo. Throughout the game, Akali is likely to die if she fails to finish the kill.
akali-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Akali has some of the lowest armor and too little energy to trade well. Poke becomes viable as Q gains levels, and kill opportunities appear when she gets R at level 6. Once she completes one core ability power item, she can kill a backline target in one combo, but failing to finish the kill can still get her killed throughout the game.

akali-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon to apply Grievous Wounds. Akali must secure a kill during her brief engage, so she loses out if the enemy still has healing available.
akali-situational-antiheal.text: If an enemy survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon to apply Grievous Wounds. Akali needs to secure the kill during her brief engage, so going in while the enemy still has healing available puts her at a disadvantage.

akali-situational-mercurial.basis: If the enemy has crowd control that can lock you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items to have a way to cleanse it. If Akali is caught by crowd control right after engaging, she is likely to die before using the second R.
akali-situational-mercurial.text: If the enemy has crowd control that can lock Akali down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items for a way to cleanse it. Getting caught immediately after engaging can kill her before she uses the second R, making that escape tool critical to survival.

akali-skill-e.basis: The second E dash follows the marked target no matter how far they go. Before using the second E, check whether the target has moved under a turret or into the enemy team. You can also place an E mark on W's smoke. Use an E mark left on the smoke as an escape route.
akali-skill-e.text: The second E dash follows its marked target no matter how far they go. Check their position before recasting, or they may pull Akali under a turret or into the middle of the enemy team. You can also leave an E mark on W’s smoke as a way to retreat.

akali-skill-q.basis: Q spreads in a cone and slows targets hit at its maximum range. Landing Q at maximum range also readies the passive ring immediately. Aim for the edge of Q's range to poke more efficiently.
akali-skill-q.text: Q spreads in a cone, slowing targets hit at its maximum range and readying the passive ring immediately. Aim for that edge instead of casting at close range for more effective poke. Because Q costs a lot of energy, use a basic attack when you’ve already created the ring.

akali-skill-r.basis: If caught in a bad position, use R to dash over the enemy and escape. Save the first cast of R unless you're sure you can get the kill.
akali-skill-r.text: R can also get you out of a bad position by dashing over an enemy. Save its first cast unless you’re sure you can secure the kill.

akali-skill-w.basis: W's smoke grants Akali stealth. W's movement speed boost helps Akali continue her combo quickly. You can be hit by skillshots during the brief moment you appear just after entering the smoke. Avoid using W only to escape in open areas. Use W just before engaging or to interrupt targeted enemy abilities.
akali-skill-w.text: W’s smoke grants stealth and a movement speed boost that helps Akali move through her combo faster. She briefly appears just after entering it and can be hit by skillshots in that window. Using W only to escape across open ground can get you caught, so cast it just before engaging or to interrupt a targeted enemy ability.

akali-teamfight.basis: Do not start teamfights. Enter after your allies start the fight, draw the enemy's attention, and force out their crowd control. In teamfights, dive the backline and kill a squishy target. Before engaging, check whether the enemy has used their targeted crowd control.
akali-teamfight.text: Let your allies start teamfights, then enter the backline after the enemy’s attention and crowd control have been spent to kill a squishy target. Before going in, check that the enemy has used their targeted crowd control.

akshan-combo-e.basis: E is a movement ability that hooks onto terrain and swings around it. While swinging with E, Akshan automatically shoots the nearest enemy. Use E to swing around your opponent and close in. Cast E a third time to land where you want and fire the final shot. Take a wide swing away from your opponent's path so hitting a champion or terrain does not end E.
akshan-combo-e.text: E (Heroic Swing) hooks onto terrain and swings around it, automatically firing at the nearest enemy during the swing. Swing in a wide arc around your opponent to close in, then use the third input to land where you want and fire the final shot. Colliding with a champion or terrain ends the swing immediately, so keep your arc clear of the path your opponent is walking toward.

akshan-combo-passive-cancel.basis: Cancel the second shot after your first basic attack by moving to gain movement speed. Fire both shots when you need to deal all your damage. To control your spacing, fire only the first shot and move immediately to cancel the second.
akshan-combo-passive-cancel.text: You can cancel the automatic second shot after a basic attack by moving, which grants movement speed. Fire both shots when you need full damage; when you need to close or create distance, move immediately after the first to cancel the second. This movement is Akshan's main way to kite.

akshan-combo-passive-third.basis: The passive deals bonus damage on every third hit from basic attacks and abilities combined. If the passive's third hit lands on a champion, you also gain a shield. Hit with Q on the way out and back, then land one basic attack to trigger the passive's third hit. Start a trade when you can land the passive's third hit.
akshan-combo-passive-third.text: Dirty Fighting (P) deals bonus damage on every third hit from basic attacks and abilities combined, and grants a shield if that hit lands on a champion. Landing Q (Avengerang) on both its outgoing and returning paths sets up the third hit with one basic attack, so start a trade only when you can land it.

akshan-combo-q.basis: Hit with Q's boomerang on both the way out and back to poke. Q's boomerang travels farther each time it hits an enemy. After throwing Q, move in the direction your opponent dodged the first hit so the returning boomerang hits them.
akshan-combo-q.text: To poke, hit with Q (Avengerang) on both its outgoing and returning paths. The boomerang travels farther each time it hits an enemy, so throwing it through a minion wave can reach an opponent much farther back than expected. Move sideways after the throw to shift its return path toward the direction they dodged the first hit.

akshan-laning.basis: In lane, trade from a distance where Q can hit on both the way out and back. Before trading, check whether you can gain the passive shield.
akshan-laning.text: Akshan's level 1 attack damage is among the lowest of all champions, so he cannot win a straight basic attack fight. His lane advantage comes from hitting with Avengerang (Q) on both passes and using the Dirty Fighting (P) shield. Trade only at a range where Q can hit on the way out and back, avoid forcing trades outside that range, and check that the shield is ready before going in.

akshan-laning-roam.basis: After pushing the wave, use E to cross terrain and roam to another lane. When roaming, approach with W's camouflage along river and jungle walls. After roaming, check E's cooldown before choosing your return route.
akshan-laning-roam.text: After pushing the wave, use E (Heroic Swing) to cross terrain and roam to another lane. Follow river and jungle walls with W (Going Rogue) camouflage to approach out of sight, then check E's cooldown before choosing your route back.

akshan-phase.basis: Akshan is weak at levels 1–2. Even if you learn E first, early trades depend on chances to land Q. Kill opportunities increase sharply once level 6 R and your first core item come together. As you build critical strike items in the mid to late game, both R's finishing power and your basic attack damage increase.
akshan-phase.text: Akshan is weak at levels 1–2. Even if you learn E (Heroic Swing) first, early trade damage comes from Q (Avengerang), so those trades depend on finding a Q angle. Kill opportunities rise sharply when level 6 R (Comeuppance) and the first core item come together; because critical strike affects R's damage, building critical strike items through the mid and late game improves both its finishing power and basic attack damage.

akshan-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing targets, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. When an enemy heals, R has less chance to finish them because its damage scales with their missing health.
akshan-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing targets, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. R (Comeuppance) deals more damage based on missing health, so an enemy who heals can move out of your finishing range entirely.

akshan-skill-e-reset.basis: A takedown resets E's cooldown. Use E to engage if the takedown is certain. After a takedown, use the reset E to reach the next target or escape. If the takedown is uncertain, avoid engaging with E so you keep a way out.
akshan-skill-e-reset.text: A takedown resets E (Heroic Swing), so use it to engage when the kill is certain, then use the reset to reach another target or escape. If the kill is uncertain, engaging with E leaves you without a way out.

akshan-skill-r-channel.basis: Akshan is rooted in place while aiming R. Aiming R also shows the target an aiming indicator. Aim R for a long time only when there is no wall along the target's escape route. You can fire R's stored bullets without fully charging it. Stop aiming and fire R before the target reaches a wall.
akshan-skill-r-channel.text: Akshan is rooted while aiming R (Comeuppance), and the target sees an aiming indicator. Charge it for a long time only if the target's escape route has no wall: moving behind terrain can waste every stored bullet. You can fire before reaching full charge, so release the shots before the target reaches a wall.

akshan-skill-r-target.basis: R's bullets hit the first enemy or structure in their path. R's bullets execute minions instantly. Use R to finish off a low-health enemy fleeing at long range.
akshan-skill-r-target.text: Comeuppance (R) shots hit the first enemy or structure in their path. Minions are executed instantly, so a wave won't block the shots, but an enemy frontliner or turret in the way will absorb them all. Because the damage increases with the target's missing health, use R to finish off fleeing enemies from long range.

akshan-skill-w-camo.basis: W's camouflage lasts longer near terrain or brush. W's camouflage ends quickly in open areas. Plan roaming and escape routes along river or jungle walls. While camouflaged, you are revealed if you enter an enemy champion's detection range. When there is a Scoundrel, a trail toward them appears and you gain movement speed.
akshan-skill-w-camo.text: W (Going Rogue) camouflage lasts longer near terrain or brush but ends quickly in the open, so plan roams and escapes along river and jungle walls. Entering an enemy champion's detection range reveals you even while camouflaged, making a camouflaged approach against a grouped team unworkable. When a Scoundrel is present, a trail toward them and bonus movement speed help you chase.

akshan-skill-w-revive.basis: An enemy who kills an ally is marked as a Scoundrel. Killing a Scoundrel revives the allies they killed. Killing a Scoundrel grants bonus gold. If an ally dies in a teamfight, look for a chance to finish off the Scoundrel. Stay alive as Akshan to secure the ally revive.
akshan-skill-w-revive.text: An enemy who kills an ally is marked as a Scoundrel; killing that Scoundrel revives the allies they killed and grants bonus gold. An ally falling can therefore create Akshan's biggest opportunity: in a teamfight, look for a chance to finish off the Scoundrel instead of retreating immediately. Akshan must survive for the revive to happen, so dying alongside the Scoundrel is the worst outcome.

akshan-teamfight.basis: Do not start a teamfight from the front. After the fight starts and the enemy has used their immobilizing abilities, enter from the side with E. In teamfights, finish off low-health targets. If an ally falls first, prioritize the Scoundrel.
akshan-teamfight.text: Akshan should not start a fight from the front. Once the fight has begun and the enemy has used their immobilizing abilities, enter from the side with Heroic Swing (E) and finish off targets whose health has been reduced. If an ally falls first, Going Rogue (W) can turn the entire fight around, so ignore other targets and focus on the Scoundrel.

alistar-combo-flash.basis: Using Flash during Q's cast moves Pulverize's area toward the target. Land Q with Flash, then immediately use W to push the target toward your allies.
alistar-combo-flash.text: Use Flash during Q’s cast to move Pulverize’s area toward the target. Landing Q from an unexpected distance and immediately using W to push the target toward your allies is Alistar’s main kill setup.

alistar-combo-qw.basis: Knock the target up with Q, then use W to push them in the direction you want. Use Q → W to peel enemies off your backline. Use Q → W to push enemies away rather than toward your allies.
alistar-combo-qw.text: Q → W knocks the target up first, then pushes them in your chosen direction. Use it to peel enemies off your backline or drive them outward instead of toward your allies.

alistar-combo-wq.basis: Right after W Headbutt, use Q Pulverize to knock up the opponent you pushed away. To send an enemy toward your allies, first get behind them and use W.
alistar-combo-wq.text: Alistar’s standard combo is W Headbutt immediately into Q Pulverize, knocking up the displaced target where they land to keep the crowd control chain going. To send an enemy toward your allies, get behind them before using W; positioning comes before the combo.

alistar-dive.basis: When an enemy is under their turret, use W to push them deeper under it. When diving, take turret shots first, activate R, and go in. Before a dive, check whether your allies have enough damage to finish the target.
alistar-dive.text: When an enemy is under their turret, Alistar can make a strong dive by using W to push them deeper beneath it. Check first that your allies have enough damage to finish the target, then take turret aggro yourself and activate R as you go in.

alistar-laning.basis: Alistar is a support who pressures the lane. Look to land Q as an enemy steps forward to last-hit. If you use both Q and W but fail to engage, you leave yourself open to a counterattack while they are down. Engage with Q and W only when your allied marksman can follow up.
alistar-laning.text: Alistar is a lane pressure support. Look for a Q Pulverize opportunity when an enemy steps forward to last-hit, but engage only when your allied marksman can reliably follow up: if you use both Q and W Headbutt and the engage fails, both abilities will be down at once, leaving you open to a counterattack.

alistar-laning-mana.basis: His abilities cost a lot of mana, so you cannot use the combo repeatedly early on. One failed engage costs you both mana and lane control. If the engage angle is uncertain, trade with E and wait for the next opportunity.
alistar-laning-mana.text: Alistar’s abilities cost a lot of mana, so he cannot repeat his combo early on. A failed engage costs both mana and lane control; if the opening is uncertain, trade with E and wait for a better chance.

alistar-phase.basis: Alistar is strong in early trades. His kill pressure is strongest at levels 2–3, when he has his crowd control. He deals very little damage late in the game. Late in the game, focus on starting fights and protecting your allies.
alistar-phase.text: Alistar’s level 1 health and armor are among the highest in the game, making him strong in early trades. His kill pressure peaks at levels 2–3, once his crowd control is available; later, when he deals very little damage, focus on starting fights and protecting allies.

alistar-situational-boots.basis: Movement speed increases your engage range, so generally choose Boots of Swiftness. If the enemy team deals mostly physical damage, choose Plated Steelcaps to survive lane and teamfights.
alistar-situational-boots.text: For Alistar, movement speed increases engage range, making Boots of Swiftness generally valuable. If the enemy team deals mostly physical damage, choose Plated Steelcaps instead to survive lane and teamfights.

alistar-skill-e.basis: While E is active, you can move through units. Activate E when moving through minions. Activate E when escaping through a narrow path. Deal enough damage to a champion with E, and your next basic attack stuns them. Build up E damage during a trade to prepare the stun.
alistar-skill-e.text: While E Trample is active, Alistar can move through units, so use it to pass through minions or escape along a narrow path. Once E has dealt enough damage to a champion, his next basic attack stuns them; build it up during a trade to gain another crowd control effect.

alistar-skill-passive.basis: Your passive gains a stack each time you stun, knock up, or push back an enemy. At full stacks, your passive heals you and nearby allies. In lane, if your passive stacks are almost full, engage once more after a trade to trigger the heal, then back off.
alistar-skill-passive.text: P Triumphant Roar gains a stack whenever Alistar stuns, knocks up, or pushes back an enemy; at full stacks, it heals him and nearby allies. Landing abilities on enemies gives him sustain in lane, so when the stacks are nearly full, engage once more after a trade to trigger the heal, then back off.

alistar-skill-r.basis: Activating R immediately removes impairing effects already on you. Activating R greatly reduces the damage you take. Activate R right after enemy crowd control catches you or as focused fire begins. R does not prevent new crowd control applied after you activate it.
alistar-skill-r.text: R Unbreakable Will immediately removes all impairing effects already on Alistar and greatly reduces incoming damage. Use it just after enemy crowd control catches you or as focused fire begins, rather than before engaging, to benefit from both effects. Account for the fact that it does not prevent crowd control applied afterward.

alistar-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, push an enemy damage dealer toward your allies. In teamfights, peel enemies off your backline. In teamfights, activate R and charge through the enemy team to break their formation.
alistar-teamfight.text: In teamfights, push an enemy damage dealer toward your allies or peel enemies off your backline. With R active, Alistar can charge through the enemy team, absorb most of its damage, and break its formation, so focus on disrupting enemy positions rather than dealing damage.

ambessa-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, use an E dash and its extra strike, a basic attack, Q at the blade’s edge, the second Q, then another basic attack. Weave basic attacks between abilities during a combo to consume passive stacks and restore resources.
ambessa-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, dash in with E, let its extra strike land as the dash ends, then use a basic attack, hit with Q (Cunning Sweep) at the blade’s edge, follow with Sundering Slam, and finish with another basic attack. Weaving attacks between abilities consumes passive stacks and restores enough resources to complete the combo.

ambessa-combo-dash.basis: If you issue a move or attack command during a cast, Ambessa dashes in the commanded direction when the cast ends. If you issue no move or attack command during a cast, Ambessa uses the ability in place. When engaging, issue a move command toward the opponent. When using an ability to disengage, issue a move command backward.
ambessa-combo-dash.text: Every Ambessa combo relies on her passive dash: issue a move or attack command during an ability’s cast, and she dashes in that direction when it ends. Without a command, she uses the ability in place. Command toward an opponent to engage or backward to retreat while casting; the same ability can take you in or out.

ambessa-combo-q-recast.basis: The first Q must hit an enemy to briefly ready Sundering Slam. Minions can also be hit by the first Q to ready Sundering Slam. If a champion is out of range of the first Q, hit a minion with it, then use Sundering Slam on the champion. If the first Q misses completely, the second strike is lost, so set up a hit before trading.
ambessa-combo-q-recast.text: Q (Cunning Sweep) must hit an enemy to ready Sundering Slam, and the second cast is available only briefly. Minions count, so if a champion is out of range, hit a minion with Cunning Sweep and aim Sundering Slam at the champion. A complete miss removes the second strike; set up a hit before trading.

ambessa-combo-ult.basis: R sends Ambessa to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line. Before using R, check that your intended target is farthest along the targeted line. After R lands, attack with E, a basic attack, Cunning Sweep, then Sundering Slam while the suppression and stun continue.
ambessa-combo-ult.text: R (Public Execution) sends Ambessa to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line, letting her reach the backline past a tank but also pulling her toward an unintended target farther along that line. Check who is last before casting. After landing, use the suppression and stun to follow with E, a basic attack, Q (Cunning Sweep), and Sundering Slam.

ambessa-laning.basis: As a melee champion in mid, Ambessa takes early poke from ranged opponents. Do not force your way onto a ranged opponent. Use Q at the blade’s edge to last-hit and poke while keeping up in levels. When the opponent steps forward to last-hit, close in with an E dash, land both Q strikes, then leave immediately. After pushing the wave, get vision at an entrance to the enemy jungle or join a side lane.
ambessa-laning.text: As a melee mid laner, Ambessa takes early poke from ranged opponents, so avoid forcing an engage. Use the blade’s edge of Q (Cunning Sweep) to last-hit and poke while keeping up in levels. When the opponent steps forward to last-hit, dash in with E (Lacerate), land Q at the blade’s edge and follow with Sundering Slam, then leave immediately; staying close lets them hit you with all their abilities. After pushing the wave, use Ambessa’s repeated dashes to gain more by getting vision at an entrance to the enemy jungle or moving to a side lane.

ambessa-phase.basis: Ambessa is weakest at levels 1–2: with only one or two abilities, she struggles to chain dashes. From level 3, once you have both Q and E, you can trade by chaining combos. At level 6, R’s passive gives her a major power boost. Almost all her damage ratios scale with bonus attack damage, so she is strongest in the mid game as she builds core items. If the opponents group up late in the game, do not engage alone; look for someone isolated on a flank.
ambessa-phase.text: Ambessa is weakest at levels 1–2, when one or two abilities give her too few dashes to chain. Trades become viable at level 3 with both Q and E, and R’s passive gives her a major boost at level 6. Almost all her damage ratios scale with bonus attack damage, making the mid game her peak as core items come together. Late in the game, dashes are her only way out after engaging, so avoid going in alone against grouped opponents and look for an isolated target from the flank.

ambessa-skill-e.basis: E’s slow is strong enough to nearly stop its target, but wears off quickly. Follow E’s slow immediately with Q to hit at the blade’s edge. If E starts a dash, its extra strike lands when the dash ends. E is an important way to close the gap, so do not spend it on farming unless you have a chance to get a kill.
ambessa-skill-e.text: E (Lacerate) hits a short area around Ambessa and applies a slow that nearly stops its target but wears off quickly. Follow immediately with Q to land the blade’s edge during that brief window. Starting a dash with E adds another strike when the dash ends, so pair it with a move command; because E is also her most reliable way to close the gap, save it from farming unless a kill is possible.

ambessa-skill-passive.basis: Passive stacks build whenever Ambessa starts a dash and disappear after a short time. While Ambessa has passive stacks, her basic attack range and attack speed increase. Weave basic attacks between abilities to consume passive stacks. Use the extra basic attack range to land another hit from a distance the opponent thinks is safe.
ambessa-skill-passive.text: Passive stacks build whenever Ambessa starts a dash and expire after a short time. They increase her basic attack range and attack speed, so weave attacks between abilities for more total damage instead of letting stacks expire unused. Use the extra range to land a hit from a distance the opponent thinks is safe.

ambessa-skill-q.basis: Cunning Sweep and Sundering Slam deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes; hits closer in deal half damage. If you are close to the opponent, dash back or sideways to create space, then hit with Q at the blade’s edge. Q deals damage based on maximum health, so it also works against opponents who build health.
ambessa-skill-q.text: Both Q (Cunning Sweep) and Sundering Slam deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes but only half damage closer in. If you are too close, dash behind or to the side of the opponent to create space and connect with the blade’s edge. Q also deals damage based on maximum health, so use it to trade against opponents who build health instead of saving it only for farming.

ambessa-skill-r.basis: Once you learn R, its armor penetration and healing based on ability damage apply even when you do not use it. Use R to engage when you have a sure kill or a chance to reach the backline. Ambessa is unstoppable during R, so crowd control cannot interrupt it.
ambessa-skill-r.text: Once learned, R (Public Execution) provides armor penetration and healing based on ability damage even while unused, giving Ambessa a substantial boost to dueling and sustain at levels 6, 11, and 16. Those effects remain after casting, so use R for a sure kill or access to the backline. Ambessa is unstoppable during the cast, and crowd control cannot interrupt it.

ambessa-skill-w.basis: W grants a shield first, then slams the area around Ambessa after a brief windup. If Ambessa takes damage from an enemy champion, large monster, or structure during W’s windup, the slam’s damage increases greatly. Damage from minions does not empower W’s slam. Use W just before the opponent uses an ability or during a tower dive.
ambessa-skill-w.text: W (Repudiation) grants a shield, then slams the area around Ambessa after a brief windup. Taking damage from an enemy champion, large monster, or structure during the windup greatly increases the slam’s damage; minion damage does not. Cast W just before an opponent uses an ability or during a tower dive, since casting it safely in advance gives you only the shield and a weaker slam.

ambessa-teamfight.basis: After your allies draw the opponents’ attention, use R from a flank to reach the backline and target one opponent. Engage after the opponents have used their key crowd control and defensive abilities. If burst damage is coming just before you engage, use W first to block it and empower the slam. Before engaging, plan a route out with an E dash after you take down one opponent.
ambessa-teamfight.text: Ambessa should not engage head-on. Once your allies draw the opponents’ attention, flank with R (Public Execution) to reach the backline and take down one target with its suppression and stun. Go in after the opponents have used their key crowd control and defensive abilities. If burst damage is about to hit just before you engage, use W (Repudiation) first to gain a shield and empower its slam with the damage taken. Plan your escape route before engaging so you can dash out immediately with E (Lacerate) after taking down the target.

amumu-combo-double-q.basis: Q stores up to two charges. After closing in with the first Q, use the second to catch the target if they escape with a mobility ability. When an ally ganks, save Q and throw it right after the target Flashes.
amumu-combo-double-q.text: Q stores up to two charges, so space them out: close in with the first, then use the second if the target escapes with a mobility ability. When ganking for an ally, the most reliable play is to hold the first charge until just after the target Flashes.

amumu-combo-engage.basis: The basic engage is Q in, then R, E, W, and an auto attack. Right after Q hits, you can land R while the target is stunned. Use R before E so allies can attack during the stun.
amumu-combo-engage.text: The basic engage is Q in, then R, E, turn on W, and auto attack. Q leaves the target stunned as Amumu arrives, so R will land; E and W then add area damage and reduce defensive stats. Use R before E so your allies can make full use of the stun.

amumu-combo-flash-r.basis: If enemies are grouped but you have no Q angle, Flash and immediately use R. After engaging with Flash, save both Q charges for disengaging or chasing. If you engage with Q first, you may be pulled toward one target and hit fewer enemies with R.
amumu-combo-flash-r.text: If enemies are grouped but you have no Q angle, Flash in and use R immediately: it erupts around Amumu, leaving both Q charges available to disengage or chase afterward. Opening with Q instead can pull you toward one target and away from the others, reducing the number hit by R.

amumu-gank.basis: Before level 6, ganks depend entirely on landing Q. Before level 6, gank when the lane is pushed toward your side and nothing blocks Q. When ganking, approach from the river or brush for a side angle on Q. After level 6, you can finish a gank with Flash and R even if Q misses.
amumu-gank.text: Before level 6, ganks depend entirely on Q. When a lane is pushed out and the target stands behind minions, Q gets blocked, so gank when the wave is pushed toward your side and approach from the river or brush for a side angle. After level 6, Flash and R can finish a gank even if Q misses.

amumu-jungle.basis: Clear the jungle mainly with E, and use W briefly to manage mana. The first jungle clear costs a lot of health, so avoid risky invades. Take auto attacks from monsters to reduce E's cooldown while clearing. Turn W off while moving to save mana for ganks and objectives.
amumu-jungle.text: Clear mainly with E and use W in short bursts to manage mana. Amumu loses a lot of health on his first clear, so avoid risky early invades and let monsters hit you to shorten E's cooldown and keep the clear moving. Turn W off while traveling; running out of mana leaves you unable to gank or contest objectives.

amumu-objective.basis: The narrow terrain around Dragon or Baron groups enemies, making Q and R easier to land. Establish vision around the objective early and look for the moment enemies enter a narrow passage.
amumu-objective.text: The narrow terrain around Dragon and Baron naturally groups enemies, making both Q and R easier to land. Amumu is more effective in these fights than in a head-on fight on open ground, so establish objective vision early and strike as enemies enter a narrow passage.

amumu-phase.basis: Amumu is weak before level 3 and loses a lot of health while clearing the jungle. Once he gets R at level 6, he becomes much stronger in ganks and objective fights. His peak is in mid to late game teamfights, when he has built magic penetration and damage over time items. His solo fighting remains weak throughout the game, so he is unsuited to fighting alone in a side lane.
amumu-phase.text: Amumu is weak before level 3 and loses a lot of health while clearing. Getting R at level 6 makes him much stronger in ganks and objective fights; he peaks in mid to late game teamfights after building magic penetration and damage over time items. His solo fighting remains weak throughout the game, so avoid fighting alone in a side lane.

amumu-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemies sustain through healing, build Morellonomicon between core items. W's continuous magic damage makes it easy to keep Grievous Wounds on multiple enemies at once.
amumu-situational-antiheal.text: If enemies rely on healing to sustain, build Morellonomicon between core items. W's continuous magic damage makes it easy to maintain Grievous Wounds on several enemies at once.

amumu-skill-e.basis: E's passive reduces physical damage taken. Each basic attack that hits you reduces E's cooldown. E deals area magic damage around you. E is Amumu's main source of damage while jungling.
amumu-skill-e.text: E, Tantrum, passively reduces physical damage taken, and each basic attack that hits Amumu shortens its cooldown. Taking hits on the frontline therefore lets him cast E more often; its active deals area magic damage around him and is his main source of jungle clear damage.

amumu-skill-passive.basis: Cursed Touch makes targets hit by your auto attacks take more magic damage. W continually reapplies the curse, and R applies it too. Weave in auto attacks after engaging to increase your allied magic damage dealers' damage.
amumu-skill-passive.text: Cursed Touch makes targets hit by Amumu's auto attacks take more magic damage; W continually reapplies the curse, and R applies it too. Staying close also increases your allies' magic damage, so weave in an auto attack after engaging to boost your team's damage.

amumu-skill-q.basis: Q is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Against a target behind minions or jungle monsters, look for a Q angle from the side. Throw Q from a brush or behind a wall to give the target less time to react. If the Q angle is uncertain, hold it so you keep a way to close in.
amumu-skill-q.text: Q, Bandage Toss, is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Minions and jungle monsters can block it, so approach a target behind a wave from the side; casting from brush or behind a wall gives them less time to react. If the angle is uncertain, hold Q, since a miss leaves Amumu without a way to close in.

amumu-skill-r.basis: R is an instant area stun around Amumu, so you need to get close to land it. As a rule, use R on multiple grouped enemies. If it can turn the fight around, use R even on a single enemy diving your allied damage dealer. Avoid aiming for multiple enemies only to miss everyone with R.
amumu-skill-r.text: R, Curse of the Sad Mummy, is an instant area stun around Amumu, so you must get close to land it. Aim for multiple grouped enemies as a rule, but stunning even one enemy diving your allied damage dealer is more valuable if it turns the fight around. The worst outcome is waiting for several targets and missing everyone.

amumu-skill-w.basis: When W is on, it continually deals damage based on nearby enemies' maximum health and reapplies the curse. Turn W off while moving to save mana, and turn it on during fights and jungle clears. In teamfights, stay beside high maximum health enemy frontliners to deal W damage.
amumu-skill-w.text: While active, W, Despair, continually damages nearby enemies based on their maximum health and reapplies the curse. It drains mana, so turn it off while moving and use it during fights and jungle clears. W is more effective against targets with high maximum health, making a spot beside the enemy frontline valuable in teamfights.

amumu-teamfight.basis: Amumu starts teamfights, but has little he can do if he engages alone without R. Wait on a flank outside enemy vision, then engage when their formation narrows. Use R when your allies are ready to follow your engage. After engaging, turn on W and stay among enemy frontliners to keep dealing damage and applying the curse.
amumu-teamfight.text: Amumu can start teamfights, but engaging alone without R leaves him little to do. Wait on a flank outside enemy vision, engage as their formation narrows, and use R only when your allies are ready to follow. Once in, keep W on and stay among the enemy frontliners to maintain both damage and the curse.

anivia-combo-basic.basis: The basic trade is to land Q, reactivate it to detonate, then use E. E deals double damage to enemies chilled by Q. If Q misses, save the cooldown and mana by holding E.
anivia-combo-basic.text: The basic trade is Q → early Q detonation → E. Q chills enemies it hits, and E deals double damage only to a chilled target. If Q misses, hold E rather than waste its cooldown and mana.

anivia-combo-r.basis: In teamfights, place R first, let it grow to full size, then use Q and E. A fully grown R chills enemies, doubling E damage even without Q.
anivia-combo-r.text: In teamfights, cast R first, wait for Glacial Storm to reach full size, then use Q → E. Once fully grown, it chills enemies, so Frostbite (E) deals double damage even without Q; casting R early sets up that bonus.

anivia-combo-wall.basis: Block their escape with W, detonate Q in front of the wall, then use E. Enemies trapped against the wall have a hard time dodging Q's explosion stun. Land E and R while the enemy is stunned by Q.
anivia-combo-wall.text: Block the enemy’s retreat with W, then detonate Q in front of the wall. An enemy trapped there cannot avoid Q’s explosion stun, giving you time to land both E and R. Wall → Q detonation → E is Anivia’s only guaranteed solo combo.

anivia-laning.basis: In lane, focus on surviving and scaling instead of forcing a win. Save Q for stopping ganks and guaranteed chances to attack rather than poking. Last-hit with basic attacks and E to keep up in levels. Anivia scales through CS more than kills.
anivia-laning.text: Anivia’s health, armor, and movement speed are all among the lowest, so focus on surviving lane rather than winning it. Save Q for stopping ganks and setting up guaranteed attacks instead of poking, and last-hit with basic attacks and E to keep up in levels. Statistically, Anivia builds her lead through CS rather than kills.

anivia-laning-gank.basis: Anivia has no mobility skill, making ganks hard to escape. If you've pushed the lane, keep W ready for a gank. When escaping a gank, place the W wall to block the path behind you as you flee.
anivia-laning-gank.text: With no mobility ability and very low movement speed, Anivia has to rely on W to survive a gank. Keep it available whenever you have pushed the lane, then place the wall behind you along your escape route rather than across the enemy’s approach.

anivia-laning-wave.basis: Learning R greatly speeds up wave clear. Use R to clear waves when you plan to push and roam or establish vision. To save mana for the opponent's next engage, don't push waves with R without a purpose.
anivia-laning-wave.text: Learning R greatly speeds up wave clear, but turning it on and off costs considerable mana. Use it on waves when you intend to push before roaming or establishing vision. Pushing without a purpose spends mana you will need for the opponent’s next engage.

anivia-phase.basis: Anivia is weakest at levels 1–5 because she lacks mana and damage. At level 6, learning R strengthens both her wave clear and sustained damage. Anivia gains strength in the mid game once items ease her mana problems. In the late game, her role in controlling terrain with W and R grows.
anivia-phase.text: Anivia is weakest at levels 1–5, when she lacks both mana and damage. Learning R at level 6 sharply improves her wave clear and sustained damage; she comes into her own in the mid game as items ease her mana problems, then takes on a greater role controlling terrain with W and R in the late game.

anivia-situational-antiheal.basis: If an enemy's self-healing offsets R's sustained damage, reduce their healing with Morellonomicon. Anivia's damage is sustained rather than a short burst.
anivia-situational-antiheal.text: If an enemy’s self-healing keeps offsetting R’s sustained damage, use Morellonomicon to reduce their healing. Anivia deals damage over time rather than in a short burst, so once healing reduction applies, every moment the enemy stays in R works in your favor.

anivia-skill-e.basis: E is Anivia's main damage skill and her only instant damage skill. E has a short cooldown, so you can use it repeatedly while an enemy is chilled. To increase E damage, chill the enemy with Q or R first. To save mana for trades, don't waste E on clearing minions without chilling them.
anivia-skill-e.text: E is Anivia’s main damage ability and her only source of instant damage. Its short cooldown lets you use it repeatedly as long as the target is chilled, making Q and R the setup for E. Using E to clear minions without chilling them can leave you short of mana when it is time to trade.

anivia-skill-passive.basis: When Anivia takes lethal damage, her passive turns her into an egg; she revives with full health. The egg must survive for a set time with altered defensive stats to revive. The egg is more likely to survive near allies or under a turret than when attacked alone. When her passive is available, you can position aggressively while accounting for the chance to revive. After reviving, position safely until the passive cooldown ends.
anivia-skill-passive.text: Rebirth (P) turns Anivia into an egg when she takes lethal damage, then revives her at full health if the egg survives for a set time with altered defensive stats. An egg left to take hits alone usually breaks, while nearby allies or a turret can help it survive. You can position more aggressively while Rebirth is available, but after it triggers, position as a fragile champion until its cooldown ends.

anivia-skill-q.basis: As Q travels, it deals damage through enemies and slows them. Q stuns in an area when reactivated or when it reaches the end of its range. If the opponent dodges Q sideways, predict their direction and detonate it a little early. When farming without needing the stun, you can let Q pass through without detonating it.
anivia-skill-q.text: While Q travels, it passes through enemies, dealing damage and slowing them; it stuns in an area only when reactivated or when it reaches the end of its range. Against opponents who read its path and sidestep, predict where they will dodge and detonate it a little early. When farming without needing the stun, you can simply let Q pass through.

anivia-skill-r.basis: R continuously consumes mana while active. The storm ends on its own if Anivia moves too far from R. Turn off R as soon as you've pushed the wave or blocked the area you intended. Anivia relies heavily on mana; keeping R active too long can leave too little mana for E in the next fight.
anivia-skill-r.text: Glacial Storm (R) continually drains mana while active and ends on its own if Anivia moves too far away. Turn it off as soon as you have pushed the wave or blocked the intended area. Anivia depends heavily on mana, and forgetting to turn R off once can cost you two E casts in the next fight.

anivia-skill-w.basis: The W wall gets longer as the skill levels up. Low-level W blocks jungle paths; high-level W divides teamfight terrain. To block an enemy's path, place the W wall perpendicular to their direction of travel. The W wall also blocks allies. When allies are engaging, position the W wall so it doesn't trap them.
anivia-skill-w.text: W’s wall grows longer with each rank: at low ranks it blocks a jungle passage, while at high ranks it can divide an entire teamfight area. The wall stands in the cursor’s direction when cast, so place it perpendicular to an enemy’s path to stop them. It blocks allies too; putting it in front of an enemy while your team is engaging can trap your allies instead.

anivia-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, position well behind your frontline. Place R where the fight will start so the storm has time to grow. When the enemy engages, use W to separate their follow-up, then clear the enemies trapped in front with Q and E. Draw teamfights toward narrow passages to increase the impact of the W wall.
anivia-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay well behind your frontline and place R where the fight will begin so the storm can grow. When the enemy engages, use W to cut off their follow-up and create a numbers advantage, then clear the enemies trapped in front with Q and E. Draw fights toward narrow passages, where a single wall has more impact.

annie-combo-solo.basis: Against one target, open with a stunning Q, then follow with W and a basic attack. Do not start a single-target combo with the short-range W.
annie-combo-solo.text: Against one target, open with a stunning Disintegrate (Q), Annie’s longest-range ability, then land Incinerate (W) and a basic attack during the stun. Starting with the shorter-range W gives the target time to escape as Annie closes in, so choose the order based on whether the remaining abilities will land before the stun ends.

annie-combo-ult-engage.basis: Ready the stun, then use R for an area stun, followed by W and Q. Before engaging with R, check that the stun is fully stacked. Do not consume a ready stun with another ability before engaging with R.
annie-combo-ult-engage.text: With the stun ready, engage with R (Summon: Tibbers) for an area stun, then follow with W (Incinerate) and Q (Disintegrate). Before going in, check that the stacks are full and that another ability has not consumed the stun.

annie-laning.basis: When the stun is unavailable, stay back and last-hit minions with Q. When the stun is fully stacked, start a combo as the opponent steps up to last-hit a minion. Do not start a fight unless your stun is ready as the opponent goes for a last hit.
annie-laning.text: While the stun is unavailable, stay behind the middle of the lane and last hit with Q (Disintegrate). Once the stacks are full, start a combo as the opponent steps forward to last hit a minion; if those two conditions do not coincide, wait.

annie-laning-roam.basis: Ready the stun, push the wave, then move to a side lane. Do not consume a ready stun while clearing the wave before roaming.
annie-laning-roam.text: Annie’s roam is especially threatening with her stun ready because she can use it as soon as she arrives. Push the wave before moving to a side lane, but do not spend all your stacks clearing it and arrive without the stun.

annie-phase.basis: Annie can stun from level 1, giving her kill opportunities early. Annie's first strong point is her level 6 R and stun combo. Annie's burst is strongest in the mid game with two or three ability power items. Late in the game, Annie's short range and lack of mobility make engaging harder. Use leads gained before the late game to close out the game.
annie-phase.text: Annie can stun from level 1, giving her early kill opportunities. Her level 6 R (Summon: Tibbers) and stun combo is her first major power spike, and her burst is strongest in the mid game with two or three ability power items. Her short range and lack of mobility make engaging harder later, so use earlier leads to close out the game.

annie-situational-tenacity.basis: After engaging with R, Annie has no mobility ability to escape. If the opponents have a lot of immobilizing crowd control, use Quicksilver Sash to cleanse one crowd control effect after engaging.
annie-situational-tenacity.text: After engaging with R (Summon: Tibbers), Annie has no mobility ability to escape. If the opposing team has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, fit Quicksilver Sash between your core items to cleanse one crowd control effect after going in.

annie-skill-e.basis: E grants a shield and increases movement speed. Use E just before engaging to get within range for W and R. Use E to absorb enemy poke. E can also be used on allies. Summoned Tibbers also receives E's effects. Use E right after summoning Tibbers if you want him to survive longer.
annie-skill-e.text: E (Molten Shield) grants a shield and movement speed. Use it just before engaging to reach W (Incinerate) and R (Summon: Tibbers) range, or to absorb enemy poke. You can also cast it on an ally; summoned Tibbers always receives its effects, so use E right after summoning him if you want him to survive longer.

annie-skill-passive.basis: After using abilities a set number of times, Annie's next damaging ability stuns. Do not move forward unless the stun is ready.
annie-skill-passive.text: Annie’s Pyromania (P) stacks as she uses abilities a set number of times, then adds a stun to her next damaging ability. Whether that stun is ready shapes every decision: opponents keep their distance when it is, giving her control of the lane, but without it she is fragile and has no mobility, so do not move forward.

annie-skill-q.basis: Killing a target with Q refunds its mana cost. Killing a target with Q halves its cooldown. Last-hit minions with Q to save mana and build stun stacks.
annie-skill-q.text: Killing a target with Q (Disintegrate) refunds its mana cost and halves its cooldown. Last hit minions with Q to build stun stacks for almost no mana, keeping up Annie’s early farming and lane pressure.

annie-skill-r-tibbers.basis: Learning R grants magic penetration as a passive effect. Cast R again to control summoned Tibbers directly. Control Tibbers to chase fleeing enemies. Control Tibbers to check vision in a bush. When Annie stuns an enemy, Tibbers becomes enraged and moves faster. Tibbers also becomes enraged and moves faster when Annie dies.
annie-skill-r-tibbers.text: Learning R (Summon: Tibbers) passively grants magic penetration, increasing the damage of Annie’s other abilities. Cast R again to direct Tibbers toward fleeing enemies or check vision in a bush. He becomes enraged and moves much faster when Annie stuns an enemy or dies, so her death does not necessarily end the fight.

annie-skill-w.basis: W hits a cone in front of Annie. Early on, use W to push the wave or secure a clear kill opportunity. Do not waste the costly, short-range W on single-target poke.
annie-skill-w.text: Incinerate (W) hits a cone in front of Annie, making it useful for pushing a wave at once or hitting several enemies in a teamfight. Its high mana cost and short range make it a poor choice for single-target poke; early on, save it for pushing the wave or a clear kill opportunity.

annie-teamfight.basis: Do not use R in a teamfight unless the stun is ready. Engage with R when two or three opponents group together. Start a teamfight with R only where your allies can follow up immediately.
annie-teamfight.text: Annie’s teamfight often hinges on a single R (Summon: Tibbers) engage. Wait until the stun is ready and two or three opponents group together, then engage only from a position where your allies can follow up immediately; Annie has no way to escape afterward.

annie-teamfight-peel.basis: If there is no opening to engage, stay back and protect your allied carry. Stun enemies who get onto an ally. When stopping an enemy who gets onto an ally, shield that ally with E.
annie-teamfight-peel.text: If there is no opening to engage in a teamfight, stay back and guard your allied carry. Stun enemies who reach that ally and cast Molten Shield (E) on the ally rather than yourself; summoning Tibbers (R) early and placing him in front of your team keeps incoming enemies burning and makes them hesitate to engage.

aphelios-combo-ult.basis: R attacks each champion it hits once more with the main weapon. The additional attack from R applies the main weapon's on-hit effects. Before using R, choose your main weapon with W. With Gravitum as the main weapon, R leads from an AoE slow into a root. R with Infernum as the main weapon greatly increases area damage.
aphelios-combo-ult.text: R Moonlight Vigil attacks every champion it hits once more with your main weapon and applies that weapon’s on-hit effects. Choosing your main weapon with W before casting R is therefore a key part of the combo: Gravitum leads from an area slow into a root, while Infernum greatly increases area damage.

aphelios-laning.basis: During the Calibrum phase, poke enemies to lower their health. During the Infernum phase, clear the wave to gain control. During the Gravitum phase, follow your support's or jungler's engage with a root. With an unfavorable weapon combination, avoid forcing a fight and manage your ammo.
aphelios-laning.text: Adjust your laning to your weapon phase: poke enemies down with Calibrum, clear the wave to gain control with Infernum, and add Gravitum’s root to your support’s or jungler’s engage. When your weapon combination is unfavorable, avoid forcing a fight and manage your ammo.

aphelios-phase.basis: Instead of leveling abilities with skill points, Aphelios gains permanent stats. Q unlocks at level 2. R unlocks at level 6. Aphelios gains a lot of power when he completes items. Farm while avoiding losses early, then look for fights after completing a core item.
aphelios-phase.text: Aphelios gains permanent stats instead of leveling abilities with skill points, so he has few of the level spikes other marksmen have. Q unlocking at level 2 and R at level 6 are the two clear exceptions; his power rises gradually otherwise. His item spikes are substantial, so focus on farming without taking losses early and look for fights after completing a core item.

aphelios-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder. Mortal Reminder's healing reduction applies when you attack with any weapon.
aphelios-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing becomes a problem, add Mortal Reminder. Weapons apply different on-hit effects, but its healing reduction applies whichever weapon you attack with.

aphelios-situational-cc.basis: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash early. Outside the Severum phase, you have no way to escape on your own.
aphelios-situational-cc.text: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier. Outside the Severum phase, you have no way to escape on your own.

aphelios-skill-calibrum.basis: Calibrum Q marks the target. Consuming a Calibrum mark lets you attack once more from beyond your normal range. During the Calibrum phase, avoid direct fights because your immediate damage is low.
aphelios-skill-calibrum.text: Calibrum is a poke weapon: its Q marks a target, and consuming the mark lets you attack once more from beyond your normal range. This is the one weapon phase in which you can win a trade without closing the distance, but its immediate damage is low, so avoid starting a direct fight.

aphelios-skill-crescendum.basis: Crescendum Q places a turret. The Crescendum turret uses the same weapon as your off-hand weapon. Use W to choose the off-hand weapon for the turret, then use Crescendum Q.
aphelios-skill-crescendum.text: Crescendum Q places a turret that uses the same weapon as your off-hand. Choose that weapon with W before placing the turret; pressing Q without considering the pairing can produce a much weaker turret for the same ammo.

aphelios-skill-gravitum.basis: Gravitum Q roots all enemies slowed by Gravitum. Apply Gravitum's slow first, then root with Q. Slow multiple enemies with off-hand Gravitum, then use W and Q to root them all. Time your team's engage around the Gravitum rotation.
aphelios-skill-gravitum.text: Gravitum Q roots every enemy slowed by Gravitum, so apply the slow with basic attacks before using Q. With Gravitum in your off-hand, slow multiple enemies, then bring it forward with W and use Q for an area root. Time your team’s engage around this rotation.

aphelios-skill-infernum.basis: Infernum Q attacks in a cone. After Infernum Q, you attack once more with the off-hand weapon. Time your wave push and preparations for a roam or objective around the Infernum phase.
aphelios-skill-infernum.text: Infernum is an area-damage weapon: its Q attacks in a cone, followed by one attack with the off-hand weapon. Its wave clear and teamfight area damage make this the phase to push the lane and prepare for a roam or objective.

aphelios-skill-severum.basis: Severum Q lets you move quickly while attacking nearby enemies. Severum Q attacks with both the main and off-hand weapons.
aphelios-skill-severum.text: Severum’s Q lets Aphelios move quickly while attacking nearby enemies with both his main and off-hand weapons. It is effectively his only way to reposition during a fight, so you can play farther forward while it is available, but if you use Q solely for damage, account for having no way out afterward.

aphelios-skill-w.basis: W swaps the main and off-hand weapons. Q is the current main weapon's ability. Use W to bring out the weapon you want, use Q, then swap back with W. Swapping weapons with W does not restore ammo.
aphelios-skill-w.text: W Phase swaps your main and off-hand weapons, while Q always uses the main weapon’s ability. Bring the weapon you want forward with W, use Q, then swap back with W. Its cooldown is short enough to swap twice during a combo, but swapping does not restore ammo.

aphelios-skill-weapon-cycle.basis: Aphelios carries one main weapon and one off-hand weapon. Basic attacks and abilities consume ammo. When the main weapon runs out of ammo, it moves to the back of the rotation. Using ammo on minions can change your weapon combination for the next fight.
aphelios-skill-weapon-cycle.text: Aphelios carries a main weapon and an off-hand weapon, and his basic attacks and abilities consume ammo. When the main weapon runs out, it moves to the back of the rotation and the next weapon takes its place. Your weapon combination depends on where you spend ammo, so even using it on minions can change what you carry into the next fight.

aphelios-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, attack from behind your frontline and make use of your range. If you have Gravitum, look for a chance to root multiple enemies. If you have Infernum, deal area damage to grouped enemies. When your weapon combination is poor, do not force a role in the fight.
aphelios-teamfight.text: Aphelios has low movement speed and can only move quickly with Severum, so poor positioning in a teamfight can get you killed. Attack from behind your frontline using your range, rooting multiple enemies with Gravitum or damaging grouped enemies with Infernum as your current weapons allow. Do not force a role in the fight when your combination is poor.

ashe-combo-engage.basis: When engaging, stun with R, land W, then activate Q and follow up with basic attacks. R's stun lasts longer the farther it travels. Before engaging, try to land R from as far away as possible.
ashe-combo-engage.text: To engage, stun with R Enchanted Crystal Arrow, follow with W Volley for damage and a slow, then activate Q Ranger's Focus and keep attacking. R stuns longer the farther it travels, so try to land it from as far away as possible before closing in.

ashe-combo-q-prestack.basis: Build stacks with basic attacks to activate Q. Build Q stacks on minions beforehand so you can start the fight with empowered basic attacks. Although Q's empowered basic attack fires multiple arrows, on-hit effects count it as one basic attack.
ashe-combo-q-prestack.text: Q Ranger's Focus requires stacks from basic attacks. Build them on minions before a fight so you can unleash empowered attacks as soon as it starts; although each attack fires multiple arrows, on-hit effects count it as a single basic attack.

ashe-laning-tower.basis: Use Q to take down turrets faster. While attacking a turret, build stacks on nearby minions to use Q repeatedly. Push the lane, then look for a chance to attack the turret.
ashe-laning-tower.text: Activate Q Ranger's Focus when taking a turret. Nearby minions let you build stacks quickly and use Q repeatedly, greatly increasing your damage to the turret. Push the lane, then look for a chance to attack it to secure your lane advantage.

ashe-laning-trade.basis: After your support engages, add slows with W and basic attacks. Avoid stepping forward to start a fight, so you don't get caught by a counter-engage.
ashe-laning-trade.text: In small bot-lane fights, let your support engage first, then follow with W Volley and basic attacks to keep the enemy slowed. Stepping forward to start the fight yourself leaves Ashe vulnerable to a counter-engage.

ashe-laning-wave.basis: Avoid pushing the lane too far, since Ashe has no mobility ability. Keep the lane pulled back and use Frost Shot's slow to discourage enemies from approaching. Always account for the routes the enemy jungler can use to engage. Check inside bushes with E before moving forward.
ashe-laning-wave.text: Ashe has no mobility ability, so avoid pushing the lane too far. Keep it pulled back and use P Frost Shot's slow to discourage enemies from approaching. Always consider the enemy jungler's possible approach routes, and check inside bushes with E Hawkshot before moving forward.

ashe-phase.basis: After level 6, Ashe puts strong pressure on the lane because R creates kill opportunities. Ashe has no way to escape on her own, making poor positioning especially dangerous. With midgame items, Ashe's slow and range make her strong in teamfights. Ashe has less late-game burst damage than other marksmen.
ashe-phase.text: Ashe can create kill opportunities with a single R Enchanted Crystal Arrow from early on, so her lane pressure rises noticeably after level 6. She has no way to escape on her own, however, and poor positioning can get her killed. With midgame items, her slow and range let her control teamfights, though she has less late-game burst damage than other marksmen.

ashe-skill-e.basis: E is a scouting tool that stores charges. Use E to check unwarded objective areas and the enemy jungler's path ahead of time. Use E so it doesn't sit at full charges. E grants vision along its flight path as well as at its destination. Aim E to sweep paths where enemies may gather.
ashe-skill-e.text: E Hawkshot stores charges and offers a safer way to scout than placing wards. Use it early to check unwarded objective areas and the enemy jungler's path, and don't let it sit at full charges. It reveals its flight path as well as its destination, so aim it along routes where enemies may gather.

ashe-skill-passive.basis: Frost Shot applies a slow through both basic attacks and abilities. Ashe's critical strikes strengthen the slow instead of dealing bonus damage. For Ashe, critical strike chance is more a way to keep enemies from escaping than a source of burst damage.
ashe-skill-passive.text: P Frost Shot slows with both basic attacks and abilities. Ashe's critical strikes strengthen that slow instead of dealing bonus damage, making critical strike chance a way to keep enemies from escaping rather than a source of burst damage.

ashe-skill-r.basis: Use R to stun targets across virtually the entire map. Predict where enemies will move before firing R. If it isn't urgent, create distance before using R to increase its stun duration. Save R for plays in other lanes instead of wasting it on lane poke.
