ashe-skill-r.text: R Enchanted Crystal Arrow can stun targets across virtually the entire map. Aim where an enemy is going, rather than where they are standing; a close-range hit has a shorter stun, so create distance before firing unless the situation is urgent. It is also valuable for plays in other lanes, so don't waste it on lane poke.

ashe-skill-w-poke.basis: Ashe relies almost entirely on W for lane poke. At low ranks, W's long cooldown and high mana cost make it costly to use. Use W only when you're sure it will hit, such as when the enemy support steps forward. W's cooldown drops significantly as it gains ranks.
ashe-skill-w-poke.text: W Volley is virtually Ashe's only lane poke. At low ranks, its long cooldown and high mana cost can cost you last hits if you use it carelessly, so fire only when you are confident it will hit, such as when the enemy support steps forward. Its cooldown drops significantly as it gains ranks, letting you poke more often.

ashe-teamfight.basis: Stay behind your allies and keep slowing enemies who engage, giving your team time to close in. Stay behind your frontline so your allies can protect you. Move with your allies when your team starts grouping.
ashe-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and keep enemies who engage slowed, giving your team time to close in. Ashe has virtually no way to protect herself, so remain behind your frontline and move with your allies as soon as they start grouping.

ashe-teamfight-r.basis: Before a fight, decide whether to use R to start the teamfight or stop an enemy engage. If your team has no other way to engage, save R to start the fight.
ashe-teamfight-r.text: Before a fight, decide whether R Enchanted Crystal Arrow will start the teamfight or stop an enemy engage. If your team has no other way to engage, it is your only way to start the fight, so don't spend it on poke or an escape.

asol-combo-fight.basis: In a full fight, use R to restrict movement, place E, then approach with W while maintaining Q. Q has no channel duration limit during W flight. Your damage is most concentrated while maintaining Q during W flight. If an enemy remains inside E when your flight ends, they may fall below its execute threshold.
asol-combo-fight.text: In a full fight, use R to restrict movement, place E (Singularity), then fly in with W (Astral Flight) while continuously channeling Q (Breath of Light). Q has no channel duration limit during W, concentrating Aurelion Sol’s damage in that window. If the enemy remains inside E when the flight ends, they may fall below its execute threshold.

asol-combo-poke.basis: In trades, place E first, then layer Q over it. While E pulls enemies in, keep Q on one target to gain bonus damage and Stardust. If you use Q before E, the enemy may walk sideways and break Q's contact.
asol-combo-poke.text: When trading, place E (Singularity) first and layer Q (Breath of Light) over it. As E pulls the enemy toward its center, hold Q on one target long enough to trigger bonus damage and Stardust. Starting with Q lets the enemy sidestep and break contact.

asol-laning-early.basis: At levels 1–5, focus on catching waves over trading. The first minion hit blocks Q, preventing it from dealing full damage to the champion behind it. Try to poke with Q when your opponent steps beside the minion wave.
asol-laning-early.text: Aurelion Sol’s health and armor are among the lowest, so at levels 1–5, catching waves takes priority over trading. Q (Breath of Light) hits the first target in its path, and a minion in front prevents full damage to the champion behind it. Poke only when your opponent steps beside the minion wave; otherwise, leave Q off.

asol-laning-wave.basis: To clear a wave, hold the minions in E, then layer Q over it. Minions inside E have zero movement speed, so they do not spread out. Each unit that dies inside E grants Stardust. Think carefully before giving up a wave to roam.
asol-laning-wave.text: To clear a wave, hold the minions in E (Singularity), then layer Q (Breath of Light) over it. Minions inside E have zero movement speed and cannot spread out, while each unit that dies there grants Stardust. Because farming provides permanent growth, giving up a wave to roam costs Aurelion Sol more than it does other mid laners.

asol-phase.basis: Aurelion Sol is weakest at levels 1–8, when he has little Stardust. At levels 1–8, stay alive and farm waves. He becomes much stronger in mid game once R is empowered and he has one core item. In late game, E's area and execute threshold, along with R's impact area, keep growing with Stardust. Buy time to stack Stardust.
asol-phase.text: Aurelion Sol is weakest at levels 1–8, when he has little Stardust; focus on staying alive and farming waves. He grows much stronger in mid game once R is empowered and he has one core item. Later, Stardust keeps increasing E’s area and execute threshold as well as R’s impact area, turning him into a late-game carry. Buying time is part of his win condition.

asol-situational-antiheal.basis: Choose Morellonomicon if the enemy's healing is a problem. Q and E's damage over time can apply healing reduction for an extended period.
asol-situational-antiheal.text: Buy Morellonomicon when enemy healing becomes a problem. The sustained damage from Q (Breath of Light) and E (Singularity) keeps healing reduction applied for an extended period.

asol-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy can dive onto you, get Zhonya's Hourglass early to withstand their engage. You stay in place while channeling Q. Without a takedown, W remains on cooldown for a long time.
asol-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy can dive onto you, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier. Channeling Q (Breath of Light) keeps you in place, and W (Astral Flight) stays on cooldown for a long time without a takedown; you need a way to survive the initial engage long enough to deal damage.

asol-skill-e.basis: Lane minions and jungle monsters inside E have zero movement speed. Champions inside E are slowly pulled toward its center. As Stardust stacks, E's area and execute threshold grow. E cannot execute epic monsters.
asol-skill-e.text: E Singularity controls terrain rather than dealing damage. Lane minions and jungle monsters inside it have their movement speed reduced to zero, while champions are slowly pulled toward the center and executed if their health falls below the threshold there. As Aurelion Sol gains Stardust, both its area and execute threshold grow, making even a path covered by E dangerous to cross later in the game. Epic monsters cannot be executed.

asol-skill-passive-stardust.basis: Aurelion Sol's growth depends heavily on his Stardust count. Stardust stacks permanently and is not lost on death. Gain Stardust by keeping Q on the same enemy for a while, holding champions inside E, and hitting champions with R. Minions and monsters that die inside E also grant Stardust. Collect Stardust from every wave, even if you cannot win lane.
asol-skill-passive-stardust.text: Aurelion Sol’s growth depends on Stardust rather than levels or items. It stacks permanently when his abilities damage champions and is never lost on death: Q earns it by staying on the same enemy for a while, E earns it while champions remain inside, and R earns it for each champion hit. Minions and monsters that die inside E also grant Stardust, so farming drives his growth. Collect it from every wave, even in a lane you cannot win.

asol-skill-q.basis: Q deals full damage to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies. Keep Q on the same target for a while to gain bonus damage and Stardust. Avoid switching targets repeatedly while using Q. If you cancel Q right after casting it, you cannot use it again for a short time.
asol-skill-q.text: Q (Breath of Light) deals full damage only to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies. Keep it on the same target long enough to trigger bonus damage and Stardust; repeatedly switching targets wastes that opportunity. Canceling immediately after casting briefly locks the ability, so avoid tapping it for short bursts of poke.

asol-skill-r.basis: After collecting enough Stardust, R changes from Falling Star, which stuns, to The Skies Descend, which knocks enemies up. Empowered R also adds a wide shockwave and a slow. Use unempowered R to follow up on ganks or block escapes. Use empowered R to start teamfights.
asol-skill-r.text: Once enough Stardust has accumulated, R changes from Falling Star, which stuns, into The Skies Descend, which knocks enemies up and adds a wide shockwave and a slow. Check which version is ready: use Falling Star to follow up on ganks or cut off escapes, and The Skies Descend to start teamfights.

asol-skill-w.basis: During W flight, Q's cooldown and maximum channel duration limit are removed. Q's base damage increases during W flight. If you help secure a takedown soon after damaging a champion, you recover almost all of W's cooldown. Use W when you have a chance to secure a takedown. When using W to escape, leave Q off so your flight speed does not drop by half.
asol-skill-w.text: Treat W (Astral Flight) as a way to strengthen Q (Breath of Light): during flight, Q’s cooldown and maximum channel duration are removed, and its base damage rises. Helping secure a takedown soon after damaging a champion refunds almost all of W’s cooldown, so use it when a takedown is within reach. Without one, W stays on cooldown for a long time; because channeling Q also halves flight speed, leave it off when flying to escape.

asol-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, hold the frontline in place and keep dealing damage with Q. Q deals damage based on maximum health, making it effective against durable enemies too. Do not overextend to reach the backline. Turn on Q after your allies draw the enemy's attention or R restricts their movement.
asol-teamfight.text: In teamfights, hold the frontline in place and keep applying Q (Breath of Light), whose maximum-health damage is effective against durable enemies. There is no need to overextend toward the backline. Channeling Q slows Aurelion Sol’s movement, so turn it on only after allies draw the enemy’s attention or R restricts their movement.

asol-teamfight-objective.basis: Low-health enemies struggle to cross E's center because they risk being executed. Before an objective fight starts, place E in a passage the enemy must cross.
asol-teamfight-objective.text: In the narrow terrain around an objective, E Singularity can block an approach. Champions can pass through it, but stepping into the center risks execution, so low-health enemies cannot cross. Before the teamfight begins, place E in a passage the enemy must take and position your allies on the opposite side.

aurora-combo-allin.basis: When going all in, use Q's first hit, W to approach, an auto attack, E, then Q's return. While approaching with W, stealth and increased movement speed give the opponent less time to react. Weave one auto attack into your all-in combo to build passive stacks. You can still deal damage along Q's return path after E hops you backward.
aurora-combo-allin.text: For an all-in, land Q’s first hit, approach with W (Across the Veil), auto attack, use E (The Weirding), then retrieve Q. W’s stealth and movement speed give the opponent less time to react, while the auto attack builds passive stacks. E provides the final hit and hops Aurora backward to disengage; Q can still damage enemies along its return path from that distance.

aurora-combo-q-recall.basis: Q's first hit applies a curse. Recasting Q retrieves it and damages enemies along its path again. After landing Q, don't retrieve it immediately. Lower the target's health with an auto attack or E first. Line up Q's return path before it returns automatically when its duration ends.
aurora-combo-q-recall.text: Q (Twofold Hex) hits twice: the first hit applies a curse, and recasting retrieves it, damaging enemies along its return path. Because the return damage scales with the target’s missing health, land an auto attack or E before retrieving it. The curse returns automatically when its duration ends, so line up the return path before then to avoid losing damage.

aurora-laning-roam.basis: Push the wave, then use W to cross terrain and roam. When roaming, use W's stealth to hide the final part of your approach. Poke safely in lane, then spend your spare time in other lanes.
aurora-laning-roam.text: Push the wave, then use W Across the Veil to cross terrain and roam. Its hop, stealth, and movement speed boost can hide the final part of your approach even if the enemy has vision of you. Aurora’s damage per minute at 14 minutes ranks among the highest while her deaths are relatively low, which fits a pattern of poking safely in lane and spending the time you gain in other lanes.

aurora-laning-trade.basis: Land Q as your opponent steps forward for a last hit. Apply Q's curse, build passive stacks with an auto attack, then retrieve Q. An opponent cursed by Q may move to avoid its return path, disrupting their farming. Use the passive's healing to take repeated short trades.
aurora-laning-trade.text: Land Q as your opponent steps forward for a last hit, then add an auto attack to build passive stacks before retrieving the curse. A cursed opponent may move off the straight return path between them and Aurora, disrupting their farming. Repeat these short trades and back off; the passive’s healing helps Aurora maintain her health.

aurora-phase.basis: Aurora is weak at levels 1–2 because Q is her only available ability. At level 3, W lets Aurora trade and roam. Learning R at level 6 lets Aurora dive and initiate teamfights. Aurora's win rate rises after she completes three core items. Early on, use safe poke and farming to complete three core items instead of forcing kills.
aurora-phase.text: Play carefully at levels 1–2, when Aurora has only Q and low armor. At level 3, W opens up trading and roaming; from level 6, R enables dives and teamfight initiation. Her laning statistics are stable, but her win rate rises after three core items, so aim to reach that point through safe poke and farming instead of forcing early kills.

aurora-situational-zhonya.basis: If opponents have a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Zhonya's Hourglass between core items, since escaping with W and E will be difficult. Use Zhonya's Hourglass to survive being trapped inside R's area after engaging.
aurora-situational-zhonya.text: If the opposing team has a lot of immobilizing crowd control aimed at Aurora, fit Zhonya’s Hourglass between core items. Her escapes depend on the hops from W and E, both of which are ineffective when she is immobilized; the item can also help her survive being trapped inside R’s zone after engaging.

aurora-skill-e.basis: E deals area damage and applies a strong slow, then hops Aurora backward. Use E as your opponent engages to counterattack and create distance. Before casting E, check where you'll land when you hop opposite the cast direction. E's slow fades over time, so use your follow-up abilities immediately.
aurora-skill-e.text: E (The Weirding) deals area damage and applies a strong slow before hopping Aurora backward. Use it as an opponent engages to counterattack and create distance at once. The hop goes opposite the cast direction, so check where you will land before casting; because the slow fades over time, use any follow-up ability immediately.

aurora-skill-passive.basis: The passive triggers after you damage the same target multiple times, dealing damage based on their maximum health. When the passive triggers on a champion, a spirit follows Aurora and restores her health. Weave auto attacks between abilities to build passive stacks. In lane, take short trades: move in, build passive stacks, then back off.
aurora-skill-passive.text: P (Spirit Abjuration) triggers after Aurora damages the same target multiple times, dealing damage based on their maximum health; when that target is a champion, a spirit follows Aurora and restores her health. Abilities alone may leave the stacks incomplete, so weave in auto attacks. This healing is her source of lane sustain: take short trades to build stacks, then back off, instead of relying only on ranged poke.

aurora-skill-q.basis: Q's return damage is greatly reduced against minions and monsters. When clearing a wave, calculate around the damage from Q's first hit. When chasing a fleeing champion, delay Q's return as long as possible so their health drops further.
aurora-skill-q.text: Use Q (Twofold Hex) differently for wave clear and champion poke: its return damage is greatly reduced against minions and monsters, so judge wave clear by the first hit, while the return is the main source of damage against champions. When chasing a fleeing opponent, delay the return as long as possible so it lands after they have lost more health.

aurora-skill-r.basis: Use R to trap opponents. Use R to stop opponents from engaging. You can recast R to end it early. Keep R's area active if enemy reinforcements are outside it. If your team needs to retreat, end R's area early and leave with them. Choose your entry point knowing you can cross to the opposite side of R's area.
aurora-skill-r.text: R (Between Worlds) can initiate a fight and control an area, trapping opponents or blocking their engage. You can recast it to end the zone early: keep it active when enemy reinforcements are outside, but end it and retreat with your team if your allies need to leave. Choose your entry point with Aurora’s ability to cross from one side of the zone to the other in mind.

aurora-skill-w.basis: W gives Aurora a hop, stealth, and a movement speed boost. A takedown resets W's cooldown. Decide whether to engage with W based on whether you can reset its cooldown with a takedown.
aurora-skill-w.text: W Across the Veil gives Aurora a hop, stealth, and a movement speed boost, and its cooldown resets when she takes part in an enemy champion takedown. In a dive where you can secure a kill, that reset lets you use W to engage and still have an escape. If a takedown is uncertain, remember that Aurora is a fragile ranged champion: engage with W only when you can count on the reset.

aurora-teamfight.basis: Don't engage first with R while your opponents still have their engage abilities. Engage with R after your opponents have used their initiation abilities or your team has applied crowd control. Trap opponents with R, slow them with E, then retrieve Q. Move more aggressively after W's cooldown resets.
aurora-teamfight.text: Do not jump in first with R while opponents still have their engage abilities: Aurora’s low durability can leave her trapped inside her own zone. Wait until they have used their initiation abilities or an ally has applied crowd control, then use R to trap them, follow with E’s slow, and retrieve Q for area damage. You can move much more aggressively once W’s cooldown resets.

azir-combo-poke.basis: To poke, place a soldier in front of the enemy with W, attack with it, then send it toward the enemy with Q. Keep the attack command active while the soldier moves with Q so it attacks again as soon as it arrives. Attack with the soldier first, then move it with Q.
azir-combo-poke.text: To poke, place a soldier in front of the enemy with W, attack through it, then move it toward the enemy with Q. Keep the attack command active as the soldier moves so it attacks again as soon as it arrives. If you cast Q first, the soldier ends up near the enemy while Azir remains farther away, so attack before repositioning it.

azir-combo-shuffle.basis: Place a soldier behind the enemy with W, use E to get past them, then use R toward your allies to push the enemy back. Place the soldier at an angle that lets E carry you past the enemy without colliding with them. Attempt the combo that pushes an enemy toward your allies only when your allies are close enough to follow up.
azir-combo-shuffle.text: To push an enemy toward your allies, place a soldier behind them with W (Arise!), dash to it with E (Shifting Sands), then immediately cast R (Emperor's Divide) toward your team. R pushes the enemy away from Azir and into your team. E stops when it hits an enemy champion, so position the soldier at an angle that lets you get past them without colliding. If the combo fails, Azir is left alone among the enemy team; attempt it only when your allies are close enough to follow up.

azir-laning-mana.basis: Placing a soldier costs mana, and the soldier disappears when its duration ends. Place a soldier only when the enemy enters range or you need to last-hit. Don't keep replacing soldiers when there is no fight or last hit to take. Aim to farm safely during laning.
azir-laning-mana.text: Each soldier costs mana to place and disappears when its duration ends. Replacing soldiers when nothing is happening drains your mana, leaving you without soldiers or mana when the enemy jungler arrives. Place them only when an opponent enters range or you need to last-hit; otherwise, it is better to stand without one. In patch 26.17 mid-lane statistics, Azir’s CS at 14 minutes ranks in the upper-middle range while his kill statistic ranks near the bottom, so aim to farm safely during lane.

azir-laning-soldier-position.basis: During laning, place soldiers between the enemy minions and the enemy champion. A soldier between the minions and the enemy champion lets you last-hit while pressuring the enemy's approach. If you place soldiers only behind the minions, you can farm but lose your poke. If you place soldiers right next to the enemy champion, you can poke but miss last hits.
azir-laning-soldier-position.text: During laning, place a soldier between the enemy minions and champion. From there, it can secure last hits while threatening the champion if they approach. Placing soldiers only behind the minions lets you farm but gives up poke; placing them right next to the champion gives you poke but costs you last hits.

azir-phase.basis: Azir is weakest early on. Early on, Q's long cooldown leaves gaps between trades. In the mid game, Q's cooldown gets shorter, letting you use soldiers more often. Azir becomes strong in the late game as he builds attack speed and ability power. Early on, minimize losses instead of looking for an advantage. Don't stand forward in lane when you don't know where the enemy jungler is.
azir-phase.text: Azir is weakest early: his health and defensive stats are among the lowest, Q’s long cooldown leaves gaps between trades, and E is his only way to survive an enemy jungle gank. He takes shape in the mid game as Q’s cooldown shortens and soldiers become available more often, then becomes a hypercarry late as he builds both attack speed and ability power. Minimize losses early instead of seeking an advantage, and do not stand forward in lane when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown.

azir-skill-e.basis: E dashes to a soldier and grants a shield. If E collides with an enemy champion, Azir stops there and regains one soldier charge. When placing a soldier, also choose where you want E to take you. Use E to create distance and escape, or to engage an enemy and regain a soldier charge.
azir-skill-e.text: E dashes Azir to a soldier and grants a shield. Colliding with an enemy champion stops the dash and restores one soldier charge, so E can either create distance for an escape or carry Azir into an enemy to recover that charge. Decide where you want E to take you when you place the soldier.

azir-skill-passive.basis: Azir's passive can raise a Sun Disc where a turret has fallen. Use the Sun Disc to defend an area where an allied turret has been destroyed. Use the Sun Disc to hold the position after taking an enemy turret. The Sun Disc has armor and magic resistance and remains for a short time. Remember where destroyed turrets are near places where objective fights may happen.
azir-skill-passive.text: Azir’s passive can raise a Sun Disc where a turret has fallen. It is especially valuable for defending an area after an allied turret is destroyed or holding ground after taking an enemy turret. The Disc has armor and magic resistance and lasts for a short time, so remember which destroyed turret sites lie near likely objective fights.

azir-skill-q.basis: Q moves soldiers to the targeted location. Soldiers moving with Q damage and slow enemies in their path. Even if multiple soldiers pass through the same enemy with Q, they deal damage only once. Use Q when you need to reposition soldiers. Early on, Q has a long cooldown, so using it carelessly can cost you the next trade.
azir-skill-q.text: Q sends soldiers to a targeted location, damaging and slowing enemies along their path. An enemy takes damage only once even if multiple soldiers pass through them, so use Q to reposition soldiers rather than to stack damage. Its cooldown is long early on, and a careless cast can cost you the entire next trade; use it only when you have a reason to place your soldiers at the destination.

azir-skill-r-defense.basis: Use R to push enemies away as they engage on your allies. The soldier wall left by R briefly blocks enemies' path. Allies can pass through the soldier wall created by R. In narrow passages, use R to block enemies trying to follow up.
azir-skill-r-defense.text: Think of R as a defensive tool first: cast it as enemies engage your allies to push them away, then use the lingering soldier wall to block their path briefly. Allies can pass through it, giving them a route that diving melee enemies cannot use. In a narrow passage, the wall can trap the enemies trying to follow up.

azir-skill-w-charges.basis: W can hold up to two charges. Place two soldiers at once only when you can secure a kill. Save one W charge so you can place a soldier to escape. Place a soldier over a wall with W, then dash to it with E to escape.
azir-skill-w-charges.text: W holds up to two charges, but place two soldiers at once only when you are certain of a kill; always keep one charge available. Placing a soldier beyond a wall and dashing to it with E is Azir’s only escape route, and E also grants a shield, so using it early while being chased has no downside. If you place a soldier poorly and run out of charges, you lose both your escape route and your means of dealing damage.

azir-skill-w-projection.basis: Azir's effective attack range depends on where he places his W soldiers. Calculate your damage angles from the soldiers' positions, not Azir's. If enemies line up along a soldier's attack path, one attack hits multiple targets. When multiple soldiers hit the same target, damage drops sharply from the second soldier onward, and on-hit effects apply at half strength. Spread two soldiers apart at different angles instead of overlapping them.
azir-skill-w-projection.text: Azir’s own attack range is short; his effective reach depends on where he places his W soldiers. When an enemy is near a soldier, that soldier attacks in a straight line, so judge damage angles from its position rather than Azir’s. One attack can hit multiple enemies lined up along that path, but if several soldiers hit the same target, damage drops sharply after the first and on-hit effects apply at half strength. Spread two soldiers apart to cover different angles instead of overlapping them.

azir-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, keep Azir back and use soldiers to attack the enemy frontline continuously. Use R to push enemies away as they dive your backline. Use R to push an enemy toward your allies only when your team is clearly winning the fight. Azir has strong sustained damage but lacks burst damage. Avoid facing an enemy alone.
azir-teamfight.text: In teamfights, keep Azir back and send soldiers forward to deal sustained damage to the enemy frontline; Azir himself should never move to the front. Focus on when to cast R rather than looking for an opening to engage: the safest use is to push enemies away as they dive your backline. Push an enemy toward your allies only when your team is clearly winning the fight. Azir deals strong sustained damage but lacks burst, so avoid facing an enemy alone.

bard-combo-q-angle.basis: If there’s no wall or another enemy behind your target, Q won’t stun them. Before firing Q, move sideways to line yourself, your target, and the wall up.
bard-combo-q-angle.text: If there’s no wall or another enemy behind your target, Q won’t stun. Before firing, take a few steps sideways to line up yourself, the target, and the wall; those two or three steps can turn the hit into a stun.

bard-combo-q-wall.basis: Q stuns only if it hits a wall or a second enemy after passing through the first target. Fire Q at an enemy with a wall behind them. Fire Q when an enemy lines up with a minion. Hitting an isolated enemy with Q in open space only slows them.
bard-combo-q-wall.text: Q (Cosmic Binding) stuns only if it hits a wall or a second enemy after passing through its first target. Fire it at an enemy with a wall behind them or when they line up with a minion; an isolated enemy in open space will only be slowed.

bard-combo-r-defense.basis: Use R to save an ally just as a finishing ability is about to hit them. Use R to put an enemy who dives in into stasis, separating them from your allies.
bard-combo-r-defense.text: Use R to save an ally just as a finishing ability is about to hit them, breaking its target lock. You can also put a diving enemy in stasis to separate them from your allies.

bard-combo-r-setup.basis: R also affects allies. Aim R so your allied damage dealer does not get caught in it.
bard-combo-r-setup.text: R (Tempered Fate) also affects allies, so aim it to avoid catching your allied damage dealer.

bard-laning-absence.basis: If Bard stays away from lane too long, his marksman has to hold the lane alone. Leave lane after the enemy has used their engage ability. Leave lane when the wave is moving toward your turret. Place W shrines before leaving lane.
bard-laning-absence.text: Bard’s long absences leave his marksman holding the lane alone. Before roaming, check that the enemy has used their engage ability, choose a moment when the wave is moving toward your turret, and place W shrines for your partner.

bard-laning-trade.basis: Slow the enemy with Q, then trade damage with a meep attack. Fight near brush by a wall or at the river tri-brush to set up a Q stun.
bard-laning-trade.text: In lane, slow the enemy with Q before trading with a meep attack. Choose fights near brush by a wall or at the river tri-brush, where the terrain also gives you a chance to stun with Q.

bard-phase.basis: Bard is ordinary at levels 1–2 because he needs time to collect chimes. As chimes build up, stronger meep attacks and increased movement speed make Bard's roams faster. From level 6, R can turn an objective fight around. Later on, Bard's main roles are catching enemies out and intervening in teamfights.
bard-phase.text: Bard is ordinary at levels 1–2 while he collects chimes, but stronger meep attacks and increased movement speed make his roams faster as they build up. From level 6, R can turn an objective fight around; later, his main roles are catching enemies out and intervening in teamfights.

bard-skill-chime.basis: Collecting more chimes strengthens Bard's meep attacks and increases his movement speed. Collect chimes when the wave is pushed out and the lane is safe. Collect chimes along your path back to lane. Do not leave your lane partner alone to chase chimes.
bard-skill-chime.text: Collecting chimes strengthens Bard’s meep attacks and increases his movement speed, but chasing them at the cost of leaving your lane partner alone is a poor trade. Pick up chimes when the wave is pushed out and the lane is safe, or along your recall route.

bard-skill-e-both.basis: Enemies can also use E portals. Before opening an E portal to escape, check whether an enemy can follow you. Allies travel through E portals faster than enemies.
bard-skill-e-both.text: Enemies can use E (Magical Journey) portals too. Before opening one to escape, check whether an enemy can follow; allies travel through them faster than enemies, but the route is open to both.

bard-skill-meep.basis: Basic attacks with meeps are one of Bard's ways to harass. When you have meeps, approach the enemy and harass them with basic attacks. Do not waste meep attacks on minions. With enough chimes, meep attacks spread to nearby targets. With enough chimes, meep attacks slow nearby targets.
bard-skill-meep.text: Meep empowered basic attacks are Bard’s way to harass: approach and hit the enemy when you have meeps, and don’t waste them on minions. With enough chimes, the attacks spread to nearby targets and slow them, making trades much more valuable.

bard-skill-w-charge.basis: W shrines heal more as they charge over time. If healing is not urgent, place a W shrine in advance and step on it later. An enemy champion destroys a W shrine by walking over it. Place W shrines behind your allies.
bard-skill-w-charge.text: W (Caretaker’s Shrine) heals more as it charges over time, so place a shrine in advance and step on it later if healing isn’t urgent. Enemy champions destroy shrines by walking over them; put yours behind your allies, away from the enemy and the middle of the lane.

bard-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, Bard catches enemies out and cuts them off. Use Q to pin an engaging enemy against a wall. Use R to briefly take the enemy's main damage dealer out of the fight. Use R to stop an enemy arriving late to the fight. Bard is not a champion who absorbs damage at the front.
bard-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Bard’s role is to catch enemies out and cut them off. Pin an engaging enemy against a wall with Q, or use R to briefly remove the enemy’s main damage dealer from the fight or stop someone arriving late. Bard should not stand at the front absorbing damage.

bard-teamfight-objective.basis: R also affects Dragon and Baron. As the enemy jungler prepares to Smite, use R to freeze both the objective and the enemy. Before using R at an objective, coordinate its timing with your jungler's Smite.
bard-teamfight-objective.text: R affects Dragon and Baron too. As the enemy jungler prepares to Smite, put both the objective and the enemy in stasis to delay the Smite contest, and coordinate the timing with your jungler beforehand.

belveth-combo-basic.basis: In a standard fight, use Q to close in and auto attack, knock them up with W, then re-engage with the reset Q. If W hits a champion, it resets Q's cooldown in the direction W was cast. Right after W lands, you can use Q once more in the same direction.
belveth-combo-basic.text: In a standard fight, close in with Q and an auto attack, knock the enemy up with W, then re-engage with the reset Q. Hitting a champion with W resets Q’s cooldown in the direction W was cast, letting you dash that way once more immediately; without the reset, Bel’Veth’s engage ends after one Q.

belveth-combo-e-timing.basis: Activate E when the enemy starts their burst combo. While E is active, Bel'Veth takes much less damage and gains lifesteal. Using another ability or pressing E again ends E immediately. Do not press Q or W while using E to survive. If you need to hold out for a while and then escape immediately with Q, cancel E on purpose.
belveth-combo-e-timing.text: Activate E as the enemy starts their burst combo, rather than immediately after engaging: Bel'Veth takes much less damage and gains lifesteal while casting it. Using another ability or pressing E again ends it immediately, so avoid Q and W while relying on E to survive. When you only need to hold out briefly before escaping with Q, cancel E deliberately.

belveth-jungle-clear.basis: When clearing the jungle, use Q to move between camps and keep your rotation going. Q deals bonus damage to monsters. At camps where you lose health, use E's lifesteal to heal while clearing.
belveth-jungle-clear.text: Keep your jungle clear moving by using Q (Void Surge) between camps and maintaining your rotation. It deals bonus damage to monsters, and its cooldown is tracked by direction, so you can use it within a camp as well. In camps that cost you health, activate E (Royal Maelstrom) to heal through lifesteal while clearing and save blue essence or potions.

belveth-jungle-gank.basis: Bel'Veth cannot gank with W alone. Gank lanes where an ally has reliable crowd control. Gank when the enemy has pushed the lane and has a long way to escape. If ganks are uncertain before level 6, clear large monsters to build stacks. If ganks are uncertain before level 6, establish vision around objectives.
belveth-jungle-gank.text: Bel’Veth cannot make a gank work with W alone. Look for lanes where an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed up and has a long way to escape. If a gank looks uncertain before level 6, clear large monsters for stacks and establish vision around objectives instead.

belveth-phase.basis: Bel'Veth is weakest at levels 1–3. At levels 1–3, avoid encounters with the enemy jungler. Duels become viable in the mid game, after maxing Q, completing your first core item, and starting to build stacks. Bel'Veth peaks in the late game once she has enough Lavender stacks.
belveth-phase.text: Bel'Veth is weakest at levels 1–3, when both her health and attack damage are low, so avoid encounters with the enemy jungler then. Duels become viable in the mid game after maxing Q, completing your first core item, and beginning to build stacks; she peaks in the late game once she has enough stacks. Because her early game stats are generally among the lowest, getting through that phase without falling behind is itself a successful start.

belveth-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing makes it hard to secure a kill with sustained damage, buy Executioner's Calling first and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Auto attacks and Q's on-hit effects can keep applying Grievous Wounds.
belveth-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing prevents your sustained damage from securing kills, buy Executioner’s Calling first and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Auto attacks and Q’s on-hit effects let Bel’Veth keep reapplying Grievous Wounds.

belveth-situational-mercurial.basis: If the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities that can lock down Bel'Veth, buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar between core items. Bel'Veth survives more easily only while she can move with Q.
belveth-situational-mercurial.text: If the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities that can lock Bel’Veth down, fit Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar between core items. She survives by keeping Q available to move, so removing the time she spends immobilized is more valuable than building armor.

belveth-skill-passive.basis: Lavender stacks from Death in Lavender grant permanent attack speed. A takedown on a large minion or large monster grants one Lavender stack. A takedown on a champion or epic monster grants two Lavender stacks. Bel'Veth's late-game strength depends on her Lavender stacks. Secure takedowns on large jungle monsters to keep scaling. Join team fights to earn takedowns. After using an ability, Bel'Veth briefly gains bonus attack speed and ghosting. When you need to pass through minions, use Q once and move through them.
belveth-skill-passive.text: Lavender stacks from Death in Lavender grant permanent attack speed: a takedown on a large minion or monster grants one, while a takedown on a champion or epic monster grants two. Bel’Veth’s late-game strength depends on those stacks, so secure takedowns on large jungle monsters and join team fights to keep scaling. After using an ability, she briefly gains bonus attack speed and ghosting; use Q once when you need to pass through minions.

belveth-skill-q-direction.basis: Q has a separate cooldown for each direction. You cannot use Q twice in a row in the same direction, but you can use it again immediately in a different direction. When escaping, use Q in different directions.
belveth-skill-q-direction.text: Q has a separate cooldown for each direction, so you cannot dash the same way twice in a row but can immediately dash in another direction. Use that to move and dodge in a zigzag, changing directions with Q as you escape instead of fleeing in a straight line.

belveth-skill-q-onhit.basis: Q applies on-hit effects to the first target it hits. If you have on-hit items, line up Q to pass through the enemy during fights. Q's cooldown gets shorter as attack speed increases.
belveth-skill-q-onhit.text: Q (Void Surge) applies on-hit effects to the first target it hits, making it both a dash and the equivalent of one basic attack. Because it becomes a major source of damage when Bel'Veth builds on-hit items, line it up to pass through enemies in fights instead of using it only to move. Its cooldown also shortens as attack speed rises, so building attack speed improves her mobility.

belveth-skill-r-coral.basis: Void Coral drops only after a takedown on a champion or epic monster. Bel'Veth must consume Void Coral to transform into her true form. Right after a kill in a fight, check where the coral dropped. Transforming increases maximum health, attack range, and attack speed. If you have secured coral, transform just before the next fight or objective contest.
belveth-skill-r-coral.text: Bel’Veth can use R to transform into her true form only by consuming Void Coral, which drops after she takes part in a champion or epic monster takedown. Check where the coral lands immediately after a kill in a fight. The transformation increases maximum health, attack range, and attack speed, so once you have coral, use it just before the next fight or objective contest rather than saving it.

belveth-skill-r-voidling.basis: If you transform using coral left by a Void epic monster, nearby minions that die become Void Remora. Void Remora push the lane. After taking a Void objective, choose a lane to pressure and transform near it.
belveth-skill-r-voidling.text: Coral left by a Void epic monster differs from ordinary coral: transforming with it turns nearby minions that die into Void Remora, which push the lane for you. After taking a Void objective, choose the lane you want to pressure and transform near it.

belveth-skill-w.basis: W is Bel'Veth's only reliable crowd control and her way to reset Q. When ganking, draw out the enemy's mobility ability or Flash before using W. If the enemy is on the opposite side of their escape route, use W to cut off their path.
belveth-skill-w.text: W (Above and Below) is Bel'Veth's only guaranteed crowd control and resets Q. Using it too early in a gank lets the enemy escape with a mobility ability after being knocked up, leaving her without a way to close the gap. Draw out their mobility ability or Flash first, or use W to cut off their direction of travel when they are on the opposite side of their escape route.

belveth-teamfight.basis: Bel'Veth is not suited to leading the front line in team fights. After your tank absorbs the enemy engage, flank with Q into the backline, kill one enemy, and escape with Q. If targeted enemy abilities focus you right after you engage, activate E. After a kill, transform with the dropped coral to prepare for the next fight. E does not require a target; it automatically targets the enemy with the lowest health. Use E to finish enemies in chaotic fights.
belveth-teamfight.text: Bel’Veth should not lead the front line in team fights. Once your tank absorbs the enemy engage, flank into the backline with Q, kill one enemy, and use Q to get out. If targeted abilities focus you right after you engage, activate E; after a takedown, consume the dropped coral to transform and gain an advantage in the next fight. E needs no target and automatically attacks the lowest-health enemy, making it especially useful for finishing opponents in chaotic fights.

blitz-combo-basic.basis: The basic combo is to pull with Q, knock up with E, and finish with R. Chain Q, E, and R without gaps to prevent a squishy target from fighting back. Try the combo within your turret's range so the turret attacks too.
blitz-combo-basic.text: The basic combo is Q to pull a target in, E to knock them up, then R to finish. Chained without gaps, these abilities leave a squishy target no time to fight back; landing the combo within your turret’s range makes it much deadlier by adding turret attacks.

blitz-combo-e-prefire.basis: Activate E just before Q hits to immediately knock up the pulled target. Pressing E after Q pulls the target gives them a window to escape with a mobility ability.
blitz-combo-e-prefire.text: Activate E just before Q hits so you knock the target up as soon as they are pulled in. Waiting until after the pull gives them time to escape with a mobility ability, so anticipate the hit and activate E early.

blitz-combo-e-reset.basis: E resets the basic attack timer. When harassing, use E immediately after a basic attack to land both attacks in quick succession.
blitz-combo-e-reset.text: E resets your basic attack timer, so when harassing, use it immediately after a basic attack to land two attacks in quick succession.

blitz-combo-w-e-first.basis: If you are unsure you can land Q, approach with W, knock up with E, then use Q. Use Q while the target is knocked up by E or when they start fleeing. Check that the enemy has used their crowd control before approaching with W. Start your W engage from brush to make your approach less visible.
blitz-combo-w-e-first.text: If you are unsure you can land Q, reverse the order: approach with W, knock the target up with E, then land Q while they are airborne or as they start to flee. Your approach will be visible, so check that the enemy has used their crowd control and start from brush.

blitz-laning.basis: Blitzcrank's grab opportunities in lane depend heavily on securing brush vision. Control the brush to conceal your grab range. When Q is on cooldown, fall back and protect your ally as they farm.
blitz-laning.text: Laning as Blitzcrank revolves around brush vision: controlling brush conceals your grab range, while enemy vision leaves few openings. When Q is on cooldown, fall back instead of stepping forward and protect your ally as they farm.

blitz-laning-invade.basis: Q is especially effective in narrow jungle chokepoints. Join early invades and try to catch the enemy jungler with Q at chokepoints. Look for chances to steal enemy camps with Q during early invades. If your lane is stable, pressure enemy jungle routes with your allies.
blitz-laning-invade.text: Q is especially strong in narrow jungle chokepoints. Join early invades to catch the enemy jungler there or create a chance to steal a camp; if your lane is stable, pressure jungle routes with your allies.

blitz-phase.basis: At level 1, using Q leaves you unable to apply much pressure for a while. Blitzcrank starts applying serious grab pressure at levels 2–3. Blitzcrank stays strong throughout the early and mid game. As the game progresses, Blitzcrank relies on allied follow-up to kill targets. In the late game, avoid grabs without allied follow-up.
blitz-phase.text: At level 1, Q’s high mana cost and long cooldown leave Blitzcrank with little threat for a while after he uses it. His grab pressure takes hold at levels 2–3 and stays strong through the early and mid game. Later, he cannot kill a target alone, so a grab without allied follow-up can work against you.

blitz-skill-passive.basis: When Blitzcrank's health falls below 30%, his passive shield activates. The passive shield scales with maximum mana. Spending mana does not reduce the passive shield's strength. Choose items that increase maximum mana to strengthen the passive shield. After the passive shield activates, look for an opening to engage while accounting for its cooldown.
blitz-skill-passive.text: Mana Barrier activates when Blitzcrank falls below 30% health, and its shield scales with maximum mana rather than decreasing as he spends mana. Items that increase maximum mana strengthen it; after it triggers, account for the time without a shield during its cooldown when looking for an engage.

blitz-skill-q.basis: Q pulls only the first enemy it hits along its path. Target enemies when they move away from minions so minions cannot block Q. Hide in brush to conceal your Q reach. Avoid spamming Q early, given its high mana cost and long cooldown. If the Q angle is uncertain, hold it to pressure the enemy into retreating.
blitz-skill-q.text: Q pulls only the first enemy it hits along its path, so wait until your target moves away from minions or hide in brush to conceal your range. Its high mana cost and long cooldown mean spamming it early can cost you the entire laning phase. Simply holding Q also creates pressure, and keeping it to make the enemy back off is often better than throwing it at an uncertain angle.

blitz-skill-r.basis: R has a relatively short cooldown for an ultimate. Use R to push waves. Use R to disrupt enemy sieges. Clear minions with R to create a Q angle. When sneaking up, keep in mind that R's automatic lightning may unintentionally hit an enemy.
blitz-skill-r.text: R has a short cooldown for an ultimate, so you can use it to push waves, disrupt a siege, or clear minions to open a Q angle. Its passive lightning triggers automatically when you enter combat and may hit an enemy unintentionally, so account for that when sneaking up.

blitz-skill-r-hold.basis: Avoid using R immediately in an extended one-on-one fight with no minions. After several hits, R's passive lightning deals more total damage than its active. Use R when you need immediate burst damage. Use R when you need a silence. Use R when you need to remove enemy shields.
blitz-skill-r-hold.text: In an extended one-on-one fight without minions, it is better to hold R: after several hits, its passive lightning deals more damage than the active cast. Use R when you need immediate burst damage or a silence, or when you need to remove an enemy shield.

blitz-skill-w.basis: Use W to approach and escape. W slows you when it ends, making escape harder. W's attack speed boost contributes greatly to attacking objectives. Use your saved W when starting to attack Dragon or Rift Herald.
blitz-skill-w.text: W helps Blitzcrank approach or escape, though its self-slow when it ends makes it less useful for getting away. Its large attack speed boost is also valuable against objectives, so activate a saved W when you start attacking Dragon or Rift Herald.

blitz-teamfight.basis: Blitzcrank struggles to kill healthy targets alone and relies on allied damage. Engage with Q only when allies can follow up immediately. After engaging, use E and W to stick to the target and maintain pressure.
blitz-teamfight.text: Blitzcrank cannot kill a healthy target alone, so throw Q only when allies can follow up immediately. After engaging, stay on the target with E and W to maintain pressure and give your allies the confidence to follow in.

brand-combo-burst.basis: For single-target burst, use W, Q, E, then W. Land W, which has a warning, during the Q stun. If Blaze reaches maximum stacks during this combo, the explosion also deals damage. E has twice the spread range when used on a burning target.
brand-combo-burst.text: For single-target burst, use W → Q stun → E → W. The Q stun lets you land the delayed second W, while Blaze reaches maximum stacks and adds an explosion. W deals more damage to a burning target, and E spreads twice as far from one, so changing the order greatly reduces what you get from the same abilities.

brand-combo-stun.basis: At range, set the target on fire with W, then stun them with Q. If the enemy is already close, use E then Q for a quick stun. The enemy must have Blaze before Q reaches them for it to stun.
brand-combo-stun.text: The key to a stun combo is to avoid opening with Q. At range, apply Blaze with W, then stun with Q; when the enemy is already close, E into Q is faster. Either way, Blaze must be on the target before Q arrives.

brand-laning.basis: Poke with W during the laning phase. Place W as the enemy marksman steps forward to last-hit. After poking with W, do not stay within the enemy's range. Brand uses a lot of mana and has low health, making him vulnerable to dying in lane.
brand-laning.text: In lane, focus on poking with W. Its long range and ability to pass through minions let you place it where the enemy marksman steps forward to last-hit. It costs a lot of mana, though, and Brand’s health is among the lowest in the game; linger within enemy range after a poke and you can die on the spot. Brand’s 14-minute death count is statistically among the highest for supports, reflecting that risk.

brand-laning-allin.basis: Go all in when the enemy has Blaze and Q is available. Before going all in, check that the enemy has Blaze. Landing Q on a burning enemy lets your allies land basic attacks and lets you use W and E during the stun.
brand-laning-allin.text: Go all in when the enemy has Blaze and Q is available. Check that they are burning before engaging: landing Q then guarantees a long stun, giving your marksman time to land basic attacks while you use W and E. An all-in opened without Blaze will not work.

brand-phase.basis: Brand's damage depends heavily on the Blaze explosion rather than individual abilities. His trades become stronger from levels 3–6, when he can chain at least two abilities. Brand is strongest in the mid game as he builds ability power. Brand struggles to contribute to late-game teamfights if he gets picked off first. In the late game, position yourself to avoid getting picked off first.
brand-phase.text: Brand’s damage comes mainly from Blaze explosions rather than individual abilities, so his trades grow stronger around levels 3–6, when he can chain at least two abilities. He peaks in the mid game as he builds ability power. Late in the game, his health remains among the lowest and he has no mobility ability, so getting picked off first leaves him unable to contribute to a teamfight. His late-game value depends on positioning rather than damage.

brand-skill-e.basis: E spreads around the targeted unit. E has twice the spread range when used on a burning target. Set a minion on fire, then use E to poke the enemy champion beside it. Set minions on fire to make it hard for enemies to stand near their minions.
brand-skill-e.text: E Conflagration spreads around its target, with twice the spread range if that target is burning. Set a minion on fire, then use E to reach an enemy champion standing beside it. Even the threat of that spread makes it hard for enemies to stand near their minions.

brand-skill-passive-blaze.basis: Brand's damage depends heavily on Blaze stacks. Landing an ability adds Blaze stacks to the target. When Blaze reaches maximum stacks on a champion or large jungle monster, it explodes shortly afterward, dealing area damage based on maximum health. Build combos around stacking Blaze. When farming, apply Blaze before last-hitting to restore mana.
brand-skill-passive-blaze.text: Blaze is central to Brand’s damage. Abilities apply stacks, and reaching maximum stacks on a champion or large jungle monster triggers an explosion shortly afterward that deals area damage based on maximum health. Build combos around applying stacks in the right order. When farming, apply Blaze before last-hitting a burning unit to restore mana.

brand-skill-q.basis: Q is a single-target projectile that stops at the first enemy hit. Q stuns only if the target is already burning. Use Q when the target is burning and no minions block its path.
brand-skill-q.text: Q Sear stops at the first enemy it hits and stuns only a target that is already burning. Opening with Q will not stun, and a minion can block it, so use it when the target is burning and the projectile’s path is clear of minions.

brand-skill-r.basis: R prioritizes bouncing toward champions with fewer Blaze stacks. The fewer targets R can bounce to, the more often it hits the same target. Count the targets R can bounce to before casting it. In fights with many champions, use R to spread stacks across the area. In smaller fights, R concentrates damage on one target.
brand-skill-r.text: R Pyroclasm prioritizes champions with fewer Blaze stacks when it bounces. Among many clustered enemies, it is harder to hit the same target repeatedly; with fewer targets, it bounces back to one target more often. Count the available targets before casting: use R to spread stacks in larger fights and to concentrate damage on one target in smaller fights.

brand-skill-w.basis: W detonates after a warning, so enemies can walk out of it. Place W ahead of the enemy's movement. Use W during an ally's immobilizing effect or your Q stun. W deals more damage to burning targets. To increase W's damage, set the target on fire first. W is Brand's only long-range poke that minions cannot block.
brand-skill-w.text: W Pillar of Flame erupts after a warning, giving enemies time to walk out. Place it ahead of their movement or layer it over an ally’s immobilizing effect or your Q stun. It deals more damage to burning targets, so apply Blaze first; its long range also makes it Brand’s only poke that minions cannot block.

brand-teamfight.basis: Stay in the back during teamfights and deal area damage. When enemies group up, set them on fire with W, spread Blaze with E, then use R. Blaze's explosion damages the frontline too, so do not move forward to target the backline.
brand-teamfight.text: Stay in the back during teamfights and deal area damage without diving in. Wait for enemies to group, apply Blaze with W, spread it with E, then cast R. Blaze’s maximum-health-based explosion also damages the frontline, so there is no need to move forward to target the backline.

brand-teamfight-choke.basis: If enemies are spread out, R stops bouncing early. Use R in narrow passages near objectives or when the enemy formation tightens. Save R if the enemies have already spread out. If enemies are spread out, use E and W to keep Blaze on the frontline.
brand-teamfight-choke.text: R needs nearby targets to keep bouncing and stops early when enemies spread out. Cast it in narrow passages near objectives or when the enemy formation tightens. If they have already spread out, save R and use E and W to keep Blaze on the frontline.

braum-combo-engage.basis: Apply the first stack with Q, close the gap with W, then build stacks with basic attacks to stun. Allied basic attacks build Concussive Blows stacks faster. Tell your allies whom to attack right after Q hits.
braum-combo-engage.text: Start an engage by landing Q (Winter's Bite) to slow the target and apply the first Concussive Blows stack, then close the gap with W (Stand Behind Me) to a forward minion or ally and use basic attacks to add the remaining stacks for a stun. Allied basic attacks stack Concussive Blows much faster, so signal which target to attack as soon as Q hits.

braum-combo-ult-chain.basis: After knocking an enemy up with R, hit Q just before they land to follow up with a slow and a stack. Enemies knocked up by R cannot use movement abilities while airborne. Follow R with Q and basic attacks to extend the crowd control into a stun.
braum-combo-ult-chain.text: After knocking an enemy up with R, land Q just before they touch down to add a slow and a stack. They cannot use movement abilities while airborne, so following R with Q and basic attacks can carry the crowd control straight into a stun.

braum-laning-vision.basis: W requires an ally or minion, so Braum has trouble moving quickly on his own. Protect your marksman in lane while maintaining vision of the river and bushes. When the enemy jungler comes in, slow their engage with Q and E.
braum-laning-vision.text: Braum gains little from roaming: his movement speed is ordinary, and W needs an ally or minion, so he cannot move quickly alone. Stay in lane to protect your marksman, maintain vision around the river and bushes, and use Q and E to delay an incoming enemy jungler.

braum-phase.basis: Braum is fairly strong in lane because he can start trades with Q from level 1. From level 6, Braum can use R to force an engage and control terrain. Braum stays strong through the mid game as he builds defensive items. In the late game, Braum's impact drops sharply if his allies have fallen behind.
braum-phase.text: Braum is fairly strong in lane: from level 1, Q can start a trade, and he has high defensive stats. At level 6, R gives him a way to force an engage and control terrain, while defensive items keep him strong through the mid game. His own damage is very low late, though, so his impact drops sharply if his allies have fallen behind.

braum-situational-cleanse.basis: If the enemy has an ability that can immobilize and burst down your marksman, buy Mikael's Blessing earlier. Braum has no way to remove crowd control already applied to an ally.
braum-situational-cleanse.text: If the enemy can immobilize and burst down your marksman, buy Mikael's Blessing earlier. Braum can block attacks with his body, but he cannot remove crowd control already applied to an ally.

braum-skill-e.basis: E intercepts and destroys projectiles coming from the direction Braum faces. E negates damage from the first projectile it intercepts and reduces damage from later ones. E cannot block projectiles coming from behind or beside Braum. Stand in front of your ally, putting your body between them and the enemy marksman. Raise E when you see the enemy begin casting a key skillshot.
braum-skill-e.text: E (Unbreakable) intercepts and destroys projectiles from the direction Braum faces, negating damage from the first and reducing damage from those that follow. It cannot block attacks from the side or behind, so stand in front of your ally and put yourself between them and the enemy marksman. Because the shield lasts only a short time, raise it when you see a key enemy skillshot being cast.

braum-skill-passive.basis: Concussive Blows starts when Braum applies the first mark. After that, allied basic attacks also add stacks. The final stack triggers a stun and magic damage. Agree with your allies on a target before starting a trade.
braum-skill-passive.text: Concussive Blows begins when Braum applies the first mark; allied basic attacks can then add stacks. The final stack stuns the target and deals magic damage, so Braum needs his marksman to attack the same target to complete the crowd control. Agree on a target with your ally before starting a trade.

braum-skill-passive-window.basis: Stacks cannot build again for a short time after the stun triggers. Braum's basic attacks deal bonus damage immediately after the stun. If allies do not attack in time after the first stack, the mark expires.
braum-skill-passive-window.text: For a short time after the stun, stacks cannot build again, but Braum's basic attacks deal bonus damage, so staying close and attacking is still worthwhile. The mark does not last long: if allies fail to follow up on the first stack, it expires.

braum-skill-q.basis: Q is a projectile that hits only the first enemy it reaches. Q heavily slows enemies. Q applies a stack of Concussive Blows. Minions block Q. In lane, look for gaps between minions to land Q. Q is Braum's main way to start a fight from range. If Q misses, it's hard to start a trade.
braum-skill-q.text: Q (Winter's Bite) hits only the first enemy in its path, heavily slowing them and applying a Concussive Blows stack. Minions block it, so look for gaps between them in lane; as Braum's main way to start a trade from range, a missed Q makes that trade hard to begin.

braum-skill-r.basis: After a long cast animation, R sends a fissure forward in a straight line. The farther R's first target is from Braum, the longer they are knocked up. Aim R's first hit at a key target farther away. The fissure left by R is a strong slowing zone.
braum-skill-r.text: R (Glacial Fissure) has a noticeably long cast animation before sending a fissure straight ahead. Its first target is knocked up longer the farther they are from Braum, so aim that first hit at a distant key target rather than an enemy nearby. The lingering fissure creates a strong slowing zone that acts as a barrier.

braum-skill-w.basis: W can leap to allied champions and minions. When W lands, Braum and the target gain armor and magic resistance. Braum gains more armor and magic resistance from W than the target does. Use W to reach an ally just before they take damage.
braum-skill-w.text: Braum can use W (Stand Behind Me) to leap to allied minions as well as champions, making minions useful for repositioning. On arrival, both Braum and his target gain armor and magic resistance, with Braum receiving the larger bonus. W protects an ally while making Braum tougher, so use it to jump toward an ally just before Braum takes a beating.

braum-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stand between your backline and the enemy damage dealers. Stay beside your marksman, then use R on enemies who dive in to break up their formation. Place R's fissure along the enemy's path for follow-up.
braum-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stand between your backline and the enemy damage dealers. Stay beside your marksman and use R lengthwise against enemies diving in to split their formation, placing the lingering fissure across the path of their follow-up so the fight is divided in two.

briar-combo-gank.basis: When ganking, stun with Q, activate W, land a basic attack, then recast W. When W is active, Briar can no longer choose her target herself. To attack a specific enemy, lock onto them with Q before activating W.
briar-combo-gank.text: For a gank, stun the target with Q (Head Rush), activate W (Blood Frenzy), land a basic attack, then recast W (Snack Attack). Use Q first because Blood Frenzy takes away Briar’s ability to choose her target; locking onto the intended enemy before activating W keeps her from attacking someone else.

briar-combo-r.basis: In teamfights, land R, then after landing, use Q to stun, land a basic attack, recast W, and use E. Interrupt enemies using channeled ultimates with R's bloodstone. If the enemy's escape route leads toward a wall, fully charge E at the end to stun them against it.
briar-combo-r.text: In teamfights, land R's bloodstone to trigger an area fear on arrival, then stun with Q, land a basic attack, recast W for the bite, and finish with E. The bloodstone also interrupts an enemy's channel on hit, so use it to stop channeled ultimates. If the enemy is escaping toward a wall, fully charge the finishing E to stun them against it.

briar-jungle-gank.basis: Briar's kill participation at 14 minutes ranks among the highest of all champions. Try ganking where an ally has guaranteed crowd control or the enemy has pushed the lane. If there is no gank opportunity, don't activate W, which is hard to undo.
briar-jungle-gank.text: Briar ranks among the highest champions for kill participation at 14 minutes, but her death statistics are also near the bottom. Her ganks are strong, yet a failed engage can quickly get her killed. Gank lanes where an ally has guaranteed crowd control or the enemy has pushed up; if there is no opening, leave W off because its taunt prevents you from turning back.

briar-phase.basis: Once Briar has Q, W, and E and learns R at level 6, she gains solo kill opportunities. Briar is strongest in the mid game when she has both attack damage and health. If Briar engages first in a late game teamfight, she may fall before she can heal. In the late game, enter after your allies start the fight and finish it.
briar-phase.text: Once Briar has Q, W, and E and unlocks R at level 6, she can find solo kills. She peaks in the mid game when she has both attack damage and health, but her level 18 health ranks among the lowest of all champions, so engaging first in a late game teamfight can get her killed before she heals. Later on, let an ally start the fight, then go in to finish it.

briar-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Briar can easily maintain healing reduction by spreading damage with her bleed and area basic attacks.
briar-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Briar’s bleed and area basic attacks spread damage in small hits, making healing reduction easy to maintain; in a fight where both sides rely on healing, the side that applies it first wins.

briar-situational-qss.basis: If the enemy has a long root, consider Mercurial Scimitar. Briar cannot heal while a root prevents her from landing basic attacks, leaving her vulnerable to losing health.
briar-situational-qss.text: Consider Mercurial Scimitar against a long root. Briar heals only while she is close enough to land basic attacks, so time spent rooted and unable to attack costs her health.

briar-skill-e.basis: E is Briar's only way to end Blood Frenzy herself and regain control. While charging E, Briar takes less damage and heals based on her maximum health. Fully charging E knocks enemies back and stuns those who hit a wall. Fully charge E against an enemy with a wall behind them. In open space, use a short E for damage and a slow.
briar-skill-e.text: E (Chilling Scream) is Briar’s only way to end Blood Frenzy herself and regain control. Charging it reduces incoming damage and heals her based on her maximum health, making it useful for survival in fights and recovery while hunting. A fully charged scream knocks enemies back and stuns them if they hit a wall, so charge it all the way against an enemy with a wall behind them; in open space, release it early for damage and a slow.

briar-skill-passive.basis: Briar has no base health regeneration and spends current health each time she uses an ability. To heal, keep attacking and maintain bleed stacks. The more health Briar is missing, the more she heals.
briar-skill-passive.text: Briar has no base health regeneration and spends current health whenever she uses an ability, so standing still will not heal her; she must keep attacking and maintain bleed stacks. The more health she is missing, the more she recovers, so low health alone is not a warning sign, but casting abilities in quick succession while low costs her even more health.

briar-skill-r.basis: The first champion hit by R's bloodstone becomes the prey. To make your intended target the prey, fire R from an angle where the frontline cannot block it. When Briar lands with R, nearby enemies other than the prey are feared. Land R where enemies are grouped to split up those nearby.
briar-skill-r.text: The first champion hit by R’s (Certain Death) bloodstone becomes Briar’s prey, so your aim determines the target. Fire from an angle where the frontline cannot block the shot if you want to reach a particular enemy. On landing, Briar fears nearby enemies other than her prey, allowing her to engage and split up a grouped team at once.

briar-skill-w-control.basis: When Briar activates W, she is taunted toward the nearest enemy and loses control. Choose your target before activating W. Use Q to close in on your target first. If the enemy frontline is in front, don't activate W first.
briar-skill-w-control.text: Activating W taunts Briar toward the nearest enemy and takes away your control, so treat it as a damage boost after choosing a target, not as an engage tool. Use Q to reach that target first; if the enemy frontline is in front of you, opening with W can pull you toward the wrong opponent.

briar-skill-w-jungle.basis: Using Q on a minion or monster during Blood Frenzy removes the priority on attacking champions. When you need to chase a champion, don't use Q on a monster.
briar-skill-w-jungle.text: Using Q on a minion or monster during Blood Frenzy removes Briar’s priority for attacking champions. This can keep a passing champion from drawing her away while she clears a camp, but avoid using Q on a monster when you need to chase a champion.

briar-skill-w-recast.basis: Recasting W makes Briar's next basic attack deal damage based on the target's missing health and heal her. To deal more damage, recast W after the enemy has lost health. If Briar is in danger, recast W immediately to heal.
briar-skill-w-recast.text: Recasting W (Snack Attack) empowers Briar’s next basic attack to deal damage based on the target’s missing health and heal her for that amount. Wait until the enemy has lost health to get more value from it, but if Briar is in danger and needs the healing, use it immediately instead of waiting for a finishing blow.

briar-teamfight.basis: Choose an R prey that your allies can immediately attack with you. Enter teamfights after your allies land their first crowd control. If things go badly during Blood Frenzy, use E to end it and regain control.
briar-teamfight.text: Briar chases one target relentlessly, so choose an R target your allies can attack alongside you right away. Landing alone in the enemy backline leaves her surrounded when the fear ends; enter after an ally lands the first crowd control, and if the fight turns bad during Blood Frenzy, use E to end it and regain control—her only way to retreat.

caitlyn-combo-e-headshot.basis: Headshot range increases against targets hit by E. After landing E, use Headshot, place W where the enemy will retreat, then use Q. Use E to create Headshot opportunities.
caitlyn-combo-e-headshot.text: Landing E increases Headshot range against that target. Follow up with a Headshot, place W where they will retreat, then use Q; treat E as a way to set up Headshot, not as a way to hold the enemy in place.

caitlyn-combo-e-reposition.basis: Use E's recoil movement to create distance. Use E's recoil movement to escape over walls.
caitlyn-combo-e-reposition.text: Fire E away from the enemy to propel Caitlyn backward. Use that recoil to create distance or escape over a wall.

caitlyn-combo-trap-q.basis: Place W under enemies or where they will retreat. When an enemy triggers W, use Headshot, then Q. Headshot range increases greatly against enemies caught in a trap. Apply the rule that Q damage is not reduced against enemies caught in a trap. Use the moment right after a trap triggers to deal maximum damage.
caitlyn-combo-trap-q.text: Place W under the enemy or where they will retreat; when the trap triggers, follow with a Headshot and then Q. A trapped target is within Headshot range from much farther away and takes full Q damage, making the moment just after the trap triggers your best chance to deal maximum damage.

caitlyn-laning-push.basis: Caitlyn ranks among the best in CS and turret plating metrics. Use your range advantage to push the wave first and keep enemies pinned under their turret. Destroy turret plates while enemies are pinned under their turret. While the wave is pushed, place W at river approaches to defend against ganks.
caitlyn-laning-push.text: Caitlyn ranks among the best in CS and turret plating. Use her range advantage to push the wave first, pin the enemy under their turret, and break its plates. While the wave is pushed, place W at river approaches to guard against ganks.

caitlyn-laning-trade.basis: Only attempt trades when Headshot is ready. Poking with basic attacks without Headshot gives enemies an opening to close in. Back out of range immediately after trading to deny enemies an engage opportunity.
caitlyn-laning-trade.text: Trade only when Headshot is ready. Poking with basic attacks without it wastes your range advantage and gives the enemy an opening to close in; after a trade, immediately back out of their range to deny an engage.

caitlyn-phase-early.basis: Caitlyn's long range lets her pressure enemies from level 1, even without items. Caitlyn excels in the laning phase. Build an early lead through CS and turret pressure.
caitlyn-phase-early.text: Caitlyn's long range lets her pressure opponents from level 1, even without items. Laning is her strongest phase, so build an early lead through CS and turret pressure.

caitlyn-phase-late.basis: In the mid to late game, Caitlyn has less raw damage output than other marksmen with strong sustained damage. Caitlyn reaches her power peak when she converts her lane lead into turrets and objectives. After her power peak, use her range advantage to attack from a safe position.
caitlyn-phase-late.text: In the mid to late game, Caitlyn's raw damage falls behind that of other marksmen with strong sustained damage. Her power peaks when she converts a lane lead into turrets and objectives; afterward, use her range advantage to deal damage from a safe position.

caitlyn-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Caitlyn's range lets her attack throughout teamfights and continuously apply Executioner's Calling's healing reduction.
caitlyn-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Caitlyn's range lets her keep attacking throughout teamfights and maintain its healing reduction.

caitlyn-skill-e-keep.basis: E is Caitlyn's only escape ability. Using E to poke first leaves you without a way to respond to an enemy engage. Save E until you confirm the enemy has used their engage ability.
caitlyn-skill-e-keep.text: E is Caitlyn's only escape. Using it to poke leaves you unable to respond to an enemy engage, so save it until you have confirmed that the enemy has used their engage ability.

caitlyn-skill-passive.basis: Headshot activates after a set number of basic attacks. Basic attacks from brush charge Headshot faster. Use the Headshot charged while moving in and out of lane brush on champions. Avoid attacking minions when Headshot is fully charged.
caitlyn-skill-passive.text: Headshot activates after a set number of basic attacks and charges faster when you attack from brush. Move in and out of lane brush to charge it, then use it on a champion; avoid hitting minions once it is ready.

caitlyn-skill-q.basis: Q deals reduced damage to targets after the first. Caitlyn stays in place while aiming Q. Do not fire Q at a champion behind minions. Use Q as soon as the enemy steps away from the minions. Use Q the moment your opponent is caught in a trap.
caitlyn-skill-q.text: Q deals reduced damage to targets beyond the first and leaves Caitlyn stationary while she aims. Firing it at a champion behind minions wastes damage, so use it only when the enemy steps clear of the minions or is caught in a trap.

caitlyn-skill-r.basis: Another enemy champion can take the hit from R instead of its target. Avoid using R in chaotic fights. Use R to finish off a fleeing target, a duel opponent, or an enemy in another lane only when no champion can block its path. Caitlyn stands still while casting R.
caitlyn-skill-r.text: Another enemy champion can intercept R, so avoid using it in chaotic fights. Use it to finish a fleeing target, a duel opponent, or an enemy in another lane only when no one can block its path; Caitlyn remains stationary while casting.

caitlyn-skill-w.basis: W stores multiple trap charges. Place W in advance so its cooldown finishes during the fight. Place W where enemies must pass, such as brush entrances, jungle entrances, or behind you.
caitlyn-skill-w.text: W can store multiple charges, so place traps before a fight to have its cooldown ready when the fight starts. Put them where enemies must pass, such as brush entrances, jungle approaches, or behind you.
