caitlyn-teamfight.basis: Attack from the edge of your maximum range in teamfights. Place W along enemy approach routes and around your feet to block their approach. Secure your position before the teamfight starts. In teamfights, save E exclusively for interrupting enemy engages.
caitlyn-teamfight.text: In teamfights, attack from the edge of Caitlyn's maximum range and place W along enemy approach routes and around your feet to stop opponents from closing in. With no mobility ability, secure your position before the fight starts and save E solely to interrupt an engage.

camille-combo-engage.basis: Engage with E to a wall → W while moving → recast E to collide → auto attack → first Q → second Q. Camille can cast W while traveling on E’s hook. Time W’s windup to end as E’s leap finishes so you slow a distant enemy. Start a fight with an auto attack on an enemy champion to activate your passive shield.
camille-combo-engage.text: Engage by using E to reach a wall → cast W while traveling on the hook → recast E for the collision stun → auto attack → first Q → second Q. Camille can cast W during the hook’s travel, so time its windup to finish as the leap ends and slow enemies even far from the wall. Open the fight with an auto attack on an enemy champion to activate your passive shield.

camille-combo-trade.basis: Trade in lane with an auto attack → first Q → wait → second Q. Waiting before recasting Q increases its bonus damage and converts part of the damage to true damage. If there’s no rush, weave another auto attack between Q casts to buy time. Hit with W’s outer edge during trades to slow the enemy and heal yourself.
camille-combo-trade.text: In lane, trade with an auto attack → first Q → wait → second Q. Delaying the recast greatly increases Q’s bonus damage and converts part of it to true damage, so weave in another auto attack between casts when you have time. Catch the enemy with W’s outer edge as well to slow them and heal yourself.

camille-combo-ult.basis: For a guaranteed kill, use W’s outer edge → R → auto attack → first Q → auto attack → second Q. To make up for R’s short range, lock the enemy down first with E’s stun or W’s slow. While casting R, use its untargetability to ignore enemy crowd control and close in.
camille-combo-ult.text: For a guaranteed kill, slow the enemy with W’s outer edge → trap them with R → auto attack → first Q → auto attack → second Q. R has a short cast range, so first hold the enemy in place with E’s stun or W’s slow. Camille is untargetable during R’s cast, letting her ignore enemy crowd control and close in.

camille-item-vs-magic.basis: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, build magic resistance to pair with the magic shield. Against magic damage opponents, choose Ionian Boots of Lucidity for ability haste. If burst damage is the problem, choose Banshee’s Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team with long chains of crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash first.
camille-item-vs-magic.text: If the opponent’s main damage is magic, Camille’s shield will be magic, making it efficient to build magic resistance alongside it. Choose Ionian Boots of Lucidity for ability haste; if burst is the problem, use Banshee’s Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team with long crowd control chains, buy Quicksilver Sash first.

camille-item-vs-physical.basis: If the enemy’s main damage is physical, her passive shield will be physical. Against physical damage opponents, buy Plated Steelcaps early to pair armor with the shield. To strengthen side-lane 1v1s against physical damage opponents, follow up with Dead Man’s Plate or Randuin’s Omen.
camille-item-vs-physical.text: If the opponent’s main damage is physical, Camille’s passive shield will be physical, complementing armor items. Buy Plated Steelcaps early, then build Dead Man’s Plate or Randuin’s Omen to gain a substantial advantage in side-lane 1v1s.

camille-laning.basis: Start lane by chipping away at the enemy with W’s outer edge. Save E while poking in lane. Lure the enemy near a wall to set up an E engage. If the enemy stands far from walls behind minions, farm instead of engaging. While E and your passive shield are on cooldown, avoid trades and preserve your health. Camille farms slowly. Focus on CS and wait for a chance to join your jungler instead of forcing an early engage.
camille-laning.text: Start lane by chipping away with W’s outer edge while saving E. Lure the enemy toward a wall for an engage, but farm if they stand behind minions and far from walls. E and your passive shield have long cooldowns, so avoid trades while they are unavailable and preserve your health. Camille farms slowly; focus on CS and wait for a chance to join your jungler instead of forcing an early engage.

camille-phase.basis: Camille is at her weakest during the first two levels. Start trading once you have Q and your passive shield available. After learning R, Camille gains control over jungle skirmishes and gank follow-ups. Camille is strongest in midgame with two core items. Late game, avoid trading head-on with ranged carries and force 1v1s in the side lane.
camille-phase.text: Camille’s low base stats and slow wave clear make her weakest at levels one and two. Start trading once Q and your passive shield are available; after learning R, you can take control of jungle skirmishes and follow up on ganks. Her strongest point is midgame with two core items. Late game, avoid a head-on fight with ranged carries and force 1v1s in the side lane instead.

camille-skill-e.basis: E’s movement requires the hook to latch onto a wall. Firing E’s hook is not movement, so Camille can use it while rooted. When E pulls Camille to a wall, it shows the direction of nearby enemies. E’s leap gains range when aimed toward a visible enemy champion. E’s leap stops at the first enemy it hits, so adjust your approach if another enemy is in front of your target. Camille relies on E to engage. Choose your target before using E.
camille-skill-e.text: E needs a wall for its hook to latch onto, though firing the hook does not count as movement and remains available while Camille is rooted. When she reaches the wall, E reveals the direction of nearby enemies, helping her spot a brush ambush. The leap gains range toward a visible enemy champion but stops at the first enemy it hits, so change your angle if someone stands in front of your target. Since Camille relies on E to engage, choose whom to catch before using it.

camille-skill-passive.basis: Camille’s passive shield activates only when a basic attack hits an enemy champion. Her passive creates either a physical or magic shield based on the enemy’s damage type. Basic attacks against minions do not activate her passive shield. Start a fight with an auto attack before using abilities to gain the passive shield. Camille relies on her passive shield for defense.
camille-skill-passive.text: Camille’s passive shield activates only when she lands a basic attack on an enemy champion, granting either a physical or magic shield based on that enemy’s damage type. Hitting a minion will not trigger it, so open a fight with an auto attack to gain the shield before using abilities and committing. Because Camille gains little health as she levels, the shield effectively serves as a defensive stat.

camille-skill-q.basis: Q acts as an on-hit ability that empowers your next basic attack. Both Q attacks can trigger Spellblade effects, such as Trinity Force, for two procs. The second Q converts part of its damage to true damage, bypassing enemy armor. Chain E’s stun, W’s slow, or allied crowd control to land both Q attacks. Basic attack negation, blinds, and dodges can block Q, so use it after those counters are spent.
camille-skill-q.text: Q is an on-hit ability that empowers Camille’s next basic attack, allowing both casts to trigger Spellblade effects such as Trinity Force. Its second hit converts part of the damage to true damage, bypassing armor. To land both hits, hold the enemy in place with E’s stun, W’s slow, or allied crowd control; because Q rides on basic attacks, wait until any attack negation, blind, or dodge has been used before committing it.

camille-skill-w.basis: W deals bonus damage only with its outer edge. W slows only with its outer edge. Hitting with W’s outer edge heals Camille. Camille relies on W’s outer edge for lane sustain and engage opportunities. Account for W’s windup: step back before casting so the enemy is caught by its outer edge.
camille-skill-w.text: W gets its value from the outer edge of its cone: only that portion deals bonus damage, slows the enemy, and heals Camille, providing her lane sustain and engage opportunities. Its windup can leave a nearby enemy inside the cone’s inner area, so step back before casting to catch them with the outer edge.

camille-teamfight.basis: R traps one target inside its area. When R’s area appears, it knocks back enemies other than the target. Get onto the enemy’s main damage dealer and trap them with R to give your team time to kill them. Time your teamfight engage with your allies’ engage. If the teamfight setup is bad, push a side-lane turret to draw enemies out.
camille-teamfight.text: In teamfights, use R to isolate one target. Trap the enemy’s main damage dealer to keep them from escaping while your team finishes them off; when R’s area appears, it knocks other enemies back and effectively forces a 1v1. Enter with your allies, since going in alone can leave you dead after catching just one target. If the teamfight setup is poor, push a side-lane turret to draw enemies out.

cass-combo-allin.basis: For a guaranteed combo, stun with R, land Q, then repeatedly use E. Use E on a poisoned target whenever it comes off cooldown to maximize damage.
cass-combo-allin.text: The guaranteed combo is R → Q → repeated E: stun the target with R, place Q's poison where they stand so it takes full effect while they cannot move, then use E on the poisoned target whenever it comes off cooldown for maximum damage. You can get the same result by placing Q's poison first and casting R as the opponent rushes onto it.

cass-combo-poke.basis: For basic poke, land Q, then use E. When Q hits a champion, Cassiopeia gains a large movement speed boost. After landing Q, use the movement speed to stay within E range and follow the target. If Q misses, do not walk forward to trade.
cass-combo-poke.text: The basic poke combo is Q → E. Hitting a champion with Q gives Cassiopeia a large movement speed boost, letting her follow while staying in E range. Q is both her damage ability and her only way to gain mobility, so walking forward to trade after missing it does not work.

cass-laning-farm.basis: In lane, apply poison with Q, then last-hit with E. Early on, stand behind minions to avoid giving the opponent an angle to poke with basic attacks.
cass-laning-farm.text: In lane, apply poison with Q and last-hit with E. E refunds mana when it kills a target, so following this sequence keeps your mana up; otherwise, you will run out before level 6. Cassiopeia has some of the lowest early armor among champions and is especially vulnerable to basic attack poke, so stand behind minions and avoid giving your opponent an angle to attack.

cass-laning-wave.basis: To keep enough mana for W in case of a gank, do not use Q to push the entire wave. If you do not need lane priority, keep the wave in the middle and clear it with E last-hits. Do not push the lane forward while the enemy jungler's location is unknown.
cass-laning-wave.text: Using Q to push an entire wave can leave you without enough mana for W when a gank comes. Unless you need lane priority, keep the wave in the middle and clear it with E last-hits; do not push forward while the enemy jungler’s location is unknown.

cass-phase.basis: Cassiopeia is weakest at levels 1–2 because trading with only one ability is difficult. From mid game, once E has been leveled up and Cassiopeia has mana items, her sustained damage rises sharply. Late game, Cassiopeia has some of the highest teamfight damage as long as she is not caught. Early on, focus on scaling rather than fighting.
cass-phase.text: Cassiopeia is weakest at levels 1–2: her armor is among the lowest in the game, and one ability is not enough to trade damage. Her sustained damage rises sharply from mid game once E has been leveled and she has mana items; late game, she has some of the highest teamfight damage as long as she is not caught. Her 14-minute CS ranks highly while her damage ranks low, so focus on scaling early and look to deal damage later.

cass-situational-mercurial.basis: If the enemy's finishing blow comes from a magic damage composition that starts with a long stun, use Quicksilver Sash to remove the stun. Every moment Cassiopeia spends under crowd control is time she cannot deal damage.
cass-situational-mercurial.text: If the enemy’s finishing blow comes from a magic damage composition that opens with a long stun, buy Quicksilver Sash to remove that stun. Every moment Cassiopeia spends under crowd control costs her damage time, so the cleanse itself is the goal rather than the magic resistance.

cass-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier, between your core items. Cassiopeia has no mobility ability, so getting caught is dangerous, but if she survives briefly, her sustained E damage can turn the fight around.
cass-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy team has an assassin, move Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in your build, between core items. Cassiopeia has no mobility ability and can die once caught, but surviving briefly lets her sustained E damage turn the fight around.

cass-skill-e.basis: E deals bonus damage and heals Cassiopeia only when used on a poisoned target. To save mana, poison the target before using E. Keep using E while Q's poison lasts. Last-hitting with E refunds mana.
cass-skill-e.text: E deals bonus damage and heals Cassiopeia only against a poisoned target, so poison first instead of spending mana on an unpoisoned one. Its cooldown is very short: keep casting it while Q’s poison lasts, and last-hit with E to refund mana and manage your resources as you farm.

cass-skill-e-stationary.basis: Use E repeatedly on a target that cannot move. Right after stunning with R, save your other abilities and use E repeatedly.
cass-skill-e-stationary.text: E is most valuable when you can use it repeatedly on a target that cannot move. While killing a monster or immediately after stunning an opponent with R, save your other abilities and keep using E until the target can leave.

cass-skill-q.basis: Q detonates at the targeted spot after a short delay. Aim Q ahead of where the opponent is walking, rather than where they are standing. If the hit is uncertain, place Q ahead of time on the opponent's path or where they will step up to last-hit.
cass-skill-q.text: Q detonates at the targeted spot after a short delay, so aim ahead of where the opponent is walking rather than where they stand. The goal is to apply poison, not deal immediate damage; if a hit is uncertain, place Q early on a path they must cross or where they will step up to last-hit.

cass-skill-r.basis: R stuns only enemies facing Cassiopeia. Cassiopeia’s R only slows enemies facing away from her. Use R when the opponent charges straight at you. Do not use R on a fleeing opponent's back or from an angle after moving behind them.
cass-skill-r.text: R stuns enemies facing Cassiopeia but only slows those facing away. Cast it into an opponent charging straight at you; using it on a fleeing opponent’s back spends its long cooldown on a slow, and moving behind an opponent to cast it is disadvantageous for the same reason.

cass-skill-w.basis: Enemies inside W's poison cloud cannot use movement abilities. Place W under an opponent who has dashed in to stop their movement. W has a long cooldown, so do not waste it on poke.
cass-skill-w.text: Use W to control space, not for its damage. Enemies inside its poison cloud cannot use movement abilities, so placing it beneath an opponent who has dashed in stops them from advancing or escaping. Its long cooldown leaves you open to the next engage if you misuse it, so do not waste it on poke.

cass-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, do not engage yourself; stand behind your frontline. From behind your frontline, apply poison with Q, then keep using E on the poisoned target. Use W on the path enemies take toward your backline or under an enemy who has already dived in. Save R for the moment several enemies charge straight at you.
cass-teamfight.text: Cassiopeia does not initiate fights. Stay behind your frontline, apply poison with Q, and keep casting E on poisoned targets for sustained damage. Use W on the route enemies take toward your backline or under an enemy who has already dived in, and save R for the moment several enemies charge at you head-on.

chogath-combo-basic.basis: Activate E in advance, close in with a basic attack, knock them up with Q, silence them with W, then land the remaining E empowered attacks. Activating E has no cast time. If Q misses, back off.
chogath-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, activate E before closing in with a basic attack, knock the target up with Q, silence them with W while they are airborne, then land the remaining E empowered attacks. E has no cast time, so turn it on before engaging; if Q misses, back off.

chogath-combo-q-timing.basis: Q shows a warning at the target location before it activates, so opponents can walk out of it. Place Q as the opponent steps forward to last hit with a basic attack. Place Q right after an ally's crowd control lands. Silence the opponent with W to lock out their mobility ability, then place Q.
chogath-combo-q-timing.text: Q warns enemies at the target location before it activates, so they can walk out of a careless cast. Place it as an opponent steps forward to last hit with a basic attack, immediately after an ally lands crowd control, or after W silences them and locks out their mobility ability.

chogath-laning-antigank.basis: Cho'Gath has no mobility ability, making him vulnerable to ganks. When a gank comes, place Q as the enemies close in and commit to a direction. To turn a gank around, place Q in the opponent's path, then use W to lock out their pursuit ability. Pull the wave toward you and draw in the enemy jungler.
chogath-laning-antigank.text: Cho'Gath has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to ganks, but Q and W can turn one around. When a gank comes, do not place Q ahead of time in your escape direction; wait until the enemies close in and commit to a direction, then place Q and use W to lock out their pursuit ability. Pulling the wave toward you and drawing in the enemy jungler suits this approach especially well.

chogath-laning-ranged.basis: Q is your only way to start a trade against a ranged opponent. Against ranged opponents, use E's spikes through minions to clear the wave and stay in lane. Call for a jungle gank when the opponent has pushed the wave. After level 6, look for a kill when the opponent forgets about your increased Feast range.
chogath-laning-ranged.text: Against ranged opponents, Q is your only way to start a trade, so do not force one. Clear minions with E's piercing spikes to stay in lane, and call for a jungle gank when the opponent pushes the wave. After level 6, watch for a chance to execute them when they forget that Feast stacks have extended your R range.

chogath-phase.basis: Cho'Gath is vulnerable at levels 1–2 because he lacks mana and abilities. You can start trading at level 3, once you have Q and W. Learning R at level 6 opens up chances to get kills and build Feast stacks. Cho'Gath relies on Feast stacks for durability in the late game.
chogath-phase.text: Cho'Gath is vulnerable at levels 1–2 because he lacks mana and abilities. Trades become viable at level 3 once he has Q and W, while R at level 6 creates opportunities for kills and Feast stacks. His base stat growth is low enough that his maximum health at level 18 ranks among the lowest, and Feast stacks make up the difference; without them, he remains an ordinary melee champion even late in the game.

chogath-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent survives through healing, choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Dealing damage consistently with Q and E can keep healing reduction active throughout a fight.
chogath-situational-antiheal.text: If an opponent survives through healing, build Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Cho'Gath can keep dealing damage with Q and E, maintaining the effect throughout a fight once it is applied.

chogath-skill-e.basis: E adds spikes to the next three basic attacks. E's spikes pierce enemies in a straight line ahead and slow them. E deals damage based on the opponent's maximum health, making it strong against frontliners who build health. E's maximum health damage increases with Feast stacks. Against monsters, E's maximum health damage is replaced by a fixed amount.
chogath-skill-e.text: E adds spikes to the next three basic attacks, piercing every enemy in a straight line ahead and slowing them. Its damage scales with the target's maximum health, making it especially strong against frontliners who build health, and that damage grows with Feast stacks. Against monsters, a fixed damage value applies instead, so E also helps clear jungle camps.

chogath-skill-passive.basis: Carnivore restores health and mana whenever you kill a unit. Carnivore restores more health and mana as you level up. Last hit consistently to sustain in lane with Carnivore. When your health is uncertain, heal by killing minions instead of forcing a trade.
chogath-skill-passive.text: Carnivore restores health and mana whenever you kill a unit, with the amount increasing as you level up. Cho'Gath struggles with mana early, so securing each last hit helps sustain you in lane. When your health is low enough to make a trade uncertain, secure minion kills to heal instead of forcing one.

chogath-skill-r-execute.basis: R's true damage ignores the opponent's armor and magic resistance. Even against a tanky opponent, lower their health enough before finishing them with R. If the kill is uncertain, save R so you do not lose a chance to grow and a way to finish the target.
chogath-skill-r-execute.text: R deals true damage, ignoring armor and magic resistance. Even a tanky opponent is a guaranteed kill once their health is low enough, making R especially valuable against tanks that are hard to finish. If the kill is uncertain, save it: its long cooldown costs you both a chance to grow and a way to finish the target.

chogath-skill-r-stacks.basis: Killing a target with R grants a Feast stack. Feast stacks increase Cho'Gath's maximum health and size. Feast stacks increase Cho'Gath's attack range and Feast range. There is a cap on Feast stacks gained from minions and normal jungle monsters. During the laning phase, reach the cap on Feast stacks from minions and normal jungle monsters. To gain Feast stacks beyond that cap, kill champions or epic monsters.
chogath-skill-r-stacks.text: Killing a target with R grants a Feast stack, increasing Cho'Gath's maximum health, size, attack range, and Feast range. Stacks from minions and normal jungle monsters have a cap; reach it during the laning phase. Beyond that cap, only champion and epic monster kills grant stacks.

chogath-skill-w.basis: W silences enemies in a cone. Use W just before a skill reliant assassin or mage casts a key ability. W costs the most mana of Cho'Gath's abilities. Early on, avoid using W too often so you have enough mana to stay in lane.
chogath-skill-w.text: W silences enemies in a cone, briefly shutting down assassins and mages who rely on abilities. Save it for just before they cast a key ability instead of using it automatically during a trade. It costs more mana than Cho'Gath's other abilities, so using it too often early can leave you unable to stay in lane.

chogath-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stand in front of your allies. Place Q in the opponent's path to slow their engage. Silence the enemy initiator with W just as they are about to use an ability. Because you cannot use a mobility ability to return, do not stray too far ahead of your frontline in teamfights.
chogath-teamfight.text: Cho'Gath should stand in front of his allies rather than dive into the backline. Place Q along the enemy's approach to delay their engage, then silence their initiator with W just as they are about to use an ability. With no mobility ability to get back after moving forward, stay no more than a step ahead of your frontline.

chogath-teamfight-ult.basis: In teamfights, use R on a low health enemy carry. A kill with R during a teamfight immediately increases your maximum health through a Feast stack. If R will secure the kill, finish the target yourself to gain a stack for the next fight.
chogath-teamfight-ult.text: In teamfights, use R on a low health enemy carry. A kill immediately grants a Feast stack and increases Cho'Gath's maximum health, making him tougher as the fight continues. When the kill is certain, finish the target yourself instead of leaving it to an ally and saving R; the stack also benefits you in later fights.

corki-combo-allin.basis: When going all in, enter with W, activate E, land an auto attack, then finish with R. Corki can move and auto attack while firing E. Reducing armor and magic resistance with E increases the damage of your following auto attacks and R.
corki-combo-allin.text: For an all-in, jump in with W to leave a trail of fire, activate E and keep auto attacking, then finish with R. Corki can move and auto attack while E fires, and its armor and magic resistance reduction makes the following attacks and R hit harder.

corki-combo-bigone.basis: Every third R shot deals heavy damage. Count your R charges and time the third shot to finish the target. Before a fight where you need the big missile, do not use the first two shots to clear the wave.
corki-combo-bigone.text: Every third R shot deals heavy damage, so count your shots and time the big missile to finish your target. If you spend the first two clearing a wave, the big one may not be ready when you need it.

corki-combo-poke.basis: When poking, land Q before firing R. Q reveals the area it hits and any champions there for a while. Repeatedly poke with Q and R at max range.
corki-combo-poke.text: For poke, fire Q before R: Q briefly reveals the area and champions it hits, making the follow-up R much easier to land. Repeating this from maximum range steadily wears down the enemy’s health.

corki-laning.basis: In lane, build small advantages by poking with Q and R. Corki is vulnerable to ganks. When you lack vision, do not push the wave toward the enemy turret. Save W to escape during the laning phase.
corki-laning.text: In lane, build small advantages with your range and Q and R poke. Corki’s very low movement speed makes him especially vulnerable to ganks, so avoid pushing toward the enemy turret without vision and keep W available to escape.

corki-objective.basis: In objective fights, deal damage with R from beyond a wall or outside enemy vision. Reveal the enemy team with Q, then fire R.
corki-objective.text: In objective fights, R lets Corki deal damage safely from beyond a wall or outside enemy vision. There’s no need to move into vision to find a position: reveal the enemy team with Q, then fire R to cut down the time they can spend attacking the objective.

corki-phase.basis: Corki is very weak at levels 1–5. At level 6, R and your first core item give you strong poke. Corki is strongest in the mid to late game with two or three items. Get through the weak early game without falling behind.
corki-phase.text: Corki’s low base stats make him very weak at levels 1–5. His level 6 R and first core item give him strong poke, and he peaks in the mid to late game with two or three items. Focus on getting through the early levels without falling behind.

corki-skill-e.basis: E reduces enemies' armor and magic resistance in a cone. The defenses reduced by E also affect your allies' damage. In teamfights, aim E at the target your allies are actually attacking. Corki can move and auto attack while firing E.
corki-skill-e.text: E reduces armor and magic resistance in a cone, increasing your allies’ damage as well as your own. In teamfights, aim it at the target your allies are attacking rather than the tank directly in front of you, and keep your position while moving and auto attacking as it fires.

corki-skill-passive.basis: Corki's passive converts part of his auto attack damage to true damage. The passive's true damage conversion also applies to Spellblade effects. Weave in auto attacks even against enemies with high armor. As of the 26.17 tooltip, Corki's passive does not include the Package. Do not count on the Package as a way to engage.
corki-skill-passive.text: Corki’s passive converts part of his auto attack damage to true damage, including damage from Spellblade effects. Weave in auto attacks even against heavily armored enemies instead of relying only on abilities. As of the 26.17 tooltip, the passive provides only this conversion, so do not plan an engage around the Package (Special Delivery) described in older guides.

corki-skill-q.basis: Throw Q into bushes or unwarded paths to check for an ambush. Hit a fleeing enemy with Q to reveal their position. Use Q to check the enemy jungler's position before an objective.
corki-skill-q.text: Q is especially valuable for the vision it provides: throw it into bushes or unwarded paths to check for ambushes, or hit a fleeing enemy to reveal their position so your allies can catch up. Use it to locate the enemy jungler before an objective, too.

corki-skill-r.basis: R stops gaining charges when it is full. Do not use every R charge and leave yourself without missiles for a fight. Landing an auto attack on a champion reduces R's charge time. Weave in auto attacks while poking to recharge missiles sooner.
corki-skill-r.text: R stops gaining charges when full, so leaving it capped wastes potential charges; emptying it completely leaves you without missiles for a fight. Auto attacking a champion reduces its charge time, so weave attacks into your poke to get missiles back sooner.

corki-skill-w.basis: W is Corki's only mobility ability. W can cross terrain. Corki has trouble escaping when W is down. Use W to enter only after the enemy's engage ability is down.
corki-skill-w.text: W is Corki’s only mobility ability and his only way to cross terrain. His movement speed is very low, so once W is down, he has virtually no way to escape. Don’t spend it to engage early; use it only after the enemy has used all its engage abilities, or save it for an escape.

corki-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, fire R from the back. Use E on the target your allies are attacking. Enter with W only after the enemy's engage abilities and targeted crowd control are both down. Corki has trouble escaping once caught.
corki-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay back and fire R while using E to reduce the defenses of the target your allies are attacking. Enter with W only after all enemy engage abilities and targeted crowd control have been used; Corki’s low movement speed makes escape difficult once he is caught.

darius-combo-basic.basis: The basic trade combo is E → auto attack → W → Q. Landing E guarantees an auto attack and W. Use W's auto attack reset to quickly reach three Hemorrhage stacks. Finish the combo with Q, taking half a step back to land the blade.
darius-combo-basic.text: The basic trade combo is E Apprehend → auto attack → W Crippling Strike → Q Decimate. Pulling an enemy into melee range guarantees the auto attack and W; W resets the auto attack timer, letting you build three Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Finish with Q, taking half a step back to land the blade.

darius-combo-execute.basis: The execution combo is E → auto attack → auto attack → W → Q → auto attack → R. R damage scales with the target's Hemorrhage stacks. Use R after reaching maximum Hemorrhage stacks. E's slow keeps the enemy in range while you add auto attacks.
darius-combo-execute.text: The execution combo is E Apprehend → auto attack → auto attack → W Crippling Strike → Q Decimate → auto attack → R Noxian Guillotine. The extra auto attack matters because R’s damage scales with the target’s Hemorrhage stacks; using R before reaching maximum stacks can let a kill escape. E’s slow keeps the enemy in range while you add those attacks.

darius-laning.basis: Freeze the wave on your side to lure the enemy into E range when they go for minions. Land E from brush or in narrow terrain to follow up with your combo. After pushing the wave, secure vision against ganks before moving forward.
darius-laning.text: Laning is about keeping the enemy within E Apprehend range. Freeze the wave on your side so they must step forward for minions, then land E from brush or narrow terrain to secure your combo. Darius has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to ganks, so establish vision before moving forward after pushing the wave.

darius-phase.basis: Darius is weak at levels 1–2, when he has few abilities available. Darius gets stronger at level 3 with W and Q available, and at level 6 when he gains R. Darius has low item dependence and stays strong through the mid game. Darius is vulnerable in prolonged wars of attrition against ranged poke opponents. Darius falls off in standard late-game teamfights where he struggles to engage. Use your lane advantage during your strong periods to secure gains.
darius-phase.text: Darius is weak at levels 1–2 while he has few abilities, but gains strength at level 3 with both W and Q available and again at level 6 when he gets R. He depends little on items and stays strong through the mid game, though his lack of mobility and sustain leaves him vulnerable to prolonged attrition against ranged poke. Engaging becomes difficult in standard late game teamfights, so turn your lane advantage into gains during his strong periods.

darius-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing turns fights around, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Darius relies on extended brawls and can easily lose his edge against sustained enemy healing.
darius-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing can turn a fight around, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Darius wins through extended brawls, where sustained enemy healing can reverse the outcome.

darius-situational-armor.basis: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy deals mostly physical damage. If the enemy deals mostly physical damage, choose Dead Man's Plate or Randuin's Omen for armor and slows that help you chase.
darius-situational-armor.text: If the enemy deals mostly physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps early, then add Dead Man’s Plate or Randuin’s Omen. Both provide armor and slow enemies while you stay close, helping Darius keep up despite his lack of mobility.

darius-situational-magic.basis: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Mercury's Treads to reduce the time you spend immobilized. If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Force of Nature after Mercury's Treads. Roots and stuns can easily disrupt Darius's combo. Prioritize tenacity over magic resistance when roots or stuns interrupt your combo.
darius-situational-magic.text: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Mercury’s Treads to shorten immobilization, then build Force of Nature. A single root or stun can ruin Darius’s entire combo because he has no mobility ability, so prioritize tenacity over magic resistance.

darius-skill-e.basis: Use E right after the enemy uses their mobility ability. You cannot use Flash during E's cast. For a surprise engage, use Flash before E. E's passive grants armor penetration. Give lower priority to penetration-focused items whose effects overlap with E's armor penetration.
darius-skill-e.text: If the enemy has a mobility ability, use E Apprehend right after they spend it: a dash can easily dodge an early E, while pulling them back as they try to escape lets you land the full combo. Flash does not work during E’s cast, so use Flash before E for a surprise engage. E’s passive already grants armor penetration, lowering the priority of penetration focused items with overlapping effects.

darius-skill-passive.basis: Hemorrhage stacks up to five times. Reaching maximum Hemorrhage stacks greatly increases attack damage. Alternate auto attacks and abilities to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Darius grows stronger as fights drag on and he builds Hemorrhage stacks. Back off from fights that started with no Hemorrhage stacks.
darius-skill-passive.text: Hemorrhage stacks up to five times, and reaching maximum stacks greatly increases Darius’s attack damage. His damage is ordinary before then, so alternate auto attacks and abilities to build stacks as quickly as possible. He grows stronger the longer a fight lasts, making survival a way to deal more damage; back off from a fight you started with no Hemorrhage stacks.

darius-skill-q.basis: Q deals full damage only to enemies hit by the blade. Q's healing scales with the number of enemy champions and large monsters hit by the blade. In lane, step back as you use Q to hit the enemy champion with the blade. Using Flash during Q's cast moves the blade's hitbox.
darius-skill-q.text: Q Decimate deals full damage only with the blade, and its healing depends on how many enemy champions and large monsters the blade hits. Casting Q while pressed against a target hits with the handle, costing you both damage and healing. In lane, step back as you cast to catch the enemy champion with the blade; you can also use Flash during the cast to move the blade’s hitbox.

darius-skill-w.basis: W resets the auto attack timer. W applies a strong slow to the target. Use W immediately after an auto attack to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Slow fleeing enemies with W to keep them in Q and R range. Avoid spending W on minions so you don't miss out on Hemorrhage stacks on champions.
darius-skill-w.text: W Crippling Strike resets the auto attack timer and applies a strong slow. Use it immediately after an auto attack to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly, or slow a fleeing enemy to keep them in Q and R range. With no mobility ability, Darius also relies on this slow to escape a bad fight. Using W on a minion costs you a stack you could have applied to a champion.

darius-teamfight.basis: Darius struggles to reach backline damage dealers, putting him at a disadvantage in head-on teamfights. In narrow terrain, pull multiple enemies with E, then hit them together with Q's blade to heal. Getting a kill with R resets its cooldown. Start a kill chain by targeting enemies you can reliably finish with R. If you cannot make use of narrow terrain, apply pressure in a side lane through 1v1s.
darius-teamfight.text: Darius is at a disadvantage in head on teamfights: he struggles to reach backline damage dealers and can be focused down before he gets there. In narrow terrain, pull multiple enemies with E Apprehend and hit them together with Q Decimate’s blade to build up healing. A kill with R Noxian Guillotine resets its cooldown, so start the chain with a target you can reliably finish. Without that terrain, pressure a side lane through 1v1s instead.

diana-combo-allin.basis: For an all-in after level 6, use Q, E, W, an auto attack, R, then the remaining E. Activate W right after closing in with E. W's orbs only burst when they touch an enemy. R pulls enemies in, then deals damage after a short delay. To stack the damage with R, use R first, then land Q and an auto attack before its damage hits.
diana-combo-allin.text: After level 6, the all-in sequence is Q, E, W, an auto attack, R Moonfall, then the remaining E. Activate W immediately after closing in with E, since its orbs only burst when they touch an enemy. R pulls enemies in before dealing damage a short time later, so to overlap that damage with Q and an auto attack, use R first and land both before it hits.

diana-combo-basic.basis: In a basic trade, land Q, close in with E, auto attack, then activate W. Using E on a target marked by Moonlight immediately resets E's cooldown. Save the reset second E for an escape instead of using it right away.
diana-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, land Q Crescent Strike, close in with E Lunar Rush, auto attack, then activate W Pale Cascade. Using E on a target marked by Moonlight immediately resets its cooldown, so save the second E as a way out instead of using it right away.

diana-combo-r-engage.basis: When several enemies are grouped, enter with E, pull them together with R, then use Q and W. R deals more damage the more champions it pulls in. Don't start a fight with R when there is only one opponent.
diana-combo-r-engage.text: When several enemies are grouped, reverse the order: enter with E, pull them together with R, then use Q and W. R deals more damage for each champion it pulls in, so its timing differs when targeting one opponent versus several; opening with R against a lone opponent wastes it.

diana-jungle.basis: In the jungle, clear camps with W's orbs and the passive's area damage. When ganking, approach from an unwarded brush or behind the opponent to line up Q. If you enter with E during a gank without landing Q, you can't get back out.
diana-jungle.text: In the jungle, clear camps quickly with W's orbs and P Moonsilver Blade's area damage. For ganks, approach through unwarded brush or from behind to line up Q, since landing it resets E; entering with E after missing Q leaves you unable to get back out.

diana-laning.basis: In mid lane, farm with Q while waiting for level 6. Clear caster minions with W to push the wave. After pushing the lane, look for gank opportunities with your jungler. After level 6, an opponent who stays after getting hit by Q presents a kill opportunity.
diana-laning.text: In mid lane, respect Diana's melee range and farm with Q while waiting for level 6. Use W to clear caster minions and push the wave, then look for gank opportunities with your jungler. After level 6, an opponent who stays after being hit by Q presents a kill opportunity.

diana-phase.basis: Diana is weakest at levels 1–2, when she has melee range and no combo. At level 3, with Q, W, and E available, Diana can trade damage. Diana's first kill opportunity comes right after learning R at level 6. Diana is strongest in the mid game once she has at least two ability power items. In the late game, Diana's value depends on whether she can kill one target and get out alive.
diana-phase.text: Diana is weakest at levels 1–2, when she has melee range and no combo. With Q, W, and E available at level 3, she can trade damage, and learning R at level 6 creates her first kill opportunity. She peaks in the mid game with at least two ability power items; in the late game, her value depends on whether she can eliminate one target and escape alive.

diana-situational-cc.basis: Diana is vulnerable if she is caught by an unavoidable root as she enters. If the enemy has an unavoidable root, get Quicksilver Sash after one core item to remove the root right after you enter.
diana-situational-cc.text: If the enemy has a root that lands without aiming, Diana will be locked down the moment she goes in, unable to do anything before she dies. Buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item to break the root immediately after engaging.

diana-skill-e.basis: E's cooldown resets only when used on a target marked by Moonlight. If you enter with E without a mark, you lose your way back out. If you aren't confident you'll land Q, land it before using E. If the opponent still has crowd control available, land Q before using E.
diana-skill-e.text: E Lunar Rush resets its cooldown only when used on a target marked by Moonlight. Entering with E without a mark lets you dive in aggressively but leaves you no way back out. If you are unsure you can land Q, or the opponent still has crowd control available, land Q before using E.

diana-skill-passive.basis: Every set number of attacks, the passive also slashes nearby enemies for area damage. Right after using an ability, the passive briefly gives a large attack speed boost. Weave auto attacks between abilities to make use of the passive damage.
diana-skill-passive.text: P Moonsilver Blade deals area damage to nearby enemies every set number of attacks and briefly grants a large attack speed boost right after you use an ability. Leaving after casting abilities alone gives up much of that damage, so weave auto attacks between them.

diana-skill-q.basis: Q travels in a curve, so it catches opponents who try to dodge in a straight line. Diana's combo depends on landing Q. Q has a short cooldown and low mana cost, so keep trying even if it misses. A target hit by Q is briefly revealed.
diana-skill-q.text: Q Crescent Strike travels in a curve, making it effective against opponents who dodge in a straight line. Diana's entire combo starts with landing Q, but its short cooldown and low mana cost mean you should keep throwing it even if you miss. A target it hits is briefly revealed.

diana-skill-r.basis: R deals damage while pulling opponents toward Diana. Use R to catch fleeing opponents. Use R to stop an engaging champion who dives onto your allies. Don't use R if you can't withstand the opponents you pull in.
diana-skill-r.text: R Moonfall deals damage and pulls opponents toward Diana, disrupting their movement. Use it to catch fleeing enemies or stop a champion diving onto your allies, but avoid it when you cannot withstand the opponents it pulls in.

diana-skill-w.basis: W's orbs only burst when they touch an enemy. W's orbs last briefly and disappear if you activate W too far from an enemy. Bursting the last W orb grants another shield and extends its duration. Stay close to enemies and burst every W orb to increase damage and survivability.
diana-skill-w.text: W Pale Cascade's orbs only burst when they touch an enemy and last briefly, so activating W from too far away lets them disappear. Bursting the last orb grants another shield and extends its duration; stay close enough to use every orb for both damage and survivability.

diana-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, approach from the side and dive toward the enemy damage dealers. Enter after the enemy's key crowd control has been used. Enter after an ally engages and draws the enemy's attention. Use R when you can pull several enemies together. If you can't pull several enemies together, save the reset E, kill one damage dealer, then get out.
diana-teamfight.text: In teamfights, approach from the side toward the enemy damage dealers instead of entering head-on. Go in once the enemy's key crowd control has been used or an ally has engaged and drawn their attention. R is most valuable when it pulls several enemies together; if that opportunity is unavailable, save the reset E, eliminate one damage dealer, and get out.

draven-combo-juggle.basis: Activate Q, auto-attack, then move to the axe landing marker to catch it and land your next auto-attack. Keep two axes going so one is in the air while you catch the other. Keeping two axes going empowers every auto-attack.
draven-combo-juggle.text: Draven’s basic rotation is to activate Q, auto-attack, move to the bouncing axe’s landing marker, catch it, and attack again. He can hold two axes at once, so aim to have one in the air while catching the other; maintaining that rhythm empowers every auto-attack.

draven-combo-w.basis: Use W just before catching an axe. Catching an axe resets W's cooldown. Activate W before catching an axe to keep the movement speed boost going without interruption.
draven-combo-w.text: Use W just before catching an axe. The catch resets W’s cooldown, letting you refresh its movement speed boost immediately and keep it active without a gap; waiting until after the catch wastes that reset.

draven-laning.basis: Draven is strong at trading damage in lane while holding axes. Move alongside the enemy marksman and auto-attack when they hit a minion. Account for a gank from the enemy jungler when moving forward to catch an axe.
draven-laning.text: With axes in hand, Draven almost never loses a damage trade in lane. Move alongside the enemy marksman and auto-attack while they hit a minion, then catch the bouncing axe to gain an advantage without taking a return hit. This pressure is why his laning CS and turret plate numbers rank among the best. His movement speed is low, though, so always account for an enemy jungler's gank as you step forward to catch an axe.

draven-phase.basis: Draven is strongest during the laning phase. Later, safe spots to catch axes become scarce and enemies have more ways to engage, making him relatively weaker. Quickly turn your early gold lead into turrets and objectives.
draven-phase.text: Draven peaks in lane: his laning kills, CS, and turret plate numbers are all among the best, and he relies on the gold earned early to close out the game. As the game goes on, safe places to catch axes disappear and enemies have more ways to engage, making him relatively weaker. How quickly you turn an early lead into turrets and objectives determines the outcome.

draven-situational-cleanse.basis: If the enemy has several forms of immobilizing crowd control, take Cleanse instead of Barrier so you can catch axes. If Cleanse isn't enough for the matchup, buy Mercurial Scimitar between core items.
draven-situational-cleanse.text: If the enemy has several forms of immobilizing crowd control, take Cleanse instead of Barrier. Draven must keep moving to catch axes; getting locked down once can make him drop an axe and lose his damage. If a summoner spell cannot cover the matchup, fit Mercurial Scimitar between your core items.

draven-skill-passive.basis: Catching an axe, killing a minion or monster, or destroying a turret grants passive stacks. Killing a champion grants bonus gold based on your passive stacks. Dying costs you half your passive stacks. When you have many passive stacks, look for a reliable kill participation instead of forcing a solo fight.
draven-skill-passive.text: Catching an axe, killing a minion or monster, and destroying a turret build passive stacks; a champion kill converts those stacks into bonus gold proportional to their number. Death removes half your stacks, so when you have plenty, look for a reliable way to participate in a kill and cash them in instead of forcing a solo fight. Dying before cashing them in is the most common way Draven loses games.

draven-skill-q-control.basis: If you throw an axe too close to the target, it’s hard to control where it lands. Axes land in the direction Draven is moving. Your movement direction when you attack determines where you’ll stand to catch the next axe. Axes don’t bounce back when you hit a turret, so the axe rotation stops.
draven-skill-q-control.text: Throwing an axe at a target who is too close makes its landing spot hard to control. Axes land in the direction Draven is moving, so your movement as you attack determines where you will need to stand for the next catch. Axes do not bounce back from turrets, so account for the interruption to your axe rotation while taking one down.

draven-skill-q-uptime.basis: If you stop auto-attacking for a while, you drop all the axes you're holding. If you won't be fighting soon, don't activate Q early. If you expect a fight, activate Q before your first auto-attack.
draven-skill-q-uptime.text: Draven drops every axe he is holding if he goes too long without auto-attacking. If you will not fight within the next few seconds, leave Q off: it costs mana, and the axes will disappear anyway. When a fight is likely, activate Q before your first auto-attack so the opening hit is empowered.

draven-skill-r.basis: R travels out and then returns. R deals less damage each time it passes through a unit, but the damage reduction resets on its return. If you think your opponent will dodge R, recast it just before it reaches them. R's execute threshold scales with League of Draven stacks.
draven-skill-r.text: R travels out and returns. Its damage falls each time it passes through a unit, but that reduction resets on the return trip. If you think an opponent will dodge it, recast just before the axe reaches them so it turns back over them with its damage reset. The execute threshold scales with League of Draven stacks, making a heavily stacked Draven's R lethal to low-health opponents within range.

draven-skill-w-collision.basis: You can move through units during W's movement speed boost. Use W when you need to pass through minions to catch an axe. Early on, save mana for fights instead of using W repeatedly just to move.
draven-skill-w-collision.text: W's movement speed boost lets Draven pass through units. Getting blocked by minions on the way to an axe is the most common reason to drop one, so use W when you need to move through them. Early on, though, its mana cost is high; using it repeatedly just to move can leave you without W when a fight starts.

draven-teamfight.basis: Don't engage first in a teamfight. After your allies initiate and the enemies use their engage abilities, move in and secure space to catch axes. When space is tight, keep just one axe going and auto-attack from a safe position. Save E to interrupt enemies engaging on your allied damage dealers.
draven-teamfight.text: Never enter a teamfight first as Draven. Let your allies initiate and the enemy use their engage abilities before moving in, so you have room to catch axes. If space is tight, maintain just one axe and auto-attack from safety instead of trying to juggle two. Save E to interrupt enemies diving your allied damage dealers.

drmundo-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, slow them with Q, close in, activate W, and land an E-enhanced basic attack. W stores the most damage taken during the brief window right after activation. Activate W just before the enemy's combo hits.
drmundo-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, slow the enemy with Q, close in, activate W, then land an E-enhanced basic attack. W stores the most damage taken in the brief window immediately after activation, so use it just before the enemy’s combo hits.

drmundo-combo-e.basis: E empowers your next basic attack, so you need to get within basic attack range. E deals more damage the more health you are missing. A minion killed with E is knocked back and damages enemies in its path. To clear the wave and harass with E at the same time, line it up so the minion is knocked toward your opponent.
drmundo-combo-e.text: E empowers your next basic attack, so you must get within attack range. Its damage increases as your health falls, making a counterattack after taking damage especially strong. A minion killed with E is knocked back and damages enemies in its path; angle the attack toward your opponent when you want to clear the wave and harass them at the same time.

drmundo-combo-w-recast.basis: An enemy champion must be nearby when W explodes to fully restore the stored gray health. Reactivate W yourself when an enemy champion is within its explosion range. If the enemy is retreating, delay reactivating W slightly until they are within its explosion range.
drmundo-combo-w-recast.text: W fully restores its stored gray health only if an enemy champion is nearby when it explodes. Reactivate it yourself while the enemy is in the explosion range instead of letting it expire; if they are retreating, delay reactivation slightly to catch them in the blast.

drmundo-laning-ranged.basis: Against a ranged opponent, getting into Q range is itself a losing trade. Against a ranged opponent, farm from behind minions and use Q to heal. Look for a chance to close in on a ranged opponent when your jungler ganks or just after the opponent uses an ability on the wave.
drmundo-laning-ranged.text: Against a ranged opponent, even entering Q range is a losing trade. Farm from behind minions and use Q only for healing, then look to close in when your jungler ganks or just after the opponent uses an ability on the wave.

drmundo-laning-sustain.basis: Healing from Q hits, passive regeneration, and canister pickups lets you stay in lane for a long time. To stay in lane, use canister and Q healing first. Time your recall for after the wave pushes toward the enemy turret. The longer Dr. Mundo stays in lane, the more he scales.
drmundo-laning-sustain.text: Healing from Q hits, passive regeneration, and canister pickups lets Dr. Mundo stay in lane without leaving. Use canister and Q healing before spending potions, and recall after the wave has pushed toward the enemy turret. The time he spends holding his lane is itself part of his scaling.

drmundo-phase.basis: Dr. Mundo has virtually no early kill pressure. In lane, survive and collect minions. From the mid game, once you have level 6 R and your first core item, your one-on-one sustain rises sharply. In the late game, stacking health items also increases the attack damage E grants.
drmundo-phase.text: Dr. Mundo has virtually no early kill pressure, ranking among the lowest champions by early kill statistics. His low deaths and strong CS make surviving and farming the right approach in lane. His one-on-one sustain rises sharply from the mid game once he has level 6 R and his first core item, while health items in the late game also increase the attack damage E grants.

drmundo-situational-attackspeed.basis: If the enemy marksman relies on attack speed, buy Frozen Heart. Frozen Heart provides armor and slows nearby enemies' attack speed, buying time to reach the backline.
drmundo-situational-attackspeed.text: If the enemy marksman relies on attack speed, buy Frozen Heart. Its armor and reduction to nearby enemies’ attack speed buy Dr. Mundo time to walk into the backline.

drmundo-situational-mr.basis: Against a magic damage composition, buy Spirit Visage earlier. Spirit Visage increases magic resistance and healing received, working with the healing from Q, W, and R.
drmundo-situational-mr.text: Dr. Mundo has very low magic resistance early, leaving him vulnerable to magic damage compositions. Buy Spirit Visage earlier in those matchups: it raises both magic resistance and healing received, directly supporting the healing from Q, W, and R.

drmundo-skill-passive-bag.basis: The passive ignores the first immobilizing effect, but costs health and drops a canister nearby. Picking up the dropped canister restores health and reduces the passive's cooldown. If an enemy champion steps on the dropped canister, it breaks. When a canister drops, consider picking it up before continuing the trade.
drmundo-skill-passive-bag.text: Dr. Mundo’s passive ignores the first immobilizing effect at the cost of health and drops a canister nearby. Picking it up restores health and reduces the passive’s cooldown, while an enemy champion can destroy it by stepping on it. When a canister drops, picking it up before continuing the trade is often worthwhile.

drmundo-skill-passive-timing.basis: While the passive is available, you can ignore the enemy's first immobilizing effect and close in. Without the passive, immobilizing effects will stop you. If the enemy jungler is missing and your passive is down, do not push the lane forward.
drmundo-skill-passive-timing.text: Whether Dr. Mundo can take a fight depends on his passive. When it is available, he can ignore the enemy’s first immobilizing effect and close in; when it is down, that effect will stop him. If the enemy jungler is missing and your passive is down, do not push the lane forward.

drmundo-skill-q.basis: Q deals damage based on the target's current health, so it is strong against full-health targets but weak for finishing them off. Q hits only the first target, so minions can block it. Hitting a minion or monster with Q can also restore health. Before throwing Q, decide whether you want a kill opportunity or healing.
drmundo-skill-q.text: Q (Infected Bonesaw) deals damage based on the target’s current health, making it strong against full-health enemies but weak as a finishing blow. It hits only the first target, so minions can block it, though hitting a minion or monster can still provide healing. Decide whether you want a kill opportunity or healing before throwing it.

drmundo-skill-r.basis: R's immediate heal scales with missing health, so it is stronger when your health is low. As your ultimate gains ranks, R heals more based on the number of nearby enemy champions. To increase the healing, activate R when several enemies surround you instead of while running away. Do not rely only on R's immediate heal; account for its healing over time too.
drmundo-skill-r.text: R (Maximum Dosage) heals immediately based on missing health, making it more effective when Dr. Mundo is low. At higher ranks, it heals more for each nearby enemy champion, so activating it while surrounded by several enemies restores more health than using it while fleeing. Account for the healing over time as well; waiting for the immediate heal alone can get you killed.

drmundo-skill-r-engage.basis: R's movement speed boost helps you engage. After joining a teamfight with Teleport, activate R and walk into the enemy backline. Choose when to fight with the difficulty of reaching the enemy backline without R in mind.
drmundo-skill-r-engage.text: R’s movement speed boost helps Dr. Mundo engage: after joining a teamfight with Teleport, activate it and walk into the enemy backline. Because he has no dash, choose fights with the understanding that he cannot reach the backline while R is unavailable.

drmundo-teamfight.basis: Dr. Mundo is not a champion who starts teamfights. After enemies engage your allies, activate R and move in, slow an enemy damage dealer with Q, then hit them with E. If enemies attack Dr. Mundo, his healing makes them spend time on him.
drmundo-teamfight.text: Dr. Mundo does not start teamfights. Once enemies engage your allies, activate R and walk in, slow an enemy damage dealer with Q, then hit them with E. If the enemies ignore Dr. Mundo, their damage dealer dies; if they attack him, his healing wastes their time. Either way, your team benefits.

ekko-combo-e-cast.basis: You can use other abilities while dashing with E. You can throw Q while dashing with E. Place the W sphere, then use E to enter it quickly and set up a stun. Use E to extend the reach of other abilities.
ekko-combo-e-cast.text: You can cast other abilities during E’s dash: throw Q as you move, or use E to reach a placed W sphere quickly and set up a stun. This lets E extend the reach of your other abilities.

ekko-combo-fast.basis: For a quick damage combo, throw Q, then use E to close in as Q returns. If Q hits on the way out and back alongside an E-enhanced basic attack, the third P hit triggers immediately.
ekko-combo-fast.text: For the fastest damage combo, throw Q, then close in with E as Q returns. The outgoing and returning Q hits overlap with E’s empowered basic attack, immediately triggering the third P hit.

ekko-combo-full.basis: For a full combo, place W first, slow with Q, then go in with E to stun, use basic attacks, and use R if needed. W takes time to set up, so place it first in a full combo. If you use W after closing in, the enemy can escape while it sets up.
ekko-combo-full.text: For a full combo, place W ahead of the enemy’s path first, slow them with Q, then use E to enter the sphere and stun them. Follow with a basic attack and use R if needed. W takes time to set up, so casting it after you close in gives the enemy time to escape.

ekko-combo-r.basis: R returns you to where you were a few seconds ago. R deals area damage where you return. Before going in, deliberately set up a place to return to with R. Use R in the middle of a group of enemies to deal damage and get out.
ekko-combo-r.text: R returns you to where you were a few seconds ago and deals area damage there. Set up your return position deliberately before going in; using R from the middle of a group of enemies lets you deal damage and escape at the same time.

ekko-laning-gank.basis: When ganking, place W along the enemy's escape route first, slow them with Q, then go in with E. Time W to land as an ally's crowd control takes effect. Placing W where the enemy can see it makes them back away from the lane.
ekko-laning-gank.text: When ganking, place W behind the enemy along their escape route, slow them with Q, then go in with E. Time W to coincide with an ally’s crowd control so the enemy cannot dodge it even after seeing the signal; placing it in plain sight too early lets them back away from the lane.

ekko-laning-split.basis: Q's wave clear and E's damage to structures make Ekko strong at split pushing. His high mobility lets him escape enemies who come to catch him. If a teamfight is not an option, pressure a side lane to draw enemies out.
ekko-laning-split.text: Q’s wave clear and E’s damage to structures make Ekko a strong split pusher, while his mobility lets him escape enemies sent to catch him. If a teamfight is not an option, pressure a side lane to draw enemies out.

ekko-phase.basis: Jungle Ekko's early clear is not especially fast. Jungle Ekko has a high gank success rate thanks to W's stun. You can start fights often from level 6, when you learn R. You can start fights often later on, when your ability cooldowns become much shorter. As you build ability power, your damage, W shield, and R healing all grow, making you strongest in the mid to late game.
ekko-phase.text: Jungle Ekko’s early clear is not especially fast, but W’s stun gives him a high chance of successful ganks. He can start fights often from level 6, when he learns R, and again later as his ability cooldowns become much shorter. As he builds ability power, his damage, W shield, and R healing all grow, making him strongest in the mid to late game.

ekko-situational-tenacity.basis: Choose Mercury's Treads if the enemy has a lot of hard crowd control. Ekko needs to keep moving; if crowd control holds him in place, he may die before using R.
ekko-situational-tenacity.text: Choose Mercury’s Treads if the enemy has a lot of hard crowd control. Ekko needs to keep moving, and being locked down once can kill him before he uses R.

ekko-skill-passive.basis: P triggers on the third hit against the same target. Triggering P on a champion increases your movement speed. Q hitting on the way out and back, plus one basic attack, can complete the third P hit. One ability hit and two basic attacks can complete the third P hit. Build your combos around landing the third P hit. Use the movement speed from P to get out.
ekko-skill-passive.text: P triggers on the third hit against the same target and grants movement speed if that target is a champion. Two Q hits, one on the way out and one on the way back, plus a basic attack will trigger it; so will one ability hit and two basic attacks. Build combos around that third hit, then use the movement speed to get out, making the risk of going in worthwhile.

ekko-skill-q.basis: Q deals more damage on its return than on its way out. Push the enemy toward a wall to improve your chances of landing both Q hits. Use Q to clear minion waves and jungle monsters. Do not overuse Q; save enough mana for a combo in a fight.
ekko-skill-q.text: Q deals more damage on its return than on its way out. Pushing an enemy toward a wall improves your chances of landing both hits. Q also clears minion waves and jungle monsters, but overusing it can leave you without enough mana for a combo when a fight starts.

ekko-skill-r.basis: R can be used to escape. R can be used to deal damage. R heals more the more health you lost during the few seconds it rewinds. If you only consider R's healing, it is better to hold out as long as possible before using it. In a teamfight, you may need to use R before crowd control or burst damage stops you.
ekko-skill-r.text: R can deal damage or get you out of danger, and it heals more when you have lost more health during the few seconds it rewinds. For healing alone, waiting as long as possible is best in theory, but in a teamfight, crowd control or burst damage may stop you before you can cast it.

ekko-skill-w.basis: Casting W leaves a signal the enemy can see. W takes time to set up after you cast it. W triggers only when Ekko enters the sphere. Place W ahead of time along the enemy's escape route or approach path. W has a long cooldown, so missing it puts you at a major disadvantage in a fight.
ekko-skill-w.text: Casting W leaves a signal the enemy can see, and the sphere takes time to set up and triggers only when Ekko enters it. Place it ahead of the enemy’s escape route or approach path instead of using it after you have already closed in. Its long cooldown means a missed W can seriously hurt your chances in a fight.

ekko-skill-w-passive.basis: W's passive makes basic attacks against low-health enemies deal bonus damage based on their missing health. When finishing an enemy, confirm the kill with one or two basic attacks even after using all your abilities. If basic attacks can finish the enemy, do not waste R to confirm the kill.
ekko-skill-w-passive.text: W’s passive makes basic attacks against low-health enemies deal bonus damage based on their missing health. Even after using all your abilities, one or two basic attacks may finish the kill, so do not waste R if those attacks will do it.

ekko-teamfight.basis: Do not go in first in a teamfight. After the enemy has used their engage abilities and crowd control and your allies have started the fight, jump into the backline. Before going in, set up a safe place to return to with R. In a teamfight, decide where R will return you before deciding where to go in.
ekko-teamfight.text: Do not go in first in a teamfight. Wait until the enemy has used their engage abilities and crowd control and your allies have started the fight, then jump into the backline. Set up a safe return point for R before entering so you can survive even if the attempt fails; decide where you will return before choosing where to go in.

elise-combo-escape.basis: During a turret dive or countergank, use Rappel to dodge targeted abilities and turret attacks as Elise rises. After landing on a unit across a wall with Rappel, return to human form to get into range. You can use Spider Form Q to reach a fleeing enemy, then escape with Rappel. If Rappel is on cooldown, do not attempt a Spider Form Q engage that relies on it to escape.
elise-combo-escape.text: During a turret dive or countergank, Spider Form E, Rappel, lets Elise dodge targeted abilities and turret attacks as she rises. Land on a unit across a wall, then immediately use R to return to human form and get into range. You can also reach a fleeing enemy with Spider Form Q and escape with Rappel, but do not make an engage that depends on that escape while Rappel is on cooldown.

elise-combo-gank.basis: For a gank, land human form E, then use W, human form Q, transform, use Spider Form Q, and basic attack. Confirm that Cocoon lands before continuing the rest of the gank combo. Transforming before using Cocoon costs you the hard crowd control needed for a gank. Landing all human form abilities before transforming lets you summon and send in the maximum number of spiderlings.
elise-combo-gank.text: For a gank, land human form E, Cocoon, place W under the target, use human form Q, transform with R, then close in with Spider Form Q and basic attacks. Confirm that Cocoon hits before continuing: transforming first gives up the hard crowd control the gank needs. Landing all your human form abilities before transforming also summons the maximum number of spiderlings for the follow-up.

elise-laning-clear.basis: Clear jungle camps mainly in Spider Form. Healing from Spider Form basic attacks reduces health lost while clearing the jungle. When entering a camp, build up spiderlings with human form abilities, then transform immediately to clear it. Health-based damage has a cap against monsters. Do not spend too long fighting a large monster alone.
elise-laning-clear.text: Clear camps mainly in Spider Form to save mana and limit health loss through its healing basic attacks. As you enter a camp, use human form abilities to build up spiderlings, then transform immediately and send them in to clear faster. Health-based damage is capped against monsters, so spending too long fighting a large monster alone is inefficient.

elise-laning-gankpath.basis: After clearing the first few camps, shift to ganks and invades. Look for ganks as soon as you learn Cocoon. Gank lanes pulled toward your side, where the enemy has pushed forward, first.
elise-laning-gankpath.text: After the first few camps, shift to ganks and invades. Start looking for ganks as soon as you learn Cocoon, prioritizing lanes pulled toward your side where the enemy has moved forward.

elise-phase.basis: Elise is strong from the time she learns Cocoon through the mid game. Elise’s ability to transform from level 1 gives her high damage for her level. A single early gank can be especially valuable. Late in the game, health-based damage matters less, and her teamfight contribution falls because Cocoon is her only hard crowd control. Turn early leads into objectives and turrets to end the game quickly.
elise-phase.text: Elise is strongest from learning E, Cocoon, through the mid game. Having her transformation from level 1 gives her high damage for her level, making an early gank especially valuable. Later, health-based damage accounts for less of her damage as enemy health grows, and her teamfight contribution falls because Cocoon is her only hard crowd control. Turn early leads into objectives and turrets to end the game quickly.

elise-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Morellonomicon adds healing reduction while maintaining magic damage. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
elise-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item. It adds healing reduction while maintaining the magic damage Elise needs for her burst.

elise-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has burst engage, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. Elise is exposed to counterattacks immediately after throwing Cocoon. Use Zhonya’s Hourglass to avoid a counterattack right after throwing Cocoon.
elise-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy has burst engage, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. Elise is most exposed immediately after throwing Cocoon, so use the item to avoid the counterattack.

elise-skill-e-cocoon.basis: Human form E, Cocoon, is Elise’s only source of hard crowd control. Cocoon affects only the first target it hits along its path. Throw Cocoon from behind or to the side of the lane so it does not hit the minion wave. Cocoon reveals stealthed enemies, so it can be used to check bushes. Do not waste Cocoon carelessly; it can decide whether a gank succeeds.
elise-skill-e-cocoon.text: Human form E, Cocoon, is Elise’s only hard crowd control, and landing it often decides whether a gank succeeds. It affects only the first unit hit, so throw it from behind or beside the lane once you have an angle clear of minions and jungle monsters. Cocoon also reveals stealthed enemies and can check bushes, but do not waste it when a gank depends on it.

elise-skill-e-rappel.basis: Elise cannot be targeted while airborne with Spider Form E, Rappel. Use Rappel to dodge targeted abilities or turret attacks. Rappel can cross a wall by landing on a nearby enemy unit. If there is no enemy unit to land on, Rappel drops Elise where she started. To escape over a wall with Rappel, first check for a minion or jungle monster on the other side.
elise-skill-e-rappel.text: Spider Form E, Rappel, is both a movement and dodge tool: Elise cannot be targeted while airborne, allowing her to avoid targeted abilities and turret attacks. She can cross a wall by landing on a nearby enemy unit, but drops back where she rose if none is available. Before using it to escape over a wall, check for a minion or jungle monster on the other side; its long cooldown leaves her without an escape once it is used.

elise-skill-form.basis: Elise can transform into Spider Form from level 1. She fights by switching between human form and Spider Form within a single fight. Each time a human form ability hits an enemy, she stores a dormant spiderling. When she transforms into Spider Form, all stored spiderlings are summoned at once. Land a human form ability, then transform into Spider Form.
elise-skill-form.text: Elise has R, Spider Form, from level 1. It changes her weapon rather than serving as a burst button, and its short cooldown lets her switch forms within a fight. Each human form ability that hits an enemy stores a dormant spiderling; transforming summons them all at once. Land your human form abilities before transforming, or you lose the spiderlings they would have provided.

elise-skill-mana.basis: Spider Form abilities cost no mana. When mana is low, save human form abilities and clear camps in Spider Form. Spider Form basic attacks deal bonus magic damage and heal Elise.
elise-skill-mana.text: Spider Form abilities cost no mana, so when mana runs low, save your human form abilities and keep clearing camps in Spider Form. Its basic attacks deal bonus magic damage and heal Elise.

elise-skill-q-threshold.basis: Human form Q is stronger the more current health the target has. Spider Form Q is stronger the more health the target is missing. Open with human form Q and finish with Spider Form Q. Using Spider Form Q while the enemy still has plenty of health deals less effective damage.
elise-skill-q-threshold.text: Human form Q, Neurotoxin, deals more damage when the target has more current health, while Spider Form Q, Venomous Bite, is strongest after the target has lost health. Open with Neurotoxin and finish with Venomous Bite; biting a healthy enemy uses its reach without getting much damage from it.

elise-skill-w-spiderlings.basis: The human form W spiderling walks to the chosen location and explodes. Use human form W after the enemy is caught or their escape direction is clear. Spider Form W increases the attack speed of both Elise and her spiderlings. Spiderlings attack the target Elise bites with Spider Form Q.
elise-skill-w-spiderlings.text: Human form W, Volatile Spiderling, walks to a chosen location before exploding, so place it after the enemy is caught or their escape direction is clear. Spider Form W, Skittering Frenzy, increases the attack speed of Elise and her spiderlings, making it most valuable when they are already attacking. Spiderlings attack the target Elise bites with Spider Form Q, Venomous Bite, so bite the enemy you want them to focus.

elise-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, look for an angle to land Cocoon instead of standing on the front line. Before a fight, stay back in human form and catch a key enemy with Cocoon. After an ally engages, close in with Spider Form and finish off a weakened target. Go in after an ally lands area crowd control or a key enemy loses health. Fight where there is a nearby unit you can land on with Rappel.
elise-teamfight.text: In teamfights, look for an angle to land E, Cocoon, instead of standing on the front line. Stay back in human form before the fight to catch a key enemy, then follow an ally’s engage in Spider Form to finish a weakened target. Go in once an ally has landed area crowd control or a key enemy has already lost health, and fight near a unit you can land on with Rappel so you have a way out.
