evelynn-combo-execute.basis: R deals much more damage to targets below a certain health threshold. Use Q and E to bring the target into execute range, then finish with R. After casting R, Evelynn retreats backward.
evelynn-combo-execute.text: R deals much more damage to targets below a certain health threshold, so use Q and E to bring them into execute range before casting it to finish. Evelynn retreats backward after R, making it both a finisher and an escape.

evelynn-combo-gank.basis: For a gank, cast W from outside vision, then use Q, empowered E, Q, and R in that order once the mark is ready. Trigger the W mark with Q to charm the target. Q has longer range than E. Use empowered E after the charm holds the target in place.
evelynn-combo-gank.text: For a gank, apply W from outside vision, approach while the mark matures, then trigger it with Q to charm the target. Follow with empowered E to dash in, recast Q, and finish with R. Q reaches farther than E, so it can trigger the charm without getting close; waiting until the target is held in place keeps the empowered E dash from missing.

evelynn-laning-clear.basis: At jungle camps, cast W on the large monster first and trigger it once the mark is ready. W charms monsters for longer. W deals more bonus damage to monsters. Deal damage with Q while clearing camps. At camps where multiple monsters line up, use empowered E to pass through them.
evelynn-laning-clear.text: At jungle camps, apply W to the large monster first, wait for the mark to mature, then trigger it. Its longer charm and greater bonus damage against monsters let Evelynn clear without losing health. Use Q for damage during the clear, and angle empowered E through every monster when several line up.

evelynn-laning-path.basis: Before level 6, clear both sides of the jungle to level up. After level 6, approach through an unwarded river or from behind a lane. Camouflage ends where Evelynn enters combat. Clear wards along your gank path first.
evelynn-laning-path.text: Before level 6, Evelynn has no camouflage, making ganks rarely viable, so focus on clearing both sides of the jungle to level up. After level 6, approach through an unwarded route, such as the river or behind a lane. Camouflage only ends when she enters combat; the real danger is a ward the enemy has placed beside one of their jungle camps. Clear wards along your gank path first.

evelynn-laning-target.basis: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret. In a pushed lane, the enemy has farther to retreat, giving the W mark time to become ready. Against enemies with several mobility abilities, choose a lane where an ally can land crowd control first.
evelynn-laning-target.text: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret: the enemy has farther to retreat, giving W time to mature. Opponents with several mobility abilities can escape before then, so against them choose a lane where an ally can land crowd control first.

evelynn-phase.basis: Evelynn's ganks are weak before level 6 because she lacks camouflage and struggles to give W time to become ready. After level 6, Evelynn gets far more kill involvement by approaching while camouflaged and using her charm. After level 6, Evelynn gets ahead through kills more than farming.
evelynn-phase.text: Level 6 is Evelynn’s turning point. Before then, she lacks camouflage and struggles to give W time to mature, making her ganks weak; afterward, she can approach unseen and open with a charm, sharply increasing her kill involvement. The numbers reflect this: at 14 minutes, her CS is among the lowest while her kills are among the highest. She wins through kills after level 6 rather than farming.

evelynn-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing keeps taking targets out of execute range, reduce their healing with Morellonomicon. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
evelynn-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing repeatedly takes targets out of execute range, reduce it with Morellonomicon after completing one core item.

evelynn-situational-zhonya.basis: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner if an enemy assassin immediately counterattacks when you engage. Use R's untargetability and Zhonya's Hourglass at separate times.
evelynn-situational-zhonya.text: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass sooner if an enemy assassin immediately counterattacks when you engage. Use its protection and R’s untargetability at separate times to survive twice during one engage.

evelynn-skill-e.basis: Use E when it is empowered. Empowered E dashes to the target and hits every enemy along its path. Unempowered E has short range and does not dash. When Demon Shade activates, E's cooldown resets and E becomes empowered again. Step out briefly between fights to activate Demon Shade and regain E. If the charm wears off, use Q instead of chasing the target just to land empowered E.
evelynn-skill-e.text: Always use E while empowered: it deals much more damage, dashes to the target, and hits every enemy along its path, whereas unempowered E has short range and no dash. Demon Shade resets E’s cooldown and empowers it again when it activates, so step out briefly between fights to regain E. If the charm wears off, use Q instead of chasing the target just to land empowered E.

evelynn-skill-passive.basis: Demon Shade activates after Evelynn goes a while without basic attacking or using abilities. Demon Shade grants camouflage starting at level 6. Taking damage from an enemy champion or turret briefly disables Demon Shade. While Evelynn is camouflaged, a yellow eye appears above an enemy champion who comes close. If that enemy champion comes closer, Evelynn is revealed. When the yellow eye appears, adjust your distance from the enemy. When low on health, recover through Demon Shade in a brush before using a potion.
evelynn-skill-passive.text: Demon Shade activates after Evelynn spends a while without basic attacking or using abilities, and grants camouflage starting at level 6. Damage from an enemy champion or turret briefly disables it. While camouflaged, a yellow eye appears above an enemy champion who comes close, and Evelynn is revealed if they come closer; use the eye to judge your distance. When low on health, recover through Demon Shade’s healing each second in a brush before using a potion.

evelynn-skill-q.basis: The first Q hit leaves a mark that increases the damage of subsequent attacks against the same target. Recast Q to fire several more spikes. The spikes from Q recasts target the nearest enemy. To hit a champion among minions, move beside the minion wave to get a clear angle for Q.
evelynn-skill-q.text: The first Q hit marks its target, adding damage to subsequent attacks against that same target, and Q can be recast to fire several more spikes. Recast spikes target the nearest enemy, making a champion hard to aim at among minions; move beside the wave for a clear angle before firing.

evelynn-skill-r.basis: Evelynn cannot be targeted while casting R. Do not use R, which sends Evelynn backward, to engage. Using R briefly prevents Demon Shade from activating again.
evelynn-skill-r.text: While casting R, Evelynn becomes untargetable, letting her avoid targeted abilities and basic attacks unless their effects are already incoming. That makes it both a finisher and a way to dodge attacks, but it sends her backward, so it is not an engage tool. Account for the brief delay before Demon Shade can activate again after R.

evelynn-skill-w.basis: Once the W mark is ready, it adds a charm and reduces magic resistance. Triggering the W mark early applies only a slow. Listen for the heart filling up, then trigger the W mark. Cast W before approaching to give the mark time to become ready.
evelynn-skill-w.text: The W mark must mature for a set time to charm and reduce magic resistance. Triggering it early with a basic attack or ability applies only a slow and can ruin the gank, so listen for the sound of the heart filling before setting it off. Cast W before approaching to give the mark time to mature, rather than applying it during the fight.

evelynn-teamfight.basis: Do not stand at the front in teamfights. Activate Demon Shade, flank or circle behind, and position yourself behind the enemy backline damage dealers. Go in when the enemy's key crowd control has been used on your frontline. Angle empowered E to pass through a grouped enemy team.
evelynn-teamfight.text: Stay off the front line in teamfights. Activate Demon Shade, circle to the side or rear, and position behind the enemy backline damage dealers; go in only after the enemy’s key crowd control has been used on your frontline. Angle empowered E through grouped enemies so it hits everyone along its path. In fights around objectives, you can combine Smite with R to attempt a steal and use R’s retreat to escape.

ezreal-combo-allin.basis: When going all-in, use W, a basic attack, Q, E to adjust your angle, then another basic attack. Finish with R if needed. During an all-in, use E to move into position to cut off the enemy's escape route. Before going all-in, judge whether Q's cooldown reduction will let you use a second Q.
ezreal-combo-allin.text: For an all-in, use W Essence Flux → basic attack → Q Mystic Shot → E Arcane Shift to change your angle and close in → basic attack, then R Trueshot Barrage if needed. Position E to cut off the enemy’s escape route, and judge beforehand whether Q’s cooldown reduction will let you fire a second Q.

ezreal-combo-poke.basis: When poking, use W, then Q, then a basic attack. Detonating the W orb with Q deals damage from both abilities. Passive stacks increase attack speed, making follow-up basic attacks faster. Use W to poke when the enemy is away from the minion wave.
ezreal-combo-poke.text: For poke, use W Essence Flux → Q Mystic Shot → basic attack. Q detonates W for damage from both abilities and a mana refund, while passive stacks increase your attack speed for the follow-up basic attack. Fire W only when the enemy is away from the minion wave, or a minion will catch it first.

ezreal-laning.basis: Last-hitting minions with Q pushes the wave. If you don't know where the enemy jungler is, farm less with Q and use basic attacks to let the lane push toward you. If the enemy jungler appears on the other side of the map, push the lane with Q, then recall or establish vision.
ezreal-laning.text: Last-hitting with Q Mystic Shot pushes the wave. With one of the lowest movement speeds in the game, Ezreal can struggle to escape a gank in a pushed lane even with E Arcane Shift, so use Q less for farming and let the wave come toward you with basic attacks when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown. Once the jungler appears on the other side of the map, push with Q, then recall or establish vision.

ezreal-laning-mana.basis: Ezreal's ability to stay in lane depends on mana management. To keep poking, attach W and detonate it with an ability to recover mana. Judge when to recall by your remaining mana rather than your health.
ezreal-laning-mana.text: Ezreal’s lane endurance depends on mana. Attach W Essence Flux and detonate it with an ability to recover mana and keep poking; getting the order wrong can leave you out of mana with the wave partly pushed. Base your recall timing on your remaining mana rather than your health.

ezreal-phase-early.basis: Ezreal is most vulnerable at levels 1–2. At levels 1–2, survive by last-hitting minions with Q. At levels 1–2, keep a safe distance instead of looking for a kill. Even after learning R at level 6, avoid stepping forward.
ezreal-phase-early.text: Ezreal is most vulnerable at levels 1–2, when his base health and armor are low and he lacks E Arcane Shift. Keep a safe distance and survive by last-hitting with Q Mystic Shot instead of looking for trades or a kill; even after unlocking R Trueshot Barrage at level 6, avoid stepping forward.

ezreal-phase-scaling.basis: Ezreal gains an advantage through CS and accumulated damage rather than early kills. Ezreal comes into his own from mid game onward, once he has completed two core items. Before completing two core items, focus on minimizing losses.
ezreal-phase-scaling.text: Ezreal builds an advantage through CS and accumulated damage rather than early kills: at 14 minutes, his kill count ranks low among marksmen, while his CS and damage per minute rank near the top. His power arrives from mid game onward once he has two core items, so focus on avoiding losses until then.

ezreal-situational-antiheal.basis: Buy Executioner's Calling early to apply Grievous Wounds from afar with Q against enemies who sustain through healing. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder to maintain Grievous Wounds throughout teamfights.
ezreal-situational-antiheal.text: Against enemies who sustain through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling early to apply Grievous Wounds from afar with Q Mystic Shot. Upgrade it to Mortal Reminder to keep Grievous Wounds applied throughout teamfights.

ezreal-skill-e-lineup.basis: Use E to move a short distance sideways and open a Q angle blocked by minions. The homing bolt fired just after E lands prioritizes targets with a W orb attached. Attach W before using E to direct its bolt at the target you want.
ezreal-skill-e-lineup.text: A short sideways E Arcane Shift can open a Q Mystic Shot angle that minions were blocking. Use it to shift your position rather than advance; the homing bolt fired on landing prioritizes a target marked by W Essence Flux, so attach W first to direct the bolt where you want it.

ezreal-skill-r.basis: R travels in a straight line, piercing and hitting multiple minion waves or jungle monsters. R deals reduced damage to minions and regular monsters. Use R to finish off a fleeing enemy you can see from long range. Before a teamfight starts, use R where the enemies are grouped.
ezreal-skill-r.text: R Trueshot Barrage travels in a straight line and pierces targets, letting it sweep through multiple waves or a jungle camp, though it deals reduced damage to minions and regular monsters. Treat wave clear as a secondary benefit: use R to finish a visible fleeing enemy from long range or hit grouped enemies before a teamfight starts.

ezreal-skill-w-objective.basis: W attaches to structures and large jungle monsters as well as champions. When attacking a turret or objective, attach W and detonate it with a basic attack or Q. Save W at an objective and use it as soon as a fight starts.
ezreal-skill-w-objective.text: W Essence Flux attaches to structures and large jungle monsters as well as champions. When taking a turret or fighting over an objective, attach W and detonate it with a basic attack or Q Mystic Shot; at an objective, save W until the fight starts.

ezreal-skill-w-order.basis: W attaches an orb to a target that you can detonate with a follow-up attack. Detonating the W orb with an ability refunds the mana spent on that ability. To manage mana, land W and detonate the orb with Q.
ezreal-skill-w-order.text: W Essence Flux attaches an orb that you detonate with a follow-up attack or ability. Detonating it with an ability refunds that ability’s mana cost, so land W before using Q Mystic Shot to manage your mana; using Q first and throwing W afterward wastes mana.

ezreal-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay at the back and keep using Q. While your frontline holds the enemy in place, build up damage with Q and W from the edge of your range. Save E so you can escape after an enemy diver reaches you.
ezreal-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay at the back and keep firing Q Mystic Shot. Ezreal is fragile and has no way to engage, so build up damage with Q and W Essence Flux from the edge of your range while your frontline holds the enemy in place. Save E Arcane Shift to escape after an enemy diver reaches you.

fiddle-combo-gank.basis: When ganking, save Q until just after the enemy uses a mobility ability. When ganking, save Q to finish the target.
fiddle-combo-gank.text: For a gank, start outside enemy vision with E Reap to trigger an automatic fear, then begin channeling W Bountiful Harvest while the target is feared. An ability hit from outside vision applies fear without a direct Q cast, and E’s reach makes it the opening ability. Save Q Terrify for just after the target uses a mobility ability or to finish them off.

fiddle-combo-ult.basis: In a teamfight, enter with R, hit E as you land, and complete W. If someone can counterattack right after R lands, use Q on that target. During the teamfight combo, keep W's channel from being interrupted.
fiddle-combo-ult.text: In a teamfight, enter with R, apply E’s slow and silence as you land, then channel W to completion. Fear is needed first for the full damage; if someone can counterattack immediately after you land, use Q on that target. Protecting W’s channel is the aim of the combo.

fiddle-laning-clear.basis: At jungle camps, group the monsters with E, then complete W. Completing W on monsters increases its damage and healing. Completing W without interruption reduces its remaining cooldown, making it easier to move on to the next camp. Jungle routes where W gets interrupted hurt clear speed and health management.
fiddle-laning-clear.text: Build your jungle route around W: group monsters with E, then complete W to deal more damage to them, heal enough to maintain your health, and reduce W’s remaining cooldown so you can move straight to the next camp. A route where W gets interrupted hurts both clear speed and health management.

fiddle-laning-gank-path.basis: When ganking, approach by circling through the brush behind the lane or a blind spot near the river. If a lane has a control ward, ask an ally to clear the vision. If you must avoid a lane with a control ward, gank another lane.
fiddle-laning-gank-path.text: Ganks depend on approaching unseen, because an ability only triggers the automatic fear when Fiddlesticks is outside enemy vision. Circle through the brush behind the lane or a blind spot near the river. A control ward cuts that lane’s gank value by at least half, so ask an ally to clear it or gank another lane.

fiddle-skill-e.basis: E silences only enemies in the center of its area. Hit with the center of E to interrupt an enemy's channel or cast. To prevent an escape, aim for E's wide slow area. Use E to start an attack from outside enemy vision.
fiddle-skill-e.text: E (Reap) covers a wide area, but only enemies in its center are silenced. Aim the center at an enemy to interrupt a channel or cast; if you need to stop an escape, the wider slow is enough. E is also the easiest ability to open an attack with from outside enemy vision.

fiddle-skill-passive-scarecrow.basis: The passive replaces trinkets with effigies. Effigies are used for scouting. When revealed, an effigy briefly mimics Fiddlesticks. From level 6, effigies reveal nearby wards. Just before a teamfight or objective, use an effigy to check vision at the entry point, then choose where to cast R. Fiddlesticks mimics an effigy when standing still for a short time. Stand still in a brush and wait to ambush passing enemies.
fiddle-skill-passive-scarecrow.text: A Harmless Scarecrow replaces Fiddlesticks’ trinket with effigies that serve as scouts and decoys. When spotted, an effigy briefly mimics Fiddlesticks and can make enemies think he is engaging; from level 6, it also reveals nearby wards. Just before a teamfight or objective, place one at your planned entry point to check enemy vision, then choose where to cast R. Fiddlesticks can also mimic an effigy by standing still briefly, letting him wait motionless in a brush to ambush passing enemies.

fiddle-skill-q.basis: Casting Q directly fears the target and deals damage based on their current health. Casting Q on a target recently feared by Fiddlesticks deals increased damage. After entering with an automatic fear, use Q to finish the target.
fiddle-skill-q.text: Q Terrify works in two ways: damaging an enemy with an ability while Fiddlesticks is out of combat and unseen, or while posing as an effigy, automatically fears them; casting Q directly targets an enemy, fears them, and deals damage based on their current health. Q deals increased damage to a target recently feared by Fiddlesticks, so after engaging with an automatic fear, use it again to finish them off.

fiddle-skill-r.basis: R's channel is visible before the blink follows. Cast R from outside enemy vision, such as behind a wall or in a brush. Choose a narrow area where enemies will have trouble spreading out as R's landing spot.
fiddle-skill-r.text: R Crowstorm shows its channel before Fiddlesticks blinks in, giving enemies time to react if they can see him. Cast it only from outside their vision, such as over a wall, from brush, or from a blind spot. Since enemies can respond by immobilizing him and moving out of range, choose narrow terrain where they cannot easily spread out.

fiddle-skill-w.basis: Completing W's channel without interruption greatly reduces its remaining cooldown. Do not start W if its channel is likely to be interrupted. W's bonus damage based on missing health lands at the end of its duration. Lower the enemy's health before using W.
fiddle-skill-w.text: Completing W (Bountiful Harvest) without interruption greatly reduces its remaining cooldown, so do not start the channel when it is likely to be interrupted. Its bonus damage based on missing health lands at the end of the channel; lower the enemy’s health first to increase that damage.

fiddle-teamfight.basis: Cast R after an ally's immobilizing effect lands. Cast R after the enemy uses a key counter ability. Choose an R landing spot where several enemies are grouped and have no room to retreat. W and R's channels can be interrupted by immobilizing effects.
fiddle-teamfight.text: Fiddlesticks’ role in a teamfight is to initiate, but both W and R involve channels, so a single immobilizing effect can ruin the whole combo if he goes in first. Cast R after an ally’s immobilizing effect lands or the enemy uses a key counter ability, and land where several enemies are grouped with no room to retreat.

fiora-combo-basic.basis: For short trades, Q toward a vital → auto → E. E empowers the next two basic attacks. E's second basic attack is a guaranteed critical strike. When a new vital appears while E is active, hit it with the second empowered auto attack.
fiora-combo-basic.text: For a short trade, Q toward a vital, auto attack, then use E. E empowers the next two basic attacks, with the second guaranteed to crit; if a new vital appears while E is active, hit it with that critical strike.

fiora-combo-vital-angle.basis: If a vital appears on the opponent's back or side, use Q to dash in that direction and hit it. Hit front-facing vitals with auto attacks and E, and save Q to chase or disengage. Hitting a vital grants movement speed, making it easier to move toward the next vital. Look for an angle to hit two vitals in succession during a single fight.
fiora-combo-vital-angle.text: The vital’s position determines the combo: if it appears on the opponent’s back or side, use Q to reach and hit it; if it appears in front, hit it with an auto attack and E, saving Q to chase or disengage. Each vital hit grants movement speed, making the next one easier to reach, so look for an angle to hit two vitals in one fight.

fiora-laning.basis: After hitting a vital, use the increased movement speed to create distance. Trade to bait out the opponent's mobility ability first and gain an advantage in mobility usage.
fiora-laning.text: Keep trades short and back off. After hitting one vital, use the movement speed to create distance before the opponent can retaliate. Trading to draw out their mobility ability first also gives Fiora an advantage when she can use hers while staying close.

fiora-laning-vs-physical.basis: If the opponent has strong physical damage trades, focus on minimizing early losses rather than winning lane. In unfavorable physical damage trading matchups, stay in experience range even if you have to give up some minions. In unfavorable physical damage trading matchups, let the wave come toward your turret. Starting in the mid game, once your items come together, force 1v1s in a side lane. Once Fiora scales, she can turn around matchups that were unfavorable early.
fiora-laning-vs-physical.text: Against an opponent with strong physical damage trades, focus on limiting early losses rather than winning lane. Give up some minions if necessary, but stay within experience range and let the wave come toward your turret. Once your items come together in the mid game, force 1v1s in a side lane; Fiora can turn an unfavorable matchup around as she scales.

fiora-phase.basis: Fiora gets stronger in 1v1s as she gains items. Avoid reckless fights early, looking ahead to 1v1s after scaling. Fiora is weak in large teamfights. Fiora excels at gaining advantages through split pushing.
fiora-phase.text: Fiora’s 1v1 grows stronger as she gains items, so there is no need to force fights early. She is weak in large teamfights and gains advantages through split pushing.

fiora-situational-antiheal.basis: Fiora fights by hitting vitals one after another, gradually wearing down her opponent's health. Fiora struggles to duel opponents who use sustained healing to recover the damage between vital hits.
fiora-situational-antiheal.text: Against an opponent who relies on sustained healing, build Executioner’s Calling between core items. Fiora wears opponents down by hitting vitals one at a time; if they heal between hits, she cannot make the duel work.

fiora-skill-e.basis: E increases attack speed. E's first empowered auto slows the opponent. E's second empowered auto is a guaranteed critical strike. Hit a vital with E's second empowered auto attack. Use E after setting up a situation where you can stay close enough to land both empowered autos.
fiora-skill-e.text: E Bladework increases attack speed, slows with its first empowered auto attack, and guarantees a critical strike on the second. Use the slow to stay close, then aim the critical strike at a vital for much more damage in the same combo. Activate E once you can stay close enough to land both attacks, or the unused empowerment will go to waste.

fiora-skill-q.basis: Q dashes in the chosen direction and attacks the nearest enemy. Q prioritizes hitting a vital if one is within its hit area. Hitting an enemy with Q greatly reduces its cooldown. Using Q without hitting anything does not reduce its cooldown. When using Q to move, make sure to hit something, even a minion or ward.
fiora-skill-q.text: Q Lunge dashes in the chosen direction and strikes the nearest enemy, prioritizing a vital within its hit area. Hitting an enemy greatly reduces Q’s cooldown, letting Fiora use it again quickly while she stays close and keeps landing hits. A miss leaves the full cooldown in place and takes away both an engage and an escape option, so hit something as you move, even a minion or ward.

fiora-skill-riposte.basis: W blocks all attacks during its brief cast time. W blocks immobilizing effects during its brief cast time. If W blocks an immobilizing effect, its counterthrust stuns instead of slowing. Save W until the opponent has to use immobilizing crowd control. Simply having W available discourages the opponent from using abilities.
fiora-skill-riposte.text: W Riposte blocks all attacks and immobilizing effects during its brief cast, then counterthrusts; blocking an immobilizing effect turns the counterthrust’s slow into a stun. Save it for a moment when the opponent must use immobilizing crowd control. Even while available, W pressures the opponent to hold their abilities.

fiora-skill-vital.basis: Hitting a passive vital deals true damage based on the opponent's maximum health. Hitting a passive vital restores health. Vitals reappear in a different position after a set time or when hit. If the current vital is at a difficult angle to hit, wait for the next one instead of forcing an engage. The true damage from vitals is not reduced by the opponent stacking armor.
fiora-skill-vital.text: Hitting a passive vital deals true damage based on the opponent’s maximum health, restores health, and grants movement speed. Vitals reappear elsewhere after a set time or when hit, so if the current one is hard to reach, wait for the next rather than forcing an engage. Because armor does not reduce this true damage, Fiora can take down tanks even when they stack armor.

fiora-teamfight.basis: Choose side lane pressure over large fights. R reveals four vitals on the target. Use R in 1v1s or skirmishes where it provides the most value.
fiora-teamfight.text: Avoid large fights and apply pressure in a side lane. R Grand Challenge reveals four vitals on its target, making it most valuable in 1v1s and small skirmishes.

fiora-teamfight-ult.basis: R's vitals deal true damage based on the opponent's maximum health. Hitting all four R vitals or killing the target heals you and nearby allies.
fiora-teamfight-ult.text: If you have to take a teamfight, Fiora can use R (Grand Challenge) on the enemy frontline instead of the backline. Its vitals deal true damage based on the target’s maximum health, making it especially valuable against opponents who have stacked armor. Striking all four vitals or killing the target heals Fiora and nearby allies, potentially turning the fight around, so it is often better to use R to bring down a hard-to-break frontline than to avoid it.

fizz-combo-e-entry.basis: Close in with E, slow the target with the landing, then use a W empowered attack followed by Q. If the enemy still has key abilities or you have no allied support, they can counterattack after you engage with E.
fizz-combo-e-entry.text: To engage with E Playful / Trickster, approach while untargetable, slow the target on landing, then follow with a W Seastone Trident empowered attack and Q Urchin Strike. This spends your escape first, so the enemy can counterattack if they still have key abilities or you have no allied support.

fizz-combo-q-entry.basis: Use Q to dash through and close in, land a W empowered attack, then dodge the counterattack with E. You are not untargetable during the Q dash, so you can be hit. Engage with Q after the enemy has used their skillshots and crowd control.
fizz-combo-q-entry.text: Engage with Q Urchin Strike by dashing through the target, landing a W Seastone Trident empowered attack, and using E Playful / Trickster to dodge the counterattack. Fizz is not untargetable during the Q dash and can be hit by attacks, so choose this engage only after the enemy has used their skillshots and crowd control.

fizz-combo-ult.basis: Land R first, then use Q to close in as the shark knocks the target up and hit them with a W empowered attack. Use the time between the fish attaching and the shark appearing to close the gap. In an assassination combo that starts with R, save E to get out.
fizz-combo-ult.text: The safest assassination combo is to land R Chum the Waters first, then close in with Q Urchin Strike as the shark knocks the target up. Hit them with a W Seastone Trident empowered attack while they are airborne to avoid a counterattack and keep E Playful / Trickster available for your escape. Use the time between the fish attaching and the shark appearing to close the gap.

fizz-laning-roam.basis: Fizz is a melee mage who does not rely on attack speed, so his tower pressure is weak. If you push your opponent out of lane, spend the time joining fights in a side lane or the jungle. Before roaming, push the wave toward the enemy tower.
fizz-laning-roam.text: Fizz is a melee mage who does not rely on attack speed, so his tower pressure is weak and he gains little from leaving a lane pushed. If you drive your opponent out of lane, use that time to join fights in a side lane or the jungle. Roaming lets your opponent push the lane, so move only after pushing the wave toward their tower.

fizz-phase.basis: Fizz can threaten kills starting at level 2 or 3. If you close in aggressively the moment you level up before your opponent, you can force their Flash or kill them. Fizz reaches his full burst potential when level 6 R coincides with his first core item. He remains strong at assassinating a single target in the late game. With effectively only one way to engage, he struggles when enemies group up.
fizz-phase.text: Fizz can threaten kills from level 2 or 3; closing in aggressively as soon as you level up before your opponent can force their Flash or secure a kill. His burst peaks when level 6 R Chum the Waters coincides with his first core item, and he remains strong at assassinating a single target late in the game. With effectively only one way to engage, though, he struggles when enemies group up.

fizz-situational-antiheal.basis: If your assassination target has healing, it may offset Fizz's burst and prevent the kill. Against an assassination target with healing, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb early; it suits Fizz's magic damage. When you can afford to delay a core item, upgrade Oblivion Orb to Morellonomicon. Executioner's Calling only gives attack damage, which does not suit Fizz's scaling.
fizz-situational-antiheal.text: Healing can offset Fizz's burst and keep an assassination target alive. Because his damage is magic, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb early against a target with healing, then upgrade it to Morellonomicon when you can afford to delay a core item. Executioner's Calling only gives attack damage, which does not suit Fizz's scaling.

fizz-skill-e.basis: E's untargetability can dodge skillshots and enemy ultimates. Early on, E costs so much mana and has such a long cooldown that you can only use it once or twice in lane. Save E and use it cautiously in the early laning phase. Avoid putting yourself in a position where E is your only escape.
fizz-skill-e.text: E (Playful / Trickster) makes Fizz untargetable, letting him dodge skillshots and enemy ultimates entirely. Early in lane, its high mana cost and long cooldown mean he can use it only once or twice, so save it and play cautiously rather than treating it like invincibility. Avoid putting yourself in a position where E is your only escape.

fizz-skill-e-recast.basis: Pressing E again while untargetable makes you leap forward and ends the effect early. Recasting E narrows its area of effect and removes the slow. Recast E when you need to increase or close the distance. If you need to dodge enemy crowd control or a delayed explosion, do not recast E; use the full untargetable duration.
fizz-skill-e-recast.text: Pressing E again while untargetable makes Fizz leap forward and ends the effect early. The recast has a smaller area and no slow, but can help him create more distance or close the gap. If you need to dodge crowd control or a delayed explosion, do not recast; stay untargetable for the full duration.

fizz-skill-passive.basis: Your passive lets you move through units. In lane, walk between minions and poke with W. Your passive reduces damage taken from every attack by a fixed amount.
fizz-skill-passive.text: Fizz’s passive, Nimble Fighter, lets him move through units, so in lane he can walk straight between minions to poke with W and approach from an angle his opponent may not expect. Its fixed damage reduction on every attack is especially noticeable in early, small trades.

fizz-skill-q.basis: Q is a dash that passes through its target and can target enemy minions. Using Q on an enemy minion to dodge a skillshot or escape a gank lets you save E. You can use Q on an enemy minion to get closer to your opponent. Q applies on-hit effects, so it can trigger items.
fizz-skill-q.text: Q Urchin Strike dashes through its target and can target enemy minions. Use a minion to dodge a skillshot or escape a gank while saving E Playful / Trickster, or dash through one to extend your approach toward an opponent. Q also applies on-hit effects, so it can trigger items.

fizz-skill-r.basis: Even if R misses, an enemy who moves to dodge the shark can lose time and leave their formation split. Throw R where the enemy is going, rather than where they are standing. To scatter the enemy formation, throw R into a clustered group.
fizz-skill-r.text: R Chum the Waters can be useful even when it misses: an enemy who moves to avoid the shark loses time and may break from a clustered formation. Throw it where the enemy is going rather than where they stand, or deliberately aim into a grouped team to scatter them.

fizz-skill-w.basis: A W empowered attack deals magic damage and applies a bleed. If a W empowered attack kills the target, it refunds mana and greatly reduces W's cooldown. Last-hit minions with W to preserve mana and use your abilities more often. If you miss a last hit with W, its full cooldown applies.
fizz-skill-w.text: A W Seastone Trident empowered attack deals magic damage and applies a bleed. Killing a target with it refunds mana and nearly resets W's cooldown, so last-hitting minions with W preserves mana and keeps it available. Miss the last hit, and W goes on its full cooldown, leaving you without that damage for trades.

fizz-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use R from the flank to target one enemy in the backline. Engage when the enemy has used their targeted crowd control and your E is available. Before engaging in a teamfight, do not use E to poke or move around. If your assassination target is hiding behind their team, give up the engage and use R to scatter their formation.
fizz-teamfight.text: In teamfights, approach from the flank and use R Chum the Waters to pick off one backline enemy. Wait until the enemy has used their targeted crowd control, and keep E Playful / Trickster available by avoiding its use for poke or movement before you engage. If your target is hiding behind their team, give up the engage and use R to scatter their formation.

galio-combo-e-windup.basis: E steps back before dashing forward, giving it more range than it appears to have. You can dodge enemy skillshots while E steps back. E's dash stops when it hits terrain.
galio-combo-e-windup.text: Justice Punch (E) steps back before dashing forward, giving it more range than it appears to have and letting you dodge enemy skillshots during the step back. The dash stops if it hits terrain, so it gets cut short against an enemy with a wall behind them.

galio-combo-full.basis: For a full combo, knock the enemy up with E, briefly charge W to taunt them, then place Q on that spot. Start charging W before E's knockup ends so the enemy cannot walk away.
galio-combo-full.text: For a full combo, knock the enemy up with Justice Punch (E), start charging Shield of Durand (W) before the knockup ends and release it quickly to follow with a taunt, then place Winds of War (Q) on that spot. If you wait until the knockup ends to start W, the enemy can walk away.

galio-combo-qe.basis: For a basic trade, place Q, then use E to knock the enemy into it. Q's vortex forms only where the two gusts overlap. Aim Q where E will knock the enemy.
galio-combo-qe.text: For a basic trade, cast Q Winds of War, then use E Justice Punch to knock the enemy into it. The vortex forms only where the two gusts overlap, so aim at where the enemy will land rather than where they are standing.

galio-combo-w-charge.basis: You can press W again at any point during the charge to release it. The longer you charge W, the longer its taunt lasts. Charging W reduces incoming damage but slows Galio. Charge W as the enemy's combo comes in to reduce its damage, then counter with a taunt.
galio-combo-w-charge.text: You can release W Shield of Durand at any point during its charge, and a longer charge extends the taunt. Charging reduces incoming damage but slows Galio, so start as the enemy’s combo comes in, absorb less damage, then answer with the taunt.

galio-laning.basis: Hit both the wave and the enemy with Q to manage mana. As a melee champion, Galio is easy for ranged opponents to poke. Against ranged opponents, save E to disengage instead of using it to engage first. Close in right after the enemy uses their main ability on minions, then follow up with W's taunt.
galio-laning.text: In lane, hit both the wave and the enemy with Q Winds of War to manage mana. As a melee champion, Galio is vulnerable to ranged poke, so save E Justice Punch to disengage against ranged opponents. Close in only just after the enemy uses their main ability on minions, then follow up with W Shield of Durand’s taunt.

galio-laning-roam.basis: Push the wave into the enemy tower, then use R to help another lane. Calculate whether Teleport can make up for the farm lost while using R to help another lane.
galio-laning-roam.text: Galio’s main job is to push the wave into the enemy tower and use R Hero’s Entrance to help another lane. Before going, account for the farm lost during the play and whether Teleport can make up for it.

galio-phase.basis: Levels 1–2 are Galio's weakest: his mana costs are high and he does not have E yet. Galio can start trading at level 3, when he learns E. Galio becomes much more valuable at level 6, when he can start using R to help other lanes. Later on, focus on engaging and crowd control rather than damage, and survive with magic resistance.
galio-phase.text: Levels 1–2 are Galio’s weakest because his mana costs are high and he does not have E Justice Punch yet. He can start trading at level 3 when he learns E, and his value rises sharply at level 6 when R Hero’s Entrance lets him influence other lanes. Later, his role shifts from dealing damage to engaging, controlling enemies, and surviving with magic resistance.

galio-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy's main damage is magic, build Spectre's Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. P's damage, W's damage reduction, and R's damage all scale with magic resistance.
galio-situational-mr.text: If the enemy's main damage is magic, build Spectre's Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. Colossal Smash (P) damage, Shield of Durand (W) damage reduction, and Hero's Entrance (R) damage all scale with magic resistance, so that defensive stat also increases Galio's damage.

galio-skill-passive.basis: Hitting a champion with an ability reduces P's cooldown each time. After landing an ability, use one empowered basic attack. P's damage scales with magic resistance.
galio-skill-passive.text: Each ability hit on a champion reduces the cooldown of P Colossal Smash, so don’t cast your abilities and retreat without landing an empowered basic attack. Its damage scales with magic resistance, letting defensive items add to your damage.

galio-skill-r-shield.basis: R grants its shield to an ally when cast, before Galio arrives. Starting R as soon as an ally is caught helps them survive while Galio flies in. Galio cannot move from his position while casting R.
galio-skill-r-shield.text: R Hero’s Entrance shields an ally when cast, before Galio arrives. Cast it as soon as an ally is caught to help them survive while Galio flies in, but choose the moment carefully: Galio cannot move from his position during the cast, so the decision cannot be taken back.

galio-skill-r-timing.basis: R knocks up all enemies around its landing point. R's cast is visible to enemies, giving them time to spread out. Use R where an ally's crowd control is holding the enemy in place.
galio-skill-r-timing.text: Hero's Entrance (R) knocks up all enemies around its landing point, but its cast is visible to them, giving them time to spread out. Land where an ally's crowd control is holding them in place; casting it on an ally who is already dying only leaves Galio alone in the middle of the enemy team.

galio-skill-w-passive.basis: W's passive grants a shield after Galio has gone a while without taking damage. In lane, one hit of poke removes W's shield. Step forward only while W's shield is up. If it breaks, back off and wait for it to recharge.
galio-skill-w-passive.text: W Shield of Durand passively grants a shield after Galio goes a while without taking damage. A single poke hit removes it in lane, so step forward only while it is up; once it breaks, back off and wait for it to recharge.

galio-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, arrive with R to knock enemies up, then use W's taunt to pull their key threats away from your allies. Taunt the champion positioned to kill an ally right now.
galio-teamfight.text: In teamfights, arrive with R Hero’s Entrance to knock enemies up, then use W Shield of Durand’s taunt to pull key threats away from your allies. Target the champion positioned to kill an ally right now.

galio-teamfight-zone.basis: Place Q's vortex in a narrow passage to cut off the way in. Use E to block the direction the enemy damage dealer will escape. Stagger your taunt and knockup to keep enemies locked down.
galio-teamfight-zone.text: Galio holds the front line and blocks off space. Place Q Winds of War’s vortex in a narrow passage to cut off the way in, and use E Justice Punch to block the enemy damage dealer’s escape route. Stagger your taunt and knockup to keep enemies controlled.

gangplank-combo-barrel-chain.basis: Powder Kegs with overlapping blast radii explode in a chain. Detonate the front Powder Keg with Q to set off the one behind it and extend your reach. A chain explosion does not damage the same target multiple times. Use a Powder Keg chain to extend your reach and keep the slow on your target.
gangplank-combo-barrel-chain.text: Powder Kegs with overlapping blast radii explode in a chain, so detonating the front keg with Q sets off those behind it and extends your reach by the length of the chain. The same target cannot take damage more than once from that chain; use it to extend your range and maintain the slow, not to increase damage.

gangplank-combo-barrel-prime.basis: A Powder Keg cannot be detonated with one Q immediately after placement. A Powder Keg loses health over time. Place a Powder Keg where you expect to fight and let it age until one hit can detonate it. Do not use Q on a Powder Keg that has not aged enough.
gangplank-combo-barrel-prime.text: A newly placed Powder Keg has too much health to detonate with one Q. Place it where you expect to fight and let its health fall over time so one hit will set it off; spending Q on a keg that has not aged enough will ruin the trade.

gangplank-combo-basic-trade.basis: Place a Powder Keg behind or beside your opponent in advance, detonate it with Q, then follow up with Q. Place a Powder Keg behind or beside your opponent in advance, detonate it with Q, then follow up with an auto attack. To land a melee auto attack, approach after the Powder Keg's slow takes effect.
gangplank-combo-basic-trade.text: Place a Powder Keg behind or beside your opponent in advance, detonate it with Q to apply the slow, then follow up with Q or a basic attack. Wait for the slow before moving in to land a melee attack.

gangplank-laning-barrel-zone.basis: Place Powder Kegs at brush entrances or river paths to block jungle entry routes. You can spot an opponent's position when they move to destroy a Powder Keg. A Powder Keg destroyed by an enemy disappears without exploding.
gangplank-laning-barrel-zone.text: Use Powder Kegs to control space: placing them at brush entrances or along river paths can block jungle entry routes, and an opponent's attempt to destroy one reveals their position. A keg destroyed by an enemy disappears without exploding.

gangplank-laning-farm.basis: Use Q to last-hit safely and hold the lane without pushing. In an unfavorable matchup, farm with Q in front of your turret.
gangplank-laning-farm.text: Gangplank can last-hit safely with Q without pushing the lane. In an unfavorable matchup, farm with Q in front of your turret and wait until you reach the level where your Powder Keg combo is ready before trading damage.

gangplank-laning-mana.basis: Overusing Powder Kegs and Q together drains mana quickly. Decide in advance how many Powder Kegs to use in a trade. Save Powder Kegs you will not use in a trade for farming. If an opponent closes in while you are out of mana, you lose both your means of fighting back and escaping.
gangplank-laning-mana.text: Overusing Powder Kegs and Q together drains mana quickly. Decide in advance how many kegs to spend on a trade and save the rest for farming; if an opponent closes in while you are out of mana, you lose both your means of fighting back and escaping.

gangplank-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Gangplank is weak because Powder Kegs have little time to age and each keg deals little damage. Gangplank grows stronger in the mid game, when his Powder Keg combo starts landing all at once. From level 6, R lets Gangplank influence the entire map. Powder Keg range and bombardment keep Gangplank strong in the late game. Get through Gangplank's weak early game while avoiding bad trades.
gangplank-phase.text: Gangplank is weak at levels 1–2 because there is little time for Powder Kegs to age and a single keg deals little damage. He grows much stronger in the mid game once his full keg combo can land at once, while R gives him map-wide influence from level 6. Keg range and bombardment keep him strong late, so get through the early game without falling behind.

gangplank-skill-passive.basis: Trial by Fire's burn applies only to melee basic attacks, not Q. Destroying a Powder Keg resets Trial by Fire's cooldown and grants movement speed. Detonate Powder Kegs in succession to chase or disengage.
gangplank-skill-passive.text: Trial by Fire’s burn applies only to melee basic attacks, not Q. Destroying a Powder Keg resets the passive’s cooldown and grants movement speed, so you can detonate kegs in succession to chase or disengage.

gangplank-skill-q.basis: Q applies on-hit effects and can critically strike. Use Q to last-hit from range or harass your opponent. Check your remaining mana before deciding whether to use Q for poke or last hits.
gangplank-skill-q.text: Q (Parrrley) applies on-hit effects and can critically strike, making it useful for both ranged last hits and harass. Check your remaining mana each time you decide whether to use it on your opponent or to secure a last hit.

gangplank-skill-r-global.basis: R can strike anywhere on the map. Use R in fights in other lanes. Watch the minimap for low-health enemies and finish them with R. Cast R ahead of a fleeing enemy's expected path to cut them off.
gangplank-skill-r-global.text: R (Cannon Barrage) can strike anywhere on the map, and its greatest value is in fights in other lanes. Watch the minimap to finish low-health enemies with it, or cast it ahead of a fleeing enemy's expected path to cut off their escape.

gangplank-skill-r-upgrade.basis: Spend the Silver Serpents earned with Q to upgrade R at the shop. Depending on the R upgrade, it adds more bombardments or true damage and a strong slow. Recall before an expected teamfight to update your R upgrade.
gangplank-skill-r-upgrade.text: Spend the Silver Serpents earned with Q to upgrade R at the shop. Depending on the upgrade, it gains more bombardments or adds true damage and a strong slow, so recall and upgrade it before an expected teamfight.

gangplank-skill-w.basis: W restores health and removes crowd control effects. Use W right after a key enemy crowd control effect lands to break their combo. W cannot answer crowd control applied after you use it.
gangplank-skill-w.text: W (Remove Scurvy) is primarily for removing crowd control, not restoring health. Don’t use it early just because you’ve lost health; use it immediately after a key enemy crowd control effect lands to break the combo. You have no answer to crowd control that lands after W is spent.

gangplank-teamfight.basis: Do not stand at the front in teamfights. Place a Powder Keg beside the enemy team in advance, then detonate it with Q from behind to maintain an area slow.
gangplank-teamfight.text: Stay behind your team in teamfights. Place a Powder Keg in advance beside an area where the enemy team might stand, then detonate it with Q from behind to maintain an area slow. Layer R (Cannon Barrage) over it to block both their retreat path and the area around the keg, leaving them nowhere to stand.

gangplank-teamfight-entry.basis: Move in yourself after the opponent has used their key targeted abilities. W can clear crowd control only once, so overlapping crowd control can easily kill you. If the opening to move in is uncertain, place a Powder Keg and back away.
gangplank-teamfight-entry.text: Move in yourself only after the opponent has used their key targeted abilities. W Remove Scurvy can clear crowd control once, so overlapping effects can kill you. If the opening is uncertain, placing a Powder Keg and backing away is enough to do your part.

garen-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, silence with a Q-empowered auto attack, then use E. Q's movement speed boost helps you close in on your opponent. Deal damage with E while Q's silence prevents your opponent from retaliating with abilities.
garen-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, use Q Decisive Strike to close the gap, land its empowered auto attack to silence your opponent, then use E Judgment while they cannot retaliate with abilities.

garen-combo-e-first.basis: If the enemy is already in melee range, use E before Q. Using Q during E does not interrupt the spin. Q's silence applies to the first basic attack after E's spin ends. Save Q until the enemy uses a counterattack ability.
garen-combo-e-first.text: If the enemy is already in melee range, use E Judgment before Q Decisive Strike. You can activate Q during the spin without interrupting it, then apply the silence with your first auto attack after E ends; this lets you save Q until the enemy tries to counterattack with an ability.

garen-combo-ult.basis: To finish your opponent, use a Q-empowered auto attack, then E, recast E to end it early, and use R. R deals true damage proportional to your opponent's missing health. If your opponent shows no sign of escaping, let E deal its full damage before using R. If your opponent shows signs of escaping, recast E to stop it and immediately use R.
garen-combo-ult.text: To finish an opponent, use Q Decisive Strike, land the empowered auto attack, then use E Judgment before casting R Demacian Justice. Because R deals true damage based on missing health, let E deal its full damage first when the opponent is staying in range; if they show signs of escaping, recast E to end the spin early and use R immediately.

garen-laning.basis: Let the wave push toward you instead of pushing it. Garen has no mobility ability, leaving him vulnerable to ganks when his lane is pushed. Always keep wards available to prepare for ganks. Trade when your opponent steps forward to last-hit a minion. After pushing the wave with E, retreat into a brush to activate P's healing.
garen-laning.text: Let the wave push toward you. Garen has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to ganks when he pushes the lane, so keep wards available. Trade as your opponent steps forward to last-hit a minion, and if E Judgment pushes the wave, retreat into a brush to recover with P Perseverance.

garen-phase.basis: Garen's base health and P healing make him strong in early melee trades. Garen peaks in the mid game when Q's duration increases and R reaches rank 2. In the late game, as enemies become more durable, Garen relies on R's execute more than E's damage. Use lane pressure and split pushing to secure your advantage in the mid game.
garen-phase.text: Garen’s base health and P Perseverance healing make him strong in early melee trades. He peaks in the mid game as Q Decisive Strike’s duration increases and R Demacian Justice reaches rank 2. Later, enemy durability makes E Judgment’s spin damage less sufficient and leaves him more reliant on R’s execute, so use lane pressure and split pushing to secure your advantage during that mid game peak.

garen-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder earlier to get healing reduction. If healing reduction is more urgent, buy Executioner's Calling first. Without healing reduction, Garen struggles to trade against opponents who heal through E's sustained damage.
garen-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder earlier; if healing reduction is needed even sooner, get Executioner’s Calling first. Healing opponents can offset E Judgment’s sustained damage, making trades difficult without healing reduction.

garen-situational-boots-slow.basis: If the enemy team has many slows, choose Boots of Swiftness over Berserker's Greaves to close in more easily while Q is on cooldown. You cannot use Q to remove slows while it is on cooldown.
garen-situational-boots-slow.text: If the enemy team has many slows, choose Boots of Swiftness over Berserker’s Greaves. Q Decisive Strike can remove a slow, but until it comes off cooldown, slow resistance helps reduce the time it takes to close the gap.

garen-situational-mr.basis: If enemy magic damage is a threat, swap your boots for Mercury's Treads, which provide magic resistance and tenacity. Garen is vulnerable to being locked down by crowd control while E spins without hitting anyone.
garen-situational-mr.text: If enemy magic damage is a threat, switch to Mercury’s Treads for magic resistance and tenacity. Tenacity is especially valuable because being locked down by crowd control while E Judgment spins without hitting anyone is particularly costly for Garen.

garen-situational-onhit.basis: E's spin damage does not apply on-hit effects. Items whose value centers on on-hit effects, such as Blade of the Ruined King, are less efficient because those effects do not apply to E. For the same cost, choose attack speed and critical strike items that work well with E.
garen-situational-onhit.text: E Judgment’s spin damage does not apply basic attack on-hit effects, making items that derive much of their value from those effects, such as Blade of the Ruined King, less efficient for Garen’s main damage source. At a comparable value, choose items that grant attack speed and critical strike chance.

garen-skill-e.basis: E hits more times during its spin with higher attack speed. E's damage can critically strike. To increase E's total damage, mix in attack speed and critical strike chance instead of building only attack damage. E reduces the armor of champions it hits multiple times. To support allied physical damage dealers, let E spin for its full duration to reduce enemy armor. E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy. During trades, position so only the enemy champion is within E's range.
garen-skill-e.text: E Judgment gains more hits per spin from attack speed and can critically strike, so mixing attack speed and critical strike chance yields more total damage than building only attack damage. Repeated hits also reduce a champion’s armor; if you have allied physical damage dealers, completing the spin helps their damage too. E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy, so during trades, position yourself with only the opposing champion inside the spin rather than catching minions alongside them.

garen-skill-passive.basis: P restores health after some time without being hit by a champion. Minion attacks do not interrupt P's healing. After a trade, briefly retreat into a brush or behind a turret to heal with P. P's healing lets Garen hold his lane even in unfavorable matchups.
garen-skill-passive.text: P Perseverance restores Garen’s health after he goes some time without being hit by a champion, and minion attacks do not interrupt the healing. After a trade, briefly retreat into a brush or behind a turret to recover before returning; this sustain can keep you in lane even in unfavorable matchups.

garen-skill-q.basis: Q removes all slows affecting Garen. Garen has no mobility ability, so he relies on Q to chase. Use Q right after your opponent slows you to remove the slow. Q's empowered auto attack remains available briefly after activation. You can activate Q outside attack range, then approach and silence with the empowered auto attack.
garen-skill-q.text: Q Decisive Strike removes all slows affecting Garen. Since he has no mobility ability, save this chase tool until just after an opponent slows you. Its empowered auto attack remains available briefly, so you can activate Q outside attack range, close in, and still apply the silence.

garen-skill-w.basis: W's shield and tenacity apply only for a very brief moment right after casting. W's damage reduction lasts longer than its shield and tenacity. Time W for the moment an enemy ability comes at you. W's passive permanently increases armor and magic resistance whenever you kill a unit. Secure last hits in lane to build up W's defenses.
garen-skill-w.text: W Courage grants a shield and tenacity for only a very brief moment after casting, while its damage reduction lasts longer. Time it for an incoming enemy ability so the shield and tenacity can help you withstand damage and crowd control. Its passive permanently increases armor and magic resistance whenever you kill a unit, so securing last hits in lane also builds your defenses.

garen-teamfight.basis: Garen cannot take the initiative in starting teamfights. Once your allies start the fight, move in while timing W. In teamfights, hold the front line and use E to reduce enemy armor. Use R in teamfights when an enemy's health drops. To avoid being kited, look for an opening to reach the enemy backline from the flank or out of vision. If there is no opening for a teamfight, split push and sustain with P without recalling to keep one enemy tied down in a side lane.
garen-teamfight.text: Garen cannot initiate teamfights himself. Once your allies engage, time W Courage as you enter, hold the front line while E Judgment reduces enemy armor, and use R Demacian Justice on an opponent whose health has fallen. Walking straight in leaves you vulnerable to kiting, so look for a flank or an approach from outside vision toward the enemy backline. If there is no opening for a teamfight, split push instead, using P Perseverance to stay in a side lane without recalling and keep one opponent occupied.

gnar-combo-flash-r.basis: If you lack an angle to knock enemies into a wall, use Flash to reposition and aim R toward the wall. R throws enemies around Gnar in the direction he is facing.
gnar-combo-flash-r.text: If you cannot line up a wall stun, use Flash to reposition and aim R (GNAR!) toward the wall. It throws nearby enemies in the direction Gnar faces, so flashing behind an opponent can turn a poor angle into a wall angle.

gnar-combo-mini.basis: For a Mini Gnar trade, use Q, then E to bounce off a unit and move forward, and finish with an auto attack. Catching the returning boomerang greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Aim your E movement along the boomerang's return path. When Mini Gnar hits the same target repeatedly, W triggers and deals bonus damage. When Mini Gnar's W triggers, his movement speed increases greatly.
gnar-combo-mini.text: For a Mini Gnar trade, use Q Boomerang Throw, then E Hop onto a minion or enemy to bounce forward, and finish with an auto attack. Catching the returning boomerang greatly reduces Q’s cooldown, so aim your E movement along its return path. Repeated hits on the same target trigger W Hyper for bonus damage and a large movement speed boost.

gnar-combo-transform.basis: For a transformation all-in, approach with E at full Rage and transform. Mini Gnar's E bounces farther if he lands on a unit. Transform during the E bounce, then land, stun with W, auto attack, and follow with Q. In a transformation all-in, do not use another ability to trigger the transformation before closing in with E.
gnar-combo-transform.text: For a transformation all-in, use E Hop at full Rage to close the gap and trigger the transformation. Landing on a unit makes Mini Gnar bounce farther; transform during the bounce to land as Mega Gnar, then stun with W Wallop, auto attack, and follow with Q Boulder Toss. Using another ability to transform before closing in leaves you without that way to reach the enemy.

gnar-combo-wall-r.basis: Use R to finish Mega Gnar's combo. R stuns enemies only if they hit a wall. Enemies knocked into a wall by R take bonus damage. Before using R, position Gnar, the enemy, and the wall in a straight line. After stunning an enemy against a wall with R, follow with W to keep them controlled. If R does not knock an enemy into a wall, its only crowd control is the knockback and slow.
gnar-combo-wall-r.text: Finish Mega Gnar’s combo with R GNAR! Position Gnar, the enemy, and a wall in a straight line before casting: only enemies thrown into a wall are stunned and take bonus damage. Follow the stun with W Wallop to keep them controlled. Without a wall hit, R only knocks enemies back and slows them.

gnar-laning.basis: As Mini Gnar, poke with ranged auto attacks and Q. Back away before entering the opponent's retaliation range. When clearing a wave, catch Mini Gnar's Q to reduce its cooldown. Commit to a close-range all-in only when you transform into Mega Gnar. Finish the trade before the transformation ends.
gnar-laning.text: In lane, poke as Mini Gnar with ranged auto attacks and Q Boomerang Throw, then back away before the opponent can retaliate. Use Q to clear waves and catch the boomerang to keep reducing its cooldown without spending mana. Commit to a close-range all-in only when you transform into Mega Gnar, and finish the trade before the transformation ends.

gnar-laning-rage.basis: Taking damage also builds Rage, so being hit without trading back can make you transform at an unwanted time. Manage your transformation so you do not waste it under the enemy turret or where you have no allied support. Choose where to transform with recalls, level-ups, and jungle involvement in mind. Adjust how much you trade to match your planned transformation timing.
gnar-laning-rage.text: Taking damage also builds Rage, so drawing minion aggro or taking hits without trading back can force a transformation at the wrong time. Transforming under the enemy turret or without allied support wastes it. Plan where to transform around recalls, level-ups, and jungle involvement, then adjust how much you trade until that moment.

gnar-phase.basis: Gnar gains an advantage at levels 1–2 by poking with ranged auto attacks and Q. Early on, avoid extended close fights even as Mega Gnar. Look for kills once you learn R at level 6. Gnar is strongest in the mid game when he completes his first core item. Late-game Gnar relies heavily on terrain where he can knock enemies into walls.
gnar-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Gnar can gain an advantage by poking with ranged auto attacks and Q Boomerang Throw. His base health is among the lowest of all champions, though, so avoid extended close fights early even as Mega Gnar. Kill opportunities open up with R GNAR! at level 6, and he peaks in the mid game after completing his first core item. Late in the game, he gets the most value from terrain that offers a wall angle.

gnar-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing makes it hard to finish the fight during Mega Gnar's duration, buy Executioner's Calling first to reduce healing. Mega Gnar has a fixed duration, so longer fights put him at a disadvantage.
gnar-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing a fight during Mega Gnar’s transformation, buy Executioner’s Calling first to reduce it. His Mega form has a fixed duration, so drawn-out fights put him at a disadvantage.

gnar-skill-e.basis: Mini Gnar's E bounces when he lands on a unit, extending its travel distance. Mega Gnar's E does not bounce, so it covers less distance when escaping than Mini Gnar's E. Mega Gnar's E deals area damage where he lands. Before engaging with E, check its cooldown to see whether you can use it to escape after returning to Mini Gnar.
gnar-skill-e.text: Mini Gnar’s E Hop bounces much farther when he lands on a unit, while Mega Gnar’s E Crunch lands without bouncing and deals area damage, giving him a shorter escape. Use E to engage as Mega Gnar, but check its cooldown first so it will be available to escape after you return to Mini Gnar.

gnar-skill-q.basis: Mini Gnar's Q returns after hitting one enemy. Mini Gnar's Q deals reduced damage to enemies it hits after the first. Catching Mini Gnar's boomerang greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Mega Gnar's Q deals area damage. The boulder from Mega Gnar's Q (Boulder Toss) stops where it hits an enemy. Throw Mega Gnar's Q where you can pick up the boulder to reduce its cooldown.
gnar-skill-q.text: Gnar’s Q works differently in each form. Mini Gnar’s Q Boomerang Throw returns after hitting an enemy, deals reduced damage to subsequent targets, and has a greatly reduced cooldown if he catches it. Mega Gnar’s Q Boulder Toss deals area damage, but the boulder stops where it hits an enemy; throw it where you can pick it up to reduce the cooldown. Catching either projectile is a key part of the damage cycle.

gnar-skill-rage.basis: Gnar gains Rage when he deals or takes damage. Once Rage is full, Gnar transforms into Mega Gnar when he uses his next ability. If it is not time to engage, hold your abilities even at full Rage to control when you transform.
gnar-skill-rage.text: Gnar’s passive, Rage Gene, builds Rage when he deals or takes damage. Once the bar is full, his next ability transforms him into Mega Gnar, so the ability use determines the timing. If you are not ready to engage, hold your abilities at full Rage and trigger the transformation when you want it.

gnar-skill-rage-window.basis: After Mega Gnar returns to Mini Gnar, he cannot gain Rage for a while. Gnar is most vulnerable just after transforming back, while he cannot gain Rage.
gnar-skill-rage-window.text: When Mega Gnar’s duration ends and he returns to Mini Gnar, he cannot build Rage for a while. This is his weakest window, so finish the fight and back off before the transformation ends. Opponents will try to engage during that window; anticipate when it will begin and position accordingly.

gnar-skill-w.basis: Mini Gnar's W is a passive that triggers when he hits the same target repeatedly. Mini Gnar's W deals damage based on maximum health, making it useful against tanks. Mini Gnar gains movement speed when his W triggers. When poking as Mini Gnar, focus auto attacks and Q on the same target to trigger W. Mega Gnar's W slams the area in front of him and stuns enemies. As Mini Gnar, be careful not to waste passive stacks by pressing W.
gnar-skill-w.text: Mini Gnar’s W (Hyper) is a passive that triggers after repeated hits on the same target, so very short trades will not activate it. Its damage scales with the target’s maximum health, making it useful against tanks, and it grants movement speed when triggered; when poking, focus auto attacks and Q (Boomerang Throw) on one target. Mega Gnar’s W (Wallop) is a separate ability that slams the area in front of him and stuns enemies, so take care not to press W in Mini form and waste passive stacks.

gnar-teamfight.basis: Gnar's teamfight impact depends heavily on finding an angle to knock enemies into a wall. Choose the fight location in advance and position so opponents have a wall behind them. Engage as Mega Gnar and start the teamfight with R. As Mini Gnar, stay back and poke with Q while building Rage. Do not force an engage to start a teamfight as Mini Gnar.
gnar-teamfight.text: Gnar’s teamfight impact depends on a wall angle. Choose the fight location in advance, position so opponents have a wall behind them, then engage as Mega Gnar and open with R GNAR! If you are still Mini Gnar, stay back and poke with Q Boomerang Throw while building Rage instead of forcing an engage.

gragas-combo-eq.basis: While dashing with E, roll Q to the landing spot, then recast Q to detonate it while the target is knocked up by E. An enemy knocked up by E cannot walk out of the barrel's radius.
gragas-combo-eq.text: Gragas’s core combo is E into Q: while dashing with E, roll Q to the landing spot, then recast it while the target is knocked up. They cannot walk out of the barrel’s radius, so both abilities are guaranteed to hit.

gragas-combo-full.basis: For the full combo, press W after E hits, then detonate Q. W takes time to drink, so press it during E's knockup to land the empowered basic attack before the knockup ends. Use R to move the opponent where you want when needed.
gragas-combo-full.text: The full combo is E hit, W, Q detonation, then R if needed. Because W takes time to drink, press it during E’s knockup so the empowered basic attack lands before the target comes down. Use R to move the opponent where you want, rather than simply to finish them off.

gragas-combo-qe.basis: Roll Q out first, then when the opponent comes near, engage with E and detonate Q as E hits. The longer the barrel stays out, the more damage and slow it gains, so do not detonate it immediately. Look for a Q-E combo in lane ganks where the opponent's retreat path is predictable.
gragas-combo-qe.text: For Q into E, roll out the barrel first and wait for the opponent to come near before engaging. The longer it stays out, the more damage and slow it gains, so time the detonation to E’s impact instead of triggering it immediately. This is especially strong in lane ganks where the opponent’s retreat path is predictable.

gragas-jungle.basis: While jungling, wear down camps with W's empowered basic attack and stay healthy with passive healing. Watch the lanes and gank when an enemy is within E's reach.
gragas-jungle.text: While jungling, wear down camps quickly with W (Drunken Rage)'s empowered basic attack and stay healthy through passive healing. E (Body Slam)'s short cooldown creates frequent gank opportunities, so watch the lanes and show up whenever an enemy is within E's reach instead of clearing every camp.

gragas-jungle-gank.basis: For a gank, circle behind the lane, place Q on the opponent's retreat path, and knock them up with E as they try to back away. If you engage with E from the front, the opponent can walk toward their turret.
gragas-jungle-gank.text: For the most reliable gank, circle behind the lane, roll Q onto the opponent’s retreat path, then use E to knock them up as they try to back away. Engaging with E from the front gives them a path to walk toward their turret and sharply reduces your chances.

gragas-phase.basis: Learning E at level 2 or 3 makes ganks possible. Learning R at level 6 creates reliable kill opportunities. Burst damage is strongest in the mid game after building one or two ability power items. In the late game, sustained damage is lacking, so focus on burst damage and disrupting enemy formations.
gragas-phase.text: Learning E at level 2 or 3 opens up ganks, while R at level 6 creates reliable kill opportunities. Gragas’s burst peaks in the mid game after one or two ability power items; in the late game, his lack of sustained damage narrows his role to burst and disrupting enemy formations.

gragas-skill-e.basis: Hitting an enemy with E greatly reduces its cooldown. If E hits, you can engage and then use E again to disengage. If E misses, you have to wait out its full cooldown. Before engaging, decide whether to use E to initiate or save it to escape.
gragas-skill-e.text: Hitting an enemy with E greatly reduces its cooldown, letting you engage and then use it again to disengage. A miss leaves you waiting out the full cooldown, so decide before going in whether to use E to initiate or save it for an escape.

gragas-skill-q.basis: The longer Q's barrel stays out, the more damage and slow it gains. In fights, detonate Q when the opponent cannot move. Q deals reduced damage to minions, so save it for fights rather than farming.
gragas-skill-q.text: Q (Barrel Roll) lets you choose when to detonate the barrel. The longer it sits, the more damage and slow it gains, but enemies can see and dodge it, so in fights, detonate it when they cannot move. It deals reduced damage to minions, making it inefficient for clearing waves; save it for fights rather than farming.

gragas-skill-r.basis: R pushes opponents outward from the explosion point. To push an opponent toward your team, land R behind them. Landing R between an opponent and your team pushes them away from your team. R cannot push opponents over walls.
gragas-skill-r.text: R pushes opponents outward from the explosion point, so land it behind a target to send them toward your team. Landing it between the target and your team pushes them away instead. It cannot push opponents over walls, so account for its limited displacement against someone standing next to one.

gragas-skill-r-split.basis: Land R between the enemy front line and back line to split their formation. Pushing the back line away with R gives your team time to clear the front line with a numbers advantage.
gragas-skill-r-split.text: R (Explosive Cask) can also split the enemy formation: land it between the front line and back line to push only the back line away. This gives your team time to clear the front line with a numbers advantage and has a more direct impact on winning a teamfight than using R to seek a kill.

gragas-skill-w.basis: W's damage reduction applies from the moment Gragas starts drinking. If you see an opponent's burst coming, press W before it hits. W's empowered basic attack also deals damage based on maximum health around the target. Use W's empowered basic attack against jungle camps and high-health opponents.
gragas-skill-w.text: W’s damage reduction starts as soon as Gragas begins drinking, so press it when you see an opponent’s burst coming, before it hits. The empowered basic attack deals maximum health based damage around its target, making it especially strong against jungle camps and high health opponents.

gragas-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, activate W, knock up the back line with E, follow with Q, and split the enemy formation with R. Before engaging, check whether the opponent has used their targeted crowd control. Before engaging, check whether your team is close enough to follow up.
gragas-teamfight.text: In teamfights, activate W, engage with E to knock up the back line, follow with Q, and use R to split the enemy formation. Before going in, check that the opponent has used their targeted crowd control and that your team is close enough to follow up. If Gragas dies first, your team loses its means of initiating.

graves-combo-engage.basis: Close the gap with E, then basic attack at point-blank range. E loads one shell into the magazine. Use E just before reloading to keep attacking without interruption. At point-blank range, cut off their vision with W, then use Q.
graves-combo-engage.text: Close the gap with E (Quickdraw), then land basic attacks at point-blank range. Since the dash loads one shell, using E just before a reload keeps your damage going without interruption. Once you are close, block the opponent’s vision with W (Smoke Screen) and follow with Q (End of the Line), leaving them little time to react.

graves-combo-q-wall.basis: Q explodes immediately when it hits terrain. Against an opponent with their back to a wall, hit the wall with Q to land the explosion quickly. Against an enemy across a wall, fire Q right against the wall to land the explosion.
graves-combo-q-wall.text: Q (End of the Line) explodes immediately on hitting terrain. Against an opponent backed up to a wall, aim at the wall so the explosion gives them no time to dodge; against an enemy on the other side, fire Q along the wall so only the explosion reaches them.

graves-combo-r.basis: R explodes again in a cone behind the champion it hits. Line up R when other enemies are lined up behind the target. Casting R knocks Graves backward. Use R's recoil to cross a wall while escaping.
