graves-combo-r.text: R (Collateral Damage) explodes again in a cone behind the champion it hits, so line it up when other enemies are behind your target. Casting it also knocks Graves backward, letting you use it to finish a target or escape over a wall.

graves-laning-gank.basis: Gank when the enemy is past the middle of the lane and an ally can lock them down. Use E to close the angle, then throw W on the enemy's escape path. W's smoke only blocks the vision of enemies inside it; it doesn't block allied vision. Use W's smoke to create an opening for allied abilities to land.
graves-laning-gank.text: Gank when the enemy has pushed past the middle of the lane and an ally can lock them down. Use E (Quickdraw) to close the angle, then throw W (Smoke Screen) onto their escape path. The smoke blocks the vision of enemies inside it without blocking allied vision, creating an opening for your ally’s abilities to land.

graves-laning-route.basis: Graves farms efficiently thanks to his fast jungle clears. At camps with plenty of walls, hit a wall with Q to clear faster. If a gank opportunity is unclear, clear camps to widen the level and gold gap.
graves-laning-route.text: Graves’s fast jungle clear makes him an efficient farmer. At camps with walls nearby, fire Q (End of the Line) into a wall to clear even faster. If a gank opportunity is uncertain, clear camps instead to build a level and gold lead.

graves-phase.basis: Graves is strong in level 2–3 fights. Learning R at level 6 gives you a finishing tool, increasing your gank success rate. Graves is vulnerable to being taken down easily if caught first in the late game. Graves reaches his peak strength in the early to mid game. Secure objectives and vision in the early to mid game to cement your lead.
graves-phase.text: Graves’s level 1 attack damage and armor are among the highest, helping him clear early camps quickly and win level 2–3 fights. R (Collateral Damage) gives him a finishing tool at level 6, improving his ganks. His short range and low magic resistance leave him vulnerable if caught first late in the game, so use his early to mid game power peak to secure objectives and vision and cement your lead.

graves-situational-antiheal.basis: Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to reduce healing. Graves concentrates his damage into a short window.
graves-situational-antiheal.text: Against opponents who survive through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Graves deals his damage in a short burst, so applying healing reduction makes a substantial difference to your chance of securing a kill.

graves-skill-e.basis: Using E toward an enemy champion grants twice as many armor stacks. Each basic attack hit reduces E's cooldown. Keep landing basic attacks so you can use E twice in one fight. Do not carelessly spend E on an early escape and lose your engage tool and armor.
graves-skill-e.text: Using E (Quickdraw) toward an enemy champion grants twice as many armor stacks, and each basic attack hit reduces its cooldown. Keep landing attacks during a fight to use E twice. Spending it carelessly on an early escape costs you both an engage tool and armor.

graves-skill-passive.basis: After using both shells in the magazine with basic attacks, you start reloading. Each basic attack fires a spread of pellets. Basic attack pellets are all blocked by the first unit they hit. Find an angle with no units between you and the target, then get close.
graves-skill-passive.text: Basic attacks use a two-shell magazine, then Graves must reload. Each shell fires a spread of pellets, all of which are blocked by the first unit they hit. You cannot hit an enemy behind a minion or ally, so approach from an angle with no units between you and your target.

graves-skill-q.basis: Q's follow-up explosion deals much more damage than its outgoing projectile. Aim Q slightly ahead or to the side so the opponent stays in the explosion area even if they dodge the projectile. At jungle camps, hit a wall with Q so the explosion covers the entire camp.
graves-skill-q.text: Q (End of the Line)’s follow-up explosion deals far more damage than the outgoing projectile. Aim slightly ahead of or beside an opponent so they remain in the explosion area even if they dodge the projectile. At jungle camps, fire Q into a wall to cover the whole camp with the explosion.

graves-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, do not initiate from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy's attention, use E to move in from the side or rear and get close to their damage dealers. Maintain a position with no units between you and the target.
graves-teamfight.text: Do not initiate teamfights from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy’s attention, use E (Quickdraw) to move in from the side or rear and get close to their damage dealers. Stay where no unit can get between you and your target; that positioning has the greatest effect on your damage.

gwen-combo-basic.basis: Stack Q with auto attacks, then use E to close in, land an empowered auto attack, and cast Q. Q has fewer snips without stacks, greatly reducing its damage. Before trading, hit even a minion to build Q stacks.
gwen-combo-basic.text: Build Q stacks with auto attacks, then close in with E, land an empowered auto attack, and cast Q. Without stacks, Q snips fewer times and deals much less damage, so hit even a minion to build stacks before trading.

gwen-combo-q-center.basis: Enemies in the center of Q's cone take some of its damage as true damage and are affected by Gwen's passive. Position so your target is in the center of Q's cone. Landing the center of Q matters more against targets with high armor and magic resistance.
gwen-combo-q-center.text: Only enemies in the center of Q’s cone take some of its damage as true damage and have Gwen’s passive applied to them. Position the target in the center rather than merely aiming Q in their direction; landing that center hit matters especially against targets with high armor and magic resistance.

gwen-combo-w-cancel.basis: Enemies outside the mist cannot target Gwen while she is inside it. Activate W as an enemy starts a targeted ability or auto attack to make it miss. W does not block turret attacks.
gwen-combo-w-cancel.text: While Gwen is inside W’s mist, enemies outside it cannot target her. Activate W just as an enemy starts a targeted ability or auto attack to make it miss, but remember that W does not block turret attacks during a dive.

gwen-combo-w-reposition.basis: Recast W to move the mist toward Gwen. If you try to leave the mist with E, W automatically recasts. Recast W yourself before leaving the mist with E to stay untargetable while moving.
gwen-combo-w-reposition.text: Recast W to draw the mist toward Gwen. If she tries to leave it with E, W recasts automatically, so move the mist yourself first to stay untargetable as you advance. When you reposition the mist determines how long W remains useful.

gwen-laning.basis: In lane, build Q stacks with auto attacks and use W to avoid the enemy's counterattack. Her damage per minute at 14 minutes ranks high, but her kill numbers tend to be low, so securing farm is important. Early on, avoid forcing an engage and focus on CS and levels.
gwen-laning.text: In lane, build Q stacks with auto attacks and use W to avoid counterattacks. Gwen ranks high in damage per minute at 14 minutes but tends to have fewer kills, so her value comes from scaling: avoid forcing early engages and focus on CS and levels.

gwen-laning-w-gank.basis: Activate W when a gank starts to avoid targeted crowd control from enemies outside the mist. Keep W available while pushing the wave so you can respond to a gank.
gwen-laning-w-gank.text: W also helps Gwen survive ganks: activating it as a gank begins can avoid targeted crowd control from enemies outside the mist. Keep it available while pushing the wave.

gwen-phase.basis: Trading is weak at levels 1–2 because Q stacks are hard to build. Once you learn W, you can avoid poke from ranged opponents. Gwen grows stronger in duels from midgame as she builds ability power items. Late game, use maximum health damage to cut down the enemy frontline directly.
gwen-phase.text: Gwen’s trades are weak at levels 1–2, before she can build Q stacks. Once she learns W, she can avoid poke from ranged opponents, and her dueling grows stronger in midgame as she builds ability power items. Late game, her maximum health damage lets her cut down the enemy frontline directly.

gwen-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing can turn a duel, buy Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Gwen can stay close and keep landing auto attacks and Q to maintain healing reduction.
gwen-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing could turn a duel, buy Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Gwen can stay close and keep landing auto attacks and Q to maintain the effect.

gwen-skill-e-range.basis: E's empowered auto attacks gain attack speed and range. Even when a ranged opponent starts backing away, try to land another attack with E's extended range.
gwen-skill-e-range.text: E’s empowered auto attacks gain both attack speed and range. After closing in on a ranged opponent, use that extra reach to land another attack even if they start backing away.

gwen-skill-e-reset.basis: The first hit with E refunds a substantial part of its cooldown. When a minion wave is present, land E to use it for both entry and escape in quick succession.
gwen-skill-e-reset.text: E refunds a substantial part of its cooldown on the first hit, even against a minion. In a wave, you can use it to engage and then escape in quick succession; in open ground with nothing to hit, the full cooldown leaves you stuck.

gwen-skill-passive.basis: Gwen's passive deals magic damage based on the target's maximum health. Her passive heals her only when it hits a champion. Gwen's sustain depends on how long she can auto attack champions. Clearing minions alone cannot heal Gwen through her passive.
gwen-skill-passive.text: Gwen’s passive deals magic damage based on the target’s maximum health and heals her only when it hits a champion. Each auto attack is worth more against a high-health frontline target, but clearing minions alone gives her no healing; her sustain depends on how long she can keep attacking champions.

gwen-skill-r.basis: R can be cast up to three times, with more needles on each cast. Hit a fleeing enemy with the first R cast to slow them and catch up. Before casting R again, check whether you can keep the enemy in range through the third cast.
gwen-skill-r.text: R can be cast up to three times, with more needles on each cast. Use the first, slowing cast to catch a fleeing enemy, then recast only if you can keep them in range long enough to land the third.

gwen-skill-r-passive.basis: R applies Gwen's passive when it hits an enemy champion. Slow the enemy with the first R cast before closing in with E.
gwen-skill-r-passive.text: When R hits an enemy champion, it applies Gwen's passive, so use the first cast from range to damage and slow them before closing in with E. It can help start an engage instead of serving only as a finisher.

gwen-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, attack the enemy frontline directly. Engage with E, use W to avoid focused attacks, then land the center of Q on the frontline. Engage when the enemy's key crowd control is down or W is ready.
gwen-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Gwen’s job is to cut down the frontline directly. Engage with E, use W to avoid focused attacks, then land Q’s true damage on the frontline with a center hit. Go in when the enemy’s key crowd control is down or W is ready.

hecarim-combo-e-r.basis: E’s remaining duration stops decreasing during R. E retains its accumulated travel distance after R ends. For maximum damage, activate E and run in, then chain R’s landing fear, the empowered E basic attack, and Q.
hecarim-combo-e-r.text: E (Devastating Charge) stops losing duration during R (Onslaught of Shadows), so you can activate E, run in, and charge with R, then land an empowered E basic attack after R ends with your accumulated travel distance intact. For maximum damage, use E → run → R → landing fear → empowered E basic attack → Q (Rampage).

hecarim-combo-gank.basis: For ganks, activate E early and run in from outside vision, then use W, Q, and the empowered E basic attack as you approach. The empowered E basic attack deals more damage based on the distance traveled after activation. The empowered E basic attack knocks the target back farther based on the distance traveled after activation. Do not attack right after activating E; loop around once to build up travel distance.
hecarim-combo-gank.text: For a gank, activate E (Devastating Charge) early, run in from outside vision, and take a wide route to build distance. As you reach the target, use W (Spirit of Dread), then Q (Rampage), then the empowered E basic attack to knock them back. Its damage and knockback distance increase with the distance traveled after activation, so circle around once instead of attacking immediately.

hecarim-combo-q-stack.basis: Q gains a stack each time it hits. Q stacks increase Q’s damage. Q stacks shorten Q’s cooldown. Hit a jungle monster with Q just before a gank or objective fight to build stacks. When you reach the fight, use your prepared, fully stacked Q twice in quick succession.
hecarim-combo-q-stack.text: Each Q (Rampage) hit adds a stack, increasing its damage and shortening its cooldown. Hit a jungle monster with Q just before a gank or objective fight to build stacks, then land two fully stacked Qs in quick succession as soon as you arrive.

hecarim-gank-angle.basis: Before level 6, look for ganks where you can get behind the enemy. Activate E outside vision and circle toward the enemy’s escape route. Use the empowered E basic attack from behind the enemy to knock them toward your allies. Avoid frontal ganks that leave little distance to travel with E.
hecarim-gank-angle.text: Before level 6, gank only when you can get behind the enemy. Activate E (Devastating Charge) outside vision, circle toward their escape route, and use the empowered basic attack to knock them toward your allies. Charging straight at them gives E too little travel distance, weakening both its damage and knockback and letting the enemy simply walk away.

hecarim-jungle-path.basis: Use Hecarim’s fast jungle clear to keep cycling through camps. Before level 6, E’s knockback is his only hard crowd control. Before level 6, focus on clearing camps and reaching level 6 instead of forcing ganks. As soon as you reach level 6, approach a lane and look for an opening to use R.
hecarim-jungle-path.text: Hecarim clears quickly, so keep cycling through camps. Before level 6, E (Devastating Charge)’s knockback is his only hard crowd control, making ganks less likely to succeed; clearing your camps and reaching level 6 is more valuable than forcing one. As soon as you hit level 6, approach a lane and look for an opening to use R (Onslaught of Shadows).

hecarim-phase.basis: After learning W, Hecarim clears the jungle faster without losing health. Hecarim reaches his first power spike at level 6 when he learns R. Hecarim’s strength peaks in the mid game once he has attack damage and ability haste. In the late game, engage from the side because it is hard to survive a frontal entry.
hecarim-phase.text: Hecarim’s early jungle clear is ordinary until Q (Rampage) gains stacks, but once he has W (Spirit of Dread), he clears faster without losing health. Level 6 and R (Onslaught of Shadows) bring his first power spike, and he peaks in the mid game with attack damage and ability haste. Late in the game, his durability falls short of a tank’s, so a frontal entry can get him killed quickly; engage from the side instead.

hecarim-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing makes it hard to finish a dive, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce healing. Buy Executioner’s Calling after completing your first core item. Sell Executioner’s Calling last if you no longer need it.
hecarim-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing keeps you from finishing a dive, buy Executioner’s Calling after your first core item to reduce that healing. If you no longer need it, sell it last.

hecarim-situational-cc.basis: Hecarim relies on movement speed for damage, making him vulnerable to crowd control that stops his movement. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after your first core item so you can remove it right after engaging.
hecarim-situational-cc.text: Hecarim’s damage depends on movement speed, so being rooted cuts his damage as well. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after your first core item to remove one immediately after engaging.

hecarim-skill-e.basis: You can pass through minions and monsters during E. Enter the lane through the minion wave with E. Adjust your position to knock the enemy in the intended direction with the empowered E basic attack.
hecarim-skill-e.text: E (Devastating Charge) lets you pass through minions and monsters. Use it to cross a lane through a wave or escape between minions, and position yourself so the empowered basic attack knocks the enemy toward your allies or toward the enemy turret, whichever you intend.

hecarim-skill-passive.basis: P converts bonus movement speed into attack damage. Start the fight when bonus movement speed takes effect. When Hecarim loses bonus movement speed, his damage drops sharply even with the same items.
hecarim-skill-passive.text: P (Warpath) converts bonus movement speed into attack damage, so the speed from E, R, Ghost, and boots all contributes to Hecarim’s damage. Start fights while that bonus speed is active; standing and fighting after it wears off sharply reduces your damage even with the same items.

hecarim-skill-q.basis: Q deals area damage around Hecarim. As a rule, use Q whenever its cooldown ends. Q deals reduced damage to minions. During fights, keep hitting monsters or minions with Q to maintain stacks.
hecarim-skill-q.text: Q (Rampage) damages enemies around Hecarim, so use it whenever it comes off cooldown. Its reduced damage to minions makes it inefficient for clearing waves, but during a fight, keep hitting something—even a monster or minion—to maintain its stacks and cooldown reduction.

hecarim-skill-r.basis: When using R, Hecarim travels only to the targeted location. R’s spectral riders always advance to the end of its range. Stop beside a nearby target with R to fear them while the spectral riders also damage enemies behind them. R’s fear duration increases with the distance charged. To extend R’s fear duration, start the charge from as far away as possible.
hecarim-skill-r.text: With R (Onslaught of Shadows), Hecarim travels only to the targeted location, while the spectral riders always continue to the end of its range. You can stop beside a nearby target to fear them and still damage enemies farther behind with the riders. Fear duration increases with the distance charged, so start from as far away as possible.

hecarim-skill-w.basis: W heals Hecarim based on damage nearby enemies take. W’s healing also counts damage allies deal to nearby enemies. Use W in the middle of a fight where allies and enemies are clustered together. W provides almost no healing when you are fleeing alone. Healing from jungle monsters during W is capped.
hecarim-skill-w.text: W (Spirit of Dread) heals Hecarim based on damage nearby enemies take, including damage dealt by allies. Activate it in the middle of a fight where allies and enemies are clustered together; it provides almost no healing when you flee alone. Healing from jungle monsters is capped, so do not rely on it solely for clearing.

hecarim-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use R from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers’ formation. Use the moment R’s fear disrupts the enemy formation as the cue for your allies to enter. After entering, stay in the middle of the fight with W active to keep healing.
hecarim-teamfight.text: In teamfights, avoid trying to push through the enemy tank; use R (Onslaught of Shadows) from the side or behind to split the damage dealers’ formation. The moment its fear disrupts the enemy team is your allies’ cue to enter. Once you engage, stay in the thick of the fight with W (Spirit of Dread) active so it can heal you.

heimerdinger-combo-basic.basis: Set up turrets where you plan to fight, hit the center of your grenade, then fire rockets while the charged turrets shoot. Auto attack the enemy you want to take down to direct your turrets' fire. Using your grenade first in a fight can instantly fully charge your turrets. Rockets converge at your cursor, and only the first hit deals full damage. Aim your cursor a little behind the enemy so they overlap the point where the rockets converge. When firing rockets, choose an angle that minions will not block.
heimerdinger-combo-basic.text: Set up turrets where the fight will happen, land E directly at its center to stun the target and fully charge the turrets, then fire W while they shoot and auto attack the enemy you want them to focus. E comes first for the instant turret charge, not its damage. W's rockets converge on your cursor, but only the first hit deals full damage, so aim a little behind the enemy to make the convergence point overlap them and choose an angle that minions cannot block.

heimerdinger-combo-r-e.basis: The empowered grenade bounces several times and has larger stun and slow areas. Throw the empowered grenade along the enemy's retreat path. Empower your grenade with your ultimate to stun the enemy, then attack with turrets and rockets. If you activate your ultimate by mistake, use it again to cancel it.
heimerdinger-combo-r-e.text: As support, usually use R to empower E: the grenade bounces several times, with larger stun and slow areas that can catch enemies the narrow direct hit would miss. After activating R, throw E along the enemy's retreat path rather than at their feet so its bounces follow them, then pour turret fire and W into the stunned target to start the teamfight. If you activate R by mistake, cast it again to cancel it.

heimerdinger-laning-mid.basis: In mid, turrets help absorb the wave, making it easier to hold the lane and farm. Cluster turrets behind the lane, then counter an enemy jungle engage with turret fire and a grenade. Heimerdinger has no mobility ability, making it hard for him to roam on his own. In mid, push the lane decisively to keep your opponent there and let your jungler gain an advantage elsewhere.
heimerdinger-laning-mid.text: In mid, turrets absorb the wave for Heimerdinger, helping him hold the lane and farm. Cluster them behind the lane and turret fire plus an E stun can punish an enemy jungler's engage, even turning a dive in your favor. His lack of mobility makes solo roams difficult, so push decisively to keep your opponent in lane and let your jungler gain an advantage elsewhere.

heimerdinger-laning-support.basis: Support Heimerdinger's turrets can push the wave. If you do not want to push, place turrets in brush outside minion range or behind the lane. To push the enemy ADC out of lane, place turrets in the lane and secure vision alongside them. Look for a direct grenade hit when the enemy steps forward to destroy a turret.
heimerdinger-laning-support.text: Support Heimerdinger's turrets can push the wave. If you do not want to push, place them outside minion range, in brush or behind the lane, so they attack enemy champions instead. To push the enemy ADC out of lane, deliberately place turrets in the lane and secure vision as you advance. An enemy stepping forward to destroy a turret gives you a good chance to land E directly.

heimerdinger-phase.basis: Levels 1–2, when Heimerdinger has only one turret, are his most dangerous period. From level 3, multiple turrets and a grenade give him control of the lane. Learning your ultimate at level 6 greatly improves your ability to start fights. Late in the game, Heimerdinger loses strength in moving skirmishes because his turrets cannot keep up. Late in the game, draw fights to a position you have chosen in advance.
heimerdinger-phase.text: Heimerdinger's health and armor are among the lowest of all champions, making levels 1–2, when he has only one turret, his most dangerous period. At level 3, multiple turrets and E give him lane control; at level 6, R greatly improves his ability to start fights. Later, his turrets cannot keep up with moving skirmishes, so draw fights to a position you have chosen in advance.

heimerdinger-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy sustains through turret damage with healing, consider Morellonomicon for Grievous Wounds. If you are short on gold as support, delay Morellonomicon until after completing one core item.
heimerdinger-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing lets them withstand your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon: turret shots deal damage gradually, and without reduced healing, that damage can be offset by their recovery. If gold is tight as support, delay it until after you complete one core item.

heimerdinger-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in all at once, include Zhonya's Hourglass in your core item order. Turrets you have already placed keep firing while Zhonya's Hourglass protects you.
heimerdinger-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy has an assassin who can dive straight onto you, fit Zhonya’s Hourglass into your core build. Heimerdinger has no mobility skill to escape once they engage, but his deployed turrets keep firing while he buys time, turning those extra moments into damage.

heimerdinger-skill-e.basis: The grenade damages and slows enemies in its area. Only enemies hit by the center of the grenade are stunned. Throw your grenade after the enemy has used their mobility ability. Layer your grenade on an ally's crowd control. If you cannot land a direct hit, predict the enemy's retreat through a narrow passage and throw your grenade there. Do not spend your grenade carelessly on wave clear; keep it available to fully charge your turrets.
heimerdinger-skill-e.text: E damages and slows enemies throughout its area, but only those hit at the center are stunned. Its unempowered direct hit area is narrow, so throw it after the enemy uses their mobility ability or over an ally's crowd control; otherwise, aim ahead toward a narrow passage on their retreat path. E also fully charges turrets, so do not spend it carelessly on wave clear.

heimerdinger-skill-passive.basis: Heimerdinger gains movement speed near allied turrets and his own turrets. Heimerdinger has no mobility ability, so he relies on the movement speed near turrets to escape. When holding a risky lane position, set up a turret on your retreat path beforehand. When defending under an allied turret, use the movement speed boost to dodge enemy engage abilities.
heimerdinger-skill-passive.text: Heimerdinger gains movement speed near allied turrets and his own. With no mobility ability, he relies on that speed to escape: when holding a risky lane position, set a turret on your retreat path beforehand, and when defending under an allied turret, use the boost to walk out of enemy engage abilities.

heimerdinger-skill-q-charge.basis: Turrets charge over time. A fully charged turret fires much more powerfully than a newly placed one. Check your turrets' charge before starting a fight. Each rocket that hits a champion charges nearby turrets a little. Hitting an enemy champion with a grenade instantly fully charges nearby turrets.
heimerdinger-skill-q-charge.text: Turrets charge slowly on their own and fire much more powerfully at full charge, so check their charge before starting a fight; a newly placed turret poses little threat. Each W rocket that hits a champion charges nearby turrets a little, while hitting an enemy champion with E fully charges them at once. Plan your engage around that charging sequence.

heimerdinger-skill-q-placement.basis: There is a limit to how many turrets you can place. Turrets far from Heimerdinger stop working after a short time. Place turrets where you plan to stand. As support, place turrets at brush entrances or river approaches for vision and poke. You can store multiple turret placement charges. Keep at least one placement charge so you can put down a turret immediately during a fight.
heimerdinger-skill-q-placement.text: Turrets have a placement limit and shut down shortly after Heimerdinger moves too far away, so place them where you intend to stand rather than throwing them ahead. As support, set them at brush entrances or river approaches instead of the middle of the lane to gain vision and poke where enemies must pass. You can store multiple placement charges; save at least one to put a turret down immediately when a fight breaks out.

heimerdinger-skill-q-priority.basis: Turrets prioritize enemies Heimerdinger has recently damaged. Turrets prioritize enemies attacking Heimerdinger. First damage the target you want your turrets to focus with an auto attack or ability. As support, if you want to target the enemy ADC, attack them first even if a tank is in front.
heimerdinger-skill-q-priority.text: Turrets prioritize enemies Heimerdinger has recently damaged or who are attacking him. Hit the target you want them to focus with an auto attack or ability first; as support, tag the enemy ADC even if a tank is standing in front. This can make a substantial difference to your turret damage.

heimerdinger-skill-r-choice.basis: A turret empowered by your ultimate does not count toward the regular turret placement limit. The empowered turret applies an area slow and is immune to crowd control. Use the empowered turret in narrow passages near objectives or when defending an allied turret. Empowered rockets deal burst damage through successive volleys. Use empowered rockets to finish off a fleeing enemy or clear an incoming wave. Abilities empowered by your ultimate cost no resources. When low on mana, you can use an empowered ability in a pinch.
heimerdinger-skill-r-choice.text: The ability you empower with R changes its role. Empowered Q creates a turret that does not count toward the placement limit, applies an area slow, and is immune to crowd control; use it to hold narrow passages near objectives or defend an allied turret. Empowered W fires successive volleys for burst damage, making it useful for finishing a fleeing enemy or clearing an incoming wave. Empowered abilities cost no resources, so you can also use one in a pinch when you are out of mana.

heimerdinger-teamfight.basis: Before a teamfight, place and charge turrets in a narrow passage near an objective or beside an allied turret. Lure enemies into your prepared turret position. Avoid moving fights in open areas where turrets struggle to contribute. When an enemy engages, stop them with a grenade stun and retreat behind your turrets. While your allies hold the position, use an empowered turret to block the route.
heimerdinger-teamfight.text: In teamfights, choose the ground before the enemy engages: place and charge turrets in a narrow passage near an objective or beside an allied turret, then draw enemies into them. Avoid moving fights in open areas where the turrets cannot contribute. If the enemy engages, interrupt them with an E stun and retreat behind your turrets; while your allies hold the position, use an R-empowered turret to block the route.

hwei-combo-poke.basis: Hit with Devastating Fire (QQ), then complete the Signature with Grim Visage (EQ). Hit with Devastating Fire (QQ), then complete the Signature with Molten Fissure (QE). You cannot attack twice in a row with spells from Subject: Disaster because they share a cooldown.
hwei-combo-poke.text: For lane poke, land Devastating Fire (QQ), then complete Signature of the Visionary with Grim Visage (EQ) or Molten Fissure (QE). Spells within Subject: Disaster share a cooldown, so two consecutive hits from that subject are impossible and the second hit must come from another subject.

hwei-combo-ult.basis: In teamfights, hit grouped enemies with R, pull them together again with Crushing Maw (EE), then finish with Molten Fissure (QE). In teamfights, hit grouped enemies with R, pull them together again with Crushing Maw (EE), then finish with Devastating Fire (QQ). While R’s slow stacks, enemies struggle to walk out of Molten Fissure’s (QE) pool.
hwei-combo-ult.text: In a teamfight, land Spiraling Despair (R) on grouped enemies, pull back anyone trying to spread out with Crushing Maw (EE), then finish with Molten Fissure (QE) or Devastating Fire (QQ). As R’s slow stacks, enemies struggle to walk out of Molten Fissure’s pool.

hwei-laning.basis: Clear waves with Molten Fissure (QE), then use Devastating Fire (QQ) to poke with the time left over. Prioritize farming over risky poke. Use a Signature combo when an enemy lines up behind minions. Mana costs are high enough that you could miss the next wave, so don’t use a subject every time its cooldown ends.
hwei-laning.text: Clear waves with Molten Fissure (QE), then use any time left over to poke with Devastating Fire (QQ). Prioritize farming over risky poke and look for a Signature of the Visionary combo when an enemy lines up behind minions. Hwei’s mana costs are high enough that wasting a subject can cost you the next wave, so avoid casting whenever a cooldown ends.

hwei-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, only one subject is available and mana is tight, so Signature poke is very weak. Signature poke becomes possible once two subjects are available. Hwei gets a major power spike at level 6 when he learns R and when he completes his first core item. At every stage, deal damage safely from behind instead of stepping forward.
hwei-phase.text: Hwei is very weak at levels 1–2: only one subject is available, leaving him without a second spell to complete Signature of the Visionary, and mana is tight. He can start poking once two subjects are available, then gains major power spikes at level 6 when he gets R and after completing his first core item. Because he is fragile and has among the lowest defensive stats, dealing damage safely from behind is more valuable at every stage than stepping forward.

hwei-situational-zhonya.basis: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against melee enemies who get close to deal damage. Hwei has virtually no mobility, making it hard to survive once caught. Using Zhonya’s Hourglass to wait out an enemy engage lets your remaining subjects come off cooldown.
hwei-situational-zhonya.text: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against melee enemies who must get close to deal damage. Hwei has virtually no mobility and is unlikely to survive being caught; Zhonya’s stasis can run down the time they have to engage while his remaining subjects come off cooldown.

hwei-skill-e.basis: Use Grim Visage (EQ) to fear the first enemy hit and stop an engage. Gaze of the Abyss (EW) leaves an eye at the target location, granting vision and rooting enemies who enter its area. Crushing Maw (EE) pulls enemies toward the target point and slows them. Place Gaze of the Abyss (EW) at river entrances or bush openings in advance for vision and protection against ganks. Under heavy jungle pressure, use Subject: Torment’s eye to guard against ganks instead of poking.
hwei-skill-e.text: Subject: Torment offers three forms of crowd control: Grim Visage (EQ) fears the first enemy hit to stop an engage, Gaze of the Abyss (EW) leaves an eye that grants vision and roots an enemy entering its area, and Crushing Maw (EE) pulls enemies toward a target point and slows them. Place the eye at a river entrance or bush opening ahead of time for vision and protection against ganks; under heavy jungle pressure, save Torment for that purpose instead of using it to poke.

hwei-skill-passive.basis: Hit an enemy champion with a spell, then hit them with a different spell to detonate the Signature. The Signature mark lasts only briefly, so follow the first hit immediately with a second spell. Land the second hit on grouped enemies to deal area damage with the Signature explosion.
hwei-skill-passive.text: Hit an enemy champion with one spell, then a different spell before the mark expires to trigger Signature of the Visionary beneath them. Follow the first hit promptly; the explosion deals area damage, so landing the second hit on grouped enemies can damage them all.

hwei-skill-q.basis: Subject: Disaster is Hwei’s main source of damage. Use Devastating Fire (QQ) to poke a single target or fight a bulky enemy. Severing Bolt (QW) can be aimed from far away, but takes time to land. Use Molten Fissure’s (QE) damage over time and slow to deny an area. The three Subject: Disaster spells share a cooldown, so choose the one you need first.
hwei-skill-q.text: Subject: Disaster is Hwei’s main source of damage. Devastating Fire (QQ) is a fast projectile that deals damage based on maximum health, making it useful for single-target poke and against bulky enemies; Severing Bolt (QW) reaches far but takes time to land, while Molten Fissure (QE) leaves a lava pool whose damage over time and slow deny an area. All three share a cooldown, so choose the spell that fits the situation before casting.

hwei-skill-q-lightning.basis: Severing Bolt (QW) deals more damage based on missing health to isolated or immobilized targets. Use Severing Bolt (QW) as a finisher right after you or an ally applies crowd control. Predict where a fleeing enemy is headed and land Severing Bolt (QW) ahead of them.
hwei-skill-q-lightning.text: Severing Bolt (QW) deals sharply increased damage based on missing health when its target is isolated or immobilized. Use it as a finisher immediately after you or an ally applies crowd control, or aim ahead of a fleeing enemy to catch them as they run.

hwei-skill-r.basis: R attaches to the first enemy champion hit, grows while stacking slows, then explodes. Land R when enemies have trouble spreading out. Attach R to the front line of grouped enemies, then follow up with Subject: Disaster.
hwei-skill-r.text: Spiraling Despair (R) attaches to the first enemy champion hit, grows while stacking slows, then ends in a large area explosion. Land it when enemies cannot easily spread out, ideally on the front line of a grouped team, and follow with Subject: Disaster.

hwei-skill-subject-system.basis: Press Q, W, or E to open that subject’s three spells, then press Q, W, or E again to cast one. The three spells in the same subject share a cooldown. Selecting a subject without casting a spell uses no resources. Select the subject you plan to use in advance to react faster.
hwei-skill-subject-system.text: Hwei’s Q, W, and E select subjects rather than cast spells: press one to open its three options, then press Q, W, or E again to cast. The three spells within a subject share a cooldown. Selecting a subject costs nothing until you cast, so choose one in advance when you can and keep the cast key ready to react faster.

hwei-skill-w.basis: Subject: Serenity is Hwei’s only way to support allies. Place Fleeting Current (WQ) along the path of allies engaging or retreating. Shield allies inside Pool of Reflection’s (WW) area. If you run low on mana midway through the laning phase, use Stirring Lights (WE) for bonus damage and mana restoration. Subject: Serenity has the longest cooldown and highest mana cost, so don’t use it out of habit.
hwei-skill-w.text: Subject: Serenity is Hwei’s only way to support allies. Fleeting Current (WQ) increases allies’ movement speed along a straight path to help them engage or retreat, while Pool of Reflection (WW) shields allies within its area. Stirring Lights (WE) adds damage to the next few hits and restores mana, making it useful when mana runs low midway through lane. Serenity has the longest cooldown and highest mana cost; using one of its spells also locks out the other two until that cooldown ends, so choose deliberately.

hwei-teamfight.basis: At the edge of your range, place Molten Fissure (QE) on the enemy’s approach to block their path. When the enemy starts an engage, use Grim Visage (EQ) to turn back the leader. Wait for an ally to catch an enemy first, then unleash Subject: Disaster. Don’t spend all of Subject: Torment on poke; keep it available to deal with enemies who reach you.
hwei-teamfight.text: In teamfights, play at the edge of Hwei’s range and place Molten Fissure (QE) across the enemy’s approach. If they begin an engage, turn back the leader with Grim Visage (EQ), then commit Subject: Disaster after an ally catches someone. Keep Subject: Torment available to deal with enemies who reach you instead of spending it all on poke.

illaoi-combo-aoe.basis: The spirit and its host can both be hit by the same area damage. Damage dealt to the spirit transfers to its host. Pull out the spirit where your allies’ area abilities can hit it.
illaoi-combo-aoe.text: The spirit and its host can both be hit by the same area ability, and damage dealt to the spirit transfers to the host. When an ally has area damage, one cast can effectively hit the host twice, so pull the spirit into a spot their ability can reach.

illaoi-combo-basic.basis: For trades, pull out the spirit with E, cast Q toward the tentacle, then use W to close in on the target. Cast Q first so the two slams overlap when W lands.
illaoi-combo-basic.text: For trades, pull out the spirit with E, cast Q toward a tentacle to start its slam, then use W to close in on the target and make every nearby tentacle strike with you. Cast Q first so two slams overlap when W lands.

illaoi-combo-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, pull out the nearest enemy’s spirit with E, use R immediately, then attack the spirit. If you use R while a spirit pulled out by E is present, the spirit also counts toward the tentacle count if hit.
illaoi-combo-teamfight.text: To start a teamfight, pull out the nearest enemy’s spirit with E, immediately use R to summon as many tentacles as possible, then start attacking the spirit. With the spirit already pulled out, a hit on it counts toward R’s tentacle count, greatly increasing the number summoned.

illaoi-laning.basis: In lane, draw the wave toward an area where you have placed tentacles. Keep the wave near a wall and cast E when the enemy steps up to last-hit. Her CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute both rank among the highest. Maintain lane pressure instead of forcing a dive.
illaoi-laning.text: In lane, draw the wave into an area where you have set up tentacles. Keep it near a wall and cast E as the enemy steps forward to last-hit. With both CS and damage per minute ranking among the highest at 14 minutes, maintaining pressure builds an advantage without forcing a dive.

illaoi-laning-tp.basis: Both active and inactive tentacles can be targeted by Teleport. Before recalling, leave a tentacle near the lane or objective you plan to return to.
illaoi-laning-tp.text: Teleport can target tentacles whether they are active or inactive. Leave one near the lane or objective you plan to return to before recalling, since its location determines how quickly you can get back to lane.

illaoi-phase.basis: At level 1, Illaoi has only one tentacle, so her trades are weak. Her laning gets stronger once she starts leveling E. Getting R at level 6 is her biggest turning point. Her damage per minute at 14 minutes ranks among the highest. Late in the game, Illaoi lacks guaranteed crowd control, so going in alone has less value and she takes a frontline role.
illaoi-phase.text: At level 1, Illaoi has only one tentacle and weak trades, but her laning grows stronger once she starts leveling E. Level 6 and R are her biggest turning point, reflected in her damage per minute ranking among the highest at 14 minutes. Later, her lack of guaranteed crowd control makes solo engages less valuable, and she shifts to a frontline role.

illaoi-skill-e-finish.basis: Damage dealt to the spirit transfers to its host, but damage dealt to the host does not transfer to the spirit. If a fleeing enemy has less health than their spirit, finish them by attacking the spirit. Land E before a fight so you can finish a fleeing enemy through their spirit.
illaoi-skill-e-finish.text: Damage dealt to the spirit transfers to its host, but damage dealt to the host does not transfer to the spirit. If a fleeing enemy has less health than their spirit, you can finish them by attacking it even after they move out of reach. That is why you should land E before starting a fight.

illaoi-skill-e-position.basis: Cast E from the side with your allied turret and tentacles. If the enemy moves in to defend the spirit, they have to fight among the tentacles. If the enemy does not move in to defend the spirit, they become a Vessel and carry tentacles with them.
illaoi-skill-e-position.text: Cast E from the side with your turret and tentacles, where it is safest. An enemy who moves in to defend the spirit must fight among the tentacles; one who stays away becomes a Vessel and carries tentacles with them. Either outcome favors Illaoi.

illaoi-skill-e-vessel.basis: A spirit pulled out by E inherits the target’s current health. To make an enemy a Vessel, lower their health before landing E.
illaoi-skill-e-vessel.text: A spirit pulled out by E inherits the target’s current health. If you want to turn the enemy into a Vessel, lower their health before landing E so you can kill the spirit quickly; against a full health target, the spirit will hold out while Illaoi wears herself down.

illaoi-skill-passive-heal.basis: When a tentacle hits an enemy champion, Illaoi heals based on her missing health. Where tentacles can reach, choose to fight back even at half health. Where tentacles cannot reach, Illaoi has virtually no way to heal.
illaoi-skill-passive-heal.text: When a tentacle hits an enemy champion, Illaoi heals in proportion to her missing health, so each slam restores more when she is low. Where tentacles can reach, fighting back at half health is better than retreating; where they cannot reach, she has virtually no way to heal.

illaoi-skill-r.basis: Use R when your allies engage or the enemy moves in. R spawns one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages. Avoid going in alone first and using R.
illaoi-skill-r.text: Use R as your allies engage or to counter an enemy’s advance, rather than to start a fight yourself. It spawns one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages, making it more valuable when enemies are grouped. If Illaoi goes in alone and uses R first, she gets fewer tentacles and is likely to be caught.

illaoi-skill-r-window.basis: After R, tentacles briefly cannot be targeted and slam faster. The brief window after R is when Illaoi deals the most damage. Have a way to keep enemies in place during R’s peak damage window.
illaoi-skill-r-window.text: After R, tentacles briefly become untargetable and slam faster. This short period is Illaoi’s peak damage window, so you need a way to keep enemies in place throughout it. If they simply spread out and walk away, R goes to waste.

illaoi-skill-tentacle-queue.basis: Give an attacking tentacle another attack command, and it will strike again right after its first attack. Use Q and W in quick succession to keep the tentacle slams going.
illaoi-skill-tentacle-queue.text: Tentacle attack commands are queued: command a tentacle that is already slamming, and it will strike again as soon as the first attack ends. Use Q and W in quick succession, overlapping the commands to produce consecutive slams without wasting either one.

irelia-combo-engage.basis: Place the first E behind the opponent, stun them with the second E, then follow up with a Q dash, a basic attack, and W. The mark left on a champion hit by E resets Q's cooldown. You can use Q twice before E's stun wears off.
irelia-combo-engage.text: For an engage, place the first E behind your opponent, stun them with the second E, then dash in with Q, land a basic attack, and use W. E marks champions it hits and resets Q’s cooldown, letting you use Q twice before the stun ends.

irelia-combo-farm.basis: Killing a low-health minion with Q resets Q's cooldown. Repeatedly resetting Q by killing minions lets you dash through them in a chain. Check the wave's position before using chained Q dashes to engage or escape.
irelia-combo-farm.text: Finishing a low-health minion with Q resets its cooldown, letting Irelia chain dashes through the wave. Those dashes are her way in and out, so check the wave’s position before engaging or escaping.

irelia-laning-melee.basis: Build passive stacks before trading with a melee opponent. Against melee opponents, repeat short trades where you engage and back off. Save E to interrupt a melee opponent's counterattack or escape.
irelia-laning-melee.text: Against melee opponents, build Ionian Fervor stacks before trading, then repeatedly go in for short trades and back off. Save E to interrupt their counterattack or escape rather than using it for damage.

irelia-laning-q-reserve.basis: Using Q carelessly on minions leaves you without an escape when the opponent approaches. Use Q only on minions you can kill to keep resetting its cooldown. Do not engage by using Q first on an unmarked opponent.
irelia-laning-q-reserve.text: Using Q carelessly on minions leaves you with no escape when an opponent closes in. Use it only to finish minions so its cooldown keeps resetting, and never open an engage by using Q on an unmarked opponent.

irelia-laning-ranged.basis: Irelia has trouble finding chances to trade against ranged opponents. Against ranged opponents, use chained Q dashes to secure CS safely and keep up in growth. After you waste E trying to force an approach against a ranged opponent, you become vulnerable to ganks.
irelia-laning-ranged.text: Against ranged opponents, chances to trade are hard to find. Use chained Q dashes to secure CS safely and keep pace in growth; forcing an approach and wasting E leaves you open to a gank immediately afterward.

irelia-phase.basis: Irelia is weak in level 1 trades. Once Irelia has her abilities at level 3, she starts winning short trades. Irelia reaches her first major power spike at level 6, when she gets R. After level 6, Irelia grows stronger as she gets items. Avoid repeated risky engages so you do not fall behind.
irelia-phase.text: Irelia is weak in level 1 trades but starts winning short trades at level 3, once she has her abilities. Her first major power spike comes with R at level 6, and she grows stronger with items after that. She also has one of the highest death rates, so repeated reckless engages can erase that growth.

irelia-situational-cc.basis: Against a team that locks you down and kills you immediately after you engage, before you can use W, get Quicksilver Sash. Irelia relies on continuing to basic attack after she closes the gap. Irelia is vulnerable to roots that stop her from continuing her basic attacks.
irelia-situational-cc.text: Buy Quicksilver Sash against a team that locks you down and kills you immediately after you engage, before you can activate W. Irelia needs to keep landing basic attacks once she closes the gap, and a single root can ruin the entire fight for her.

irelia-skill-e-placement.basis: E's two blades fly toward each other, stunning enemies between them. Place the first E behind the opponent or along their escape route to account for their movement. If you do not recast E, it fires automatically from Irelia's position after a short delay. Adjust Irelia's position so the automatic E cast does not go to waste.
irelia-skill-e-placement.text: E sends two blades toward each other, stunning enemies caught between them. Placement is everything: put the first blade behind your opponent or on their escape route to catch them whichever way they move. If you do not recast E, the second blade fires automatically from Irelia’s position after a short delay, so poor positioning can waste it.

irelia-skill-mark-vision.basis: Hitting a champion or large monster marked by E or R with Q resets Q's cooldown. Use Q repeatedly on a marked target to stay on them. Using marks in the jungle speeds up your clear.
irelia-skill-mark-vision.text: Hitting a champion or large monster marked by E or R with Q resets Q’s cooldown. Chain Q onto a marked opponent to stay on them, and use marks on large monsters to speed up your jungle clear.

irelia-skill-passive.basis: Attack speed increases as passive stacks build. At maximum passive stacks, basic attacks deal bonus damage. Attacking a champion, structure, or large monster refreshes the passive's duration. Hit minions with abilities just before a fight to build passive stacks.
irelia-skill-passive.text: Ionian Fervor grants more attack speed as its stacks build, and at maximum stacks Irelia’s basic attacks deal bonus damage. Attacking a champion, structure, or large monster refreshes its duration, so build stacks by hitting minions with abilities just before a fight; going in stacked can change the outcome of a 1v1.

irelia-skill-r.basis: R traps the first champion it hits inside a blade wall. An opponent who crosses R's blade wall takes damage and is heavily slowed. An opponent can Flash out of R's blade wall. Aim R to block the opponent's escape route. Place R so its blade wall opens toward your allies, letting them catch the trapped target.
irelia-skill-r.text: R traps the first champion it hits inside a blade wall. To leave, the target must cross it and take damage and a heavy slow, or use Flash. Aim it across the escape route, with the wall opening toward your allies so they can catch the trapped target.

irelia-skill-w.basis: You cannot move while charging W. You take reduced damage while charging W. Save W instead of using it early for damage. Use W as an enemy assassin engages or a gank arrives. From mid game onward, bait out the opponent's abilities before using W.
irelia-skill-w.text: Irelia cannot move while charging W, but takes reduced damage. Save it for the moment an enemy assassin dives in or a gank arrives instead of spending it early for damage. From mid game onward, try to bait out your opponent’s abilities before activating it.

irelia-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use R to split the enemy formation. Stun a target trapped by R with E, then chain Q dashes into the backline. To survive teamfights, engage after your allies land crowd control.
irelia-teamfight.text: Start a teamfight by using R to split the enemy formation, stun a trapped target with E, then chain Q dashes into the backline. Irelia is a priority target for the enemy team, so wait for your allies’ crowd control to land before going in if you want to survive.

ivern-combo-daisy.basis: Summon Daisy!, command her to attack, then use E on her. You can cast E on Daisy! as well as allies. Use E on Daisy! in the middle of the enemy team to slow multiple enemies. Keep Daisy! attacking the same target so her third attack knocks them up.
ivern-combo-daisy.text: Summon Daisy!, command her to attack, then put E on her. E works on Daisy! as well as allies, turning her into an area slow when she stands in the middle of the enemy team. Keep her attacking the same target so her third hit knocks them up.

ivern-combo-e-timing.basis: E explodes after a short delay, not immediately when applied. Use E a little early so it explodes as Q's root ends. If E's slow takes hold as the root ends, the enemy has no opening to escape.
ivern-combo-e-timing.text: E explodes after a short delay, so apply it early enough for the explosion to coincide with the end of Q’s root. The slow then takes over as the root ends, leaving the enemy no opening to escape.

ivern-combo-gank.basis: After landing Q, use E on an ally as they close in, then recast Q to engage if needed. An ally who attacks an enemy rooted by Q automatically dashes into attack range. Use Q once your ally is ready to close in.
ivern-combo-gank.text: For a gank, land Q (Rootcaller), cast E (Triggerseed) on an ally as they close in, and recast Q to follow if needed. An ally who attacks the rooted target automatically dashes into range, so Rootcaller is your ally’s way in rather than a source of damage for Ivern. Wait until your ally is ready before casting Q, or the root duration will go to waste.

ivern-jungle-route.basis: Plant a seed at a camp, try to gank a lane, then return to harvest it. Spend more time showing up in lanes.
ivern-jungle-route.text: Monsters do not attack Ivern, so clearing the jungle does not cost him health. Plant seeds at camps, head straight to a lane to try a gank, then return to harvest once the seeds have grown. His pathing should overlap camp growth with lane visits: Ivern grows by spending more time showing up in lanes rather than lingering in the jungle.

ivern-jungle-vision.basis: Ivern is very weak in a 1v1. Avoid routes where you might meet the enemy jungler. Secure vision first and path toward your allies. Help all three allied lanes in turn instead of counterjungling.
ivern-jungle-vision.text: Ivern is very weak in a 1v1, so avoid routes where you might meet the enemy jungler. Secure vision first and path toward your allies; rotating among all three allied lanes is more valuable than counterjungling.

ivern-phase.basis: Ivern can gank with Q from level 2 or 3, giving him early gank pressure. Getting Daisy! at level 6 greatly increases Ivern's control over fights. In the mid and late game, keep your allied carry alive and stop enemy engages. Ivern relies on his allies' damage, so he has less to do if they fall behind.
ivern-phase.text: Ivern can gank with Q as early as level 2 or 3. Daisy! gives him much more control over fights at level 6, while his role in the mid and late game is to protect his allied carry and stop enemy engages. He depends on his allies’ damage, so if they fall behind, he has little he can do.

ivern-skill-e.basis: If E does not hit an enemy, the shield refreshes. Put E on your allied carry before the fight starts.
ivern-skill-e.text: If E (Triggerseed) does not hit an enemy, its shield refreshes, so there is no downside to putting it on your allied carry before a fight when it is safe to do so. Recasting it over an existing shield is wasteful, though; look for the moment your ally is about to start taking damage.

ivern-skill-passive-jungle.basis: Ivern does not fight monsters other than epic monsters. Plant a grove at a camp, then harvest it when fully grown for gold and experience. Planting a grove at a camp costs health and mana. Plant groves at several camps in advance, then make a circuit to harvest them. Groves grow faster as Ivern levels up.
ivern-skill-passive-jungle.text: Ivern does not fight monsters other than epic monsters. Instead, he plants a grove at a camp and harvests it once it has grown for gold and experience. Planting costs health and mana, and growing takes time, so plant at several camps ahead of time and make a circuit to harvest them. Groves grow faster as Ivern levels up.

ivern-skill-passive-smite.basis: Using Smite on a growing grove frees the camp immediately. If it is nearly time to take Dragon or Rift Herald, save Smite instead of using it on a camp. Ivern can attack epic monsters directly. In objective fights, deal damage with basic attacks and Daisy!.
ivern-skill-passive-smite.text: Smite immediately frees a camp with a growing grove, speeding up Ivern’s jungle clear. Save it when Dragon or Rift Herald is coming up, though, since you also need Smite for objectives. Ivern can attack epic monsters directly, so use basic attacks and Daisy! to damage them during objective fights.

ivern-skill-q.basis: Q has long range, but it is a skillshot that can hit only one target. Hitting a monster with Q halves its cooldown. While moving or escaping, hit a nearby camp monster with Q to prepare for the next gank. Do not waste Q on a monster right before a fight.
ivern-skill-q.text: Q has long range but is a skillshot that hits only one target, and it is Ivern’s way to start a fight. Hitting a monster with it halves its cooldown, so landing Q on a nearby camp monster while moving or escaping can have it ready for the next gank. Do not spend it on a monster right before a fight.

ivern-skill-r.basis: Daisy! can take non-targeted abilities for allies. Position Daisy! between your allied carry and an incoming enemy engage. Daisy!'s third consecutive hit on the same target knocks them up. When aiming for Daisy!'s knockup, do not keep switching her target.
ivern-skill-r.text: Daisy! can block non-targeted abilities for your allies, so position her between your carry and an incoming enemy engage. Her third consecutive hit on the same target knocks them up; keep her focused on that target rather than repeatedly changing her orders.

ivern-skill-w.basis: Brush created by W blocks vision and creates ambush spots. Brush created by W adds damage to the basic attacks of Ivern inside it and nearby allies. If your team loses vision inside the brush, it disappears. Keep vision inside ambush brush with a ward or an ally's position. Just before a teamfight, create brush under your allies for stronger basic attacks and a vision advantage.
ivern-skill-w.text: Brush created by W blocks vision, creates ambush spots, and adds damage to the basic attacks of Ivern inside it and nearby allies. It disappears if your team loses vision inside it, so maintain vision with a ward or an ally’s position when setting an ambush. Placing brush under your allies just before a teamfight gives them stronger basic attacks and a vision advantage.

ivern-teamfight.basis: Start teamfights from the back. Catch an enemy with Q so your allies can attack them. Use E the moment an enemy engage reaches your allied carry. Use Daisy! as a wall in front of your allied carry. If the enemy formation has already broken, place Daisy! in their escape path to look for a knockup. If Ivern stands in front and dies, his shield and Daisy! disappear together.
ivern-teamfight.text: Start teamfights from the back, catching one enemy with Q for your allies to attack and using E the moment an enemy engage reaches your carry. Keep Daisy! in front of the carry as a wall; if the enemy formation has already broken, place her in their escape path to seek a knockup. If Ivern stands in front and dies, his shield and Daisy! disappear with him.

janna-combo-q-brush.basis: When aiming for a fully charged Q, hide the tornado behind a wall or in a bush as it charges. Launch Q the moment an enemy enters the tornado's path. Follow up an ally's immobilizing crowd control with Q. Enemies can hear Q charging and back away.
janna-combo-q-brush.text: To land a fully charged Q, hide the tornado behind a wall or in a bush while it charges, then launch it the moment an enemy enters its path. You can also follow an ally’s immobilizing crowd control with Q for a guaranteed hit. The charge makes a sound, though, so account for enemies hearing it and backing away.

janna-combo-r-timing.basis: Use R to interrupt an enemy's engage the moment it reaches an ally. Use R to interrupt an enemy's channeled ultimate as soon as it starts. Use R just before an ally is caught and killed. You can Flash into the middle of the enemy formation, then use R to split their front and back lines. If you Flash in and use R, Janna remains in the enemy formation.
janna-combo-r-timing.text: R can turn a fight by interrupting the enemy’s engage as it reaches an ally, a channeled ultimate as it begins, or an attempt to kill an ally just before it succeeds. You can Flash into the middle of the enemy formation and use R to separate their front and back lines, but Janna will be left among them.

janna-laning.basis: If the enemy support walks in, knock them up immediately with Q, then slow them with W. To conserve mana, avoid using Q and W to clear minions or for pointless poke. Save Q for a tower dive, then launch it immediately when the enemy goes in.
janna-laning.text: Janna’s goal in lane is to stop enemy engages, not secure kills. When the opposing support walks in, fire Q immediately to knock them up, then slow them with W to end the trade. Because these abilities cost a lot of mana, avoid using them to clear minions or for pointless poke; save them for moments when your carry is actually at risk of being hit. The same applies to turret dives: hold Q until the enemy goes in, then fire it immediately to disrupt the entire dive.

janna-phase.basis: Janna has very little kill pressure in the early laning phase. Janna is very good at surviving the laning phase. At level 6, learning R makes Janna stronger because she can stop enemy engages. From the mid game, as support items build up, her shields and healing become more valuable. In the late game, she can change the outcome of a teamfight by keeping her allied carry alive longer.
janna-phase.text: Janna has little kill pressure in early lane, but she is among the best supports at staying alive. Learning R at level 6 gives her the power to shut down an enemy engage, while support items make her shields and healing more valuable from the mid game onward. Late in the game, keeping an allied carry alive longer can change the outcome of a teamfight.

janna-roaming.basis: W's passive and ghosting let Janna roam quickly without getting blocked by minions. Roam away from lane only when the wave has been pushed safely or your ADC has recalled. Place vision around mid or jungle entrances to spot enemy ganks early.
janna-roaming.text: W’s passive movement speed and ghosting let Janna roam quickly without getting caught on minions. Her greatest value, though, comes from stopping engages beside her ADC, so leave lane only when the wave is safely pushed or your ADC has recalled. Otherwise, spend that time placing vision near mid or jungle entrances to spot ganks early.

janna-situational-cleanse.basis: If the enemy's plan is to lock down and kill your allied carry, buy Mikael's Blessing early. E's shield cannot remove crowd control that has already landed.
janna-situational-cleanse.text: If the enemy is locking down and killing your allied carry, buy Mikael’s Blessing earlier. E’s shield cannot remove crowd control that has already landed, so when being locked down is what gets your carry killed, the cleanse takes priority over the shield.

janna-skill-e.basis: E grants its target a shield and attack damage. Cast E as damage is about to land. Disrupting an enemy champion's movement with Q or W reduces E's cooldown.
janna-skill-e.text: E (Eye Of The Storm) grants a shield and attack damage, so cast it as damage is about to land; using it early only wastes its duration. Each time Janna hinders an enemy champion’s movement with an ability, E’s cooldown is reduced, meaning that landing Q or W on a champion helps her shield more often. Her defense depends on successful harassment.

janna-skill-e-turret.basis: You can cast E on an allied turret. When enemies attack or dive an allied turret, cast E on it to help it survive longer.
janna-skill-e-turret.text: E can also shield an allied turret. If enemies are diving or pushing it, the shield can let it withstand a few more hits. Remember this option when responding to a dive, alongside shielding your carry.

janna-skill-passive.basis: P increases an ally's movement speed when they move toward Janna. When retreating, stay ahead of your allies in the direction of retreat. When chasing, move ahead so your allies can follow you.
janna-skill-passive.text: P Tailwind speeds up allies moving toward Janna. Stay ahead of them in the direction of retreat so they can escape faster, and move ahead when chasing so they can catch up. Janna’s position itself provides this utility.

janna-skill-q-charge.basis: Q charges where it is cast and launches when recast. The longer Q charges, the greater its range, damage, and knockup duration. Launch Q immediately to stop an enemy engage. Only charge Q when the enemy is out of vision.
janna-skill-q-charge.text: Q Howling Gale grows where Janna casts it and launches when recast. A longer charge increases its range, damage, and knockup duration, but Janna can do nothing while it charges, and enemies who see the tornado can walk out of its path. Fire it immediately to stop an engage; charge it only when the enemy is out of vision.

janna-skill-r.basis: R heals nearby allies throughout its duration. R ends immediately if Janna moves or uses an ability. If you need R's healing, stand still after casting it. If you need to escape after the knockback, give up R's healing and move immediately. R's knockback cannot push enemies over walls.
janna-skill-r.text: R Monsoon immediately knocks enemies back, then heals nearby allies for its duration. Moving or using an ability ends it at once, so stand still after casting if you need the healing. If you only need the knockback to escape, move immediately and give up the healing. The knockback cannot push enemies over walls.

janna-skill-w.basis: W's passive grants movement speed and ghosting. W's ghosting lets you pass through minions. Using W while you have bonus movement speed increases its poke damage.
janna-skill-w.text: W Zephyr passively grants movement speed and ghosting, letting Janna pass through minions and choose her angle freely. When used, W deals more damage with additional movement speed, so poke with it while you have a movement speed bonus.

janna-teamfight.basis: Stay beside your allied carry instead of standing in front of an enemy looking for an engage. As the enemy engages, push them back with Q or R. Against a dive-focused enemy composition, save R to stop their engage. If the enemy composition struggles to engage, use E and W to give your allied carry more time to attack.
janna-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Janna stops the enemy’s engage. Stay beside your allied carry instead of standing in front of an enemy looking for an opening, then push the enemy back with Q or R as they go in. Against a dive focused composition, save R to stop the engage; if the enemy struggles to engage, use E and W to give your carry more time to deal damage.

jarvan-combo-eq.basis: Place your flag with E, then immediately use Q to dash toward it and knock up enemies along the path. Press E and Q almost simultaneously so the enemy cannot leave the flag's range. Place the flag beyond the enemy to dash past them and block their path. Place the flag between the enemy and your allies to drive the enemy toward your team.
jarvan-combo-eq.text: Everything starts with EQ: place E (Demacian Standard), then immediately use Q (Dragon Strike) to dash toward the flag and knock up enemies in your path. Press the abilities almost simultaneously so your target cannot walk away while the flag lands. Placing it beyond the target lets Jarvan IV dash past and block their path; placing it between the target and your allies drives them toward your team.

jarvan-combo-eq-flash.basis: Flash after the EQ dash begins to change where you land and knock up an enemy beyond its normal range. Save EQ Flash for a target you absolutely need to interrupt.
jarvan-combo-eq-flash.text: Flash after the EQ dash begins to shift its endpoint and knock up a target beyond its normal range. Because enemies may judge the distance by the flag's position, save EQ Flash for a target you must interrupt.

jarvan-combo-full.basis: After knocking them up with EQ, land an auto attack as soon as you land, trap them with R, then use W. Weave an auto attack between abilities so you do not miss the bonus damage from Martial Cadence.
jarvan-combo-full.text: For the full combo, knock the target up with EQ, auto attack as soon as you land to apply Martial Cadence’s bonus damage, trap them with R Cataclysm, then use W Golden Aegis for a shield and slow. Always weave in that auto attack between abilities, or you lose the passive damage.

jarvan-laning-gank.basis: When ganking, get close enough to put the enemy within EQ range. Gank after your ally's lane has been pushed in. Before ganking, check whether the enemy has used their mobility ability. Place your flag in advance, then use only Q when the enemy approaches.
jarvan-laning-gank.text: A gank starts with getting the enemy into EQ range. If your ally's lane is pushed toward the enemy turret, wait until it comes back before entering, and check whether the target has used their mobility ability. Placing your flag ahead of time and using only Q as the enemy approaches is harder to predict and more likely to succeed.

jarvan-phase.basis: You can gank from level 2, once you have EQ. Early jungle clear speed and damage per minute are average. Early on, gain an advantage through early ganks and objective pressure. At level 6, R lets you catch out one enemy. Jarvan IV is strongest through the mid game, as his items come together. In the late game, contribute through engages and trapping enemies more than damage.
jarvan-phase.text: Jarvan IV can gank from level 2, once he has EQ. His early clear speed and damage per minute are average, so farming camps alone is not enough; look for early ganks and objective pressure to build an advantage. At level 6, R lets him catch out a target, and he is strongest through the mid game as his items come together. Later, his value comes more from engaging and trapping enemies than from damage.

jarvan-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Trapping an enemy with R lets you stay close and fight, making it easier to maintain Grievous Wounds.
jarvan-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Trapping a target with R lets Jarvan IV stay close and fight long enough to maintain the healing reduction.

jarvan-skill-e-aura.basis: E grants attack speed through its passive effect even when you do not use it. Placing a flag also increases nearby allied champions' attack speed. When attacking an objective, place a flag beside it. When no fight is underway, place your flag outside enemy vision so you do not reveal your angle of approach.
jarvan-skill-e-aura.text: E grants attack speed passively even when unused, and placing its flag increases nearby allied champions' attack speed too. Put a flag beside an objective when you start attacking it; outside fights, place it beyond enemy vision so it does not reveal your angle of approach.

jarvan-skill-passive.basis: Martial Cadence deals bonus damage based on current health to the same target once every set period. An auto attack with Martial Cadence hits hardest against a full-health enemy. Land your first auto attack of the trade on the enemy champion. Time your auto attacks around when Martial Cadence can trigger again.
jarvan-skill-passive.text: Martial Cadence deals bonus damage based on the target's current health and can trigger on the same target only once every set period. It hits hardest when the enemy is at full health, so make your first auto attack in a trade against the champion and time later attacks around when the passive can trigger again.

jarvan-skill-q-unstoppable.basis: The Q dash toward your flag still works while slowed or rooted. Before entering a dangerous area, leave a flag in your escape direction.
jarvan-skill-q-unstoppable.text: The Q dash toward a flag still works while slowed or rooted, so you can escape as long as the flag remains. Before entering a dangerous area, leave one in the direction you may need to flee.

jarvan-skill-q-wall.basis: Throw a flag over a thin wall and dash to it with Q to cross the wall. Before a fight, identify walls you can cross with EQ. In the jungle, use EQ to cross walls between camps and shorten travel time.
jarvan-skill-q-wall.text: Throw a flag over a thin wall and dash to it with Q to cross the terrain. This gives you another way in or out, so identify walls you can cross before a fight; in the jungle, use the same move to cut between camps and save time.

jarvan-skill-r-cage.basis: The wall created by Cataclysm also blocks your allies' movement. Check where you will land before using R so you do not trap your allied damage dealers. If needed, recast R to bring down the wall immediately. Use R's wall to cut off an enemy chasing an ally.
jarvan-skill-r-cage.text: Cataclysm's wall blocks allies as well as enemies, so check where you will land before using R to avoid trapping your own damage dealers. Recast R to bring the wall down immediately if needed, or use it defensively to cut off an enemy chasing an ally.

jarvan-skill-w.basis: Golden Aegis absorbs more damage for each enemy champion it hits. Use W after entering a group of enemies instead of activating it early when you are alone. Use W's slow to limit an enemy's escape route or delay their approach.
jarvan-skill-w.text: Golden Aegis absorbs more damage for each enemy champion it hits, so use W after entering a group instead of activating it early while alone. Its slow is more useful for limiting an enemy's escape route or delaying their approach than simply finishing a combo.

jarvan-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, trap one enemy backline damage dealer with R. Use R where your allies can follow up immediately. If an ally is engaged on first, use R to stop the enemy engager.
jarvan-teamfight.text: In teamfights, use R to isolate an enemy backline damage dealer, but trap them only where your allies can follow up immediately; fighting alone inside the wall can get you killed. If the enemy engages on your team first, use R to stop their engager instead.

jarvan-teamfight-object.basis: In objective fights, place your flag in advance to increase your allies' attack speed. In objective fights, save EQ for the enemy's approach route.
jarvan-teamfight-object.text: In objective fights, place E Demacian Standard in advance to boost your allies’ attack speed, and save EQ for the enemy’s approach. Coordinate the engage with your team: if Jarvan IV goes in first, the enemy may steal the objective.

jax-combo-trade.basis: For short trades, use basic attack → W → basic attack. W resets your basic attack timer. Press W before the basic attack animation finishes to cancel it. Hit minions before trading to stack your passive. After activating R, time W with the bonus damage from consecutive attacks to concentrate your burst damage.
jax-combo-trade.text: For short trades, use basic attack → W → basic attack. W Empower resets your basic attack timer, so press it before the attack animation finishes to fit in another hit. Stack P Relentless Assault on minions before trading, then, after activating R, time W with the bonus damage from consecutive attacks for a burst.

jax-laning.basis: Aim to get through the laning phase without falling behind. Start trades with passive stacks already built up. When E is on cooldown, farm from outside the opponent's range. Position yourself between the opponent and their turret first to make E and Q easier to land. If you need a safe recall window, use E's recast area damage to push the wave into the enemy turret.
jax-laning.text: Aim to get through lane without falling behind. Start trades with P Relentless Assault stacks already built, and when E Counter Strike is on cooldown, farm only from outside the opponent’s range. Move behind the opponent so they must pass Jax to return to their turret; that position makes E and Q more likely to connect. E’s recast also deals area damage, so save it to push a wave into the enemy turret and create a safe recall window.

jax-phase.basis: Jax is strong in level 1 melee slugfests. Jax is weakest at levels 2–5 because he lacks poke, farming abilities, and sustain. Jax gets a sharp power spike at level 6 when he learns R. Jax gets a sharp power spike when he completes his first core item.
