Late game, with passive stacks and items built up, Jax excels in head-on fights against champions who rely on basic attacks. As the game goes on, Jax lacks damage against tanks who build both health and armor.
jax-phase.text: Jax is strong in level 1 melee trades but weakest at levels 2–5, before he has his full set of abilities, because he lacks poke, a farming ability, and sustain. His fighting power rises sharply when he unlocks R at level 6 and when he completes his first core item. Late in the game, passive attack speed stacks combined with items let him dominate head-on fights against champions who rely on basic attacks, though his damage increasingly falls short against tanks building both health and armor.

jax-situational-item.basis: Choose situational items based on how you are dying. If an enemy auto attack carry is doing well, use Frozen Heart to reduce their attack speed and help you trade blows after E ends. If magic burst kills you before you can act, use Banshee's Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team composition that kills you as soon as you are crowd controlled, use Sterak's Gage to survive.
jax-situational-item.text: Choose situational items based on how you are dying. If an enemy basic attack carry is doing well, Frozen Heart reduces their attack speed and can turn the fight after E Counter Strike ends. If magic burst kills you before you can act, use Banshee’s Veil to block the opening ability; against a composition that kills you as soon as you are crowd controlled, take Sterak’s Gage to survive.

jax-skill-e-core.basis: E dodges all basic attacks except turret attacks for its duration. E's recast damage increases in proportion to the number of attacks dodged. Activate E just as the opponent starts their auto attack animation. E also dodges bonus damage and crowd control carried by basic attacks. You can choose when to recast E. Approach with E active, feint a retreat, then immediately jump in with Q or Flash to reduce the opponent's reaction time. During a gank, activate E immediately when two enemies attack you at once.
jax-skill-e-core.text: E Counter Strike is a defining part of Jax’s skill ceiling: while active, it dodges every basic attack except turret attacks, and its recast deals more damage for each attack dodged. Activate it as the opponent starts an attack animation to avoid both the attack and any bonus damage or crowd control carried by it. Choosing when to recast E is central to the mind game: approach with E active, click back as if retreating, then immediately close in with Q or Flash to leave little time to react. If two enemies attack you at once during a gank, activate E immediately.

jax-skill-e-limit.basis: E's dodge only applies to basic attacks. Of ability damage, E only partially reduces area-of-effect ability damage. Against opponents who mainly deal magic damage with abilities, do not assume E will let you withstand their damage. Against opponents who mainly deal magic damage with abilities, activate R as you enter combat to gain armor and magic resistance. Use E to negate the opponent's key basic attacks or crowd control carried by basic attacks.
jax-skill-e-limit.text: E Counter Strike dodges basic attacks but reduces ability damage only slightly, and only when it comes from area-of-effect abilities. Against opponents who deal mainly magic damage through abilities, activate R Grandmaster-at-Arms as you enter combat for its armor and magic resistance instead of relying on E to survive. Save E for key basic attacks or crowd control carried by them.

jax-skill-e-vs-melee.basis: Jax has the advantage in level 1 trades against melee opponents. E dodges enemy and minion basic attacks, the main sources of damage in level 1 trades. Use the health advantage gained from a level 1 trade against a melee opponent to get through the rest of the laning phase.
jax-skill-e-vs-melee.text: Jax has the advantage in level 1 trades against melee opponents. With only one ability available to each side, basic attacks and minion aggro account for most of the damage; E Counter Strike lets him dodge those attacks while adding increased recast damage and a stun. Use the health lead from this strong window to get through the weaker laning phase that follows.

jax-skill-e-vs-ranged.basis: Against ranged opponents, save E for an all-in you can reliably win or for responding to a gank instead of spending it on a single poke. After using E against a ranged opponent, stay outside their range until its cooldown ends, even if you have to give up CS. Against ranged opponents, look for opportunities to engage with Q. When engaging a ranged opponent, activate E just before Q so the stun follows your landing.
jax-skill-e-vs-ranged.text: Against ranged opponents, save E Counter Strike for an all-in you can reliably win or to respond to a gank instead of using it against a single poke. With E on cooldown, Jax has no defensive tool, so stay outside the opponent’s range until it is ready, even if that means giving up CS. Look for an angle to engage with Q Leap Strike, activating E just before the leap so the stun follows your landing.

jax-skill-q.basis: Use Q primarily to engage and disengage rather than to deal damage. Q targets units and can also be used on minions and wards. Use a pre-placed ward as an escape route with Q. Against melee opponents, start trades by moving into range and save Q to chase or disengage. When the opponent advances away from their turret, use Q to land on their retreat path.
jax-skill-q.text: Use Q Leap Strike to engage or escape rather than primarily for damage. Its long range and unit targeting let you jump to minions and wards, so a ward placed in advance can create both an escape route and an approach angle. Against melee opponents, move into range to start a trade and save Q to chase or disengage. If an opponent moves forward away from their turret, Q can put Jax on their retreat path and make escape difficult.

jax-skill-r.basis: R's passive deals bonus magic damage on every third consecutive attack. Keep attacking without breaking your auto attack rhythm to make use of R's bonus damage. R's active grants more armor and magic resistance based on the number of champions hit. Use R from a position where it can hit multiple enemy champions. Both W and R have AP ratios. W and R's AP ratios let Jax make efficient use of items that grant both attack damage and ability power.
jax-skill-r.text: R Grandmaster-at-Arms passively adds magic damage to every third consecutive attack, so keep attacking without breaking your basic attack rhythm. Its active grants more armor and magic resistance for each champion hit; activate it where several enemies are grouped to get the most from it. Both W Empower and R have AP ratios, allowing Jax to make full use of items that grant both attack damage and ability power.

jax-teamfight.basis: Use Q to jump into grouped enemies and stun several of them with E. When entering a teamfight, activate E before leaping with Q. To survive, go in second, following an ally's crowd control or engage. If there is no reason to start a teamfight, push side-lane turrets to draw enemy defenders.
jax-teamfight.text: Jax’s main contribution to a teamfight is the area stun from E Counter Strike. Activate E before using Q Leap Strike to jump into grouped enemies and stun several at once. Because he lacks sustain and defensive stats, enter second, following an ally’s crowd control or engage. When there is no reason to start a teamfight, pushing side-lane turrets can draw enemy defenders away.

jayce-combo-allin.basis: After landing cannon Q, use R to switch to hammer, then attack with Q leap, a basic attack, W Lightning Field, and E knockback, in that order. Your first basic attack right after switching to hammer deals bonus magic damage. Basic attack immediately after switching to hammer.
jayce-combo-allin.text: Land Q Shock Blast in cannon form, switch to hammer with R, then leap in with Q To the Skies! and follow with a basic attack, W Lightning Field, and E Thundering Blow to knock the target back, in that order. The first basic attack after switching to hammer deals bonus magic damage, so land it immediately after the switch.

jayce-combo-e-knockback.basis: Hammer E knocks the opponent back. To keep chasing, knock the opponent toward your allies or a wall. Angle E so you don’t knock the opponent out of your range and interrupt your combo. Use hammer E to push out an opponent who dives under your turret or to peel off an enemy engaging on you.
jayce-combo-e-knockback.text: Hammer E Thundering Blow knocks opponents back, so aim it carefully. Pushing someone toward your allies or a wall lets you keep chasing, while a careless knockback can send them out of your range and break your combo. It is most useful for pushing an opponent out from under your turret or peeling away an enemy who engages on you.

jayce-combo-gate-poke.basis: In cannon form, place E Acceleration Gate and fire Q Shock Blast through it. Q gains range, movement speed, and damage when it passes through the gate. Minimize the delay between E and Q so it hits before the opponent sees the gate and dodges.
jayce-combo-gate-poke.text: In cannon form, place E Acceleration Gate and fire Q Shock Blast through it. Passing through the gate increases the blast’s range, speed, and damage, letting it reach the opponent before they can react. Place the gate and fire Q with as little delay as possible, since placing it early gives the opponent time to sidestep.

jayce-combo-shred.basis: Your first basic attack after switching from hammer to cannon lowers the opponent’s armor and magic resistance. After your melee combo, switch to cannon and land one basic attack as you disengage. Lowering their resistances with a cannon swap basic attack strengthens your follow-up Q poke and your allies’ damage.
jayce-combo-shred.text: Your first basic attack after switching from hammer to cannon lowers the opponent’s armor and magic resistance. Land one as you disengage after a melee combo to strengthen your follow-up Q poke and your allies’ damage.

jayce-laning.basis: Farm in cannon form while poking with Q from outside the opponent’s range. Keep the wave near the middle and disrupt the opponent’s last hits. If the opponent closes in, switch to hammer to raise your armor, then counter with a Q leap and E knockback.
jayce-laning.text: Farm in cannon form while poking with Q from outside the opponent’s range. Keep the wave near the middle instead of pushing it all the way in, and disrupt the opponent’s last hits. If they close in, use R to switch to hammer for the added armor, then counter with a Q leap and E knockback.

jayce-phase.basis: Jayce can use both forms from level 1, so he is strongest early. Build a lead in the early to mid game by securing lane advantage and objectives.
jayce-phase.text: Jayce can use both forms from level 1, making him strongest early; build a lead in the early to mid game through lane advantage and objectives.

jayce-situational-antiheal.basis: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the opponent sustains through your damage with healing. Jayce’s poke comes in separate hits, so without stopping the opponent’s healing, the health you chipped away comes back.
jayce-situational-antiheal.text: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the opponent sustains through your damage with healing. Jayce’s poke lands in separate hits, so an opponent who can keep healing will recover the health you chipped away.

jayce-situational-mercurial.basis: If the opponent opens with crowd control that locks you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. Jayce can easily die when caught by crowd control that locks him down.
jayce-situational-mercurial.text: If the opponent opens with crowd control that locks you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. Jayce’s health and armor are among the lowest, so being held in place can quickly get him killed.

jayce-skill-e-gate.basis: Allies also gain movement speed when they pass through Acceleration Gate. Place Acceleration Gate along your allies’ path when following up on a gank or retreating.
jayce-skill-e-gate.text: Allies also gain movement speed when they pass through Acceleration Gate, so place it along their path when following up on a gank or retreating.

jayce-skill-passive.basis: Each weapon swap briefly increases your movement speed. Keep swapping weapons while moving to dodge the opponent’s poke or close the distance. Keep the swap cooldown running to reduce the time needed to prepare your combo.
jayce-skill-passive.text: Each weapon swap briefly increases your movement speed. Even when you do not intend to trade, swapping while moving helps you dodge poke or close the distance; keeping the swap cooldown running also shortens the time needed to prepare a combo.

jayce-skill-q-cannon.basis: Cannon Q explodes when it hits an enemy or reaches max range, dealing area damage. Fire Cannon Q so its explosion overlaps where your opponent is moving. Cannon Q explodes where it hits a minion. An opponent behind a minion takes damage only if they are within Cannon Q's explosion radius.
jayce-skill-q-cannon.text: Cannon Q Shock Blast explodes on hitting an enemy or reaching maximum range, dealing area damage. Aim its explosion at where your opponent is moving rather than relying on a direct hit. A minion causes it to explode on contact, so an opponent behind the minion takes damage only if they are within the explosion radius.

jayce-skill-r-defense.basis: Hammer form increases your armor and magic resistance. Switch to hammer form when you’re likely to take heavy damage or get caught.
jayce-skill-r-defense.text: Hammer form increases your armor and magic resistance. Switch to it when you are likely to take heavy damage or get caught to improve your chances of surviving.

jayce-skill-w.basis: Hammer W’s passive restores mana with every hammer basic attack. When mana is tight, clear minions in hammer form. Cannon W speeds up your next few attacks. Save cannon W for attacking objectives or pressuring turrets.
jayce-skill-w.text: Hammer W Lightning Field passively restores mana with every hammer basic attack, so clear minions in hammer form when mana is tight. Cannon W Hyper Charge speeds up your next few attacks; save it for attacking objectives or pressuring turrets.

jayce-teamfight.basis: Open teamfights by poking with cannon Q from the back. Go in briefly only when the enemy formation breaks up. Switch to hammer, combo the backline, then immediately switch to cannon and disengage.
jayce-teamfight.text: Open teamfights with cannon Q from the back, entering briefly only after the enemy formation breaks up. Land a hammer combo on the backline, then immediately switch to cannon and disengage; staying where you entered leaves you vulnerable to being picked off.

jhin-combo-lane.basis: Use basic attacks to lower caster minions' health so Q can kill them in succession. Hit a champion with the final bounce of a Q empowered by minion kills, then land the empowered final shot.
jhin-combo-lane.text: For a lane trade, use basic attacks to set up caster minions for successive Q kills, angle Q so each kill strengthens the next bounce, and let the final bounce hit the enemy champion before immediately following with your empowered final shot. Together, the grenade and final shot can take a substantial portion of an opponent’s health in a single midgame trade.

jhin-combo-root.basis: Root an enemy caught in an E trap with W, use basic attacks through the final shot, then finish with R if needed. Using W first on an unmarked target deals damage without rooting them.
jhin-combo-root.text: For a reliable combo, catch the target with an E trap or an ally’s immobilizing effect, root them with W, then basic attack through your final shot and finish with R if needed. Casting W first on an unmarked target deals damage but does not root.

jhin-laning.basis: After using the final shot, retreat out of the enemy's range. Use abilities to secure CS while reloading. Before recalling or leaving to place traps, clear the caster minions with Q to push the wave.
jhin-laning.text: Manage your reloads during lane: after firing the final shot, step out of the enemy’s range and use abilities to secure CS until the reload finishes. Q can clear caster minions at once, so use it to push the wave before recalling or leaving to place traps.

jhin-phase-early.basis: Jhin is easily pressured by enemies who can close the gap quickly. Early on, threaten your opponent while holding your final shot and securing CS. Jhin is better suited to playing safely early than building up damage on opponents.
jhin-phase-early.text: Jhin’s fixed attack speed and low movement speed make him vulnerable to enemies who close the gap quickly. Early on, hold your final shot to keep opponents back while securing CS. At 14 minutes, his damage per minute is relatively low but his deaths are the lowest, reflecting how much better he is at surviving safely early than steadily wearing opponents down.

jhin-phase-power.basis: Jhin excels at burst damage rather than sustained damage. Once Jhin learns R at level 6, he can join fights outside his lane. As Jhin gets more items, Q and his final shot make it easier to kill fragile targets. Jhin is weak against enemies who build a lot of health. Prioritize less durable enemies as attack targets.
jhin-phase-power.text: Jhin excels at burst damage rather than sustained damage. Once he learns R at level 6, he can influence fights outside his lane, and as his items accumulate, Q and his final shot can pick off fragile targets. Enemies who build a lot of health remain difficult for him, so prioritize less durable targets.

jhin-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing kills, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder against enemies whose healing needs to be reduced. When enemies heal, it becomes harder for Jhin to calculate finishing damage with his final shot and R.
jhin-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing kills, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Jhin relies on his final shot and R to finish targets as their missing health increases, so healing can throw off that damage calculation.

jhin-skill-e.basis: E stops recharging when both charges are available. Keep one E charge for escaping or following up. Place spare E traps in bushes and along the river to block gank routes in advance. E traps slow enemies who step on them. Place E in areas without vision to reveal them.
jhin-skill-e.text: E, Captive Audience, stops recharging when both charges are available. Keep one for escaping or following up, and place spare traps in bushes and along the river as they become available to block gank routes. Their vision, slow, and ability to set up a W root make them especially valuable in areas without vision.

jhin-skill-e-stack.basis: When an enemy steps on overlapping traps, the rear trap usually deals reduced damage. If two traps are placed in exactly the same spot, they explode together and deal full damage. Stack traps only in front of objectives where you know exactly where enemies will enter.
jhin-skill-e-stack.text: When an enemy steps on overlapping traps, the later trap usually deals reduced damage. Two placed in exactly the same spot explode together for full damage, but stacking them sacrifices their use for vision or stopping a chase. Reserve that setup for an objective where you know exactly where enemies will enter.

jhin-skill-passive.basis: Jhin has a fixed attack speed. His final shot always critically strikes. His final shot deals more damage based on the target's missing health. Landing his final shot increases his movement speed.
jhin-skill-passive.text: Jhin’s Whisper fixes his attack speed and makes him reload after a set number of shots. His final shot always critically strikes, deals more damage based on the target’s missing health, and grants movement speed, so save it for a champion instead of spending it on a minion. Simply holding that shot can force an opponent back; there’s no need to fire it immediately.

jhin-skill-q-bounce.basis: Q bounces to the nearest target it has not yet hit. Q does not prioritize low-health targets or champions. Plan Q's bounce path around target positions and the number of targets. Each target Q kills during a bounce increases the damage of its next hit. Set up Q so its final bounce hits a champion.
jhin-skill-q-bounce.text: Q, Dancing Grenade, bounces only to the nearest target it has not hit; it neither prioritizes low health targets or champions nor hits the same target twice. Plan its path around target positions and the number of targets, using kills on successive bounces to strengthen the next hit and send the final bounce into a champion.

jhin-skill-q-timing.basis: Q's travel time between bounces depends on the distance between targets. If Q's targets are far enough apart, there is time to add a basic attack between bounces. While Q is bouncing, lower a target's health with a basic attack to strengthen a later bounce.
jhin-skill-q-timing.text: Q’s travel time between bounces depends on the distance between targets. If they are far enough apart, add a basic attack while the grenade is bouncing to lower a target’s health before a later, stronger bounce reaches them.

jhin-skill-r.basis: R grows stronger as the target's missing health increases. Do not waste R's high-damage final shot on a target with almost no health left. Roots, slows, and blinds cannot interrupt R. Use R from a safe position where you can avoid stuns or knockbacks that interrupt it.
jhin-skill-r.text: R, Curtain Call, deals much less damage to a full health target and grows stronger as the target loses health, making it a tool for picking off retreating enemies rather than opening a teamfight. Its final shot hits especially hard, so avoid wasting it on someone with almost no health left. Roots, slows, and blinds cannot interrupt R, but stuns and knockbacks can; open it from a safe position.

jhin-skill-r-lane.basis: From far enough away, R's firing cone covers the entire lane. Against an enemy fleeing down a narrow lane, keep your distance and open R.
jhin-skill-r-lane.text: From far enough away, R’s firing cone covers the entire lane, leaving an opponent no room to escape sideways. When targeting someone fleeing down a narrow lane, opening R from a distance is more accurate than firing from close range.

jhin-skill-reload.basis: You can use Q, W, and E while reloading. Jhin is weakest when he's out of ammo. Don't stand still while reloading; use Q, W, and E to cover the downtime.
jhin-skill-reload.text: Jhin is weakest when he runs out of ammo, but he can still use abilities while reloading. Keep moving and use Q, W, and E to cover that downtime.

jhin-skill-w.basis: W has very long range. When aiming W, account for its cast time rather than travel time after firing. W is very narrow, making it easy to dodge. Use W after an ally's immobilizing effect or your trap has hit. Before approaching a fight, look for a target you can hit with W from afar.
jhin-skill-w.text: W, Deadly Flourish, has exceptional range and reaches its target almost as soon as it fires, so account for the cast time when aiming. Its narrow width makes an unsupported shot easy to dodge; fire after an ally immobilizes the target or your trap triggers, and scan for targets you can hit from afar before approaching a fight.

jhin-skill-w-root.basis: W roots only targets recently hit by Jhin's basic attack, his trap, or an ally's attack. Targets outside W's range do not receive a mark. Targets do not receive a mark before W is learned. To root a target with W, first mark them with a basic attack or trap.
jhin-skill-w-root.text: W roots only targets recently hit by Jhin’s basic attack, his trap, or an ally’s attack. Targets outside its range, or targets hit before Jhin learns W, receive no mark. To secure a root, mark the target first with a basic attack or trap.

jhin-teamfight.basis: Jhin relies heavily on durable frontline allies who provide immobilizing effects. In teamfights, stay at the back and make full use of your range. In teamfights, use W and R right after an ally's crowd control lands. Jhin has no mobility ability, making it hard to escape when caught. Place traps in advance along routes enemies may use to engage.
jhin-teamfight.text: Jhin relies heavily on his team: he needs a durable frontline to stand behind and an ally’s immobilizing effect to land W reliably. In teamfights, stay as far back as possible while using your range, and fire W and R right after allied crowd control lands. With no mobility ability to escape once caught, place traps along enemy engage routes in advance.

jhin-teamfight-scout.basis: If deep vision spots an enemy alone in the jungle, target them from afar with W or R. While waiting for a teamfight, use vision and traps to limit enemy routes.
jhin-teamfight-scout.text: Jhin’s long range and traps provide scouting and area control. Deep vision can reveal an enemy alone in the jungle for a long range pick with W or R; while waiting for a teamfight, use vision and traps to narrow the routes enemies can take.

jinx-combo-escape.basis: When chased, place E behind you along your escape route, then slow the pursuer with W. E's traps root targets as soon as they step on them. Place E traps together in a narrow passage so the pursuer has to pass through them.
jinx-combo-escape.text: When chased, place E traps behind you along your escape route and slow the pursuer with W. The traps root enemies as soon as they step on them, so place them together in a narrow passage to force the pursuer through them.

jinx-combo-fight.basis: Slow the enemy with W, attack from a distance with rockets, then switch to the minigun if they close in. If an enemy champion gets too close, prioritize attack speed over range.
jinx-combo-fight.text: Slow the enemy with W and deal damage from a distance with rocket basic attacks, then switch Q to the minigun for its attack speed if they close in; once a champion is too close, attack speed is more valuable than range.

jinx-combo-rocket-poke.basis: Switch Q to rockets, then basic attack a minion next to the enemy champion. Rocket basic attacks deal full damage to every enemy in the blast radius. To poke a champion without drawing minion aggro, hit an adjacent minion with a rocket basic attack.
jinx-combo-rocket-poke.text: Switch Q to rockets and basic attack a minion beside the enemy champion to poke without drawing minion aggro: the blast deals full damage to every enemy in its radius.

jinx-laning-mana.basis: Rocket basic attacks consume mana with every attack. To conserve mana, use rockets only for poke and take routine CS with the minigun. When Jinx runs out of mana, she struggles to clear waves and protect herself. Find a chance to recall before running out of mana.
jinx-laning-mana.text: Every rocket basic attack costs mana. Use rockets only for poke and take routine CS with the minigun to conserve it; running out makes both wave clear and self protection difficult, so find a chance to recall before that happens.

jinx-phase-early.basis: Jinx is not strong at gaining an early lane advantage. Early on, focus on rocket poke and safe CS to reach your item timing sooner instead of forcing trades.
jinx-phase-early.text: Jinx’s early kill participation and damage per minute are about average for a marksman, so she is not a champion that pulls ahead in lane. Her range is also relatively short; prioritize rocket poke and safe CS over forced trades to reach her item timing sooner.

jinx-phase-late.basis: Jinx uses Get Excited! to turn a fight win into an advantage in the next fight. After winning a late game teamfight, use Get Excited! to keep control of the game.
jinx-phase-late.text: As a hypercarry, Jinx grows much stronger with each core item. Get Excited! can carry a won fight into the next one, so winning a late game teamfight can let her take control of the game.

jinx-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Executioner's Calling is effective because rocket basic attacks can apply Grievous Wounds to multiple enemies at once.
jinx-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Rocket basic attacks deal area damage, letting you apply Grievous Wounds to multiple enemies at once.

jinx-skill-e.basis: E has a long cooldown. Jinx relies on E to protect herself. Save E for an enemy engage instead of spending it on poke. To deter an enemy engage, place E in a narrow passage near an objective or at a brush entrance in advance.
jinx-skill-e.text: E has a long cooldown and is Jinx’s only way to protect herself, so spending it on poke leaves her defenseless against an engage. Placing it in a narrow passage near an objective or at a brush entrance in advance can deter enemies from moving in.

jinx-skill-passive.basis: Jinx’s passive activates when you participate in a champion takedown. Jinx’s passive also activates when you kill an epic monster. Jinx’s passive also activates when you destroy a structure. Right after destroying a turret, use the passive’s movement speed boost to move to the next objective. Right after destroying a turret, use the passive’s movement speed boost to chase the enemy.
jinx-skill-passive.text: Get Excited! activates when Jinx participates in a champion takedown, kills an epic monster, or destroys a structure. After taking a turret, use its large movement speed and attack speed boosts to move to the next objective or chase an enemy.

jinx-skill-q-minigun.basis: The minigun builds attack speed stacks with consecutive basic attacks. The minigun is strongest at full attack speed stacks. When a fight looks likely, build minigun stacks in advance, even if you have to attack minions.
jinx-skill-q-minigun.text: Consecutive minigun basic attacks build attack speed stacks, making it strongest at full stacks. If a fight looks likely, build them in advance by attacking minions if necessary so you can deal full damage from the start.

jinx-skill-q-rocket.basis: Q rockets increase basic attack range. Q rocket basic attacks deal area damage. Q rocket basic attacks cost mana. Attack speed is slower while using Q rockets. Use rockets only to poke, clear waves, siege turrets, or attack grouped enemies; use the minigun otherwise.
jinx-skill-q-rocket.text: Q rockets give Jinx more range and area damage, but each attack costs mana and her attack speed is slower. Use them to poke, clear waves, siege turrets, or hit grouped enemies; switch back to the minigun otherwise.

jinx-skill-r.basis: R deals more damage the farther it travels. R deals bonus damage based on the target's missing health. Use R to finish off fleeing enemies or enemies in other lanes from afar, rather than enemies right in front of you.
jinx-skill-r.text: R deals more damage the farther it travels, plus bonus damage based on the target’s missing health. It is weak at close range, so use it to finish fleeing enemies or enemies in other lanes from afar, rather than firing at someone right in front of you.

jinx-skill-w.basis: W attacks from very long range. W reveals the location of the first enemy it hits. Use W to check vision in brush or ahead of an objective. Slow the enemy with W before moving in. Once minigun stacks increase your attack speed, W's cast time gets shorter, making it easier to land.
jinx-skill-w.text: W has very long range and reveals the location of the first enemy it hits. Use it to check brush, gain vision ahead of an objective, or slow an enemy before moving in. Its cast time shortens as your attack speed rises, making it easier to land after building minigun stacks.

jinx-teamfight.basis: When a teamfight starts, poke with rockets and W from the edge of the fight. Move in with the minigun only once you're sure it's safe. Jinx has no dash and struggles to survive once caught. Jinx relies on positioning to deal enough damage in teamfights.
jinx-teamfight.text: At the start of a teamfight, poke with rockets and W from the edge, and move in with the minigun only when you are sure it is safe. Jinx has no dash and can die once caught, so her positioning determines how much damage she can deal.

kaisa-combo-allin.basis: For an all-in, approach with E, stack Plasma with basic attacks, then use Q last. Use E's unit passing and movement speed boost during its charge to close the gap. Time the final Q's damage to overlap with the Plasma detonation. Using Q before you approach lets the enemy back away, causing the missiles to split among minions.
kaisa-combo-allin.text: Start an all-in by closing the gap with E, using its movement speed and ability to pass through units while charging. Once in range, build Plasma with basic attacks, then use Q last so its damage overlaps with the detonation. Using Q before closing in gives the enemy time to retreat and leaves its missiles split among minions.

kaisa-combo-poke.basis: For a poke combo, use W, follow with a basic attack, and finish with Q. W applies multiple Plasma stacks, setting up a detonation with one or two basic attacks. Time Q to hit as Plasma detonates. If W misses, save Q and retreat.
kaisa-combo-poke.text: For a poke combo, use W, follow with one or two basic attacks to detonate the multiple Plasma stacks it applies, and time Q to overlap with the detonation for more damage when the target’s health is low. If W misses, save Q and back off.

kaisa-combo-r-entry.basis: For a long-range engage, apply a mark with W, wait for the enemy to use their response ability, then follow with R and finish with basic attacks and Q. Use R after the enemy has reacted to your ally's engage by using their immobilizing and counterattack abilities. If the enemy still has a way to counterattack, avoid using R immediately after W hits.
kaisa-combo-r-entry.text: For a long-range engage, mark the target with W, wait until they respond to your ally’s engage with their immobilizing and counterattack abilities, then follow with R and finish with basic attacks and Q. Dashing in as soon as W lands leaves you alone against an enemy who still has every means to fight back.

kaisa-laning.basis: In lane, let the wave push toward you and poke with W. When the enemy marksman pushes the lane, farm CS from behind. When you need to push, clear the damaged wave at once with Q. Recall or secure vision right after clearing the wave with Q.
kaisa-laning.text: In lane, let the wave push toward you and poke with W. Kai'Sa’s low armor makes direct trades unfavorable, so if the enemy marksman pushes, stay back and collect CS instead of forcing your way forward. When you need to push, clear a damaged wave with Q, then recall or secure vision.

kaisa-phase-early.basis: Kai'Sa is weakest at levels 1–2. At levels 1–2, prioritize safe farming over trading. At levels 1–2, chip away at the enemy's health with W poke. Learning R at level 6 does not give Kai'Sa an immediate power spike.
kaisa-phase-early.text: Kai'Sa is weakest at levels 1–2: her range is short even among marksmen, and her base attack damage and armor are low. Farm safely instead of starting trades, and settle for chipping away with W. Unlocking R at level 6 does not make her immediately strong.

kaisa-phase-evolution.basis: Kai'Sa's power spikes depend more on completed items than on levels. Abilities evolve when their stat thresholds are met. Kai'Sa grows stronger with each completed core item. Until your first core item, focus on avoiding losses. After completing your second core item, start fights proactively.
kaisa-phase-evolution.text: Kai'Sa’s power spikes depend on items rather than levels. Her abilities evolve when their stat thresholds are met, making each completed core item a step up in strength. Focus on avoiding losses before your first core item, then start fights proactively once you have your second.

kaisa-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy's healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after your first core item. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder for healing reduction. Healing reduction items work well because repeated basic attacks keep the effect active.
kaisa-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy’s healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling after your first core item and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Kai'Sa’s repeated basic attacks keep the healing reduction active for a long time.

kaisa-situational-mercurial.basis: If the enemy team can lock Kai'Sa down with immobilizing effects, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier. Kai'Sa relies on E and R to find an engage angle, so immobilizing her can stop her engage.
kaisa-situational-mercurial.text: If the enemy team can immobilize Kai'Sa and kill her, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier. She needs E and R to find an engage angle, and a single immobilizing effect can stop the entire engage.

kaisa-skill-e.basis: E's charge time decreases as attack speed increases. Early on, when attack speed is low, E charges slowly and is hard to rely on for escape. Activating E lets you pass through units. After activating E, move through the minions. Each basic attack reduces E's cooldown.
kaisa-skill-e.text: E Supercharge charges faster as your attack speed increases. Its slow charge early on makes it unreliable for escaping, but activating it lets you pass through units, so use it to move through minions. Each basic attack reduces its cooldown; keep attacking during a teamfight to get a second E.

kaisa-skill-passive.basis: Stack Plasma with basic attacks and W. At maximum stacks, Plasma detonates, dealing magic damage based on the target's missing health. Detonating Plasma after the target has lost more health is more effective. Plasma also gains a stack when an ally immobilizes the target. With a support who has hard CC, count your Plasma stacks one step ahead.
kaisa-skill-passive.text: Plasma is central to every calculation. Stack it with basic attacks and W, then detonate it at maximum stacks for magic damage based on the target’s missing health; the lower their health when it triggers, the better. An ally immobilizing the target also adds a stack, so count ahead when playing with a support who has hard CC.

kaisa-skill-q-target.basis: Q missiles automatically split among and track nearby enemies. Repeated Q missile hits on the same target deal much less damage. Q is most effective when only one enemy champion is in range. If minions and champions are together, Q missiles split between them, weakening your trade. Use Q to trade when the enemy steps away from the wave.
kaisa-skill-q-target.text: Q Icathian Rain missiles automatically track and split among nearby enemies, with repeated hits on the same target dealing much less damage. It is most effective when only one enemy champion is in range; minions nearby draw missiles away and weaken your trade. Use Q when your opponent steps away from the wave.

kaisa-skill-q-wave.basis: Q deals much more damage to low-health minions. Before recalling or roaming, use basic attacks to lower minions' health evenly, then clear the wave with Q. When you need to let the wave push toward you, avoid using Q to farm.
kaisa-skill-q-wave.text: Q Icathian Rain deals much more damage to low-health minions. Before recalling or roaming, lower the wave’s health evenly with basic attacks so one Q can clear it; when you need the lane to push toward you, avoid using Q to farm.

kaisa-skill-r.basis: R can dash only to enemies with a Plasma mark. Apply a Plasma mark with W or a basic attack before using R to engage. Save R for finishing enemies and adjusting your angle.
kaisa-skill-r.text: Kai'Sa's R (Killer Instinct) can dash only to an enemy with a Plasma mark, so it is not a free repositioning tool: you must first mark the target with W or a basic attack. Using it carelessly can leave you in the middle of the enemy team with only a shield, so it is safer to save R for finishing enemies or adjusting your angle rather than using it to engage.

kaisa-skill-w.basis: W has very long range. W costs a lot of mana, so missing it hurts your laning. Hitting a champion with W refunds most of its cooldown. Use W only when you are confident it will hit. W grants true sight of the target it hits, revealing their position even after they hide in brush or stealth.
kaisa-skill-w.text: W Void Seeker has very long range, but it costs a lot of mana, and missing it puts you behind in lane. Hitting a champion refunds most of its cooldown, so fire only when you’re confident it will land; don’t force it against someone hiding behind minions. A hit also grants true sight, letting you keep track of a target who flees into brush or stealth.

kaisa-teamfight.basis: Start teamfights from the back by applying marks with W. After the enemy frontline has used all its immobilizing abilities and engage tools on your frontline, use E and R to find an angle to enter. After entering a teamfight, detonate Plasma with basic attacks. Before entering with R, check whether E is available for your escape.
kaisa-teamfight.text: Start teamfights from the back, applying marks with W. Once the enemy frontline has spent its immobilizing abilities and engage tools on your frontline, use E and R to find an angle in and detonate Plasma with basic attacks. R’s shield only covers the cost of entering once; check that E is available to get out before you commit.

kaisa-teamfight-vs-stealth.basis: Against stealth champions, land W just before a fight to keep track of their position. Landing W on a stealth champion gives you a chance to chase them with R.
kaisa-teamfight-vs-stealth.text: Against a stealth champion, W’s true sight is valuable on its own. Land it just before a fight to keep seeing their position even if they disappear, and its mark also gives you an angle to follow with R.

kalista-combo-trade.basis: Stack spears with Q, maintain distance with auto attacks and hops, then use E when the enemy retreats. If the enemy closes in, keep auto attacking while hopping backward. If the enemy retreats, hop forward to stay within attack range.
kalista-combo-trade.text: A basic trade starts with one spear stack from Q, followed by auto attacks that add stacks and hops after each attack to maintain distance; use E when the enemy retreats. If they close in, keep attacking while hopping backward. If they pull away, hop forward to stay within attack range.

kalista-situational-antiheal.basis: Choose Executioner's Calling if the enemy team has a champion with healing. Kalista relies on sustained auto attack damage, so she can keep Grievous Wounds applied.
kalista-situational-antiheal.text: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the enemy team has a champion with healing. Kalista’s sustained auto attack damage lets her keep Grievous Wounds applied.

kalista-skill-e-lasthit.basis: Killing a target with E resets its cooldown and refunds mana. Kill multiple speared minions with E to clear the wave and reset its cooldown.
kalista-skill-e-lasthit.text: When E Rend kills a target, its cooldown resets and it refunds mana, making it a reliable tool for last hits. If several speared minions remain, one E can clear the wave and reset its cooldown.

kalista-skill-passive-hop.basis: Issue a move command during an auto attack or Q windup to hop in that direction. Keep moving by hopping as you auto attack. The more attack speed you have, the more often you hop in the same amount of time. Kalista's mobility depends on how often she auto attacks.
kalista-skill-passive-hop.text: Kalista’s passive, Martial Poise, lets her hop in the direction of a move command issued during an auto attack or Q windup. This keeps her moving while she attacks; more attack speed means more hops in the same time and greater effective mobility. Her mobility comes from how often she attacks, rather than her movement speed stat.

kalista-skill-passive-limit.basis: A single move command to hop keeps your original auto attack target. You cannot hop if there is no target within attack range. Attack speed slows also reduce the distance you travel by hopping.
kalista-skill-passive-limit.text: A single move command to hop keeps Kalista’s original auto attack target, letting her reposition without switching targets. She cannot hop when nothing is within attack range, and attack speed slows reduce how far she travels over time. Without something to attack, she is slow.

kalista-skill-q.basis: If Q kills the first target it hits, it passes through and leaves spear stacks on the next target. Check the front minion's health, then use Q to clear the wave and stack spears on a target behind it. You can hop with Martial Poise during Q's cast animation. Choose your hop direction as you fire Q to retreat or close in.
kalista-skill-q.text: If Q Pierce kills the first target it hits, it passes through and leaves spear stacks on the next target. Check the front minion’s health before firing to clear the wave and stack spears on a target behind it. Martial Poise also lets Kalista hop during Q’s cast animation, so choose a direction as you fire to retreat or close in.

kalista-skill-r.basis: Coordinate your R plan with your Oathsworn support before using it. Use R to pull in and rescue an allied support in danger of being caught. Your Oathsworn cannot act while in stasis, so use R when your team is ready.
kalista-skill-r.text: Coordinate R Fate’s Call with your Oathsworn support beforehand, since pulling them in and throwing them can go to waste without a plan. It can start a fight or rescue a support in danger of being caught. Your Oathsworn cannot act while in stasis, so use R when your team is ready.

kalista-skill-w.basis: W's passive triggers only when you and your Oathsworn attack the same target. During trades, attack the same target as your support. Use W's active to scout around objectives or enemy jungle entrances.
kalista-skill-w.text: W Sentinel’s passive triggers only when Kalista and her Oathsworn attack the same target, so follow your support’s target during trades for the extra damage. Use its active to scout around objectives or enemy jungle entrances; there is no need to save it.

kalista-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, hop just behind the front line and deal sustained damage. Hop backward as soon as an enemy with an engage ability closes in. Stack spears on one target, then use E when that target retreats. Look for chances to use R to rescue an ally in teamfights.
kalista-teamfight.text: In teamfights, hop to just behind the front line and deal sustained damage, then hop backward immediately when an enemy with an engage ability closes in. Stack spears on one target and use E as that target retreats. Using R to rescue an ally is often safer than using it to start a fight.

karma-combo-engage.basis: Slow with Q, root with W, then use E to help your ally move in while they attack. If you can't get close, cast E on yourself for movement speed, then move into W range.
karma-combo-engage.text: Open by slowing with Q, holding the enemy for W’s root, then using E to help an ally move in while they deal damage. If you can’t get close enough, cast E on yourself for movement speed and enter W range.

karma-combo-mantra-q.basis: Mantra Q's burning zone detonates shortly after the first explosion. Use Mantra Q on an enemy rooted by W. Use Mantra Q while an ally's crowd control holds the enemy in place. If you poke with Mantra Q without any crowd control, the enemy can walk out of the zone.
karma-combo-mantra-q.text: Mantra Q’s burning zone detonates shortly after the first explosion. Place it on a target rooted by W or held by an ally’s crowd control so the full damage lands; without crowd control, an enemy you’re poking can walk out and take only half.

karma-laning-disengage.basis: As support Karma, focus on peeling against engages in lane. When the enemy support engages, use W to catch the engaging champion and E to get your allied marksman out.
karma-laning-disengage.text: As support Karma, prioritize peeling over starting fights in lane. When the enemy support engages, use W Focused Resolve to hold the engaging champion and E Inspire to get your marksman out. Even one successful response can put an enemy engage composition at a disadvantage throughout the lane phase.

karma-laning-mana.basis: Using Q and E carelessly will leave you short on mana by the middle of the laning phase. Use Q only when you have a chance to hit an enemy champion. Don't waste Q just to clear minions.
karma-laning-mana.text: Karma cycles Mantra through poke, but careless use of Q and E can drain her mana by the middle of the laning phase. Cast Q only when you have a chance to hit an enemy champion, rather than spending it just to clear minions.

karma-phase.basis: Karma can use Mantra from level 1, making her relatively strongest in early 2v2 fights. Single-target burst has less impact later in the game. Later in the game, keep allies alive with area shields and movement speed.
karma-phase.text: Mantra is available from level 1, making Karma relatively strongest in early 2v2 fights. As levels and items build up, her single-target burst becomes less effective; later, focus on keeping allies alive with area shields and movement speed.

karma-roaming.basis: E's movement speed makes roaming with an ally faster. When preparing for a mid gank or to join an objective fight, save Mantra so you can move together with Mantra E.
karma-roaming.text: E’s movement speed makes roaming with an ally faster. When preparing for a mid gank or to join an objective fight, consider saving Mantra to accelerate nearby allies together with Mantra E.

karma-situational-cc.basis: If the enemy team can lock down your carry with immobilizing crowd control, get Mikael's Blessing early. E's shield blocks damage but does not remove crowd control.
karma-situational-cc.text: If the enemy can lock down your carry with immobilizing crowd control, get Mikael’s Blessing early. E’s shield blocks damage but cannot remove crowd control.

karma-skill-e.basis: E grants both a shield and movement speed. Cast E on an ally just before they go in or pull back. Mantra E also shields nearby allies.
karma-skill-e.text: E Inspire grants both a shield and movement speed, making it useful for helping an ally engage or escape as well as blocking damage. Cast it just before they go in or pull back rather than after they have been hit; Mantra E also shields nearby allies.

karma-skill-passive.basis: Damaging an enemy champion with an ability reduces Mantra's cooldown. When you can poke, land abilities to keep Mantra cycling.
karma-skill-passive.text: Karma’s passive, Gathering Fire, reduces Mantra’s cooldown whenever an ability damages an enemy champion. Keep landing abilities to cycle Mantra rather than saving it; playing passively stalls that cycle, so poke whenever you have the chance.

karma-skill-q.basis: Q damages and slows the first target hit and nearby enemies. Minions block Q. Look for Q when the enemy champion steps out from behind the minion wave. Hitting an enemy champion with Q reduces Mantra's cooldown. Place Mantra Q's burning zone where the enemy has to stay.
karma-skill-q.text: Q, Inner Flame, damages and slows the first target hit and nearby enemies. Minions can block it, so aim for the moment an enemy champion steps out from behind the wave; a hit also reduces Mantra’s cooldown. Mantra Q leaves a burning zone after the explosion, so place it where the enemy has to stay.

karma-skill-r-early.basis: Mantra is available from level 1 without a skill point. If a level 1–2 fight breaks out, use your advantage from having an empowered ability.
karma-skill-r-early.text: Mantra is available from level 1 without a skill point, giving Karma an empowered ability while other champions are still without their ultimates. Use that advantage whenever a level 1–2 fight is possible.

karma-skill-w.basis: W only roots if the tether stays connected. Use W when you've slowed the enemy with Q or can keep up with E. Mantra W restores missing health and extends the root duration. When you're caught, use Mantra W to survive.
karma-skill-w.text: W, Focused Resolve, roots only if the tether stays connected, so an enemy can usually walk out of W on its own. Use it after slowing them with Q or when E lets you keep up. Mantra W restores missing health and extends the root, making it a way to survive when you’re caught.

karma-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, Gathering Fire can recharge Mantra multiple times. Don't hold back your first Mantra in a teamfight. Use Mantra W when you need to stop an enemy engage. Use Mantra E against teams with area burst damage. Use Mantra Q when you need to secure an already favorable position. After using Mantra, keep landing basic abilities to bring the next Mantra up sooner.
karma-teamfight.text: Gathering Fire can recharge Mantra multiple times in a teamfight, so use your first cast promptly. Choose Mantra W to stop an enemy engage, Mantra E against area burst, or Mantra Q to secure an already favorable position; afterward, keep landing basic abilities to bring the next Mantra up sooner.

karthus-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, place W along the opponent's escape path, then land Q beyond the wall. Enemies who pass through W lose magic resistance and take more damage from the Q that follows. Enemies slowed by W have a harder time dodging Q's warning indicator.
karthus-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, place W along your opponent’s escape path, then land Q beyond it. Crossing the wall reduces their magic resistance, making Q hit harder, while the heavy slow makes Q’s warning indicator harder to dodge.

karthus-combo-melee.basis: In close combat, turn on E, stay close to the opponent, and land Q at their feet. E deals continuous damage while active, so staying close to the opponent increases its damage. In close combat, land Q when the opponent is not overlapping with minions. Turn off E as soon as the fight ends to save mana for the next fight.
karthus-combo-melee.text: In close combat, turn on E, stay close to your opponent, and land Q at their feet when they are clear of minions. E deals damage continuously while they remain in range. Turn it off as soon as the fight ends to save mana for the next one.

karthus-laning-clear.basis: At camps, turn on E and land Q where the monsters overlap. If your mana falls below half, do not force another camp. Karthus's CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute are among the highest of jungle champions. Clear camps and waves instead of repeatedly trying to gank.
karthus-laning-clear.text: At camps, turn on E and land Q where the monsters overlap. If your mana drops below half, do not force another camp. Karthus ranks among junglers with the highest CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute, so clear camps and waves instead of repeatedly trying to gank.

karthus-laning-gank.basis: Karthus has no mobility ability or instant immobilizing effect, making it hard for him to pull off a gank alone. Gank when an ally has already immobilized the opponent or the opponent has pushed far up the lane. In other ganks, use W to limit the opponent's escape path and help your allies engage.
karthus-laning-gank.text: Karthus has no mobility ability or instant immobilizing effect, making it hard to gank alone. Go in when an ally has already immobilized the opponent or the opponent has pushed far up the lane; otherwise, use W to limit their escape path and help your allies engage.

karthus-phase.basis: Before level 6, Karthus has no way to escape and is easy for the enemy jungler to catch. From mid game, once Karthus has R and core ability power items, he can affect the entire map. Karthus keeps dealing damage after dying in late-game teamfights.
karthus-phase.text: Before level 6, Karthus has no way to escape and is easy for the enemy jungler to catch. Once he has R and core ability power items in the mid game, he can affect the entire map; in late game teamfights, he keeps dealing damage even after dying.

karthus-situational-banshee.basis: If the opponent deals heavy magic damage and can interrupt R with a targeted immobilizing effect, buy Banshee's Veil. Blocking the first ability often lets you finish channeling R.
karthus-situational-banshee.text: If the enemy team deals heavy magic damage and can interrupt R with a targeted immobilizing effect, buy Banshee’s Veil. Blocking the first ability often lets you finish channeling R.

karthus-situational-zhonya.basis: If the opponent has a way to jump onto Karthus, buy Zhonya's Hourglass early. Karthus has no mobility ability, so he is easy to catch when an opponent gets close. If an opponent's engage interrupts R's channel, the ultimate has no effect.
karthus-situational-zhonya.text: If an opponent can jump onto Karthus, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. He has no mobility ability and is easy to catch up close; if an engage interrupts R’s channel, the ultimate has no effect.

karthus-skill-e.basis: E can be toggled on and off, and it drains mana quickly while active. Keep E on only while close to an opponent, and turn it off as soon as they leave its range. E's passive restores mana whenever Karthus kills an enemy unit. To restore mana, Karthus must last-hit the enemy unit himself. The mana restored by E from killing enemy units is Karthus's only source of mana.
karthus-skill-e.text: E can be toggled on and off, but it drains mana quickly while active. Keep it on only while an opponent is in range, then turn it off immediately. Its passive restores mana whenever Karthus kills an enemy unit, so secure the last hit yourself; this is his only source of mana.

karthus-skill-passive-death.basis: After dying, Karthus can use all his abilities without mana for a short time. If you have little health left, die among the enemies and use E and Q in spirit form. Die near enemies so you can make use of your time in spirit form.
karthus-skill-passive-death.text: After dying, Karthus can use all his abilities without mana for a short time, so if you have little health left, die among the enemies and use E and Q in spirit form. Stay close enough to make full use of that time.

karthus-skill-passive-r.basis: Karthus can use R in spirit form. If you can use R when you die and the enemy is low on health, finish them with R. Do not let your time in spirit form pass without using abilities.
karthus-skill-passive-r.text: Karthus can use R in spirit form, so if it is available when you die and an enemy is low on health, use it to finish them off. Do not let your time in spirit form pass without casting abilities.

karthus-skill-q.basis: Q deals much more damage when it hits only one enemy. When trading, hit an opponent who is not overlapping with minions with Q. When farming, use Q where multiple targets overlap.
karthus-skill-q.text: Q deals much more damage when it hits only one enemy. In trades, aim at opponents who are clear of minions; when farming, cast it where multiple targets overlap.

karthus-skill-r.basis: R damages all enemy champions regardless of distance. R has no effect if its channel is interrupted. Use R from a safe position or when an ally can protect its channel. At the start of a teamfight, use R to lower every enemy's health and help your allies engage. Pressure scattered opponents at the same time with R to go for an objective. Ask your allies how other lanes are doing to time your R.
karthus-skill-r.text: R Requiem hits every enemy champion regardless of distance, but its channel must finish or the entire effect is lost. Cast it only from a safe position or when an ally can protect the channel. It is not just a finishing move: using it at the start of a teamfight lowers every enemy’s health and creates an opening for your allies to engage. It can also pressure scattered opponents at the same time to open up an objective. Ask your allies how the other lanes are doing to choose the right moment.

karthus-skill-w.basis: Enemies can pass through W, so it cannot block their path. Enemies who pass through W are heavily slowed and lose magic resistance. Place W where the opponent must pass through it. The magic resistance reduction from W increases the damage of the Q and R that follow.
karthus-skill-w.text: Enemies can pass through W, but doing so heavily slows them and reduces their magic resistance. Place it where an opponent must cross it to make the following Q and R deal more damage.

karthus-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, keep landing Q from the back. In teamfights, position yourself to die as late as possible. If the entire enemy frontline has engaged your allies, turn on E and move in to deal area damage. If you are going to die, die among the enemies to make use of E and Q in spirit form.
karthus-teamfight.text: In teamfights, keep landing Q from the back and position yourself to die as late as possible. If the entire enemy frontline has engaged your allies, turn on E and move in to deal area damage. If you are going to die, do so among the enemies to make use of E and Q in spirit form.

kassadin-combo-burst.basis: For a basic burst combo, enter with R, then use E, a W-empowered basic attack, and Q in that order. After entering, keep the enemy close with E's slow. Use a W-empowered basic attack to restore some mana for the next R. Save Q for the end of the combo to interrupt the enemy's channel.
kassadin-combo-burst.text: For a basic burst combo, enter with R, Riftwalk, then use E, Force Pulse, a W, Nether Blade, empowered basic attack, and Q, Null Sphere, in that order. R’s entry damage and E’s slow help keep the target close, while the W attack restores some mana for your next R. Hold Q until the end to interrupt an enemy movement ability or channel.

kassadin-combo-chase.basis: Use R repeatedly when a chase is sure to secure the kill. Before chasing, calculate how many more times you can use R with your remaining mana. When Kassadin runs out of mana, he cannot move with R and is vulnerable to counterattacks.
kassadin-combo-chase.text: Chase with repeated R, Riftwalk, casts. From the second cast onward, each costs twice as much mana but also deals more damage, so use them freely when they will secure the finish. Before chasing, count how many casts your remaining mana allows: running out removes your escape tool and leaves you open to a counterattack.

kassadin-laning-early.basis: Kassadin is vulnerable to one-sided poke at levels 1–5. Early on, focus on securing CS while using Q's shield to absorb magic poke. Keep the early wave near your turret without pushing it. Early on, focus on staying alive and buying time to scale.
kassadin-laning-early.text: As a melee mage, Kassadin takes one sided poke at levels 1–5. Use Q, Null Sphere’s, shield to absorb magic poke, focus on CS, and keep the wave near your turret without pushing it. His 14 minute kills and CS rank near the bottom among mid laners, while his deaths are among the lowest; surviving and buying time is the normal path.

kassadin-laning-wave.basis: Nearby spell casts reduce E's cooldown, speeding up waveclear. After pushing the wave, retreat to a warded area to prepare for an attack from the enemy jungler.
kassadin-laning-wave.text: Once E, Force Pulse, is leveled, nearby spell casts reduce its cooldown and speed up waveclear. Staying near the lane despite enemy poke can therefore be worthwhile, but pushing the wave leaves Kassadin especially vulnerable to the enemy jungler. After pushing, retreat into an area where you have vision.

kassadin-phase-late.basis: Kassadin has strong carry potential late in the game. Even if you fall behind early, play to extend the game. In unfavorable matchups, give up some CS if needed to keep leveling safely.
kassadin-phase-late.text: Kassadin is a late game hypercarry, so even after an early setback, play to extend the game. Dying while trying to force a lane win delays the growth he depends on. In a bad matchup, give up a few CS if necessary and keep leveling safely.

kassadin-phase-six.basis: At level 6, Kassadin can turn the lane in his favor once he gets R. R's cooldown drops sharply as its rank increases. Kassadin comes into his own after maxing R. Do not overextend by treating the moment you hit level 6 as your strongest point.
kassadin-phase-six.text: Level 6 is a turning point for Kassadin: gaining R, Riftwalk, lets him slip past poke and reach opponents, shifting control of the lane. Its cooldown falls sharply with each rank, however, so his strongest period comes after maxing R. Overextending right at level 6 as though he has already peaked will delay his growth.

kassadin-situational-banshee.basis: Against a composition that blocks your entry with magic damage and targeted immobilization, choose Banshee's Veil to create an opening. Banshee's Veil improves survivability alongside the passive's magic damage reduction.
kassadin-situational-banshee.text: Against a composition built around magic damage and targeted immobilization that stops your entry, buy Banshee’s Veil. Blocking the first spell creates an opening to engage with R, Riftwalk, and, together with the passive’s magic damage reduction, greatly improves your survival.

kassadin-skill-e.basis: Each nearby spell cast reduces E's cooldown. Position with both a safe distance from poke and E's cooldown reduction in mind.
kassadin-skill-e.text: Each nearby spell cast reduces E, Force Pulse’s cooldown, so spells exchanged by both teams can bring it back faster while Kassadin stays near the lane. Farther away, it must run its full cooldown; balance a safe distance from poke against the faster E cycle.

kassadin-skill-passive.basis: The passive reduces magic damage taken. The passive lets Kassadin ignore unit collision. When chasing, cut through minion waves to take the shortest path.
kassadin-skill-passive.text: Kassadin’s passive reduces incoming magic damage and lets him pass through units. The damage reduction helps him withstand lane opponents who deal magic damage, while the lack of unit collision lets him chase straight through a minion wave along the shortest path—even when an opponent retreats behind it.

kassadin-skill-q.basis: Q interrupts enemy channels. Q grants a shield that absorbs magic damage. Time Q to absorb an enemy mage's poke.
kassadin-skill-q.text: Q, Null Sphere, interrupts channels and grants a shield that absorbs magic damage. In lane, treat it as a defensive tool: time it for an enemy mage’s poke or use it to stop a channeled ability. Spending it on a minion for damage leaves you exposed to that poke.

kassadin-skill-r.basis: Using R repeatedly in a short time doubles its mana cost. Using R repeatedly in a short time increases its damage. Kassadin's sustained damage depends on his remaining mana. Secure the blue Smite buff to ease R's mana cost.
kassadin-skill-r.text: Casting R, Riftwalk, repeatedly within a short time doubles its mana cost and increases its damage. It is both Kassadin’s mobility tool and his main damage ability, so his remaining mana determines how much damage he can still deal. Before going in, decide how many casts you can afford and whether to save one to escape; securing the blue Smite buff greatly eases the mana burden.

kassadin-skill-w.basis: W's passive adds magic damage to basic attacks. Using W greatly empowers the next basic attack. The W-empowered basic attack restores missing mana. W restores much more mana when it hits a champion. In late-game teamfights, use a W-empowered basic attack to get the mana needed for the next R.
kassadin-skill-w.text: W, Nether Blade, passively adds magic damage to basic attacks; activating it greatly empowers the next attack and restores missing mana. The restoration is much greater against a champion, so when mana runs low, landing a W attack on an opponent can be faster than recalling. In a late teamfight, that mana can fund another R after repeated casts have drained you.

kassadin-teamfight.basis: Do not start teamfights from the front. Once the enemy has used immobilizing abilities on your frontline and their formation breaks, use R to enter their backline. After bursting down the backline, use R to get out. Before entering, set aside R casts for both entry and escape.
kassadin-teamfight.text: Never start a teamfight from the front. Once the enemy has spent immobilizing abilities on your frontline and their formation has broken, use R, Riftwalk, to reach the backline, deal burst damage, and use it again to leave. Decide beforehand how many casts to spend entering and how many to reserve for escape.

kassadin-teamfight-side.basis: Kassadin is suited to side-lane play because R lets him join fights and leave quickly. While no teamfight is happening, collect waves in a side lane. If a fight starts while you are in a side lane, join it.
kassadin-teamfight-side.text: R, Riftwalk, lets Kassadin join and leave fights quickly, making side lane play effective. When no teamfight is starting, collect waves in a side lane, then join once a fight begins to maximize your growth. Standing in the middle of a quiet standoff instead leaves you vulnerable to being picked off.

kata-combo-allin.basis: For the full combo, place daggers with W and Q, E to the Q dagger to engage, then pick up the remaining W dagger while using R. Place the two daggers in different spots so you can reposition during R to pick one up.
kata-combo-allin.text: For the full combo, use W to set up a dagger, Q to place another behind the enemy, then E to the Q dagger to engage. Pick up the remaining W dagger and use R. Placing the daggers in different spots gives you the option to reposition and pick one up during R.

kata-combo-qe.basis: For the basic combo, wait for the Q dagger to land behind the enemy, then E to it. Picking up a dagger deals passive damage to all nearby enemies. Picking up a dagger almost resets E's cooldown. After Q, check where the dagger will land before using E directly on the enemy.
kata-combo-qe.text: For Katarina’s basic combo, use Q, watch for its dagger to land behind the enemy, then E to the dagger. Picking it up deals passive damage to all nearby enemies and nearly resets E’s cooldown. If you E directly to the enemy after Q, you lose that entire sequence, so check where the dagger lands first.

kata-combo-w-during-r.basis: Use W just before R to deal extra damage without interrupting R. While channeling R, walk to a nearby dagger and pick it up for extra passive damage.
kata-combo-w-during-r.text: Press W just before R to add damage without interrupting R. You can move while channeling, so walk over a nearby dagger during R to pick it up and add passive damage.

kata-combo-we.basis: W throws a dagger above Katarina that lands on the ground shortly afterward. Pick up the W dagger while overlapping the enemy to guarantee damage. From a distance, use W, then E to your dagger to recover E's cooldown. Use W as a way to make E available again.
kata-combo-we.text: W throws a dagger above Katarina that lands on the ground shortly afterward. Use it while standing on top of an enemy, then pick up the dagger for guaranteed damage; from a distance, use W → E to leap to your own dagger and immediately recover E’s cooldown. Think of W as a way to make E available again, rather than a movement speed boost.

kata-laning.basis: In lane, focus on poking with Q bounces through minions and last-hitting. Avoid forcing the wave to push during lane. Focus on spotting the enemy's mistakes more than on farming. Right after the enemy uses a skill on the wave, try to engage with E using the Q dagger.
kata-laning.text: In lane, focus on last-hitting and poking with Q bounced through minions without forcing the wave to push. Katarina tends to have a low CS count, so look for an opponent’s mistake rather than focusing on farming. The best moment to engage with Q → E to its dagger is right after the opponent uses a skill on the wave.

kata-laning-reset.basis: Katarina excels at building on a lead by refreshing her skills through takedowns. After clearing the wave, use dagger rotations to join a side lane or objective fight quickly. Each kill makes your next move faster. To make use of her strengths, avoid staying in lane just to farm.
kata-laning-reset.text: Katarina builds a lead by refreshing her skills through takedowns. After clearing the wave, use dagger rotations to reach a side lane or objective fight quickly; each kill speeds up your next move. Staying in lane solely to farm leaves her strengths unused.

kata-phase.basis: Katarina is weak at levels 1–2, when Q has a long cooldown and it is hard to cycle daggers. Start looking for short trades at level 3, once you have both Q and E. Use the increased kill opportunities at level 6, when you learn R, and when you finish your first core item. Katarina spends no separate resource, so she can use her skills continuously. Katarina relies on E leaps for defense, so she can struggle to engage even late in the game against teams with crowd control.
kata-phase.text: Katarina is weak at levels 1–2 because Q has a long cooldown and she cannot reliably cycle through daggers. Short trades become possible at level 3 once she has both Q and E; kill opportunities rise sharply at level 6 when she learns R and again when she finishes her first core item. She has no resource cost, so she can keep using skills, but E leaps are her only defensive tool, making it difficult to engage against teams with crowd control even late in the game.

kata-skill-e.basis: E can target an enemy, ally, or dagger and move Katarina to a chosen spot near that target. Using E on a dagger brings its cooldown back almost immediately; using it on another target applies the full cooldown. Practice until you have a feel for E's maximum range. Before engaging with E, check for a dagger or ally you can use to escape. E can also leap to jungle plants and interactive objects.
kata-skill-e.text: E can target an enemy, ally, or dagger and move Katarina to any chosen spot near it. Using E on a dagger restores its cooldown almost immediately, while using it on another target leaves the full cooldown. Learn its maximum range, and before leaping in, check for a dagger or ally you can use to escape. E can also leap to jungle plants and interactive objects, opening unexpected ways to engage or get out.

kata-skill-passive.basis: When a champion Katarina recently damaged dies, her passive greatly reduces all her skill cooldowns. As soon as a kill reduces your cooldowns, continue the combo on the next target. In teamfights, kill the lowest-health target first to chain passive resets.
kata-skill-passive.text: When a champion Katarina recently damaged dies, Voracity greatly reduces all her skill cooldowns, restoring the combo she needs to move on to the next target. In teamfights, aim to finish off the lowest-health enemy first and chain those resets.

kata-skill-passive-radius.basis: The damage area from picking up a dagger is much larger than the area where you can pick it up. Dagger pickup damage is centered on Katarina, not the dagger's location. Pick up a dagger as you move into the middle of a group of enemies.
kata-skill-passive-radius.text: The damage area when Katarina picks up a dagger is much larger than its pickup area, and the damage is centered on her rather than the dagger. Pick it up as you move into the middle of a group of enemies to hit more of them.

kata-skill-q.basis: Q hits its targeted enemy, then bounces to nearby targets. The Q dagger lands behind the first target hit. Q a front minion to poke safely from a distance with the bounce. Account for where the Q dagger will land behind the minion, and decide in advance whether to engage or stop at poke.
kata-skill-q.text: Q targets an enemy, bounces to nearby targets, and drops a dagger behind the first target hit. In lane, target a front minion to hit your opponent with a bounce and poke safely from farther away. The dagger will also land behind that minion, so decide beforehand whether its position allows an engage or makes this a poke only.

kata-skill-r.basis: R channels rapid attacks against the three nearest enemy champions. R applies healing reduction to enemies it hits. R partially applies on-hit effects, triggering item effects too. Before casting R, check that the enemy's immobilizing skills are on cooldown so crowd control does not interrupt it. If you need to escape, cancel R before it finishes.
kata-skill-r.text: R channels rapid attacks against the three nearest enemy champions, applies healing reduction to those it hits, and partially applies on-hit effects, including item effects. Check that the enemy’s immobilizing skills have been used before casting, since crowd control can interrupt the channel. Depending on the situation, canceling R early to escape is a valid choice.

kata-teamfight.basis: Avoid engaging first in teamfights. Engage after the enemy uses its immobilizing skills on your frontline. E to a dagger placed in advance to reach the backline, then use R. Before engaging, secure one escape dagger or an ally you can E to.
kata-teamfight.text: Do not engage first in a teamfight. Wait until the enemy uses its immobilizing skills on your frontline, then use a dagger placed in advance to reach the backline and cast R. Before going in, leave yourself a dagger or an ally you can E to for an escape.

kata-teamfight-antiheal.basis: R applies healing reduction to targets it hits. Against an enemy with strong healing, position to include them in R as their healing begins.
kata-teamfight-antiheal.text: R applies healing reduction to targets it hits. Against an enemy with strong healing, do not save it only to finish a kill; as their healing begins, position so R includes them.

kayle-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, use Q, then an E empowered basic attack, and follow with regular basic attacks. Q's armor and magic resistance reduction helps increase the damage of follow-up basic attacks and E. E empowers the next basic attack. E increases the range of the next basic attack. Right after a basic attack hits, use E before its recovery animation ends to bring forward the next basic attack.
kayle-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, use Q (Radiant Blast), an E (Starfire Spellblade) empowered basic attack, then regular basic attacks. Q slows and reduces armor and magic resistance, making the follow-up hits stronger. E also extends the next attack’s range; press it just after a basic attack lands, before the recovery animation ends, to bring the next attack forward without breaking your rhythm.

kayle-combo-stack.basis: Before level 16, attack minions or jungle monsters to reach maximum P stacks before starting a fight. Prestacking P gives you its maximum attack speed bonus from the start of a fight. At levels 11–15, prestacking P lets you use fire waves from the start of a fight.
kayle-combo-stack.text: Before level 16, build maximum P (Divine Ascent) stacks on minions or jungle monsters before starting a fight. This lets Kayle open with her full attack speed bonus and, from level 11 onward, fire waves. Entering without stacks leaves her taking damage while she builds them.

kayle-laning.basis: Before level 6, avoid trades. Before level 6, stay behind the wave and only last-hit. Before level 6, save Q for escaping. If your opponent engages, retreat using Q and W. If your health falls below half, prioritize staying inside your turret's range over CS.
kayle-laning.text: Before level 6, avoid trades, stay behind the wave, and take only safe last hits while saving Q (Radiant Blast) for escape.
