If your opponent engages, retreat with Q and W (Celestial Blessing). Below half health, stay within your turret’s range even if it costs CS, since one enemy jungle gank can kill you.

kayle-laning-wave.basis: Before level 6, keep the wave near your turret. Avoid farming in front of the enemy turret, where you are exposed to ganks. After level 11, push the lane quickly before joining your team. After level 11, you can also keep the opposing laner occupied in a side lane.
kayle-laning-wave.text: Keep the wave near your turret before level 6; farming in front of the enemy turret exposes Kayle to ganks when she has no dash to escape. After level 11, use her area damage to push quickly, then join your team or keep the opposing laner occupied in a side lane.

kayle-phase-11.basis: From level 11, basic attacks at maximum P stacks launch fire waves. From level 11, E explodes around the target on hit. At level 11, Kayle gains area damage, making her stronger at wave clear and teamfights. After level 11, push the lane quickly and join objective fights.
kayle-phase-11.text: At level 11, basic attacks at maximum P (Divine Ascent) stacks send out fire waves, and E (Starfire Spellblade) begins exploding around its target on hit. The added area damage improves both wave clear and teamfight damage. Before then, slow rotations are acceptable; afterward, push the lane quickly and join objective fights.

kayle-phase-16.basis: At level 16, P's Exalted state remains active permanently. At level 16, P brings her basic attack range to its maximum. At level 16, she gains P's maximum attack speed bonus without stacking it first. Kayle aims to scale into the late game, reaching her full fighting strength at level 16. Before level 16, avoid rushing into decisive fights.
kayle-phase-16.text: Level 16 completes Kayle’s transformation: P (Divine Ascent) keeps her Exalted state active permanently and raises her range to its maximum. She can start fights with maximum range, attack speed, and fire waves without building stacks first. Aim to reach this point; trying to force a decisive fight earlier usually puts Kayle at a disadvantage.

kayle-phase-6.basis: At level 6, P increases her basic attack range to ranged. From level 6, use the extra range to harass melee opponents with basic attacks. Manage the wave from late level 5 to reach level 6 before your opponent. Use the moment after reaching level 6 to try trades that were difficult before.
kayle-phase-6.text: Level 6 is Kayle’s first major power spike. P (Divine Ascent) gives her ranged basic attacks, letting her harass melee opponents and take trades she could not take before. Manage the wave from late level 5 to reach level 6 before your opponent, then look for your first trades.

kayle-phase-early.basis: Kayle is very weak at levels 1–5. At levels 1–5, prioritize survival while securing experience and CS.
kayle-phase-early.text: Levels 1–5 are Kayle’s weakest point in the game: she has melee range, the lowest magic resistance of any champion, and no mobility or defensive skill, so an enemy laner and jungler who commit to killing her can do so. Focus on staying alive and collecting experience and CS rather than winning the lane; giving up a few CS is a normal decision, not a mistake.

kayle-phase-tradeoff.basis: Kayle's fighting strength depends heavily on her level. Avoid dying and leaving the lane so you do not delay your level milestones. Avoid joining fights if it means losing wave experience. Early on, avoid joining counterjungling attempts to prevent experience loss. If your team can buy time, farm CS in a side lane to scale.
kayle-phase-tradeoff.text: Kayle’s strength depends heavily on her level, so protect your experience. Dying and leaving lane, losing a wave to a forced rotation, or joining an early counterjungle attempt all delay her power spikes. If your team can buy time, farming CS in a side lane is itself a contribution.

kayle-situational-antiheal.basis: Kayle's sustained basic attacks are well suited to maintaining Grievous Wounds. Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb first to suit Kayle's magic damage. When you need healing reduction and can spare a core item slot, upgrade to Morellonomicon. Avoid Executioner's Calling because its attack damage does not suit Kayle's scaling.
kayle-situational-antiheal.text: Kayle’s sustained basic attacks can keep Grievous Wounds applied against opponents who rely on healing. Since her damage is primarily magic, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb first and upgrade to Morellonomicon when you can spare a core item slot. Avoid Executioner’s Calling; its attack damage does not suit Kayle’s scaling.

kayle-skill-e.basis: E adds magic damage to basic attacks even when you do not activate it. Activating E makes the next basic attack deal bonus damage based on the target's missing health. Use E on a damaged opponent rather than one at full health. E applies on-hit effects and magic item effects. From level 11, use E's explosion to clear waves.
kayle-skill-e.text: E (Starfire Spellblade) adds magic damage to basic attacks even when inactive. Activating it extends the next attack’s range and adds damage based on the target’s missing health, so it hits much harder after an opponent has already taken damage. It applies on-hit and magic item effects; from level 11, its explosion also makes it central to wave clear.

kayle-skill-q.basis: Q stops at the first enemy hit but also damages enemies behind them. Use Q's slow and resistance reduction to follow up on allied ganks. When escaping, use Q to slow pursuing enemies. Before level 6, avoid using Q for unnecessary minion clearing or poke so you can respond to ganks.
kayle-skill-q.text: Q Radiant Blast stops at the first enemy hit but also damages enemies behind them. Its slow and armor and magic resistance reduction help Kayle follow up on allied ganks or escape. Before level 6, Q is her only ranged tool and her only aid to escaping, so avoid spending it on wave clear or pointless poke when you may need it if the enemy jungler arrives.

kayle-skill-r.basis: R grants damage immunity to one ally, including Kayle herself. R deals area damage around its target. Crowd control can still affect a target during R's damage immunity. Use R on an ally as their engage reaches the enemy team.
kayle-skill-r.text: R Divine Judgment makes one ally, including Kayle herself, immune to damage and deals area damage around that target. Use it to survive when Kayle gets caught or to support an ally’s engage as it reaches the enemy team. The immunity does not prevent crowd control, so casting R while immobilized can waste its duration. Casting it too early wastes immunity before damage arrives, while casting it too late means the target is already dead; aim to use it just before the enemy’s burst damage lands or as your ally’s engage reaches the enemy team.

kayle-skill-w.basis: Prioritize W's movement speed boost over its heal. Use W's movement speed boost to escape ganks or enemy engages. If you do not select a target, W targets the most injured ally. When you need to survive, target yourself directly with W.
kayle-skill-w.text: W (Celestial Blessing) is more valuable for its movement speed than its early heal, which is too small to turn most trades. Use the speed to escape ganks or enemy engages. Without a selected target, W goes to the most injured ally, so target yourself directly when you need it to survive.

kayle-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use your increased range to keep attacking from the back. While your frontline blocks enemy engages, hit multiple enemies with fire waves. Before an enemy assassin reaches you, decide whether to use R on yourself or an ally who has engaged.
kayle-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay at the back and use Kayle’s increased range to keep attacking while your frontline stops enemy engages and her fire waves hit multiple targets. Decide before an assassin reaches you whether R (Divine Judgment) will go on Kayle or an ally who has engaged.

kayn-combo-gank.basis: For a standard gank, use E to pass through a wall, slow the target with W, land Q and a basic attack, then finish with R. R can only be cast on a target Kayn has recently damaged. Land W or Q before using R to meet its cast condition.
kayn-combo-gank.text: For a standard gank, approach through a wall with E (Shadow Step), slow the target with W (Blade's Reach) as you emerge, then close in with Q (Reaping Slash), land a basic attack, and finish with R (Umbral Trespass). R can only target an enemy Kayn has recently damaged, so land W or Q first.

kayn-combo-r.basis: Kayn remains untargetable while inside the target with R. Use R to dodge a key enemy ability as it comes in. Keep attacking after exiting R. You can choose where to exit R during the cast. Choose an exit position from R toward your escape route.
kayn-combo-r.text: Kayn is untargetable while inside a target with R (Umbral Trespass), making it both a finisher and a way to dodge an enemy's key ability as it arrives. Keep attacking when you emerge, and choose an exit position toward your escape route during the cast.

kayn-combo-shadow-assassin.basis: Shadow Assassin's bonus damage only applies for a short window after entering combat with an enemy champion. Shadow Assassin gets right next to the enemy and lands Q, a basic attack, and W during the bonus damage window. If Shadow Assassin lacks damage, use R to pull back, then re-enter when the bonus damage window returns.
kayn-combo-shadow-assassin.text: Shadow Assassin deals bonus damage only for a short window after entering combat with an enemy champion. Get right next to the target and fit Q (Reaping Slash), a basic attack, and W (Blade's Reach) into that window instead of spacing your abilities out like poke; if the damage is insufficient, pull back with R (Umbral Trespass) and re-enter when the bonus damage window returns.

kayn-laning-clear.basis: Plan a route that uses E to cross walls between camps and cut travel time. Prioritize a full jungle clear over risky early ganks.
kayn-laning-clear.text: Plan your route around using E (Shadow Step) to cross walls between camps and save travel time. Kayn’s clear is not slow, so completing a full early jungle clear to speed up his transformation is safer than forcing risky early ganks.

kayn-laning-gank.basis: In a gank, approach through a wall behind the lane with E to cut off the enemy's escape route. Enter a wall with E as your ally starts trading damage, then come out immediately. Even without a kill, consider the value of a gank that earns orbs by fighting an enemy champion.
kayn-laning-gank.text: For a gank, approach through a wall behind the lane with E (Shadow Step) to cut off the enemy's escape. Because enemies can see Kayn inside the wall, enter as your ally starts trading damage and emerge immediately instead of waiting there. Fighting an enemy champion earns orbs, so even a gank without a kill has value.

kayn-phase-early.basis: Kayn is weak in fights before transforming. Early on, prioritize clearing camps and collecting orbs over fighting. Avoid risky early jungle invades.
kayn-phase-early.text: Kayn is weak in fights before transforming, so prioritize clearing camps and collecting orbs over early skirmishes. Avoid risky jungle invades that could set you back.

kayn-phase-form.basis: Kayn starts to show his full strength once he transforms. Shadow Assassin's assassination power is strongest from just after transforming through the mid game. Shadow Assassin dies easily in late teamfights. Darkin has underwhelming power immediately after transforming. Darkin gains strong teamfight sustain as he builds items.
kayn-phase-form.text: Kayn's power spike begins when he transforms. Shadow Assassin's assassination power peaks from immediately after transformation through the mid game, but he dies easily in late teamfights. Darkin is underwhelming right after transforming, then gains more teamfight sustain as he builds items, so your form affects when you should aim to end the game.

kayn-skill-e.basis: E lets Kayn pass through terrain. Nearby enemies see an indicator showing which wall Kayn entered with E. Don't wait inside the wall for long; exit as soon as you have an opening to engage. E's duration is greatly reduced while fighting enemy champions. Don't rely on E to escape during a fight.
kayn-skill-e.text: E (Shadow Step) lets Kayn pass through terrain, but nearby enemies see an indicator showing which wall he is inside. Don't wait there for long; emerge as soon as you have an opening. Its duration is greatly reduced while fighting enemy champions, so don't rely on it to escape a fight.

kayn-skill-e-form.basis: E ends immediately if Kayn is immobilized. E ends immediately if Kayn stays outside terrain for too long. Don't stay in a wall for long with E while the enemy still has a root or stun available. E grants increased movement speed in Shadow Assassin form. Shadow Assassin is immune to slows while using E.
kayn-skill-e-form.text: E (Shadow Step) ends immediately if Kayn is immobilized or stays outside terrain too long. An enemy root or stun can knock him out of a wall during his approach, so don't stay inside one for long while those abilities are available. In Shadow Assassin form, E also grants movement speed and slow immunity, letting him cross the same wall faster.

kayn-skill-passive-form.basis: Gain the orbs needed to transform by fighting enemy champions. Fighting melee champions grants Darkin orbs. Fighting ranged champions grants Shadow Assassin orbs. Plan your route around ganking the champion type that grants orbs for your desired form.
kayn-skill-passive-form.text: Choosing a form is Kayn's biggest decision. Fighting enemy champions grants transformation orbs: melee champions fill the Darkin (Rhaast) side, while ranged champions fill the Shadow Assassin side. If you want a particular form, plan your route around ganking that type of champion.

kayn-skill-passive-pick.basis: Choose your form based on both team compositions. Choose Shadow Assassin if the enemy has many squishy damage dealers and your team has a frontline. Choose Darkin if the enemy team is mostly melee or durable and fights will last longer; Darkin heals from ability damage. Darkin heals more when his abilities hit multiple enemies. Healing from hitting multiple enemies makes Darkin valuable in teamfight compositions.
kayn-skill-passive-pick.text: Choose your form based on both team compositions. Shadow Assassin suits a match with many squishy enemy damage dealers and an existing allied frontline; Darkin is better when the enemy team is mostly melee or durable and fights will last longer, since he heals from ability damage. Hitting multiple enemies with his abilities increases that healing, making him valuable in teamfight compositions.

kayn-skill-q.basis: Both the dash and strike of Q deal damage. Q deals bonus damage to minions and jungle monsters. Start camps with Q to clear them faster. Save Q just before a gank so you can close the gap. Don't enter the enemy jungle when both Q and E are on cooldown.
kayn-skill-q.text: Both the dash and strike of Q (Reaping Slash) deal damage, with bonus damage against minions and jungle monsters. Start camps with Q to clear faster, but save it to close the gap if you're about to gank. Since Q and E (Shadow Step) are Kayn's only movement tools, don't enter the enemy jungle with both on cooldown.

kayn-skill-w.basis: W is a linear ability with a cast animation. Predict the enemy's movement to land W. In a gank, land W first so its slow gives you room to chase even without Q. Before transforming, use W in ganks after an ally lands crowd control or the enemy uses their mobility ability.
kayn-skill-w.text: W (Blade's Reach) is a straight-line ability with a cast animation, so predict the enemy's movement to land it. Its slow lets you chase even without Q (Reaping Slash), making it a good first ability in a gank. Before transforming, a missed W can ruin the gank, so use it after an ally lands crowd control or the enemy has used their mobility ability.

kayn-skill-w-form.basis: Shadow Assassin can move while casting W. Rhaast's W knocks up enemies it hits. Shadow Assassin follows the enemy to narrow their dodge angle and land W. Rhaast looks to knock enemies up with W just before an ally engages.
kayn-skill-w-form.text: W (Blade's Reach) changes with Kayn's form: Shadow Assassin can move while casting it to extend its reach, while Rhaast knocks up enemies it hits. As Shadow Assassin, follow the enemy to narrow their dodge angle and land W; as Rhaast, aim to knock them up just before an ally engages.

kayn-teamfight.basis: Shadow Assassin should not start teamfights. After the enemy uses its crowd control, Shadow Assassin approaches from the flank or rear with E. Shadow Assassin focuses on one damage dealer in teamfights. After killing a damage dealer, Shadow Assassin uses R's untargetable window to disengage.
kayn-teamfight.text: Shadow Assassin should not start teamfights. Once the enemy has used its crowd control, flank or circle behind them with E (Shadow Step), focus on one damage dealer, and use R's (Umbral Trespass) untargetable window to disengage after the kill. Entering at the wrong time can get you killed before you accomplish anything.

kayn-teamfight-rhaast.basis: Darkin stays up front, hitting multiple enemies with his abilities and sustaining through healing. Darkin looks for angles to hit as many enemies as possible with W and R. Darkin enters after the enemy uses its key crowd control on his team's frontline. Darkin relies on healing to survive. Darkin should be more cautious about engaging if the enemy has healing reduction.
kayn-teamfight-rhaast.text: Darkin fights up front, hitting multiple enemies with abilities and sustaining through healing. Look for angles that catch as many enemies as possible with W (Blade's Reach) and R (Umbral Trespass), and enter after the enemy has used its key crowd control on your frontline. Since healing is his only means of survival, engage more cautiously against enemies with healing reduction.

kennen-combo-stun.basis: For the basic stun combo, land Q, use a basic attack with W's passive ready, then cast W. Use your abilities in the right order to complete the stun with three marks.
kennen-combo-stun.text: For the basic stun combo, land Q for the first mark, use a basic attack with W’s passive ready for the second, then cast W for the third. Keep that order to secure the stun; using your abilities haphazardly lets the marks go to waste.

kennen-combo-teamfight.basis: For a teamfight combo, enter with E, then use R, W, and Q in that order. Use R immediately after entering to give the marks time to build up for an area stun. Hitting at least one enemy with E restores energy. When entering with E, choose a path that passes through at least one enemy.
kennen-combo-teamfight.text: In a teamfight, enter with E, then use R, W, and Q in that order. Activate R immediately so its repeated marks have time to build toward an area stun. E restores energy if it hits at least one enemy, letting you use the next ability right away, so choose an entry path that passes through someone.

kennen-laning-poke.basis: Against melee opponents, use your range to poke only with Q. Keep the opponent at no more than two marks until they step up for a last hit. When the opponent steps forward for a last hit, complete the stun with a basic attack and W.
kennen-laning-poke.text: Against melee opponents, use your range to poke with Q alone. Keep them at no more than two marks, then complete the stun with a basic attack and W when they step forward for a last hit. Stunning them early wastes the chance to follow up with damage.

kennen-laning-wave.basis: W's passive lets you clear waves with basic attacks alone, without casting abilities. Kennen relies on E to escape, so pushing the lane without vision leaves him vulnerable to ganks. After pushing the lane, secure river vision first. After pushing the lane, save E to respond to a gank.
kennen-laning-wave.text: W’s passive lets you clear waves with basic attacks alone. Since E is Kennen’s only escape, pushing without vision leaves him vulnerable to ganks. After pushing, secure river vision first and keep E ready to respond to a gank.

kennen-phase.basis: Kennen is strong against melee opponents early by focusing his ability points on Q for poke. Look for your first solo kill at level 6, when you learn R. Kennen peaks in the mid game when he has both an engage item and ability power. Late game Kennen depends heavily on making a single engage work.
kennen-phase.text: Putting points into Q for poke makes Kennen strong against melee opponents early, and level 6 gives him his first chance at a solo kill when R becomes available. He peaks in the mid game with an engage item and ability power. Late in the game, his health is among the lowest of all champions, so making one successful engage becomes crucial.

kennen-situational-banshee.basis: If the enemy's damage is mostly magic, add Banshee's Veil between core items. Choose Banshee's Veil to block the first targeted ability that hits you as you enter.
kennen-situational-banshee.text: If the enemy’s damage is mostly magic, fit Banshee’s Veil between your core items. Kennen tends to take a targeted ability as soon as he enters, and blocking that first hit is worth more than the magic resistance alone.

kennen-skill-e.basis: You can pass through units during E. E applies a mark to enemies you pass through. Your attack speed increases when E ends. Hitting at least one enemy with E restores energy. Decide in advance whether to use E, your only escape, to enter or to leave.
kennen-skill-e.text: E lets Kennen pass through units and marks enemies he passes through, then grants attack speed when it ends. Decide whether to use it to enter or escape, since it is his only way out. Hitting at least one enemy restores energy and makes an engage efficient, but Kennen is vulnerable to being caught once E is gone.

kennen-skill-passive.basis: Three stacks of Mark of the Storm stun the target. Mark of the Storm stacks expire over time. When applying the second mark, check that you still have a way to apply the third. If you have no way to apply the third mark, delay applying the first.
kennen-skill-passive.text: Three stacks of Mark of the Storm stun the target, but the stacks expire over time. Before applying the second mark, make sure you can follow with a third; if you cannot, it is better to delay the first mark altogether.

kennen-skill-q.basis: Q hits only the first enemy it strikes. Use Q as your main poke tool in lane. When using Q to apply a mark, prioritize landing it over dealing damage. Q's cooldown drops significantly as you level it up.
kennen-skill-q.text: Q hits only the first enemy it strikes, so it cannot reach an opponent standing behind minions. Use it as your main lane poke and to apply the first mark, prioritizing a hit over damage when the mark is your goal. Its cooldown drops significantly as you level it, letting you poke more often.

kennen-skill-r.basis: R repeatedly damages nearby enemies throughout its duration. R repeatedly applies marks to nearby enemies, causing an area stun. Kennen gains armor during R. Kennen gains magic resistance during R. Save R if your angle would only catch one enemy.
kennen-skill-r.text: R repeatedly damages and marks all nearby enemies throughout its duration, setting up an area stun while granting Kennen armor and magic resistance. It helps him survive after entering the middle of the enemy team, so save it if your angle would catch only one enemy.

kennen-skill-w.basis: W's passive adds damage to a basic attack after a set number of attacks. A basic attack empowered by W's passive applies a mark to the target. Casting W attacks nearby marked enemies all at once. Use the basic attack empowered by W's passive before casting W.
kennen-skill-w.text: W’s passive periodically adds damage and a mark to a basic attack, while casting W hits nearby marked enemies at once. Use the empowered basic attack before casting W; casting it before the passive is ready leaves you with only one mark.

kennen-teamfight-entry.basis: Before activating R, find an angle to enter where the opponents are grouped. Enter only when an ally has caught an enemy or you can flank from outside their vision. Avoid walking in from the front, where you could be caught before activating R.
kennen-teamfight-entry.text: Before activating R, find an angle into a group of opponents. Enter only when an ally has caught an enemy or you can flank from outside their vision; walking in from the front risks getting caught before you can activate R.

kennen-teamfight-exit.basis: Save E to escape after landing an area stun with R. If you use E to enter, check that your allies can follow immediately.
kennen-teamfight-exit.text: Hold E after activating R to land an area stun and get out. If you use E to engage, your allies need to follow immediately; otherwise, you’ll land the stun and be left alone. Deciding whether to use E to engage or escape is the key choice in Kennen’s teamfights.

khazix-combo-assassination.basis: Start an isolated-target assassination by breaking vision with a brush or R to activate Unseen Threat. As soon as E lands, attack with Q, an empowered basic attack, then W. Use Q immediately after E so Leap’s landing damage and Q hit together.
khazix-combo-assassination.text: Start an isolated-target assassination from outside the enemy’s vision: use brush or R to activate Unseen Threat, then close in with E and use Q → empowered basic attack → W as soon as you land. Use Q immediately after E so its damage overlaps with Leap’s landing damage, without another action between them.

khazix-combo-gank.basis: When ganking, it is usually better to save E instead of using it to engage. For a gank, walk in, slow the target with W, then attack with Q. Save E to follow the target’s Flash or to escape. If you use E first, it is hard to chase when the target Flashes.
khazix-combo-gank.text: When ganking, it is usually better to walk in, slow the target with W, and use Q up close while saving E to follow their Flash or escape. If you use E to engage, you cannot follow when the target Flashes.

khazix-combo-r-reload.basis: Disappearing from sight with R during a fight refreshes Unseen Threat. After disappearing with R, move to the side, then follow up with an empowered basic attack and Q. Use R to repeat your combo, not just to escape.
khazix-combo-r-reload.text: R’s Void Assault lets Kha’Zix escape or refresh Unseen Threat by disappearing from enemy vision during a fight. Use R, move to the side, then follow with an empowered basic attack and Q to repeat the combo; saving R only for escape gives up that damage.

khazix-gank-angle.basis: When ganking, avoid the river entrance, wait behind a wall, then cross it with E. E’s Leap can cross terrain. Look for a moment when the wave is pushing toward the enemy turret and the target is separated from allied minions.
khazix-gank-angle.text: Set up ganks from beyond a wall. E’s Leap crosses terrain, so avoid river entrances the enemy has vision of, wait behind a wall, then jump over. If the target is close to allied minions, they are not isolated and the chance of a kill is lower, so look for a moment when the wave has pushed toward the enemy turret.

khazix-jungle-path.basis: Path through the jungle to create isolated targets. An enemy ahead of the wave in a side lane is isolated. An enemy jungler clearing a camp alone is also isolated. If you can read the enemy jungler’s path, take a camp on the opposite side and leave.
khazix-jungle-path.text: Choose jungle paths that create isolated targets: an enemy ahead of the wave in a side lane or a jungler clearing a camp alone can be isolated. Kha’Zix is strong in a one-on-one encounter in the enemy jungle, and if you can read the opposing jungler’s path, taking a camp on the opposite side and leaving gives you an advantage.

khazix-phase.basis: Level 6, when Kha'Zix gains his first evolution, is his first power spike. Before level 6, spend time on camps and vision instead of forcing fights. Kha'Zix reaches his peak strength in the mid game when he has two or more evolutions. If enemies keep grouping in the late game, isolated targets disappear and Kha'Zix’s impact drops sharply. As the game goes late, create chances to catch enemies who split off.
khazix-phase.text: Level 6, when Kha’Zix gains his first evolution, is his first power spike. Until then, spend time on camps and vision instead of forcing early fights. He is strongest in the mid game with two or more evolutions, but his impact drops sharply if enemies stay grouped late and leave no isolated targets. As the game goes on, focus on catching enemies who split off rather than teamfighting.

khazix-situational-antiheal.basis: An assassination target is hard to kill if their healing offsets your burst damage. Against an assassination target with healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items.
khazix-situational-antiheal.text: If an assassination target can heal enough to offset your burst damage, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items.

khazix-skill-evolve-e.basis: Evolving E increases Leap’s range. Evolved E resets its cooldown when you participate in a champion takedown. Use evolved E’s reset to escape after an assassination or move to the next target. Prioritize evolving E more when the enemy formation is tight and escaping after engaging will be difficult.
khazix-skill-evolve-e.text: Evolving E increases Leap’s range and resets its cooldown when you participate in a champion takedown. The extra range opens more ways to engage, while the reset lets you escape after an assassination or move straight to the next target. Prioritize E more when the enemy formation is tight and escaping after you engage will be difficult.

khazix-skill-evolve-q.basis: Each time you rank up R, evolve one ability for an added effect. Evolving Q increases the range of Q and basic attacks. Using evolved Q on an isolated target reduces its cooldown. Choose Q as your default first evolution to attack from outside counterattack range and clear camps faster.
khazix-skill-evolve-q.text: Each time you rank up R, you can evolve one ability for an added effect. Evolving Q increases the range of Q and basic attacks and reduces Q’s cooldown against isolated targets, making it a good default first evolution for dealing damage from beyond counterattack range and clearing camps faster.

khazix-skill-evolve-r.basis: Evolving R increases its stealth duration. Evolving R increases its number of uses. Consider evolving R if you need to engage twice in a teamfight. Consider evolving R if dense enemy vision makes approaching difficult. Lower the priority of R evolution when you only need to assassinate one target.
khazix-skill-evolve-r.text: Evolving R extends its stealth duration and gives it more uses, letting you engage, leave, and reengage once more. Consider it when you need to enter a teamfight twice or dense enemy vision makes approaching difficult; give it lower priority when assassinating one target is enough.

khazix-skill-evolve-w.basis: Evolving W fires spikes in three directions. Evolving W adds a slow and reveals targets. Evolved W slows isolated targets more strongly. Choose W evolution when you need to poke because you cannot get close. Choose W evolution when you need to catch a fleeing target. Choose W evolution when enemies group up and isolation is hard to create.
khazix-skill-evolve-w.text: Evolving W fires spikes in three directions, adds a slow, and reveals targets; the slow is stronger against isolated enemies. Choose it when you can only poke from a distance, need to keep a fleeing target within reach, or face grouped enemies who are hard to isolate.

khazix-skill-isolation.basis: Kha'Zix’s decision to fight depends heavily on whether the target is isolated. An isolation marker appears when no allied units are near the target. Q deals nearly double damage to an isolated target. Check for the isolation marker on screen before engaging. Do not expect an isolated Q against a target near a wave, allied units, or jungle monsters.
khazix-skill-isolation.text: Kha’Zix’s decision to fight hinges on isolation: a marker appears when no allied units are near the target, and Q deals nearly double damage to a marked target. Check the visible marker before engaging; an enemy near a wave, allied units, or jungle monsters is not isolated.

khazix-skill-w-sustain.basis: Kha'Zix heals if he is within W’s explosion radius. When clearing the jungle, fire W close to the monster to reduce health loss.
khazix-skill-w-sustain.text: Void Spike (W) heals Kha’Zix when he is within its explosion radius. Fire it while close to a monster during jungle clears to reduce health loss.

khazix-teamfight.basis: Do not engage a teamfight from the front. Wait on the flank or behind the enemy, then engage when an enemy backline damage dealer separates from the formation. Engage after the enemy has used their targeted crowd control. After engaging, break vision with R, pull back, then go in again. Do not stay in a fight hitting a tank with unevolved abilities.
khazix-teamfight.text: Wait on a flank or behind the enemy rather than entering a teamfight from the front, and engage only when a backline damage dealer separates from the formation and the enemy has used their targeted crowd control. After engaging, break vision with R, pull back, and go in again. Do not remain in the fight hitting a tank with unevolved abilities.

kindred-combo-basic.basis: Apply E, weave in Q, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Wolf's pounce. Q's attack speed boost helps you meet the conditions for Wolf's pounce faster. Don't switch targets while building stacks for E's pounce.
kindred-combo-basic.text: Apply E to a target, weave in Q for its attack speed boost, and keep basic attacking that same target to trigger Wolf's pounce sooner. Switching targets resets E's progress, so stay focused on one target.

kindred-combo-w-zone.basis: In a fight, place W first, then use Q repeatedly inside its zone to reposition. Q's cooldown is much shorter inside W's zone. Wolf only fights inside W's zone. Place W where the enemy will stand.
kindred-combo-w-zone.text: Place W where the enemy will stand before starting a fight. Inside its zone, Q's cooldown is much shorter, letting you reposition repeatedly, and Wolf can only fight there. Using W first improves both damage and survival; stepping outside its zone interrupts your Q rotations.

kindred-ganking.basis: With only E's slow for crowd control, it's hard to make a gank work alone. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far up the lane. If gank conditions are poor, clear vision and apply pressure by counterjungling. Dying from an overaggressive early engage severely disrupts your mark progress.
kindred-ganking.text: With only E's slow for crowd control, Kindred struggles to make a gank work alone. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or an enemy has pushed too far up the lane; otherwise, clear vision and pressure through counterjungling. Kindred is prone to early deaths, and one overaggressive engage can derail mark progress.

kindred-jungle-pathing.basis: Low movement speed makes wasted trips costly. Plan a route that clears camps toward the mark. If a gank is uncertain, use W's bonus monster damage to farm and counterjungle for marks.
kindred-jungle-pathing.text: Kindred has some of the lowest movement speed in the game, so wasted trips are costly. Check where the mark appears and clear camps toward it instead of walking in the opposite direction and doubling back. W (Wolf's Frenzy) helps clear camps quickly with its bonus monster damage, so when a gank is uncertain, farming and counterjungling for marks is the better bet.

kindred-phase.basis: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, making encounters with the enemy jungler easy to lose. In the mid game, Kindred can duel once marks have stacked up and attack speed items are ready. Once marks start increasing Kindred's range, Kindred can fight melee champions without taking hits back. If you don't collect marks on time, it's hard to make use of Kindred's mid-game power spike. Early on, prioritize marks and farming over fights.
kindred-phase.text: Early Kindred is fragile and slow, making encounters with the enemy jungler easy to lose. Duels become viable in the mid game after Kindred gains several marks and attack speed items; once marks begin increasing their range, they can fight melee champions without taking hits back. Missing marks on time can erase that growth, so prioritize marks and farming over early fights.

kindred-situational-antiheal.basis: Build Grievous Wounds against enemies with strong healing. Kindred deals sustained damage with basic attacks, so Mortal Reminder provides armor penetration and Grievous Wounds together with less disruption to the core item build.
kindred-situational-antiheal.text: Build Grievous Wounds against strong healing. Because Kindred deals sustained damage through basic attacks, Mortal Reminder provides both armor penetration and Grievous Wounds while disrupting the core build less.

kindred-skill-e.basis: E slows the enemy. E's Wolf's pounce deals more damage the more health the enemy is missing. Apply E as you engage, then use basic attacks to meet the conditions for the pounce. If the enemy looks likely to escape with a mobility ability, use E first for the slow.
kindred-skill-e.text: E slows enemies and sets up Wolf's pounce, which deals more damage the more health its target is missing. The pounce is stronger later in a fight, but its conditions cannot build until E is applied, so applying it as you engage and following with basic attacks is the reliable approach. Use E early for the slow if the enemy looks ready to escape with a mobility ability.

kindred-skill-passive.basis: You gain a mark for participating in a takedown, and each mark is permanent. Marks strengthen your basic abilities. Collecting enough marks increases your basic attack range. In the first few minutes, focus on securing marks over kills.
kindred-skill-passive.text: Kindred's growth depends on marks: participating in a takedown grants one, and each permanent mark strengthens their basic abilities. Collecting enough also increases basic attack range, so prioritize marks over kills in the first few minutes. Missing two or three marks can leave Kindred unable to fill a ranged damage dealer's role later.

kindred-skill-passive-choice.basis: Kindred can choose which champion to mark. When an enemy jungle monster is marked, work counterjungling into your route. When you mark a champion, work a gank on that lane into your route. The enemy can also see that they have been marked. Only go for a mark deep in unseen enemy territory when your team has lane priority.
kindred-skill-passive-choice.text: The champion you choose to mark shapes your route: a marked enemy jungle monster gives you a reason to counterjungle, while marking a champion gives you a reason to gank their lane. Enemies can see marks too, so the opposing jungler may be waiting. Only pursue a mark deep in unseen enemy territory when your allies have lane priority.

kindred-skill-q.basis: Q is a short leap that fires arrows, useful for both dodging and attacking. Outside W's zone, save Q for escaping because its cooldown is long. Inside W's zone, use Q often because its cooldown is short. While clearing the jungle, use Q between monster attacks to reposition and take fewer hits.
kindred-skill-q.text: Q combines a short leap with arrow damage, making it useful for both dodging and attacking. Save it for an escape outside W's zone, where its cooldown is long; inside the zone, its short cooldown makes frequent use worthwhile. While clearing, reposition with Q between monster attacks to take fewer hits.

kindred-skill-r-basic.basis: R creates a zone at the chosen location where allies, enemies, and monsters cannot die. A target whose health falls near zero inside R's zone takes no damage or healing until the zone ends. Everyone inside the zone is healed when R ends. Use R to make the enemy waste a finishing ability and Ignite.
kindred-skill-r-basic.text: R creates a zone at a chosen location where allies, enemies, and monsters cannot die. Once someone's health falls near zero inside it, they receive neither damage nor healing until the zone ends, when everyone still inside is healed. Use it to waste an enemy finishing ability or Ignite.

kindred-skill-r-timing.basis: R also saves enemies. Activate R right after an enemy engages on your team's main damage dealer. At an objective, activate R as the enemy comes in to use Smite. Lower the enemy's health while R is active. Finish the enemy as R's zone ends.
kindred-skill-r-timing.text: Timing is everything with R (Lamb's Respite) because it saves enemies too: use it too early and you may spare an opponent your team was about to kill; use it too late and your allies may already be dead. Activate it just after an enemy engages on your team's main damage dealer, or as an opponent moves in to use Smite at an objective. Keep dealing damage inside the zone to lower the enemy's health, then finish them as it ends.

kindred-skill-w.basis: W's Wolf deals bonus damage to jungle monsters. When clearing a camp, place W in the middle so Wolf can attack. Once movement and attacks fully stack your passive, your next basic attack heals you based on your missing health. When low on health, use the healing from your passive stacks to keep clearing camps.
kindred-skill-w.text: W is central to both damage and clear speed. Wolf deals extra damage to jungle monsters but attacks only inside the zone, so place W in the middle of a camp. Movement and attacks also build passive stacks; once full, your next basic attack heals you based on your missing health. Using that heal when low can let you clear another camp.

kindred-teamfight.basis: Don't engage first in a teamfight. After your team starts the fight, place W behind your allies, then reposition with Q inside its zone while basic attacking. Don't stand at the front while the enemy still has an engage ability available.
kindred-teamfight.text: Do not engage first in a teamfight. Once your allies start the fight, place W behind them and basic attack while repositioning with Q inside its zone. Kindred has low health and only R as a reliable way to avoid death, so standing at the front while an enemy engage ability is available can leave you unable to contribute, regardless of your marks.

kled-combo-basic.basis: Engage with E, land Q, hit four W-enhanced basic attacks, then recast E to disengage. E's recast only goes toward the target hit by the first cast. To use E's recast to disengage, hit your opponent with the first E.
kled-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, use E (Jousting) to close the gap and land Q (Bear Trap on a Rope), then stay close while attacking with W (Violent Tendencies) active. Once Q pulls the target in, finish W’s fourth hit with your remaining basic attacks and recast E to disengage. The recast travels only toward the target hit by the first E, so you must land that cast on your opponent if you want to use it to get out.

kled-combo-q-hold.basis: After landing Q, stay close for a short time to trigger the pull and heavy damage. As soon as Q lands, use E or W to stay close to your opponent. If your opponent uses a mobility ability to get out of Q's range, the follow-up effect is lost.
kled-combo-q-hold.text: Landing Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) is only the start: stay close for a short time afterward to trigger its pull and heavy damage. Use E (Jousting) or W (Violent Tendencies) to keep up as soon as the trap lands, since your opponent will try to escape. If they use a mobility ability to get out of range, the follow-up effect is lost.

kled-laning.basis: Kled is strong at trading from level 1. If Skaarl is nearly out of health, back off instead of trading and build Courage. Encountering the enemy jungler while dismounted can easily get Kled killed.
kled-laning.text: Kled trades well from level 1 thanks to his high attack damage, but his own health is the lowest of any champion. Treat Skaarl’s health bar as his effective health: if Skaarl is nearly depleted, back off instead of trading and build Courage. An enemy jungler arriving while Kled is dismounted can kill him outright.

kled-laning-wave.basis: Step forward in lane when Q is available. Without Q, you cannot hold your opponent in place, making trades difficult. While Q is unavailable, use E to pull the wave and keep the lane on your side. While Q is unavailable, use basic attacks to reduce W's cooldown. If you win a trade, pressure the turret to turn it into an advantage.
kled-laning-wave.text: Step forward in lane when Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) is available; without the trap, Kled has no way to hold an opponent in place for a trade. While Q is unavailable, use E (Jousting) to pull the wave toward your side and basic attacks to reduce W (Violent Tendencies)’s cooldown. After winning a trade, turn that advantage into turret pressure.

kled-phase.basis: Kled is strongest during laning and mid-game skirmishes. In late-game teamfights, Skaarl can be lost easily after an R engage, and Kled's reduced champion damage while dismounted weakens his sustained damage. Build on an early lead and decide the game through turrets and objectives in the mid game.
kled-phase.text: Kled peaks in lane and mid-game skirmishes, where early kills and turret plates can build a lead. In late-game teamfights, he can lose Skaarl soon after engaging with R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!), and his reduced champion damage while dismounted weakens his sustained damage. Build on your early lead and aim to decide the game through turrets and objectives in the mid game.

kled-situational-antiheal.basis: If your opponent's healing lets them withstand W's maximum-health damage, buy Executioner's Calling earlier. Kled stays close and keeps attacking, so he can apply Grievous Wounds consistently.
kled-situational-antiheal.text: If an opponent’s healing lets them survive W (Violent Tendencies)’s maximum-health damage, buy Executioner’s Calling earlier. Kled stays close and keeps attacking, making it easy to apply Grievous Wounds consistently.

kled-situational-mr.basis: Against magic damage, Skaarl can be lost in an instant. If the enemy's main damage is magic, buy Maw of Malmortius between core items for its shield and magic resistance to help you survive after dismounting.
kled-situational-mr.text: Kled’s level 1 magic resistance is among the lowest, so magic damage can strip away Skaarl quickly. If the enemy’s main damage is magic, fit Maw of Malmortius between your core items; its shield and magic resistance help you survive after dismounting.

kled-skill-courage.basis: Attacking champions builds Courage fastest. You can also build Courage by attacking epic monsters or structures, or by killing minions. When Courage fills, Skaarl returns with restored health and Kled remounts. If you have nowhere to run while dismounted, attack a turret or minion wave to fill your Courage bar. If you can stay close to your opponent while dismounted, attack them to build Courage quickly.
kled-skill-courage.text: Attacking champions builds Courage fastest, though attacking epic monsters or structures and killing minions also fills the bar. Once it is full, Skaarl returns with restored health and Kled remounts, effectively gaining a second health bar. If you have nowhere to run while dismounted, attack a turret or minion wave for Courage; if you can stay close to an opponent, attack them to build it much faster.

kled-skill-dismount.basis: When Skaarl runs out of health, Kled dismounts. Dismounted Kled has very low health and deals less damage to champions. Dismounted Kled gains movement speed when moving toward enemy champions. Dismounted Kled gains armor and magic resistance based on the number of nearby enemy champions. When you dismount, stay close to enemies to build Courage.
kled-skill-dismount.text: When Skaarl runs out of health, Kled dismounts, leaving him with very low health and reduced damage against champions. He gains movement speed toward enemy champions, plus armor and magic resistance based on how many are nearby. Stay close and attack to build Courage after dismounting; running away at this point weakens him most.

kled-skill-e.basis: As Kled dashes, E pulls minions and small monsters in front of him. Use E to pull a minion wave or group a jungle camp. Hitting a champion or large monster with E grants movement speed. If E hits a champion or large monster, you can recast it shortly afterward to return to that target. Use E to dash out and dodge an opponent's ability, then recast it to return.
kled-skill-e.text: E (Jousting) pulls minions and small monsters in front of Kled as he dashes, letting you draw a wave toward you or group a jungle camp. Hitting a champion or large monster grants movement speed and allows a recast shortly afterward toward the same target. You can use that return trip to avoid an opponent’s ability and then go back in.

kled-skill-pistol.basis: While dismounted, Q becomes Pocket Pistol, a ranged attack that knocks Kled backward when cast. Pocket Pistol's recoil pushes you opposite the direction you aim. Right after dismounting, aim Pocket Pistol so its recoil pushes you toward your escape route. You can build Courage with Pocket Pistol while escaping.
kled-skill-pistol.text: While dismounted, Q becomes Pocket Pistol, a ranged attack whose recoil pushes Kled backward, opposite the direction he aims. Aim at an opponent to retreat while building Courage, and immediately after dismounting, account for the recoil so it carries you toward your escape route. Pocket Pistol is your only way to build Courage while fleeing.

kled-skill-r.basis: Because R starts from far away, cast it based on where the enemy team will be when you arrive. R's shield forms during the charge and lasts briefly after it ends. Use R's shield to survive the burst combo that hits right after you engage. R charges only the first enemy champion along its path.
kled-skill-r.text: Because R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) can start from very far away, aim for where the enemy team will be when you arrive. Its shield forms during the charge and lasts briefly afterward, helping you survive the burst that follows your engage. Skaarl charges only the first enemy champion along the path, so you cannot pass a tank to hit the back line.

kled-skill-w.basis: W's fourth attack deals damage based on the target's maximum health. Activate W when you can land all four basic attacks. Each basic attack reduces W's cooldown, and hitting a champion reduces it further. Stay close to your opponent during a fight and keep using basic attacks to get W back.
kled-skill-w.text: W (Violent Tendencies) puts maximum-health damage on its fourth landed attack, so activate it when you can land all four rather than when your opponent is about to escape. Every basic attack reduces W’s cooldown, with a larger reduction against champions; staying close and continuing to attack during a fight can bring it back for another use.

kled-teamfight.basis: Start teamfights with R. Use R along a path your allies can follow with its movement speed boost. Even if you lose Skaarl after engaging, stay in the skirmish to build Courage instead of retreating immediately. After engaging with R, survive the skirmish and remount to start a second fight.
kled-teamfight.text: Open teamfights with R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) along a path your allies can follow, since they also gain movement speed on its route. If Skaarl is lost after the engage, stay in the skirmish to build Courage instead of retreating immediately. Survive long enough to remount and start a second fight.

kogmaw-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, activate W, auto-attack, land Q, then keep auto-attacking. Activating W first lets you start auto-attacking from outside the enemy's response range. Use Q after closing in so its resistance reduction overlaps with W's on-hit damage. If you throw Q first, W's duration runs down while the enemy backs away.
kogmaw-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, activate W and start auto-attacking from outside the enemy’s response range, then use Q once you’ve closed in so its armor and magic resistance reduction overlaps with W’s on-hit damage. Keep auto-attacking afterward; if you use Q first, W’s duration runs down while the enemy backs away.

kogmaw-combo-finish.basis: Cut off the escape route with E, then fire R repeatedly to finish them off. R is most efficient when fired in a burst after the enemy's health drops below a certain point. Firing R repeatedly at a high-health enemy wastes mana.
kogmaw-combo-finish.text: To finish an enemy, cut off their escape route with E, then fire R repeatedly. R’s damage rises sharply once their health falls below a certain threshold, so a burst of shots is most efficient after they reach it; firing repeatedly at a high-health target only drains your mana.

kogmaw-combo-kite.basis: Walk backward, place E along your retreat path, then auto-attack again when the enemy is slowed. E leaves a trail where its projectile passes. Throw E ahead of where the enemy will move rather than aiming to hit them directly.
kogmaw-combo-kite.text: Kite by walking backward and placing E along your retreat path, then resume auto-attacking when the enemy steps on the trail and slows. Because E leaves a trail wherever its projectile passes, you do not need a direct hit; aim where the enemy is about to move.

kogmaw-laning.basis: Low movement speed and no mobility ability make him vulnerable to ganks. When W is down, position yourself behind the middle of the lane. Move forward only while W is active. Before moving forward, check both W's cooldown and the enemy jungler's position.
kogmaw-laning.text: Kog’Maw has some of the lowest movement speed among champions and no mobility ability, making him especially vulnerable to ganks. When W is down, stay behind the middle of the lane and move forward only while it is active. Always consider both W’s cooldown and the enemy jungler’s position before advancing.

kogmaw-laning-wave.basis: Do not force the wave forward. E hits every enemy in a line and can clear waves, but you also need it to escape ganks. Let the lane push toward you and farm near your turret. Push forward only where your support has established vision.
kogmaw-laning-wave.text: Do not force the wave forward. E can clear enemies in a line, but using it on the wave puts your gank escape slow on cooldown. Let the wave come to you, farm near your turret, and push forward only where your support has established vision.

kogmaw-phase.basis: Kog'Maw is weakest at levels 1–2. His range advantage grows as W gains levels. He is strong in the mid to late game once he has at least two attack speed and damage items. As a hypercarry who fights with range and attack speed, he benefits from longer games. Even if you fall behind early, you can recover by keeping up your farm.
kogmaw-phase.text: Kog’Maw is weakest at levels 1–2. His range advantage grows as W gains levels, and he peaks in the mid to late game once he has at least two attack speed and damage items. As a hypercarry built around range and attack speed, he benefits from longer games and can recover from an early deficit by continuing to farm.

kogmaw-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy's healing is enough to turn a fight, reduce it with Executioner's Calling. You can keep the healing reduction active with sustained auto-attacks.
kogmaw-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy’s healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce it. Kog’Maw’s sustained auto-attacks keep the healing reduction active.

kogmaw-situational-qss.basis: Getting caught once by reliable immobilizing crowd control can easily get you killed. If the enemy has reliable immobilizing crowd control, buy Mercurial Scimitar between core items.
kogmaw-situational-qss.text: Reliable immobilizing crowd control can kill Kog’Maw as soon as it catches him. Against it, fit Mercurial Scimitar between core items so you can free yourself.

kogmaw-skill-passive.basis: After dying, Kog'Maw briefly moves through units, then explodes to deal true damage. Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce his passive's explosion damage. If the enemy backs away, walk toward your allies or an objective in passive form to deny the area.
kogmaw-skill-passive.text: After dying, Kog’Maw can briefly move through units before exploding for true damage that armor and magic resistance cannot reduce. This is your last chance to deal damage; if enemies retreat, walk toward your allies or an objective to deny that area instead of chasing them.

kogmaw-skill-q.basis: Putting a point in Q grants attack speed through its passive. Landing Q reduces the target's armor and magic resistance. Q's resistance reduction also increases the damage your allies deal. Land Q on the enemy frontline just before a dragon or Rift Herald fight.
kogmaw-skill-q.text: A point in Q grants passive attack speed, while landing it reduces the target’s armor and magic resistance. That reduction also benefits your allies, so apply Q to the enemy frontline just before a dragon or Rift Herald fight to increase your team’s damage.

kogmaw-skill-r-mana.basis: Using R repeatedly in a short time increases its mana cost in steps. Spamming R for poke in lane leaves you short on mana for fights. Fire only one or two R shots for poke. Fire R repeatedly only when you can secure the finish. R reveals targets that are not stealthed, so you can use it to check brush.
kogmaw-skill-r-mana.text: R’s mana cost rises in steps when you cast it repeatedly within a short time. Spamming it for poke in lane can leave too little mana for a fight, so stop after one or two shots and fire repeatedly only when you can secure a kill. R also reveals targets that are not stealthed, making it useful for checking brush.

kogmaw-skill-w.basis: W increases your range for its duration and adds magic damage based on maximum health to your auto-attacks. W has a limited duration and a long cooldown. Using W to clear waves makes it hard to use its range advantage in a fight. W's damage against monsters has a cap. Most of your damage to objectives comes from auto-attacks and items.
kogmaw-skill-w.text: W defines Kog’Maw: it temporarily extends his range and adds magic damage based on maximum health to his auto-attacks, but it has a long cooldown. Spend it on wave clear and you lose its range advantage for the fight. Its damage against monsters is capped, so damage to objectives comes mainly from auto-attacks and items.

kogmaw-teamfight.basis: Attack enemies from behind your frontline using W's range. You have no way to escape enemies who dive onto you by yourself. Stay within range of your allies' protective abilities. If your frontline collapses, stop attacking and retreat.
kogmaw-teamfight.text: Kog’Maw’s condition for joining a fight is positioning: attack from behind your frontline at W range and stay within reach of your allies’ protective abilities, since you cannot escape a diver on your own. If your frontline collapses, stop dealing damage and retreat.

kogmaw-teamfight-target.basis: W's damage based on maximum health makes attacking a high-health enemy frontline worthwhile. Attack the nearest enemy in range instead of moving forward to target the backline.
kogmaw-teamfight-target.text: Because W deals damage based on maximum health, attacking a high-health frontline target is worthwhile. Moving forward to reach the backline can get you killed, so focus the nearest enemy within range.

ksante-combo-allin.basis: Build Q stacks, pull the enemy in with the shockwave, then chain a W stun, R toward a wall, E to close the gap again, an auto attack, and Q. Each ability leaves a passive mark. Weave an auto attack between abilities to get the full passive damage.
ksante-combo-allin.text: For a full combo, build Q stacks and pull the enemy in with the shockwave, stun them with W, drive them into a wall with R All Out, then use E to close the gap again and follow with auto attacks and Q. Each ability leaves a passive mark, so weave an auto attack between abilities to deal the full damage.

ksante-combo-q-shockwave.basis: Each Q hit builds a stack. At full stacks, the next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls in and stuns enemies. Hitting minions also builds Q stacks. Hit the wave with Q just before a fight to build stacks in advance.
ksante-combo-q-shockwave.text: Q Ntofo Strikes needs repeated casts to reach its full effect: each hit builds a stack, and at full stacks the next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls in and stuns enemies. Minions also grant stacks, so hit the wave with Q just before a fight to prepare the shockwave for your opponent.

ksante-combo-w-timing.basis: K'Sante is unstoppable while charging W. K'Sante takes reduced damage while charging W. Start charging W as the enemy's combo lands to reduce the damage. Charging W longer increases the stun duration. Only charge W for a long time after the enemy has used their mobility ability or been caught by the Q shockwave, so they cannot simply walk away.
ksante-combo-w-timing.text: While charging W Path Maker, K'Sante is unstoppable and takes reduced damage. Start charging as the enemy's combo lands to absorb the damage, then counterattack. A longer charge extends the stun but gives the enemy time to walk aside, so hold it only after they have used their mobility ability or been caught by the Q shockwave.

ksante-laning-farm.basis: Keep the wave in the middle of the lane instead of forcing a push. Last-hit minions with Q. Build Q stacks and catch the enemy with the shockwave only when they move among the minions. Focus on surviving and preventing the enemy jungler from intervening instead of repeatedly taking short trades.
ksante-laning-farm.text: K'Sante does not need to force the wave forward to win lane. Keep it in the middle and last-hit with Q, building stacks to catch your opponent with the shockwave only when they move among the minions. His damage output is relatively low, so surviving and keeping the enemy jungler from intervening is more valuable than repeatedly taking short trades to chip away at their health.

ksante-laning-trade.basis: After slowing the enemy with Q, proc the mark with an auto attack, then retreat with E if they fight back. Keep E available for disengaging so you have a way out after going in. Only use E to dive in right after the enemy uses a mobility ability or key ability.
ksante-laning-trade.text: Slow the enemy with Q, collect the mark with an auto attack, then retreat with E if they fight back. Save E primarily for disengaging, since using it to go in leaves you without a way out; dive in with E only immediately after the enemy uses a mobility ability or key ability.

ksante-phase.basis: Levels 1–2 are K'Sante's weakest point because he has only Q to rely on. Start trading at level 3, once you have W and E. At level 6, look for a solo kill when you can drive the enemy into terrain with R. K'Sante is strong in the mid game as defensive items improve Q's damage and cooldown. In the late game, focus on engaging and crowd control over damage.
ksante-phase.text: Levels 1–2 are K'Sante's weakest because he has only Q to rely on. Once W and E are available at level 3, he can trade; at level 6, look for a solo kill if you can drive the enemy into terrain with R. His strongest period is the mid game, when defensive items improve both Q's damage and cooldown. Late game, contribute through engages and crowd control more than damage.

ksante-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between defensive items. Because K'Sante spends a long time fighting up close in All Out, it is easy to keep applying a healing reduction item's effect.
ksante-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between defensive items. K'Sante spends extended periods fighting up close in All Out, making it easy to keep the healing reduction applied.

ksante-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy's main damage is magic, buy Spectre's Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. Magic resistance items provide defense while improving Q's damage and cooldown.
ksante-situational-mr.text: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, buy Spectre’s Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. K’Sante has relatively low base magic resistance, and because his Q damage and cooldown scale with magic resistance, these items improve both his defense and offensive power.

ksante-skill-e-ally.basis: Using E on an allied champion greatly increases its dash range. Using E on an allied champion also shields that ally. Save E to reach and shield an ally who gets caught.
ksante-skill-e-ally.text: Using E Footwork on an allied champion greatly extends the dash and shields that ally too. Keep it available to reach and shield a teammate who gets caught, rather than using it only to go in yourself.

ksante-skill-passive.basis: Proc the passive marks left by your abilities with auto attacks. Finish trades with an auto attack after an ability. In All Out, both auto attacks and abilities gain damage based on maximum health. In All Out, keep using abilities and stay on the enemy to attack.
ksante-skill-passive.text: Abilities leave passive marks that you collect by hitting the target with an auto attack. Casting an ability and backing away leaves much of that damage unused, so finish trades with an auto attack after an ability. During All Out, both auto attacks and abilities gain damage based on maximum health; keep using your abilities and stay close enough to attack.

ksante-skill-q-scaling.basis: Q deals more damage as armor and magic resistance increase. Q's cooldown decreases as armor and magic resistance increase. Prioritize defensive items over attack items to improve both Q's damage and cooldown.
ksante-skill-q-scaling.text: Q Ntofo Strikes gains damage and a shorter cooldown from both armor and magic resistance. Building defensive items improves both, so prioritizing them over attack items ultimately makes Q hit harder.

ksante-skill-r-transform.basis: Using R transforms K'Sante into his All Out form. If R pushes an enemy into a wall, they fly through it and take an additional hit. Use R on enemies with terrain behind them to get the additional hit. In All Out, K'Sante loses a large amount of maximum health and bonus armor and magic resistance. Only use R when the enemy's main crowd control is down and your team can follow up immediately.
ksante-skill-r-transform.text: R All Out transforms K'Sante. Pushing an enemy into a wall sends them through it and deals an extra hit, making R especially valuable when they have terrain behind them. All Out also sharply reduces K'Sante's maximum health, bonus armor, and magic resistance, turning him from a tank into a melee damage dealer. Even with defensive items, he is vulnerable during it, so activate R only when the enemy's main crowd control is down and your team can follow up immediately.

ksante-skill-r-upgrades.basis: In All Out, Q and E have shorter cooldowns. In All Out, E dashes faster. Entering All Out resets W's cooldown. In All Out, W gains true damage. In All Out, W does not knock back or stun enemies. Use all your crowd control for holding enemies in place before activating R. After entering All Out, focus on staying close to the enemy and attacking.
ksante-skill-r-upgrades.text: During All Out, Q and E have shorter cooldowns, E dashes faster, and W’s cooldown resets. W also gains true damage, but no longer knocks enemies back or stuns them. Use all your crowd control to hold enemies in place before activating R; afterward, focus on staying close and attacking.

ksante-teamfight-r.basis: In teamfights, prioritize using R to push one enemy backline damage dealer toward your team and isolate them. Using R in a teamfight also leaves K'Sante in the middle of the enemy team. K'Sante becomes less durable the moment he uses R. Only use R when your team is close enough to follow up immediately. If your team is not ready, save R and hold the front line with the Q shockwave and W stun.
ksante-teamfight-r.text: In teamfights, your first priority is to use R to push an enemy backline damage dealer toward your team and isolate them. Activating it also leaves K'Sante in the middle of the enemy team and makes him less durable, so do so only when your allies are close enough to follow up immediately. If they are not ready, save R and hold the front line with the Q shockwave and W stun.

leblanc-combo-basic.basis: The basic combo is to mark the target with Q, dash in with W to detonate the mark, then recast W to return. The Q mark detonates when you hit the target with another ability.
leblanc-combo-basic.text: The basic combo is to apply Q (Sigil of Malice), dash in with W (Distortion) to detonate the mark, then recast W to return. The mark only detonates when another ability hits the target, so landing Q alone deals only half the damage.

leblanc-combo-e-lock.basis: As the E root activates, use Q, then W. E roots the target after the chain remains attached for a while. Stay within chain range until the E root activates.
leblanc-combo-e-lock.text: The most reliable combo is to land E (Ethereal Chains), then use Q (Sigil of Malice) into W (Distortion) as the root activates. The chain must remain attached for a while before it roots, so stay within its range until then.

leblanc-combo-full.basis: The full combo is to dash in with W, use Q and R, then return with W. R mimics your most recently used ability. Use the ability you want to mimic immediately before R.
leblanc-combo-full.text: The full combo is W in → Q → R to mimic W and detonate the mark → W back. R mimics the most recently used ability, so place the ability you want to mimic immediately before it; otherwise, R will mimic a different ability.

leblanc-combo-w-return.basis: You can return with W only for a short time after the dash. Check that your W return point is safe before going in. Choose whether to go in again or return with W based on the enemy's remaining counterattack abilities. If you miss the W return window, you cannot use it to escape.
leblanc-combo-w-return.text: W (Distortion) lets you return only for a short time after dashing. Check that the return point is safe before going in, then decide whether to press forward or return based on the enemy’s remaining counterattack abilities. If the return window expires, you lose that escape option.

leblanc-laning-push.basis: Clear the wave quickly with Q, then join fights in a side lane or the jungle. Stay in lane if you have not pushed the wave.
leblanc-laning-push.text: Push the wave before roaming. Clear it quickly with Q, then join a fight in a side lane or the jungle; stay in lane if you have not pushed the wave.

leblanc-laning-trade.basis: Trade damage only right after the enemy uses a key ability. Repeat short trades by going in with W and returning. Go in only while your W return is available.
leblanc-laning-trade.text: Trade only right after the enemy uses a key ability. LeBlanc is fragile and loses extended damage trades, so keep exchanges short: go in with W (Distortion) and return every time. Never engage unless the W return is available.

leblanc-phase.basis: LeBlanc is strongest from just after she learns R at level 6 through the mid game. Kill opportunities are most frequent from just after level 6 through the mid game. In the late game, once enemies have magic resistance and vision, LeBlanc is vulnerable to counterattacks if an assassination fails. If LeBlanc cannot build a lead earlier, her late-game impact drops sharply.
leblanc-phase.text: LeBlanc is strongest from just after learning R (Mimic) at level 6 through the mid game, when kill opportunities are most frequent. Late in the game, enemies have magic resistance and vision, and a failed assassination leaves her vulnerable to a counterattack; without an earlier lead, her impact drops sharply.

leblanc-situational-banshee.basis: If the enemy mid laner is a mage with targeted burst damage, choose Banshee's Veil to block the first ability in their combo. LeBlanc cannot counterattack once she is locked down.
leblanc-situational-banshee.text: If the enemy mid laner is a mage with targeted burst damage, buy Banshee’s Veil to block the first ability in their combo. Once LeBlanc is locked down, she cannot counterattack, so blocking that opening ability changes the fight.

leblanc-skill-e-aim.basis: E's chain must stay connected for 1.5 seconds to root the target. Casting E straight at the enemy makes the chain easy to break. Cast E from a bush or behind minions while out of sight. Use W to get beside the enemy and narrow the angle, then cast E. Landing E grants true sight of the target. Use the vision from landing E to track a fleeing enemy.
leblanc-skill-e-aim.text: E (Ethereal Chains) must stay connected for 1.5 seconds to root, so a straight shot is easy to break. Cast from a bush or behind minions while out of sight, or use W (Distortion) to get beside the enemy and narrow the angle before casting. Landing E also grants true sight, which helps you track a fleeing target.

leblanc-skill-passive-clone.basis: P briefly makes you invisible when your health falls below a certain threshold. P creates a clone when your health falls below a certain threshold. You can control the clone created by P separately. When escaping, send the clone in the opposite direction to confuse pursuers.
leblanc-skill-passive-clone.text: P (Mirror Image) briefly turns LeBlanc invisible and creates a clone when her health falls below a certain threshold. You can control the clone separately; when escaping, send it in the opposite direction to throw off pursuers.

leblanc-skill-q.basis: If the Q hit or mark detonation kills the target, all mana spent is refunded. If the Q hit or mark detonation kills the target, Q's remaining cooldown is reduced. Use the refund on kills to clear the wave or secure last hits with Q.
leblanc-skill-q.text: If a Q (Sigil of Malice) hit or mark detonation kills the target, it refunds all the mana spent and reduces Q’s remaining cooldown. That makes Q relatively inexpensive for clearing waves or securing last hits, letting you push the lane quickly.

leblanc-skill-r-choice.basis: When a kill is certain, use R to mimic Q. If you need another engage or an escape, use R to mimic W. If you need guaranteed crowd control, use R to mimic E. Decide which ability R will mimic before starting your combo.
leblanc-skill-r-choice.text: Choose what R (Mimic) will copy before starting your combo: copy Q (Sigil of Malice) when a kill is certain, W (Distortion) when you need another engage or escape, or E (Ethereal Chains) when you need guaranteed crowd control.

leblanc-teamfight.basis: Avoid going in first in a head-on teamfight. After the fight starts and the enemy focuses on your allied tank, go in from the side. Before going in, pick one enemy backliner to eliminate. After eliminating your target, disengage with W.
leblanc-teamfight.text: Do not go in first in a head-on teamfight. Once the fight starts and the enemy focuses on your allied tank, enter from the side, eliminate one chosen backliner, then disengage with W (Distortion). Going in without a target will get you killed.

leblanc-teamfight-pick.basis: LeBlanc gets more value from picks than from teamfights. Use E to root and eliminate enemies moving alone through areas without vision. Look first for picks that can prevent a teamfight instead of starting one.
leblanc-teamfight-pick.text: LeBlanc gets more value from picks than from teamfights. Root and eliminate an enemy traveling alone through an area without vision using E (Ethereal Chains), and you can take an objective for free. Look first for a pick that prevents a teamfight from happening.

leesin-combo-basic.basis: The basic gank combo is Q's first cast, basic attack, E's first cast, basic attack, then Q's second cast, adding E's second cast if needed. Weave Flurry-empowered basic attacks between abilities in your gank combo. Use Q's second cast in your gank combo after lowering the opponent's health.
leesin-combo-basic.text: For a basic gank, use Sonic Wave (Q) → basic attack → Tempest (E) → basic attack → Resonating Strike (Q), then Cripple (E) if you need the slow. Weave Flurry-empowered basic attacks between abilities, and use Resonating Strike after lowering the opponent’s health.

leesin-combo-insec.basis: To perform an Insec, land Q's first cast, approach with Q's second cast, get behind the opponent, then use R to kick them toward your allies. To perform a ward Insec, land Q's first cast, use a ward and W to get behind the opponent, then use R to kick them toward your allies. To change R's direction with Flash, start casting R, then Flash during the cast. Before starting an Insec, make sure your allies are close enough to follow up with attacks.
leesin-combo-insec.text: For an Insec, land Q's first cast, get behind the opponent with Q's second cast or a ward and W, then use R to kick them toward your allies. If using Flash to change the kick's direction, cast R first and Flash during its cast for the most reliable timing. Check that your allies are close enough to follow up before starting.

leesin-combo-r-q2.basis: If your allies are far away, land Q's first cast, use R to kick the opponent toward them, then follow with Q's second cast. Hold Q's second cast until after R so you can close the gap created by the kick.
leesin-combo-r-q2.text: When your allies are far away, land Q's first cast but hold the second, kick the opponent toward your team with R, then use Q's second cast to follow and catch them again. This lets Lee Sin close the gap created by the kick and keep the opponent within his team's reach.

leesin-combo-ward-jump.basis: To ward jump, place the ward first, then use W before the ward lands. To approach from outside Q range, place a ward over a wall or behind the opponent and use W to dash to it. When escaping with a ward hop, place a ward over a wall toward your team's side.
leesin-combo-ward-jump.text: To ward jump, place the ward first and press W before it lands. A ward over a wall or behind an opponent lets you close the gap from outside Q range; when escaping, place one over a wall toward your team instead.

leesin-laning.basis: Plan your jungle route to turn your early strength into an advantage. Steal camps or influence a lane when the enemy jungler is tied up on the opposite side. Keep in mind that you have no escape tools immediately after using both Q and W. Save W to escape when going deep into the enemy jungle.
leesin-laning.text: Plan your jungle route to turn Lee Sin's early strength into an advantage. His high movement speed and many ways to engage make it easy to steal camps or affect a lane when the enemy jungler is occupied on the opposite side. Once both Q and W are spent, he has no escape, so keep at least W available when venturing deep into the enemy jungle.

leesin-phase-early.basis: Lee Sin is strongest in early jungle duels and counter-jungling. Look for a chance to disrupt the enemy jungler's route immediately after clearing your first two or three camps. From level 6, when R becomes available, look for opportunities to break open a lane with an Insec.
