maokai-teamfight-ult.text: Casting R head-on gives enemies time to see it and retreat, so use it from the side or behind, or when they enter a narrow passage with nowhere to dodge. If you can choose where to fight, a spot with walls on both sides, such as the entrance to the dragon or Baron pit, can change how many enemies R hits.

masteryi-combo-basic.basis: Activate E as you engage, use R if needed, then go in with Q and keep basic attacking. E and R durations do not tick down during Q and W.
masteryi-combo-basic.text: For a standard engage, activate E (Wuju Style), add R (Highlander) if needed, then enter with Q (Alpha Strike) and follow up with basic attacks. E and R do not lose duration during Q or W (Meditate), so activating them before you engage costs nothing; waiting until after Q to activate E delays your basic attacks.

masteryi-combo-q-cd.basis: Each basic attack reduces Q's cooldown. Just before a fight or objective, hit a camp to reduce Q's cooldown. With no other targets nearby, Q hits the same enemy repeatedly for maximum single-target damage. In a 1v1, lure the enemy away from minions and monsters.
masteryi-combo-q-cd.text: Each basic attack reduces Q (Alpha Strike)’s cooldown, even when it hits a jungle monster, so hit a camp before a fight or objective to bring Q back sooner. With no other targets nearby, Q repeatedly hits the same enemy for maximum single-target damage; in a 1v1, draw the enemy away from minions and monsters.

masteryi-combo-q-dodge.basis: Master Yi cannot be targeted during Q. Dodge targeted crowd control or a finishing blow with Q as it comes in. If the enemy has guaranteed crowd control, walk in and save Q to dodge it.
masteryi-combo-q-dodge.text: Master Yi cannot be targeted while casting Q (Alpha Strike), so use it as targeted crowd control or a finishing blow comes in. Against an enemy with guaranteed crowd control, walk in and save Q to dodge it; using Q only to engage gives up that option.

masteryi-combo-w.basis: W Meditate restores health and reduces damage taken. Activate W as the enemy's burst damage lands. Double Strike stacks build during W's channel. R and E durations pause during W's channel. Immobilizing crowd control interrupts W, so use it after the enemy has spent their crowd control.
masteryi-combo-w.text: W (Meditate) restores health and reduces damage taken, so activate it as the enemy’s burst damage lands. Double Strike stacks build during the channel, making the basic attack immediately afterward stronger, while E and R durations pause. Immobilizing crowd control interrupts W, so use it after the enemy has spent that crowd control.

masteryi-jungle-clear.basis: Q deals bonus damage to monsters, and basic attacks reduce Q's cooldown. Master Yi's high movement speed cuts travel time between camps. Early on, turn fast jungle clears into a lead in growth.
masteryi-jungle-clear.text: Master Yi’s early game is for clearing the jungle. Q (Alpha Strike) deals bonus damage to monsters, basic attacks reduce its cooldown, and his movement speed is among the highest of all champions, saving time between camps. Use that clearing speed to build a growth lead rather than chase kills early.

masteryi-jungle-counter.basis: Early on, basic attacks are his only fighting tool, so junglers with crowd control can catch him easily. Get vision and confirm the enemy jungler is at camps on the opposite side before counterjungling.
masteryi-jungle-counter.text: Avoid meeting the enemy jungler head-on. Early on, Master Yi has only basic attacks to fight with, making him easy for junglers with crowd control to catch. Attempt to counterjungle only after securing vision and confirming that the enemy jungler is at camps on the opposite side.

masteryi-jungle-gank.basis: Master Yi has no crowd control. Look for a gank when an ally has applied crowd control or the enemy has used their mobility and escape abilities. If the conditions for a gank are not there, steal enemy jungle camps or prepare an objective. In games with frequent fights, plan your path around the time you cannot spend helping lanes.
masteryi-jungle-gank.text: Master Yi has no crowd control, so gank only when an ally has already applied crowd control or the enemy has spent their mobility and escape abilities. Otherwise, steal enemy jungle camps or prepare an objective. In games with frequent fights, plan your route around the long stretches when you cannot help lanes.

masteryi-phase.basis: From level 1 until you learn R, focus on farming; fights are usually unfavorable. After learning R, takedowns reduce ability cooldowns and accelerate your growth. The mid to late game, when you have at least two items with attack speed and penetration, is your strong period. You become weaker again if the enemy has both crowd control and defensive items.
masteryi-phase.text: From level 1 until you learn R (Highlander), focus on farming; fights are usually unfavorable. Once you have R, takedowns bring your abilities back sooner and let you snowball. Master Yi peaks in the mid to late game with at least two items providing attack speed and penetration, then weakens again when the enemy has both crowd control and defensive items.

masteryi-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy has a champion with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Master Yi keeps Grievous Wounds applied through repeated basic attacks.
masteryi-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy has a champion with strong healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Master Yi’s repeated basic attacks keep Grievous Wounds applied.

masteryi-situational-qss.basis: If the enemy has several sources of guaranteed crowd control, consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar before damage items. Master Yi struggles to act when locked down by crowd control. Q's untargetability does not remove crowd control already applied.
masteryi-situational-qss.text: If the enemy has several sources of guaranteed crowd control, consider buying Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar before damage items. Master Yi cannot act while locked down, and Q (Alpha Strike)’s untargetability cannot remove crowd control that has already landed.

masteryi-skill-e.basis: E adds true damage to basic attacks. E's true damage is not reduced by armor, so it matters more against enemies who build defensive stats. E's duration does not tick down during Q and W. E has a short duration, so wait until you have a target before activating it.
masteryi-skill-e.text: E (Wuju Style) adds true damage to basic attacks. Armor does not reduce that damage, so it accounts for more of your damage against enemies who build defensive stats. Its duration pauses during Q and W, allowing you to activate it before engaging, but because it lasts only a short time, wait until you have a target.

masteryi-skill-passive.basis: The passive makes a basic attack strike twice after a set number of attacks. Passive stacks remain when you switch targets. Build passive stacks on jungle monsters or minions before attacking a champion. Passive stacks build during W's channel, strengthening the first basic attack after Meditate.
masteryi-skill-passive.text: Double Strike makes a basic attack hit twice after a set number of attacks. Its stacks persist when you switch targets, letting you build them on jungle monsters or minions before attacking a champion. They also build during W (Meditate)’s channel, making the first basic attack after it ends especially strong.

masteryi-skill-r.basis: R increases movement speed and attack speed and grants immunity to slows. Use R to close the gap against enemies who use slows to keep their distance. A takedown during R extends its duration and greatly reduces basic ability cooldowns. Activate R when you can secure a takedown.
masteryi-skill-r.text: R (Highlander) increases movement and attack speed and makes Master Yi immune to slows, letting him close the gap against enemies who rely on slows to keep their distance. A takedown extends R and greatly reduces basic ability cooldowns, so activate it when you can secure a kill and carry that momentum to the next target. Using it before an opening appears leaves you with nothing.

masteryi-teamfight.basis: Do not engage first in teamfights. Wait out of vision until the enemy has used their immobilizing crowd control, then use Q to reach the backline. Take down the first target, use R's takedown effect to get Q back, and move to the next target. If you cannot take down the first target in a teamfight, you can die easily. Pressure a side lane and wait for the enemy to split up instead of facing them head-on at an objective.
masteryi-teamfight.text: Do not engage first in teamfights. Wait out of vision until the enemy has used its immobilizing crowd control on your allies, then use Q (Alpha Strike) to reach the backline. Take down the first target, use R (Highlander)’s takedown effect to bring Q back, and move to the next; if you fail to secure that first takedown, you die. Pressuring a side lane and waiting for the enemy to split makes this opening easier to find than a head-on standoff at an objective.

mel-combo-basic.basis: After landing E's root, follow up with Q and an auto, then finish with R if you have enough Overwhelm. Q keeps exploding after the first blast, so the target must stay in place to take every hit. Use Q on the rooted target after E's root lands.
mel-combo-basic.text: Land E's root, place Q on the rooted target, then auto; use R if you have enough Overwhelm. Q continues exploding after its first blast, so the target must remain in place to take every hit. Confirm the root before casting Q instead of trying to land E afterward.

mel-combo-execute.basis: Overwhelm stacks from both ability and auto damage, with no stack limit. When its stored damage exceeds the target's remaining health plus shields, your next attack becomes an execute. Attack right after the target's shield breaks or expires.
mel-combo-execute.text: Ability and auto damage both stack Overwhelm, with no stack limit. Once its stored damage exceeds the target's remaining health plus shields, your next attack executes them. A shield raises that threshold, so attack just after it breaks or expires.

mel-combo-passive.basis: Each ability you use adds extra projectiles to your next auto. Using several abilities in a row lets you load the maximum number of extra projectiles onto one auto. Weave one auto into the end of your combo to fire your stored extra projectiles.
mel-combo-passive.text: Each ability adds extra projectiles to your next auto, and casting several abilities in a row can load that single auto to the maximum. Use your abilities first, then weave in an auto at the end of the combo so the stored projectiles do not go to waste.

mel-phase.basis: Mel is weakest at levels 1–2 because her mana costs are high and W has a long cooldown. At level 6, learning R increases Overwhelm's damage and lets you finish fights from afar. Mel has a low win rate with only one core item, but it rises sharply as she completes her core build. Play safely early and wait for your core items.
mel-phase.text: Mel is weakest at levels 1–2: high mana costs prevent constant ability use, and W has a long cooldown. At level 6, R increases Overwhelm's damage and gives her a long-range finisher, enabling roams and involvement in distant fights. Her win rate is low with only one core item but rises sharply as she completes her core build, so play safely early and wait for those items.

mel-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing keeps raising the execute threshold, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Overwhelm's execute checks the target's remaining health plus shields.
mel-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing keeps raising the execute threshold, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Overwhelm checks stored damage against the target's remaining health plus shields, so cutting healing helps bring them into execute range.

mel-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier in your core build. W only reflects projectiles, so it cannot stop dashes or targeted engages.
mel-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier in your core build. W only reflects projectiles, so dashes and targeted engages still reach Mel; with armor among the lowest, she cannot rely on W once caught.

mel-skill-e.basis: E roots targets hit by the center of its orb and deals slow and damage over time around it. Even if the root misses, use E's lingering area to cut off the target's path. E deals reduced damage to minions, so do not use it to farm.
mel-skill-e.text: E roots only targets hit by the center of its orb; the surrounding area slows and deals damage over time. Even if the root misses, the area lingers briefly and can cut off an opponent’s path. Its reduced damage to minions makes it inefficient for waveclear, so do not use it to farm.

mel-skill-q.basis: Use Q when the target has a reason to stay in its blast area. Look for Q when the target is rooted, steps among minions for a last hit, or is trapped in a narrow passage. In lane, use Q to clear the wave and harass at the same time.
mel-skill-q.text: Q is a targeted bombardment that pays off when the opponent has reason to stay in its blast area: while rooted, among minions for a last hit, or trapped in a narrow passage. In lane, use it regularly to clear the wave and harass at the same time.

mel-skill-r.basis: R hits every enemy with Overwhelm, regardless of distance. Use R to join fights in other lanes or around objectives when you have vision. Use R before the remaining Overwhelm stacks on enemy champions expire. If you can add another Overwhelm stack, do so before using R for more damage. Learning R increases Overwhelm's damage, letting you reach the execute threshold sooner.
mel-skill-r.text: R hits every enemy with Overwhelm regardless of distance, letting you finish fights in other lanes or around objectives when you have vision. Enemy champions must still have Overwhelm when you cast it, but if you can add another stack before they expire, wait for the extra damage. Learning R also increases Overwhelm's damage, bringing targets to the execute threshold sooner.

mel-skill-w.basis: W is more about reflecting projectiles than its shield. W lasts briefly, so use it as an enemy skillshot projectile approaches. W's reflected damage is calculated using the original caster's stats. Look to reflect an enemy's key ability with W. W cannot reflect dashes. W cannot reflect area effects that have already been cast. If you miss W's reflection timing, its long cooldown leaves you vulnerable until the next fight. Choose one enemy grab ability to target for reflection with W.
mel-skill-w.text: W is chiefly for reflecting projectiles, not for its shield. Its window is brief, so time it as an enemy skillshot projectile approaches, ideally a key ability: reflected damage uses the original caster's stats. It cannot reflect dashes or area effects already on the ground. Missing the timing leaves you vulnerable through its long cooldown, so pick one enemy grab ability to watch for and reflect.

mel-skill-w-mana.basis: Leveling W reduces both its cooldown and mana cost. W is maxed last in the statistically preferred skill order, so its mana cost and cooldown remain a burden during lane. In the early and mid game, save W to reflect projectiles. Later, when mana is no longer a concern, use it defensively.
mel-skill-w-mana.text: Leveling W reduces both its cooldown and mana cost, but the statistically preferred skill order maxes it last, leaving it costly and slow to recharge throughout lane. Save it for a reflection in the early and mid game; once mana is no longer a concern later on, you can use it more freely for defense.

mel-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay at the back and use Q on grouped enemies to apply Overwhelm to several of them. Use W as an enemy engage ability comes toward you. If you miss the chance to use W in a teamfight, do not step forward. Use R after the enemies have lost health and several have Overwhelm stacks.
mel-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay at the back and cast Q into grouped enemies to apply Overwhelm to several at once. Use W the moment an enemy engage ability comes toward you; if you miss that chance, do not step forward. Wait to cast R until enemies have lost health and several have Overwhelm stacks so it can finish multiple targets together.

milio-combo-trade.basis: In lane, use E on an ally and proc the passive with a basic attack, then use Q to knock the enemy back if they close in. Starting a trade with Q knocks the enemy out of your ally's attack range.
milio-combo-trade.text: In lane, cast E on an ally, let their basic attack trigger the passive, then use Q to knock the enemy back if they counterattack and close in. Opening with Q pushes the enemy out of your ally’s attack range and ends the trade, so use it to finish the exchange rather than start it.

milio-laning-early.basis: From the early levels when E can hold two charges, your allies can better withstand poke. When the enemy support pokes, absorb it with E and maintain the wave. Take a head-on fight only when W has increased your allies' range.
milio-laning-early.text: Once E can hold two charges in the early levels, your allies become noticeably better at weathering poke. When the enemy support steps up to harass, absorb it with E and maintain the wave; take a head-on fight only while W is active and giving your allies a range advantage.

milio-phase.basis: Milio has low kill participation and damage early on. Early on, keep your allies alive instead of starting fights. Milio's shields and healing grow as he gets more items. Milio is strongest in late teamfights where his allied marksman can keep attacking. Don't overextend and die early.
milio-phase.text: Milio ranks near the bottom in both early kill participation and damage. Focus on keeping allies alive instead of starting fights early; his shields and healing grow as he gains items. He is strongest in late teamfights where his allied marksman can keep attacking from within range, making an unnecessary early death especially costly.

milio-skill-e-charges.basis: E has two charges, and its shields stack on the same target. If an ally needs a large shield, use E on them twice. If a fight is coming, keep one E charge ready.
milio-skill-e-charges.text: E has two charges that stack on the same target. Use both on one ally for a larger shield, or split them between two allies to give each movement speed. If a fight is coming, keep one charge ready: spending both at once leaves you unable to protect allies until E recharges.

milio-skill-e-speed.basis: E's movement speed boost is used more often than its shield. Use E on an ally before roaming or moving to an objective. Use E on an ally before an enemy skillshot hits them.
milio-skill-e-speed.text: E’s movement speed boost is used more often than its shield. Apply it before an ally roams, moves toward an objective, or dodges an enemy skillshot to give them more options. It is more valuable before they get hit than afterward.

milio-skill-passive.basis: Allies touched by Milio's abilities deal bonus damage on their next attack. Use E on an ally just before a trade to add passive damage. While W lasts, it reapplies the passive at regular intervals. Start lane trades by using an ability on an ally.
milio-skill-passive.text: Milio’s passive adds bonus damage to the next attack of an ally touched by one of his abilities. Apply E just before a trade to increase that ally’s damage; W reapplies the passive at regular intervals while it lasts. As a rule, start lane trades by using an ability on an ally.

milio-skill-q-aim.basis: Q knocks back the first enemy it hits, then bounces up and explodes. Aim Q differently to peel an enemy away or slow a group. Hitting a champion with Q refunds some mana.
milio-skill-q-aim.text: Q knocks back the first enemy it hits, then bounces up and explodes at that spot. Because the knockback lands in a different place from the area damage and slow, aim differently when peeling an enemy off an ally than when slowing a clustered group. Hitting a champion refunds some mana, greatly reducing Q’s effective cost.

milio-skill-q-peel.basis: Q is Milio's only displacement tool. Save Q to peel enemies off your allied marksman. Don't spend Q on lane poke.
milio-skill-q-peel.text: Q is Milio’s only displacement tool, so save it to peel an engaging enemy off your allied marksman instead of spending it on lane poke. Without Q, Milio has no way to stop an enemy who engages.

milio-skill-r.basis: R provides area healing, cleanses immobilizing effects, and grants tenacity. R cannot cleanse airborne effects. Use R when multiple allies are immobilized.
milio-skill-r.text: R heals allies in an area, cleanses immobilizing effects, and grants tenacity. It cannot cleanse airborne effects, so do not hold it to remove knockbacks or knockups. Time it for when several allies are immobilized, but do not sit on it until the last moment when there is nothing to cleanse: the healing alone is valuable.

milio-skill-w-follow.basis: W follows the ally closest to where it was cast. Place W on the ground near the ally you want it to follow. If W follows the wrong ally, recast it to switch targets. In a teamfight, recast W immediately if the ally it follows retreats or falls.
milio-skill-w-follow.text: W follows the ally closest to where it is cast. It does not target an ally directly, so place it on the ground near the ally you want it to follow; if it attaches to the wrong one, recast it to switch. Recast it immediately during a teamfight if that ally retreats or falls.

milio-skill-w-timing.basis: W's main value is increasing allies' attack range. Use W when your allied marksman starts attacking the enemy frontline. Don't use W before a fight just for the healing.
milio-skill-w-timing.text: W’s real value is its attack range increase, not its healing. Cast it as your allied marksman starts attacking the enemy frontline to get the full range benefit; using it early just to heal missing health leaves that range unavailable when the fight starts.

milio-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay behind your team's main damage dealer and use W to increase their range. In teamfights, spread E among your allies. Use R right after the enemy's area crowd control lands. Save Q for champions who engage on your allies.
milio-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay behind your team’s main damage dealer, extend their range with W, and spread E among allies. R is available only once, so use it right after enemy area crowd control lands, and reserve Q for champions who engage on your allies. Plan your ability sequence ahead of time or you will be too late during the fight.

missfortune-combo-lovetap.basis: Love Tap triggers only when you basic attack a different target from the previous one. In lane, alternate basic attacks between minions and the enemy champion to harass. Basic attacking the same enemy repeatedly greatly reduces your harass damage.
missfortune-combo-lovetap.text: Love Tap triggers only when you basic attack a target different from the previous one. In lane, harass by alternating basic attacks from a minion to the enemy champion and back to a minion; repeatedly attacking the same target greatly reduces your harass damage.

missfortune-combo-q-bounce.basis: Use Q on a front minion to harass the enemy champion behind it with the bounce. If Q kills the first target, it always critically strikes the second target. To increase Q bounce harass damage, choose a low-health minion as the first target.
missfortune-combo-q-bounce.text: Use Q Double Up on a front minion to bounce it onto the champion behind it. If Q kills the first target, the bounce always critically strikes the second, so targeting a low-health minion greatly increases your harass damage.

missfortune-combo-teamfight.basis: At the start of a fight, slow the enemy formation with E, then use R. If an ally's area crowd control lands first, skip E and use R immediately.
missfortune-combo-teamfight.text: Start a fight by slowing and holding the enemy formation with E Make It Rain, then pour R Bullet Time into them. If an ally’s area crowd control lands first, save E and start R immediately to give yourself time to channel it.

missfortune-laning-roam.basis: W's movement speed bonus lets Miss Fortune return from base and rejoin the lane faster than other marksmen. Moving without taking damage lets W's movement speed bonus reach its maximum. After pushing the enemy out of lane, actively look for chances to join your team at mid or an objective.
missfortune-laning-roam.text: Miss Fortune can return from base and rejoin the lane faster than other marksmen because W Strut’s movement speed reaches its maximum as she walks without taking damage. After pushing the enemy out of lane, look for chances to move toward mid or an objective.

missfortune-laning-wave.basis: Harassing with Q inevitably pushes the lane toward the enemy. Continuously pushing the lane without knowing the enemy jungler's path leaves you open to ganks. Without vision, save Q and harass only with passive basic attacks. If you plan to push the lane, use Q to clear minions quickly. After pushing the lane, use W's movement speed to get river vision or recall.
missfortune-laning-wave.text: Harassing with Q Double Up inevitably pushes the lane toward the enemy, leaving you open to ganks if you keep pushing without knowing the enemy jungler’s path. Without vision, save Q and harass only with Love Tap basic attacks. If you intend to push, clear the minions quickly with Q, then use W Strut’s movement speed to get river vision or recall.

missfortune-phase.basis: Miss Fortune is an early-game marksman who can gain a harass advantage from level 1 with her passive and Q. Once you learn R at level 6, use your support's landed crowd control as a kill opportunity. Miss Fortune has no dash and average range, making it hard for her to position alone in the late game. Play to end the game with the lead you build in the early and mid game.
missfortune-phase.text: Miss Fortune is an early-game marksman who can gain a harass advantage from level 1 with Love Tap and Q Double Up. Once she learns R Bullet Time at level 6, a single crowd control effect from her support can create a kill opportunity. Later, her lack of a dash and average range make it hard to position alone, so use the lead built in the early and mid game to end the match.

missfortune-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy has a champion with healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. With Executioner's Calling, each hit of R reapplies Grievous Wounds.
missfortune-situational-antiheal.text: If an enemy champion has healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. Each hit of R Bullet Time reapplies the effect, making the item especially effective on Miss Fortune.

missfortune-situational-qss.basis: If enemy stuns keep interrupting R, buy Quicksilver Sash before other defensive items. Miss Fortune's teamfight impact depends heavily on completing R's channel.
missfortune-situational-qss.text: If enemy stuns keep interrupting R Bullet Time, buy Quicksilver Sash before other defensive items. Miss Fortune’s teamfight impact depends heavily on completing the channel.

missfortune-skill-e.basis: E's main value is its slow and the vision it provides, more than its damage. Use E to stop the enemy from engaging. Use E to gain vision inside a brush. Use E to block the enemy's escape route. Just before a teamfight, place E on the enemy's approach to discourage an engage.
missfortune-skill-e.text: E Make It Rain is more valuable for its slow and vision than its damage. Use it to stop an enemy engage, reveal a brush, or block an escape route; placing it on the enemy’s approach just before a teamfight can discourage them from engaging altogether.

missfortune-skill-passive.basis: Each Love Tap trigger reduces W's cooldown. If W is on cooldown, switch basic attack targets to trigger Love Tap.
missfortune-skill-passive.text: Each Love Tap trigger reduces the cooldown of W Strut. Alternating attacks between minions and champions in lane keeps W coming back, so if it is still on cooldown, try hitting a different target once.

missfortune-skill-q.basis: Q is targeted, so it cannot miss. Q costs a lot of mana, so using it too often will leave you out of mana by mid-laning phase. Using Q only on minions without an angle to bounce it onto a champion pushes the lane without gaining any harass advantage. Look to harass with Q when the enemy champion stands behind a minion.
missfortune-skill-q.text: Q Double Up is targeted, so it cannot miss, but its high mana cost will leave you out of mana by the middle of the laning phase if you use it too often. Casting it on a minion without an angle to bounce onto a champion only pushes the lane, so wait until the enemy champion stands behind a minion.

missfortune-skill-r.basis: If R's channel is interrupted, all remaining waves are lost. Use R when you have at least one of these conditions: you are at the edge of its range, you have a wall or brush behind you, or an ally has just landed crowd control. R's cone direction is fixed when you cast it. Before enemies spread out, aim R where it will hit the most of them.
missfortune-skill-r.text: If R Bullet Time’s channel is interrupted, all remaining waves are lost. Cast it only when at least one condition is met: you are at the edge of its range, you have a wall or brush behind you, or an ally has just landed crowd control. Its cone direction locks when you cast it, so aim along the line that will catch the most enemies before they spread out.

missfortune-skill-w.basis: W's movement speed bonus reaches its maximum only after you spend time without taking damage. Miss Fortune uses W's movement speed bonus to survive and roam. Activate W for trades that need attack speed or when taking down a turret, rather than to escape.
missfortune-skill-w.text: W Strut’s movement speed reaches its maximum only after you spend time without taking damage. Miss Fortune’s base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions, making this bonus vital for surviving and roaming; activate W for trades that need attack speed or when taking down a turret, rather than to escape.

missfortune-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, deal area damage from the back line. After your team absorbs the enemy engage, use R when the enemies group up in one direction. If you use R before the enemy formation overlaps and they spread out, its damage drops sharply. When R is unavailable, use E to discourage enemy engages. When R is unavailable, rely on basic attacks to get through teamfights.
missfortune-teamfight.text: In teamfights, deal area damage from the back line. Once your team has absorbed the enemy engage, cast R Bullet Time when the enemies group up in one direction; using it before their formation overlaps can scatter them and sharply reduce its damage. When R is unavailable, use E Make It Rain to discourage engages and rely on basic attacks to get through the fight.

mordekaiser-combo-basic.basis: Start a basic trade by pulling the enemy in with E, then landing Q. Follow up Q with basic attacks. Use Q from an angle where the enemy does not overlap with minions. Without using E first, the enemy can walk out of Q range.
mordekaiser-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, pull the enemy in with E to close the gap, land Q on them alone, then weave in basic attacks. Q deals much more damage to a single target, so aim from an angle that avoids minions; without E first, the enemy can walk out of Q range.

mordekaiser-combo-passive.basis: The passive aura activates after landing three abilities or basic attacks on enemy champions or jungle monsters. Weave a basic attack between E and Q to activate the passive aura in time. When the passive aura activates, your movement speed increases, making it easier to chase.
mordekaiser-combo-passive.text: The passive aura activates after three ability or basic attack hits on an enemy champion or jungle monster, with each basic attack counting as one hit. Weave a basic attack between E and Q instead of relying only on abilities to activate it in time; once active, the aura also grants movement speed to keep the chase going.

mordekaiser-combo-w.basis: On activation, W converts stored damage dealt and taken into a shield. Use W's shield after exchanging damage. W's stored amount decays over time. Recasting W heals you for a percentage of the remaining shield. If you will not take more damage, recast W to heal while the shield is still large.
mordekaiser-combo-w.text: W stores damage dealt and taken, then converts it into a shield when activated. Using it at the start of a fight gives you a thin shield, so wait until you have exchanged damage, but use it before the stored amount decays after the fight. Recasting W restores health based on the remaining shield; if you expect no more incoming damage, convert it while the shield is still large.

mordekaiser-laning-melee.basis: Start a trade by pulling a melee opponent with E as they step forward to last-hit. Stay close to melee opponents, weaving in basic attacks until the passive aura activates. Keep pressuring melee opponents once the passive aura activates.
mordekaiser-laning-melee.text: Against a melee opponent, start a trade with E as they step forward to last-hit. Stay close and weave in basic attacks until the passive aura activates, then keep up the pressure while it is active.

mordekaiser-laning-ranged.basis: Do not push the wave against ranged opponents. Farm safely with Q against ranged opponents. Mordekaiser has no mobility ability, so forcing an approach against ranged opponents can easily cost him health. Against ranged opponents, fight back with R after level 6 in coordination with your jungler's gank.
mordekaiser-laning-ranged.text: Against a ranged opponent, avoid pushing the wave and farm safely with Q. Mordekaiser has no mobility ability, so forcing your way close will only cost you health. The most reliable chance to fight back is to pair your level 6 R with an allied jungler's gank.

mordekaiser-phase.basis: Start looking for trades from level 3 onward, when you have both E and Q. Look for kills in lane once you learn R at level 6. Use R for clear kill opportunities rather than forcing early dives. Late in the game, R can isolate only one enemy, so its impact varies greatly with the enemy composition.
mordekaiser-phase.text: Look for trades from level 3, once you have both E and Q; at level 6, R creates a clear chance for a lane kill. This is not a statistically strong win-rate phase, so save R for a reliable opportunity instead of forcing an early dive. Later, R can remove only one enemy, making its impact heavily dependent on the opposing composition.

mordekaiser-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing becomes a problem, choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction. The passive aura's continuous damage makes it easy to maintain Morellonomicon's healing reduction. Morellonomicon's healing reduction is especially effective when forcing a duel inside R.
mordekaiser-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Morellonomicon. The passive aura's continuous damage makes its healing reduction easy to maintain, especially when you force a duel inside R.

mordekaiser-skill-e.basis: E passively provides magic penetration even without being cast. Do not delay putting skill points into E to increase your overall damage. E pulls all enemies within its area. In teamfights, use E to pull multiple enemies into Q and passive aura range.
mordekaiser-skill-e.text: E Death's Grasp grants magic penetration passively, even when you do not cast it, so do not delay putting points into it: each rank increases your overall damage. When cast, it pulls every enemy in its area, letting you group multiple opponents within Q and passive aura range in a teamfight.

mordekaiser-skill-q.basis: Q deals greatly increased damage when it hits a single target. When trading in lane, avoid minions and hit only the enemy champion with Q. When using Q to clear waves, account for giving up its single-target damage bonus. Do not try to trade and farm with the same Q.
mordekaiser-skill-q.text: Q Obliterate deals much more damage when it hits only one target. In lane trades, angle it around minions to hit the enemy champion alone; when using it to clear a wave, account for losing that single-target bonus. Trying to trade and farm with the same Q compromises both.

mordekaiser-skill-r-cast.basis: R is a short-range targeted ability. Use R immediately after pulling the enemy in with E. Use Flash to close the distance and cast R. Use R on a clear target rather than holding it until you miss the chance to cast it.
mordekaiser-skill-r-cast.text: R is a short-range targeted ability, so use it immediately after pulling an enemy in with E or close the gap with Flash before casting it. Commit it to a clear target instead of holding it until the chance to cast it is gone.

mordekaiser-skill-r-duel.basis: R takes one target into another realm, forcing a one-on-one duel for its duration. Neither side's allies can intervene inside R. R steals a portion of the target's key stats. R's stat steal gives you a chance to win duels against enemies who are hard to beat outside it.
mordekaiser-skill-r-duel.text: R Realm of Death takes one target into another space and forces a one-on-one duel for its duration. Neither side's allies can intervene there, and Mordekaiser steals some of the target's key stats, giving him a chance to beat an opponent he could not defeat outside R.

mordekaiser-skill-r-target.basis: Mordekaiser relies heavily on his choice of R target. Taking an enemy frontliner with R leaves your allies to face the remaining enemy damage dealers. Taking an enemy damage dealer with R leaves your allies to face the remaining frontline. Among targets you can kill within R's duration, choose the most important champion in the enemy composition. Exclude high-health frontliners and enemies with instant-cast invulnerability from your R targets.
mordekaiser-skill-r-target.text: Choosing the right R target is central to playing Mordekaiser. Taking an enemy frontliner leaves your allies facing the remaining damage dealers, while taking a damage dealer leaves them facing only the frontline. Pick the most important enemy champion you can kill within R's duration, excluding high-health frontliners and opponents with instant-cast invulnerability who would survive the timer.

mordekaiser-teamfight.basis: Use E to group multiple enemies in teamfights. In teamfights, hold your ground among enemies with the passive aura active. Cast R on a key enemy champion after they use their main abilities. Choose your initial entry position carefully, as having no mobility ability makes it hard to retreat and re-engage.
mordekaiser-teamfight.text: In teamfights, use E to group multiple enemies, activate the passive aura, and hold your ground among them. It is safer to cast R on a key opponent after they use their main abilities than immediately when the fight starts. Choose your entry position carefully: without a mobility ability, you cannot easily close the gap again after backing off.

morgana-combo-basic.basis: When you have a kill opportunity, root the target with Q, place W under them, then use R. Time R so its stun follows as the Q root ends. If Q misses, don't use R first; the target can walk away.
morgana-combo-basic.text: For a kill, land Q (Dark Binding), place W (Tormented Shadow) under the target, then use R (Soul Shackles). Time R’s stun to trigger as Q’s root ends, leaving no chance to escape; if Q misses, don’t reverse the order and lead with R, since the target can simply walk away.

morgana-combo-r-flash.basis: Flash into the enemy team right after casting R, keeping the chains connected to bind more enemies. Morgana gains movement speed while casting R.
morgana-combo-r-flash.text: Flash into the enemy team immediately after casting R (Soul Shackles) to keep the chains connected and catch more enemies. The movement speed Morgana gains during R lets her push in after activating it.

morgana-combo-r-survive.basis: If Morgana dies before R's stun triggers, the chains break. Use Zhonya's Hourglass to survive until R's stun triggers. If you have no way to survive after using R, use it only after an ally holds the enemy in place.
morgana-combo-r-survive.text: If Morgana dies before R (Soul Shackles) stuns, the chains break. Use Zhonya’s Hourglass to survive until the stun triggers; without a way to stay alive after activating R, use it only once an ally has already held the enemy in place.

morgana-laning-mana.basis: Missing Q repeatedly can leave you out of mana and unable to respond. Don't cast Q if the angle is uncertain. If landing Q is unlikely, poke only with W and conserve mana. When the enemy can engage, prioritize keeping enough mana for E.
morgana-laning-mana.text: Repeatedly missing Q (Dark Binding) can drain your mana and leave you unable to act. Hold it when the angle is uncertain; poke with W (Tormented Shadow) and conserve mana instead. Whenever the enemy can engage, make sure you have enough mana for E (Black Shield).

morgana-laning-wave.basis: In bot lane, avoid pushing the wave unnecessarily with W. Place W under an enemy champion to poke and deny space. Only push the wave with W when leaving bot lane to ward or roam. If you're holding a lane alone, use W to farm.
morgana-laning-wave.text: In bot lane, avoid pushing the wave unintentionally with W (Tormented Shadow). Place it under an enemy champion to poke and deny space, and use it on the wave to push only when leaving lane to ward or roam. When holding a lane alone, use W to farm.

morgana-phase.basis: Morgana's laning strength depends heavily on landing Q. At level 6, learning R gives Morgana her first reliable kill opportunity. From mid game, once she has items, use E and R to start and stop teamfights. Statistically, Morgana has low early kill participation. Don't force kills early.
morgana-phase.text: Morgana’s laning strength depends directly on whether Q (Dark Binding) lands. Learning R (Soul Shackles) at level 6 gives her the first reliable kill opportunity; once she has items in the mid game, E (Black Shield) and R let her start or stop teamfights. Her early kill participation is statistically low, so don’t force early kills.

morgana-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, choose Morellonomicon to reduce it. Dealing continuous damage with W and R makes it easier to maintain healing reduction.
morgana-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Morellonomicon to reduce it. Morgana’s sustained damage with W (Tormented Shadow) and R (Soul Shackles) makes the healing reduction easy to maintain.

morgana-skill-e-self.basis: You can cast E on yourself. If an enemy engages on you, cast E on yourself to buy time to use R. Using E on yourself leaves your allied damage dealer unprotected from the next engage, so choose the shield target carefully.
morgana-skill-e-self.text: You can cast E (Black Shield) on yourself when an enemy engages on you, blocking the crowd control and buying time to activate R (Soul Shackles). That leaves your allied damage dealer unprotected from the next engage, so decide which one of you needs the shield.

morgana-skill-e-timing.basis: E blocks crowd control and immobilizing effects while the shield remains. Use E as soon as you see the enemy begin casting, rather than applying it early. Use E to block the crowd control an enemy uses to engage.
morgana-skill-e-timing.text: E (Black Shield) blocks crowd control and immobilizing effects while the shield remains. Its duration is short, so watch for the enemy’s cast and apply it at that moment instead of using it early. Its key purpose is to stop the crowd control the enemy uses to engage.

morgana-skill-e-vs-engage.basis: Against enemies who start combos with a pull or knockback, save E to block that engage. Don't use E for anything else until the enemy's key engage ability is spent.
morgana-skill-e-vs-engage.text: Against enemies who start combos with a pull or knockback, save E (Black Shield) specifically for that ability. Using it elsewhere before their engage ability is spent leaves you vulnerable to one-sided trades throughout lane.

morgana-skill-q.basis: Q roots only the first target it hits. Minions block Q. Cast Q along a clear line, such as beside the wave or through a jungle entrance. Morgana relies on landing Q to make her other abilities more effective.
morgana-skill-q.text: Q (Dark Binding) roots only the first target it hits, so minions will block it. Fire along a clear line beside the wave or through a jungle entrance, rather than trying to shoot through the wave. Morgana’s other abilities gain value when Q lands, so creating a clear angle for it is the focus of laning.

morgana-skill-r.basis: R is an area ability centered on Morgana. Move among enemies to hit them with R. Use R only when allies can follow up immediately, since you need to survive until its stun triggers. Gain vision of every enemy affected by R.
morgana-skill-r.text: R (Soul Shackles) affects an area around Morgana, so move among enemies to catch them. Because its stun takes time and Morgana must survive until it triggers, activate R only when allies can follow up immediately. It also grants vision of every affected enemy.

morgana-skill-w.basis: W deals more damage the more health its target has lost. Use W to force a wounded enemy out of an area. Each time Morgana heals through her passive, W's cooldown decreases. Use W freely during fights.
morgana-skill-w.text: W (Tormented Shadow) deals more damage the more health its target has lost, making it a threat to wounded enemies. Use it to force them out of an area as well as to deal damage. Each time Morgana heals through her passive, W’s cooldown decreases, so use it freely during fights.

morgana-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, prioritize using E to block the enemy engage champion's crowd control. In teamfights, block the engage with E, then prioritize using R. Q is hard to land once a teamfight starts, so line up a shot beforehand.
morgana-teamfight.text: In teamfights, first use E (Black Shield) to block the enemy engage champion’s crowd control, then use R (Soul Shackles). Failing to use both leaves Morgana with little impact on the fight. Since Q (Dark Binding) is difficult to land once fighting starts, look for an angle before the fight begins.

naafiri-combo-allin.basis: For an all-in, activate W, land the first Q, close in with E, then land the second Q and an auto attack. Activate W before going in: it boosts attack damage and movement speed and adds two packmates. Save E so you can follow if the enemy backs away.
naafiri-combo-allin.text: For an all-in, activate W before engaging for its attack damage, movement speed, and two extra packmates, then land the first Q, close in with E, and follow with the second Q and an auto attack. If you spend E too early, you cannot follow an enemy who backs away.

naafiri-combo-q.basis: You can use Q's two casts separately. The second Q deals extra damage based on missing health if it hits a bleeding target. Apply bleed with the first Q, then line up the second Q while the bleed lasts. When the first Q hits, the pack leaps at the target and helps close the gap.
naafiri-combo-q.text: Q’s two casts can be spaced apart. The second deals extra damage based on missing health only if the target is still bleeding, so apply the bleed with the first, then line up the second before it expires. The first hit also sends the pack leaping at the target, helping Naafiri close the gap.

naafiri-combo-r.basis: R is a targeted dash to a champion. A takedown reveals nearby enemies and lets you cast R again. The second R cast grants a shield. Use R to engage when you can secure the first takedown, then use the second R to escape or move on to the next target.
naafiri-combo-r.text: R is a targeted dash to a champion. A takedown reveals nearby enemies and allows a second cast, which grants a shield; engage only when you can secure the first takedown, then use that second R to escape or move to the next target.

naafiri-laning.basis: As a melee mid laner, Naafiri struggles to farm against ranged opponents. The pack helps attack minions, and Q's bleed can secure last hits from range. Clear waves the enemy has pushed in with the pack and Q to keep up in levels. Go in when the enemy's skillshot is on cooldown.
naafiri-laning.text: As a melee mid laner, Naafiri struggles to farm against ranged opponents, but her pack helps attack minions and Q’s bleed can secure last hits from range. Clear waves the enemy pushes toward you with the pack and Q to keep up in levels, and close in only after the enemy has used a skillshot.

naafiri-laning-roam.basis: Naafiri has high movement speed, and W makes her faster, so she can roam quickly. Push the lane, then move to a side lane or the enemy jungle to create a numbers advantage. Roam to get ahead instead of only farming mid.
naafiri-laning-roam.text: Naafiri’s high movement speed, boosted further by W, lets her roam quickly. Push the lane, then move to a side lane or the enemy jungle to create a numbers advantage and build a lead; staying mid to farm alone wastes that strength.

naafiri-phase.basis: Even early on, the pack lets Naafiri clear waves and harass. At level 6, learning R gives Naafiri many more kill opportunities with its targeted dash. Naafiri is strongest at roaming and flanking in the mid game. In late-game front-to-back teamfights, area damage can wipe out the pack and reduce her damage. Build on your lead before the game goes long.
naafiri-phase.text: Even early on, the pack helps Naafiri clear waves and harass. Learning R at level 6 gives her many more kill opportunities through its targeted dash, while mid-game roams and flanks are her strongest plays. In late-game front-to-back teamfights, area damage can wipe out the pack and cut her damage, so build on your lead before the game goes long.

naafiri-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Naafiri chips away at health with bleed and her pack, so enemy healing makes assassinations harder.
naafiri-situational-antiheal.text: If an enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Naafiri wears targets down with bleed and her pack, so if their healing goes unchecked, she cannot secure the assassination.

naafiri-skill-e.basis: E recalls the pack and fully restores its health. If area damage has hurt the pack, use E during the fight to heal it. When the pack is at full health, you can use E to engage.
naafiri-skill-e.text: E recalls the pack and fully restores its health, so if area damage has hurt your pack, use E during the fight to heal it as well as to close the gap. When the pack is at full health, you can use E purely to engage.

naafiri-skill-pack.basis: The pack accounts for a significant share of Naafiri's damage. Packmates replenish slowly, one at a time. Hitting a champion or large monster with an ability speeds up packmate regeneration. Just before a fight, land an ability to replenish your pack. If every packmate dies, Naafiri loses a lot of damage.
naafiri-skill-pack.text: The pack provides a significant share of Naafiri’s damage. Packmates replenish slowly, one at a time, but hitting a champion or large monster with an ability speeds up regeneration, so land an ability before a fight to build up the pack, even if you have to throw one out for that purpose. With every packmate dead, Naafiri is a melee champion whose damage falls far short.

naafiri-skill-pack-target.basis: The pack follows and attacks Naafiri's designated target. If you hit a minion just before trading, the pack goes after it, delaying your damage against the champion. Just before closing in, target the enemy champion or mark them with Q to send the pack ahead.
naafiri-skill-pack-target.text: The pack attacks Naafiri’s designated target. Hitting a minion just before a trade sends the pack after it, delaying all of its damage against the enemy champion; target that champion or hit them with Q before closing in to send the pack ahead.

naafiri-skill-r-vision.basis: You need a takedown to cast R a second time. A takedown reveals nearby enemies, letting you choose your next target. If you engage with R without a secure takedown, you have no way back.
naafiri-skill-r-vision.text: R requires a takedown before you can cast it again, making it a way to chain engages after a kill. The takedown also reveals nearby enemies so you can choose your next target; if you engage without a secure takedown, you have no way back.

naafiri-skill-w.basis: W briefly makes Naafiri untargetable and recalls the pack. W does not heal the recalled pack. Use E to restore the pack's health. Use W's untargetability when targeted crowd control or a finishing ability is coming.
naafiri-skill-w.text: W briefly makes Naafiri untargetable and recalls the pack, but it does not restore the pack’s health; use E when you need to heal it. Time W’s untargetability to avoid targeted crowd control or a finishing ability.

naafiri-skill-w-aoe.basis: Recall the pack with W or E before enemy area damage hits. Recalled packmates cannot be targeted, so they avoid area damage.
naafiri-skill-w-aoe.text: Recall your pack with W or E before an enemy area-of-effect ability hits. Recalled packmates become untargetable, so they avoid the damage and rejoin the fight at full strength once the ability passes. Against opponents with many area-of-effect abilities, this sequence alone can decide the fight.

naafiri-teamfight.basis: Do not enter teamfights from the front. From the side or behind, use the first R to take out a backline target, then use the second R gained from the takedown to reach another target or escape. Check your pack count and whether the enemy has area damage before going in. If the pack has taken damage, heal it with E before going in.
naafiri-teamfight.text: Avoid entering teamfights from the front. Approach from the side or behind, use R to take out a backline target, then spend the second cast earned from the takedown to reach another target or escape. Before engaging, check your pack count and the enemy’s area damage; if the pack is hurt, restore it with E first.

nami-combo-engage.basis: To engage, use R to knock enemies up, then place Q where they will land. R travels slowly, so confirm it hits before throwing Q. Chain Q's stun as R's knockup ends to leave the enemy no time to react.
nami-combo-engage.text: To engage, knock the enemy up with R, then place Q where they will land. Because R travels slowly, wait to confirm the hit before throwing Q; its stun will begin as the knockup ends, leaving no time to react.

nami-combo-trade.basis: For lane trades, cast E on your ADC, throw Q when the enemy steps up, then use W while they are stunned. E empowers a fixed number of attacks. Use E after checking that your ally is in position to land basic attacks.
nami-combo-trade.text: For lane trades, cast E on your ADC when they are in position to land basic attacks, throw Q as the enemy steps forward, then use W during the stun. E empowers a fixed number of attacks, so casting it after the enemy has backed away wastes it.

nami-combo-w-bounce.basis: W bounces between allies and enemies. W hits each target only once. W is most effective when allies and enemies are close together. Choose W's first target based on whether healing or damage takes priority. W only bounces to visible enemies.
nami-combo-w-bounce.text: W bounces between allies and enemies, hitting each target only once. It gets the most value when they are close together, so choose whether to start on an ally for healing or an enemy for damage. It only bounces to visible enemies, making it less effective without vision.

nami-laning.basis: In lane, sustain through W's healing. Look for Q when the enemy steps forward. Do not push the lane while Q is unavailable. Keep your distance while Q is unavailable. Prioritize staying alive and holding the lane.
nami-laning.text: In lane, sustain with W's healing and look for Q when the enemy steps forward. While Q is unavailable, keep your distance and avoid pushing the lane. Nami's top-tier 14-minute death metric reflects the value of staying alive and holding the lane.

nami-phase.basis: Nami is weak at level 1 because she has only one way to intervene. Once Nami learns W, she gains an advantage through lane sustain. Learning R at level 6 gives Nami her first engage tool. As Nami gains ability power, her healing and buffs grow stronger. Nami can still be caught easily late in the game, so do not stand in front.
nami-phase.text: Nami is weak at level 1 because she has only one way to intervene, but gains an advantage through lane sustain once she learns W. R gives her a first engage tool at level 6, and ability power strengthens her healing and buffs. Her health is among the lowest of all champions, though, so standing in front can get her caught even late in the game.

nami-roaming.basis: When roaming, chain Q and R with your mid laner's crowd control. Nami has no mobility ability, so roaming and returning takes a long time. Roam only after pushing the wave in to keep the enemy bot lane occupied. Do not go into the river without a purpose.
nami-roaming.text: When roaming, Nami is better at following her mid laner's crowd control with Q and R than catching enemies on her own. She has no mobility ability, so the trip out and back takes time; roam only after pushing the wave in to keep the enemy bot lane occupied. Going into the river without a purpose can get her caught.

nami-situational-cleanse.basis: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down allies, choose Mikael's Blessing to cleanse it. Nami cannot cleanse crowd control from allies on her own.
nami-situational-cleanse.text: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down allies, use Mikael's Blessing to free them. Nami can heal, but she cannot cleanse crowd control herself, so she needs this type of item to save an ally who has been caught.

nami-skill-e.basis: E has a short duration. E empowers a limited number of attacks. Use E after a fight starts instead of casting it in advance. During a chase, use E's slow to keep the enemy from getting away. When escaping, cast E on an ally to slow pursuers.
nami-skill-e.text: E lasts only a short time and empowers a fixed number of attacks, so cast it after a fight starts instead of in advance. Its slow can hold an enemy in place during a chase even without immobilizing crowd control; when escaping, cast it on an ally to slow pursuers.

nami-skill-passive.basis: When Nami's abilities touch an ally, P increases that ally's movement speed. Trigger P with W and E to help allies engage and disengage. Allies hit by R receive double the movement speed bonus from P. Even if R will not hit an enemy, send it through allies to help them engage.
nami-skill-passive.text: P increases an ally's movement speed when Nami's abilities touch them, so W's healing and E's enhancement also help allies engage or disengage. Allies hit by R receive twice the movement speed bonus; even if R will miss the enemy, you can send it through allies to help them engage.

nami-skill-q.basis: Q takes time to land, so enemies can dodge it by walking away. Throw Q when an enemy starts a last-hit animation. Throw Q at enemies already under crowd control. Time Q with an ally's dash. Q has a long cooldown, leaving a long gap in your ability to intervene if it misses.
nami-skill-q.text: Q takes time to land, so enemies can dodge a casual throw by walking away. Cast it as an enemy starts a last-hit animation, onto existing crowd control, or in time with an ally's dash. Its long cooldown leaves you unable to intervene for a while if it misses.

nami-skill-q-terrain.basis: Q lands at a targeted location, so you can cast it over walls. Predict the path of an enemy fleeing into a bush or behind a wall and catch them with Q, even without vision. Enemies may anticipate Q over a wall, so do not use the same angle repeatedly.
nami-skill-q-terrain.text: Q lands at a targeted location and can cross walls. Predict the path of an enemy fleeing into a bush or behind a wall to catch them even without vision, but vary your angle because enemies know Q can come over walls.

nami-skill-w-mana.basis: W costs a lot of mana. Nami's lane sustain depends on W's healing. Avoid using W only to poke enemies so you have enough mana left to heal allies. Early on, save W until an ally's health is actually at risk. During trades, use W only when it can bounce between an ally and an enemy.
nami-skill-w-mana.text: W costs a lot of mana and provides Nami's lane sustain. Using it only to poke can leave you without mana when an ally needs healing, so early on, save it until an ally's health is actually at risk. During trades, use it only when it can bounce between an ally and an enemy.

nami-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stand behind your ADC. In teamfights, keep E on your ADC. In teamfights, use W to heal allies. For safer teamfights, prioritize using R to stop enemy engages over starting fights. Use R to cut off a fleeing enemy's escape route.
nami-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stand behind your ADC, keep E on them, and use W to heal allies. Using R to stop an enemy engage is safer than opening a fight with it; because it blocks an entire path, it can also cut off a fleeing enemy's escape. If Nami has to move to the front to open with R, her team is already positioned poorly.

nami-vision.basis: Do not venture blindly into areas without vision. Use a Control Ward to clear enemy vision. Check the enemy's position before entering a bush.
nami-vision.text: Nami has low health and no mobility, so entering an area without vision can get her killed before she has a chance to react. Clear enemy vision with a Control Ward, check the enemy’s position before entering a bush, and choose your route for placing vision carefully; that route is what keeps her alive.

nasus-combo-basic.basis: Use W → E → Q in fights. Lowering armor with E before landing Q deals more damage than using Q first.
nasus-combo-basic.text: In fights, use W Wither → E Spirit Fire → Q Siphoning Strike. W keeps the target in E’s area while E greatly reduces their armor, letting Q deal its full physical damage. Using Q first deals noticeably less damage, even with the same stacks.

nasus-laning-freeze.basis: Stack safely when the enemy pushes the wave and lets you last-hit with Q under your turret. Avoid forcing a push and take Q last hits from incoming waves. Conserve mana while collecting incoming waves.
nasus-laning-freeze.text: An enemy pushing the wave can work in your favor: last-hitting with Q Siphoning Strike under your turret is the safest way to build stacks. Avoid forcing the wave forward; catch incoming waves, collect Q last hits, and conserve mana.

nasus-laning-zoned.basis: If enemy pressure makes Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap. Without building Q stacks, Nasus struggles to grow stronger as the game progresses.
nasus-laning-zoned.text: If enemy pressure makes even Q Siphoning Strike last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap instead of trying to hold on alone. Nasus will not grow stronger over time without stacks, so leaving him unable to farm is the worst choice.

nasus-phase.basis: Nasus is weakest at levels 2–3. At levels 2–3, Nasus loses head-on fights against most bruisers. At levels 2–3, Nasus relies on W to fight back. Nasus becomes much stronger from the mid to late game, once he has built up Q stacks and has R available. Late in the game, Nasus is difficult to face head-on while R is active.
nasus-phase.text: Nasus is weakest at levels 2–3, when he loses head-on fights against most bruisers and has only W Wither to fight back. He becomes much stronger in the mid to late game once he has built Q Siphoning Strike stacks and can activate R Fury of the Sands; late in the game, he is very difficult to face head-on while R is active.

nasus-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. With Executioner's Calling, even a single Q can apply healing reduction.
nasus-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling. Because Q Siphoning Strike triggers on-hit effects, a single hit applies healing reduction.

nasus-situational-defense.basis: Without enough defensive stats, Nasus falls quickly to focused attacks even while R is active. Even with a damage-focused build, buy at least one survival item, such as Dead Man's Plate, to withstand focused attacks.
nasus-situational-defense.text: Without enough defensive stats, Nasus can fall quickly to focused attacks even while R Fury of the Sands is active. Include at least one survival item, such as Dead Man’s Plate, even in a damage-focused build.

nasus-skill-e-mana.basis: E lowers enemy armor, increasing Q's damage. E has a high mana cost. Using E during the laning phase pushes the wave. Limit E poke to save mana for W → E → Q when following up on ganks or fighting.
nasus-skill-e-mana.text: E Spirit Fire reduces armor and boosts Q Siphoning Strike damage, but it costs a lot of mana and pushes the wave. During lane, save E for gank follow-up and fights; casting it whenever it is ready can leave you without enough mana for W → E → Q when your jungler arrives.

nasus-skill-e-wave.basis: Using E near your turret pushes the wave and causes you to miss Q last hits. While holding out under your turret, avoid using E and focus on Q last hits.
nasus-skill-e-wave.text: Using E Spirit Fire near your turret pushes the wave away and costs you several Q Siphoning Strike last hits. While holding out under your turret, skip E entirely and focus on last-hitting with Q.

nasus-skill-q-stack.basis: Nasus's damage depends heavily on Q stacks. Prioritize last-hitting with Q throughout the laning phase. Killing champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q grants more stacks. Do not miss opportunities to last-hit champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q.
nasus-skill-q-stack.text: Nasus’s damage comes almost entirely from Q Siphoning Strike stacks, so prioritize Q last hits throughout the laning phase. Killing champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q grants far more stacks, making those opportunities especially important; the stacks you build now largely determine your late-game damage.

nasus-skill-q-tower.basis: Dealing damage with Q triggers on-hit effects. Q's bonus damage also applies to turrets. Once you have built up Q stacks, consider split-pushing to pressure turrets with your fast demolition.
nasus-skill-q-tower.text: Q Siphoning Strike triggers on-hit effects when it deals damage, and its bonus damage applies to turrets. Once you have built up stacks, you can push a lane alone and take turrets quickly, giving you the option to pressure through split-pushing instead of teamfighting.

nasus-skill-r.basis: R increases maximum health, armor, and magic resistance. R deals continuous damage to nearby enemies based on their maximum health. R greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Activate R at the start of a teamfight to use its continuous damage and repeated Q attacks. In skirmishes, wait until the enemy commits, then activate R at the last moment to use the health increase.
nasus-skill-r.text: R Fury of the Sands increases maximum health, armor, and magic resistance, deals continuous damage to nearby enemies based on their maximum health, and greatly reduces Q Siphoning Strike’s cooldown. Activate it at the start of a teamfight for sustained area damage and repeated Q attacks; in a skirmish, it is better to wait until the enemy commits, then activate R at the last moment to use the health increase.

nasus-skill-r-objective.basis: Combining R's health and defense increases with P's life steal lets you tank an objective's attacks alone. A team with Nasus can attempt Baron relatively early. Suggest attempting an objective when R comes off cooldown.
nasus-skill-r-objective.text: R Fury of the Sands grants health and defenses that, together with P Soul Eater’s life steal, let Nasus tank and attack an objective alone. His team can attempt Baron earlier than other teams, so time objective calls for when R comes off cooldown.

nasus-skill-w.basis: W's slow grows stronger over time. W also reduces the target's attack speed. Prioritize enemy carries who rely on basic attacks when choosing a target for W. W is a targeted ability with a cooldown that is not short. Nasus has no dash, so he relies on W to stop enemies from kiting him.
nasus-skill-w.text: W Wither slows more strongly over time and reduces attack speed as well as movement speed, making it especially effective against champions who rely on basic attacks. Because it targets one enemy and has a substantial cooldown, choose an enemy carry carefully; without a dash, Nasus also relies on W to stop enemies from kiting him.

nasus-teamfight.basis: Nasus has no dash or guaranteed crowd control, making him very vulnerable to kiting. Avoid leading the charge alone; enter after your teammates start the fight. Use W on the enemy carry to hinder their movement. Use Q on enemies standing in E's area. If an enemy ignores Nasus and goes for your backline, use W on that enemy.
nasus-teamfight.text: Nasus has no dash or guaranteed crowd control, making him highly vulnerable to kiting. Enter after your teammates initiate, use W Wither to pin down the enemy carry, and land Q Siphoning Strike while the target stands in E Spirit Fire. If an enemy ignores Nasus and goes for your backline, holding that enemy with W alone can turn the teamfight.

nautilus-combo-engage.basis: For a standard engage, land Q, then use a passive auto attack → E → W. As the Q stun ends, follow up with a passive auto attack to keep the target under crowd control. To chain crowd control after Q, do not skip the passive auto attack.
nautilus-combo-engage.text: For a standard engage, land Q, auto attack immediately after the pull, then use E → W. That first attack applies Nautilus’s passive root as the Q stun ends, keeping the target under crowd control; skipping it breaks the chain.

nautilus-combo-flash-q.basis: To catch an enemy outside Q range, Flash and use Q before they can react. If Q lands after Flash, follow up with a passive auto attack → E. Taking too long to line up Q without Flash makes it easier for the enemy to escape.
nautilus-combo-flash-q.text: To catch an enemy outside Q range, Flash first and throw Q immediately, before they can react. If it lands, follow with a passive auto attack → E. Nautilus is among the slowest champions, so the longer you spend lining up Q without Flash, the more time the enemy has to escape.

nautilus-combo-gank.basis: During a gank or when entering a narrow passage, aim Q at terrain beside the enemy to close the gap more reliably. Use E immediately after closing the gap with Q on terrain. When Q hits terrain, you recover a substantial portion of its cooldown and mana cost.
nautilus-combo-gank.text: During a gank or when entering a narrow passage, aim Q at terrain beside the enemy to close the gap more reliably, then use E immediately. Hitting terrain refunds a substantial portion of Q’s cooldown and mana cost, so a failed attempt costs less.

nautilus-combo-ult-chain.basis: Auto attack an enemy knocked up by R to follow up with your passive root. Save Q until the enemy tries to escape. To lock down one enemy for as long as possible, use R → passive auto attack → Q.
nautilus-combo-ult-chain.text: After R knocks an enemy up, auto attack to apply your passive root, then save Q for the moment they try to escape. R → passive auto attack → Q keeps one target locked down for as long as possible.

nautilus-laning-level2.basis: Reaching level 2 first opens your strongest trading window, letting you lock down the enemy for a long time. After reaching level 2 first, trade with Q → passive auto attack → E. Push the first wave quickly to reach level 2 first. Before starting a trade, check whether your ADC can follow up.
nautilus-laning-level2.text: Reaching level 2 first opens Nautilus’s strongest trading window: Q → passive auto attack → E keeps the enemy locked down for a long time. Push the first wave quickly to reach level 2 first, then check that your ADC can follow up before starting the trade.

nautilus-phase.basis: Nautilus gains kill pressure at level 2, when both Q and E are available. Nautilus is strongest at level 6, when R gives him a reliable engage. Nautilus deals very little damage of his own in the late game. In the late game, focus on engaging and shutting down the enemy carry.
nautilus-phase.text: Nautilus gains kill pressure at level 2, when both Q and E become available, and is strongest at level 6, when R gives him a reliable engage. He deals very little damage of his own late in the game, so focus on engaging and shutting down the enemy carry.

nautilus-skill-e.basis: E explodes in multiple waves. E's first explosion has a delay. Use E while fleeing to slow the enemy's pursuit. Use E ahead of time along the enemy's approach to deter their engage.
nautilus-skill-e.text: E explodes in several waves, with a delay before the first. Leave it behind while fleeing to slow pursuit, or place it ahead of time along the enemy’s approach to make them hesitate before engaging.

nautilus-skill-q.basis: Q only affects the first target it hits. Minions block Q. In lane, use Q when a gap opens between minions. In lane, line up Q from a brush or the side.
nautilus-skill-q.text: Q affects only the first target it hits, so minions can block it. In lane, throw it when a gap opens between minions or from a brush or the side; lining it up openly from the front risks hitting a minion first.

nautilus-skill-q-terrain.basis: If Q hits terrain, you get a cooldown and mana refund. When returning to lane, roaming, or joining an objective fight, hit terrain with Q to travel.
nautilus-skill-q-terrain.text: Hitting terrain with Q refunds some of its cooldown and mana cost, letting you use it to travel along walls when returning to lane, roaming, or joining an objective fight.

nautilus-skill-r.basis: R follows its targeted enemy. R also knocks up other enemies along its path. When targeting a backline carry, aim R's path to knock up enemies in front and open a path for your team to engage.
nautilus-skill-r.text: R follows its targeted enemy and knocks up other enemies along its path. When targeting a backline carry, angle the path through the enemy team to knock up those in front and open a way for your team to engage.

nautilus-skill-w.basis: W grants a shield. While W lasts, your auto attacks deal area damage around the target. While W is active, weave in auto attacks to make use of its area damage. Use W just before the enemy's burst damage hits.
nautilus-skill-w.text: W grants a shield and adds area damage around the target of your auto attacks while it lasts. Weave in attacks to make full use of it, and activate W just before the enemy’s burst damage hits so the shield does not go to waste.

nautilus-teamfight.basis: Prioritize the enemy's main damage dealer as your teamfight engage target. If there is no opening to engage, do not force Q. If there is no opening to engage, hold the front line with W and E and draw out the enemy's engage. After the enemy uses their engage ability, use R as the signal for your team to go in.
nautilus-teamfight.text: Prioritize the enemy’s main damage dealer when engaging a teamfight. If there is no opening, do not force Q; hold the front line with W and E and draw out the enemy’s engage. Once they have used their engage ability, use R as the signal for your team to go in.

neeko-combo-basic.basis: Root with E, then place Q and follow up with an auto attack. E's root can hold the target in Q's area until it bursts again. Don't throw Q before E; the target can walk out of it.
neeko-combo-basic.text: The basic combo is E root → Q → auto attack. Place Q after the root so the target stays in its area through the bursts; Q bursts again when it damages a champion, allowing one root to hold them for every explosion. If you throw Q first, they can simply walk out.

neeko-combo-e-minion.basis: If E hits something first, it grows larger and faster, and its root lasts longer. In lane, throw E at an angle that lets it pass through minions and hit your opponent. Don't walk around the minion wave to cast E.
neeko-combo-e-minion.text: E grows larger and moves faster after hitting something, and its root lasts longer. In lane, angle it through a minion toward your opponent: it is easier to land and more effective than walking around the wave to avoid it.

neeko-combo-r.basis: Approach in disguise, start preparing R, then use E or allied crowd control to hold the target for R's landing. While Neeko is disguised, opponents cannot see R's preparation animation. The disguise wears off shortly after you cast R, revealing where you started preparing it.
neeko-combo-r.text: Approach in disguise, begin preparing R, then use E or an ally’s crowd control to hold the target for R’s landing. Opponents cannot see the preparation animation while Neeko is disguised, giving them no cue to react, but the disguise wears off shortly after R is cast and reveals where you began preparing it.

neeko-laning.basis: Neeko's laning depends heavily on landing E; without it, Q and R are also hard to land reliably. If you don't have an angle for E, don't force it. Harass with W's empowered auto attack and wait. Watch for an enemy engage while E is on cooldown.
neeko-laning.text: Neeko’s lane depends on landing E: without its root, Q and R are not guaranteed to land. If you have no angle, save E and wear the enemy down with W’s empowered auto attacks while you wait; also account for the enemy’s chance to engage once E is on cooldown.

neeko-laning-roam.basis: Support Neeko gets especially high value from roaming. After pushing the lane, disguise yourself as an ally while crossing the river to establish vision and find angles for E and R. Crossing the river disguised as an ally can delay the enemy's reaction even if they spot you.
neeko-laning-roam.text: Support Neeko gets her greatest value from roaming. Push the lane, then disguise yourself as an ally on the way to establish vision across the river; even if enemies see you, the disguise can delay their reaction long enough to secure E and R. Making that disguise part of your vision route improves your chances of a successful gank.

neeko-phase.basis: At levels 1–5, Neeko struggles to withstand trades from melee champions who dive in. Once Neeko learns R at level 6, combining it with her disguise gives her the power to turn a fight around. Neeko's power peaks in the mid game as she builds ability power. In the late game, Neeko has few options left after using both E and R.
neeko-phase.text: At levels 1–5, Neeko’s armor is among the lowest, making trades against melee champions who dive in difficult. At level 6, R combined with her disguise gives her the power to turn a fight around, and she peaks in the mid game as she builds ability power. In the late game, she has little left after using E and R, so the order in which she engages matters even more.
