neeko-skill-passive.basis: P lets Neeko disguise herself as an allied champion or a nearby unit. Immobilizing crowd control breaks the disguise. Using a damaging ability breaks the disguise. Taking damage equal to the disguised unit's health breaks the disguise.
neeko-skill-passive.text: P lets Neeko disguise herself as an allied champion or nearby unit. Immobilizing crowd control, a damaging ability, or damage equal to the disguised unit’s health breaks the disguise, so use it to approach rather than to stay hidden during a fight, and plan your angle knowing your first damaging ability will reveal you.

neeko-skill-passive-credibility.basis: If the ally you're disguised as appears elsewhere, enemies will spot the disguise right away. Disguise yourself as an ally who isn't currently visible to the enemy. Walk along a path that ally would likely take. To make the disguise most convincing, blend in with your allies and move with them.
neeko-skill-passive-credibility.text: Disguise yourself as an ally the enemy cannot currently see; if that ally is already visible elsewhere, the deception is immediately obvious. Walk a route they would plausibly take, ideally blending in and moving with your allies.

neeko-skill-q.basis: Q bursts again in the same spot if it kills a unit or damages a champion or large monster. Place Q over both the minion wave and your opponent to clear the wave and harass them. If Q hits nothing, it ends after the first burst. In objective fights, hit the large monster with Q to trigger another burst.
neeko-skill-q.text: Q bursts again in the same spot when it kills a unit or damages a champion or large monster. Place it over the wave to chain bursts through minion kills, clearing and harassing at once; if it hits nothing, it ends after the first burst. Its repeated bursts also make it valuable in objective fights when it hits a large monster.

neeko-skill-r.basis: R leaps only after its preparation animation ends, and its area stun applies on landing. If opponents scatter while R is preparing, you may miss them when you land. If the enemy frontline is sturdy and strong crowd control is still available, wait for an ally's engage or your E root to hold enemies before using R.
neeko-skill-r.text: R leaps only after its preparation animation ends and stuns an area when Neeko lands. If enemies scatter during the preparation, you can miss everyone and end up alone in their midst. A sturdy frontline with strong crowd control still available can prevent the engage entirely, so wait for an allied engage or your own E root to hold enemies before using R.

neeko-skill-w-active.basis: Casting W makes Neeko briefly invisible and sends a clone running in the chosen direction. Use W's brief invisibility to interrupt enemy targeted abilities and throw off their aim. When escaping, send the clone in the opposite direction to mislead pursuers. W's clone copies Neeko's ability and recall animations.
neeko-skill-w-active.text: Casting W briefly turns Neeko invisible and sends a clone running in the chosen direction. Use that invisibility to interrupt targeted abilities and disrupt enemy aim, or send the clone the opposite way while escaping to mislead pursuers. The clone also copies Neeko’s ability and recall animations, so you can leave it appearing to recall.

neeko-skill-w-passive.basis: W's passive grants bonus damage and a brief movement speed boost on every third auto attack. Track W's empowered auto attack and use it on the enemy champion. Auto attack minions twice, then hit your opponent with the third, empowered auto attack.
neeko-skill-w-passive.text: W’s passive adds damage and a brief movement speed boost to every third auto attack. Count the cycle in lane so the empowered hit lands on the enemy champion instead of a minion: attack minions twice, then hit your opponent with the third attack.

neeko-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, start with E from the backline, then finish with R after your allies' engage holds the enemy in place. If you cast R first and dive in alone, you may be taken down during its preparation animation. Once caught in a teamfight, W's invisibility is Neeko's only way out.
neeko-teamfight.text: In teamfights, start with E from the backline and finish with R after your allies’ engage holds the enemy in place. Casting R first and diving in alone leaves you vulnerable during its preparation animation; Neeko’s armor is among the lowest, and once caught, W’s invisibility is her only way out.

nidalee-combo-cougar.basis: In cougar form, close the gap with Pounce, then use Takedown and Swipe. In cougar form, Takedown is applied to your next basic attack. Use Takedown once you are in basic attack range.
nidalee-combo-cougar.text: In cougar form, the standard sequence is to close in with Pounce, use Takedown to finish the target, then deal any remaining damage with Swipe. Takedown empowers your next basic attack, so wait until you are in basic attack range before using it.

nidalee-combo-gank.basis: When ganking, land Javelin Toss from a distance, transform into cougar form, then use Pounce, Takedown, and Swipe in that order. Landing Javelin Toss in human form applies the Hunted mark and resets the transformation cooldown. If Javelin Toss misses, don't force an engage hoping for the empowered effect.
nidalee-combo-gank.text: For a gank, land Javelin Toss from long range in human form to apply Hunted and reset Aspect Of The Cougar’s cooldown, then transform, close in with an empowered Pounce, and use Takedown followed by Swipe. If the spear misses, you get neither the reset nor the empowered effect, so don’t force the engage.

nidalee-jungle-path.basis: Nidalee has no crowd control, so her gank success depends on help from allied laners. Gank lanes with allies who can lock down enemies first. If no ally can lock down the enemy, gain an advantage by farming the jungle or invading the enemy jungle.
nidalee-jungle-path.text: Nidalee has no crowd control, so her ganks depend on allied laners. Prioritize lanes where an ally can lock down the enemy; if none can, gain an advantage by farming or invading the enemy jungle instead.

nidalee-phase.basis: Nidalee clears the jungle quickly early on thanks to cougar form. Pressure objectives with Javelin Toss poke even before level 6. Avoid fighting the enemy jungler head-on. Nidalee is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability power. Nidalee has less impact late in the game if she cannot land Javelin Toss.
nidalee-phase.text: Cougar form gives Nidalee a fast early jungle clear, and she can pressure objectives with Javelin Toss poke even before level 6. Her low health and magic resistance make a single catch deadly, so avoid fighting the enemy jungler head-on. She peaks in the mid game as she builds ability power, but loses impact late if she cannot land Javelin Toss.

nidalee-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy has healing, choose Morellonomicon to stop them from healing between fights. If the enemy heals between fights, you have fewer chances to finish them with Takedown.
nidalee-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy has healing, build Morellonomicon. Nidalee relies on a burst of damage from her spear and cougar combo, so healing between fights can take away her chance to finish a target with Takedown.

nidalee-skill-cougar-q.basis: Takedown in cougar form deals more damage the lower the target's health is. Takedown is stronger against a target with the Hunted mark. Use Takedown to finish an enemy when their health is low.
nidalee-skill-cougar-q.text: Takedown in cougar form deals more damage as the target’s health falls and is stronger against a Hunted target. Save it to finish a low-health enemy instead of using it first on someone at full health.

nidalee-skill-e-heal.basis: Primal Surge in human form heals more when more health is missing. Use Primal Surge after your health has dropped somewhat. Using Primal Surge on an ally increases their attack speed. Use Primal Surge on an allied damage dealer just before an objective fight.
nidalee-skill-e-heal.text: Primal Surge heals more the more health its target is missing, so wait until some health has been lost before using it. Cast it on an allied damage dealer just before an objective fight to grant attack speed as well.

nidalee-skill-passive-brush.basis: Prowl increases movement speed when passing through bushes. Prowl increases movement speed when there is a Hunted target. Plan your jungle routes through bushes. Move in and out of bushes to position yourself during fights, too.
nidalee-skill-passive-brush.text: Prowl increases movement speed when you pass through bushes or have a Hunted target. Routing through bushes speeds up your jungle movement, and moving in and out of them helps you position during fights.

nidalee-skill-pounce.basis: Pounce in cougar form can cross terrain to escape. Don't spend every Pounce on engaging; save one for escape. Pounce travels farther when used toward an enemy with the Hunted mark.
nidalee-skill-pounce.text: Pounce in cougar form can cross terrain, making it an escape tool as well as a way to engage. As a rule, save a use for getting out instead of spending every Pounce going in; its longer leap toward a Hunted enemy also makes pursuit easier.

nidalee-skill-q.basis: Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther it travels. Look for an angle to land Javelin Toss at maximum range. Landing Javelin Toss grants true sight of an enemy even if they are hiding in a bush.
nidalee-skill-q.text: Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther it travels, making a point-blank hit nearly worthless; look for an angle to land it at maximum range. A hit also grants true sight of the target, keeping them visible even in a bush and making pursuit much easier.

nidalee-skill-r-form.basis: Aspect Of The Cougar switches forms and has a short cooldown. Applying Hunted in human form immediately resets Aspect Of The Cougar's cooldown. Switch to cougar form when closing in on an enemy. Switch to human form when healing or creating distance. Switching back to human form makes your basic attacks ranged.
nidalee-skill-r-form.text: Aspect Of The Cougar switches forms, has a short cooldown, and resets immediately when you apply Hunted in human form. Switch to cougar form to close in and back to human form to heal or create distance; your basic attacks become ranged again, letting you deal damage while retreating.

nidalee-skill-w-trap.basis: Bushwhack in human form lasts a long time and reveals enemies who step on it. Place Bushwhack traps at river entrances and jungle junctions ahead of time to track the enemy jungler's path. An enemy who steps on Bushwhack gets the Hunted mark.
nidalee-skill-w-trap.text: Bushwhack lasts a long time in human form and reveals enemies who step on it. Set traps at river entrances and jungle junctions ahead of time to track the enemy jungler’s route; when one is triggered, it applies Hunted and lets you follow up with a chase combo.

nidalee-teamfight.basis: Don't engage head-on in teamfights. In teamfights, throw Javelin Toss from the side or behind in human form to apply the mark. Engage in cougar form only after the enemy's main damage dealer has lost enough health. After finishing an enemy in a teamfight, escape with Pounce. Nidalee is fragile and is easily caught if hit by crowd control.
nidalee-teamfight.text: Avoid engaging head-on in teamfights. Throw Javelin Toss from the side or behind in human form to apply Hunted, then enter in cougar form only after the enemy’s main damage dealer has lost enough health; finish them and escape with Pounce. Nidalee is fragile enough to die if caught by a single crowd control effect.

nilah-combo-allin.basis: When going all in, enter with E, use Q during the dash, basic attack, then finish with W and R. Activate W after the opponent's basic attacks and sustained damage start hitting.
nilah-combo-allin.text: For an all-in, enter with E, cast Q during the dash, basic attack, activate W once the opponent’s basic attacks and sustained damage begin, then pull them together with R to finish. Using W as soon as you enter wastes it before it blocks anything.

nilah-combo-eq.basis: Cast Q while dashing through a target with E to hit enemies along the path too. Q used during E has a different hit check from Q used after E passes through. When several enemies overlap, use Q during E.
nilah-combo-eq.text: Nilah’s key combo is to cast Q during E. Pressing Q while Slipstream passes through a target sends a wave that hits every enemy along the path. Its hit detection differs from casting Q after the dash, so always use Q during E when several enemies overlap.

nilah-combo-trade.basis: For a short trade, land Q to activate its buff, then basic attack. Q's buff activates only when Q hits a target, such as a minion or champion. Before closing in on an opponent, hit a minion with Q to activate the buff.
nilah-combo-trade.text: For a short trade, land Q on a minion or opponent to gain its range and attack speed buffs, then basic attack. Q must hit something to grant the buffs, so using it on a minion before closing in can briefly offset Nilah’s short range.

nilah-laning.basis: As a melee marksman, Nilah struggles to last-hit against ranged opponents. During lane, avoid forcing an approach and use Q to last-hit from range. Enter with E when an opponent steps forward to attack a minion. During lane, focus on keeping up in levels without falling far behind.
nilah-laning.text: As a melee marksman, Nilah struggles even to last-hit against ranged opponents. Avoid forcing your way in: use Q to secure last hits from range and keep up in levels, then enter with E only when an opponent steps forward to attack a minion. The goal in lane is to get through it without falling far behind.

nilah-laning-trade.basis: Because her support's shields and healing are amplified, Nilah can fight back in 2v2s. Nilah must fight at melee range, leaving her vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Enter after the opponent uses their key skillshot crowd control.
nilah-laning-trade.text: Nilah can take 2v2 fights because her support’s shields and healing are amplified, but her melee range leaves her vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Enter only after the opponent has used their key skillshot crowd control.

nilah-phase.basis: Nilah is very weak at levels 1–2 because of her range and health disadvantages. Nilah grows stronger from mid game as critical strike items increase Q's penetration and lifesteal. In late game teamfights, Nilah can save allies with W and R.
nilah-phase.text: Nilah is very weak at levels 1–2 because she is disadvantaged in both range and health. As critical strike items build up, Q grants more penetration and lifesteal, making her much stronger from mid game; in late game teamfights, W and R can also help keep her allies alive. Survive the early game and time favors Nilah.

nilah-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent sustains through healing, buy Executioner's Calling while building your core items. Nilah needs to stay close and attack for a long time, so an opponent's healing makes fights hard to finish.
nilah-situational-antiheal.text: If an opponent survives through healing, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items. Nilah has to stay close and attack for a long time, and unchecked healing makes those fights difficult to finish.

nilah-skill-e.basis: E dashes through a targeted unit, so you can target minions too. Nilah uses E both to enter and escape, so spending all its uses to enter makes escaping difficult. Before entering, identify a unit you can target with E to get out.
nilah-skill-e.text: E dashes through a targeted unit, including a minion, and serves both as an entry and an escape. Spending every use to get in leaves Nilah no way out, so check which unit you can dash through to escape before committing; an enemy minion wave can provide routes in both directions.

nilah-skill-passive.basis: When Nilah last-hits a minion, the nearest ally regains half the experience lost from sharing it. During lane, keep your support close to Nilah. If the support leaves lane, Nilah loses her experience advantage.
nilah-skill-passive.text: When Nilah last-hits a minion, the nearest ally regains half the experience lost from sharing it. Keep your support close during lane so both of you level faster; if the support leaves, that benefit disappears entirely.

nilah-skill-passive-heal.basis: Nilah amplifies healing and shields she receives from allies. The ally who provided the healing or shield also receives the amplified effect. Nilah benefits greatly from pairing with a support who provides shields or healing. During fights, stay within range of your support's healing and shields.
nilah-skill-passive-heal.text: Nilah amplifies healing and shields allies give her, and the ally who provided them also receives the amplified effect. She benefits most from a support with healing or shields, so staying within that support’s range during fights helps keep her alive.

nilah-skill-q.basis: Q's passive grants armor penetration and basic attack lifesteal based on critical strike chance. As Nilah's critical strike chance rises, both her damage and sustain improve. Excess healing becomes a shield. Even at full health, attack minions to turn excess healing into a shield.
nilah-skill-q.text: Q's passive grants armor penetration and basic attack lifesteal based on critical strike chance, so building critical strike items sharply improves Nilah's damage and ability to stay in a fight. Excess healing becomes a shield, making it worthwhile to attack minions even at full health.

nilah-skill-r.basis: Use R to pull together and finish opponents who are already grouped. R heals Nilah and nearby allies based on the damage it deals to champions. The more champions R hits, the more it heals allies. Use R to group enemies where your allies' area abilities will hit.
nilah-skill-r.text: Use R to pull together and finish opponents who are already grouped, rather than to initiate. Damage dealt to champions heals Nilah and nearby allies, so hitting more enemies restores more health to the team; pulling only one also reduces the healing. Prioritize a position that gathers enemies into your allies’ area abilities.

nilah-skill-w.basis: While W is active, Nilah dodges all basic attacks. Use W when the opposing marksman or a basic attack focused champion attacks. While W is active, Nilah can pass through units. Use W to escape when minions block your path. Allies Nilah touches while W is active also dodge basic attacks. When entering with W, take a path that touches your allied marksman or support.
nilah-skill-w.text: W lets Nilah dodge all basic attacks for its duration, so use it when an opposing marksman or another basic attack focused champion starts dealing damage rather than spending it for movement speed on entry. It also lets her pass through units to escape a wall of minions. Allies she touches during W gain the same dodge effect, so entering along a path that brushes past your marksman or support can protect both of you from basic attacks.

nilah-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, avoid entering first; go in second. After the opponent engages on an ally, move in with W. When enemies group up, pull them together with R to heal your allies. If Nilah takes the front line first, she is likely to die from focused crowd control.
nilah-teamfight.text: In teamfights, enter second. After an opponent engages on an ally, move in with W to shut down basic attack damage, then use R when enemies group up to pull them together and heal your allies. Taking the front line first exposes Nilah to all their crowd control and can get her killed.

noct-combo-e-hold.basis: E only triggers fear if the tether to the target holds. Apply E after closing in on the target. If you close in along the Q trail before applying E, the target has a harder time leaving tether range. If you apply E from far away, the enemy can walk back to break the tether.
noct-combo-e-hold.text: E only triggers fear if the tether holds, so apply it after closing in. Landing E once you are already beside the target on the Q trail leaves little room to escape its range; from farther away, the target can break the tether simply by walking back.

noct-combo-gank.basis: When ganking, land Q, follow the trail to close in, apply E, and trigger your passive with a basic attack. Enemies hit by Q also leave a trail. After landing Q, chase along the trail the enemy leaves.
noct-combo-gank.text: For a standard gank, land Q to lay a trail, run along it to close in, apply E, then trigger your passive with a basic attack. Enemies hit by Q leave a trail too, so their escape route becomes Nocturne’s path of pursuit.

noct-combo-ult.basis: Use R to cut off vision, recast it to dash in, activate W just before landing, then attack with E and basic attacks. W remains active while Nocturne flies in with R.
noct-combo-ult.text: Activate R to cut off vision, recast it to dash to your target, turn on W just before landing, then apply E and follow with basic attacks. W stays active during the R dash, so activating it early can block crowd control the target uses in a hurry.

noct-laning.basis: Before level 6, prioritize ganking lanes where an ally can hold the enemy in place. During a gank, apply E after closing in on the enemy. If there is no gank opportunity, clear camps to reach level 6 sooner.
noct-laning.text: Before level 6, gank success depends on your ally’s crowd control, so prioritize lanes where they can hold the enemy in place. Lay down Q’s trail along your approach and enter from a brush or out of vision, then use E once you are close. If there is no gank opportunity, clear camps to reach level 6 sooner.

noct-laning-r-timing.basis: After level 6, look at the lane state and use R proactively. If the enemy laner has pushed the wave and stepped forward, and your ally can follow up, engage with R. In R's darkness, enemies cannot see their allies, increasing the chance of a successful dive.
noct-laning-r-timing.text: After level 6, use R when the lane state calls for it instead of holding it. If an enemy laner has pushed the wave and stepped forward, and your ally can follow up, you can cut off vision with R and engage even from the opposite side of the jungle. Enemies cannot see their allies during the darkness, which greatly improves the chance of a successful dive.

noct-phase.basis: Nocturne's jungle clear speed at levels 1–2 is average. Using the Q trail and W's attack speed helps clear camps faster. Level 6, when Nocturne learns R, is his first power spike. Nocturne is strongest in the mid game after completing his first core item. In the late game, Nocturne is easily killed if he engages poorly.
noct-phase.text: Nocturne’s jungle clear is average at levels 1–2, but the Q trail and W’s attack speed make camps go faster. Learning R at level 6 is his first power spike, allowing him to gank anywhere on the map. He peaks in the mid game after completing his first core item; late in the game, his fragility means a poor engage can get him killed immediately.

noct-skill-e.basis: E triggers fear only if the tether to the target holds for a set time. Nocturne gains a large movement speed boost when moving toward a feared enemy. Chase the target as soon as fear triggers. Draw out the enemy's mobility ability or force them toward a wall before applying E.
noct-skill-e.text: E triggers fear only after its tether to the target holds for a set time. Once the target is feared, Nocturne gains a large movement speed boost when moving toward them, making that the easiest moment to chase. Draw out their mobility ability or force them toward a wall before applying E to improve your chances of landing the fear.

noct-skill-passive.basis: Periodically, your passive adds area damage and healing to your next basic attack. Each basic attack reduces your passive's cooldown. Hitting a champion or jungle monster reduces your passive's cooldown by more. Keep using basic attacks while clearing camps to benefit from your passive's healing.
noct-skill-passive.text: Your passive periodically adds area damage and healing to your next basic attack. Each basic attack reduces its cooldown, with a larger reduction when you hit a champion or jungle monster. Keep attacking while clearing camps: those attacks bring the healing back sooner and help preserve your health.

noct-skill-q.basis: Q damages enemies and leaves a trail. On the Q trail, Nocturne can move through units and gains movement speed and attack damage. Q leaves a trail even if it misses enemies. Outside combat, use the Q trail to close the gap or escape. When ganking, lay the Q trail along your approach in advance.
noct-skill-q.text: Q deals damage and provides mobility: on its trail, Nocturne moves through units and gains movement speed and attack damage. The trail remains even if Q misses, so you can use it outside combat to close a gap or escape. When ganking, lay it along your approach in advance to reach the target faster.

noct-skill-r.basis: R reduces every enemy's vision radius. R prevents enemies from sharing vision with each other. You can use R without dashing to conceal an ally's engage or the start of an objective.
noct-skill-r.text: R reduces every enemy’s vision radius and stops them from sharing vision, so it can conceal an ally’s engage or the start of an objective even without a dash. At a decisive moment, activating it is worthwhile even if you cannot dash in.

noct-skill-r-target.basis: To dash with R, you must be able to see a target in range. If enemies scatter in R's darkness, pick an isolated target and dash in. Do not use R to dive into the middle of an enemy group if one shield will not be enough to survive.
noct-skill-r-target.text: R’s dash targets an enemy, so you must be able to see someone in range. Ideally, wait for enemies to scatter in the darkness and choose an isolated target; diving into the middle of a group leaves you with more damage to survive than one shield can handle.

noct-skill-w.basis: W's shield blocks one enemy ability for a short time. Blocking an ability with W doubles your attack speed. Activate W to block the enemy's key immobilizing ability.
noct-skill-w.text: W briefly shields Nocturne from one enemy ability; blocking it doubles his attack speed, making W both a defensive tool and a damage boost. Time it for a key immobilizing ability, since letting the shield expire without blocking anything gives only half the attack speed benefit.

noct-skill-w-monster.basis: W can also block monster abilities. Block a dragon attack with W to gain attack speed and hit the objective faster. Save W if the enemy jungler can reach the objective.
noct-skill-w-monster.text: W also blocks monster abilities. Blocking something like a dragon attack activates the attack speed boost and lets Nocturne damage the objective much faster. Keep this in mind before an objective fight, but save the shield if the enemy jungler is likely to arrive.

noct-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, target one backline enemy in the darkness instead of the frontline. After activating R, wait for the enemies to scatter before dashing in. Activate W as you engage to block the enemy support's crowd control. Engage after your allies start the fight.
noct-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Nocturne’s job is to pick off one backline enemy in the darkness rather than fight the frontline. After activating R, wait for reduced vision to make the enemies split up before dashing in. Engage after your allies start the fight, using W on entry to absorb the enemy support’s crowd control so the shield gets its value.

nunu-combo-gank.basis: Roll W long enough from outside vision to knock the enemy up, then throw E and finish with R. Start rolling W far from the enemy and outside vision so it can gain size and speed. W started near an enemy has little size or speed and is easy to dodge.
nunu-combo-gank.text: For a gank, start rolling W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) far from the lane and outside enemy vision, build it to maximum speed, then hit the target. Throw E (Snowball Barrage) during the knockup and finish with R (Absolute Zero). Starting W near the enemy gives it too little size or speed, making it easy to dodge.

nunu-combo-r-setup.basis: If you cast R on its own, the enemy can walk out and take almost no explosion damage. Cast R alongside W's knockup, E's root, or an ally's immobilizing crowd control. If the enemy tries to escape with a cleanse, recast R immediately to detonate it.
nunu-combo-r-setup.text: R (Absolute Zero) is channeled, so casting it alone lets enemies walk away and take almost no explosion damage. Pair it with W’s knockup, E’s root, or an ally’s immobilizing crowd control. If the target tries to escape with a cleanse, recast R immediately to detonate it instead of waiting for maximum damage.

nunu-laning-jungle.basis: Try your first gank after learning W at level 3. After a lane gank, grow your snowball while rolling around the Rift Scuttler, then gank again. Q deals true damage to monsters, helping clear jungle camps quickly. Statistically, both CS and damage per minute rank near the bottom. Focus on securing objectives and ganking over competing in farm.
nunu-laning-jungle.text: Your first gank comes after learning W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) at level 3. After a lane gank, you can grow another snowball while rolling around the Rift Scuttler and immediately gank again. Q (Consume) clears camps quickly with its fixed damage to monsters, but CS and damage per minute both rank near the bottom statistically, so get value from objectives and ganks instead of competing in farm.

nunu-phase.basis: Ganks become stronger from level 3, when you learn W. Objective fights are strongest after you learn R at level 6. Statistically, early damage is among the lowest overall, making solo kills difficult. As health and ability power build up in the mid and late game, Q's sustain and R's burst both improve. Keep engaging fights and protecting allies in the late game.
nunu-phase.text: Ganks become strong when you learn W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) at level 3, and objective fights peak after you add R (Absolute Zero) at level 6. Early damage ranks among the lowest statistically, making solo kills difficult. As you build health and ability power in the mid and late game, Q’s sustain and R’s burst both improve; you can still engage fights and protect allies late.

nunu-situational-slowresist.basis: Rolling W also slows Nunu himself. Slow resistance helps the snowball reach maximum speed sooner. Slow resistance makes it easier to land E's root on a fleeing enemy. If the enemy has many slows, take Mercury's Treads and Unflinching together.
nunu-situational-slowresist.text: Rolling W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) also slows Nunu himself. Slow resistance helps the snowball reach maximum speed sooner and makes it easier to land E’s root on a fleeing enemy. If the opposing team has many slows, Mercury’s Treads and Unflinching become especially valuable together.

nunu-skill-e.basis: An enemy hit by all three E snowballs is slowed, then rooted after a delay. If you have no way to hold the enemy in place after throwing E, the root will rarely trigger. If the enemy's escape path is clear, land all three E hits and chase. E can reveal a stealthed enemy.
nunu-skill-e.text: E throws snowballs three times; enemies hit by all three are slowed, then rooted after a delay. The root rarely triggers if you have no way to keep the enemy in place, but if their escape route is clear, land all three hits in advance and give chase. Because E is not targeted, you can also use it to reveal stealthed enemies.

nunu-skill-passive.basis: The passive increases attack speed and movement speed for Nunu & Willump and one nearby ally. The passive's duration starts when you damage a large monster. When attacking an objective, stand beside your allied marksman to give them the passive buff. Passive-empowered basic attacks also damage enemies around the target. At jungle camps, position so the empowered basic attack hits multiple monsters.
nunu-skill-passive.text: P (Call of the Freljord) grants attack speed and movement speed to Nunu & Willump and one nearby ally. Its duration starts when you damage a large monster, so stand beside your allied marksman while attacking an objective to share the buff. Empowered basic attacks also hit around the target; at jungle camps, position so they strike multiple monsters.

nunu-skill-q-heal.basis: Q heals far more when used on a minion or monster than on a champion. If you need healing, click a minion precisely and use Q instead of targeting a champion. Q heals more when your health falls below half. At low health, you can use Q on a jungle monster to heal instead of running away.
nunu-skill-q-heal.text: Q (Consume) heals far more from a minion or monster than from a champion, so if you need sustain, click the minion precisely to keep your cursor from targeting the champion. Healing increases further below half health; when you’re low, biting a jungle monster can be more valuable than running away.

nunu-skill-r-peel.basis: Use R beneath your allied carry to stop enemies from engaging, even if it deals no explosion damage. Nunu gains a shield while channeling R.
nunu-skill-r-peel.text: Cast R (Absolute Zero) beneath your allied carry to stop an enemy engage, even if the explosion deals no damage. Nunu also gains a shield while channeling, making him harder to kill.

nunu-skill-w-cleanse.basis: Nunu slows himself while rolling the snowball with W. While rolling W, Nunu turns sideways more slowly than he moves forward.
nunu-skill-w-cleanse.text: W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) slows Nunu while he rolls it, so account for the fact that he turns sideways more slowly than he moves forward.

nunu-skill-w-momentum.basis: The snowball's size and speed increase with movement speed bonuses on Nunu. Roll W while benefiting from terrain effects or ally buffs that increase movement speed. Take a wide route around the river to give the snowball room to roll and find a hidden approach angle.
nunu-skill-w-momentum.text: Movement speed bonuses multiply the size and speed W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) gains as it rolls. Terrain effects or ally buffs that increase movement speed produce a much larger, faster snowball over the same distance. Taking a wide route around the river also gives it room to grow while hiding your approach angle.

nunu-skill-w-timing.basis: W's cooldown starts when you begin rolling the snowball. Once the snowball is fully grown, collide with the enemy right away if you're confident you'll hit. In open areas, roll W in a circle to keep enemies from entering.
nunu-skill-w-timing.text: W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) starts its cooldown when you begin rolling, not when you release the snowball. Once it reaches full size, hit the enemy right away if you’re confident it will connect. In a wide open area, you can instead keep rolling in a circle to deny enemies entry to a particular area.

nunu-teamfight.basis: Start the teamfight when the snowball reaches the enemy backline. Engage with W only when allies are close enough to follow. If you engage alone, your low damage makes you easy to take down. If you have no engage angle, cast R in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy engage.
nunu-teamfight.text: Nunu & Willump start a teamfight when the snowball reaches the enemy backline, but their low damage makes a solo engage easy to punish. Roll W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) in only when allies are close enough to follow. If there is no engage angle, cast R (Absolute Zero) in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy’s approach.

olaf-combo-allin.basis: When going all in, land Q, close in for a basic attack, activate W, then finish with E. E's true damage goes through even if the opponent builds armor or magic resistance. Save E for the final hit of an all in.
olaf-combo-allin.text: When going all in, land Q, close in for a basic attack, activate W, and finish with E. Its true damage still goes through if the opponent builds armor or magic resistance, so save it for the final hit.

olaf-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, throw Q in the direction your opponent is moving, pick up the axe as you close in, then use a basic attack followed by E. Picking up the axe reduces Q's cooldown. If you fail to pick up the axe, the long gap before your next Q can leave you open to a counterattack. Throw Q where the path to retrieve the axe also lets you close in.
olaf-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, throw Q in the direction your opponent is moving to slow them, then close in along the axe’s landing path, pick it up to reduce Q’s cooldown, land a basic attack, and use E. Missing the axe leaves a long gap before your next Q and opens you to a counterattack, so throw it only where retrieving it also lets you approach.

olaf-combo-ult.basis: Use R just before or just after the opponent's crowd control hits you. Each basic attack or E hit on a champion extends R's duration. After activating R, stay on the opponent and keep attacking.
olaf-combo-ult.text: R is for clearing the opponent’s crowd control, not for starting an engage; activate it just before the control lands or immediately after it does. Each basic attack or E hit on a champion extends R’s duration, so stay close and keep attacking once it’s active.

olaf-laning.basis: Against melee opponents, close in early to win trades. Drop Q between you and the opponent, rather than beyond the wave, so you can pick it up as you close in. Olaf has limited mana, so failing to retrieve a Q costs him.
olaf-laning.text: Against melee opponents, close in early to win trades. Drop Q between you and the opponent instead of beyond the wave, so retrieving it and approaching become one movement. Olaf has limited mana, making an unretrieved Q a costly trade.

olaf-laning-vs-ranged.basis: Against ranged opponents, avoid forcing your way in; use Q to last hit and scale. Activate R and engage when a ranged opponent has used their poke ability or your jungler can follow up. Poking with Q from a position where you cannot retrieve the axe costs you.
olaf-laning-vs-ranged.text: Against ranged opponents, don’t force an approach; use Q to secure last hits and keep up in levels and growth. Activate R and engage only after they have used their poke ability or when your jungler can follow up, and avoid poking from a position where you cannot retrieve the axe, since that trade costs you.

olaf-phase-early.basis: Olaf is strong in level 1 trades against melee opponents. Olaf is strongest between levels 3 and 6, when he can use Q and E together. Late in the game, Olaf struggles against long range compositions that keep him from closing in.
olaf-phase-early.text: Olaf’s level 1 attack damage and movement speed are among the highest of all champions, making him strong in trades against melee opponents from the start. He is strongest from levels 3 to 6, when Q and E are both available, but struggles later against long range compositions that prevent him from closing in.

olaf-phase-lowhp.basis: Berserker Rage gives Olaf more attack speed and lifesteal the more health he has lost. Even below half health, Olaf can fight hard if he stays close to a target he can lifesteal from.
olaf-phase-lowhp.text: Berserker Rage increases Olaf’s attack speed and lifesteal as he loses health. Falling below half health does not always mean he should retreat: if a target he can lifesteal from is within reach, that can be his strongest moment, especially with W and R active together.

olaf-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent's healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Olaf stays close and attacks for a long time, so he can keep Grievous Wounds applied.
olaf-situational-antiheal.text: If the opponent’s healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Olaf stays close and attacks for a long time, allowing him to keep Grievous Wounds applied.

olaf-skill-e.basis: E costs Olaf health to deal true damage. If E kills the target, Olaf gets back the health it cost. Each basic attack reduces E's cooldown. Keep using E while you stay close to the opponent. If you're low on health and a kill isn't certain, hold E so its health cost doesn't kill you first.
olaf-skill-e.text: E costs Olaf health to deal true damage, but refunds that cost if it kills the target. Each basic attack reduces E’s cooldown, so keep using it while you stay close; if you’re low on health and the kill is uncertain, hold it or its health cost could kill you first.

olaf-skill-q-armor.basis: Champions hit by Q briefly lose armor. In a teamfight, time Q with the engage of allies who mainly deal physical damage. The armor reduction from a Q timed with your allies' physical damage engage increases the team's total damage.
olaf-skill-q-armor.text: Champions hit by Q briefly lose armor. In a teamfight, time it to land as allies who mainly deal physical damage engage, increasing the team’s total damage instead of using it only for your own.

olaf-skill-q-axe.basis: The Q axe stays on the ground, and picking it up greatly reduces its cooldown. The route to retrieve the axe determines Olaf's movement path. When chasing, throw Q ahead of the opponent and pick it up as you follow. When retreating, throw Q along your escape route behind you and pick it up as you leave. Before throwing an axe over a wall, check whether the terrain lets you retrieve it.
olaf-skill-q-axe.text: The Q axe stays on the ground, and picking it up greatly reduces its cooldown, so its landing spot determines Olaf’s path. When chasing, throw it ahead of the opponent and retrieve it as you follow; when retreating, throw it behind you along your escape route and pick it up as you leave. Check the terrain before throwing it over a wall, or you may be unable to retrieve it.

olaf-skill-r.basis: R prevents movement impairing effects but does not prevent damage. If the opponent has already used their crowd control, there's no reason to activate R. If you activate R before the opponent uses their crowd control, they can hold the ability and wait out R's duration. Use R a beat after the opponent's crowd control comes out.
olaf-skill-r.text: R prevents movement impairing effects, but damage still gets through. There’s no reason to activate it after the opponent has used their crowd control, while using it too early lets them hold that ability until R expires; activate it a beat after their crowd control comes out.

olaf-skill-w.basis: W provides both attack speed and a shield. W's shield grows stronger the more health you have lost. Activating W early at full health makes its shield less effective. After taking the opponent's combo, activate W and use its attack speed and shield to counterattack.
olaf-skill-w.text: W grants both attack speed and a shield, and the shield grows stronger the more health you have lost. Activating it early at full health wastes that value; take the opponent’s combo first, then use W’s attack speed and shield together to counterattack.

olaf-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use R to ignore crowd control and run straight at the backline damage dealers. In a narrow approach, throw Q behind the opponent first to slow them, then engage and retrieve the axe.
olaf-teamfight.text: In teamfights, don’t spend time fighting the frontline: use R to ignore crowd control and run straight at the backline damage dealers. If the approach is narrow, throw Q behind your target first, then push toward the axe to slow them and retrieve it during the engage.

orianna-combo-e-delivery.basis: E is the only way to move the ball beyond Q's range. Use E on an engaging ally to make the ball move with them. Before a teamfight, first consider the path E will take to send the ball to an engaging ally.
orianna-combo-e-delivery.text: E is the only way to send the ball beyond Q’s range. Cast it on an engaging ally so the ball follows them, then activate R or W where they arrive. Since this can place the ball much deeper than Q can reach, always consider this route first before a teamfight.

orianna-combo-flash-ult.basis: If you cannot get the ball where you want it, use Flash to move Orianna there, then cast R. Save Flash if the ball is near the enemy or on an ally and gives you the same R angle.
orianna-combo-flash-ult.text: If you cannot get the ball where you want it for R, Flash to move Orianna into position, then cast R. If the ball is already near the enemy or attached to an ally and gives you the same angle, save Flash.

orianna-combo-poke.basis: For basic poke, use Q then W. Press W right after Q to make W activate when the ball arrives. If the ball is near Orianna, pressing W before Q makes W activate out of the enemy's reach.
orianna-combo-poke.text: For basic poke, use Q to send the ball toward your opponent, then press W immediately so it activates as the ball arrives. Pressing W first makes it activate near Orianna, out of reach; the order determines whether the poke lands.

orianna-combo-ult.basis: Before starting an R combo, place the ball beyond or beside the enemy group. After placing the ball, use R, then Q, then W. R pulls enemies toward the ball. Place the ball where R can pull enemies toward your team. Poor ball placement can make R pull enemies away from your team.
orianna-combo-ult.text: For an R combo, place the ball beyond or beside the enemy group, then use R → Q → W. R pulls enemies toward the ball, so position it to pull them toward your team; a misplaced ball can pull them away instead.

orianna-laning.basis: In lane, use Q for both last hits and poke. Manage your mana in lane. Keep the ball near the enemy while staying farther back yourself. Send Q to a spot where the enemy and the backline minions overlap to clear the wave and poke at the same time.
orianna-laning.text: In lane, manage your mana while using Q for both last hits and poke. Keep the ball near your opponent while standing farther back, and send Q where the opponent overlaps with the backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time.

orianna-laning-wave.basis: Orianna is vulnerable to jungle ganks when she pushes the wave all the way in. Without vision, keep the wave in the middle instead of pushing it all the way in. Without vision, poke with Q while keeping the wave in the middle.
orianna-laning-wave.text: Orianna’s short range and very low movement speed leave her exposed to jungle ganks if she pushes the wave all the way in. Without vision, hold it near the middle and poke with Q instead.

orianna-phase.basis: Orianna can be taken down in a single catch early on. Orianna gets stronger once Q's cooldown becomes shorter. Orianna gets stronger at level 6, when she gains R. Orianna peaks in the mid to late game, when she has enough items to turn a teamfight with one R.
orianna-phase.text: Orianna’s level 1 health, armor, and magic resistance are all among the lowest of any champion, so an early catch can take her down at once. She grows stronger as Q’s cooldown shortens and again at level 6 when she gains R, then peaks in the mid to late game once she has enough items to turn a teamfight with a single R.

orianna-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has an assassin who can engage, buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner to survive after using R. Orianna is most likely to be focused right after using R.
orianna-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy has an assassin who can dive in, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier. Orianna is most vulnerable immediately after using R, so surviving that moment helps your team deal damage.

orianna-skill-ball-position.basis: All of Orianna's abilities work around the ball's position. Q sends the ball to a target location, where it stays. W and R activate at the ball's location. E attaches the ball to an ally. Decide where to place the ball before choosing which ability to use.
orianna-skill-ball-position.text: All of Orianna’s abilities depend on the ball’s position: Q sends it to a target location and leaves it there, W and R activate where it sits, and E attaches it to an ally. Decide where the ball needs to go before choosing an ability.

orianna-skill-ball-return.basis: The ball returns automatically if it gets too far from Orianna. While the ball is away from Orianna, she loses the armor and magic resistance from E's passive. Orianna is most vulnerable right after casting Q, when she loses E's passive. Move through dangerous areas with the ball returned to Orianna.
orianna-skill-ball-return.text: The ball returns automatically if it gets too far from Orianna. While it is away, she loses the armor and magic resistance from E’s passive, making her most vulnerable right after casting Q. Retrieve the ball before moving through dangerous areas.

orianna-skill-e.basis: E shields its target. E sends the ball to an ally. An ally carrying the ball gains armor and magic resistance from E's passive. Before a teamfight, use E to attach the ball to the ally who will engage. If you expect to be targeted, use E on yourself to retrieve the ball and gain a shield.
orianna-skill-e.text: E gives its target a shield and delivers the ball; an ally carrying it also gains armor and magic resistance from its passive. Attach the ball to your engaging ally before a teamfight, or cast E on yourself if you expect to be targeted to retrieve the ball and gain a shield.

orianna-skill-passive.basis: P adds magic damage to basic attacks. P's bonus damage increases with consecutive attacks on the same target. Early in lane, trade back if the opposing mage starts a basic attack trade.
orianna-skill-passive.text: P adds magic damage to basic attacks, increasing with consecutive hits on the same target. Orianna wins short basic attack trades against other mages, so early in lane, trade back when one starts attacking you.

orianna-skill-w.basis: W deals area damage around the ball. W slows enemies around the ball. W increases the movement speed of allies at that location. When allies engage or you retreat together, keep the ball near them and use W to help them move.
orianna-skill-w.text: W deals area damage and slows enemies around the ball while giving allies there movement speed. Use it for more than damage trades: when an ally engages or you retreat together, place the ball near your allies and activate W to help them move.

orianna-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use R to pull multiple enemies toward your team. Send the ball to an engaging ally with E, then use R. Cast R the moment the ally you gave the ball to with E reaches the enemy. Going up to the enemy team with the ball on Orianna and using R is a last resort.
orianna-teamfight.text: In teamfights, use R to pull multiple enemies toward your team. The most reliable setup is to attach the ball to an engaging ally with E and cast R the moment they reach the enemy. Casting R with the ball on Orianna requires you to walk up to the enemy team, so treat it as a last resort.

ornn-combo-brittle.basis: Land W's final flame, then auto attack for bonus damage and a knockback. Only enemies hit by W's final flame become Brittle. Move forward until W's final flame can reach the target.
ornn-combo-brittle.text: For a damage trade, use W → auto attack. Only enemies hit by W’s final flame become Brittle; an auto attack against them then deals bonus damage and knocks them back. Move close enough for that final flame to connect, or the combo loses half its value.

ornn-combo-order.basis: Brittle extends the duration of immobilizing crowd control. If you're already close to the target, apply Brittle with W, then knock them up with E. If you're already close to the target, apply Brittle with W, then knock them up with R. If the target has a mobility ability, lock them down with E first, then land W. If the target has a mobility ability, lock them down with R first, then land W.
ornn-combo-order.text: Ability order changes how much you get from a combo. Brittle extends immobilizing crowd control, so if you’re already close, apply it with W before the knockup from E’s shockwave or an R headbutt. When landing W reliably matters more, use E or R to lock down a target with a mobility ability first, then follow with W.

ornn-combo-pillar.basis: Place a pillar with Q, then use E to hit it and knock up nearby enemies. A magma pillar rises at the end of Q's path. Q's pillar lets you knock up enemies with E even in open terrain. Before casting Q, choose where to place the pillar you'll hit with E.
ornn-combo-pillar.text: Ornn’s basic engage is Q → E: a magma pillar rises at the end of Q’s path, and charging into it with E shatters it, releasing a shockwave that knocks up nearby enemies. This is his only way to set up a knockup himself in open terrain, so decide where the pillar needs to stand before casting Q.

ornn-combo-ult.basis: The first spirit summoned by R slows enemies it passes through and makes them Brittle. Recast R to headbutt the spirit, changing its direction and knocking up enemies. Summon the spirit behind the target, let it pass through the enemy team, then headbutt it back toward your allies from the other side.
ornn-combo-ult.text: R has two casts. The spirit first travels toward Ornn, slowing enemies it passes through and making them Brittle; only when he recasts R to headbutt it does it change direction and knock enemies up. Summon it behind the target so it passes through the enemy team, then meet it from the other side and send it back toward your allies.

ornn-laning.basis: Ornn's early damage is among the lowest of top lane champions. In lane, farm safely with Q and keep up in CS and levels. If your opponent pushes the lane, farm under your turret. When your opponent recalls, use Living Forge to finish an item and reverse the item gap.
ornn-laning.text: Ornn’s early damage is among the lowest of top lane champions. Rather than seeking an advantage in lane, farm safely with Q and aim to keep up in CS and levels. If your opponent pushes, let the wave come in and farm under your turret; when they recall, finish an item with Living Forge to reverse the item gap.

ornn-phase.basis: Ornn is weakest at levels 1 and 2, when his cooldowns are long and his damage is low. Once you get R at level 6, you can force a fight with your allies. Ornn's real power spike comes in mid game, after he builds two or three defensive items. Late game, the Masterwork upgrades you've given your allies increase your value to the team.
ornn-phase.text: Ornn is weakest at levels 1–2, when his cooldowns are long and his damage is low. R gives him a way to force an engage with allies at level 6, while his real power window comes in mid game after he has built two or three defensive items. Late in the game, his contribution comes from the Masterwork upgrades granted to his allies rather than his own damage, so his value to the team grows as the game goes on.

ornn-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing makes them hard to finish with sustained damage, build healing reduction. Ornn deals magic damage, so buy Oblivion Orb on the way to Morellonomicon. Morellonomicon's health also helps Ornn serve as a frontliner. Executioner's Calling only provides attack damage, so it doesn't suit Ornn. Ornn's fights last a long time, making it easy for him to maintain healing reduction.
ornn-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing keeps Ornn’s sustained damage from finishing them, build healing reduction. His damage is magic, so start with Oblivion Orb and upgrade it to Morellonomicon; the health it provides also suits his front line role. Executioner’s Calling offers only attack damage, a stat Ornn cannot use well. His fights last long enough to keep healing reduction applied.

ornn-situational-thornmail.basis: If the enemy's main damage is physical and they attack Ornn with auto attacks, buy Thornmail early. Ornn can use Thornmail's reflected damage and healing reduction while taking hits on the front line.
ornn-situational-thornmail.text: If the enemy’s main damage is physical and they wear Ornn down with auto attacks, buy Thornmail earlier. He already takes hits on the front line, so its reflected damage and healing reduction get direct use.

ornn-skill-e.basis: E must hit terrain to knock up enemies. If E doesn't hit terrain, it only deals damage as Ornn passes through. If an enemy created wall blocks your allies' escape route, break it with E. If your allies aren't nearby, save E to disengage.
ornn-skill-e.text: E is both Ornn’s engage tool and a way to destroy terrain. It only knocks enemies up when it hits terrain; against an opponent without a wall behind them, it merely deals damage as Ornn passes through. It can also clear enemy-created walls blocking your allies’ escape route. Using E to engage leaves no way to disengage, so save it when your allies aren’t nearby.

ornn-skill-forge.basis: Living Forge lets you spend gold to craft items anywhere. Stay in lane and craft items while continuing to farm CS and pressure the turret. Crafting takes time, so don't try it when an enemy is close. Don't try to craft items when the jungler's location is unclear.
ornn-skill-forge.text: Ornn’s P, Living Forge, lets him spend gold to craft items anywhere, which is his entire laning advantage: opponents must recall to shop, while he can stay to farm CS and pressure the turret. Crafting takes time, so avoid it when an enemy is close or the jungler’s location is unclear.

ornn-skill-masterwork.basis: Masterwork upgrades strengthen allies' completed items without costing gold. Prioritize Masterwork upgrades for your main damage dealer with plenty of items. Prioritize allies whose item upgrade can directly change the outcome of a teamfight. As Ornn levels up, the number of upgrades he can grant increases. If there's no reason to save a Masterwork upgrade, use it as soon as it becomes available.
ornn-skill-masterwork.text: Masterwork upgrades are worth more to Ornn’s allies than to Ornn himself: they strengthen allies’ completed items at no gold cost, raising the whole team’s power for free. Prioritize a main damage dealer who already has plenty of items and allies whose upgraded item could directly change a teamfight’s outcome. As Ornn levels up, he can have more upgrades granted at once, so use each one as soon as it becomes available unless you have a reason to save it.

ornn-skill-q.basis: If Q hits an enemy champion, the fissure stops there and the pillar rises near them. If Q misses enemy champions, the pillar rises at maximum range. When using Q to farm and poke, hit your opponent with it. To position the pillar for E's shockwave, cast Q past your opponent. Place Q's pillar where your opponent would approach to farm CS or along the jungler's entry path to block the way.
ornn-skill-q.text: Q’s fissure stops when it hits an enemy champion, placing the pillar near their feet; if it misses, the pillar rises at maximum range. Aim to hit your opponent when farming or poking, but cast past them when you need the pillar in a specific spot for E’s shockwave. Keep those aims distinct so the pillar lands where you intend. It also acts as terrain, so placing it where an opponent must approach to farm CS or along the enemy jungler’s entry path can block that area entirely.

ornn-skill-w.basis: Ornn is Unstoppable while moving forward with W. Use W to push through opponents who stop your engage with slows or knockbacks. W's direction is fixed and its movement speed is low, so its final flame is hard to land on opponents who escape with mobility abilities. Use W right after your opponent uses a mobility ability or when they're cornered against a wall.
ornn-skill-w.text: Ornn is Unstoppable while advancing with W, making it a way through opponents who try to stop his engage with slows or knockbacks. Its direction is fixed and its movement is slow, though, so the final flame will miss someone who escapes with a mobility ability. Use W just after they use that ability or when they’re cornered against a wall.

ornn-teamfight.basis: Start teamfights near terrain you can use to knock enemies up with E. In a narrow passage with walls, hit a wall with E to knock enemies up, then apply Brittle with W. In open terrain, let the R spirit sweep through opponents, then use E. Counter the enemy engage and protect your damage dealers.
ornn-teamfight.text: Start teamfights near terrain. In a narrow passage with walls, the most reliable sequence is to hit a wall with E for the knockup, then apply Brittle with W. If you must fight in the open, send the R spirit through the opponents first and follow with E. Ornn is no damage dealer: hold position in front of your carries, counter the enemy engage, and protect them instead of chasing the enemy backline.

pantheon-combo-allin.basis: The basic engage is W leap, empowered basic attack, E, then tap Q. W targets an enemy, so it cannot miss. If the passive is fully stacked right after W lands, the empowered basic attack hits multiple times.
pantheon-combo-allin.text: The basic engage is W, an empowered basic attack, E, then a tap Q. W targets an enemy and cannot miss, making it a reliable way to start; if Mortal Will is fully stacked when W lands, the empowered basic attack hits multiple times.

pantheon-combo-poke.basis: Tap Q to thrust or hold it to throw the spear. Tapping Q greatly reduces its cooldown. Use tap Q to farm and stack the passive. When you cannot get close enough, poke with held Q.
pantheon-combo-poke.text: Tap Q to thrust, greatly reducing its cooldown so you can farm and stack Mortal Will. Hold Q to throw the spear and poke when you cannot get close enough; choosing between the two is fundamental to playing Pantheon.

pantheon-laning.basis: Chip away at the enemy's health with held Q, then use W to close in when they focus on last-hitting. Use brush to set up an angle to approach with W. Engage with W only right after the enemy uses their counterattack ability.
pantheon-laning.text: Chip away at the enemy's health with held Q, then close in with W when they focus on last-hitting. Pantheon's short range makes the approach risky, so use brush to set up your angle and engage only right after the enemy uses their counterattack ability.

pantheon-laning-support.basis: As support, prioritize building up poke damage. Pantheon support has very high kill participation but also dies often. If your engage fails, the enemy marksman gets ahead. Use W only when your allies are close enough to follow up.
pantheon-laning-support.text: As support, prioritize repeated poke over fights that risk your life. Pantheon support has very high kill participation but also dies often, and a failed engage can put the enemy marksman ahead. Use W only when your allies are close enough to follow up.

pantheon-laning-top.basis: In top lane, use tap Q to secure CS while stacking the passive. Go in with W right after the enemy uses their poke ability. Against ranged enemies, use E like a shield to close the gap. If you cannot close the gap, poke with held Q.
pantheon-laning-top.text: In top lane, use tap Q to secure CS while stacking Mortal Will, then go in with W right after the enemy uses their poke ability. Against ranged enemies, use E like a shield to close the gap; if you cannot get close enough, switch to poking with held Q instead of forcing the engage.

pantheon-phase.basis: Pantheon is strongest early. Tap Q has a short cooldown, letting you poke throughout the laning phase. Once you learn R at level 6, you can influence other lanes. As items build up in the late game, Pantheon's damage and durability both fall behind. Use the lead you built early to end the game.
pantheon-phase.text: Pantheon's level 1 base stats are among the best, making him strongest early. Tap Q's short cooldown lets you poke throughout the laning phase, and learning R at level 6 lets you influence other lanes. As items build up, his damage and durability fall behind, so use your early lead to end the game.

pantheon-situational-antiheal.basis: Buy Executioner's Calling early if the enemy has a way to heal. Pantheon deals his damage in a short burst, so enemy healing during the fight can take away your chance to secure a kill.
pantheon-situational-antiheal.text: Buy Executioner's Calling early if the enemy can heal. Pantheon deals damage in a short burst, and healing during the fight can erase your chance to secure a kill.

pantheon-skill-e.basis: E only blocks damage coming from the direction Pantheon faces. E does not block turret damage. While using E, keep facing the enemy. E is almost useless when you are surrounded from multiple directions. Recast E to end it early and trigger the finishing strike sooner. If there is no more damage to block, end E immediately and move to your next action.
pantheon-skill-e.text: E only blocks damage from the direction Pantheon faces and cannot block turret damage. Keep facing the enemy while using it; if you are surrounded from multiple directions, it is almost useless. Recasting E ends it early and brings forward the finishing strike, so if there is nothing left to block, end it immediately and move to your next action.

pantheon-skill-passive.basis: After enough abilities and basic attacks, the passive empowers the next basic ability. Stack the passive with tap Q and basic attacks before a fight. Decide whether to empower W or E, then use that ability last. Hitting minions also stacks the passive.
pantheon-skill-passive.text: Mortal Will empowers your next basic ability after enough ability uses and basic attacks. Before a fight, stack it with tap Q and basic attacks, including attacks on minions, then decide whether to empower W or E and use that ability last.

pantheon-skill-q-finish.basis: Thrown Q deals much more damage to low-health enemies. Throw Q to finish fleeing enemies when they are in range. Do not use Q early during a chase.
pantheon-skill-q-finish.text: Thrown Q deals much more damage to low-health enemies, so use it to finish a fleeing target while they are in range instead of chasing them down. Save Q until then during a chase.

pantheon-skill-r.basis: R is an area ability that makes Pantheon leap and land at a chosen location. You need vision of the area to aim R's landing spot accurately. Land with R toward an allied ward. Enemies have time to move away while Pantheon is descending with R. Time R's landing to coincide with allied crowd control.
pantheon-skill-r.text: R makes Pantheon leap and land at a chosen location, damaging an area. You need vision there to aim the landing accurately, so land toward an allied ward and time your descent with allied crowd control, since enemies have time to move away before you land.

pantheon-skill-w.basis: W is Pantheon's only engage ability. W only closes the gap toward an enemy, so it cannot be used to escape. Before using W, check the enemy's mobility abilities and where your allies are positioned to help.
pantheon-skill-w.text: W is Pantheon's only way to engage and moves him toward an enemy, so it cannot be used to escape. Using it commits you to the fight; check the enemy's mobility abilities and where your allies are positioned to help before you go in.

pantheon-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, push through the frontline and lock down the enemy carries. Use E to block damage from the front as you move in, then use W to reach a priority target. If you engage alone first, you have no way out after W. Engage with W after an ally lands crowd control. When engaging with R, land alongside your allies.
pantheon-teamfight.text: In teamfights, push through the frontline and lock down the enemy carries: use E to block damage from the front as you move in, then W to reach a priority target. You have no way out after W if you engage alone first, so go in after an ally lands crowd control or land with R alongside your allies.

poppy-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, use E to stun the enemy against a wall, then follow with Q and a basic attack. During the E stun, Q's zone detonates beneath the enemy, dealing damage both times. If you can catch the enemy, use E before Q so they cannot dodge the zone's detonation.
poppy-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, use E to stun the enemy against a wall, then follow with Q and a basic attack. The E stun holds them in Q’s lingering zone long enough for both the initial hit and the detonation to land. If you use Q first, they can walk out before the zone detonates, so lead with E whenever you have a way to hold them in place.

poppy-combo-e-angle.basis: To stun with E, Poppy, the enemy, and the wall must line up. If there is no wall behind the enemy, move around them to create an angle that pushes them into a wall, then use E. In lane, look for a short angle that pushes the enemy into a side wall rather than straight ahead.
poppy-combo-e-angle.text: E pushes its target in the direction Poppy is facing, so line up Poppy, the enemy, and a wall to secure the stun. If there is no wall behind them, move around first to create the angle. In lane, the shorter angle is usually toward a side wall rather than straight ahead.

poppy-combo-passive.basis: The passive shield tends to land near a wall, making it easy to collect after pushing an enemy into the wall with E. After stunning with E, walk forward to collect the shield and continue trading while shielded. If you kill the target, the shield returns immediately, so you do not need to collect it when finishing them off.
poppy-combo-passive.text: Iron Ambassador’s shield tends to land near a wall, so the path to collect it often follows naturally from pushing an enemy into that wall with E. After the stun, walk forward to pick it up and continue trading with a shield. If you kill the target, the shield returns immediately, so there is no need to collect it.

poppy-jungle-gank.basis: When ganking, approach from behind the lane and find an E angle that pushes the enemy into a side wall. If you charge in with E from the front, you may only push the enemy away. Draw the enemy toward places with nearby walls, such as a river entrance or beside a turret.
poppy-jungle-gank.text: For a jungle gank, the approach angle must give you a wall stun. Enter from behind the lane and position to push the enemy into a side wall with E; charging straight at them may only push them away. Drawing them toward a nearby wall, such as one at a river entrance or beside a turret, is key to a successful gank.

poppy-laning-melee.basis: When a melee opponent steps forward to last hit, use E from an angle with a wall behind them. A wall stun with E guarantees a follow-up Q and basic attack. If there is no wall stun angle, save E and harass with the passive shield. Save W while the enemy still has an engage ability available.
poppy-laning-melee.text: When a melee opponent steps forward to last hit, use E from an angle that puts a wall behind them. The stun guarantees a follow up Q and basic attack, making the trade one sided. If the angle is unavailable, save E and harass only with Iron Ambassador’s shield; keep W ready while the enemy still has an engage ability available.

poppy-laning-ranged.basis: Against ranged opponents, avoid forcing an engage with E; harass with the passive shield and secure CS. Collecting the shield lets you stay in lane longer.
poppy-laning-ranged.text: Against ranged opponents, avoid forcing an engage with E; use the passive shield’s extended range to harass while securing CS. Poppy moves relatively quickly, so when an opponent has just used a poke ability, walk forward to close the gap and save E for that moment. Picking up the shield for its protection also helps you stay in lane longer.

poppy-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Poppy has a long Q cooldown and no E, so she has little ability to force a fight. Once you learn E and Q's cooldown gets shorter, you can pressure melee opponents. At level 6, learning R lets you intervene in dives and teamfights. As items build up in the mid to late game, Poppy becomes especially valuable. In the late game, your raw damage falls behind, so focus on stopping enemy damage dealers.
poppy-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Q’s long cooldown limits your harass, and without E you have little ability to force a fight. Once you learn E and Q’s cooldown shortens, you can pressure melee opponents; after learning R at level 6, you can also take part in dives and teamfights. Poppy gains substantial health and Armor with levels, making her especially valuable with items in the mid to late game. Her raw damage falls behind late, so focus on stopping enemy damage dealers rather than trying to deal damage yourself.

poppy-situational-antiheal.basis: Against an enemy with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. If you are building defensive items, upgrade Executioner's Calling into a completed item. Poppy stays close to enemies for a long time, making it easy to maintain Grievous Wounds.
poppy-situational-antiheal.text: Against a champion with strong healing, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce it, then upgrade it into a completed item if you are building defensive items. Poppy stays close to enemies for extended periods, making Grievous Wounds relatively easy to maintain.

poppy-skill-e.basis: E is both an engage tool and a reliable stun, so do not use it just to move around. If E does not knock the target into terrain, it only pushes them and deals no stun or bonus damage. Even without a wall stun, you can angle E to push the enemy toward your team.
poppy-skill-e.text: E is both Poppy’s engage tool and her only guaranteed stun, so do not spend it just to move. Without terrain to knock the target into, it only pushes them and provides neither a stun nor bonus damage. You can still use it to start a fight without a wall stun by positioning to push the enemy toward your team.

poppy-skill-passive.basis: When the passive is ready, your next basic attack gains a large amount of range. Do not use the passive shield on a minion when you need it to harass a ranged opponent. A shield that lands near the enemy disappears if they step on it, so do not overextend to collect it.
poppy-skill-passive.text: When Iron Ambassador is ready, your next basic attack gains substantial range. It is one of melee Poppy’s few ways to harass a ranged opponent, so do not spend it on a minion. An enemy can destroy the dropped shield by stepping on it; if it rolls toward them, give it up rather than overextend to collect it.

poppy-skill-q.basis: Q deals immediate damage, then its lingering zone detonates once more. Q's maximum health damage deals more damage to enemies with more health. Q has a damage cap against minions and monsters, so its farming efficiency is average. When finishing an enemy off, you can use Q first to slow them.
poppy-skill-q.text: Q deals damage immediately, then its lingering zone detonates once more after a short delay; if you cannot keep the enemy in place, only half the damage lands. Its damage scales with the target’s maximum health, making it more valuable against high-health enemies, but a damage cap against minions and monsters keeps its farming efficiency average. Since the zone’s slow also helps you chase, you can cast Q first to pin down an enemy when setting up a finish.

poppy-skill-r.basis: In a 1v1, cast R without charging it to interrupt the enemy's counterattack. Fully charging R lengthens the fissure and knocks all enemies hit far away. When charging R for a long time, start behind a wall or out of vision so the enemy has trouble seeing Poppy slow down. When using R to peel an enemy off your damage dealer, calculate the direction that will knock them toward the Nexus.
poppy-skill-r.text: R has two uses: cast it without charging for a quick knockup on enemies in front of you that can interrupt a counterattack in a 1v1, or charge it fully to lengthen the fissure and knock every enemy hit far away, splitting up a teamfight. Poppy slows down and her movement is obvious while charging, so start behind a wall or out of enemy vision. When peeling an enemy off your damage dealer, plan for the knockback to send them toward the Nexus.

poppy-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, position yourself to protect your backline. Stop the enemy engager's dash with W, then stun them against a wall with E. When your damage dealer is targeted, save E to intercept the enemy instead of using it to engage.
poppy-teamfight.text: Poppy’s role in a teamfight is to guard her backline rather than dive in first. Stand in the enemy engager’s path, stop their dash with W, then stun them against a wall with E. Using E to engage takes you away from the ally W needs to protect, so if your damage dealer is likely to be targeted, save E to intercept the attacker.

pyke-combo-qe.basis: The basic kill combo is to pull with Q, then immediately use E, a basic attack, and R in that order. Using E right after Q lands makes the phantom's stun hit as the target can move again. If you leave a gap between Q and E, the target can escape with Flash.
pyke-combo-qe.text: For a basic kill combo, hold Q to pull the target, use E as soon as they are pulled in, then follow with a basic attack and R. E must come immediately after Q lands so the phantom stuns them just as they can move again; leave a gap and they can escape with Flash.

pyke-combo-r-engage.basis: When engaging with R, hold Q to pull the target immediately after arriving. When engaging with R, you can use E immediately after arriving. Targets with plenty of health are less likely to expect an R engage, giving them less time to react.
pyke-combo-r-engage.text: R can also start an engage: immediately after arriving, hold Q to pull the target or follow up with E. Enemies with plenty of health are less likely to expect R, giving them less time to react.

pyke-combo-w-approach.basis: Approach from outside vision while camouflaged with W, then tap Q when in range and use E. Tapping Q casts much faster. At close range, don’t charge Q.
pyke-combo-w-approach.text: To approach from outside vision, use W to close in while camouflaged, tap Q once in range, then use E. A tapped Q casts much faster, so there is no need to charge it at close range.

pyke-laning.basis: Pyke is a support who takes almost no CS and grows through kills. In lane, move between brushes and blind spots to keep opponents under pressure within Q range. Look for an opening to engage together after your ADC pushes the wave. Taking one heavy hit removes your chance to engage, so do not force the first attack.
pyke-laning.text: Pyke is a support who takes almost no CS and grows through kills. In lane, move between brushes and blind spots to keep opponents under pressure within Q range, then look to engage together after your ADC pushes the wave. One heavy hit can erase that opportunity, so avoid forcing the first attack.

pyke-laning-w-pressure.basis: Simply activating W can pressure opponents into backing away. While W pushes opponents back, secure river vision or roam mid. Roam only when the wave is pushing toward the enemy and your ADC can hold the lane alone.
pyke-laning-w-pressure.text: Simply activating W can make opponents back away as they worry about a gank, a close range Q, or getting caught. Use that pressure to secure river vision or roam mid, even without closing in. Roam only when the wave is pushing toward the enemy and your ADC can hold the lane alone.

pyke-phase.basis: Kill opportunities start at level 2, when you have both Q and E. Pyke's power rises sharply at level 6, when he learns R. Pyke reaches his peak when he completes his first core lethality item. After completing your first core lethality item, roam to pressure other lanes.
