Late in the game, it is hard to bring enemies with increased health below the execution threshold. In late game teamfights, Pyke is fragile and can easily die first.
pyke-phase.text: Kill opportunities begin at level 2, when Pyke has both Q and E, and his power rises sharply at level 6 when he learns R. He peaks on completing his first core lethality item; from then on, roam to pressure other lanes. Late in the game, enemies with more health are harder to bring below the execution threshold, and Pyke is fragile enough to die first in teamfights.

pyke-skill-e.basis: E stuns when the phantom left at the starting point returns, not during the dash itself. To stun with E, keep the target on the line between your starting and ending points. E works for both engaging and escaping. Before engaging, decide whether E or allied crowd control will give you a way out.
pyke-skill-e.text: E stuns when the phantom left at Pyke’s starting point returns to him, rather than during the dash itself. Keep the target on the line between your starting and ending points to land the stun. Because E serves as both an engage and an escape, decide before going in whether E or allied crowd control will give you a way out.

pyke-skill-passive.basis: P stores some damage taken from enemy champions and heals Pyke when he leaves enemy vision. After a fight, break vision with W or a brush, heal, then engage again. If P's healing has not started, the enemy can still see you.
pyke-skill-passive.text: P stores some of the damage Pyke takes from enemy champions and heals him when he leaves their vision. After going in, break vision with W or a brush to heal before engaging again; if the healing has not started, the enemy can still see you.

pyke-skill-passive-ad.basis: Pyke converts all bonus maximum health into attack damage, regardless of its source. Items with health increase both durability and damage. Items with only armor or magic resistance do not convert into damage.
pyke-skill-passive-ad.text: Pyke converts all bonus maximum health into attack damage, regardless of its source, so health items improve both durability and damage. Armor or magic resistance alone adds no damage.

pyke-skill-q.basis: Tap Q to stab forward. Hold Q to throw the harpoon and pull the target. Even a half charged Q pulls the same distance at close range. Cancel Q before its channel ends or hit an enemy champion to recover most of the mana spent.
pyke-skill-q.text: Tap Q to stab forward, or hold it to throw a harpoon that pulls the target. You do not need to throw from maximum range: even a half charged harpoon at close range pulls the same distance. If the channel ends early or Q hits an enemy champion, you recover most of its mana cost, so canceling a poor attempt costs little.

pyke-skill-r.basis: R teleports Pyke to enemies below its health threshold in the X shaped area and executes them. R deals only half damage to enemies above its execution threshold. R's execution threshold rises with bonus attack damage and lethality. Use Q and E to lower the health of enemies you cannot execute yet.
pyke-skill-r.text: R teleports Pyke to and executes enemies below its health threshold within the X shaped area, but deals only half damage to those above it. The execution threshold rises with bonus attack damage and lethality, expanding your kill opportunities as you gain items. If a target is still too healthy to execute, lower their health with Q and E before using R.

pyke-skill-r-gold.basis: When Pyke gets a kill with R, the kill gold goes to the last ally who assisted, and Pyke receives a separate reward. Use R without hesitation on a target an ally has damaged. If an enemy champion dies within R's X shaped area, you can use R again for a short time. In teamfights, execute the lowest health enemy first with R to keep the recasts going.
pyke-skill-r-gold.text: When Pyke kills an enemy with R, the last ally who assisted receives the full kill gold, while Pyke gets a separate reward. Use it without hesitation on targets an ally has damaged. If an enemy champion dies within R’s X shaped area, you can cast it again for a short time, so execute the lowest health target first in teamfights to keep the recasts going.

pyke-skill-w.basis: W camouflages Pyke, hiding him until he enters an enemy champion's detection range. Use W to approach from an unexpected angle. In a one on one trade, it is often better to save W for P's healing.
pyke-skill-w.text: W camouflages Pyke until he enters an enemy champion’s detection range, letting him cross a route he would normally have to go around and approach from an unexpected angle. In a one on one trade, it is often better to save W to trigger P’s healing after taking damage.

pyke-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, target the single most dangerous enemy in the backline. Once allied crowd control lands and draws the enemy's attention, use W to enter from the flank. Leave yourself an escape route when entering a teamfight. If other enemies are grouped around a low health target, use R to aim for both the execution and area damage.
pyke-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Pyke should eliminate the most dangerous enemy in the backline. After allied crowd control lands and holds the enemy’s attention, enter from the flank with W while leaving yourself an escape route. If other enemies are grouped around a low health target, aim R to secure the execution and area damage together.

qiyana-combo-basic.basis: After taking an element, use E and Q during the dash, land a basic attack, then reset with W and use Q again. Use E first and save W so you can reset and have a way out. While holding an element, weave basic attacks between abilities.
qiyana-combo-basic.text: For a basic assassination combo, take an element with W, dash to the target with E, cast Q during the dash, and land a basic attack. Then use W on a different terrain type to reset Q’s cooldown and Royal Privilege before casting Q again. Use E before that second W so it provides both the reset and an escape route. While holding an element, Qiyana gains attack speed and bonus basic attack damage, so always weave basic attacks between abilities.

qiyana-combo-bush.basis: You become invisible inside the area created by brush element Q. While brush element Q blocks the enemy's vision, use E and W to set up an ambush angle. When chased, use brush element Q to break pursuit. You are revealed as soon as you leave brush element Q's area. While inside brush element Q's area, plan your W path to the next terrain.
qiyana-combo-bush.text: Brush element Q makes Qiyana invisible inside the area it creates. While the enemy has lost sight of you, use E and W to set up an ambush; when chased, use it to break pursuit. You are revealed as soon as you leave the area, so plan your W path to the next piece of terrain while still inside it.

qiyana-combo-ult.basis: To finish an enemy, push them into a wall with R to stun them, then switch elements with W and land Q and a basic attack. Use R first, then land your remaining attacks during the stun. When using Flash in the combo, reposition with Flash before casting R toward the terrain.
qiyana-combo-ult.text: To finish an enemy, use R to knock them into a wall and stun them, then switch elements with W and land Q and a basic attack during the stun. Saving R until the end can leave you pushing away an enemy who is already ready to escape. If you use Flash, reposition first, then cast R toward the terrain.

qiyana-laning-trade.basis: Approach with the brush element, land E and Q, then immediately use W on different terrain to escape. After using all your abilities, avoid staying in the middle of the lane where you can be hit back. Look for the moment an enemy steps forward to last-hit a minion.
qiyana-laning-trade.text: In lane, keep trades short and use brush to approach: take the brush element, land E and Q, then immediately use W on different terrain to get out. Staying in the middle of the lane after spending all three abilities leaves Qiyana open to retaliation. Her level-one health is relatively low, so avoid extended fights against ranged opponents and strike when they step forward to last-hit a minion.

qiyana-laning-wave.basis: Qiyana gains an advantage by moving to other lanes and the jungle rather than staying in lane to build up CS. Push the wave toward the enemy turret, then move along the river. Do not leave lane when the wave is pushing toward your side.
qiyana-laning-wave.text: In patch 26.17 mid lane stats, Qiyana ranks low in CS at 14 minutes but near the top in damage per minute and kills. She gains advantages by pushing waves and moving to side lanes and the jungle, rather than staying in lane to farm CS. After pushing a wave toward the enemy turret, travel along the river to pick up an element naturally; leaving while the wave is pulled toward your side leaves you at a disadvantage.

qiyana-phase.basis: Qiyana becomes much stronger when she learns R at level 6. Qiyana is at her strongest in the mid game with one or two core items. In the late game, enemy defensive items make it harder to kill in one burst, and engaging becomes riskier. Use your mid-game lead to take objectives and push towers, bringing the game to a close sooner.
qiyana-phase.text: Qiyana becomes much stronger when she learns R at level 6. Before then, she is a melee champion limited to short trades; afterward, she can use terrain to secure a stun and get a solo kill. She peaks in the mid game with one or two core items. Later, defensive items make enemies harder to burst down, and her low durability makes engaging riskier. Use a mid-game lead to take objectives and push towers to close out the game sooner.

qiyana-skill-e-autotarget.basis: E is a dash that passes through its target and moves you behind them. If you use Q while dashing to a champion with E, Q automatically targets that champion. To land Q, use it immediately after using E on a champion. Do not use E carelessly on minions; it is your only targeted way in.
qiyana-skill-e-autotarget.text: E dashes through its target, carrying Qiyana behind them. Press Q during an E dash toward a champion and it automatically targets that champion, so follow E immediately with Q to land it without having to aim. E is your only targeted way in; do not waste it on minions.

qiyana-skill-element.basis: Qiyana chooses how to fight based on the element she takes with W. An element taken from the river gives Q a root. An element taken from a wall or rock deals extra damage when finishing off an enemy below half health. Using Q with a brush element makes Qiyana invisible and increases her movement speed inside the area it creates. Choose the element you need before a fight and move to that terrain first.
qiyana-skill-element.text: Qiyana’s decisions start with the element she takes using W: river ice adds a root to Q, wall or rock adds damage against enemies below half health, and brush makes her invisible and faster inside the area created by Q, helping her approach or escape. Before a fight, decide which element you need and move toward that terrain first.

qiyana-skill-q-range.basis: Without an element, Q is a short melee attack; with an element, its range increases. Avoid using Q without an element out of habit in case you need to get close. Before farming with Q, check whether there is nearby terrain you can target with W. Do not use E to farm; it costs a lot of mana. To save mana, clear waves with the attack speed and bonus basic attack damage you gain while holding an element.
qiyana-skill-q-range.text: Without an element, Q is a short melee swing; holding one extends its range. Avoid putting Q on cooldown without an element out of habit, or it may be unavailable when you need to close the gap. Even when farming with Q, first check for nearby terrain you can target with W. E costs a lot of mana, so clear waves with the bonus basic attack damage and attack speed you gain while holding an element instead.

qiyana-skill-r-terrain.basis: R's shockwave knocks enemies back. If it hits a wall, river, or brush, the entire edge of that terrain explodes. Aim R along the line between the enemy and the terrain. If R hits a long stretch of river, the explosion covers a long area too. R's stun duration is proportional to the distance its shockwave travels. Fight in narrow passages or by the river to use R's terrain explosion.
qiyana-skill-r-terrain.text: R sends out a shockwave that knocks enemies back. If it reaches a wall, river, or brush, the entire edge of that terrain explodes, so aim along the line between the enemy and the terrain. Hitting a long stretch of river extends the explosion’s area, while the stun lasts longer the farther the shockwave travels. Look to fight in narrow passages or by the river.

qiyana-skill-w-reset.basis: W is a movement ability that resets Q's cooldown. After using Q, take a different element with W and use Q again. Taking a new element with W also resets the passive's cooldown on each target. Use W's reset to deal the passive's bonus damage twice to the same enemy.
qiyana-skill-w-reset.text: W is a movement ability that also resets Q’s cooldown. After using Q, take a different element with W to use Q again immediately. Taking a new element also resets Royal Privilege’s cooldown on every target, letting you deal its bonus damage twice to the same enemy. Using W only as a dash gives up much of your combo damage.

qiyana-teamfight.basis: If enemies group in a narrow passage or near a river or brush, start the teamfight with R. If you have no angle to engage with R, wait for an ally to engage and draw out enemy abilities, then use W and E to reach the backline. Engage after the enemy uses targeted crowd control and defensive abilities on your ally who engages. Before engaging, check which terrain you can target with W when retreating.
qiyana-teamfight.text: In a teamfight, choose between opening with R to knock the enemy team into terrain and cleaning up the backline. If enemies group in a narrow passage or near the river or brush, engage with R. Otherwise, wait for an ally to engage and draw out enemy abilities, then use W and E to reach the backline. Go in once the enemy has used its targeted crowd control and defensive abilities on your engaging ally, and identify terrain you can target with W to retreat before committing.

quinn-combo-allin.basis: When going all in, dash with E, land an empowered auto as soon as you land, then follow with Q and autos. E marks the target with Harrier, so your next auto is empowered. The empowered auto triggers W's passive, increasing the attack speed of your follow-up autos. When going all in, do not save E until the end.
quinn-combo-allin.text: For an all-in, dash with E, land an empowered auto as soon as you land, then follow with Q and more autos. E applies a Harrier mark directly to the target, so that first auto is always empowered and triggers W's passive for faster follow-up attacks. Saving E for the end loses that sequence.

quinn-combo-e-direction.basis: E reaches the target, then vaults back to land, so the direction you use it determines where you land. Use E from the far side of the enemy to knock them toward your team while backing away. Using E with your back to a wall can let you land across the terrain.
quinn-combo-e-direction.text: E reaches the target, then sends Quinn backward to land, so your approach determines where she ends up. Use it from the far side of an enemy to knock them toward your team while retreating to safety; with your back to a wall, you can also land on the other side of the terrain.

quinn-combo-harrier.basis: After a marked auto, land one or two more autos with W's passive, then use E to knock the target back and retreat. The faster you consume a Harrier mark, the sooner the next one appears. Take short trades in sync with Harrier's mark cycle.
quinn-combo-harrier.text: When a Harrier mark appears, hit the target with an auto, use the attack and movement speed from W's passive to land one or two more, then knock them back with E and retreat. Consuming the mark sooner brings the next one sooner, so keep trades short and repeat them in time with the mark cycle.

quinn-laning.basis: When a melee opponent steps up for a last hit, land a marked auto and retreat immediately. If the opponent closes in to retaliate, use E to knock them back and escape. Repeat short trades with marked autos to chip away at the opponent's health and build a lane advantage.
quinn-laning.text: Quinn has the range advantage over melee opponents in top lane. When one steps up for a last hit, land a marked auto and retreat immediately, repeating these short trades to chip away at their health. If they close in to retaliate, knock them back with E and escape. Marked poke alone can build a lane advantage without committing to a large trade.

quinn-laning-wave.basis: Push the wave into the enemy turret, then use R to move to another lane or the enemy jungle and create a numbers advantage. Even if you lose ground in top lane while roaming, push it back out from the side lane. To make use of Quinn's strengths, avoid holding the lane near your turret and playing defensively.
quinn-laning-wave.text: Quinn gets value after pushing her lane: shove the wave into the enemy turret, then use R to reach another lane or the enemy jungle and create a numbers advantage. If you lose ground in top lane while roaming, push it back out from the side. Holding the wave near your turret and playing defensively gives up Quinn's strengths.

quinn-phase.basis: Quinn has a strong early lane phase, pressuring melee opponents with marked autos from level 1 or 2. At level 6, Quinn gains R's mobility and can move across the map. Quinn is strongest in the mid game after her first core item. Quinn lacks sustained damage in late-game front-to-back teamfights, greatly reducing her role. End the game in the mid game or maintain your impact through side-lane pressure.
quinn-phase.text: Quinn's lane phase is strong as early as levels 1–2, when marked autos can pressure melee opponents. At level 6, R gives her mobility rather than damage and opens up the whole map; she peaks in the mid game after her first core item. Her low health and lack of sustained damage sharply limit her role in late-game front-to-back teamfights, so aim to end the game in the mid game or keep up side-lane pressure.

quinn-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent sustains through your poke with healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Quinn's short trades lose their poke value if the opponent heals the damage.
quinn-situational-antiheal.text: If your opponent sustains through your poke with healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Quinn relies on short trades, and that poke loses its value if the opponent heals back the damage.

quinn-skill-e.basis: E follows its target even if they Flash or use a mobility ability deeper into enemy territory. Before engaging with E, check whether the opponent's mobility ability is down. Before engaging with E, check whether your team can follow up. Quinn is easily killed when caught by crowd control.
quinn-skill-e.text: E follows its target even if they Flash or use a mobility ability to retreat deeper into enemy territory, which can leave Quinn landing in the middle of the enemy team. Before engaging, check whether the opponent's mobility ability is down and your team can follow up. Quinn has very low health and can die to a single crowd control effect.

quinn-skill-passive.basis: Harrier periodically marks nearby enemies. Consuming a Harrier mark on a minion also restarts the mark cycle. If the opponent is in trading range, save the mark for the champion instead of consuming it on a minion. Quinn's trades depend heavily on whether a Harrier mark is available.
quinn-skill-passive.text: Harrier periodically marks nearby enemies, and consuming a mark on a minion restarts the mark cycle too. If your opponent is within trading range, save the mark for them instead of using it on a minion; whether a mark is available can decide the trade.

quinn-skill-q.basis: If Q first hits a non-champion, only that target is disabled; champions receive neither the mark nor reduced vision. Aim Q straight at the opponent when they step outside the minion line. Q deals greatly increased damage to jungle monsters. Use Q to clear camps or contest objective steals.
quinn-skill-q.text: If Q first hits a non-champion, only that target is disabled; champions receive neither the mark nor reduced vision. In lane, wait for your opponent to step clear of the minion line before aiming at them. Q deals greatly increased damage to jungle monsters, making it useful for clearing camps or contesting objective steals.

quinn-skill-r.basis: R is a travel tool that activates after its channel completes. R's movement speed bonus ends when Quinn takes damage from anything other than minions. When traveling with R, take a route outside enemy vision. Push the lane, then use R to move to another side lane. Right after a teamfight ends, use R to push the lane on the opposite side.
quinn-skill-r.text: R is a travel tool, not a damage ability. It activates only after the channel completes, and damage from anything other than minions ends its movement speed bonus, so take routes outside enemy vision. Push your lane before using R to reach another side lane, or use it to push the opposite lane right after a teamfight.

quinn-skill-w.basis: Attacking a target marked by Harrier increases both your attack speed and movement speed through W's passive. Save W's active for information on the jungler's position and to check around objectives and in bushes.
quinn-skill-w.text: W's passive is the core of the ability: attacking a Harrier-marked target grants both attack speed and movement speed, helping Quinn deal damage in a trade and get away. Save the active to locate the jungler or check vision around objectives and in bushes.

quinn-teamfight.basis: Avoid entering teamfights from the front. Come in from the side or behind and only finish off targets already under attack. Save E to knock back an enemy who closes in and escape.
quinn-teamfight.text: Avoid entering teamfights from the front. Come in from the side or behind to finish targets your team has already caught, and save E to knock back an enemy who closes in and escape. Landing in the middle of the enemy team will get Quinn killed.

quinn-teamfight-split.basis: Consider pushing the opposite side lane instead of taking a front-to-back teamfight. If a teamfight looks likely, R's mobility lets you delay the decision to join. If your team can hold out, keep pushing the side lane. If your team is likely to collapse, join them early.
quinn-teamfight-split.text: Pushing the opposite side lane is always an option instead of taking a front-to-back teamfight. If a fight looks likely, R lets you delay the decision to join: keep pushing if your team can hold out, but join early if they are likely to collapse.

rakan-combo-e-w-e.basis: To go in and out, use E to reach an ally, knock the enemy up with W, then recast E to return. E can only be recast for a short time after its first use. Recasting E costs nothing. Check that you can recast E before using W.
rakan-combo-e-w-e.text: For an in-and-out combo, use E Battle Dance to reach an ally and move forward, knock the enemy up with W Grand Entrance, then recast E to return to your ally. The recast costs nothing but is available only for a short time after the first cast, so check that it is still available before using W.

rakan-combo-engage.basis: Start a basic engage with W to knock them up, then follow with Q and an auto attack. W moves in two stages: a dash, then a leap to land. During W's cast, the enemy has time to move away from the landing spot. Use W from a brush or out of vision, keeping the travel distance short.
rakan-combo-engage.text: Open with W Grand Entrance to knock the enemy up, then use Q Gleaming Quill and an auto attack. W has two stages—a dash followed by a leap to its landing spot—so the enemy has time to move aside during the cast. Start from brush or outside vision and keep the travel distance short to land it.

rakan-combo-q-heal.basis: If Q hits a champion or epic monster, Rakan and nearby allies heal shortly afterward. If Rakan touches an ally after Q hits, the heal triggers immediately. During a trade, land Q, then use E to reach an ally and trigger the heal sooner.
rakan-combo-q-heal.text: When Q Gleaming Quill hits a champion or epic monster, it heals Rakan and nearby allies after a short delay; touching an ally triggers the heal immediately. During trades, make a habit of landing Q and then using E Battle Dance to reach an ally, skipping the wait for the heal. W Grand Entrance can also bring you toward an ally right after Q.

rakan-combo-r-w.basis: After level 6, charm an enemy with R, then immediately knock them up with W. R gives another large movement speed boost the moment it touches the first champion. Rakan's dash speed scales with his movement speed. Using W when R's speed boost triggers on the first champion gives you the longest, fastest dash.
rakan-combo-r-w.text: After level 6, start an engage by touching an enemy with R The Quickness to charm them, then immediately knock them up with W Grand Entrance. R grants another large movement speed boost when it touches the first champion, and Rakan’s dash speed scales with his movement speed, so W travels farthest and fastest at that moment.

rakan-laning.basis: In lane, use Q to chip away at the enemy's health and reduce the passive shield's cooldown. Only start an all in when W is available and an allied E target is close. Do not force the wave to push. Catch the enemy marksman with W the moment they step in front of the minion line.
rakan-laning.text: In lane, use Q Gleaming Quill to chip away at the enemy’s health while reducing the cooldown of P Fey Feathers’ shield. Start an all-in only when W Grand Entrance is available and an allied E Battle Dance target is close. Do not force the wave to push; catch the enemy marksman with W when they step in front of the minion line.

rakan-laning-roam.basis: Rakan's two mobility abilities make his roams very effective. Roam mid right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret. When returning from a roam, use E on your allied mid laner to shorten your travel time.
rakan-laning-roam.text: With two mobility abilities, Rakan is one of the most effective roaming supports. Head mid right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret, then use E on your allied mid laner on the way back to cut travel time. For vision, use W and E to move deep and return safely to an ally.

rakan-phase.basis: Rakan has weak poke at level 1, so play quietly through it. From level 2, with both W and E, you can go all in and get back out. Getting R at level 6 gives Rakan his second power spike. Rakan is strongest in the mid game, when his mobility can shape the game. In the late game, getting caught once right after engaging can easily kill him.
rakan-phase.text: Rakan’s poke is weak at level 1, so play quietly until level 2, when having both W Grand Entrance and E Battle Dance lets you go all in and get back out. R The Quickness brings a second power spike at level 6. His mobility has the most impact in the mid game; late in the game, his low health and defenses mean getting caught once right after engaging can kill him.

rakan-situational-cc.basis: If Rakan is crowd controlled right after engaging, he cannot act despite having mobility abilities. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item to remove a root that hits right after you engage.
rakan-situational-cc.text: Crowd control right after an engage can leave Rakan unable to act despite his mobility abilities. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item to remove a root that catches you immediately after engaging.

rakan-skill-e.basis: E requires an allied champion to cast. E cannot target minions. When moving away from allies, Rakan becomes a melee champion with no mobility ability. Do not cross the jungle or areas without vision alone.
rakan-skill-e.text: E Battle Dance can only be cast on an allied champion, not a minion. Away from allies, Rakan is a melee champion without a mobility ability, so do not cross the jungle or areas without vision alone.

rakan-skill-passive.basis: Rakan's passive periodically grants a shield. Each auto attack or ability that hits an enemy champion reduces the passive's cooldown. Poke with Q before engaging to bring the passive shield back. Engaging with the shield up greatly improves your chances of surviving.
rakan-skill-passive.text: P Fey Feathers periodically grants Rakan a shield, and each auto attack or ability that hits an enemy champion reduces its cooldown. Poke with Q Gleaming Quill a few times before engaging so the shield is ready when you go in; having it up makes a substantial difference to your survival.

rakan-skill-q.basis: Q damages only the first enemy it hits. Q is used up if it hits a minion in front. Throw Q from an angle clear of the minion line. Q heals only when it hits a champion or epic monster. Hit an enemy champion with Q to get both poke and lane sustain.
rakan-skill-q.text: Q Gleaming Quill damages only the first enemy it hits, so a minion in front will absorb it. Throw Q from an angle clear of the minion line. Since its heal triggers only on a champion or epic monster, you must hit an enemy champion to get both poke and lane sustain.

rakan-skill-r.basis: Activating R gives a large movement speed boost. Enemies Rakan touches while rushing with R are charmed. To charm multiple enemies, move in from an angle where they are lined up. When escaping, use R's movement speed even if you cannot hit an enemy.
rakan-skill-r.text: Activating R The Quickness gives Rakan a large movement speed boost and charms enemies he touches while rushing; the path you take determines whom it hits. Approach from an angle that lines up several enemies to charm them all, or use the speed to escape even if you touch no one.

rakan-skill-w.basis: W is Rakan's only forced engage tool and effectively his only escape tool. If you use W to poke first, it is hard to respond to a gank or counterattack afterward. Decide whether to engage with W based on whether an ally is available for E.
rakan-skill-w.text: W Grand Entrance is Rakan’s only way to force an engage and effectively his only escape. Using it to poke leaves you without a way to respond to a gank or counterattack. You can use W to engage when an ally is nearby for E Battle Dance, so check for an E target before committing.

rakan-teamfight.basis: Before a teamfight, decide whether your role is to engage or protect. When you need to catch the enemy carries, charm multiple enemies with R, then knock them up with W. When you need to protect your carries, save W to knock up an enemy champion diving in. When protecting your carries, hold out with E's shield and Q's heal. If you split your role between engaging and protecting in a teamfight, it is hard to do both well.
rakan-teamfight.text: Before a teamfight, decide whether to engage or protect. If your team needs to catch the enemy carries, charm multiple enemies with R The Quickness and follow with W Grand Entrance to knock them up. If you need to protect your carries, save W to knock up a diving enemy, then hold out with E Battle Dance’s shield and Q Gleaming Quill’s heal. Trying to split your role between the two makes it hard to do either well.

rammus-combo-basic.basis: Collide with Q to knock back and slow the target, then taunt a priority enemy with E, activate W, and auto-attack. Do not activate W before engaging. Activate it right after the enemy starts hitting Rammus.
rammus-combo-basic.text: The basic engage is to roll in with Q (Powerball), collide to knock back and slow the target, then use E (Frenzying Taunt) on a priority enemy, activate W (Defensive Ball Curl), and auto-attack. Turn on W just after the enemy starts hitting Rammus so its duration is not wasted before the engage.

rammus-combo-qr.basis: Using R while rolling with Q knocks enemies at the center of the area airborne. If you use R after Q collides with an enemy and stops, it does not knock them airborne. Use R while Q is still rolling, just before reaching the enemy.
rammus-combo-qr.text: Use R (Soaring Slam) while Q (Powerball) is still rolling to knock enemies at the center of its area airborne; if Q has already collided and stopped, the knockup is lost. Cast R just before reaching the enemy, ideally after Q reaches maximum speed, since higher movement speed also expands R’s area.

rammus-combo-taunt-tower.basis: Taunting an enemy with E near an allied turret makes them auto-attack Rammus, causing the turret to attack them. Taunt enemies diving under your turret with E instead of knocking them back with Q.
rammus-combo-taunt-tower.text: Near an allied turret, E (Frenzying Taunt) makes the target auto-attack Rammus, causing the turret to attack them. It is his most reliable way to counter a dive, so taunt an enemy under your turret instead of knocking them back with Q (Powerball).

rammus-laning-jungle.basis: Statistically, Rammus ranks among the lowest overall in early CS and damage per minute. Clear camps quickly, then use Q's long engage range to spend time on ganks and objectives. Statistically, Rammus ranks among the highest in deaths.
rammus-laning-jungle.text: Rammus ranks near the bottom overall in early CS and damage per minute, so he cannot win by competing on farm. Clear camps quickly, then use Q Powerball’s long engage range to spend time on ganks and objectives. His death rate is also among the highest, so when there is no good opening, the default is to use Q to get out.

rammus-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Rammus clears camps slowly and deals almost no damage on his own. Ganks become viable once you have both Q and E. Once you learn R at level 6, you can force fights over objectives. As defensive items stack up, the passive also increases Rammus's damage, so he peaks in the mid to late game. Later in the game, destroying turrets becomes a separate source of pressure.
rammus-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Rammus clears camps slowly and deals almost no damage alone. Ganks become viable once he has both Q (Powerball) and E (Frenzying Taunt), and after learning R (Soaring Slam) at level 6, he can force fights over objectives. Defensive items also increase his damage through Spiked Shell, making the mid to late game his peak; later, turret destruction gives him another way to apply pressure.

rammus-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, do not build only armor. The passive converts magic resistance into attack damage, and W also increases magic resistance. If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buying Spirit Visage or Banshee's Veil early does not reduce your damage.
rammus-situational-mr.text: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, stacking only armor is a disadvantage. Spiked Shell also converts magic resistance into attack damage, and W (Defensive Ball Curl) raises magic resistance, so buying Spirit Visage or Banshee’s Veil earlier does not reduce Rammus’s damage.

rammus-skill-e-taunt.basis: E is a targeted taunt, so it cannot miss. Enemies affected by E walk toward Rammus and only auto-attack. E interrupts enemy ability casts and channels. Use E on one of the enemy team's main damage dealers. Using E just as an enemy tries to escape with a mobility ability makes that ability useless.
rammus-skill-e-taunt.text: E (Frenzying Taunt) is targeted, so it cannot miss: the affected enemy walks toward Rammus and can only auto-attack. It interrupts casts and channels, preventing that enemy from damaging your team for the duration. Save it for one of the opposing team’s main damage dealers; casting it just as they try to escape with a mobility ability also renders that ability useless.

rammus-skill-passive.basis: Rammus's passive converts armor and magic resistance into attack damage. Increasing your defensive stats with defensive items also increases auto-attack damage and turret destruction speed. The armor and magic resistance gained from W also count toward the passive.
rammus-skill-passive.text: Rammus’s passive, Spiked Shell, converts armor and magic resistance into attack damage, so building defensive stats also raises his auto-attack damage and turret destruction speed without forcing in offensive items. The stats gained while W (Defensive Ball Curl) is active count too.

rammus-skill-q.basis: Q gains movement speed the longer it rolls. When ganking, start Q out of vision so you arrive at maximum speed. Q stops when it hits an enemy, minion, or neutral monster, so roll along a path that avoids them. Recast Q to end it early if you want to change direction. When escaping with Q, choose a direction clear of enemies and minions so you do not stop midway.
rammus-skill-q.text: Q (Powerball) gains movement speed the longer it rolls, so start it out of vision before a gank to arrive at maximum speed; starting when the enemy comes into view leaves you rolling in slowly. Colliding with an enemy, minion, or neutral monster stops Q, so choose a clear path, and recast it early if you need to change direction. When escaping, likewise head away from enemies and minions so the roll does not stop midway.

rammus-skill-r-tower.basis: R deals double damage to turrets. Later in the game, combine auto-attacks boosted by W with R to destroy turrets quickly, even alone. If a teamfight stalls, disengage and attack structures.
rammus-skill-r-tower.text: R (Soaring Slam) deals double damage to turrets. Combined with auto-attacks boosted by the stats from W (Defensive Ball Curl), it lets Rammus destroy turrets quickly on his own later in the game. If a teamfight stalls, disengage and attack structures.

rammus-skill-r-zone.basis: After landing, R causes repeated aftershocks in the same spot, stacking slows. Use R in narrow paths enemies must cross or in objective pits. Do not use R where an enemy has already escaped from.
rammus-skill-r-zone.text: After Rammus lands, R produces repeated aftershocks in the same spot, stacking slows. It works as area denial rather than a burst of damage: place it in a narrow path enemies must cross or inside an objective pit, since using it where they have already escaped has no value.

rammus-skill-w.basis: Activating W greatly increases armor and magic resistance for a set duration. Enemies who hit Rammus while W is active take reflected damage. Activate W after the enemy actually starts hitting Rammus. When you no longer need W, recast it to end it early and start its cooldown sooner.
rammus-skill-w.text: W (Defensive Ball Curl) greatly increases armor and magic resistance for a fixed duration and reflects damage to enemies who hit Rammus. Activate it after they actually start attacking rather than waiting with it on, then recast to end it early and start its cooldown sooner when it is no longer needed.

rammus-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, taunt a main damage dealer in the enemy backline with E. Engage with Q, taunt with E, and use R to lock down that area. If you cannot reach a target to taunt, stand in front of your carry and counter the enemy engage with Q's knockback and E's taunt.
rammus-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Rammus aims to neutralize a main damage dealer in the enemy backline with E (Frenzying Taunt). Engage with Q (Powerball), taunt the target, and use R (Soaring Slam) to lock down that area. If no taunt target is reachable, stand in front of your carry instead and counter the enemy engage with Q’s knockback and E’s taunt.

rammus-teamfight-vs-marksman.basis: Rammus's W reflected damage and E taunt pressure ranged damage dealers who rely on auto-attacks. Against a ranged damage dealer who relies on auto-attacks, keep positioning within their vision to disrupt their attacks.
rammus-teamfight-vs-marksman.text: Against a ranged damage dealer who relies on auto-attacks, Rammus’s presence alone creates pressure: W (Defensive Ball Curl)’s reflected damage and E (Frenzying Taunt) mean they can neither safely attack him nor ignore him. Stay in their vision to keep them from auto-attacking, even without committing to an engage.

reksai-combo-gank.basis: Approach while burrowed, knock the enemy up with W, build Fury with Q-empowered basic attacks, then finish with E. Press Q right after the W knockup to land all three empowered basic attacks on the enemy. Use E after building Fury. If the enemy is already caught, walk up while unburrowed and start with a basic attack.
reksai-combo-gank.text: For a gank, approach while burrowed, emerge beneath the enemy with W to knock them up, then press Q immediately to land all three empowered basic attacks. Build Fury with attacks before finishing with E. If the target is already caught, walk up while unburrowed and start attacking instead; this deals more damage.

reksai-phase.basis: Rek'Sai can make an impact through ganks from level 3, when she has W, until level 6, when she learns R. Rek'Sai's power peaks in the mid game when she gets her core items. Late in the game, Rek'Sai's relative damage falls, making it hard to kill backline enemies alone. Gain an advantage through ganks and objectives in the early and mid game to end the game sooner. Late in the game, engage with R and knock up an enemy.
reksai-phase.text: Rek'Sai can influence the game through ganks from level 3, when she has W's knockup, through level 6, when she gains R; her peak comes in the mid game with her core items. Her relative damage falls later, and she is not especially durable, making it difficult to eliminate the backline alone. Build a lead through ganks and objectives early and in the mid game to end the game sooner, then shift to engaging with R and knocking up an enemy in late-game fights.

reksai-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rek'Sai stays close and keeps basic attacking, so she can maintain Grievous Wounds throughout a fight.
reksai-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rek'Sai stays close and keeps basic attacking, allowing her to maintain Grievous Wounds throughout a fight.

reksai-situational-mercurial.basis: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down Rek'Sai when she goes in, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item. Rek'Sai can be killed easily if she is crowd controlled right after going in with R.
reksai-situational-mercurial.text: If the enemy has plenty of crowd control that can lock Rek'Sai down on entry, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item. Getting caught immediately after going in with R can get her killed, so breaking that one lockdown is more valuable than adding more attack damage.

reksai-skill-q.basis: Unburrowed Q empowers the next three basic attacks to hit nearby enemies too. Each basic attack refreshes the duration of unburrowed Q. After using unburrowed Q, keep your basic attacks going without interruption. Burrowed Q fires soil at range and reveals the location of enemies it hits. Dealing damage with burrowed Q can meet R's targeting requirement.
reksai-skill-q.text: Unburrowed Q (Queen's Wrath) empowers Rek'Sai's next three basic attacks to hit nearby enemies, and each attack refreshes its duration. Keep attacking without interruption to make the most of its area damage when clearing jungle camps or fighting grouped enemies. Burrowed Q (Prey Seeker) instead fires soil from range and reveals enemies it hits. It is Rek'Sai's only ranged option, and damaging an enemy with it meets R's targeting requirement, letting her begin a catch from beyond melee range.

rell-combo-engage.basis: Use E to approach with an ally, knock enemies up with W, stun them with Q, then pull them together with R. E's explosion triggers on whichever hits first: your next basic attack or Q. Landing Q right after W's knockup applies crowd control and E's explosion together.
rell-combo-engage.text: For a standard engage, activate E Full Tilt to speed up alongside an ally and close the gap, knock enemies up with W Ferromancy: Crash Down, stun them with Q Shattering Strike, then pull them together with R Magnet Storm. E’s explosion triggers on whichever lands first, your next basic attack or Q, so using Q immediately after W delivers the stun and explosion together.

rell-combo-flash.basis: Rell's W, Ferromancy: Crash Down, immediately hits the area around her. Right after closing the gap with Flash, knock them up with W and stun them with Q.
rell-combo-flash.text: W Ferromancy: Crash Down immediately hits the area around Rell, making it effective with Flash: close the gap with Flash, press W to knock enemies up, then follow with Q Shattering Strike to stun them.

rell-combo-remount.basis: You can use two knockups by switching between W's two forms. Using W to remount after Crash Down grants movement speed. Your next basic attack after remounting knocks an enemy up. The shield gained from Crash Down disappears when you remount. Remount when your shield is already depleted or you need to catch a fleeing enemy.
rell-combo-remount.text: W lets Rell knock enemies up in both forms: after landing with Ferromancy: Crash Down, press W again to remount, gain movement speed, and knock up an enemy with your next basic attack. Remount only after the shield from Crash Down is depleted or when you need to catch a fleeing enemy, since the shield disappears as soon as you remount.

rell-laning.basis: Rell struggles to reach enemies on foot, so she relies on vision and brush in lane. Keep the wave pulled toward your allied turret. Look for the moment an enemy enters W's Crash Down range from the brush. Basic attack range and attack speed increase in armored form. Once you close the gap, keep trading with basic attacks.
rell-laning.text: Rell struggles to reach enemies on foot, so laning depends on vision and brush. Pull the wave toward your turret and engage from brush only when an enemy enters W Ferromancy: Crash Down range. Once you close the gap, stay in armored form and keep trading with basic attacks, which gain range and attack speed.

rell-laning-roam.basis: Activate E when setting out to roam. Activate E and move with your marksman toward the river or mid; both of you move faster. Roam right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret. Account for your slow movement speed when timing your return so you do not lose the bot turret.
rell-laning-roam.text: Activate E Full Tilt when setting out to roam: moving toward the river or mid with your marksman speeds up both of you. Roam right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret, and account for Rell’s slow movement speed when timing your return so you do not lose the bot turret.

rell-phase.basis: Starting with W at level 1 and gaining Q at level 2 is Rell's first strong window. Following W's knockup with Q's stun can force the enemy marksman to use an escape tool. Getting R at level 6 gives Rell a second power spike. Rell peaks in the mid game as she builds defensive items. Late in the game, her short range and lack of an escape after engaging make solo engages easy to punish.
rell-phase.text: Rell starts with W’s knockup at level 1, and gaining Q at level 2 creates her first strong window: chaining the knockup into a stun can force the enemy marksman to use an escape tool. R at level 6 brings a second power spike, and she peaks in the mid game as she builds defensive items. Late in the game, her short range and lack of an escape after engaging mean a solo engage can get her killed.

rell-situational-armor.basis: If the enemy's physical damage is strong, buy Plated Steelcaps and build armor first. Against a team centered on basic attacks, prioritize Frozen Heart over Thornmail to protect your allied damage dealer too.
rell-situational-armor.text: If the enemy’s physical damage is strong, buy Plated Steelcaps and build armor first. Against a team that deals damage through basic attacks, prioritize Frozen Heart over Thornmail to protect your allied damage dealer too.

rell-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, build magic resistance first. Build Spirit Visage earlier against a team that deals mostly magic damage. If a single burst of damage is the problem rather than sustained damage, use Banshee's Veil to block one engage ability.
rell-situational-mr.text: Rell’s level 1 magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions. If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, build magic resistance first and move Spirit Visage earlier in your build; if a single burst is the problem rather than sustained damage, use Banshee’s Veil to block one engage ability.

rell-skill-e.basis: E increases movement speed for Rell and one ally. E's movement speed increase doubles when moving toward an enemy or each other. Activate E just before engaging to close the gap. When retreating after a fight, E's double-speed condition no longer applies, halving its effectiveness. Rell's base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions. Do not look for an engage while E is unavailable.
rell-skill-e.text: E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and one ally, with the increase doubling when they move toward an enemy or each other. Activate it just before engaging to close the gap; retreating after a fight no longer meets that condition and halves its effectiveness. Because Rell’s base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions, do not look for an engage while E is unavailable.

rell-skill-passive.basis: Each basic attack and ability hit steals the target's armor and magic resistance, stacking the passive. After using crowd control, keep weaving in basic attacks in armored form to maintain passive stacks. Maintaining passive stacks also increases your allied damage dealer's damage.
rell-skill-passive.text: P Break the Mold steals and stacks an enemy’s armor and magic resistance whenever Rell hits them with a basic attack or ability. After using her crowd control, keep weaving in basic attacks in armored form to maintain the stacks and increase your allied damage dealer’s damage.

rell-skill-q.basis: Q thrusts in a straight line and briefly stuns enemies. Q destroys all shields on targets it hits. If the enemy support grants a shield, use Q as soon as it appears. Q cannot destroy monster shields.
rell-skill-q.text: Q Shattering Strike thrusts in a straight line, briefly stuns enemies, and destroys every shield on targets it hits. Against a support who grants shields, save Q until a shield appears; it cannot destroy monster shields.

rell-skill-r.basis: R pulls nearby enemies toward Rell, then keeps pulling them briefly. R has short range, so walking in to use it alone leaves Rell exposed. Use R immediately after W's knockup to keep enemies grouped together. Use R after an ally has already engaged.
rell-skill-r.text: R Magnet Storm pulls nearby enemies toward Rell and continues pulling briefly. Its range is short, so walking in to cast it alone leaves her exposed; use it immediately after W’s knockup or after an ally has already engaged to keep enemies from scattering.

rell-skill-w.basis: W switches between mounted and dismounted forms. While mounted, the movement speed makes it easier to approach. Dismounting into armored form increases armor, magic resistance, attack speed, and basic attack range. Movement speed drops sharply in armored form. Stay in armored form to withstand a fight that has already started. Remount when moving to find the next fight.
rell-skill-w.text: W switches between mounted and armored forms. While mounted, Rell gains movement speed to approach enemies; dismounting increases her armor, magic resistance, attack speed, and basic attack range but slows her sharply. Use armored form to withstand a fight already underway, then remount before moving to find the next one.

rell-teamfight.basis: Group enemies together so your allies' area abilities hit them. Engage when your allies are ready to go in with you. Engage when at least two enemies are within R range. If the enemy team is spread out, stay in armored form in front of your allied damage dealer and absorb the dive.
rell-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Rell’s job is to group enemies for her allies’ area abilities. Engage only when your allies are ready to follow and at least two enemies will be within R Magnet Storm range when you cast it. If the enemy team is spread out, stay in armored form in front of your allied damage dealer and absorb the dive.

renata-combo-order.basis: Slow with E, root with Q, then recast Q to throw the target where you want. E's slow helps you land Q's slow projectile. To save an ally, use W first and E's shield afterward. You can't use W after an ally has already died.
renata-combo-order.text: To start a fight, slow the target with E (Loyalty Program), root them with Q (Handshake), then recast Q to throw them where you want; E’s slow helps the slow Q projectile land. To save an ally, use W (Bailout) before E’s shield, since W cannot be used after they die.

renata-combo-q.basis: Q roots the first enemy it hits. Enemies hit by a champion thrown with Q are stunned. When enemies are grouped, throw the champion caught by Q into them to stun multiple enemies. When an ally needs to close the gap, pull the enemy caught by Q toward that ally.
renata-combo-q.text: Q (Handshake) roots the first enemy it hits, then can be recast to throw them in a chosen direction. Enemies struck by a thrown champion are stunned, making Q a way to start a fight with multiple stuns: throw a target into grouped enemies to stun several, or toward your allies when they need to close the gap.

renata-combo-q-direction.basis: If you don't recast Q, only the root remains. Throw a fleeing enemy toward your allies with Q. Use Q to push an enemy who jumps on an ally away from them. When Q roots an enemy, move your cursor toward the throw direction, then recast Q.
renata-combo-q-direction.text: Without a recast, Q (Handshake) only roots its target. Throw a fleeing enemy toward your allies to close the distance, or throw one who has jumped onto an ally in any direction that moves them away. The cursor determines the throw direction, so move it as soon as the root lands, then recast.

renata-laning.basis: Don't stand in front of the enemy in lane. Support your ally's trades with E's shield. In lane, just apply the auto-attack mark briefly. Use Q when the enemy support steps forward or a gap opens between minions.
renata-laning.text: Renata Glasc’s level-one health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, so stay back. In lane, support your ally’s trades with E (Loyalty Program)’s shield and briefly apply your basic attack mark. Save Q (Handshake) for when the enemy support steps forward or a gap opens between minions.

renata-laning-trade.basis: Hit the enemy with E as they step forward to last-hit. E damages and slows the enemy while shielding your allied marksman. Don't step forward in lane while E is on cooldown.
renata-laning-trade.text: Hit the enemy with E (Loyalty Program) as they step forward to last-hit. It damages and slows them while shielding your allied marksman, letting one cast start and finish the trade. Stay back while E is on cooldown.

renata-phase.basis: Renata Glasc is weak at level 1, when she has only one ability. Kill opportunities open up once you learn Q. At level 6, Renata Glasc becomes much stronger because R lets her counter enemy engage compositions. Late in the game, Renata Glasc deals almost no damage herself. Her ability to save allies and disrupt the enemy formation remains useful until the end of the game.
renata-phase.text: Renata Glasc is weak at level one with only one ability, but learning Q (Handshake) creates kill opportunities. Her strength rises sharply at level six, when R (Hostile Takeover) can shut down an enemy engage composition. She deals almost no damage herself late in the game, yet saving allies and disrupting the enemy formation remain useful until the end.

renata-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing keeps undoing your allies' damage, buy Blighting Jewel first to apply healing reduction. The basic attack mark and E let you deal steady damage, making healing reduction easy to maintain.
renata-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing keeps undoing your allies’ damage, buy Blighting Jewel first to apply healing reduction. Renata Glasc can keep it active with steady damage from her basic attack mark and E (Loyalty Program).

renata-skill-e.basis: E's missiles damage and slow enemies while shielding allies. If an ally and an enemy are in the same line, fire E at the enemy beyond your allied damage dealer. Use E, with its short cooldown, as your main tool for trading damage in lane. Use E's slow to start a fight.
renata-skill-e.text: E (Loyalty Program) fires missiles that damage and slow enemies while shielding allies. When an ally and enemy line up, fire through your allied damage dealer toward the enemy to affect both at once. Its short cooldown makes E your main lane trading tool, and its slow can also start a fight.

renata-skill-passive.basis: Your basic attack mark can only be on one target at a time. When an ally hits a marked target, the mark is consumed and deals bonus damage. The basic attack mark's damage based on maximum health is effective against the enemy frontline too. In lane, mark the enemy marksman with a basic attack to help your ally trade damage.
renata-skill-passive.text: Your basic attack mark can be on only one target at a time; when an ally hits that target, the mark is consumed and deals bonus damage. Because the damage scales with maximum health, it works against the enemy frontline too. In lane, a single basic attack on the enemy marksman leaves a mark that increases your allied marksman’s trade damage.

renata-skill-w-nature.basis: An ally with W briefly revives at full health when they die. An ally revived by W gradually loses health. An ally revived by W survives if they get a takedown during that time. Use W on an ally dealing damage now, rather than one certain to die.
renata-skill-w-nature.text: W (Bailout) strengthens an ally and delays their death. If they die, they briefly revive at full health before gradually losing it, and a takedown during that time lets them survive. W is a bet on whether that ally can secure a takedown now, so use it on someone currently dealing damage rather than someone certain to die.

renekton-combo-allin.basis: When you have kill pressure, build Fury, then use E → empowered W → Q → basic attack → E. You can land both Q and a basic attack during empowered W's stun. Empowered abilities do not generate Fury. After level 6, use R just before engaging. R grants bonus maximum health for its duration and removes it when it ends. R continuously generates Fury for its duration. Use the Fury gained from R to attempt a second combo or a dive.
renekton-combo-allin.text: For a kill, build Fury, then use E → empowered W → Q → basic attack → E. Empowered W stuns long enough to land both Q and the attack; empowered abilities generate no Fury, so pack your damage into that stun. From level 6 onward, activate R just before engaging. It grants bonus maximum health and steadily generates Fury, giving you resources for a second combo or a dive even if you started with none. Its bonus health disappears when R ends, so make use of its duration.

renekton-combo-basic.basis: Use the basic combo in this order: E in → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q → E out. W replaces your next basic attack, so use it between basic attacks. E can only be cast again if the first dash hits a unit. If you expect to lose the trade, take a short trade with E → W → basic attack → Q → E.
renekton-combo-basic.text: In lane, engage with E → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q → E to disengage. W replaces your next basic attack, so weaving it between attacks costs nothing; the first E dash must hit a unit to unlock the second. This engage, trade, disengage sequence is Renekton’s basic poke pattern. If you expect to lose a longer trade, shorten it to E → W → basic attack → Q → E.

renekton-laning.basis: In lane, keep your Fury near half full. Manage Fury with last hits and Q farming without pushing the lane far enough to expose yourself to a gank. Engage right after your opponent uses a poke ability. After using W and E, avoid aggressive positioning until both abilities are off cooldown.
renekton-laning.text: In lane, keep your Fury near half full through last hits and Q farming, but avoid hitting minions so often that you push the wave and expose yourself to a gank. Engage just after your opponent uses a poke ability. Once you have used W and E, avoid aggressive positioning until both are off cooldown.

renekton-phase.basis: Renekton poses little threat at levels 1–2, when he lacks abilities. Renekton poses a strong threat at level 3, when he has his basic abilities, and level 6, when he gains R. Renekton is strong in lane and objective fights through the mid game, when core items come in. Renekton's lack of sustained damage and long cooldowns leave him weak in extended fights after his combo. Renekton's value drops sharply in the late game. Turn an early lead into objectives and lane pressure.
renekton-phase.text: Renekton poses little threat at levels 1–2 while his abilities are incomplete, but spikes at level 3 with Q, W, and E and again at level 6 with R. He can dominate lane and objective fights through the mid game as core items arrive. With no sustained damage abilities and generally long cooldowns, though, he struggles if a fight continues after his combo. His value drops sharply late, so turn an early lead into objectives and lane pressure.

renekton-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent's healing turns trades in their favor, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Renekton loses his advantage against opponents who heal back the damage from his short combo.
renekton-situational-antiheal.text: If an opponent’s healing turns trades in their favor, fit Executioner’s Calling between core items. Renekton relies on short combos, and he loses that advantage when the opponent heals back a combo’s damage.

renekton-situational-armor.basis: If the opponent's physical damage is strong, buy Plated Steelcaps early. If you keep losing trades, buy Chain Vest first to survive lane. If the enemy has multiple physical damage dealers, buy Randuin's Omen for armor and health.
renekton-situational-armor.text: If your opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps early. If you keep losing trades, get Chain Vest first to survive lane; against multiple enemy physical damage dealers, follow up with Randuin’s Omen for armor and health.

renekton-skill-e.basis: If the first E dash misses all units, you cannot use the second dash. Before engaging, choose a minion or opponent to hit with the first E so you have a way out. Empowered E's armor reduction applies only to the second cast. Give empowered E low priority unless an allied physical damage dealer will keep attacking the same target.
renekton-skill-e.text: The first E, Slice and Dice, must hit a unit to unlock the second dash. Before engaging, choose a minion or opponent to hit so you retain a way out. Its empowered armor reduction applies only to the second cast, so spending Fury on E is a low priority unless an allied physical damage dealer will keep attacking the same target.

renekton-skill-fury.basis: Gain Fury by hitting enemies with basic attacks and Q, W, or E. Fury steadily decreases out of combat. Just before trading, build Fury with minion last hits and basic attacks. If you lack Fury, engage with E, hit both your opponent and minions with Q, then use empowered W. For a simple trade or sustain, choose empowered Q for its increased healing. When you have kill pressure, choose empowered W for its longer stun. Renekton uses ability haste efficiently because it speeds up both Fury generation and spending.
renekton-skill-fury.text: Basic attacks build Fury in fixed amounts, and Q, W, and E also generate it when they hit enemies; out of combat, it steadily drains. Build it with minion last hits and basic attacks just before trading. If you lack enough Fury, engage with E, hit both your opponent and minions with Q, then follow with empowered W. Choose empowered Q for its increased healing in a simple trade or when you need sustain, and empowered W for its longer stun when you have kill pressure. Ability haste is especially valuable to Renekton because it speeds up both Fury generation and spending.

renekton-skill-q.basis: Q heals more as it hits more targets. Empowered Q increases both damage and healing. Use Q where there are targets to hit so it can heal you.
renekton-skill-q.text: Q Cull the Meek hits everyone nearby, healing Renekton for each target struck; empowered Q increases both its damage and healing. Using it where a minion wave overlaps an enemy champion can restore a lot of health, letting you bait the opponent in by appearing low on health and turn the fight with a single empowered Q. With nothing to hit, it provides no sustain, so use it only when targets are in range.

renekton-skill-w.basis: W cancels the basic attack animation and activates immediately. W has slightly more range than a basic attack. Against an opponent walking away, use W immediately after a basic attack. Use W immediately after Flash to attempt a surprise stun. Empowered W destroys the target's shield before its third hit.
renekton-skill-w.text: W, Ruthless Predator, replaces Renekton’s next basic attack, cancels its animation, activates immediately, and reaches slightly farther. Against an opponent walking away, use W after a basic attack to catch them; Flash → W can also deliver a surprise stun. Empowered W breaks the target’s shield before its third hit, making it especially useful against opponents who rely on shields.

renekton-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, land empowered W on a key enemy damage dealer, then disengage with E. Before entering a teamfight, secure a target for E so you can disengage. Decide when to use R before entering a teamfight. If the enemy frontline is sturdy, attack the backline from the side.
renekton-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Renekton’s job is to land empowered W on a key enemy damage dealer and disengage with E, rather than stand at the front. His threat fades after his combo because he lacks sustained damage, so plan both a target for the first E dash and your R timing before going in. If the enemy frontline is sturdy, approach from the side and target the backline instead of forcing your way through.

rengar-combo-choose.basis: Use empowered E to root enemies who can escape. If an enemy you have already reached can retaliate with an immobilizing ability, remove it with empowered W. If the enemy has no way to escape or retaliate, maximize damage with empowered Q. Choose your empowered ability before engaging.
rengar-combo-choose.text: Choose where to spend Ferocity based on how the enemy can survive: use empowered E to root someone who can escape, empowered W to remove an immobilizing counterattack once you have reached them, or empowered Q to maximize damage if they can neither escape nor retaliate. Make that choice before engaging so you can act immediately after the leap.

rengar-laning-clear.basis: Focus on W when clearing the jungle. Rengar's resource is not mana, so mana costs do not limit him. Use W to maintain health while clearing camps in succession and ganking often.
rengar-laning-clear.text: Focus on W when clearing the jungle: it deals bonus damage to monsters and restores much of the damage Rengar has taken, keeping him healthy. Because his resource is not mana, ability costs do not limit him, allowing him to clear camps in succession and gank often.

rengar-phase.basis: Rengar is strongest in the mid game, when he has R and his first core item. In the mid game, pick off enemies in the backline. In the late game, enemy vision and defensive items make it harder to engage. Use the lead built in the mid game to finish the game.
rengar-phase.text: Before level 6, Rengar’s ganks depend on brush and can be inconsistent; statistically, his deaths by 14 minutes are also relatively high among junglers. He is strongest in the mid game, once he has R and his first core item, and should use that window to pick off backline enemies. As enemy vision and defensive items make engages much harder late in the game, use the lead built in mid game to finish it.

rengar-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rengar deals damage in a short burst, so healing just before a kill can easily turn the outcome.
rengar-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rengar deals damage in a short burst, so a single heal just before a kill is secured can easily turn the outcome.

rengar-skill-e.basis: E briefly reveals the location of the first enemy it hits. If you lose sight of an enemy during a chase, throw E along their expected path to locate them. Use E to find enemies hiding in brush. Maximum-Ferocity E roots instead of slowing. Spend Ferocity on E when you need to root an enemy without a mobility ability.
rengar-skill-e.text: E Bola Strike briefly reveals the location of the first enemy it hits, making it both a damage ability and a scouting tool. If you lose sight of someone during a chase, throw it along their expected path to locate them; it can also find enemies hiding in brush. At maximum Ferocity, E roots instead of slowing, so spend Ferocity on it when you need to hold an enemy without a mobility ability in place. E has no cast time during a leap, allowing you to throw it in midair.

rengar-skill-q.basis: Q empowers the next basic attack and increases attack speed. Use Q right after a basic attack to fill the gap between attacks. At maximum Ferocity, Q deals much more damage and grants much more attack speed. Use maximum-Ferocity Q when you can reliably stay on the target.
rengar-skill-q.text: Q Savagery empowers your next basic attack and increases attack speed; it is not a separate damage ability. Press Q right after a basic attack to fill the gap between attacks, since pressing it early wastes the time before the empowered attack lands. At maximum Ferocity, Q grants much more damage and attack speed, so use it only when you can reliably stay on the target.

rengar-skill-r-scout.basis: There is a brief delay after activating R before you become camouflaged. During R's delay, you gain vision around the nearest enemy champion. Use the vision from R to locate your target before approaching. While camouflaged by R, you become visible if you enter an enemy's detection range. When approaching with R, avoid coming from the front. Take a wide route around the side or back.
rengar-skill-r-scout.text: R Thrill of the Hunt does not camouflage you immediately: there is a brief delay during which you gain vision around the nearest enemy champion. Use that vision to locate your target before approaching. You become visible if you enter an enemy's detection range while camouflaged, so take a wide route around the side or back instead of approaching from the front.

rengar-skill-w.basis: W heals some of the damage taken recently. Use W right after taking heavy damage to heal more. Maximum-Ferocity W removes crowd control. Save Ferocity for W if the enemy still has an immobilizing ability. W deals bonus damage to jungle monsters and heals a large portion of the damage taken.
rengar-skill-w.text: W Battle Roar restores some of the damage taken in the recent past, so use it immediately after a heavy hit to heal more. At maximum Ferocity, W removes crowd control; save Ferocity for it if the enemy still has an immobilizing ability. It also deals bonus damage to jungle monsters and restores a large portion of damage taken, making it central to managing your health while clearing.

rengar-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, kill enemies in the backline. Use R's vision to find your target, then circle around to engage from the side or behind. Engage after the enemy uses their immobilizing abilities on your frontline. Before engaging, plan an escape route for after your burst damage.
rengar-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Rengar’s job is to kill backline enemies. Use R’s vision to locate a target, then circle around to engage from the side or behind once the enemy has used its immobilizing abilities on your frontline. Plan an escape route before going in: after dealing burst damage, use W’s healing and empowered W’s crowd control removal to get out.

riven-combo-basic.basis: Use this basic trade combo: Q1 → basic attack → Q2 → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q3. Weave a basic attack between each Q to secure damage. Using Q casts back to back leaves no time for basic attacks and reduces your damage.
riven-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, use Q1 → basic attack → Q2 → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q3. The key is weaving in basic attacks, not memorizing the order: casting Q repeatedly leaves no time for them and cuts your damage in half.

riven-combo-burst.basis: Use this kill combo: E → Q1 → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q2 → basic attack → Q3 → activate R → recast R. Activate R while the target is airborne from Q3. Wind Slash deals more damage the more health the target has lost. Use Wind Slash at the end of the combo.
riven-combo-burst.text: For a kill, close in with E, then use Q1 → basic attack → W stun → basic attack → Q2 → basic attack → Q3 knockup. Activate R while the target is airborne and finish with Wind Slash; it deals more damage the more health the target has lost, so use it at the end of the combo.

riven-combo-cancel.basis: Use Q before the basic attack animation ends to cancel its recovery. Cancel Q's recovery with a basic attack, E, or W. If animation cancels are unfamiliar, focus on landing one basic attack.
riven-combo-cancel.text: Press Q (Broken Wings) before Riven’s basic attack animation ends to cancel its recovery with the Q dash, then cancel Q’s recovery with a basic attack, E (Valor), or W (Ki Burst). Her damage comes from fitting more basic attacks into the same window through these cancels, not from ability scaling. If you haven’t mastered them, reliably landing one basic attack will deal more damage than forcing a cancel.

riven-laning.basis: Riven uses no resources, so she can trade whenever her abilities come off cooldown. Riven is most vulnerable just after using all her Q casts to clear minions. When pushing a wave, save at least one Q cast to respond to a counterattack.
riven-laning.text: Riven uses no resources and can trade whenever her abilities come off cooldown, but she is most vulnerable just after spending all her Q casts to clear minions. When pushing a wave, save at least one cast so you can respond to a counterattack.

riven-phase.basis: Riven is weak at levels 1–2. Once Riven has Q, W, and E at level 3, she can look for a kill with a full combo. Riven hits her first power spike when she learns R at level 6. Riven is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability haste and attack damage. In the late game, choose your engage carefully because it is hard to break through a tanky frontline alone.
riven-phase.text: Riven is weak at levels 1–2 because she has only one or two abilities and long cooldowns. With Q, W, and E available at level 3, she can look for a kill with a full combo; adding R at level 6 gives her first power spike. She is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability haste and attack damage, but in the late game she cannot break through a frontline with increased health and armor alone, so choose your engage carefully.

riven-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent sustains through healing, buy Executioner's Calling early to finish them after your combo. Riven relies on burst damage concentrated in a short window.
riven-situational-antiheal.text: If the opponent is surviving through healing, buy Executioner’s Calling early. Riven relies on burst damage in a short window, and active healing can keep the target alive even after the full combo lands.

riven-skill-e.basis: E grants a shield as Riven dashes. E's shield scales with bonus attack damage. E cannot cross terrain.
riven-skill-e.text: E (Valor) gives Riven both a dash and a shield. Because the shield scales with bonus attack damage, it remains useful for defense into the late game even if you build only attack items. E cannot cross terrain; use the third Q (Broken Wings) to go over walls. If you use E to engage, account for having only your third Q left to disengage.

riven-skill-passive.basis: Using an ability grants a passive stack. Basic attacks consume passive stacks. Using only abilities without basic attacks wastes passive stacks beyond the cap. Even while clearing a wave, leave yourself a chance to use passive stacks on the opposing champion.
riven-skill-passive.text: Each ability charges Riven’s blade through Runic Blade (P), and basic attacks consume those charges. Because charges have a cap, using abilities repeatedly without basic attacks wastes any additional charges. Even while clearing a wave, leave yourself a chance to spend them on the opposing champion.

riven-skill-q-cursor.basis: If your cursor is over a champion when you cast Q, the dash direction locks toward that champion. To dash past an opponent with Q, place your cursor beyond them. Casting Q with your cursor over the opponent stops you in front of them.
riven-skill-q-cursor.text: If your cursor is over a champion when you cast Q, the dash direction locks toward them. To dash past an opponent, place the cursor beyond them; casting Q with the cursor over them stops you in front.

riven-skill-q-terrain.basis: Q can cross terrain only on its third cast. The third Q knocks up nearby enemies. To escape or chase over a wall, use Q twice beforehand and save the third cast. If you use the third Q to deal damage during a trade, you lose your escape route over a wall.
riven-skill-q-terrain.text: Only Q’s third cast can cross terrain, and it knocks up nearby enemies. To escape or chase over a wall, use the first two casts beforehand and save the third; spending Q3 on damage during a trade removes that escape route.

riven-skill-r.basis: Activating R increases attack damage. Activating R increases the range of basic attacks and abilities. Wind Slash can be used only once while R is active. Unless it will secure the finish, save Wind Slash and keep fighting with R's bonus attack damage.
riven-skill-r.text: Activating R increases Riven’s attack damage and the range of her basic attacks and abilities, letting her Q and basic attacks reach farther than the opponent expects. Wind Slash can be used only once while R is active, so save it unless it will secure the finish and keep fighting with R’s bonus attack damage.

riven-skill-w.basis: W stuns in a very short area around Riven. Get close with Q or E before using W. W interrupts an opponent's channeled ultimate. Save W if the opponent is in a position to use a channeled ability.
riven-skill-w.text: W is a stun with a very short radius around Riven, so get close with Q or E before using it or it will miss. It can also interrupt channeled ultimates; if the opponent is poised to channel an ability, save W instead of spending it in a trade.

riven-teamfight.basis: Engage the enemy backline from the side or out of vision with E and Q3. Before engaging, check whether you will have a Q cast left to disengage. Riven has no self-healing.
