riven-teamfight.text: Riven should avoid fighting the frontline head-on. Aim to reach the enemy backline from a flank or out of vision with E (Valor) and the third Q (Broken Wings), checking before you engage whether you’ll have a Q cast left to disengage. She has no self-healing, and her E shield is her only protection, so if there’s no opening to engage, pushing a side lane is the better choice.

riven-teamfight-multi-melee.basis: Riven is strong in scrappy fights against multiple melee champions at once. Q3 and W can hit multiple opponents at once. Riven struggles when a ranged damage dealer attacks while keeping a safe distance. If you cannot reach the ranged damage dealer, wait for another chance to engage.
riven-teamfight-multi-melee.text: Riven fares well in scrappy fights against multiple melee champions because Q3 and W can hit several enemies at once. A ranged damage dealer attacking from a safe distance is her worst situation; if you cannot close the gap, wait for another opening rather than forcing an engage.

rumble-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, fire both E shots, then use Q. Landing the second E on an enemy slowed by the first greatly amplifies the slow and magic resistance reduction. If you activate Q after landing only one E, the enemy can walk out of range.
rumble-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, use E → E → Q: the first E slows the enemy, and landing the second on that slowed target greatly amplifies the slow and magic resistance reduction, letting you keep them in range of Q’s short cone for its full duration. If you activate Q after only one E, they can simply walk away.

rumble-combo-heat.basis: In fights, enter the Danger Zone with one E shot, then use Q. Most of Rumble's damage relies on his empowered Q in the Danger Zone. Avoid using abilities blindly, and leave enough Heat capacity to activate Q.
rumble-combo-heat.text: In fights, land one E to enter the Danger Zone, then activate Q. Most of Rumble’s damage comes from the empowered Q; using it outside the Danger Zone costs the same cooldown but delivers only half the value. Casting abilities without a plan can push Heat close to overheat and leave no room to activate Q when you need it.

rumble-combo-r.basis: Cut off the escape route with R, then slow the enemy with E and use Q. Drag while casting R to adjust its trajectory. Set R's final angle based on where the enemy will flee. In fights you are already winning, use R to cut off escape routes.
rumble-combo-r.text: Use R to cut off the enemy’s escape route, then slow them with E and follow with Q. You can drag during R’s cast to change its trajectory, so watch where they will flee before setting the final angle. If you are already winning the fight, R is more valuable as a barrier to their escape than as a source of damage.

rumble-laning.basis: In lane, safely chip away at the enemy's health with E. When the enemy steps forward to last-hit, slow them with E and approach with Q. Avoid activating Q first if you have no opening to get close to the enemy.
rumble-laning.text: Rumble has no separate resource to spend, so he can keep casting, but Q has short range and he has no mobility ability. In lane, chip away safely with E, then slow the enemy with E and move in with Q only when they step forward to last-hit. Activating Q without an opening to get close builds Heat without dealing damage.

rumble-phase.basis: Rumble is at a major disadvantage against magic damage opponents from levels 1–2. You can take early trades against melee opponents who deal physical damage. Rumble's ability to influence lanes increases greatly at level 6, when he learns R. Rumble is strongest in the mid game as he builds ability power. In the late game, Rumble's weakness is getting killed easily before he can reach the enemy.
rumble-phase.text: Rumble’s magic resistance is among the lowest of all champions, putting him at a major disadvantage against magic damage from levels 1–2. His health and armor rank high, though, so he can take early trades against physical damage melee opponents. His ability to influence lanes rises sharply when he learns R at level 6, and he peaks in the mid game as he builds ability power; late in the game, he can die before reaching the enemy.

rumble-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy's self-healing offsets Q's damage over time, buy Morellonomicon to reduce their healing. Rumble builds up damage by continuously burning enemies.
rumble-situational-antiheal.text: If an enemy’s self-healing offsets Q’s damage over time, buy Morellonomicon to reduce that healing. Rumble deals damage by burning enemies continuously rather than in one burst, so applying healing reduction can greatly increase the damage that sticks over the same period.

rumble-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy's main damage is magic, buy Force of Nature between core items to give yourself more time to stay close. Rumble's damage depends on how long he survives while staying close to the enemy.
rumble-situational-mr.text: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, Rumble’s extremely low magic resistance becomes a weakness. Buy Force of Nature between core items to survive longer while staying close. Since Rumble must remain near enemies to deal damage, more time alive means more damage.

rumble-skill-e.basis: E can store up to two shots. Landing both E shots in succession amplifies the slow, letting you keep the enemy within Q range. E's magic resistance reduction also boosts allied mages' damage. Avoid standing in front of the wave after using both E shots, as you have fewer ways to approach or escape.
rumble-skill-e.text: E is Rumble’s ranged poke and his only source of reach, with up to two shots stored. Landing both in succession amplifies the slow enough to keep an enemy within Q range, while the magic resistance reduction also benefits allied mages. If you stand in front of the wave after spending both shots, you have no way to close in or escape.

rumble-skill-passive.basis: Heat rises each time you use an ability. Heat decreases when you do nothing. Check your current Heat and choose your ability order to stay in the Danger Zone. If you can secure the kill in melee range, deliberately overheat to use empowered basic attacks. While overheated, the silence limits your ability to escape using abilities.
rumble-skill-passive.text: Heat rises whenever you use an ability and falls when you do nothing. Staying in the Danger Zone is central to playing Rumble, so choose your ability order based on your current Heat instead of pressing each ability as it comes off cooldown. If you can secure a kill at melee range, you can deliberately overheat for empowered basic attacks, but account for the silence: you will have no ability to help you escape.

rumble-skill-q.basis: While Q is active, move and turn to keep the enemy inside its cone. Q deals reduced damage to minions. Manage Q so you do not use it all on farming when you need it for trades. Q's max health damage makes it especially strong against tanks.
rumble-skill-q.text: Q projects a continuous cone while active, so move and turn to keep the enemy inside it. It deals reduced damage to minions, making it inefficient for wave clear; spending the whole cast on farming leaves Q unavailable when a trade starts. Its damage scales with the target’s maximum health, making it especially strong against tanks.

rumble-skill-r.basis: Draw R between the enemy frontline and backline to separate them. Once a fight has started, use R to cut off the enemy's retreat. R is most effective in narrow passages. Check the terrain in front of objectives beforehand to find narrow passages to block with R.
rumble-skill-r.text: R is an area denial tool before it is a damage tool. It is more reliable when drawn between the enemy frontline and backline to separate them, or across their retreat path after a fight has begun, than when used to open a teamfight. It is most valuable in narrow passages, so inspect the terrain around objectives beforehand.

rumble-skill-w.basis: W provides both a shield and a brief movement speed boost. With no mobility ability, Rumble relies on W's movement speed boost to engage and disengage. In the Danger Zone, both W's shield and movement speed boost are increased. After building Heat, use W as you close in on the enemy.
rumble-skill-w.text: W grants a shield and a brief movement speed boost. Because Rumble has no mobility ability, that speed is effectively his only way to engage or disengage, and both the shield and boost grow stronger in the Danger Zone. Build Heat first, then use W as you close in rather than activating it hurriedly just before taking a hit.

rumble-teamfight.basis: Find a position just in front of the enemy frontline where Q can hit multiple enemies. Avoid trying to assassinate the backline, as you have no way to dive that deep. Reduce the enemy's magic resistance with E to increase allied mages' damage. In teamfights, always follow your frontline after they engage.
rumble-teamfight.text: In teamfights, position just in front of the enemy frontline so Q’s cone covers multiple targets. Rumble has no way to dive the backline, so avoid assassination attempts and use E to lower enemies’ magic resistance, increasing allied mages’ damage as well. Always enter after your frontline.

ryze-combo-core.basis: The basic combo is E to apply a mark, then Q. Q deals increased damage to an E-marked target and bounces to nearby marked targets. Using another ability resets Q's cooldown. For damage, focus on the right ability order instead of pressing them quickly.
ryze-combo-core.text: Every combo starts with E → Q: Q deals increased damage to an E-marked target and bounces to nearby marked enemies. Each other ability resets Q’s cooldown, so Ryze’s damage depends on ability order, not how quickly you press the keys.

ryze-combo-full.basis: For an all-in, use E → W → Q → E → Q. The first Q consumes the mark, so reapply it with E before the second Q. When calculating mana for an all-in combo, account for casting E twice.
ryze-combo-full.text: For an all-in, use E → W (root) → Q → E → Q. The first Q consumes the mark, so reapply it with E before using the reset Q; account for both E casts when calculating the combo’s mana cost.

ryze-combo-root.basis: Use E, then W for a guaranteed root. W only slows a target without an E mark. Even when you need to stop an opponent quickly, don't use W first.
ryze-combo-root.text: Use E → W for a guaranteed root; without an E mark, W only slows. Even when you need to stop someone quickly, don’t use W first or you’ll lose the chance to lock them down.

ryze-combo-rune-ms.basis: Q grants a large movement speed boost when cast with two runes charged. To close in or escape, stack two runes with E and W, then use Q. Time Q according to whether you need maximum damage or survivability.
ryze-combo-rune-ms.text: Q grants a large movement speed boost when cast with two runes charged. To close in or escape, stack two runes with E and W before using Q; whether you need maximum damage or a way out determines when to cast it.

ryze-laning.basis: During the laning phase, clear the wave with E, then secure last hits with Q. Poke right after your opponent uses an ability on the wave. When poking, use a quick E → Q, then back off. When your mana falls below half, stop trading damage and just manage the wave.
ryze-laning.text: In lane, focus on farming: clear the wave with E and secure last hits with Q. Poke with a quick E → Q and back off only after your opponent uses an ability on the wave. If your mana falls below half, stop trading damage and manage the wave.

ryze-laning-push.basis: E clears waves quickly, making it easy to push the lane. Roaming on foot costs you a lot. After level 6, push the lane, then use R to join your allies.
ryze-laning-push.text: E clears waves quickly, making it easy to push, but Ryze has no mobility ability, so roaming on foot costs him a lot. After level 6, push the lane and use R to join your allies.

ryze-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier, between your core items. If an assassin who dives in catches you, it's hard to buy time to use your combo.
ryze-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy has a diving assassin, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier, between your core items. Ryze has no mobility ability, so once he is caught, he has no way to buy time for his combo.

ryze-skill-e-spread.basis: E has a very short cooldown, and its mark spreads around the enemy it hits. Just before a fight, use E on a minion or frontliner to set up Q's area damage. Don't repeatedly spend mana on E without a purpose. Don't hold back E when preparing for a teamfight.
ryze-skill-e-spread.text: E has a very short cooldown, and its mark spreads around the enemy it hits. Just before a fight, use it on a minion or frontliner to spread marks and increase the area damage from one Q. Avoid spending mana on E without a purpose, but use it to prepare for a teamfight.

ryze-skill-passive-mana.basis: The bonus mana from Ryze's passive also contributes to his damage. When mana runs low, it's hard to continue a combo, and the remaining abilities deal less damage. During the laning phase, check your remaining mana before deciding whether to poke.
ryze-skill-passive-mana.text: Through Ryze’s passive, bonus mana also increases his damage. Running low on mana makes it harder to complete a combo and effectively reduces the damage of your remaining abilities, so check how much you have before spending it on a poke in lane.

ryze-skill-q-aim.basis: Q travels in a straight line and hits only the first target. Mark an opponent among the minions with E, then use Q when they step out of the wave. Q without a mark has neither increased damage nor a bounce.
ryze-skill-q-aim.text: Q travels in a straight line and hits only the first target, so minions will block it against an opponent standing in the wave. Apply the mark with E, then use Q as they step out; without a mark, Q has neither increased damage nor a bounce.

ryze-skill-r-cast.basis: R activates after a short delay following its cast. Moving or using other abilities while R is charging does not cancel the cast. Being immobilized or unable to use abilities while R is charging cancels the cast. Cast R from a safe spot outside enemy vision, and deal damage until it activates.
ryze-skill-r-cast.text: R Realm Warp activates after a short delay. Moving or using other abilities while it charges will not cancel it, but being immobilized or prevented from using abilities will. Cast it from a safe spot outside enemy vision and deal damage while it charges.

ryze-skill-r-use.basis: R transports nearby allies with Ryze. Use R to ambush at objectives. Use R to join allies who are far away. Use R to leave after a teamfight. Tell your allies before using R so they can travel with you.
ryze-skill-r-use.text: R Realm Warp moves Ryze and nearby allies rather than dealing damage. Use it to ambush at objectives, join separated allies, or leave after a teamfight. Using it only to escape alone wastes its value, and you need to tell allies beforehand or Ryze may travel without them.

ryze-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, spread E marks through the frontline, then deal area damage with Q. Ryze's range is not especially long, so you may need to step forward during teamfights. Move in second, after an ally uses an engage ability.
ryze-teamfight.text: In teamfights, spread E marks through the frontline before dealing area damage with Q. Ryze’s range is not especially long, so you may need to step forward; move in second, after an ally uses an engage ability.

samira-combo-allin.basis: Follow your support's crowd control with a basic attack to close the gap, then build Style with Q, a basic attack, E, a basic attack, and W. Use R at S. Once you reach the enemy, alternate attack types to build Style.
samira-combo-allin.text: When your support lands crowd control in lane, close the gap with a basic attack, then build Style with a close-range Q (Flair) slash → basic attack → E (Wild Rush) to get behind the enemy → basic attack → W (Blade Whirl). Use R (Inferno Trigger) the moment you reach S. Delaying while you build Style gives enemy backup time to arrive, so alternate attack types from the moment you get in range.

samira-combo-cc-dash.basis: Basic attacking an immobilized enemy makes you dash to them even from maximum basic attack range. When you close in on an airborne enemy with a basic attack, you rise with them and keep them airborne. Be within basic attack range when your support uses an engage ability.
samira-combo-cc-dash.text: Basic attacking an immobilized enemy makes Samira dash to them even from maximum basic attack range; if they are airborne, she rises with them and keeps them there. Allied crowd control, especially a knockup, therefore gives her a way in and extends the hold, so be within basic attack range when your support uses an engage ability.

samira-combo-eq.basis: Press Q during your E dash to hit enemies along its path at once. Press Q when using E into a group of overlapping enemies. Using Q separately after E ends hits only one target.
samira-combo-eq.text: Press Q during Wild Rush (E) to strike every enemy along the dash’s path at once after it ends, combining your engage, area damage, and a Style increase. Use this combination whenever you dash into a group; casting Q separately after E ends hits only one target.

samira-laning.basis: Samira has short range for a marksman, so trading damage with ranged poke champions can easily put her behind. When facing ranged poke, give up on building Style and farm under your turret. In a poke matchup, engage when the enemy support steps forward or your jungler intervenes. Against a melee composition, or with engage crowd control from your support, take control from level 2.
samira-laning.text: Samira has short range for a marksman, so trading into ranged poke usually puts her behind. In that matchup, give up on building Style and farm under your turret until the enemy support steps too far forward or your jungler intervenes, then engage all at once. Against a melee composition, or alongside a support with engage crowd control, take control from level 2.

samira-laning-trade.basis: Fight within melee range to get a worthwhile damage trade. Only engage with E when your support's crowd control or Flash is available. Repeat short trades where you get close, raise your Style rank by two or three steps, then back off.
samira-laning-trade.text: A worthwhile damage trade requires melee range, which also puts Samira within the enemy support’s ability range. Using E to enter removes her escape, so close in only when your support’s crowd control or Flash is available. Repeated short trades—getting close, gaining two or three Style ranks, then backing off—will keep wearing down the enemy.

samira-phase.basis: Once you have Q and E at level 2, your first all-in opportunity opens up. Learning R at level 6 gives you the power to turn a fight around. Samira peaks in the mid game as she builds critical strike items. In the late game, enemy defensive items and crowd control mean you need allies to create an opening for you to engage.
samira-phase.text: Getting Q and E at level 2 opens Samira’s first all-in opportunity, and R at level 6 lets her turn a fight around on her own. She peaks in the mid game as she builds critical strike items and, statistically, has the highest 14-minute kill count among marksmen, making early gains essential. Her damage holds up late, but enemy defensive items and crowd control make reaching melee range harder, so she needs allies to create an opening.

samira-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy frontline sustains through healing, choose Mortal Reminder for your armor penetration item slot. Samira's abilities do not apply Grievous Wounds. If you only need armor penetration and not Grievous Wounds, stick with Lord Dominik's Regards.
samira-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy frontline sustains through healing, use Mortal Reminder in your armor penetration slot. Samira fights up close for extended periods, so ongoing enemy healing keeps her in melee range longer, and her abilities provide no Grievous Wounds. If you only need armor penetration, keep Lord Dominik’s Regards.

samira-situational-cc.basis: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items to reduce the damage lost when R is interrupted. If you are immobilized during R, the remaining shots are lost and your reset Style rank does not return.
samira-situational-cc.text: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, fit Quicksilver Sash between core items. Samira fires Inferno Trigger (R) from one spot for its duration, so being immobilized partway through costs her every remaining shot after Style has already reset.

samira-skill-e.basis: E passes through enemies and structures, letting you chase or escape past turrets. When a kill is certain, use E to engage, knowing it will reset. If a kill is uncertain, save E to escape.
samira-skill-e.text: E (Wild Rush) dashes through enemies and structures, letting you chase or escape past turrets. If an enemy champion you damaged dies shortly afterward, its cooldown resets, so you can use it to engage when a kill is certain and still have a way out. If the kill is uncertain, save E as your only escape. Much of playing Samira comes down to that choice.

samira-skill-melee-range.basis: Samira deals her full damage within melee range. At melee range, Q becomes a sword slash instead of a gunshot. At melee range, her passive adds magic damage based on the target's missing health. Create an opening to get close enough to deal damage.
samira-skill-melee-range.text: Although Samira is a ranged champion, she deals her full damage only within melee range. There, Flair (Q) becomes a sword slash instead of a gunshot, and Daredevil Impulse adds magic damage that increases with the target’s missing health. Staying back to basic attack leaves her with less range than other marksmen, so look for an opening to get close.

samira-skill-passive-grade.basis: Hitting an enemy champion with a different type of attack from the one you last hit them with raises your Style rank by one. Alternate different types of attacks among basic attacks, Q, W, and E to build your Style rank to S in one fight. Each increase in Style rank grants movement speed.
samira-skill-passive-grade.text: Style rises one rank when you hit an enemy champion with a different type of attack from your previous hit. Repeated basic attacks or two Q uses in a row stall it, so alternate attacks—basic attack → Q → basic attack → W → basic attack → E—to climb all six ranks from E to S in one fight. Each rank also grants movement speed, making Style management a source of damage and survivability.

samira-skill-w.basis: W destroys enemy projectiles that enter its area. Time W against the enemy marksman's basic attacks or projectile abilities. If the enemy has a crucial projectile, build Style with basic attacks, Q, and E, and save W for defense.
samira-skill-w.text: Blade Whirl (W) destroys enemy projectiles that enter its area, making it a defensive tool when timed against a marksman’s basic attacks or projectile abilities. It also builds Style, so holding it indiscriminately delays R. If the enemy has a crucial projectile, build Style with basic attacks, Q, and E, and save W for defense.

samira-teamfight.basis: Do not engage first in teamfights. Before diving into the middle of several enemies, reach Style rank S so you can use R.
samira-teamfight.text: Never engage first in a teamfight. Once your frontline has stopped the enemy with crowd control, move in, alternate attack types to build Style, and use R (Inferno Trigger) the moment you reach S. Its life steal makes the middle of several enemies the safest place to be, but only when your Style is already at S; going in at a lower rank leaves Samira a fragile ranged carry.

sejuani-combo-gank.basis: During a gank, knock the target up with Q, build stacks with W, stun with E, then auto-attack. Auto-attack immediately after the E stun to trigger the passive's bonus damage.
sejuani-combo-gank.text: For a gank, use Q to dash in and knock the target up, land all of W to build Permafrost stacks, then stun with E once the stacks are full. Follow the stun with one auto-attack: missing it forfeits the passive’s bonus damage based on the target’s maximum health.

sejuani-combo-r.basis: R stuns longer when it travels farther before hitting. Throw R from as far away as possible. After R hits, engage with Q while its area slow remains, then follow with W and E. Approach from the side so a champion in front does not take the R instead.
sejuani-combo-r.text: R stuns longer the farther it travels before hitting, so throw it from as far away as possible rather than at close range. Its area slow lingers after impact, giving you time to follow with Q, W, and E. Only the first champion hit is stunned, so approach from the side to avoid hitting a champion in front of your intended target.

sejuani-combo-walkup.basis: If the target has a mobility ability, save Q when engaging. Walk in, build stacks with W, and stun with E. Use Q to follow when the target escapes with a mobility ability. Q's knockup is brief, and using it to engage leaves you without an escape.
sejuani-combo-walkup.text: If the target has a mobility ability, save Q instead of opening with it. Its knockup is brief enough to give them time to react, and using it to engage leaves you without a way out. Walk in, build stacks with W, and stun with E first; then use Q to follow as they try to escape with their mobility ability, making the kill more reliable.

sejuani-laning-gank.basis: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret, where the enemy has a long way to retreat. Avoid hitting camps right before a gank so Frost Armor stays active. Allied melee champions' auto-attacks build E stacks, letting you stun sooner during a gank. The more melee champions on your team, the more likely your ganks are to succeed.
sejuani-laning-gank.text: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret, where the opponent has a long way to retreat. Avoid hitting a camp just before engaging so Frost Armor is active. In a lane with an allied melee champion, their auto-attacks can build stacks for you and bring out the E stun much sooner; the more melee champions on your team, the more likely your ganks are to succeed.

sejuani-laning-path.basis: Her early kills and damage per minute are low, so jungle routes aimed at early kills do not suit her. Early on, clear camps safely to gain levels. Start fights in lanes where your ally already has the advantage. Move with Frost Armor active to prepare for counterjungling.
sejuani-laning-path.text: Sejuani’s jungle path should focus on safe camp clears and gaining levels rather than early kills. Her kills at 14 minutes and damage per minute rank near the bottom, while her deaths rank among the highest, so her win rates favor starting fights only in lanes where an ally already has the advantage. Keep Frost Armor active while moving as basic protection against counterjungling.

sejuani-phase.basis: Before level 6, ganks are slow because you need full stacks to stun. From level 6, you can start fights with R regardless of stacks. The passive's bonus defensive stats scale with Sejuani's armor and magic resistance, while W's damage scales with her maximum health.
sejuani-phase.text: Before level 6, ganks are slow because Sejuani must fully stack Permafrost to stun. Once R becomes available at level 6, she can reliably start a fight in any lane regardless of stacks. Her passive grants bonus defensive stats that scale with her armor and magic resistance, while W scales with maximum health, making defensive items a source of both damage and survivability. Win rates also rise sharply when she completes her three core items.

sejuani-skill-e.basis: E can only be used on a target with full stacks. W and Sejuani's auto-attacks build stacks. Nearby allied melee champions' auto-attacks also build E stacks. Watch which target an allied melee champion is attacking to see who will be ready for an E stun. E targets the enemy closest to your cursor. Stacks cannot build again for a while on an enemy stunned by E.
sejuani-skill-e.text: E can only be used on a target with full stacks, which build from Sejuani's W and auto-attacks as well as nearby allied melee champions' auto-attacks. Watch whom a melee ally is attacking to see where a stun is becoming available, and position your cursor to select the intended target, since E targets the enemy closest to it. Stacks cannot build on an enemy for a while after E stuns them, so choose the target carefully.

sejuani-skill-passive.basis: Frost Armor activates after Sejuani avoids damage from champions and large jungle monsters for a set time, granting slow immunity and defensive stats. Just before a fight, avoid hitting camps and wait for Frost Armor to activate. Auto-attack stunned enemies to deal the passive's damage based on their maximum health.
sejuani-skill-passive.text: Frost Armor activates after Sejuani goes a set time without taking damage from champions or large jungle monsters, granting slow immunity and defensive stats. Before a fight, avoid hitting a camp and wait briefly so you enter with the armor active; that wait before a gank is preparation. Her first auto-attack against an enemy she has stunned also deals bonus damage based on their maximum health, so make a habit of attacking after the stun.

sejuani-skill-q.basis: Q can be used for movement and to start fights. Q can interrupt channeled abilities. Q stops when it hits an enemy champion but passes through minions. When using Q to cross a wall or escape, check that no enemy champion is in your path.
sejuani-skill-q.text: Q is a movement tool, a way to start fights, and a means of interrupting channeled abilities. It stops on contact with an enemy champion, so make sure none is in your path when crossing a wall or escaping. Minions do not stop the charge, allowing you to engage through a lane.

sejuani-skill-w.basis: W swings twice, with most of its damage and its slow on the second hit. When using W, land the second hit too. W's first hit pushes minions and jungle monsters, which can hurt camp clears. Max W first for its second-hit damage and faster stack building.
sejuani-skill-w.text: W swings twice, with most of its damage and its slow on the second hit. Finish the cast: backing off after the first hit gives you only half the stacks and damage. The first hit pushes minions and jungle monsters, which can scatter a camp and make clearing less efficient. W is commonly maxed first because of the second hit's damage and how quickly it builds stacks.

sejuani-teamfight.basis: With Frost Armor active, cast R at an angle that reaches the enemy backline damage dealer. When R hits, follow in with Q and hold the target down with W and E. Engage when your allied damage dealers can immediately damage the R target. If your allied damage dealers cannot follow up, use W from the front to slow the enemy's engage and save R.
sejuani-teamfight.text: Your role is to start teamfights. With Frost Armor active, throw R from an angle that reaches an enemy backline damage dealer, then follow a hit with Q and hold the target down with W and E. Engage only when your damage dealers are positioned to damage the R target immediately. Otherwise, use W from the front to slow the enemy's engage and save R for the next fight.

senna-combo-pick.basis: When you have a chance to kill, land W, then time Q and an attack with the root. Time the delay between W's hit and root with an ally's engage ability.
senna-combo-pick.text: For a kill combo, land W (Last Embrace) to set up the root, then time Q (Piercing Darkness) and a basic attack to hit as it takes hold. Sync the delay between W’s hit and its root with an ally’s engage so the target is locked down twice in a row. If W misses, use Q first to slow the target, then look for another W.

senna-combo-teamfight.basis: To start a teamfight, approach with allies using E, root opponents in the center with W, then use R. R's ally shield covers a wider area than its damage hitbox. Aim R so allies are also within the beam's width.
senna-combo-teamfight.text: To start a teamfight, approach with allies using E, root opponents in the center of their formation with W, then use R, Dawning Shadow, to help finish the fight while shielding allies. Its shield covers a wider area than its damage hitbox, so aim the beam to include allies instead of focusing only on a kill.

senna-laning-souls.basis: Stepping forward to collect a soul is the most dangerous moment. Check both the soul's position and the range of enemy abilities. Step forward to collect a soul when key enemy abilities are on cooldown. Avoid last-hitting minions so you do not take CS from your allied marksman.
senna-laning-souls.text: Stepping forward for a soul is especially dangerous. Check its position and the range of enemy abilities, and move up only while key enemy abilities are on cooldown; be willing to give up souls near the enemy turret. Avoid last-hitting minions so your allied marksman gets the CS, but collect the souls.

senna-laning-trade.basis: Senna attacks slowly and has a long pause after each attack. Do not aim for consecutive attacks when poking in lane. Land an attack followed by Q to gain Mist, then retreat immediately.
senna-laning-trade.text: Senna attacks slowly and has a long pause after each attack, so trying to land consecutive attacks while poking in lane invites retaliation. Land an attack, follow it with Q to collect Mist, then retreat immediately and repeat that rhythm.

senna-phase.basis: Senna can die easily if caught early. Senna becomes more impactful from the mid game onward as Mist increases her attack damage and range. In the late game, Senna deals damage from a safe position using her range advantage. Collect Mist early without dying.
senna-phase.text: Senna's level-one health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, making an early catch potentially fatal. Her impact rises sharply from mid game as Mist increases her damage and range; late game, that range lets her deal damage from a safe position. Focus on collecting Mist without dying early.

senna-skill-e.basis: Allies inside E's mist are camouflaged too. Allies who leave E's mist become wraiths that conceal their identities. Use E just before a teamfight and approach with your allies to make it harder for opponents to target them. Use E when engaging with allies, not just to escape.
senna-skill-e.text: E, Curse of the Black Mist, is most valuable for starting an engagement. Allies inside the mist are camouflaged, and those who leave it become wraiths that conceal their identities. Approach together just before a teamfight to make it harder for opponents to target your allies; saving E only for escapes gives up that team benefit.

senna-skill-mist-champ.basis: Hit the same enemy champion twice with attacks or abilities to gain Mist. Hit the same enemy champion twice with attacks or abilities to deal bonus damage based on their current health. When you have a safe chance to poke, take it. Combine one attack and one Q in a single approach to gain Mist.
senna-skill-mist-champ.text: Senna also gains Mist by hitting the same enemy champion twice with attacks or abilities, dealing bonus damage based on their current health. Poking is therefore part of her growth: take safe opportunities, and combine one attack with Q to collect Mist in a single approach.

senna-skill-q.basis: Q travels in a straight line through the targeted ally or enemy. If you cannot hit an opponent directly with Q, target a minion in front of them to hit them behind it. Q's cast range scales with attack range. Q's cast time scales with attack speed.
senna-skill-q.text: Q, Piercing Darkness, travels in a straight line through a targeted ally or enemy. You can target an allied champion or a minion in front of an opponent to hit them even when they are outside Q's direct targeting range. Its cast range scales with attack range, while its cast time improves with attack speed, so Mist and attack speed make Q stronger.

senna-skill-q-cooldown.basis: Each attack reduces Q's cooldown. After using Q, follow up with two attacks to reduce its cooldown. Instead of saving Q only for urgent ally healing, use attacks to reduce its cooldown.
senna-skill-q-cooldown.text: Each attack reduces Q's cooldown, so follow Q with two attacks to bring it back sooner. Weaving in attacks lets you use Q more often than holding it solely for an urgent heal on an ally.

senna-skill-r.basis: R is an area beam that extends beyond the screen. R's shield strength scales with the amount of Mist collected.
senna-skill-r.text: R (Dawning Shadow) is a wide beam that reaches beyond the screen, letting Senna influence fights in other lanes. Use it to shield allies in a losing fight as well as to finish enemies. The shield absorbs more damage as she collects Mist, so growth from her passive directly strengthens R.

senna-skill-range-growth.basis: At certain Mist thresholds, Senna gains attack range and critical strike chance. In the late game, Senna's increased range lets her attack before other marksmen. As your range grows, position to make use of it when attacking.
senna-skill-range-growth.text: At certain Mist thresholds, Senna gains both attack range and critical strike chance. By late game, her range lets her attack before other marksmen, changing how she should position compared with the early game; step forward to land attacks and make use of that growth.

senna-skill-souls.basis: Senna grows by collecting Mist through her passive, Absolution. When a unit dies near Senna, it has a chance to leave a soul behind. Attack a soul to collect Mist. Souls disappear over time, so watch where they appear and collect them. Support Senna gains attack damage from Mist without taking CS.
senna-skill-souls.text: Senna grows by collecting Mist through her passive, Absolution. When a unit dies near her, it has a chance to leave a soul that she must attack to collect. Souls disappear over time, so watch where they land and walk over to claim them; for support Senna, this is her only way to gain attack damage without taking CS.

senna-skill-w.basis: W attaches to the first target it hits, then roots nearby targets after a short delay. Minions block W. Account for W's delayed root and aim where the opponent is going. Hit grouped opponents with W to root several at once.
senna-skill-w.text: W Last Embrace attaches to the first target it hits, then roots nearby enemies after a short delay. Minions can block it, so in lane, fire through gaps between them or from a side without minions. Aim where your opponent is going rather than where they stand, and look for grouped opponents to root several at once.

senna-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, heal allies with Q from the backline. In teamfights, attack from the backline using your increased range. Hold W to stop an enemy engage. If you cannot use W on an approaching enemy, use it when it lines up with an ally's engage ability. In teamfights, Senna should only move forward when engaging with E.
senna-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay in the backline, healing allies with Q and adding attacks from your increased range. Hold W to stop an enemy engage; if no approaching enemy gives you that opportunity, use it when it lines up with an ally's engage ability. Senna's low health makes stepping forward dangerous, so advance to engage only when using E.

seraphine-combo-cc-chain.basis: E roots enemies who are already slowed. E stuns enemies who are immobilized. Apply a slow from yourself or an ally first, then root them with E. If you land E first without a slow, it only slows.
seraphine-combo-cc-chain.text: E Beat Drop roots enemies who are already slowed and stuns those who are immobilized. Apply a slow from Seraphine or an ally first to guarantee the root; without that setup, E only slows.

seraphine-combo-passive-echo.basis: The passive casts every third basic ability twice. If both hits of Echo E land, the first E slows and the second roots. Count your basic ability casts before a fight to line up Echo with E or W.
seraphine-combo-passive-echo.text: P Stage Presence casts every third basic ability twice. When both casts of an Echoed E Beat Drop hit, the first slows and the second roots. Count your casts before a fight so Echo lines up with E or W.

seraphine-combo-ult-follow.basis: Charm with R, root with E, then finish with Q. Using Q before E costs you damage based on missing health.
seraphine-combo-ult-follow.text: After charming an enemy with R (Encore), follow up with E (Beat Drop) to hold them in place as they walk toward you, then use Q (High Note) to finish them once their health has dropped. Using Q first loses damage based on their missing health.

seraphine-combo-ult-range.basis: R also extends its range when it hits an allied champion. In teamfights, cast R through allies lined up in front of you. Allies hit by R gain a full stack of Notes.
seraphine-combo-ult-range.text: R Encore extends its range when it hits an allied champion. In teamfights, aim through allies lined up in front of you to reach much farther; allies hit also gain a full stack of Notes.

seraphine-laning-mana.basis: Q and W cost a lot of mana, so excessive early poke can leave you unable to use E and W when you need them. Trade when the enemy stops to last-hit a minion. When you aren't trading, focus on positioning and securing vision.
seraphine-laning-mana.text: Q and W cost a lot of mana, so excessive early poke can leave you unable to cast E and W when you need them. Trade only when the enemy stops to last-hit a minion; otherwise, focus on positioning and vision.

seraphine-phase.basis: Seraphine can poke comfortably in lane thanks to her ability range and Notes from allies. Seraphine struggles to get kills alone. Her teamfight impact rises sharply after learning R at level 6. Seraphine is strongest in the mid to late game as she builds ability power. Never stand in front at any stage of the game.
seraphine-phase.text: Seraphine can poke comfortably in lane thanks to her ability range and Notes from allies, but struggles to secure kills alone. Her teamfight impact rises sharply once she learns R at level 6, and she is strongest in the mid to late game as she builds ability power. Her health and movement speed are very low, so never stand in front at any stage of the game.

seraphine-situational-mikael.basis: If the enemy team has a lot of reliable crowd control, get Mikael's Blessing earlier. If an ally is caught in crowd control, they may die before Seraphine's shield and heal can reach them.
seraphine-situational-mikael.text: If the enemy team has a lot of reliable crowd control, buy Mikael’s Blessing earlier. Seraphine’s job is to keep allies alive, but a controlled ally may die before her shield and heal reach them.

seraphine-skill-e-save.basis: E is Seraphine's only reliable crowd control. Save E for an ally's engage or to stop an enemy's dash. E deals reduced damage to minions. Don't use E to clear waves.
seraphine-skill-e-save.text: E (Beat Drop) is Seraphine’s only reliable crowd control. Save it for an ally’s engage or to stop an enemy dash: spending it on poke leaves you without a way to answer an enemy engage. It deals reduced damage to minions, so don’t use it to clear waves.

seraphine-skill-q.basis: Q deals more damage the more health the target is missing. Use Q to finish low-health enemies or clear waves.
seraphine-skill-q.text: Q (High Note) deals more damage the more health the target has lost, so poking a full-health enemy with it is inefficient. Use it to finish a wounded enemy or clear a wave instead.

seraphine-skill-w-double.basis: If you use W again while your shield is still active, it also heals. Echo W provides both a shield and a heal in one cast. Before a major fight, line up Echo with W.
seraphine-skill-w-double.text: W Surround Sound also heals if you cast it again while your shield is still active. An Echoed W gives you both a shield and a heal in one cast, so line up Echo with W before a major fight.

seraphine-skill-w-timing.basis: W also increases allies' movement speed. Use W as you engage or retreat to make use of its movement speed and shield.
seraphine-skill-w-timing.text: W (Surround Sound) also boosts your allies’ movement speed. Use it as you begin to engage or retreat so you benefit from both the speed boost and shield, rather than waiting until everyone has taken damage and using it to heal.

seraphine-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and protect them with W. Send E through grouped enemies to root them. If R can reach the enemy backline, use it just before your allies engage.
seraphine-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and shield them with W, then send E through grouped enemies to root them. Use R when you have an angle to reach the enemy backline, casting it just before your allies engage to prevent the enemy from responding.

seraphine-teamfight-ult-defense.basis: R's charm can turn an engaging enemy back as a defensive tool. If your carry gets jumped, use R immediately instead of waiting to hit multiple enemies.
seraphine-teamfight-ult-defense.text: R is also valuable defensively: its charm can turn an engaging enemy back. If your carry gets jumped, cast it immediately rather than waiting for a chance to hit multiple enemies and losing your ally.

sett-combo-basic.basis: For a basic trade, use two Q-empowered attacks, then E and W in order. Q has no cast time, so using it between attacks or while moving keeps your attack rhythm intact. Use Q as your attacks connect, rather than activating it before getting in range. Immediately line up W with the enemies pulled together by E to guarantee a center-line hit.
sett-combo-basic.text: For a basic trade, activate Q, land two basic attacks, then pull enemies together with E and follow up with W. Q has no cast time, so you can use it between attacks or while moving without breaking your attack rhythm; activate it as soon as you can land an attack rather than before you get in range. E pulls the targets in front of Sett, letting you aim W along the same line immediately afterward for a guaranteed center-line hit.

sett-combo-r.basis: For an R engage combo, use E and W after landing, then finish with Q-empowered attacks. R moves the grabbed target forward in the direction Sett is facing. To send an enemy into the middle of your team, use R with your back to your allies. The strong slow around R's landing point makes the follow-up E easier to aim.
sett-combo-r.text: For an R engage, grab and throw the target with R, then use E at the landing point, W, and Q-empowered basic attacks. R carries the target forward in the direction Sett is facing, so move behind the enemy and face your allies before throwing them to land them in the middle of your team. The strong slow around the landing point makes the immediate follow-up E easier to aim.

sett-laning-ranged.basis: Sett struggles to reach ranged opponents before learning R. Against ranged opponents, give up trading and pull the wave toward your turret to farm. Against ranged opponents, only attempt guaranteed crowd control with E and R when your jungler comes. Avoid forcing your way toward ranged opponents and losing health while out of range.
sett-laning-ranged.text: Before unlocking R (The Show Stopper), Sett has no way to close the gap on ranged opponents. Give up trades, pull the wave toward your turret and farm; use E (Facebreaker) and R for guaranteed crowd control only when your jungler arrives. Forcing your way in merely builds Grit while you lose health outside your attack range.

sett-laning-trade.basis: When trading against melee opponents, wait for them to use an ability instead of engaging first. Sett's trading efficiency depends on the Grit he builds before striking back.
sett-laning-trade.text: Against melee opponents, let them use an ability first, turn the damage into Grit, then trade back with Q (Knuckle Down) empowered attacks and W (Haymaker). If Sett engages first, his Grit is empty and the same combo delivers only half its value.

sett-phase.basis: Sett has a weak period at levels 1–2. Sett reaches his first power spike at level 3, when he has Q, W, and E. Sett reaches his second power spike at level 6, when he learns R. Sett peaks in the mid game, when health items increase his Grit capacity. In the late game, Sett's impact depends on R usage because he struggles to reach ranged formations.
sett-phase.text: Sett is weak at levels 1–2 with only one or two abilities available. His first two power spikes come at level 3, when Q (Knuckle Down), W (Haymaker) and E (Facebreaker) are all available, and level 6, when he gains R (The Show Stopper). His Grit capacity grows with his health, making the mid game, as he builds health items, his peak. Late in the game, he struggles to reach ranged formations, so his impact depends on where he uses his one R.

sett-situational-antiheal.basis: Buy Executioner's Calling if the enemy's healing is enough to turn trades around. Sett deals damage through multiple empowered attacks, making healing reduction easy to maintain.
sett-situational-antiheal.text: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the enemy’s healing is strong enough to turn trades around. Sett spreads damage across multiple empowered attacks, making healing reduction easy to maintain.

sett-situational-mr.basis: Buy an early Null-Magic Mantle to reduce losses in early trades against magic damage opponents. Against magic damage opponents, buy a magic resistance item after completing your first core item.
sett-situational-mr.text: Sett has one of the lowest level 1 magic resistance values among champions, making him especially vulnerable to magic damage. Buy an early Null-Magic Mantle to reduce losses in early trades, then build a magic resistance item after completing your first core item.

sett-skill-e.basis: E only stuns if it grabs at least one enemy on each side. E only slows if it grabs enemies on just one side. E can affect all enemy units, including champions. Position between minions and the enemy champion to land an E stun even in a 1v1.
sett-skill-e.text: E (Facebreaker) stuns only when it grabs at least one enemy on each side of Sett; grabbing enemies on just one side only slows them. Any enemy unit counts, so position with a minion wave on one side and the opposing champion on the other to land a stun even in a 1v1. Using E straight ahead without setting this up wastes its cooldown on a slow.

sett-skill-passive.basis: Sett's passive right punch hits harder and faster than his left punch. When trading basic attacks, finish with the right punch before backing off. Sett's passive increases his health regeneration as his missing health increases. Even after taking damage, consider using his passive healing to stay in lane.
sett-skill-passive.text: Sett’s passive, Pit Grit, makes his right punch faster and stronger than his left. If you start attacking, land the right punch before backing off; leaving after only the left loses you damage in the trade. His health regeneration also increases with missing health, making it possible to stay in lane and recover after taking damage.

sett-skill-q.basis: Q empowers your next two attacks. Q increases movement speed when walking toward enemy champions. Use Q the moment you start chasing a fleeing enemy. Use both Q-empowered attacks on champions instead of minions. Q's damage cap per punch against monsters limits its contribution to jungle clearing.
sett-skill-q.text: Q (Knuckle Down) empowers Sett’s next two attacks and grants movement speed while he walks toward enemy champions, making it useful for both chasing and dealing damage. Activate it as you start pursuing a fleeing enemy, and land both empowered attacks on the champion rather than spending them on minions. Each punch has a damage cap against monsters, so Q contributes less to jungle clearing than you might expect.

sett-skill-w-aim.basis: W deals true damage only to enemies on its center line. W deals physical damage to enemies outside its center line. Aim W's center line precisely at tanks with high armor. W grants its shield before the punch goes out. When you urgently need to survive, use W for the shield before worrying about aim.
sett-skill-w-aim.text: W (Haymaker) deals true damage only along its center line and physical damage outside it, so line up the center precisely against high-armor tanks. Its shield applies before the punch, though, so if you urgently need to survive, you can use W for the shield without taking time to aim.

sett-skill-w-grit.basis: W stores Grit based on the damage Sett takes. W's Grit rapidly decays shortly after taking damage. To maximize W's shield and damage, use it immediately after taking a major enemy ability. W provides almost no shield when Grit is empty. In lane, consider deliberately taking some poke to build Grit.
sett-skill-w-grit.text: W (Haymaker) stores the damage Sett takes as Grit, which rapidly decays shortly after he takes damage. Use it right after getting hit, especially by a major enemy ability, when both its shield and damage are strongest. With empty Grit, W provides almost no shield; deliberately taking some poke in lane can build the gauge.

sett-teamfight-entry.basis: Instead of starting a teamfight, enter one already underway while building Grit. In narrow passages, pull multiple enemies into a line with E, then hit them with W's center line. Avoid frontal engages in open areas, where you can easily die before getting in range.
sett-teamfight-entry.text: Sett works best entering a fight already underway while building Grit, rather than starting the teamfight himself. In a narrow passage, pull multiple enemies into a line with E and place W’s center line over them for maximum damage. Walking straight into a fight in open space can get you killed before you reach anyone.

sett-teamfight-r.basis: R's damage scales with the grabbed target's bonus health. To increase R's damage, target a frontline enemy with health items. A target grabbed by R is suppressed and cannot escape with movement abilities. If you have an angle to move a key damage dealer into the middle of your team, prioritize disrupting their formation over R's damage.
sett-teamfight-r.text: R (The Show Stopper) deals more damage based on the grabbed target’s bonus health, so grabbing a frontline enemy with health items produces a harder hit. The target is suppressed and cannot escape with movement abilities. Disrupting the enemy formation can be more valuable, though: if you can throw a key damage dealer into the middle of your team, choose that angle over extra R damage.

shaco-combo-box-camp.basis: Place W before starting a jungle camp, then attack while the monsters are feared. W's fear lasts much longer on monsters than on champions. Use W during early jungle clears to lose less health. W has a fairly short cooldown, so using one at each camp won't slow your clear.
shaco-combo-box-camp.text: Place W Jack In The Box before starting each jungle camp, then attack while the monsters are feared. Its fear lasts much longer on monsters than on champions, letting Shaco finish his early clear with little health lost; the cooldown is short enough to use a box at every camp without slowing the clear.

shaco-combo-gank.basis: When ganking, place W on the escape route, use Q to get behind the target, land an empowered basic attack, then finish with E. When entering with Q, position yourself so the empowered basic attack hits the target from behind. The empowered basic attack from behind after Q is a critical strike. Place W in the direction the target will flee to block their escape.
shaco-combo-gank.text: For a gank, place W Jack In The Box along the target’s escape route, then use Q Deceive to appear behind them, land the empowered basic attack, and finish with E Two-Shiv Poison. The attack after Q is a critical strike when it hits from behind, so position the teleport accordingly while the box blocks their retreat.

shaco-combo-r-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, send the R clone toward the enemy backline to draw attention, then use Q to get behind them from the other side. Engage when the R clone explodes and the small boxes trigger their fear. Do not keep the R clone beside Shaco, or both may be hit by the same area-of-effect ability.
shaco-combo-r-teamfight.text: In teamfights, send the R Hallucinate clone toward the enemy backline to draw attention while Shaco uses Q Deceive to get behind them from the opposite side. Engage as the clone explodes and its three small boxes trigger fear, scattering the enemy formation. Keep the clone away from Shaco so the same area-of-effect ability does not hit both.

shaco-jungle-path.basis: Shaco is a jungler who gets ahead through kill participation more than farming. Clear camps safely with W, then use the health you saved for ganks and jungle invades. Place W in front of enemy camps to prepare for invades and gain vision against counter-invades.
shaco-jungle-path.text: Shaco gets ahead through kill participation rather than farming. Clear camps safely with W Jack In The Box, then spend the health you saved on ganks and jungle invades. A box in front of an enemy camp also helps you prepare for invades and provides vision against counter-invades.

shaco-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, use W to clear camps safely. Once you have both Q and E at level 3, you can make your first gank. Shaco's burst damage peaks in the mid game with two items. With two items in the mid game, look for chances to pick off enemy backliners alone. Shaco's ability to win solo fights falls off late game. When enemies have vision late game, Shaco has fewer angles to engage from. Late game, use W and the R clone to disrupt enemy vision and apply pressure. Shaco can easily fall behind the pace of the game if he fails to gain an early advantage.
shaco-phase.text: At levels 1–2, clear camps safely with W Jack In The Box; once Shaco has both Q Deceive and E Two-Shiv Poison at level 3, he can make his first gank. His burst peaks with two items in the mid game, when he can pick off enemy backliners alone. Late game, his solo fighting weakens and enemy vision limits his engage angles, so use boxes and the R Hallucinate clone to disrupt vision and apply pressure. Without an early advantage, he can fall behind the pace of the game.

shaco-situational-antiheal.basis: If a target you need to pick off survives through healing, buy Executioner's Calling early. If an enemy heals during Shaco's burst, you may lack the damage to kill them.
shaco-situational-antiheal.text: If a target you need to pick off can survive through healing, buy Executioner's Calling early. Shaco's burst needs to finish the kill quickly; if they heal during that window, you may fall short on damage and be left committed to the engage with no way to escape.

shaco-situational-cc.basis: Consider Quicksilver Sash if the enemy has a lot of crowd control that prevents movement. If Shaco is immobilized before he can use Q to escape, he is easy to catch where he engaged.
shaco-situational-cc.text: Consider Quicksilver Sash when the enemy has plenty of crowd control that prevents movement. Q Deceive is Shaco’s only way out, so being immobilized before he can teleport leaves him easy to catch where he engaged.

shaco-skill-e.basis: While E is off cooldown, your basic attacks slow. When chasing an enemy, hold E to keep the slow on your basic attacks. E's active deals much more damage when the target is low on health. Use E to finish targets from range.
shaco-skill-e.text: While E Two-Shiv Poison is off cooldown, Shaco’s basic attacks slow. Hold it while chasing to keep that slow available, then use its active from range to finish a target whose low health makes it deal much more damage.

shaco-skill-passive.basis: P Backstab activates when you attack a target from behind. P Backstab applies to E as well as basic attacks. The lower the target's health, the more bonus damage P adds to E. Get behind the target to deal more damage.
shaco-skill-passive.text: P Backstab activates when Shaco attacks from behind and applies to E Two-Shiv Poison as well as basic attacks. Its bonus damage on E grows as the target’s health falls, so getting behind them directly increases Shaco’s damage.

shaco-skill-q.basis: Q provides a short teleport and invisibility. You can cross walls with Q. Your first basic attack during Q's invisibility is empowered. Your first basic attack from behind after Q is a critical strike. If you use Q to engage, its long cooldown makes it hard to use again to escape that fight. If you cannot secure the kill, save Q to escape. Turrets and true sight reveal Q's invisibility.
shaco-skill-q.text: Q Deceive gives Shaco a short teleport and invisibility, allowing him to cross walls and escape places that seem to have no exit. His first basic attack from stealth is empowered and critically strikes from behind, making Q an engage tool and the start of his burst. Its long cooldown leaves him without the same escape during that fight, so save it for disengaging unless you can secure the kill. Turrets and true sight reveal him while invisible.

shaco-skill-r.basis: Shaco briefly disappears while creating his clone with R. Use the moment Shaco disappears during R to dodge an enemy's targeted ability. The R clone takes increased damage and does not last long. The R clone explodes when it dies and leaves three small boxes that trigger immediately. The R clone applies on-hit effects. Control the R clone separately by holding Alt and right-clicking.
shaco-skill-r.text: Shaco briefly disappears while creating his R Hallucinate clone, which can let him dodge a targeted ability. The clone takes increased damage and does not last long, but on death it explodes and leaves three small boxes that trigger immediately. It also applies on-hit effects, so item choices affect its damage. Hold Alt and right-click to control it separately.

shaco-skill-w-objective.basis: Before starting Dragon or Rift Herald, place W at each entrance enemies could use. If an enemy jungler coming to steal an objective is feared by W, their Smite timing is disrupted. When W triggers, it warns you that an enemy is approaching. Delay starting the objective if you need time to place W.
shaco-skill-w-objective.text: Before starting Dragon or Rift Herald, place W Jack In The Box at every entrance enemies could use. Fear can throw off an enemy jungler’s Smite timing during a steal attempt, and a triggered box warns you of their approach. Delay the objective if you need more time to set up the boxes.

shaco-skill-w-vision.basis: W disappears from sight shortly after placement and lasts a long time. Place W early at entrances to your jungle, around objectives, and in bushes enemies may pass through to gain vision. Place W on an enemy's approach path to block their entry. Leveling W increases its fear duration against champions.
shaco-skill-w-vision.text: W Jack In The Box disappears from sight shortly after placement and lasts a long time, serving as both a trap and a source of vision. Set boxes in advance at entrances to your jungle, around objectives, and in bushes enemies may pass through to spot and block their approach. Leveling W also extends its fear against champions, making the investment more valuable if you plan to rely on boxes.

shaco-teamfight.basis: Avoid head-on teamfights. Shaco is fragile and can easily fall to a few area-of-effect abilities. Draw fights into areas where you have already placed W. Send the R clone ahead to draw attention, then target the enemy backline from the side. Engage when an enemy damage dealer steps forward.
shaco-teamfight.text: Avoid head-on teamfights: Shaco is fragile enough to fall to a few area-of-effect abilities. Draw the fight into an area where W Jack In The Box is already set, send the R Hallucinate clone ahead to draw attention, and approach the enemy backline from the side. Wait to engage until an enemy damage dealer steps forward.

shen-combo-basic.basis: The basic combo is Q, then E to taunt, followed by three basic attacks. Q empowers several of your next basic attacks instead of dealing immediate damage. After using Q, land your empowered basic attacks. Use Q before E to land empowered basic attacks during the taunt. Using Q and E in succession reduces the health you lose right after engaging through your passive shield.
shen-combo-basic.text: The basic combo is Q → E to taunt → three basic attacks. Q empowers several of Shen’s next basic attacks instead of dealing immediate damage, so using it and backing off deals almost none. Cast Q before E to spend the full taunt duration landing empowered attacks; casting both abilities also triggers the passive shield, reducing the health lost when you engage.

shen-laning.basis: Shen ranks near the bottom among top champions in CS and damage per minute. Get through lane safely and use R to help other lanes. Avoid risky trades so you have enough health to use R. Manage the wave safely during laning phase.
shen-laning.text: Shen is among the lowest of top lane champions in CS and damage per minute. Aim to get through lane evenly and use R to help other lanes win. Risky trades can leave you without enough health to use R when it matters, so manage the wave safely during laning phase.

shen-laning-energy.basis: Shen uses energy, which regenerates over time. Dealing damage with Q and E restores energy. Against mana users, take repeated short trades to drain their resources first.
shen-laning-energy.text: Shen uses energy, which regenerates over time, and dealing damage with Q and E restores it. Against mana users, repeated short trades favor Shen: their resources run low while his recover.

shen-laning-wave.basis: When Shen uses R to go to another lane, his own lane is left empty. If a fight looks likely in another lane, push the wave toward the enemy turret before using R. Using R without pushing the wave can cost you heavily in your own lane.
shen-laning-wave.text: Using R leaves Shen’s lane empty. If a fight looks likely elsewhere, push the wave toward the enemy turret beforehand to limit what you lose while away. An R without that preparation can save one ally at the cost of your lane.

shen-phase.basis: Shen is weakest at levels 1–5, when he lacks damage and mobility. From level 6, when Shen learns R, he can affect the entire map. After level 6, Shen's impact depends heavily on R's cooldown. Shen's real peak comes in the mid to late game as cooldown reduction builds up.
shen-phase.text: Shen is weakest at levels 1–5, when he lacks damage and mobility. Learning R at level 6 lets him affect the entire map; from then on, his impact follows R’s cooldown more than the state of his own lane. His real peak comes in the mid to late game as cooldown reduction builds up.

shen-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy's main damage is magic, W can block very little of it. If the enemy's main damage is magic, choose a magic resist item such as Bandlepipes as your third item.
shen-situational-mr.text: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, W can block very little of it. Choose a magic resistance item such as Bandlepipes for your third item to survive longer.

shen-situational-thornmail.basis: If the enemy's main damage is physical and relies heavily on basic attacks, buy Thornmail between core items. Because W blocks basic attacks, Thornmail adds defensive value against opponents who rely on them.
shen-situational-thornmail.text: If the enemy’s main damage is physical and comes from basic attacks, buy Thornmail between core items. Shen’s W (Spirit's Refuge) also blocks basic attacks, so the two provide overlapping defensive value against opponents who rely on them.

shen-skill-blade.basis: Shen's ability use depends heavily on the spirit blade's position. Q calls the spirit blade toward Shen, hitting enemies in its path. W's zone appears at the spirit blade's location. R moves Shen and the spirit blade together.
shen-skill-blade.text: Shen’s play revolves around the spirit blade’s position. Q calls it toward him and hits enemies in its path, W creates its zone where the blade is, and R moves Shen and the blade together. Always check where the blade is before deciding which ability to use.

shen-skill-e.basis: E taunts enemies and lets Shen move during fights. Save E to respond when an opponent engages. Engage with E first only when you are sure you can win. If E misses, it gives the opponent time to counterattack.
shen-skill-e.text: Shadow Dash (E) is both Shen’s taunt and his only mobility tool. Using it to engage leaves no way out, so generally save it to counter an opponent’s engage and go in first only when you are sure you can win. A missed E gives the opponent time to counterattack.

shen-skill-passive.basis: Shen gains his passive shield when he uses an ability. Hitting an allied or enemy champion with an ability reduces the cooldown of his passive shield. In lane, clip the enemy champion with Q to get your next shield sooner.
shen-skill-passive.text: Ki Barrier grants Shen a shield whenever he uses an ability, and hitting an allied or enemy champion with an ability reduces its cooldown. Keep landing abilities to sustain yourself; even clipping your lane opponent with Q brings the next shield back sooner.

shen-skill-q.basis: If the blade returning with Q hits an enemy champion, your empowered basic attacks deal more damage and your attack speed increases. When trading with a tank, position yourself so the blade passes through them. Q deals more damage to jungle monsters. Use Q to clear camps and objectives.
shen-skill-q.text: Twilight Assault (Q) deals far more damage when the returning blade passes through an enemy champion: its empowered basic attacks gain substantially more maximum health damage and attack speed. Position the blade to pass through your target when trading with a tank. Q also deals increased damage to jungle monsters, making it useful for camps and objectives.

shen-skill-r-shield.basis: R's shield grows the more health the targeted ally has lost. Use R after an ally starts taking damage. Before using R, judge whether the targeted ally can survive until the channel ends. R moves Shen to the targeted ally's location. If you decide to use R, tell the targeted ally to hold their position.
shen-skill-r-shield.text: Stand United (R) grants a larger shield the more health its target has lost, so use it after an ally starts taking damage rather than as soon as a fight begins. Before casting, judge whether they can survive the channel: if they die before it ends, nothing remains. Shen lands at the ally’s location, so a fleeing target can carry him somewhere unintended. Once you commit, tell the ally to hold their position.

shen-skill-w.basis: W blocks basic attacks but does not block ability damage. Use W against opponents who rely on basic attacks. If there is no allied champion to protect inside the zone, W takes a moment to activate. Do not cast W early where there is no champion to protect.
shen-skill-w.text: Spirit’s Refuge (W) blocks basic attacks, but ability damage passes through it. Use it against opponents who rely on basic attacks; placing it in front of allies against a mage will not help. If no allied champion is inside the zone to protect, it takes a moment to activate, so casting it early on an empty spot only wastes the cooldown.

shen-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use E to taunt enemies off your carries. Position the spirit blade so W's zone appears around your carries. In teamfights, position yourself to protect your backline rather than engage forward. Do not get tied up in a separate 1v1 during a teamfight.
shen-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Shen’s job is to turn back an enemy engage rather than deal damage. Use E to taunt enemies off your carries and position the spirit blade so W’s zone protects them. Stay back to guard your team’s backline; accepting a separate 1v1 leaves it exposed.

shyvana-combo-clear.basis: At jungle camps, detonate E on the large monster as you approach, then activate W and follow with a Q-empowered auto attack. Stay close to the monster while the shield lasts so the W explosion hits the camp. Jungle monsters do not run away, so you can use W's full duration.
shyvana-combo-clear.text: Start a jungle camp by detonating E Molten Burst on the large monster, then close in, activate W Inferno Aegis, and follow with a Q Emberstrike empowered auto attack. W is especially effective in the jungle because monsters do not run away and take its full duration; stay close while the shield lasts so its explosion also hits the camp.

shyvana-combo-gank.basis: For ganks after level 6, pass through the enemy with R, hit them with E as they retreat, and finish with a Q empowered auto attack. You are unstoppable during R's movement, so enemy crowd control cannot interrupt your engage.
shyvana-combo-gank.text: After level 6, gank by passing through the enemy with R Dragon's Descent, then slow them with E as they retreat and finish with a Q empowered auto attack. R makes you unstoppable during its movement, so you can push through a narrow approach even if the enemy support has crowd control ready.

shyvana-combo-w-recast.basis: Reactivating W makes it explode before its duration ends. If the enemy looks likely to escape before the shield expires, reactivate W as soon as you reach them. If the enemy stays close, delay the W explosion to use the movement speed boost longer. In dragon form, the W explosion heals you only if it hits a champion.
shyvana-combo-w-recast.text: Reactivating W Inferno Aegis makes it explode immediately. If an enemy looks likely to escape before the shield expires, reactivate it as soon as you reach them; if they stay close, delay the explosion to keep the movement speed boost longer. In dragon form, the explosion heals you only when it hits a champion, making its timing vital to your survival.

shyvana-jungle-path.basis: At level 5 or below, Shyvana has no immobilizing crowd control, so her ganks are less likely to succeed. Early on, use your fast movement between camps to scale through full clears and invasions of camps on the opposite side. Start looking for committed ganks once you have R.
shyvana-jungle-path.text: At level 5 or below, Shyvana has no immobilizing crowd control, so her ganks are less likely to succeed. Her movement speed is among the highest and W makes travel between camps even faster, so focus early on full clears and invading camps on the opposite side to build a lead. Begin ganking in earnest once you have R.

shyvana-phase.basis: Levels 1–5 are a farming phase with weak ganks because Shyvana has no crowd control. Once you get R at level 6, you can start fights. Shyvana peaks in the mid game when she has attack speed and core items. Late in the game, she gets taken down early in teamfights if P stacks and defensive items do not make up for her low health growth.
shyvana-phase.text: Levels 1–5 are a farming phase with weak ganks because Shyvana has no crowd control. At level 6, R gives her engage and area damage, allowing her to start fights for the first time. She peaks in the mid game with attack speed and core items, but her low health growth leaves her fragile late in the game; without enough P Scalemail stacks and defensive items, she can be taken down first in teamfights.

shyvana-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Shyvana stays close and attacks for a long time, making her weak against sustained enemy healing. Shyvana's abilities do not apply Grievous Wounds.
shyvana-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Shyvana stays close and attacks for a long time, so sustained enemy healing prolongs trades, and none of her abilities apply Grievous Wounds.

shyvana-skill-e.basis: In human form, E stops and explodes on the first enemy it hits. To target a champion behind minions, fire E from the side to avoid the minion wave. In dragon form, E's enlarged fireball passes through enemies and leaves flames in its path. When enemies line up in a narrow passage, hit several of them with dragon form E.
shyvana-skill-e.text: In human form, E Molten Burst stops and explodes on the first enemy it hits, so fire from the side to reach a champion behind a minion wave. In dragon form, the fireball grows larger, passes through enemies, and leaves flames in its path. Use it when enemies line up in a narrow passage to slow several of them and deal damage based on their maximum health at once.

shyvana-skill-passive.basis: Participating in a champion, large minion, or large monster takedown permanently stacks P's armor and magic resistance. P stacks persist through death. Shyvana has low health growth late in the game, so she becomes less durable without enough P stacks.
shyvana-skill-passive.text: Participating in a champion, large minion, or large monster takedown permanently adds armor and magic resistance through P Scalemail. The stacks persist through death, so even one extra camp early becomes durability later. Shyvana has very low health growth by level 18 and becomes fragile late in the game without enough stacks.

shyvana-skill-q.basis: Q empowers your next auto attack. Press Q in time with an auto attack so you do not waste it. Each auto attack that hits reduces Q's cooldown, making attack speed valuable for Shyvana. When targeting a single champion in dragon form, save Q's extra cast.
shyvana-skill-q.text: Q Emberstrike empowers your next auto attack, so press it in time with the attack to avoid wasting it. Each auto attack that hits reduces Q's cooldown, which makes attack speed especially valuable for Shyvana. In dragon form, Q gains an extra cast that bites a single target; save that cast when focusing one champion.

shyvana-skill-r-fury.basis: R becomes available through the Fury gauge instead of a cooldown. Auto attacks and ability hits build Fury. Area damage against non-champion targets generates much less Fury. Fury fills much faster in dragon form. Fill your Fury gauge before an objective fight.
shyvana-skill-r-fury.text: R becomes available through Shyvana’s Fury gauge instead of a cooldown. Basic attacks and ability hits build Fury, but area damage against non-champions generates much less, while Fury builds much faster in dragon form. Clearing camps with area damage alone delays R, so mix in champion fights or single-target basic attacks to have it ready on time. Fill the gauge before an objective fight.

shyvana-skill-r-timing.basis: Generally, use R at the start of a fight to benefit from empowered abilities and bonus health throughout it. If the enemy has reliable engage crowd control, you can save R to push through it. Fighting without transforming greatly reduces Shyvana's damage and durability.
shyvana-skill-r-timing.text: R serves both as an engage tool and as a period when Shyvana cannot be stopped. Generally, use it at the start of a fight to benefit from empowered abilities and bonus health throughout the fight. If the enemy has reliable crowd control to start an engagement, saving R to push through that ability is also reasonable. Without transforming, Shyvana’s damage and durability are both cut in half, so the worst outcome is holding R and never using it.
