shyvana-skill-w.basis: W grants a shield and increases your movement speed more as you get closer to enemy champions. When ganking, activate W first to close the gap. W's shield absorbs more damage based on the number of nearby enemy champions.
shyvana-skill-w.text: W Inferno Aegis grants a shield and movement speed that increases as you get closer to enemy champions. Activate it first when approaching a gank, since it speeds you up more while closing in than while escaping. Its shield also absorbs more damage for each nearby enemy champion, making it especially useful when entering a group.

shyvana-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, choose an entry angle that puts several enemies in R's path. Stand among enemy champions so dragon form W's explosion hits several of them. Use the piercing E when enemies group together. Use R on enemies after an ally applies crowd control.
shyvana-teamfight.text: In teamfights, choose an entry angle that puts several enemies in R's path instead of heading straight for an enemy damage dealer. Stand among champions so dragon form W's explosion hits them and heals you, while piercing E gains value when enemies group together. Shyvana has no way to hold enemies in place, so let an ally apply crowd control before following up with R.

singed-combo-flash-fling.basis: Press E during Flash to Fling the enemy as soon as you arrive. Combining Flash and E lets you force an engage despite E's short range. Use the Flash–E combo only for fights you can win.
singed-combo-flash-fling.text: Flash turns the short-range E Fling into a way to force an engage. Press E during Flash so the Fling goes off as soon as Singed arrives, leaving the enemy no time to react. This is his only way to force an initiation, so use it only for fights you can win.

singed-combo-fling-glue.basis: Fling the enemy behind you with E, then place W where they land to root them. If you place W first, the enemy can back out of the adhesive.
singed-combo-fling-glue.text: The key combo is to use E Fling to throw the enemy behind Singed, then place W Mega Adhesive where they will land; they must land on it to be rooted. Placing W first gives them time to see it coming and retreat, so covering the landing spot after the throw is much more reliable. Since Fling sends the target behind Singed, check which way he is facing before using it.

singed-combo-tower.basis: Near a turret, use E to throw the enemy into turret range, then place W on top of them. Placing W on an enemy inside turret range makes it take longer for them to escape, so they take more turret shots.
singed-combo-tower.text: Near a turret, use E Fling to throw an enemy into its range, then place W Mega Adhesive on them. They must walk out, and the adhesive delays their escape long enough for the turret to hit them several times.

singed-laning-proxy.basis: In lane, focus on keeping your opponent tied to the lane rather than killing them. Push a wave into the enemy turret, then clear the next wave behind it with Q. Clearing the next wave behind the turret keeps the enemy in lane while your teammates can move. Go behind the turret just after the enemy jungler is spotted on the other side of the map.
singed-laning-proxy.text: In lane, aim to keep your opponent there rather than beat them directly. Push a wave into the enemy turret, then go behind it and clear the next wave with Q Poison Trail; the opponent cannot leave lane while your teammates are free to move. Go behind the turret just after the enemy jungler is spotted on the other side of the map, since doing so without knowing their location can get you caught.

singed-laning-trade.basis: Pass by the enemy with Q active to lay poison, then Fling them with E if they stand their ground. Don't stand still and trade basic attacks with the enemy. Look for an E right after the enemy uses their escape ability to clear the wave or for another purpose. If the enemy still has their escape ability, they can get away immediately after you Fling them with E.
singed-laning-trade.text: For a trade, pass by the enemy with Q Poison Trail active to lay poison, then use E Fling to catch them if they stand their ground. Singed loses if he stands still and trades basic attacks. Wait until the enemy has used their escape ability to clear a wave or for another purpose; if it is still available, they can get away immediately after the Fling.

singed-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Singed only has Q, so his damage is low and he runs out of mana quickly. At level 3, Singed can combine W and E, giving him his first chance to catch an enemy. At level 6, R completes Singed's ability to escape and lure enemies. After getting two core items, Singed can withstand multiple enemies while pushing the lane. Singed falls off late if he hasn't completed his items.
singed-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Singed has only Q Poison Trail, so his damage is low and he runs out of mana quickly. At level 3, W Mega Adhesive enables a combo with E Fling and gives him his first chance to catch an enemy; at level 6, R Insanity Potion completes his ability to escape and lure opponents. With two core items, he can keep pushing the lane and survive even when three enemies come for him, making this his most troublesome period. His health growth is relatively low later on, though, so he loses strength if time passes without more items.

singed-situational-armor.basis: If most of the enemy's damage is physical, build armor first. Dead Man's Plate provides armor and movement effects that suit catching enemies and running around. Build Plated Steelcaps early to survive against enemies who rely on basic attacks.
singed-situational-armor.text: If most enemy damage is physical, build armor first. Dead Man's Plate provides armor and movement effects that suit catching enemies and running around, while buying Plated Steelcaps early helps you survive against opponents who rely on basic attacks.

singed-situational-tenacity.basis: Choose Quicksilver Sash if the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities. Singed must keep moving to survive and cannot directly remove crowd control with his abilities.
singed-situational-tenacity.text: Choose Quicksilver Sash if the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities. Singed needs to keep moving to survive, being held in place can mean death, and none of his abilities can directly remove crowd control.

singed-skill-e.basis: E deals damage based on maximum health, so it hurts tanky enemies too. Fling the enemy carry toward your team with E. Use E to throw back an enemy attacking your carry. Before using E, check whether the direction you'll throw the enemy favors you. If the enemy is already in the middle of your team, avoid using E to throw them to safety.
singed-skill-e.text: E Fling deals damage based on maximum health, so it hurts tanky enemies, but its real value is repositioning them. Throw an enemy carry toward your team or move an enemy attacking your carry away from them. Check where the target will land first: if they are already surrounded by your team, a Fling could send them to safety.

singed-skill-passive.basis: P grants movement speed when you pass through allied or enemy champions. P has a separate cooldown for each champion. Zigzag through a group of champions to refresh P's movement speed bonus.
singed-skill-passive.text: P Noxious Slipstream grants movement speed whenever Singed passes through an allied or enemy champion. Its cooldown is separate for each champion, so zigzagging through a group keeps refreshing the speed bonus. Diving into the middle of the enemy team may look reckless, but it is the route that makes him fastest.

singed-skill-q.basis: Q toggles on and off and has no cooldown, but drains mana continuously while active. Q leaves poison behind Singed in the direction he moves. With Q active, keep moving and lead the enemy along a path where they'll step in the poison. Turn off Q after the fight to save mana.
singed-skill-q.text: Q Poison Trail toggles on and off and has no cooldown, but drains mana continuously while active. It leaves poison behind Singed, so standing still accomplishes nothing. Keep moving and guide enemies along a path they want to take through the poison, then turn Q off after the fight to save mana.

singed-skill-r.basis: While R is active, Q's poison reduces healing. Activate R and move as if fleeing to lure the enemy into Q's poison. Use R when an enemy chases Singed because he looks low on health.
singed-skill-r.text: R Insanity Potion raises several stats at once and makes Q Poison Trail reduce healing for its duration. Activate it to draw enemies through your poison while appearing to flee, especially when Singed looks close to death and they start chasing.

singed-skill-w.basis: W slows enemies and prevents them from using movement abilities. Against an enemy escaping with a movement ability, place W along their expected escape path. Rather than saving W, throw it when you read where the enemy will retreat.
singed-skill-w.text: W Mega Adhesive slows enemies, but its main value is preventing movement abilities. Against someone with a dash or blink to escape, placing it on their escape path can shut that ability down. Its cooldown is fairly short, so read where the enemy will retreat and throw it there instead of saving it.

singed-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, your role is to disrupt the enemy formation. Activate Q, run through the enemy team, refresh your speed with P, then Fling the enemy carry toward your team with E. Keep moving after the Fling so multiple enemies chase Singed. Stay alive as long as possible while they chase.
singed-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Singed's job is to disrupt the enemy formation rather than deal damage. Activate Q Poison Trail, run through their team, keep refreshing your speed with P Noxious Slipstream, and use E Fling to throw an enemy carry toward your allies. Keep moving afterward so several enemies chase you; the longer you stay alive while drawing them away, the easier the fight becomes for your team.

sion-combo-engage.basis: When engaging, follow the stun from R's collision with Q, W, then E. After R stuns, charge Q only long enough to knock the target up, then land it. Activate W's shield just before engaging. Detonate W after the opponents group up.
sion-combo-engage.text: When engaging, follow R's collision stun with Q, W, then E. There usually is not enough time to charge Q fully before the stun ends, so release it as soon as it gains the knockup to make sure it lands. Activate W's shield just before engaging, then detonate it once the opponents group up.

sion-combo-setup.basis: For basic poke, slow the target with E, then land Q. Use E to set up Q. If you start Q without E, the opponent has plenty of time to see it and walk out.
sion-combo-setup.text: For basic poke, use E to slow the target, then land Q. The slow keeps them from escaping even if you charge Q fully, so treat E as setup for Q rather than a damage skill. Without E, the opponent has plenty of time to see Q coming and walk out.

sion-laning.basis: At 14 minutes, Sion is among the champions with the fewest kills and the fewest deaths. In lane, focus on farming safely and stacking maximum health with W rather than getting kills. Use E to push minions into the opponent for poke. In lane, use Q when the opponent is immobilized. Even if you lose a trade, secure CS and turret plates.
sion-laning.text: At 14 minutes, Sion ranks among the champions with the fewest kills and deaths, so focus on safe farming and stacking maximum health through W rather than chasing kills in lane. Push minions into opponents with E to poke, use Q only when they are immobilized, and prioritize CS and turret plates even if you lose a trade.

sion-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Sion struggles to apply pressure with just one ability. His first power spike comes at level 6, after putting points into Q and unlocking R. Sion is strongest in the mid to late game, when the maximum health stacked through W combines with defensive items. In the mid to late game, his revival passive lets him effectively fight twice even if he dies. If he falls far behind early, he lacks the damage to turn things around on his own.
sion-phase.text: Sion struggles to apply pressure with a single ability at levels 1–2. His first power spike comes at level 6, after investing points in Q and unlocking R. He is strongest in the mid to late game, when the maximum health gained through W combines with defensive items; even if he dies, Glory in Death effectively lets him fight twice. If he falls far behind early, he lacks the damage to turn things around on his own.

sion-situational-spirit.basis: If most enemy damage is magic, choose Spirit Visage as a defensive item. Spirit Visage amplifies W's shield and Sion's life steal during his revival.
sion-situational-spirit.text: If most enemy damage is magic, choose Spirit Visage as a defensive item. Its healing and shield amplification benefits both W's shield and Sion's life steal during his revival, giving it value beyond its defensive stats.

sion-situational-thornmail.basis: If an enemy physical damage dealer is sustaining through healing, build Thornmail earlier. Sion takes hits on the frontline, making it easy to keep applying Thornmail's reflected damage and healing reduction.
sion-situational-thornmail.text: If an enemy physical damage dealer is sustaining through healing, build Thornmail earlier. Sion already takes hits on the frontline, putting him in an easy position to keep applying its reflected damage and healing reduction.

sion-skill-e.basis: E stops at the first target it hits, but pushes a minion or monster backward if it hits one. Enemies struck by a unit pushed by E take the same damage and effects. In lane, use E to push a minion toward the opponent and hit them. When engaging with an allied physical damage dealer, use E first to reduce the target's armor.
sion-skill-e.text: E stops at the first target it hits, but striking a minion or monster pushes that unit back and applies the same damage and effects to enemies it hits. Pushing a minion into your opponent is Sion's main lane poke. E also reduces armor, so use it first when engaging alongside an allied physical damage dealer.

sion-skill-passive.basis: During his post-death revival, all abilities are replaced by one, his attack speed and life steal increase greatly, and his hits deal damage based on maximum health. Before dying, decide what to do during the revival. During the revival, attack a turret, push a wave, or buy time for allies to retreat.
sion-skill-passive.text: During his post-death revival, Sion's abilities are replaced by a single ability, his attack speed and life steal rise sharply, and his hits deal damage based on maximum health. Decide what to do before you die: usually attack a turret, push out a wave, or buy time for allies to retreat.

sion-skill-q-charge.basis: Q deals more damage the longer you charge it. After charging for a while, Q knocks enemies up; charging it longer also stuns them. Sion cannot move while charging Q, so opponents can walk out of its range. Aim for a fully charged Q when the opponent is already immobilized.
sion-skill-q-charge.text: Q deals more damage the longer you charge it, gaining a knockup after a certain point and a stun with further charge. Sion cannot move while charging, so opponents can walk out; in lane, releasing Q as soon as it gains the knockup is often the right call. A full charge is worthwhile only when the opponent is already immobilized.

sion-skill-q-target.basis: Q deals reduced damage to minions and greatly increased damage to jungle monsters. Use Q to pressure objectives and the jungle. When taking a large monster with your jungler, save Q for it.
sion-skill-q-target.text: Q deals reduced damage to minions but greatly increased damage to jungle monsters, making it useful for pressuring objectives and the jungle rather than pushing waves. When taking a large monster with your jungler, save Q for it to speed up the clear noticeably.

sion-skill-r.basis: Sion is unstoppable while charging with R, but can only steer a little. Use R on straight paths and avoid curved ones. R deals more damage and stuns longer the farther Sion travels. Recast R to stop before colliding with the wrong target. R also stops when it hits a wall.
sion-skill-r.text: Sion is unstoppable during R, but its limited steering makes straight paths the best approach; avoid winding routes and walls, which stop the charge. Damage and stun duration increase with distance, so start from far away, and remember that you can recast R to stop before hitting the wrong target.

sion-skill-w.basis: After activating its shield, you can recast W a short time later to detonate it. Watch the shield indicator and detonate W just before the shield expires. W's passive permanently increases your maximum health each time you kill a unit. Last-hit units to build up maximum health.
sion-skill-w.text: W is a two-stage ability: it grants a shield that you can detonate with a recast after a short delay. Watch the indicator for how much shield remains and detonate it just before it disappears to get both protection and damage. Its passive also permanently increases your maximum health whenever you kill a unit, so securing last hits helps you scale.

sion-teamfight-engage.basis: Start R from fog of war or behind a wall, where the opponent cannot see you. Use R to charge toward the enemy backline. Before using R, check that your allies are close enough to follow.
sion-teamfight-engage.text: Start R from fog of war or behind a wall and charge toward the enemy backline; a charge from straight ahead gives opponents time to sidestep. Check that your allies are close enough to follow, because arriving alone means landing one stun and dying.

sion-teamfight-role.basis: In teamfights, use E from the frontline to reduce enemy armor. In teamfights, keep enemies pinned down with Q's area stun and W's explosion. In teamfights, fall in a position that blocks enemies from reaching your damage dealers. The revival is especially valuable around objectives, so avoid dying without a reason.
sion-teamfight-role.text: In teamfights, hold the frontline, reduce enemy armor with E, and keep opponents pinned down with Q's area stun and W's explosion. Since his passive lets him fight again after death, Sion is better off falling while blocking the path to his damage dealers than retreating to survive. That revival is most valuable around objectives, though, so dying without a reason still puts your team behind.

sivir-combo-r.basis: After activating R, each basic attack against a champion reduces your basic abilities' cooldowns. A takedown resets R's duration.
sivir-combo-r.text: After activating R On The Hunt, each basic attack against a champion reduces your basic abilities’ cooldowns, so keep attacking to bring Q Boomerang Blade and W Ricochet back faster than usual. A takedown resets R’s duration; keep R active and continue basic attacking until you’re sure the teamfight is over.

sivir-combo-w-reset.basis: Activating W resets your basic attack timer. Activate W right after a basic attack, then immediately attack again. Do not activate W early while waiting.
sivir-combo-w-reset.text: Activating W Ricochet resets Sivir’s basic attack timer, so use it right after an attack to land a second one immediately. Make basic attack → W → basic attack a habit, and don’t activate W in advance while waiting.

sivir-combo-wave.basis: To clear a wave, activate W, attack the front minions, then finish with Q. Q deals less damage with each non-champion target it hits in sequence. Q's sequential damage reduction resets on its return. Throw Q so both its outgoing and return paths overlap the minion wave.
sivir-combo-wave.text: To clear a wave, activate W Ricochet and attack a front minion to start the bounces, then finish with Q Boomerang Blade. Q deals progressively less damage to non-champion targets, but that reduction resets on its return, so line up both paths with the minion wave to hit it twice.

sivir-laning.basis: Push the lane to keep your opponent under their turret and damage its plates. Save E to block the enemy jungler's engage ability.
sivir-laning.text: Sivir clears waves faster than almost any bot lane duo. Push your opponents under their turret and take its plates, but secure river vision first because pushing leaves you exposed to ganks. Save E Spell Shield for the enemy jungler’s engage ability.

sivir-laning-e-bait.basis: Activate E when the actual ability comes in, not when your opponent starts the engage animation. If you are unsure when to block with E, back away. Sivir is easy to kill if caught while E is down.
sivir-laning-e-bait.text: Opponents may feint an engage to draw out E Spell Shield. Use it when an ability actually comes toward you, rather than at the first sign of an engage; if you are unsure, back away. Sivir is easy to kill if caught while E is down, and opponents know it.

sivir-objective.basis: A Sivir composition wins through sieging. Clear waves quickly to keep your opponents under their turret. Use R to get your team onto the turret and push it down. If your opponents leave the turret, use R to retreat.
sivir-objective.text: A Sivir composition wins through sieging. Clear waves quickly to pin opponents under their turret, then use R On The Hunt to bring your team forward and take it. If the opponents come out, use R to retreat; this gives Sivir’s team the first move during a standoff around an objective.

sivir-phase.basis: Q costs Sivir a lot of mana, making extended laning difficult. Sivir's wave clear is among the best. Learning R at level 6 lets you help your team engage and disengage. Sivir is strongest during midgame sieges once she has attack speed and critical strike. Sivir has no dash, making her weak in late-game duels.
sivir-phase.text: Sivir’s high Q mana cost makes extended laning difficult, though her wave clear is among the best. At level 6, R On The Hunt lets her team engage or disengage, and she is strongest during midgame sieges once she has attack speed and critical strike. With no dash, she is weak in late-game duels, so look for larger fights where she can maintain her range.

sivir-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling after one core item. W's bounces can spread Grievous Wounds to multiple opponents.
sivir-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner’s Calling after one core item. W Ricochet can bounce across multiple opponents, spreading Grievous Wounds through their team.

sivir-skill-e.basis: E is Sivir's only defensive tool. Use E to block roots or stuns rather than poke. Blocking an ability with E restores health and triggers the passive movement speed. Counterattack immediately after blocking an ability with E.
sivir-skill-e.text: E Spell Shield is Sivir’s only defensive tool. Save it for abilities that root or stun you instead of spending it on poke. A successful block restores health and triggers the movement speed from Fleet of Foot, making that the moment to counterattack.

sivir-skill-passive.basis: Each time you damage an enemy champion, your passive movement speed increases sharply. Sivir has no dash, so she relies on her passive movement speed to dodge. Reposition with your passive movement speed right after landing Q or a basic attack.
sivir-skill-passive.text: Fleet of Foot sharply increases Sivir’s movement speed whenever she damages an enemy champion. She has no dash, so use that speed to dodge: reposition immediately after landing Q or a basic attack, moving between attacks.

sivir-skill-q.basis: Q returns to Sivir when it reaches maximum range. After throwing Q, move sideways to hit your opponent on its return path. In lane, do not waste the mana-heavy Q.
sivir-skill-q.text: Q Boomerang Blade returns to Sivir at maximum range. Move sideways after throwing it to change its return path and hit an opponent who dodged it on the way out. Its high mana cost makes a missed Q especially costly in lane.

sivir-skill-r.basis: R increases the movement speed of your entire team. Activate R when your team engages or retreats. Before using R, check that your teammates are grouped.
sivir-skill-r.text: R On The Hunt speeds up your entire team: activate it as your allies engage or retreat. Using it just to escape alone wastes its value, so check that your teammates are grouped first.

sivir-skill-w.basis: W-empowered attacks prioritize targets they have not hit yet. W-empowered attacks bounce to each target only a set number of times. Even if you hit the enemy front line with W, the damage reaches the back line. When you do not want to push the lane, do not attack minions with W active.
sivir-skill-w.text: W Ricochet prioritizes targets its bounces have not hit yet and can bounce to each target only a set number of times. Attacking the enemy front line can therefore damage the back line too. Low-health minions die immediately to it, so avoid attacking minions with W active when you don’t want to push the lane.

sivir-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay in the back line and hit the enemy front line with W. Hitting the front line with W lets the bouncing attacks reach the back line. Activate R when your team signals an engage or retreat. After activating R, keep attacking to reduce Q and W's cooldowns.
sivir-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay in the back line and attack the enemy front line with W Ricochet. Its bounces reach the back line, so there’s no need to overextend to hit enemy damage dealers directly. Activate R On The Hunt when your team signals an engage or retreat, then keep attacking to reduce Q and W’s cooldowns.

skarner-combo-engage.basis: Activate Q before engaging, use E to push the target into a wall and stun them, then land a Q-empowered basic attack. When your allies close in, pull the target with R. Activate Q in advance near a minion or jungle monster so you can land empowered basic attacks immediately after engaging.
skarner-combo-engage.text: Before engaging, activate Q on a minion or jungle monster so you can land empowered basic attacks immediately instead of spending time casting it after you enter. Charge through terrain with E, drag the target into a wall to stun them, and stack Quaking with Q-empowered basic attacks during the stun. As your allies close in, suppress the target with R and pull them toward your team.

skarner-combo-r-turn.basis: Targets suppressed by R are dragged in the direction Skarner moves. To pull a target farther into your team's position, turn around just before R ends.
skarner-combo-r-turn.text: Targets suppressed by Skarner’s R are dragged in the direction he moves. Just before it ends, turn back the other way: the target shifts to the opposite side of his model, extending the drag once more. Always use this final turn when pulling someone deep into your team.

skarner-laning-gank.basis: When ganking, choose the wall first, then approach from the opposite side with E to push the target into it. E cannot stun in an open area without a wall. When ganking in an open area, use Q's slow and your allies' crowd control. Delay ganks in lanes where you cannot line up a wall hit until after level 6.
skarner-laning-gank.text: For the strongest gank, choose the wall you want to hit, then enter from the opposite side with E and push the target into it. E cannot stun in open ground, so there you must rely on Q's slow and your allies' crowd control. Delay ganks in lanes without a wall angle until after level 6.

skarner-laning-path.basis: Skarner's early jungle path is not focused on getting kills. Early on, clear camps safely to gain levels and items, then take control of objectives. When counterjungling out of enemy vision, use E routes that cross walls.
skarner-laning-path.text: Skarner's early jungle route is not built around kills: his kills at 14 minutes and damage per minute rank near the bottom, while his death statistic ranks near the top. Clear camps safely to gain levels and items, then take control of objectives. E routes through walls also help you avoid enemy vision when counterjungling.

skarner-phase.basis: Before level 6, Skarner's ganks work when E can slam the target into a wall. From level 6, R's suppression lets you gank regardless of terrain. Skarner grows stronger as he gets items because Q and E scale with health and W's shield scales with maximum health.
skarner-phase.text: Before level 6, Skarner can stun during a gank only if E slams the target into a wall. Once R becomes available at level 6, its guaranteed suppression makes ganks possible in any lane regardless of terrain. Q and E scale with health, while W grants a shield based on maximum health, so defensive items also increase his damage. Win rates rise sharply once three core items are completed; the more time Skarner has to build, the stronger he gets.

skarner-skill-e.basis: E passes through terrain and drags a champion or large monster it hits until the charge ends. You must hit a wall with the target you drag using E to stun them. When engaging with E, line up your approach so a wall is behind the target. Hitting a target against a wall with E greatly reduces its cooldown. If E cannot hit a wall, recast it to end the charge early.
skarner-skill-e.text: E charges through terrain and drags any champion or large monster it catches until the charge ends. To stun the target, you must slam into a wall together, so approach with the wall behind them. A successful wall hit greatly reduces E's cooldown, letting you use it again soon; if the angle is unavailable, recast E to end the charge early and limit the loss.

skarner-skill-passive.basis: Basic attacks, Q, and R stack Quaking. At maximum stacks, Quaking deals magic damage based on the target's maximum health. In teamfights, stack Quaking on high-health frontline champions too. Quaking stacks have a duration. Once you stick to a target, don't switch targets midway.
skarner-skill-passive.text: Basic attacks, Q, and R stack Quaking, which deals magic damage based on the target's maximum health at full stacks. That makes it worthwhile to stack on high-health frontline champions in teamfights. Since stacks expire, stay on the same target once you commit.

skarner-skill-q.basis: Activating Q empowers your next basic attacks and increases attack speed. The final hit carries the maximum health damage and slow. Recasting Q gives up the remaining empowered hits to throw a rock and deal damage from range. If you are in range of the target, land all of Q's empowered basic attacks. If the target has already escaped basic attack range, recast Q to throw the rock.
skarner-skill-q.text: Activating Q empowers your next few basic attacks and increases attack speed, with the final hit delivering the maximum-health-based damage and slow. Recasting it gives up the remaining hits to throw a rock that deals the same damage at range. If you can stay in basic attack range, land every empowered hit; throw the rock only after the target escapes that range.

skarner-skill-r-mechanic.basis: Most mobility abilities and Cleanse cannot break R's suppression. R is not a channel, so stuns and silences cannot interrupt it. Quicksilver Sash and Mercurial Scimitar remove R's suppression. Before using R, check whether the target has Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar. Use R to pull enemies standing at the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit into the pit.
skarner-skill-r-mechanic.text: R suppresses its target, so most mobility abilities and Cleanse cannot free them; because it is not a channel, stuns and silences cannot interrupt it either. Quicksilver Sash and Mercurial Scimitar can remove the suppression, so check the target's build before casting. R can also drag enemies across terrain, including from the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit into the pit.

skarner-skill-r-target.basis: R suppresses multiple targets hit in front of Skarner at once. To stop an enemy engage, suppress the champion coming in with R. Use R to pull an enemy away from your carry. Before a fight, decide whether to use R to stop an engage or protect your carry.
skarner-skill-r-target.text: R can suppress multiple targets in front of Skarner at once, but choose whom to catch. Suppressing an enemy engage champion stops their team's initiation, while pulling an enemy off your carry protects your damage dealer. Decide which use you need before the fight so you do not waste R in a rush.

skarner-skill-w.basis: W grants a shield based on Skarner's maximum health and slows nearby enemies in an area. Use W just before enemy damage lands or when you're already caught. Health items also increase W's shield.
skarner-skill-w.text: W grants a shield based on Skarner’s maximum health and slows nearby enemies. Its short duration means casting it before engaging can leave you without a shield when the damage lands, so use it just before taking a hit or when you’ve already been caught. Health items increase the shield, letting tank items improve both defense and damage.

skarner-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, engage from the front and use R to pull one key target toward your team. Engage when your carry is positioned to damage the R target immediately. If your carry cannot damage the R target immediately, hold R and buy time with Q's slow and W.
skarner-teamfight.text: In teamfights, engage from the front to isolate a target rather than deal damage. Pull a key enemy toward your team with R to create a temporary numbers advantage, but commit only when your carry can damage that target immediately. Otherwise, hold R and buy time with Q's slow and W.

smolder-combo-escape.basis: When escaping, slow the enemy with W, cross a wall with E, and heal with R if needed. Choose where to go before crossing a wall with E. If E stops ignoring terrain halfway through a wall, you can get stuck.
smolder-combo-escape.text: To escape, slow the enemy with W, fly over a wall with E, then cast R beneath yourself for healing if needed. Decide which way you'll cross the wall beforehand: E ignores terrain only briefly, and you can get stuck if that effect ends halfway through.

smolder-combo-trade.basis: Look for a W hit before trading damage. If W misses, give up the trade and back off.
smolder-combo-trade.text: Start a trade by landing W (Achooo!) to gain a stack, then follow up with Q (Super Scorcher Breath) and a basic attack. Since Q is targeted and guaranteed to hit, use the less reliable W first to check for an opening before moving in. If W misses, give up the trade and back off.

smolder-laning-wave.basis: Before Q's first evolution, you have virtually no way to push the wave. Before Q's first evolution, let the wave come toward your tower and last hit there. Once Q starts damaging enemies around its target, faster waveclear gives you lane priority. When you gain lane priority, secure vision and objectives.
smolder-laning-wave.text: Before Q's first evolution, you have virtually no way to push a wave, so let it come toward your tower and last hit there. Once Q starts damaging enemies around its target, faster waveclear gives you lane priority; use that opening to secure vision and objectives.

smolder-phase.basis: Smolder is weakest at levels 1–2 and early on when he has few stacks. Smolder gets noticeably stronger each time Q evolves. Smolder becomes powerful late in the game as he gains both stacks and items. The further behind you are, the more you should favor farming for stacks over fighting.
smolder-phase.text: Smolder is weakest at levels 1–2 and early on with few stacks. He grows noticeably stronger with each Q evolution and becomes a hypercarry late in the game as stacks and items accumulate. You can catch up by continuing to stack even when behind, so the further behind you are, the more you should favor farming over fighting.

smolder-skill-e.basis: E lets you fly over terrain. E automatically attacks the enemy with the lowest health. You cannot choose E's target directly. E is Smolder's only escape tool and way to cross walls. Save E for potential ganks instead of using it to attack first.
smolder-skill-e.text: E lets Smolder fly over terrain while automatically attacking the enemy with the lowest health. You cannot choose its target, so the enemy you want to hit must have the lowest health. As Smolder's only practical escape and way to cross walls, E should be saved for potential ganks instead of used early for damage.

smolder-skill-passive.basis: Hitting a champion with an ability grants a Dragon Practice stack. Killing an enemy with Q grants a Dragon Practice stack. Dragon Practice stacks never expire. Even if you fall behind in lane, don't miss Q last hits.
smolder-skill-passive.text: Dragon Practice stacks when you hit a champion with an ability or kill an enemy with Q, and those stacks never expire. Every Q last hit is permanent growth, making each minion more valuable to Smolder than to most marksmen; even if you fall behind in lane, don't miss one.

smolder-skill-q-evolve.basis: Q evolves whenever Dragon Practice reaches certain stack thresholds. Before its first evolution, Q damages only one target. After its first evolution, Q's damage spreads around the target. After its next evolution, Q's explosions travel beyond the target. After its final evolution, Q burns the target, dealing damage based on their maximum health over time. Each Q evolution greatly improves waveclear and teamfight impact.
smolder-skill-q-evolve.text: Q evolves at certain Dragon Practice stack thresholds: it starts as single-target damage, then spreads damage around its target, sends explosions beyond the target, and finally burns the target for damage based on their maximum health over time. Each evolution brings a sharp increase in waveclear and teamfight impact, so the stacks remaining until the next one are a measure of your progress.

smolder-skill-q-mana.basis: Killing a target with Q refunds mana. Using Q repeatedly only on champions drains mana quickly. Harass with Q between minion last hits to recover mana.
smolder-skill-q-mana.text: Killing a target with Q refunds mana, so Smolder rarely runs out while farming, but repeatedly using it only on champions drains his mana quickly. When harassing, weave Q between minion last hits to recover mana.

smolder-skill-r.basis: R damages a wide area and slows enemies at its center. Smolder heals when R's flames reach him. In teamfights, aim R at the center of grouped enemies.
smolder-skill-r.text: R (MMOOOMMMM!) deals damage over a wide area, slows enemies at its center, and heals Smolder when its flames reach him. Cast it beneath yourself while retreating to gain both healing and a slow. In teamfights, center it on grouped enemies; if you’re in danger, cast it at your own position without hesitation.

smolder-skill-w.basis: W explodes only when it hits a champion. W grants one stack per champion hit. Using W on minions does not trigger explosion damage. Using W on minions does not grant stacks. When W hits multiple champions, each later explosion deals less damage. In teamfights, position W so it hits your intended target first. Use W's slow to keep enemies who get close away.
smolder-skill-w.text: W explodes only when it hits a champion and grants one stack per champion hit; using it on minions gives you neither explosion damage nor stacks. If it hits multiple champions, each successive explosion deals less damage, so line it up to hit your intended target first, even in a teamfight. Its slow also helps you disengage from enemies who get close.

smolder-teamfight.basis: Smolder is a backline damage dealer with no way to engage. In teamfights, stay behind your frontline and use Q whenever it is ready. Save E to survive teamfights.
smolder-teamfight.text: Smolder is a backline damage dealer with no way to engage and low movement speed. Positioning is everything: stay behind your frontline and use Q whenever it is ready, saving E to survive rather than using it for damage.

smolder-teamfight-target.basis: Q targets an enemy directly, so it can damage your intended target even in a chaotic fight. In teamfights, attack the closest enemy in range first. Attacking a frontline enemy with evolved Q also spreads damage to nearby enemies.
smolder-teamfight-target.text: Q targets an enemy directly, so its damage stays reliable even in a chaotic fight. Don't overextend to reach the backline; start with the closest enemy in range. Once Q evolves, hitting that frontline target also spreads damage to nearby enemies.

sona-combo-r.basis: R is an area stun that travels in a straight line. If R is out of range, Flash and immediately cast R through the enemy formation, then use E to help your allies engage. If the enemy engages first, cast R across the incoming enemies to stun them. The aura after R depends on the last basic ability used before R.
sona-combo-r.text: R, Crescendo, is a straight-line area stun that works for both engaging and disengaging. If the target is out of range, Flash and immediately cast R through the enemy formation, then use E to speed up your allies’ engage. If the enemy engages first, sweep R across the incoming champions to stop them. R does not set Sona’s aura; the last basic ability used before it does, so choose that aura in advance.

sona-laning.basis: Sona relies heavily on mana management during laning. Early on, poke mainly with Q. Use W when guaranteed enemy damage is coming in. Against melee engage supports, secure vision in the brush first.
sona-laning.text: Laning as Sona is a test of mana management: her health and attack damage are among the lowest of all champions, so taking hits leaves her at a disadvantage, while repeatedly healing with W (Aria of Perseverance) drains her mana first. Poke mainly with Q (Hymn of Valor) early and use W only when guaranteed enemy damage is coming in. Against a melee engage support, secure brush vision first to deny their opening.

sona-phase.basis: Sona is weakest early on. At level 6, learning R lets her start or stop fights. From mid game, Accelerando stacks and support items build up, letting her cycle abilities faster. Late game, sustained aura use improves her team's staying power in teamfights.
sona-phase.text: Sona is weakest early: her health and attack damage are among the lowest in the game, and her high mana costs make it hard to control lane. At level 6, R lets her start or stop fights. From mid game, Accelerando stacks and support items let her cycle abilities noticeably faster; late game, continuous aura use sustains her whole team through extended teamfights.

sona-roaming.basis: E lets Sona join fights and roam quickly. Roam when you've pushed the wave or your AD carry has recalled. Keep vision around the mid entrances and river to help your jungler move in. After level 6, head mid with R ready and look for a gank.
sona-roaming.text: E lets Sona join fights and roam quickly, but leaving lane exposes her AD carry. Roam when the wave is pushed or your AD carry has recalled; otherwise, spend time securing vision around the mid entrances and river to open a path for your jungler. After level 6, arriving mid with R ready improves the chance of a successful gank.

sona-skill-accelerando.basis: Effective basic ability casts permanently stack Accelerando's ability haste. Once Accelerando reaches its cap, subsequent stacks reduce her ultimate's cooldown. Q must hit a champion to stack Accelerando. W must actually heal an ally or block damage with its shield to stack Accelerando.
sona-skill-accelerando.text: Effective basic ability casts permanently stack Accelerando’s ability haste; once it reaches its cap, further stacks directly reduce Sona’s ultimate cooldown. Q must hit a champion, while W must actually heal an ally or block damage with its shield. Casting into empty space earns no stack, so landing useful abilities in lane helps Sona use her ultimate more often later.

sona-skill-aura-switch.basis: Sona's basic abilities have an immediate effect and a briefly lingering aura. Only the aura from her most recently used basic ability remains active. Keep the aura your team needs active. Right after casting, move toward allies so the aura reaches them.
sona-skill-aura-switch.text: Sona’s basic abilities each have an immediate effect and an aura that lingers briefly around her. Only the aura from her most recent ability remains, so casting abilities back to back replaces the previous aura; using all three at once wastes two. Choose the aura your team needs and keep it active. Because allies must enter its range to benefit, step toward them right after casting, then back away.

sona-skill-powerchord.basis: After using basic abilities a set number of times, her next basic attack is empowered. If Q was used last, Power Chord deals more bonus damage. If E was used last, Power Chord slows the target. When a kill is within reach, finish stacking Power Chord with Q. When escaping or helping allies chase, finish stacking Power Chord with E.
sona-skill-powerchord.text: Power Chord empowers Sona’s next basic attack after she uses basic abilities a set number of times. Its effect depends on the last ability used: finishing with Q increases its bonus damage, while finishing with E slows the target. Choose the final cast accordingly—Q when a kill is within reach, or E when escaping or helping allies chase.

sona-skill-q.basis: Q automatically attacks two nearby enemies, prioritizing champions. Q's aura empowers allies' next basic attacks. Use Q when your AD carry can land a basic attack. During laning, Q is the main way to stack Accelerando.
sona-skill-q.text: Q, Hymn of Valor, automatically hits two nearby enemies and prioritizes champions, even when minions stand in front of them. Its aura empowers allies’ next basic attacks, so use Q when your AD carry can land one to get value from both effects. Q is also Sona’s main way to stack Accelerando during laning.

sona-skill-w.basis: W heals immediately and provides a brief aura shield. Time W's shield for the moment an enemy ability is about to hit. W costs the most mana of her basic abilities. During laning, don't spam W just to restore a little health.
sona-skill-w.text: W, Aria of Perseverance, heals immediately and grants a brief shield through its aura. The shield lasts too little time to apply well in advance, so cast W as an enemy ability is about to hit. It has the highest mana cost of Sona’s basic abilities; spamming it for small heals in lane can leave her unable to respond when a trade starts.

sona-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay back while keeping allies within aura range. Before a fight starts, use E to speed up your allies' engage. Once the fight starts, alternate W and Q to give your allies their auras. If enemies group up, hit multiple targets with R.
sona-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay back but close enough for your auras to reach allies. Use E (Song of Celerity) to speed up their engage before the fight starts, then alternate W (Aria of Perseverance) and Q (Hymn of Valor) while keeping your auras on them. Aim R (Crescendo) through multiple grouped enemies, unless you can reliably stop a single enemy engaging on your carry; that is more valuable.

soraka-combo-eq.basis: Using E alone rarely lands the root. Slow the enemy with Q, then place E over them to try to root them. Place E over an enemy caught in an ally's crowd control.
soraka-combo-eq.text: E alone rarely roots an enemy. Land Q first to slow them so they cannot walk out before E's area expires, then place E over them; you can also place it over an enemy already slowed or caught in an ally's crowd control. The order is not E into Q.

soraka-combo-qw.basis: Land Q on an enemy champion, then use W. Landing Q on an enemy champion nearly removes the health cost of the following W. W used after landing Q also passes the Rejuvenation effect to an ally. Using W before Q costs Soraka much more health for the same healing.
soraka-combo-qw.text: The basic sequence is to land Q on an enemy champion, then use W. A champion hit by Q grants Soraka Rejuvenation, which nearly eliminates W’s health cost and passes the effect to the ally she heals. Using W first costs far more of Soraka’s health for the same healing.

soraka-laning-position.basis: Soraka has no mobility ability. Against enemies that engage, save E to stop their entry. Right after Soraka uses E to poke is a good time to engage.
soraka-laning-position.text: Soraka has some of the lowest movement speed and health, with no mobility ability. Against an engage opponent, hold E to stop them as they come in instead of spending it on poke. The moment after you use E to poke is their best opportunity to engage.

soraka-phase.basis: Learn Q at level 1 if you want to reach level 2 first or take early poke control. Learn W at level 1 if you plan to help leash your jungler or play defensively. After that, the usual approach is to prioritize healing. Soraka's map-wide impact grows in the mid to late game as R's cooldown gets shorter.
soraka-phase.text: At level 1, learn Q if you want to reach level 2 first or gain control through early poke; learn W if you plan to help leash your jungler or play defensively. After that, the usual approach, as the statistics indicate, is to prioritize healing. Soraka’s map-wide impact grows in the mid to late game as R’s cooldown gets shorter.

soraka-skill-e-interrupt.basis: E casts instantly and can interrupt channeled abilities. Enemies inside E are silenced. Place E ahead of time in the path an enemy will take when engaging. Place E ahead of time at an enemy's Teleport landing spot.
soraka-skill-e-interrupt.text: E casts instantly, so it can interrupt channeled abilities, and its silence can stop enemies from engaging through the area. In practice, placing it ahead of time on a path the enemy must cross or at a Teleport landing spot works more often than trying to land the root.

soraka-skill-e-nowave.basis: E does not damage minions or jungle monsters. Save E for fights instead of using it to manage the wave.
soraka-skill-e-nowave.text: E does not damage minions or jungle monsters, so it cannot clear a wave. Save its cooldown for fights instead of spending it on wave management.

soraka-skill-passive.basis: P only grants movement speed when moving toward a heavily wounded ally. An ally marked by P receives increased healing from R. Use the P marker on an ally to help decide when to cast R. An enemy can notice a nearby low-health ally from Soraka's sudden speed boost.
soraka-skill-passive.text: P grants movement speed only while Soraka moves toward a heavily wounded ally. Its marker also identifies an ally who will receive increased healing from R, so use it to time R for maximum effect. Enemies can read Soraka’s sudden speed boost as a sign that a low-health ally is nearby, so take care when that ally needs to move discreetly.

soraka-skill-q-lead.basis: The farther you cast Q, the longer it takes to land. At long range, cast Q ahead of time where the enemy will retreat after last-hitting. When you must land Q, cast it from as close to the enemy as possible.
soraka-skill-q-lead.text: The farther Soraka casts Q, the longer the star takes to fall. At long range, aim for where the enemy will retreat after a last hit rather than where they are standing now. When landing Q is urgent, cast from as close to the enemy as possible to shorten its fall time.

soraka-skill-q-vision.basis: Q briefly reveals the area where it lands. When checking a brush yourself is risky, cast Q into it.
soraka-skill-q-vision.text: Q briefly reveals where it lands. If you want to save a ward or checking a brush yourself is risky, cast Q into the brush instead. For a support, this is Q's second use.

soraka-skill-r.basis: R heals all allies regardless of distance. R heals heavily wounded allies more. Save R if it is certain that only one ally will die and R cannot save them.
soraka-skill-r.text: R heals every ally regardless of distance, with more healing for those who have lost a large amount of health. Even during laning, use it to help fights in other lanes rather than holding it. Save it only when you are certain that just one ally will die and R cannot save them.

soraka-skill-w-cost.basis: Soraka spends her own health when she uses W. Using W repeatedly without Rejuvenation quickly drains Soraka's health. Soraka cannot use W when her health falls below a certain level.
soraka-skill-w-cost.text: W costs Soraka health rather than mana. Casting it repeatedly in a short time without Rejuvenation quickly drains her health, and she cannot cast it at all below a certain health threshold. If you have to spam heals during a trade, your positioning has already gone wrong.

swain-combo-lane.basis: In lane trades, place W in the enemy's path, root them with E, pull them in, then use Q at close range. Place W first to make E harder for the enemy to dodge.
swain-combo-lane.text: In lane trades, place W in the enemy’s path ahead of time, land E while they are slowed, recast E to pull them in, then hit them with Q at close range. W comes first to deny them room to dodge E, rather than for its damage.

swain-combo-q-close.basis: Q hits with more overlapping bolts up close, but only one bolt at maximum range. Use Q to finish an enemy after catching them, rather than to poke at range. Pull the enemy in with E before using Q so its damage does not drop to half or less.
swain-combo-q-close.text: Q fires several bolts that overlap up close, while only one hits at maximum range. Use it to finish an enemy after catching them rather than to poke from afar; using Q before pulling them in with E can cut its damage to half or less.

swain-combo-ult.basis: Activate R, root the enemy with E, recast E to pull them in, then recast R. Don’t recast R as soon as it’s available. Wait until you’ve gained as much drain and healing as possible.
swain-combo-ult.text: Activate R, root the enemy with E, recast E to pull them in, then recast R. Wait until you have gained as much drain and healing as possible before that final recast, even if it becomes available sooner.

swain-laning-poke.basis: Manage the lane by hitting both the wave and the enemy with Q. Use Q when the enemy ADC steps forward to last-hit.
swain-laning-poke.text: Swain ranks among the top supports in CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute, reflecting how central it is to his laning to hit both the wave and the enemy with Q. Cast Q as the opposing ADC steps forward to last-hit, poking them while clearing the wave.

swain-laning-zone.basis: Landing E makes it hard for the enemy bot duo to approach the wave for a while. Do not save E only for kill opportunities; use it whenever it is off cooldown to pressure the lane. Do not push the lane while E is on cooldown and you have no way to catch the enemy.
swain-laning-zone.text: Landing E keeps the enemy bot duo away from the wave for that window. Even without a kill, pressuring them whenever E comes off cooldown creates a CS lead, so use it to control the lane instead of saving it only for kill opportunities. While E is down, you have no way to catch them, so do not push the lane.

swain-phase.basis: At level 1, you lack the mana for repeated fights. Wave clear and poke become stronger as you level Q. After learning R at level 6, you become stronger in 2v2 fights. As Soul Fragments stack, your health rises and you become tougher over time. As long as you do not fall too far behind early, you retain your late-game value.
swain-phase.text: Swain has E at level 1, but lacks the mana for repeated fights. Wave clear and poke strengthen as you level Q, and learning R at level 6 lets you win 2v2 fights. Soul Fragments steadily increase your health, making you tougher over time and preserving your late-game value as long as you do not fall too far behind early.

swain-roaming.basis: Swain has low movement speed and no dash or escape ability. Roaming takes too much time, so stay in lane and keep up the pressure. Limit trips out of lane to managing river vision. If the enemy jungler catches you while roaming, escaping is difficult.
swain-roaming.text: Swain has low movement speed and no dash or escape ability. The round trip for a roam costs too much, so stay in lane to maintain pressure and limit trips out to managing river vision; if the enemy jungler catches you while roaming, you have no way out.

swain-situational-zhonya.basis: Get Zhonya's Hourglass early if an engaging damage dealer can kill Swain quickly. R becomes more valuable the longer Swain stays alive.
swain-situational-zhonya.text: Build Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier if the enemy has an engaging damage dealer who can kill Swain in an instant. His R gains value for as long as he stays alive, so surviving even one burst of damage can change the outcome of a fight.

swain-skill-e-pull.basis: When waiting for an ally to engage, leave E's root in place without recasting it. Recast E immediately when you need to move the enemy toward your allies or out of turret range. Pulling an enemy with E grants a Soul Fragment. If you are unsure whether to pull, choose the option that grants a Soul Fragment.
swain-skill-e-pull.text: Pulling an enemy after rooting them with E is optional. If you need to wait for an ally to engage, let the root hold them; if you need to move them toward your allies or out of turret range, recast immediately. The pull grants a Soul Fragment, so favor it when the other benefits are unclear.

swain-skill-e-range.basis: E sends out a wave that travels forward and then returns. Land E at maximum range, where the enemy has less time to react. If you use E up close, the enemy can see the wave's path and walk out of it. Rooting an enemy with E from far away also helps secure a Soul Fragment.
swain-skill-e-range.text: E sends out a wave that returns, so aim to land it at maximum range. From that distance, the enemy has little time to react, making the root nearly certain and helping secure a Soul Fragment; up close, they can see the wave’s path and walk out of it.

swain-skill-passive.basis: Hitting a champion with W, pulling one with E, or an enemy champion dying grants a Soul Fragment. Soul Fragments permanently increase maximum health. To build health for the late game, use W and E on champions during the laning phase.
swain-skill-passive.text: Hitting a champion with W, pulling one with E, or an enemy champion dying grants a Soul Fragment, which permanently increases maximum health. Landing abilities on champions is itself a way to grow, so using W and E on champions throughout the laning phase instead of on minions builds a health advantage for later.

swain-skill-r.basis: R stays active only if it keeps draining enemy champions. If the enemy walks out of R’s range, demonic energy quickly runs out and R ends. Activate R only when you have a way to hold the enemy in place. If E is down and your allies have no crowd control, activating R just lets time pass with nothing to drain.
swain-skill-r.text: R stays active only while it keeps draining enemy champions. If they walk out of range, its demonic energy quickly runs out and it ends, so activate it only when you have a way to hold them nearby. With E on cooldown and no allied crowd control, there is nothing to drain and R’s time simply runs out.

swain-skill-w.basis: W takes time to land, but covers a wide area and reveals it. Use W to check brushes or track the enemy jungler's path. Use W to interrupt an enemy's recall. Overlap W with E to force the enemy's Flash. It is best not to use W to clear minions.
swain-skill-w.text: W takes time to land, but covers and reveals a wide area. Use it for information and to force a response: check brushes, interrupt recalls, track the enemy jungler’s path, or overlap it with E to force Flash. Clearing minions is its least valuable use.

swain-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stand just behind your frontline and pull in one enemy with E. Activate R when enemies engage as a group and it can reach several of them. Without a dash, Swain has trouble walking in first to start a teamfight.
swain-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stand just behind your frontline and pull one enemy in with E. Activate R when the enemy engages as a group, where it can reach several champions and stay active. Swain cannot walk in first to start a fight without a dash.

sylas-combo-basic.basis: Use E's first cast to close in, then hit the second cast to knock the target up. Follow with an empowered basic attack, Q, a basic attack, W, and a basic attack. Each ability cast grants one passive stack.
sylas-combo-basic.text: Close in with E's first cast, land the second chain to knock the target up, then use an empowered basic attack, Q, a basic attack, W, and another basic attack. Each ability grants one passive stack, so weave basic attacks between casts to deal the full damage instead of using your abilities back to back.

sylas-laning.basis: His abilities cost a lot of mana, so using them all on the wave quickly leaves him short on mana. Clear minions with Q's explosion, but save one ability cast for a trade. Save W to sustain in lane. Expect to fall behind in farm and plan to make up for it through fights and roams.
sylas-laning.text: His abilities cost a lot of mana, so using them all on the wave quickly drains it. Clear minions with Q's explosion, but keep one ability cast for a trade and save W for lane sustain. Sylas ranks near the bottom in CS, so expect to fall behind in farm and plan to make it up through fights and roams.

sylas-laning-wave.basis: Do not push the wave too hard before level 6. His short range leaves him exposed to the enemy jungler when he stands in front of a pushed wave. After learning R, push the lane and join fights in other lanes or around objectives.
sylas-laning-wave.text: Do not push the wave too hard before level 6: Sylas's short range leaves him exposed to the enemy jungler when he stands in front of a pushed wave. Once you learn R, shift to pushing the lane and joining fights elsewhere or around objectives.

sylas-phase.basis: Sylas is weak at levels 1–2 because of his short range and tight mana supply. His first power spike comes at level 6, when he can steal an enemy ultimate. He is strongest in the mid game when he has built both ability haste and ability power. In the late game, his short range and low durability make direct fights difficult. In the late game, look for an opening to make an impact with one stolen ultimate.
sylas-phase.text: Sylas is weak at levels 1–2 because of his short range and tight mana supply. His first power spike comes at level 6, when he can steal an enemy ultimate, and he is strongest in the mid game once he has built both ability haste and ability power. Late in the game, his short range and low durability make direct fights difficult, so look for an opening where one stolen ultimate can make an impact.

sylas-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing is enough to undo your trades, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Build Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
sylas-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing is enough to undo your trades, reduce it with Morellonomicon after completing one core item.

sylas-skill-e.basis: E has two casts: a dash, then a chain that pulls Sylas to the target and knocks them up. When escaping, use only E's first cast and save the second. When engaging, use E's first cast only if you have an angle to land the second.
sylas-skill-e.text: E starts with a dash, then throws a chain that pulls Sylas to the target and knocks them up. Using only the first cast to engage leaves you with no way out, so use only that cast when escaping and save the second; when engaging, dash only if you have a clear angle to land the chain.

sylas-skill-passive.basis: Petricite Burst's empowered basic attack also damages enemies around the target. Attack speed increases while passive stacks remain. Save empowered basic attacks for trades instead of using them on minions.
sylas-skill-passive.text: Petricite Burst's empowered basic attack damages enemies around the target and grants attack speed while stacks remain. Save those attacks for trades and use them together instead of spending them on minions.

sylas-skill-r-mechanic.basis: Use R to copy an enemy champion's ultimate. A stolen ultimate's power scales with Sylas's own R rank and stats. Stolen ultimates with attack damage ratios are converted to ability power ratios.
sylas-skill-r-mechanic.text: R Hijack copies an enemy champion's ultimate. Its power depends on Sylas's own R rank and stats, and even an ultimate with attack damage scaling is converted to ability power scaling, so Sylas's ability power items still apply when he steals an AD champion's ultimate.

sylas-skill-r-priority.basis: Prioritize stealing area crowd control and engage ultimates. If your team has no way to engage, choose an ultimate that starts fights. If you need to pick off an enemy carry, choose an ultimate that locks them down. Even if you steal a single-target execute ultimate, it is hard to find an opening to use it.
sylas-skill-r-priority.text: Prioritize area crowd control and engage ultimates. If your team lacks a way to engage, steal one that starts fights; if you need to pick off an enemy carry, choose one that holds them in place. Single-target execute ultimates are less valuable because Sylas has trouble finding an opening to use them.

sylas-skill-r-target.basis: After stealing a champion's ultimate, you cannot steal from that champion again for a long time. Keep several champions available to steal from, and take a different champion's ultimate in each fight.
sylas-skill-r-target.text: After stealing a champion's ultimate, you cannot steal from that champion again for a long time. Keep several targets available and steal from a different champion in each fight to keep using R; if you rely on just one, you will have no ultimate for the next fight.

sylas-skill-w.basis: W is both a dash and a heal. W's healing scales with missing health. In a trade, land W on an enemy champion after taking damage.
sylas-skill-w.text: W is both a dash and a heal, and its healing scales with missing health, so using it for damage at full health wastes the most value. In a trade, land it on an enemy champion after taking damage to turn the exchange around.

sylas-teamfight.basis: His role in teamfights depends on the ultimate he has stolen. Secure an ultimate with R before the fight starts. When diving in with E, enter second, after an ally has engaged. In a chaotic fight, use W to heal as soon as you have taken damage.
sylas-teamfight.text: Sylas’s role in a teamfight depends on the ultimate he has stolen, so secure one with R before the fight starts. When diving in with E, follow an ally’s engage rather than entering first, or you may be killed before you have a chance to heal. In a chaotic fight, use W to heal as soon as you take damage instead of saving it to finish someone off; surviving longer is more valuable.

syndra-combo-burst.basis: Place a sphere with Q, pick it up and throw it with W, push the remaining sphere with E to stun, then finish with R. R also fires spheres on the field. Place as many spheres as possible with Q before casting R to increase its damage.
syndra-combo-burst.text: For a full combo, place a sphere with Q, pick it up and throw it with W, push a remaining sphere with E to stun, then finish with R. R also fires spheres on the field, so placing as many as possible with Q before casting it determines how much damage it deals.

syndra-combo-self-peel.basis: If an enemy gets close, place Q under yourself or where they will land, then push them away with E to create distance. Against an enemy with a gap closer, be ready to create distance with Q and E.
syndra-combo-self-peel.text: When an enemy closes in, place Q beneath yourself or where they will land, then use E for both a stun and a knockback to regain distance. Have this sequence ready against enemies with gap closers.

syndra-combo-stun.basis: Place Q behind the enemy, then push it with E to stun them. Only enemies hit by a Dark Sphere pushed by E are stunned. Using E without a sphere only pushes enemies away.
syndra-combo-stun.text: Place Q beyond the enemy, then push its Dark Sphere through them with E to stun them. The sphere must be past the enemy, rather than between you and them: E only stuns enemies hit by a sphere it pushes, and without one, E merely knocks them back.

syndra-combo-wq.basis: Hit an enemy with a sphere or minion thrown by W to slow them. Follow a W slow immediately with Q to make your poke more likely to land.
syndra-combo-wq.text: Hit an enemy with a sphere or minion thrown by W to slow them, then follow immediately with Q. Casting Q after the slow makes it much more likely to land.

syndra-laning.basis: Prioritize safe farming with your long range over risky poke. Place Q where the enemy will step up to last-hit to poke them. Save E for an enemy engage. Avoid fully pushing the wave and giving the enemy jungler a gank opportunity.
syndra-laning.text: Syndra's CS statistics are among the best, so prioritize safe farming with her long range over risky poke. Place Q where an enemy will step up to last hit for low risk harass, save E for their engage, and avoid fully pushing the wave into a position that gives their jungler a gank opportunity.

syndra-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, mana costs and cooldowns make it hard for Syndra to poke often. As Q levels up, Syndra gains an advantage in lane. Learning R at level 6 gives Syndra her first chance to secure a kill. Syndra peaks in the mid to late game as she gains splinters and ability power. Syndra is vulnerable when poorly positioned.
syndra-phase.text: At levels 1–2, mana costs and cooldowns limit how often Syndra can poke. As Q levels up, she gains an advantage in lane, and R gives her a first chance to secure a kill at level 6. She peaks in the mid to late game as she gains splinters and ability power, but her health and armor are among the lowest, so poor positioning can end a fight for her immediately.

syndra-situational-antiheal.basis: Choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction against enemies who sustain through damage. Syndra relies on killing an enemy in one combo. If an enemy heals through Syndra's combo, she must wait for her cooldowns before the next one.
syndra-situational-antiheal.text: Against enemies who sustain through damage, buy Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Syndra aims to kill with one combo; if an enemy heals through it, she must wait for her cooldowns before trying again.

syndra-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner to survive their initial engage. Syndra has no mobility ability. If Syndra lets an enemy close the gap, one E may not be enough to escape.
syndra-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner to survive their initial engage. Syndra has no mobility ability, and once an enemy closes the gap, a single E may not be enough to escape.

syndra-skill-e.basis: E has a long cooldown. Syndra relies on E to defend herself. Against an enemy with a gap closer, save E for their engage instead of using it to poke. If the enemy has no way to close the gap, actively look for stuns with Q and E.
syndra-skill-e.text: E has a long cooldown and is Syndra's only defensive ability. Against an enemy with a gap closer, save it for their engage instead of spending it on poke; if they have no way to close the gap, look actively for stuns with Q and E.

syndra-skill-passive.basis: Gain Splinters of Wrath by putting points into abilities and hitting champions. Each ability gains an additional effect when your splinters pass certain thresholds. Maxing one ability quickly gives you a power spike. Gaining splinters also restores mana. Keep hitting champions to gain splinters and restore mana.
syndra-skill-passive.text: Syndra gains Splinters of Wrath by putting points into abilities and hitting champions. Her abilities gain additional effects at certain splinter thresholds, so quickly maxing one creates a power spike. Gaining splinters also restores mana, making consistent hits on champions part of managing it.

syndra-skill-q.basis: Q spheres remain on the field briefly after casting. Q spheres can be used by W, E, and R. If a fight is likely, place Q in advance to set up an angle, even if it deals no damage. You can cast Q while moving.
syndra-skill-q.text: Q spheres linger briefly after casting and can be used by W, E, and R, making Q both a damage ability and a setup tool. If a fight is likely, place one in advance to create an angle even if it deals no damage; you can cast Q while moving, whether you are retreating or approaching.

syndra-skill-r.basis: R fires the spheres orbiting Syndra and those on the field at one target. Place as many spheres as possible with Q before casting R. Once you have enough Splinters of Wrath, R executes targets with low health.
syndra-skill-r.text: R fires both the spheres orbiting Syndra and those on the field at one target, so it is much weaker without spheres. Place as many as possible with Q before casting it. Once you have enough Splinters of Wrath, R executes low health targets, changing when you can use it to finish a fight.

syndra-skill-w.basis: W can pick up and throw enemy minions and normal monsters as well as spheres. You can still poke with W while Q is on cooldown. If mana is tight in lane, throw minions with W to keep trading. If you do not select a target for W, it picks the nearest sphere.
syndra-skill-w.text: W can pick up and throw enemy minions and normal monsters as well as spheres, so it remains a poke option while Q is on cooldown. If mana is tight in lane, throw minions to keep trading. Without a selected target, W picks up the nearest sphere.

syndra-teamfight.basis: At the start of a teamfight, stay at the back and pressure the enemy formation with Q and W. Save E to push away enemies who engage. Use R only on a target you can reliably kill. Place Q spheres before the teams clash to strengthen R. Place Q spheres before the teams clash to set up a stun with E.
syndra-teamfight.text: Start teamfights from the back, pressuring the enemy formation with Q and W while saving E to push away anyone who engages. Use R only on a target you can reliably kill. Placing Q spheres before the teams clash strengthens R and sets up a stun with E.

tahmkench-combo-allin.basis: In close combat, knock them up with W, build stacks with basic attacks, then stun with Q and use R. After W begins channeling, its landing spot stays hidden from enemies briefly. Hitting a champion with W refunds part of its cooldown and mana cost. Missing W makes both engaging and escaping difficult, so engage when you can land it.
tahmkench-combo-allin.text: To engage at close range, emerge beneath the enemy with W (Abyssal Dive) to knock them up, build stacks with basic attacks, stun them with Q (Tongue Lash), then use R (Devour). W’s landing spot remains hidden from enemies briefly after its channel begins, making it useful for a surprise engage, and hitting a champion refunds part of its cooldown and mana cost. A miss leaves you without a way to engage or escape for a long time, so open with W only when you can land it reliably.

tahmkench-combo-qr.basis: Press R while Q is in flight to swallow a target with three stacks from range as Q hits. Against a target with two stacks, prepare the Q–R combo and look for an angle to land Q.
tahmkench-combo-qr.text: Press R while Q is in flight, and if it hits a target with three stacks, Tahm Kench swallows them from range. This is his only way to swallow someone without getting close, so prepare the Q–R combo against a target with two stacks and look for an angle to land Q.

tahmkench-combo-stack.basis: Tahm Kench’s combos start with counting An Acquired Taste stacks. Basic attacks and Q each add one An Acquired Taste stack. At three stacks, Q can stun the enemy and R can swallow them.
tahmkench-combo-stack.text: Every Tahm Kench combo starts with counting An Acquired Taste stacks: basic attacks and Q each add one, and when the third lands, Q stuns the target and R can swallow them. Stacks expire over time, so build them quickly with a basic attack–Q–basic attack sequence while staying close, and aim to make Q the third hit to secure the stun.

tahmkench-laning.basis: When a target with two stacks steps forward to last-hit, stun them with Q. Follow a Q stun with a basic attack. Pressure the enemy only while your stacks remain active. Trading aggressively at close range with no stacks offers little benefit.
tahmkench-laning.text: Top lane is a fight over stacks. When an enemy with two stacks steps forward to last-hit, land Q (Tongue Lash) to secure the stun, then add a basic attack. Trading aggressively at close range with no stacks offers little benefit, so pressure them only while your stacks remain active.

tahmkench-laning-bait.basis: Even below half health, Q healing and E’s stored gray health make you tougher than your health bar suggests. Hold on near your turret at low health, then counter an enemy engage with a stun and R.
tahmkench-laning-bait.text: Even below half health, Q healing and E’s stored gray health make Tahm Kench much tougher than his health bar suggests. Enemies often dive based on that bar alone, so stay near your turret at low health and look to counter their engage with a stun and R.

tahmkench-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, you pose little threat before building stacks. At level 6, learning R lets you save allies. Tahm Kench peaks in the mid to late game, when health items increase both basic attack damage and the amount E stores. Tahm Kench struggles to end games alone at any stage, so stay with your allies.
tahmkench-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Tahm Kench poses little threat before he builds stacks. At level 6, R (Devour) lets him save allies; he peaks in the mid to late game as health items increase both his basic attack damage and the amount E (Thick Skin) stores. He cannot end games alone at any stage, so stay with your allies.

tahmkench-situational-mr.basis: If the enemy team’s damage is mostly magic, fit Spectre’s Cowl between your core items. Because E stores gray health based on damage taken, magic resistance improves how effectively you store it and helps you survive longer.
tahmkench-situational-mr.text: If the enemy team’s damage is mostly magic, fit Spectre’s Cowl between your core items. Because E (Thick Skin) stores gray health in proportion to damage taken, magic resistance improves how effectively Tahm Kench stores it and helps him survive longer.

tahmkench-skill-e.basis: E stores damage already taken as gray health, then converts it into a shield. Pressing E with no stored gray health has no effect. After taking heavy damage, use E just before the next burst hits. With several enemy champions nearby, E stores a higher share of damage as gray health. Between fights, let stored gray health restore your health instead of using E.
tahmkench-skill-e.text: E stores damage already taken as gray health and converts it into a shield, so pressing it with nothing stored does nothing. Using it before a fight is a waste; after taking heavy damage, press it just before the next burst for the most value. Several nearby enemy champions increase the share of damage stored, making the shield especially strong in teamfights. If you go without taking damage for a while, stored gray health restores your health on its own, so let it heal you between fights instead of using E.
