tahmkench-skill-passive.basis: Basic attacks deal bonus magic damage based on bonus health. Health items increase both defense and basic attack damage, leaving little reason to mix in attack items. In lane, weave in basic attacks to build stacks and deal damage.
tahmkench-skill-passive.text: Tahm Kench’s basic attacks deal bonus magic damage based on his bonus health. Health items therefore improve both his defense and damage, leaving little reason to add attack items just for damage. Weave basic attacks into lane trades to build stacks and deal damage at the same time.

tahmkench-skill-q.basis: Q is Tahm Kench’s only ranged poke and healing tool. Hitting a champion with Q heals you based on your missing health. If you do not urgently need healing, save Q to stun a target with three stacks.
tahmkench-skill-q.text: Q is Tahm Kench’s only ranged poke and healing tool. Hitting a champion heals you based on your missing health, making it more effective the lower you are and potentially saving you in a crisis. If healing is not urgent, consider holding Q to stun a target with three stacks.

tahmkench-skill-r-ally.basis: An ally swallowed with R cannot be targeted while inside. An ally swallowed with R gains a large shield after being spat out. Swallow an ally with R just before an enemy’s finishing ability hits them. A swallowed ally can leave on their own, so coordinate with them.
tahmkench-skill-r-ally.text: An ally swallowed with R (Devour) cannot be targeted while inside Tahm Kench and gains a large shield after being spat out. This is Tahm Kench’s greatest value, so swallow them just before an enemy’s finishing ability arrives rather than waiting until they are about to die. The ally can leave on their own at any time, so coordinate with them.

tahmkench-skill-r-enemy.basis: While swallowing an enemy, Tahm Kench is heavily slowed and rooted in place. Use R on an enemy when your allies can kill them immediately afterward. Use R on an enemy when you are somewhere safe, such as under a turret. When swallowing an enemy is risky, save R to protect an ally.
tahmkench-skill-r-enemy.text: While swallowing an enemy with R (Devour), Tahm Kench is heavily slowed and rooted, leaving him vulnerable. Use it on an enemy only when your allies can kill them immediately or when you are in a safe position, such as under a turret; otherwise, save R to protect an ally.

tahmkench-skill-r-taxi.basis: You can still use W while carrying an ally, and you briefly gain movement speed. Swallow an ally with R, then use W to carry them out of danger. Swallow an ally with R, then use W to carry them deep into the enemy team. Before engaging with an ally inside, check that you can spit them out where they can fight immediately.
tahmkench-skill-r-taxi.text: While carrying an ally, Tahm Kench is rooted, but he can still use W (Abyssal Dive) and briefly gains movement speed. Swallow an ally with R (Devour), then use W to carry them out of danger or bring an ally with an engage ability deep into the enemy team. Before using it to engage, check that you can spit them out somewhere they can fight immediately.

tahmkench-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay beside your allied carry instead of engaging. Do not die early in a teamfight; stay alive to protect your allied carry.
tahmkench-teamfight.text: In teamfights, prioritize staying beside your allied carry over engaging. The moment an enemy engage reaches them, swallow the carry with R to negate it, then use Q’s slow and W’s knockup to keep the enemy away. If Tahm Kench dies first on the front line, your team loses its way to protect the carry.

taliyah-combo-ewq.basis: Place E, then use W to push the enemy into it and land Q while they're stunned. If you use W before E, you can push the enemy but won't stun them.
taliyah-combo-ewq.text: Place E, then use W to push the enemy across its rocks; they will be stunned when the rocks erupt, giving you time to land Q. Using W first only pushes the enemy without stunning them.

taliyah-combo-gank.basis: If the enemy is already fleeing, aim W to push them toward your allies. Taliyah chooses the direction W pushes the enemy.
taliyah-combo-gank.text: If the enemy is already fleeing, aim W (Seismic Shove) to push them toward your allies; Taliyah chooses the direction of the push.

taliyah-laning-jungle.basis: If Q shards hit different monsters, each deals damage without the reduction. Early on, clear camps quickly to grow stronger instead of forcing ganks. Look for counterganks where you can predict the enemy jungler's route.
taliyah-laning-jungle.text: When Q (Threaded Volley) shards hit different monsters, each deals damage without reduction, so clear camps quickly to build an early lead instead of forcing ganks, then look for counterganks where you can predict the enemy jungler’s route.

taliyah-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, mana costs are high, so conserve your abilities. Your combo becomes available at level 3, when you have Q, W, and E. Your first power spike comes at level 6, when you learn R and can move around the map to intervene. Taliyah is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability power items. Late in the game, letting an enemy engage even once can get you killed.
taliyah-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Taliyah is very fragile and spends a lot of mana, so conserve your abilities. Her combo becomes available at level 3, when she has Q, W, and E; her first power spike comes at level 6, when R lets her move across the map to intervene. She is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability power items, but her health and armor are among the lowest in the game, so allowing even one enemy engage late can mean death.

taliyah-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy team has a champion who survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon after one core item. Taliyah's sustained damage helps keep Grievous Wounds applied after the first application.
taliyah-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy team has a champion who survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon after one core item. Taliyah’s sustained damage keeps Grievous Wounds applied for a long time after the first application.

taliyah-skill-e.basis: E alone only slows and deals a little damage. Enemies are stunned if they dash or are pushed across E. Place E in narrow passages or entrances ahead of time to stop enemies from dashing in.
taliyah-skill-e.text: E alone only slows and deals a little damage; it stuns an enemy only when they dash or are pushed across its rocks. Use it to deny an area by placing it in a narrow passage or entrance ahead of time, so an enemy who dashes in stuns themselves.

taliyah-skill-passive.basis: When out of combat, moving near walls grants movement speed from Rock Surfing. Plan your jungle routes and roams along walls. Stay close to walls when crossing the river, too.
taliyah-skill-passive.text: Rock Surfing increases your movement speed near walls while you are out of combat. Route your jungle clears and roams along walls to cover the same distance much faster, and stay close to a wall when crossing the river.

taliyah-skill-q-direction.basis: Q's shards fly in a line in the cast direction and cannot change direction midflight. Fire Q when the enemy cannot change their direction of movement. If successive Q shards hit the same target, damage drops sharply starting with the second shard.
taliyah-skill-q-direction.text: Q’s shards fly in a fixed line in the cast direction, so an enemy moving sideways can dodge them all. Fire when they cannot change their direction of movement. Successive shards deal sharply reduced damage to the same target starting with the second, so landing every shard on one champion does not give each shard its full value.

taliyah-skill-q-worked-ground.basis: Using Q creates Worked Ground beneath Taliyah. Using Q again on Worked Ground fires one slowing boulder instead of shards. Q on Worked Ground costs almost no mana and has half the cooldown. Clear jungle monsters and minion waves with Q shards from fresh ground. Use Q's boulder from Worked Ground when chasing champions or escaping.
taliyah-skill-q-worked-ground.text: Using Q creates Worked Ground beneath Taliyah. Casting Q there again costs almost no mana and halves its cooldown, but fires one slowing boulder instead of shards. Use shards from fresh ground to clear jungle camps and minion waves, and the Worked Ground boulder when chasing champions or escaping.

taliyah-skill-r-wall.basis: You can use R without riding the wall. During teamfights, use R's wall to separate the enemy frontline from their backline. Block a fleeing enemy's escape route with R's wall. You can immediately destroy a completed R wall by casting the ability again. If R's wall blocks your allies' pursuit, destroy it immediately.
taliyah-skill-r-wall.text: R is useful even if you do not ride the wall. In a teamfight, place it through the middle of the enemy formation to separate their frontline from their backline, or block a fleeing enemy’s escape route. Once the wall is complete, you can destroy it immediately by casting R again; do so without delay if it blocks your allies’ pursuit.

taliyah-skill-w-peel.basis: Enemies knocked up by W are briefly unable to participate in the fight. Use W to push melee champions away from your allied marksman. W has a delayed activation, so cast it ahead of time on the enemy's approach path.
taliyah-skill-w-peel.text: W’s knockup briefly takes an enemy out of the fight, and pushing a melee champion away from your allied marksman can save a teamfight. Because W takes time to activate, cast it on the enemy’s approach path before they reach your ally.

taliyah-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay back and place E on an approach path to narrow the enemy's way in. Place R's wall where grouped enemies are entering to split their formation. Place R's wall along the enemy backline's escape route.
taliyah-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Taliyah stays back and shapes the terrain: place E on an approach path to narrow the enemy’s way in, then use W to push away anyone who still enters. Use R to split the enemy formation, placing its wall where grouped enemies are entering or along the enemy backline’s escape route.

taliyah-teamfight-objective.basis: Taliyah has an advantage in fights in tight spaces, such as the Dragon or Baron pit. In objective fights, place E in tight terrain and use R to block the entrance. Check R's cooldown before an objective fight.
taliyah-teamfight-objective.text: Taliyah is strongest in fights inside tight spaces such as the Dragon or Baron pit. Place E in the already narrow terrain and block the entrance with R to leave enemies no way in or out. Check R’s cooldown before committing to an objective fight.

talon-combo-fast.basis: For a fast combo, cast W, close in with Q just before it returns, then use a basic attack to trigger Blade's End. Time W's return hit with Q's landing to complete the Blade's End stacks. In the fast combo, avoid using a basic attack right before Q so the attack after Q is not delayed.
talon-combo-fast.text: For a fast combo, cast W, then close in with Q just before W returns. Its return hit will land as Q lands, completing your Blade's End stacks so one basic attack immediately triggers the bleed. Do not basic attack before Q: doing so makes you wait for the next attack and throws off the timing.

talon-combo-fastest.basis: The fastest combo is to use Q right after W's first hit, cast R during the leap, then trigger Blade's End with a basic attack on landing. Using R to engage spends the invisibility you could use to escape. Use the W-Q-R engage combo only when you are sure you can kill the target.
talon-combo-fastest.text: For the fastest combo, throw W, use Q just after its first hit passes, and activate R during the leap. The stacks will be full when you land, so one basic attack triggers Blade's End's bleed. Because using R to engage leaves you without its invisibility to escape, only use this combo when you're certain you can kill the target.

talon-combo-reliable.basis: A reliable combo is to close in with Q, cast W, then use a basic attack to trigger Blade's End. Closing in with Q first makes it easier to land both hits of W. Start the combo with Q when you need a reliable hit.
talon-combo-reliable.text: For a reliable combo, leap in with Q, cast W at close range, then use a basic attack to trigger Blade's End. Starting with Q lets both the outgoing and returning hits of W land, filling the stacks so one basic attack triggers the bleed. Use this sequence when you need to land the combo reliably.

talon-laning.basis: Talon is a melee champion with very short range. Do not step forward first in lane. Chip away at the enemy's health with W before engaging. Close in with Q only when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. When trading, trigger Blade's End with a basic attack, then back off.
talon-laning.text: Talon is a melee champion with very short range, so stepping forward first in lane puts him at a disadvantage. Chip away at the enemy with W, then close in with Q only when they step forward to last-hit. Once you start a trade, follow through with a basic attack to trigger Blade's End before backing off; retreating with only stacks applied wastes mana.

talon-phase.basis: Talon deals high damage from levels 1–2. Push the wave quickly and look for an early kill as soon as you reach level 2 first. If the enemy reaches the next level first, do not step forward during that window. Talon's roaming and burst damage peak after he learns R. Talon's impact falls off as the game goes on. In the late game, Talon can easily die where he engaged even if he kills one backline target. When ahead, keep applying pressure to end the game.
talon-phase.text: Talon deals high damage from levels 1–2. Push the wave quickly: reaching level 2 before your opponent creates his best early kill opportunity. If they level up first, do not step forward during that window. His roaming and burst peak after he learns R, but his impact falls as the game goes on; later, he can die where he engages even after killing a backline target. When ahead, keep applying pressure to end the game.

talon-roam.basis: Talon's greatest strength is roaming across terrain with E. After pushing the wave, cross jungle walls with E to create a numbers advantage in a side lane. Before moving to set up a roaming ambush, clear enemy vision with a Control Ward. When roaming, choose a route outside enemy vision.
talon-roam.text: Talon's greatest strength is roaming across terrain with E. Push the wave, cross jungle walls to reach a side lane, and create a numbers advantage. If the enemy has vision in the jungle, the ambush loses its value, so clear that vision with a Control Ward or choose an unseen route before moving.

talon-situational-antiheal.basis: Against an enemy with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. Blade's End deals bleed damage over time, making Grievous Wounds easy to maintain.
talon-situational-antiheal.text: Against an enemy with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. Blade's End deals bleed damage over time, making the healing reduction easy to maintain.

talon-skill-e.basis: Assassin's Path crosses terrain. After crossing a piece of terrain, you cannot cross it again for a considerable time. The time before you can cross the same terrain again is especially long early on. Choose terrain for your escape route in advance and save it while roaming. Assassin's Path counts as a dash, so targeted chain abilities can interrupt it. Assassin's Path can also cross terrain created by allies or enemies. The restriction on crossing the same terrain again also applies to terrain created by allies or enemies.
talon-skill-e.text: E, Assassin's Path, crosses terrain, but you cannot cross the same piece again for a considerable time, especially early on. Plan which terrain you will use to escape and save it while roaming. E counts as a dash, so targeted chain abilities can interrupt it; it can also cross terrain created by allies or enemies, with the same restriction on crossing it again.

talon-skill-passive.basis: Blade's End stacks with abilities and triggers with a basic attack. Only abilities build Blade's End stacks. Blade's End stacks last 6 seconds. To reach 3 stacks, land abilities in quick succession.
talon-skill-passive.text: Blade's End builds stacks through abilities and triggers with a basic attack. Only abilities add stacks, and they last 6 seconds, so land your abilities in quick succession to reach three stacks.

talon-skill-q.basis: Using Q within melee range lands a critical hit without a leap. Using Q outside melee range makes Talon leap to the target. To increase Q's damage, get into melee range first with Flash or E. Killing a target with Q refunds half its cooldown. Use Q to last-hit minions for lane sustain and mana efficiency.
talon-skill-q.text: Q lands a critical hit without leaping when used in melee range; outside that range, Talon leaps to the target. Getting close with Flash or E before using Q therefore deals more damage with the same ability. Killing a target with Q refunds half its cooldown, so use it to last-hit minions for lane sustain and mana efficiency.

talon-skill-q-aa.basis: Right after a Q leap, the basic attack windup is shorter, so the attack comes out immediately. When finishing with Q, the fastest sequence is to use Q as your last ability, then basic attack.
talon-skill-q-aa.text: Immediately after a Q leap, the shorter basic attack windup lets the attack come out at once. When finishing a combo with Q, use it as your last ability and follow with a basic attack for the fastest sequence.

talon-skill-r.basis: Shadow Assault grants both stealth and increased movement speed. If a basic attack ends the stealth, the blades converge on that target, concentrating the damage. If Q ends the stealth, the blades converge on that target, concentrating the damage. If the stealth ends without a target, the blades converge on Talon, revealing the direction he fled.
talon-skill-r.text: R, Shadow Assault, grants stealth and increased movement speed. Ending the stealth with a basic attack or Q sends the blades toward that target instead of Talon, concentrating the damage on one enemy. If it ends without a target, the blades converge on Talon and reveal the direction he fled, so account for that when using R to escape.

talon-skill-w.basis: W's return hit deals more damage than its outgoing hit. W's return hit applies a slow. Cast W from close range to land both hits. Use W as your main ability in lane. Early on, avoid overusing W so you have mana left for kill opportunities.
talon-skill-w.text: W's returning hit deals more damage than its outgoing hit and applies a slow. Cast it from close range to land both hits; throwing it out from afar for poke gets only half its value. W is your main laning ability, but its early mana cost is high, so avoid overusing it and leaving yourself unable to cast when a kill opportunity appears.

talon-teamfight.basis: Choose your kill target before a teamfight. In teamfights, focus your abilities on one target instead of spreading them across several enemies. Engage after the enemy has used their crowd control on your allies. Save R's invisibility for a safe escape. If a frontal teamfight is difficult, flank with E and target the side of the enemy backline.
talon-teamfight.text: Choose your target before a teamfight. Committing all of Talon's abilities to one enemy secures the kill, while spreading them across several can leave everyone alive and Talon exposed. Engage after the enemy has used their crowd control on your allies, and save R's invisibility for a safer escape. If a frontal fight is difficult, use E to flank the enemy backline.

taric-combo-engage.basis: Use W on an ally about to engage, then use R, E, two Bravado basic attacks, and Q in that order. Time R's activation to coincide with the peak of the trade following E's stun.
taric-combo-engage.text: To start a fight, link W to the ally who is about to engage, cast R early, stun with E, land two Bravado basic attacks, then heal with Q. The key is to time R’s activation for the peak of the damage trade after E’s stun; with this sequence, your ally can deal damage while invulnerable just after the stun ends.

taric-combo-w-e.basis: E also activates from the position of the ally linked by W. Stand slightly apart from your linked ally to reduce the space enemies can dodge through between the two E beams. Use W on an ally about to dash in, then start the fight by activating E from their position.
taric-combo-w-e.text: E also activates from the ally linked by W. Stand slightly apart from that ally to spread the two beams and leave enemies less room to dodge. Linking an ally who is about to dash in also lets you start a fight with E from their position, even if they move beyond Taric’s range, without following them in.

taric-laning.basis: As a melee champion, Taric struggles to reach enemies without E. Use E to start a trade, not to poke. Against a ranged support, don't move forward if you have no opening to land E.
taric-laning.text: As a melee champion, Taric has no way to reach enemies without E. Save it to open a trade instead of using it to poke. Against a ranged support, you must endure their poke while E is down, so stay back when there is no opening to land it.

taric-laning-cs.basis: When using up Bravado basic attacks, avoid minions that are about to be last-hit. Use Bravado basic attacks on healthy minions or targets the turret has already hit.
taric-laning-cs.text: Using Bravado basic attacks on minions can easily steal your ADC’s last hits, so avoid minions that are nearly dead and hit healthy ones or targets the turret has already struck. Skipping basic attacks altogether slows your ability rotation; the choice is what to hit, not whether to hit anything.

taric-phase.basis: Taric becomes strong in melee trades at levels 2–3, when he has both E and Q. Taric is strong in early head-to-head fights because Bravado's damage scales with armor. At level 6, R lets Taric stop enemy dives and explosive engages. In the mid to late game, as he builds armor items, Taric uses that armor both to frontline and to deal damage.
taric-phase.text: Taric’s melee trades become strong at levels 2–3 once he has both E and Q. His armor is among the highest at level one, and Bravado’s damage scales with armor, making early head-to-head fights surprisingly strong. At level six, R can completely negate enemy dives and explosive engages. As armor items accumulate in the mid to late game, that same stat helps him frontline and deal damage.

taric-roaming.basis: Taric's movement speed is relatively high among supports, making it easier for him to join fights and roam. When ganking, account for E's delay and aim ahead in the enemy's escape direction. Follow your jungler's engage ability with E. Don't rush toward enemies in areas without vision.
taric-roaming.text: Taric’s relatively high movement speed among supports makes joining fights and roaming manageable, but E’s delay means casting it only after arriving at a gank is too late. Predict the enemy’s escape route and cast ahead, or follow your jungler’s engage ability to secure the stun. Avoid rushing in without vision, which is especially dangerous for a melee support.

taric-skill-bravado.basis: Bravado speeds up Taric's next two basic attacks after he uses an ability and makes them deal bonus damage. Bravado basic attacks reduce the cooldowns of his basic abilities. After using an ability, land two Bravado basic attacks. When backing off after a trade, use two Bravado basic attacks on minions to get E back sooner.
taric-skill-bravado.text: Bravado makes Taric’s next two basic attacks faster and stronger after he uses an ability, and those attacks reduce his basic ability cooldowns. His basic rhythm is ability, then two attacks; without the attacks, his ability rotation slows by half. Even when backing off after a trade, using both attacks on minions brings E back noticeably sooner.

taric-skill-bravado-armor.basis: Bravado and E's bonus damage scale with bonus armor. Taric can deal strong damage in early melee trades.
taric-skill-bravado-armor.text: Bravado’s bonus damage and E’s damage both scale with bonus armor, so building armor improves Taric’s offense as well as his defense. Combined with his level 1 armor, which ranks among the highest of all champions, this makes his early melee trades hit harder than you might expect.

taric-skill-e.basis: E is a stun that activates after a short delay. Aim E ahead of time where the enemy will be when it activates. Land E as an enemy moves in to last-hit a minion. Follow an ally's immobilizing crowd control with E.
taric-skill-e.text: E (Dazzle) stuns after a short, clearly telegraphed delay, so aim at where the enemy will be when it activates rather than where they are now. Catch them as they step in to last-hit a minion, or follow an ally’s immobilizing crowd control to secure the hit.

taric-skill-q.basis: Q stores charges, and each Bravado basic attack that hits adds one charge. Q costs the same amount of mana regardless of how many charges you use. If it isn't urgent, save Q charges to heal several allies at once. Don't use a one-charge Q just to trigger Bravado.
taric-skill-q.text: Q (Starlight’s Touch) stores charges, gaining one each time a Bravado basic attack hits. Its mana cost stays the same regardless of how many charges it uses, so spending them one at a time is inefficient. Unless healing is urgent, save them to heal several allies at once; using a one-charge Q solely to trigger Bravado wastes mana.

taric-skill-r.basis: After a significant delay, R makes nearby allies immune to damage. Use R just before a fight or right after E, anticipating where things will stand a few seconds later. R's damage immunity does not prevent crowd control.
taric-skill-r.text: R Cosmic Radiance makes all nearby allies invulnerable after a significant delay, so casting it only once they are in danger is too late. Use it just before a fight begins or right after E, anticipating the situation a few seconds ahead. The invulnerability blocks damage but not crowd control; if allies are locked down when it activates, its duration ticks away while they cannot act.

taric-skill-w-link.basis: When an ally linked by W is nearby, Taric's abilities also activate from that ally's position. Before a teamfight, use W on an ally covering the side you won't stand on to extend your abilities' reach. Recasting W moves the link to another ally and grants a shield. When moving W to an ally in danger, account for the change in where your abilities will activate.
taric-skill-w-link.text: W (Bastion) gives Taric a second point from which to cast: while the linked ally is nearby, all his abilities also activate at that ally’s position. Before a teamfight, link someone on the side you will not occupy to cover more of your team. Recasting W moves the link and grants a shield, so switch it to allies in danger while accounting for where your abilities will now activate.

taric-teamfight.basis: If you're at the front in a teamfight, use W on a backline damage dealer. If you need to stay back in a teamfight, use W on an ally who is engaging. Engage when E is ready and you can account for R's activation delay.
taric-teamfight.text: Taric usually stands on the front line in teamfights, using W to extend his abilities to a second position. If you are up front, link a backline damage dealer; if you need to stay back, link an ally who is engaging. Go in when E is ready and you can cast R early enough to account for its delay.

teemo-combo-allin.basis: Use Q to block retaliatory autos, apply E's poison with an auto, then throw R into the enemy's retreat path to finish them off. Throw R where you predict the enemy will flee, rather than at their feet.
teemo-combo-allin.text: For the finishing combo, use Q Blinding Dart to stop a retaliatory auto, land an auto to apply E Toxic Shot’s poison, then throw R Noxious Trap into the enemy’s retreat path. Predict where they will flee and place the mushroom there, rather than at their feet, to layer on the slow and finish off their remaining health.

teemo-combo-trade.basis: Emerge from brush stealth with a surprise auto attack, follow with Q and one or two autos, then disengage with W. The attack speed boost from breaking stealth makes trades started from brush stronger than those started by walking up. E's poison keeps dealing damage after a single auto, so back off instead of staying close.
teemo-combo-trade.text: The basic trade is to wait stealthed in brush, emerge with a surprise auto, apply Q Blinding Dart, land one or two more autos, then disengage with W Move Quick. Breaking stealth grants attack speed, making this stronger than walking up to start a trade; one auto also leaves E Toxic Shot’s poison ticking, so there is no need to stay close.

teemo-laning.basis: Against melee opponents, use your range and E's poison to repeatedly land one auto and back off. In lane, use Q when the enemy starts a retaliatory auto. Teemo is very vulnerable to ganks. After pushing the lane, place R in the river and brush before resuming trades.
teemo-laning.text: Against melee opponents, use Teemo’s range and E Toxic Shot’s poison to chip away with repeated single autos followed by retreats. Save Q Blinding Dart for the moment they begin a retaliatory auto. His low defensive stats and movement speed make him highly vulnerable to ganks, so after pushing the lane, plant R Noxious Trap mushrooms in the river and brush before trading again.

teemo-phase.basis: From level 3 onward, Teemo enters his strongest laning phase against melee opponents. Even from level 3 onward, Teemo remains vulnerable in lane to poke opponents with longer range. From the mid game onward, Teemo excels at side lane play and map control through mushrooms. Teemo struggles to serve as a frontline in late-game head-on teamfights. Teemo racks up high damage per minute through damage over time and mushroom damage.
teemo-phase.text: From level 3 onward, Teemo is strongest in lane against melee opponents, but that same phase is a weakness against longer range poke. From mid game, he controls side lanes and the map with mushrooms; in late head on teamfights, he is too fragile to stand at the front. His high damage per minute reflects accumulated damage over time and mushroom damage.

teemo-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to survive while mushrooms and poison deal damage. Teemo has no mobility ability, making it hard for him to survive once caught. Mushrooms already placed and poison already applied keep dealing damage while you survive with Zhonya's Hourglass.
teemo-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in your core build. Teemo has no mobility ability and is fragile enough to die once caught, but mushrooms already planted and poison already applied keep dealing damage, so surviving briefly with Zhonya’s can make the exchange worthwhile.

teemo-skill-e.basis: E adds poison to autos, dealing damage over time. Use E's damage over time to repeatedly trade with one auto before backing off. Disengage immediately if a poisoned opponent approaches to retaliate.
teemo-skill-e.text: E Toxic Shot adds damage over time to Teemo’s autos, so a single hit keeps dealing damage after he backs away. Trade by repeatedly hitting and retreating rather than staying in range; if a poisoned opponent approaches to retaliate, disengage without hesitation.

teemo-skill-passive.basis: Stand still briefly without taking any action to enter stealth with P. Inside brush, P's stealth persists even while moving. Breaking P's stealth grants attack speed. Set up an ambush in brush ahead of time to use the attack speed gained from breaking stealth.
teemo-skill-passive.text: Teemo enters stealth through P Guerrilla Warfare after standing still briefly without acting, and he can remain stealthed while moving inside brush. Entering brush ahead of time sets up the ambush: breaking stealth grants attack speed, turning that preparation into damage.

teemo-skill-q.basis: Q's blind only disables basic attacks and does not block ability damage. Use Q to poke enemies who deal damage mainly through abilities. Time Q for the moment the enemy starts their auto attack animation.
teemo-skill-q.text: Q Blinding Dart disables basic attacks but does not stop abilities. It can negate an entire trade against an auto attack reliant opponent, while serving mainly as poke against an ability reliant one. Cast it as the enemy begins an auto; using it early wastes part of the blind duration.

teemo-skill-q-monster.basis: Q's blind lasts longer on minions and jungle monsters than on champions. When allies are clearing jungle camps or fighting large monsters, prioritize considering Q on the monster.
teemo-skill-q-monster.text: Q Blinding Dart lasts much longer on minions and jungle monsters than on champions. When your jungler is clearing a camp or your team is fighting over a large monster, consider using Q on the monster first; a single cast can be more valuable there than on a champion.

teemo-skill-r-bounce.basis: Throw R onto an existing mushroom to make it bounce and land farther away. Use mushroom bounces to place R over walls or in areas without vision without exposing yourself. R uses a charge system. If there is no urgency, save R charges to block a path with several mushrooms at once.
teemo-skill-r-bounce.text: Throwing R Noxious Trap onto an existing mushroom makes it bounce farther, letting you plant it over a wall or in an area without vision without exposing yourself. Because R stores charges, save them when there is no urgency and place several together to block an entire route.

teemo-skill-r-place.basis: Mushrooms placed with R last a long time. R's mushrooms reveal enemies who step on them. Place R around objectives and along enemy jungle routes to provide vision. Use R to clear the wave when you need to leave a side lane and rotate. Avoid spending all your R charges on farming so you have charges left to place where fights will happen.
teemo-skill-r-place.text: R Noxious Trap mushrooms last a long time and reveal enemies who step on them, so planting them around objectives and along enemy jungle routes also provides vision. They clear waves well when you need to leave a side lane and rotate, but spending every charge on farming leaves none for the places where fights will happen.

teemo-skill-w.basis: W's passive movement speed bonus stops when a champion or turret hits you. W's active movement speed bonus persists even while taking hits. Use W's active to move during fights. Use W to get a favorable fighting angle as well as to escape.
teemo-skill-w.text: W Move Quick’s passive movement speed ends when a champion or turret hits Teemo, while its active speed persists through hits. Use the passive to move before a fight and the active during one, whether to escape or take a favorable angle.

teemo-teamfight.basis: Place R in advance along enemy entry and retreat paths where a teamfight will happen. Once a teamfight starts, attack from the back with autos to apply E's poison. If you expect an objective fight, spend all your R charges placing mushrooms around the area before it starts.
teemo-teamfight.text: Teemo should prepare the site of a teamfight with R Noxious Trap mushrooms rather than enter the fight himself. Once it starts, stay back and apply E Toxic Shot’s poison with autos; the mushrooms should already cover the enemy’s entry and retreat routes. Before an expected objective fight, spend all available charges planting them around the area.

tf-combo-pick.basis: Lock in a gold card with W, move into auto-attack range, then use the stun auto, Q, and another auto in that order. A locked-in card disappears if you don’t use it with an auto-attack within 6 seconds. Pick a card from a distance where you can reach auto-attack range, then move in.
tf-combo-pick.text: For the basic combo, lock in a gold card with W (Pick a Card), move into auto-attack range, then stun with an auto, use Q (Wild Cards), and auto again. The locked card disappears if you do not use it within 6 seconds, so select it from a distance where you can reach auto-attack range before moving in.

tf-combo-ult.basis: When roaming, use R to gain vision, lock in a gold card, then use R to move. Stun with an auto attack as soon as you land, then use Q. Pick a gold card before using R to move.
tf-combo-ult.text: When roaming, use R (Destiny) to gain vision, lock in a gold card, then cast R again to move. Stun with an auto as soon as you land and follow with Q (Wild Cards); if you travel before selecting a card, your target can escape while you have nothing ready to use.

tf-laning.basis: In lane, focus on pushing the wave before looking for kills. Clear the back-line minions with Q to push the lane, then roam or establish vision. While your opponent clears the pushed wave, create a numbers advantage in another lane.
tf-laning.text: In lane, aim to push the wave first rather than chase kills. Clear the back-line minions with Q (Wild Cards), then use the time to roam or establish vision. While your opponent clears the pushed wave, create a numbers advantage in another lane.

tf-laning-poke.basis: Against melee opponents, keep poking from beyond Q range. Do not stand in front of a melee opponent when you have no gold card.
tf-laning-poke.text: Against melee opponents, repeatedly poking from beyond Q range can build an advantage. If they close the gap, a gold card stun is your only way out, so do not stand in front of them without a card ready.

tf-phase.basis: Avoid direct fights before level 6. Twisted Fate's first strong point comes at level 6, when he learns R. After level 6, push the lane and move to other lanes to build an advantage. In the late game, add damage from the back line and keep moving as you fight.
tf-phase.text: Before level 6, Twisted Fate has some of the lowest attack damage, health, and defensive stats, making direct fights unviable. Learning R gives him mapwide reach and his first power spike; from there, push the lane and build your lead by making plays in other lanes. He remains fragile in the late game, so keep dealing damage from the back line and moving around the map.

tf-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing keeps undoing your poke damage, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
tf-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing keeps undoing your poke damage, reduce it with Morellonomicon after completing one core item.

tf-skill-e.basis: E is a passive that increases attack speed and periodically adds damage to auto attacks. After pushing the lane, attack the turret briefly to make use of E's turret damage.
tf-skill-e.text: E (Stacked Deck) is a passive that increases attack speed and adds damage to every few auto-attacks. Its effect is reduced against structures, but it still helps take down turrets, making a brief window to hit one after pushing the lane worthwhile.

tf-skill-q.basis: Q's three cards spread in a fan, and only one can hit each target. To hit a champion behind the wave, angle Q around the side of the wave.
tf-skill-q.text: Q (Wild Cards) sends three cards out in a fan, but only one can hit each target. A straight cast will be caught by the front minions, so angle it around the side of the wave to reach a champion behind them.

tf-skill-r-cancel.basis: The teleport on R's second cast is canceled if you are hit by an interrupting effect. Use R to move from a position outside enemy vision.
tf-skill-r-cancel.text: The teleport on R’s (Destiny’s) second cast is canceled by interrupting effects. Cast it from outside enemy vision so an opponent cannot interrupt the move.

tf-skill-r-vision.basis: R grants vision across the entire map even if you do not move. Even without a good place to move, use R to locate the enemy jungler and mid laner and tell your team.
tf-skill-r-vision.text: R’s mapwide vision is often more valuable than its teleport. Using it without moving can reveal the enemy jungler and mid laner to your team and create an opportunity to fight over an objective, so you need not save R just because there is nowhere good to teleport.

tf-skill-w-cards.basis: W cycles through blue, red, then gold cards. Use a blue card to restore mana while holding the lane. Use a red card to damage and slow nearby targets when clearing waves or chasing. Use a gold card to stun when starting a fight. Count the card order to lock in the color you want quickly.
tf-skill-w-cards.text: W (Pick a Card) cycles through blue, red, and gold in that order. Blue restores mana for staying in lane, red damages and slows nearby targets for wave clear or chases, and gold stuns to start a fight. Count the sequence to lock in the color you want more quickly.

tf-skill-w-hold.basis: If you hold a gold card, opponents can see it and back away early. Use a gold card as soon as you lock it in and get close, or pick it outside enemy vision.
tf-skill-w-hold.text: Opponents can see a gold card in your hand and back away, so lock it in only when you can close the gap and use it immediately, or select it outside their vision. Holding a card throughout the laning phase wastes mana and costs you control of the wave.

tf-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, position at the very back and deal damage with Q. Stun enemies who jump onto your allies with a gold card. When enemies group up, hold your position and look for an angle to land Q.
tf-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay at the very back and deal damage with Q (Wild Cards), saving a gold card to stun enemies who jump onto your allies. Interrupt those enemies instead of initiating with a stun; grouped opponents make Q easier to land, so holding your position lets the damage add up.

thresh-combo-dive.basis: After landing Q, recast it to engage, block the path behind the enemy with R, then push them toward your allies with E. Only recast Q to engage deep when you can immediately bring an ally in with W.
thresh-combo-dive.text: After landing Death Sentence (Q), recast it to engage, block the path behind the enemy with The Box (R), then push them toward your allies with Flay (E). Only engage this deeply when you can immediately bring an ally in with Dark Passage (W).

thresh-combo-flay-first.basis: Q and E can be chained in either order. Against an enemy already close to you, pull them with E first, then use Q at close range. Q is easier to land immediately after E disrupts an enemy's movement.
thresh-combo-flay-first.text: Death Sentence (Q) and Flay (E) work in either order. Against an enemy already close to you, pull them in with Flay first, then cast Death Sentence at close range, where it is easier to land immediately after their movement is disrupted.

thresh-combo-hook-first.basis: After landing Q, basic attack, pull the enemy toward your allies with E, then use R to block their escape if needed. Chain E as Q's stun ends to keep the enemy immobilized.
thresh-combo-hook-first.text: After landing Death Sentence (Q), basic attack, pull the enemy toward your allies with Flay (E), then use The Box (R) to block their escape if needed. Time Flay for the moment Q's stun ends to keep the enemy immobilized.

thresh-laning.basis: Secure brush first to create Q angles hidden from the enemy. If the enemy pressures the brush, back off and collect souls. If enemies pressure the brush, switch to protecting your allied carry's CS.
thresh-laning.text: Secure brush first to find Death Sentence (Q) angles hidden from the enemy. If they pressure the brush, back off, collect souls, and protect your carry's CS.

thresh-phase-early.basis: Thresh can initiate in lane and create kill opportunities with Q as early as levels 1–2. Early on, focus on forcing enemies out of lane rather than getting kills. Focus on collecting souls in the early game.
thresh-phase-early.text: Thresh can initiate in lane and create kill opportunities with Death Sentence (Q) as early as levels 1–2. Early on, focus on forcing enemies out of lane and collecting souls rather than getting kills.

thresh-phase-scaling.basis: Thresh's late-game durability depends on how many souls he has collected. Keep collecting souls after laning by passing through fight locations and around jungle camps.
thresh-phase-scaling.text: Thresh's late-game durability depends on how many souls he collects, so keep gathering them after laning by passing through fight locations and around jungle camps.

thresh-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing prolongs fights, buy Oblivion Orb first for healing reduction. Thresh's abilities have ability power ratios, so he can make use of Oblivion Orb's ability power.
thresh-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing prolongs fights, buy Oblivion Orb first for healing reduction. Thresh's abilities have ability power ratios, so he can make use of the item's ability power.

thresh-situational-mikael.basis: Against a composition that locks down your carry with immobilizing effects, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build to remove them. W and E cannot remove immobilizing effects already applied to allies.
thresh-situational-mikael.text: Against a composition that immobilizes your carry, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build to remove those effects; Dark Passage (W) and Flay (E) cannot remove immobilization already applied to an ally.

thresh-skill-e.basis: E pushes or pulls enemies depending on the direction you sweep. Aim E in opposite directions when engaging and when protecting allies. From behind your allied carry, sweep E outward to peel off an assassin on them.
thresh-skill-e.text: Thresh’s E, Flay, pushes or pulls enemies in the direction you sweep: sweep from behind an enemy to pull them toward your allies, or from in front to push them away. That means you use it in opposite directions when engaging and protecting allies; to peel an assassin off your allied carry, stand behind the carry and sweep outward.

thresh-skill-e-passive.basis: E's passive grows stronger the longer you wait after your last basic attack. Save your basic attacks until you trade, then use them one at a time. In lane, combine one empowered basic attack with E to harass.
thresh-skill-e-passive.text: Flay (E)'s passive grows stronger the longer Thresh waits after his last basic attack, so save attacks until a trade and use them one at a time. In lane, pair one empowered attack with Flay to harass.

thresh-skill-passive.basis: Collecting souls permanently increases armor. Collecting souls permanently increases ability power. You can collect souls from units you did not kill yourself. Collected souls strengthen W's shield. Collected souls increase E's damage.
thresh-skill-passive.text: Through Damnation, each soul Thresh collects permanently increases his armor and ability power, even if he did not kill the unit; those souls also strengthen Dark Passage (W)'s shield and Flay (E)'s damage.

thresh-skill-passive-safety.basis: Stepping forward to collect souls leaves you vulnerable to attacks. Use W's lantern to collect souls within the enemy's range.
thresh-skill-passive-safety.text: Stepping forward to collect souls leaves Thresh vulnerable to attacks, so use Dark Passage (W)'s lantern to collect souls within enemy range.

thresh-skill-q.basis: Q has a long windup, making it easy for enemies to see and dodge in open areas. Use Q from brush or angles outside enemy vision. Use Q when an enemy is locked into a last-hit animation or an ability cast. Landing Q grants true sight of the target. Landing Q reduces its cooldown.
thresh-skill-q.text: Death Sentence (Q) has a long windup that enemies can see and dodge in the open, so cast it from brush or outside their vision, or while they are locked into a last-hit animation or ability cast. Landing it grants true sight of the target and reduces its cooldown.

thresh-skill-q-recast.basis: Recasting Q sends Thresh flying toward the enemy it hit. Do not recast Q where allies cannot follow up. Once your allies' engage is confirmed, recast Q to close in, then use E followed by R.
thresh-skill-q-recast.text: Recasting Death Sentence (Q) sends Thresh flying toward the enemy it hit, so leave it unrecast if allies cannot follow up. Once their engage is confirmed, recast it to close in, then follow with Flay (E) and The Box (R).

thresh-skill-r.basis: Only enemies who pass through an R wall take damage. Only enemies who pass through an R wall are heavily slowed. Once one R wall collapses, the remaining walls deal no damage. Once one R wall collapses, the slow duration of the remaining walls is halved. Place R to cover both the enemy's escape route and the direction their reinforcements will come from.
thresh-skill-r.text: Only enemies who pass through a wall of The Box (R) take damage and suffer its heavy slow. Once one wall collapses, the others deal no damage and their slow duration is halved, so place The Box to cover both the enemy's escape route and the direction their reinforcements will come from.

thresh-skill-w.basis: An ally must click the lantern themselves to travel with W. Coordinate with allies beforehand on how to use W's lantern. Use W to bring your allied jungler into lane from across a wall. W shields Thresh and the first ally to take the lantern. Use W just before enemy burst damage lands.
thresh-skill-w.text: An ally must click the Dark Passage (W) lantern to travel with it, so coordinate its use beforehand. It can bring your jungler into lane from across a wall, and it shields Thresh and the first ally to take it; throw it just before enemy burst damage lands.

thresh-teamfight.basis: Choose between engaging and protecting allies based on the teamfight setup. Hold Q when your allies are fighting from the back. When your allies are fighting from the back, use E to peel enemies off your carry. When your allied engage champion goes in first, target an enemy in the backline with Q.
thresh-teamfight.text: Choose whether to engage or protect allies based on the teamfight setup. When your team fights from the back, hold Death Sentence (Q) and use Flay (E) to peel enemies off your carry; when an allied engage champion goes in first, target a backline enemy with Q.

thresh-teamfight-r-escape.basis: When allies are being chased, place R's walls across the pursuit route to slow enemies. When using R to retreat, angle its walls differently than when trapping enemies.
thresh-teamfight-r-escape.text: When allies are being chased, place The Box (R)'s walls across the pursuit route to slow the enemy, and angle them differently for a retreat than you would to trap opponents.

tristana-combo-burst.basis: Apply E, build stacks with basic attacks, use Q to increase attack speed, then detonate the final stack with W. If you jump in, detonate the bomb, and get a takedown, W resets.
tristana-combo-burst.text: For a finishing combo, attach E Explosive Charge, build stacks with basic attacks, then activate Q Rapid Fire to stack it faster and detonate the final stack with W Rocket Jump. If the explosion helps secure a takedown as you jump in, W resets so you can jump straight back out.

tristana-combo-e-reset.basis: E Explosive Charge resets Tristana's basic attack animation. Use E right after a basic attack lands, then follow with another basic attack. Pressing E during a basic attack's windup cancels that attack.
tristana-combo-e-reset.text: E Explosive Charge resets Tristana’s basic attack animation: press it immediately after a basic attack lands, then attack again to fit an extra hit into the same window. Pressing E during an attack’s windup cancels that attack, so use them in sequence rather than at the same time.

tristana-combo-jump-r.basis: Jump over an enemy with W, then use R to knock them toward an ally or allied turret. Only use the W jump-over combo when the enemy cannot immediately retaliate. After jumping over the enemy with W, you remain on their side. You can use R while airborne during W to disengage.
tristana-combo-jump-r.text: Jump over an enemy with W Rocket Jump, then use R Buster Shot to knock them toward an ally or allied turret. This is powerful, but it leaves you on the enemy’s side with W unavailable, so use it only when they cannot immediately retaliate. You can also cast abilities while airborne, allowing you to combine W and R to disengage.

tristana-laning-siege.basis: If the enemy is absent from lane, push immediately to pressure the turret. Use Q and E together to damage a turret quickly. Do not start pressuring a turret while W is on cooldown.
tristana-laning-siege.text: When the enemy is absent from lane, push immediately to pressure the turret. Using Q Rapid Fire and E Explosive Charge together damages it quickly, making Tristana’s pushing power a strength. Do not start pressuring the turret while W Rocket Jump is on cooldown.

tristana-laning-wave.basis: E's passive naturally pushes the lane. Consciously choose whether to push the lane to pressure the turret and vision or avoid hitting minions with E damage to let the lane push toward you.
tristana-laning-wave.text: E Explosive Charge’s passive naturally pushes the lane. Choose deliberately between accepting the push to pressure the enemy turret and secure vision, or keeping E’s damage off minions so the lane pushes toward you. Pushing without thinking leaves you vulnerable to the enemy jungler.

tristana-phase.basis: Tristana is weak early because her cooldowns are long and her damage is low. Early on, farm with E's passive and play safely. Her burst remains underwhelming through the mid game until she has attack damage items. Her damage is strong with a completed build, so longer games favor her.
tristana-phase.text: Tristana is weakest early, when her cooldowns are long and her damage is low. Farm safely through that stage with E Explosive Charge’s passive. Her burst remains underwhelming into the mid game until she gets attack damage items, but her damage with a completed build is among the best, so longer games favor her.

tristana-skill-e-charge.basis: If you apply E to a champion, build it to maximum stacks. Do not use E if the enemy is about to escape. Apply E at the start of a fight so you have time to build stacks. Keep attacking the target with E to increase its explosion damage.
tristana-skill-e-charge.text: If you apply E Explosive Charge to a champion, build it to maximum stacks. Skip it if the enemy is about to escape; apply it as a fight begins so you have time to stack it, then keep hitting that target with basic attacks or abilities to increase the explosion damage.

tristana-skill-e-passive.basis: E's passive deals area damage when you kill an enemy with a basic attack. Kill a low-health minion near an enemy champion to hit them with E's damage. When minions are grouped, kill the weakest one first.
tristana-skill-e-passive.text: E Explosive Charge’s passive deals area damage when a basic attack kills an enemy. Since this is effectively your only early poke, last-hit a low-health minion on the side nearest the enemy champion to catch them in the damage. When minions are grouped, kill the weakest one first to make the remaining last hits easier.

tristana-skill-passive-range.basis: As Tristana levels up, P Draw a Bead increases her basic attack and ability range. In late-game teamfights, use the extra range to attack from afar.
tristana-skill-passive-range.text: As Tristana levels up, P Draw a Bead increases both her basic attack and ability range. Late in the game, she can attack from farther away than most marksmen, so use that range advantage in teamfights without jumping in unnecessarily.

tristana-skill-w-dash.basis: W Rocket Jump counts as a dash. Traps at your W landing spot will trigger. Enemy crowd control can interrupt W while you are airborne. Use W to escape area-of-effect skillshots.
tristana-skill-w-dash.text: Despite its appearance, W Rocket Jump counts as a dash: traps at your landing spot trigger, and enemy crowd control can interrupt you while airborne. It works well for escaping area skillshots, but it will not let you ignore guaranteed crowd control.

tristana-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, use your range advantage to basic attack from the back. Save W to disengage in teamfights. Only jump in with W when the enemy formation has broken and a takedown is certain. After jumping in, use the reset W to reach the next target.
tristana-teamfight.text: In teamfights, use your range advantage to basic attack from the back and save W Rocket Jump to disengage. Jump in only when the enemy formation has collapsed and a takedown is certain, then use the W reset to reach your next target.

tristana-teamfight-r.basis: Use R to knock away an enemy who jumps on an ally. Use R to interrupt a dangerous cast. R can knock several grouped enemies over a wall. When needed, use R to knock an enemy toward your team.
tristana-teamfight-r.text: R Buster Shot is primarily a knockback tool rather than a source of damage. Use it to peel an enemy off an ally or interrupt a dangerous cast; it can also knock several grouped enemies over a wall. You do not always need to send an enemy away, so consider knocking them toward your team when appropriate.

trundle-combo-e-cut.basis: When chasing, use W to catch up, place E ahead of the enemy's path, then use Q on them after the pillar knocks them back. When disengaging, place E between yourself and the pursuer.
trundle-combo-e-cut.text: To chase, use W to gain movement speed and catch up, place E ahead of the enemy’s path, then hit them with Q after the pillar knocks them back. A pillar placed behind them blocks nothing, so set it where they are headed; when disengaging, place it between yourself and your pursuer.

trundle-combo-r.basis: Use R right after starting a fight, while the enemy still cannot escape. When engaging, cast W, use R, block the escape route with E, then land a Q empowered auto attack.
trundle-combo-r.text: Use R immediately after starting a fight, while the enemy cannot yet escape: half its damage and armor and magic resistance steal apply at once, and the rest over its duration, so you need to stay on the target. Engage by placing W, casting R, blocking the escape route with E, and landing a Q empowered auto attack.

trundle-laning.basis: As the enemy steps forward to last hit, close in with W and use Q. Using E in a trade quickly drains mana. In lane, save E for ganks.
trundle-laning.text: Trundle’s level 1 attack damage and movement speed are among the highest, making him strong in auto attack fights. When an enemy steps forward to last hit, move in on W and hit them with Q so their attack damage is reduced as they retaliate. Adding E to trades drains mana quickly, so save it for responding to ganks.

trundle-laning-wave.basis: Trundle has no area damage ability to push the lane himself, so waves naturally stack up. Keep the wave in the middle and apply pressure from a distance where you can close in on the enemy at any time. Only push the lane and recall when the enemy leaves lane or backs off with low health.
trundle-laning-wave.text: Trundle has no area damage ability to push the lane himself, so waves naturally stack up. Work with that tendency: keeping the wave in the middle and pressuring from a distance where you can engage at any time is safer than pushing it toward the enemy tower. Push and recall only when the enemy leaves lane or retreats with low health.

trundle-phase.basis: Trundle is strong from the start of lane. Trundle is strong in one on one fights after reaching level 6 and getting R. Trundle is strong in midgame objective fights when his core items come in. In the late game, shift to holding one enemy in the side lane.
trundle-phase.text: Trundle’s high base attack damage makes him strong from the start of lane, though his abilities alone do not deal explosive damage, so his early numbers are less striking. His strongest periods are one on one fights after he gains R at level 6 and midgame objective fights once he has core items. In the late game, his lack of area damage reduces his teamfight impact, so shift to holding one enemy in the side lane.

trundle-skill-e.basis: E creates impassable terrain and pushes enemies directly on top of the pillar away. Place E in a narrow path or beside a wall to block passage. Use E to draw out a terrain crossing ability from an enemy who has one.
trundle-skill-e.text: E creates impassable terrain and pushes away enemies directly on top of the pillar. Placing it in a narrow path or beside a wall can block the passage entirely, making it strongest around river and jungle entrances. Against an enemy without a way to cross terrain, it can effectively trap them; against one who can cross, use it to draw out that ability.

trundle-skill-e-gank.basis: If you are in a position to be ganked, place E on the jungler's approach to delay their entry. When your jungler comes to gank, place E on the enemy's escape route. In lane, save E to respond to ganks.
trundle-skill-e-gank.text: E also helps you respond to ganks. If your lane is pushed up and you are vulnerable, place it on the jungler's approach to delay their entry; when your jungler comes to gank, put it on the enemy's escape route. Spending E on lane trades leaves you without that response.

trundle-skill-passive.basis: When an enemy unit dies nearby, P heals you based on that unit's maximum health. When you are low on health, decide whether to clear the wave to heal.
trundle-skill-passive.text: P heals you based on an enemy unit’s maximum health whenever it dies nearby. Each minion provides healing, so a large clashing wave can steadily restore your health, while high health jungle monsters provide even more when killed. If you are low, consider clearing the wave to heal instead of recalling immediately.

trundle-skill-r.basis: R deals damage based on the target's maximum health and steals armor and magic resistance. Use R on the tankiest enemy.
trundle-skill-r.text: R deals damage based on the target’s maximum health and steals armor and magic resistance, so it gives the most value against the tankiest enemy. It weakens their frontline while making Trundle tougher; using it on an already fragile target yields fewer defensive stats.

trundle-skill-w.basis: In W's area, your attack speed, movement speed, and healing received increase. Cast W where you expect the fight to happen. When engaging with allies, place W around where they will stand.
trundle-skill-w.text: W creates an area that lasts for its duration, giving you a way to choose where to fight. Your attack speed, movement speed, and healing received increase only while you stand in it, so place it where you expect the fight and draw the enemy inside. Securing that ground early is much stronger than casting W after the fight begins. Its healing bonus also applies to heals from an allied support, so when engaging with allies, place W where they will stand.

trundle-teamfight.basis: Trundle has no dash. In teamfights, place W in front of your team's formation, split the enemy formation with E, then take down the separated side first. Once the fight has started, use R on the enemy frontline.
trundle-teamfight.text: Trundle has no dash, so do not walk straight into a teamfight. Place W in front of your team to set the fighting area, use E to split the enemy formation, and take down the separated side first. R weakens the frontline rather than preventing escape, so cast it on the foremost enemy once the fight is underway.

tryndamere-combo-allin.basis: When going all in, use W to lower the enemy's attack damage, then close in with E. Once you're close, use W to slow the enemy when they turn their back and start fleeing.
tryndamere-combo-allin.text: When going all in, use W to lower the enemy’s attack damage before closing in with E. If you lead with E, they can fight back at full attack damage and turn the trade around. Once you’re close, build Fury with basic attacks; when they start to flee, W slows them as soon as they turn their back.

tryndamere-combo-e-reset.basis: Each critical strike reduces E's cooldown, and critical strikes against champions reduce it further. If you used E to engage, keep landing basic attacks to get E back for your escape. Make sure you have enough Fury before engaging with E. If your critical strike chance is low, using E to engage can leave you trapped without E to escape.
tryndamere-combo-e-reset.text: Each critical strike reduces E’s cooldown, with a larger reduction when you critically strike a champion. After using E to engage, keep landing basic attacks to get it back for your escape; engaging with a low critical strike chance can leave you trapped. Check that you have enough Fury before going in.

tryndamere-combo-r-escape.basis: R can be activated even while under crowd control. When death is certain, activate R, then escape with E and Flash before it expires. When death is certain, activate R, then heal with Q to keep fighting. Plan your escape route first so your health isn't depleted when R ends.
tryndamere-combo-r-escape.text: R can be activated even while you’re under crowd control. When death is certain, use it, then either escape with E and Flash before it expires or heal with Q and keep fighting. Plan your escape route before activating R, since surviving until it ends means little if your health is depleted.

tryndamere-laning-farm.basis: Tryndamere ranks among the best in CS and turret plates at 14 minutes. Tryndamere's advantages come from staying in lane and pressuring turrets. Clear waves quickly with E and basic attacks. Attack the turret whenever the enemy cannot stay in lane.
tryndamere-laning-farm.text: Tryndamere ranks among the best in CS and turret plates at 14 minutes: his advantages come from staying in lane and pressuring turrets rather than getting kills. With no resource cost, he can clear waves quickly using E and basic attacks, then hit the turret whenever the enemy cannot stay in lane.

tryndamere-laning-trade.basis: Against ranged opponents, wait until they enter E range. If a ranged opponent stays outside E range, take some damage to secure CS. Against melee opponents, build Fury, then use W to lower their attack damage before going in.
tryndamere-laning-trade.text: Against ranged opponents, accept some damage to secure CS while waiting for them to enter E range. Check river vision before closing in, since using E only to engage leaves you without an escape if a gank comes. Against melee opponents, build Fury first, then use W to lower their attack damage before going in.

tryndamere-phase.basis: Tryndamere has no resource cost, so he can keep using abilities from level 1. Early on, he has no critical strike chance, so his trades are weak. Learning R at level 6 is his first turning point. His one on one fights become stronger from mid game as he builds critical strike items. If your team lacks damage in late game teamfights, create value by split pushing.
tryndamere-phase.text: Tryndamere’s abilities cost no resource, so he can keep using them from level 1, though his trades are weak before he has critical strike chance. Level 6 and R mark his first turning point, and from mid game, critical strike items make him nearly unbeatable one on one. Late game, if your team lacks teamfight damage, split pushing is his only way to create value.

tryndamere-situational-armorpen.basis: If enemy armor reduces your basic attack damage, buy Last Whisper or Lord Dominik's Regards for armor penetration. If the enemy builds armor, move up your armor penetration purchase after completing one core item.
tryndamere-situational-armorpen.text: When enemy armor starts to blunt your basic attacks, buy Last Whisper or Lord Dominik’s Regards for armor penetration. Critical strike items lose value sharply against armor, so move the penetration purchase up after completing one core item.

tryndamere-skill-e-wave.basis: E cuts through every enemy in its path. Using E through a minion wave builds Fury multiple times at once. Just before a fight, use E to engage through the wave and build Fury.
tryndamere-skill-e-wave.text: E cuts through every enemy in its path. Using it through a minion wave builds Fury multiple times at once and greatly raises your critical strike chance, making a dash across the wave just before a fight the fastest way to build Fury while engaging.

tryndamere-skill-passive.basis: Fury drains after you've been out of combat for a while. Hit minions or jungle monsters to build Fury just before a fight.
tryndamere-skill-passive.text: Fury drains after you’ve been out of combat for a while, so hit minions or jungle monsters just before engaging to start the fight with a chance to critically strike. With no Fury, Tryndamere is just a basic-attack champion.

tryndamere-skill-q-timing.basis: Q's passive increases attack damage based on missing health. If you can survive, delay Q's heal to keep the attack damage gained from missing health. Q's healing scales with your remaining Fury. Use Q before your Fury drains.
tryndamere-skill-q-timing.text: Q’s passive grants attack damage based on missing health, so healing as soon as you take damage gives up that damage. If you can survive, delay Q until you need it, but use it before your Fury drains because its healing scales with the Fury you have left.

tryndamere-skill-r-bait.basis: Hold R until just before you die instead of activating it early. After making the enemy use their abilities and Flash, survive with R and look to turn the fight. If you activate R early, the enemy can back away and wait out its duration.
tryndamere-skill-r-bait.text: Hold R until just before you die, giving the enemy reason to commit their abilities and Flash because they think they can finish you. Surviving after that can turn the fight; activate R too early and they can simply back away until it expires.

tryndamere-skill-w.basis: W only slows enemies whose backs are turned to Tryndamere. When chasing, use W as the enemy starts to flee. When fighting face to face, use W's attack damage reduction to weaken the enemy's basic attacks.
tryndamere-skill-w.text: W only slows enemies whose backs are turned to Tryndamere, so time it for when a fleeing target starts to run. In a face-to-face trade, use its attack damage reduction to weaken a round of the enemy’s basic attacks rather than counting on the slow.

tryndamere-splitpush.basis: With R available, you can survive even if two enemies come for you in a side lane. When an objective is coming up, push the opposite side lane to draw enemy players away. Without R available, you are at high risk of dying in a side lane.
tryndamere-splitpush.text: With R available, Tryndamere can survive even when two enemies come for him in a side lane. When an objective is coming up, pushing the opposite side to draw enemy players away is often more valuable than joining the teamfight; without R, staying in the side lane can simply get him killed.

tryndamere-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, approach from the side or behind and target the enemy ranged carry. Enter the teamfight, draw focused attacks, then activate R just before dying and take out the carry. Engage as soon as the enemy uses its immobilizing crowd control on your front line.
tryndamere-teamfight.text: In teamfights, go around the side or back to target the enemy ranged carry instead of fighting the front line. Engage after the enemy uses its immobilizing crowd control on your front line, draw their focused attacks, then activate R just before dying and take out the carry during its duration.

twitch-combo-burst.basis: Use Q to approach from the side, stack Deadly Venom with W and basic attacks, then finish with E. Throw W at the feet of an approaching enemy. Do not use E when Deadly Venom has few stacks.
twitch-combo-burst.text: Approach from behind or the side with Q camouflage, throw W at the enemy’s feet to slow them and apply Deadly Venom, then build more stacks with basic attacks before finishing with E. E’s damage depends on the number of Deadly Venom stacks, so using it too early can ruin the combo.

twitch-combo-e-finish.basis: E does not target an enemy, so it hits enemies within range even if they leave vision. If an enemy you are chasing with basic attacks is about to escape, finish them with E. Save E during a trade if you have too few Deadly Venom stacks.
twitch-combo-e-finish.text: E (Contaminate) needs no target and hits enemies in its wide range even if they enter brush or leave vision. Hold it to finish an enemy who is about to escape while you chase with basic attacks; using it midway through a trade for a little extra damage leaves it weak if Deadly Venom has too few stacks.

twitch-combo-r.basis: Activating R alone does not break camouflage. Your first basic attack during camouflage reveals you. Position with Q, activate R, then start attacking from an angle that lets your attacks pierce enemies.
twitch-combo-r.text: Activating R does not break camouflage; your first basic attack does. Position while hidden with Q, activate R, then begin attacking along a line that lets your shots pierce enemies. You reveal yourself with the increased range already active, forcing enemies to react after you have gained a range advantage.

twitch-laning.basis: Twitch is weak in basic attack trades, but can threaten a kill with E after stacking Deadly Venom. Twitch builds a lane advantage through kill opportunities rather than farming. In lane, gradually chip away at the enemy's health with Deadly Venom. Wait for the enemy to enter E range.
twitch-laning.text: Twitch is weak in basic attack trades, but E (Contaminate) remains a kill threat once Deadly Venom is stacked. His kills at 14 minutes rank near the top while his CS ranks near the bottom, so he gets ahead through kill opportunities rather than farming. Chip away at the enemy with Deadly Venom and wait for them to enter E range.

twitch-laning-roam.basis: Use Q to hide in brush or by the river and get behind the enemy. When Twitch disappears from vision, enemies may back off, giving him control of the wave. Q's camouflage lasts long enough to reach another lane. Tell your teammates when you leave lane.
twitch-laning-roam.text: In lane, look to use Q (Ambush) from brush or the river to get behind the enemy. Even without a kill, Twitch disappearing can force them back and give you control of the wave. Camouflage lasts long enough to reach another lane, though, so tell your teammates when you leave to keep them from misreading your position.

twitch-phase.basis: Twitch is weakest at levels 1 and 2. As E levels up, its damage per Deadly Venom stack increases, creating kill opportunities. Twitch is strong in the mid to late game once he has attack speed and critical strike. Look for early kills, but do not overextend and die.
twitch-phase.text: Twitch is weakest at levels 1 and 2. As E (Contaminate) levels up, its damage per Deadly Venom stack creates kill opportunities, and he peaks in the mid to late game when attack speed and critical strike come together. Win rate also rises sharply once three core items are completed, so look for early kills without overextending and dying.

twitch-situational-antiheal.basis: Deadly Venom's damage over time is easily offset by enemy healing. If enemy healing offsets Deadly Venom's damage, buy Executioner's Calling after one core item.
twitch-situational-antiheal.text: Deadly Venom deals damage over time that enemy healing can readily offset. If healing cancels out that damage, buy Executioner’s Calling after one core item.

twitch-situational-qss.basis: Consider Mercurial Scimitar if the enemy has persistent crowd control that restricts your movement. If your movement is restricted while attacking with R, it is hard to use your range advantage.
twitch-situational-qss.text: Consider Mercurial Scimitar against persistent crowd control that restricts movement. Twitch needs to hold his position to deal damage with R (Spray and Pray); being locked down removes his range advantage and leaves him vulnerable to being caught.

twitch-skill-e.basis: E deals damage per stack to every nearby enemy affected by Deadly Venom. If several enemies have Deadly Venom stacks, finish them together with E. Max E first. Build Deadly Venom stacks with basic attacks and W, then use E last.
twitch-skill-e.text: E (Contaminate) deals damage per Deadly Venom stack to every affected enemy nearby, making it both a finisher against one target and a way to clean up several in a teamfight. That is why maxing E first has become standard in the statistics: build stacks with basic attacks and W (Venom Cask), then use E last.

twitch-skill-passive.basis: Deadly Venom deals true damage and gains a stack each time a basic attack hits. Deadly Venom stacks disappear after a while. Deadly Venom's true damage is unaffected by enemy armor. Q's cooldown resets when an enemy champion affected by Deadly Venom dies. Check whether you can use Q again right after a kill.
twitch-skill-passive.text: Each basic attack that hits adds a stack of Deadly Venom, which deals true damage unaffected by armor and expires after a while. When an enemy champion affected by it dies, Q (Ambush) resets, letting you hide and reposition after each takedown in a teamfight. Check whether Q is available immediately after a kill.

twitch-skill-q.basis: Q grants camouflage and increased movement speed. Q grants more movement speed near enemies who cannot see you. An enemy who gets very close reveals you during camouflage. Use brush and indirect paths when approaching with Q. Start the fight after camouflage ends, while your attack speed is increased.
twitch-skill-q.text: Q (Ambush) grants camouflage and movement speed, with a larger speed boost near enemies who cannot see you. Very close enemies reveal you, so approach through brush or along a flanking route instead of coming straight in. Since Q also grants attack speed when camouflage ends, ideally use its full duration and enter the fight with that boost active.

twitch-skill-r.basis: R increases basic attack range and makes attacks pierce enemies. Before activating R, move to a position where the enemies line up. R basic attacks deal slightly less damage each time they pierce an enemy. R's piercing damage has a minimum, so targets farther back still take damage.
twitch-skill-r.text: R (Spray and Pray) is valuable chiefly for its added range and piercing basic attacks. Before activating it, move sideways to line enemies up so the piercing matters. Damage drops slightly with each target pierced but has a minimum, so targets farther back still take meaningful damage.

twitch-skill-w.basis: W has longer range than basic attacks. Enemies inside W's poison cloud keep gaining Deadly Venom stacks. Throw W ahead of the enemy's path. Slow the enemy with W, stack Deadly Venom, then finish with E.
twitch-skill-w.text: W reaches farther than basic attacks, letting you hold enemies who are outside your attack range. Its poison cloud keeps applying Deadly Venom while they remain inside it, so throw W ahead of their path rather than at their current position. Use its slow and stacks to set up an E finish.

twitch-teamfight.basis: Do not stand at the front in teamfights. Use Q to reach the flank or backline, activate R, then fire basic attacks through grouped enemies. Reveal yourself after the enemy has used their engage abilities on your frontline. When an enemy dies and Q resets, reposition.
