twitch-teamfight.text: Stay off the front line in teamfights: use Q to reach a flank or a position behind the enemy, activate R, and fire basic attacks through grouped enemies. Twitch has low health and armor, so a single targeted crowd control ability can end the fight for him; wait until the enemy has used their engage abilities on your frontline before revealing yourself. When someone dies and Q resets, reposition.

udyr-combo-awaken.basis: To Awaken a stance, press its key again while it is on cooldown. Awakening resets that stance’s cooldown and adds an ultimate effect. You can use Awakening only once per fight, so choose which stance to Awaken before engaging.
udyr-combo-awaken.text: To Awaken a stance, press its key again while that stance is on cooldown. Doing so immediately after activating it resets its cooldown and adds an ultimate effect. Awakening has its own cooldown and can be used only once per fight, so decide which stance to Awaken before engaging.

udyr-combo-engage.basis: Approach with E, stun with the first basic attack, land two Q empowered basic attacks, then withstand damage with W. E’s stun applies only to the first attack against each target after activating the stance. Switch to Q right after stunning with E to deal damage.
udyr-combo-engage.text: For a gank, approach with E (Blazing Stampede), stun with the first basic attack, switch to Q (Wilding Claw) for two empowered attacks, then use W (Iron Mantle) to withstand damage. E stuns a target only on the first hit after you activate the stance, so switch to Q and deal damage as soon as the stun lands.

udyr-combo-rotation.basis: After activating a stance, use two empowered basic attacks, then switch to the next stance. The stance effect applies to the next two basic attacks. The next two basic attacks after using an ability gain attack speed.
udyr-combo-rotation.text: The basic rotation is to activate a stance, land two empowered basic attacks, then switch stances and land two more. Each stance affects your next two basic attacks, so switching before using both wastes the remaining effect. Those two attacks gain attack speed after an ability, and each hit reduces Awaken’s cooldown; treat stance changes and basic attacks as a pair.

udyr-ganking.basis: Udyr’s only guaranteed crowd control is his E stun, and he has no ranged way to engage. Start ganks from brush or behind terrain, or go in after an ally’s crowd control. Look for a gank from behind when the enemy is pushing the lane. If Udyr approaches head-on, a single enemy mobility ability can easily foil his gank.
udyr-ganking.text: Udyr’s only guaranteed crowd control is the stun from E (Blazing Stampede), and he has no ranged engage. Gank only when you can get close: start from brush or behind terrain, or enter after an ally applies crowd control. Catching an enemy from behind while they push the lane is the most reliable approach; walking in from the front lets them escape with a single mobility ability.

udyr-jungle-route.basis: Udyr moves quickly between camps thanks to his high movement speed and E’s speed boost. Path deep into the enemy jungle, alternating between camps and lane ganks. Udyr sustains his health by switching stances, letting him jungle for a long time without recalling.
udyr-jungle-route.text: Udyr has one of the highest movement speeds among champions, and E (Blazing Stampede) makes him faster still, letting him move between camps exceptionally quickly. Take long routes through the enemy jungle and alternate lane ganks with camps to build experience and vision advantages. Switching stances sustains his health, allowing him to stay out for a long time without recalling.

udyr-phase.basis: Udyr puts levels into one ability, making his early camp clears and 1v1s strong. Udyr is strongest in the early and mid game, when jungle pressure and objective fights are frequent. Late in the game, Udyr’s lack of range and area damage pushes him toward a frontline role. Secure your lead through early and mid-game objectives and control of the enemy jungle.
udyr-phase.text: Putting levels into one ability gives Udyr strong early camp clears and 1v1s. He peaks in the early and mid game, when jungle pressure and objective fights are frequent. Later, his limited range and area damage shift him from a damage dealer toward the frontline, so use objectives and control of the enemy jungle to secure your lead before then.

udyr-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing could turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Udyr stays close and keeps basic attacking, so he can easily maintain Grievous Wounds.
udyr-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing could turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Udyr stays close and keeps basic attacking, allowing him to maintain Grievous Wounds.

udyr-situational-armor.basis: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy’s physical damage is strong. Building armor first greatly increases your effective durability alongside the W shield.
udyr-situational-armor.text: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy’s physical damage is strong. Because armor increases the effective protection of the W (Iron Mantle) shield, building it first also gives Udyr a substantial durability boost.

udyr-skill-e.basis: Awakened E briefly blocks immobilizing and disrupting effects and ignores unit collision. Use Awakened E when unavoidable crowd control is coming. E stance’s basic attack is not canceled by knockbacks or pulls.
udyr-skill-e.text: Awakened E briefly grants immunity to immobilizing and disruptive effects and lets Udyr pass through units. If you know which guaranteed crowd control the opponent has, activate it as that ability arrives to push through. Basic attacks in this stance cannot be canceled, so the attack still lands even if Udyr is knocked back or pulled.

udyr-skill-q.basis: Q empowered basic attacks deal damage based on maximum health to high-health enemies and objectives. Q’s temporary range increase lets you hit melee opponents slightly earlier. Use Q as your main stance in 1v1s and when clearing camps. Alternate Q and W while jungling to reduce health loss.
udyr-skill-q.text: Q (Wilding Claw) adds maximum health based damage to empowered basic attacks, making it effective against high health enemies and objectives. Its brief range increase also lets Udyr hit melee opponents slightly sooner. Use Q as your main stance in 1v1s and camp clears, alternating it with W (Iron Mantle) to clear the jungle without losing health.

udyr-skill-r.basis: R’s storm stance deals area damage over time and slows nearby enemies. Use R in fights where several players are grouped together. Use Q over R in 1v1s. Basic attack a fleeing target before Awakening R so the storm follows them.
udyr-skill-r.text: R (Wingborne Storm) deals area damage over time and slows nearby enemies, making it more valuable in crowded fights; Q (Wilding Claw) is better in a 1v1. Awakened R leaves a storm that follows the last enemy Udyr basic attacked, so hit a target likely to flee before Awakening it.

udyr-skill-w-shield.basis: The W shield is depleted after defensive stats reduce the damage. Increasing armor and magic resistance lets the W shield absorb more actual damage.
udyr-skill-w-shield.text: The W shield is depleted only after armor and magic resistance reduce incoming damage. Raising those stats therefore lets the same shield withstand more actual damage, making defensive items more effective on Udyr than on other champions.

udyr-skill-w-timing.basis: Activate the W shield just before a large hit lands. If you need to withstand damage over time, Awaken W for healing over time.
udyr-skill-w-timing.text: Activating W after taking a hit wastes the shield, so use it just before a large hit lands. If you need to endure sustained damage for a long time, Awaken W instead to gain healing over time based on maximum health.

udyr-teamfight.basis: Engage in teamfights when Awakened E can get you past the enemy’s crowd control that stops engages. If you cannot get past that crowd control, stay beside your frontline, keep dealing R damage, and meet the enemy’s engage. Once you reach the enemy, withstand damage with W and body-block the damage dealers’ path.
udyr-teamfight.text: Engage a teamfight when Awakened E (Blazing Stampede) can carry you through the enemy crowd control that would stop your entry. If it cannot, stay beside your frontline, maintain area damage with R (Wingborne Storm), and meet enemies who engage. Once you get close, use W (Iron Mantle) to withstand damage and body block the enemy damage dealers’ path.

urgot-combo-basic.basis: In basic trades, weave in basic attacks while W is active. Both basic attacks and W shots trigger leg cannons. In trades, stay close to your opponent and keep firing with W active.
urgot-combo-basic.text: For basic trades, weave basic attacks into W fire. Both trigger Urgot’s leg cannons, so his damage depends on how long he keeps firing; staying close with W active is more rewarding than trading briefly and backing away.

urgot-combo-engage.basis: Slow your opponent with Q, then dash in with E to stun and throw them before dealing damage with W and basic attacks. E stops at the first champion it hits and cannot cross terrain. Slow your opponent with Q first to land E. An opponent hit by E is thrown behind Urgot. To throw an opponent toward your allies, face away from your allies when using E.
urgot-combo-engage.text: Start by slowing your opponent with Q, then dash in with E to stun and throw them before using W and basic attacks. E stops at the first champion it hits and cannot cross terrain, so Q’s strong slow helps secure the hit. E always throws its target behind Urgot; to throw someone toward your allies, start E with your back to them.

urgot-combo-legs.basis: There is one cannon on each of Urgot's six legs, and each has its own cooldown. If the cannon facing the target is on cooldown, that shot deals no cannon damage. Circle your opponent to point legs that can still fire toward them.
urgot-combo-legs.text: Urgot has a cannon on each of his six legs, each with its own cooldown. A shot gains no cannon damage if the leg facing the target is on cooldown, so circle your opponent to bring ready cannons into range. That movement makes the difference between standing still and dealing much more damage.

urgot-combo-r.basis: Land R, lower the target's health with Q, W, and basic attacks, then recast R to execute them. R's slow grows stronger the more health the target has lost. If the target falls below the execution threshold, R triggers automatically when its duration ends, so there is no need to rush the recast.
urgot-combo-r.text: Land R to slow the target, use Q, W, and basic attacks to bring them below the execution threshold, then recast R to pull them in and execute them. The slow grows stronger as the target loses health, making escape harder as you deal damage. If they remain below the threshold when R’s duration ends, it activates automatically, so there is no need to rush the recast.

urgot-laning.basis: Urgot is classified as a ranged champion, but his range is very short. Urgot has an advantage against melee opponents and a disadvantage against long-range opponents. In lane, approach with W active and pressure your opponent by circling to fire your leg cannons.
urgot-laning.text: Urgot is classified as ranged, but his very short range favors him against melee opponents and puts him at a disadvantage against true ranged champions. His level 1 health and armor are among the highest of any champion, so repeated short trades favor him. Keep up the pressure by approaching with W active and circling to fire his leg cannons.

urgot-laning-wave.basis: With W active, nearby minions are hit automatically too, pushing the wave. To pull the wave toward you, turn off W and only last-hit. Manage W according to the wave state to avoid unwanted pushing and exposure to ganks.
urgot-laning-wave.text: W automatically hits nearby minions, pushing the wave. To draw the wave toward you, turn W off and last hit only. Watch the wave and manage the toggle together, or an unwanted push can expose you to a gank.

urgot-phase.basis: Urgot is weak at levels 1–2, when Q deals little damage. His trades grow stronger as he puts levels into W. His laning peaks when level 6 R coincides with his first core item. Later on, his short range makes it hard to enter teamfights. In the mid game, secure your lead through lane pressure and turrets.
urgot-phase.text: Urgot is weak at levels 1–2 because Q deals little damage, but his trades improve as he levels W. His laning peaks when level 6 R coincides with his first core item. His short range makes teamfight engages harder later, so use midgame lane pressure and turrets to secure your lead.

urgot-situational-antiheal.basis: If the opponent's healing is enough to turn a duel around, buy Executioner's Calling after completing your first core item. Dealing continuous damage with W lets you keep Grievous Wounds applied.
urgot-situational-antiheal.text: If an opponent’s healing can turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing your first core item. Urgot’s continuous W damage keeps Grievous Wounds applied.

urgot-skill-e.basis: E gives Urgot a shield as he dashes. E pushes through targets other than champions, but cannot cross terrain. Against an opponent with a mobility ability, engage with E after they use it. When ganked, use E's shield and stun to escape.
urgot-skill-e.text: E shields Urgot as he dashes, making it useful for both engaging and surviving. It pushes through targets other than champions, allowing him to pass through minions, but cannot cross terrain. Against an opponent with a mobility ability, wait until they have used it before engaging with E; when ganked, use E’s shield and stun to escape.

urgot-skill-q.basis: Q has long range and applies a very strong slow. When looking for a kill, save Q to set up an E engage. When holding the lane, use Q to poke.
urgot-skill-q.text: Q (Corrosive Charge) has long range and slows so heavily that its target can barely move. It works for lane poke and stopping escapes, but spending it on poke can leave you without a way to set up an E (Disdain) engage. When looking for a kill, save Q to start the engage; use it to poke only when you are simply holding the lane.

urgot-skill-r-fear.basis: R executes the target in front of Urgot and fears nearby enemies at that moment. In teamfights, pull in a target from the middle of the enemy group with R to fear multiple enemies. If you execute an enemy fleeing alone with R, there are no other enemies to fear.
urgot-skill-r-fear.text: R executes its target in front of Urgot and fears nearby enemies at that moment, making it both a finisher and an area crowd control tool in teamfights. Pull in a target from the middle of the enemy group to fear multiple opponents; executing someone fleeing alone fears no one. Choose your R target by position, not damage.

urgot-skill-w-mark.basis: W prioritizes the champion most recently hit by another ability. To make W fire at your chosen target in a skirmish, hit them with Q or E first. If no champion has been hit by another ability, W fires at the nearest enemy or minion.
urgot-skill-w-mark.text: W prioritizes the champion most recently hit by another ability, so land Q or E on your chosen target first during a skirmish. Without a marked target, W fires at the nearest enemy or minion. Q therefore serves both as poke and as a way to aim W.

urgot-skill-w-toggle.basis: At max rank, W becomes a toggle that lasts indefinitely. Before maxing W, use it sparingly and account for its duration. Activating W greatly reduces Urgot's movement speed and increases his slow resistance. Turn on W when fighting up close. Turn off W when fleeing.
urgot-skill-w-toggle.text: At max rank, W becomes an indefinite toggle; until then, it has a limited duration and should be used sparingly. While active, it greatly reduces Urgot’s movement speed but increases his slow resistance, so turn it on for close fights and off when fleeing. Managing the toggle is central to playing Urgot.

urgot-teamfight.basis: Before entering a teamfight, look for a chance to pull a target from behind the enemy frontline with E. Damage the target pulled in by E with Q and W, then execute them with R. If the enemies are grouped and there is no opening for E, attack the frontline with W and look for a chance to finish someone with R.
urgot-teamfight.text: Enter a teamfight when you can pull a target out from behind the enemy frontline with E. Ideally, damage that target with Q and W, then execute them with R. If the enemies are grouped and offer no opening, avoid forcing an engage; keep wearing down the frontline with W and look for an R finish.

varus-combo-blight.basis: Blight stacks detonate only when another of Varus’s abilities hits the target. Stack Blight to the maximum with basic attacks, then detonate it with E. Stack Blight to the maximum with basic attacks, then detonate it with Q.
varus-combo-blight.text: For a basic trade, build Blight to its maximum stacks with basic attacks, then detonate it by hitting the target with E Hail of Arrows or Q Piercing Arrow. Blight does not detonate on its own, and using an ability before stacking it fully gives up some of the damage based on the target’s maximum health.

varus-combo-q-charge.basis: The longer you charge Q, the more its range, damage, and Blight detonation effect increase. Varus slows himself while aiming Q. At close range, fire Q immediately instead of fully charging it. If you aim Q incorrectly when no enemies are nearby, cancel it to recover half its mana cost.
varus-combo-q-charge.text: The longer Varus charges Q Piercing Arrow, the greater its range, damage, and Blight detonation effect, but he slows himself while aiming. In close combat, fire immediately instead of charging it fully; if you aim incorrectly when no one is around, cancel it to recover half the mana cost.

varus-combo-ult.basis: Enemies rooted by R gain Blight stacks automatically for its duration. Start with R, then detonate the Blight stacks twice with E and Q. To increase total damage, use R to start a fight rather than to finish one.
varus-combo-ult.text: Open a teamfight with R Chain of Corruption, then use E and Q. A target rooted by R gains Blight stacks automatically throughout its duration, letting you detonate full stacks twice without basic attacks. Opening with R deals more total damage than saving it to finish the fight.

varus-laning-safety.basis: Varus has low movement speed, no dash, and relatively low armor growth. Before stepping past the wave to aim Q, check both the opponent’s engage abilities and the jungler’s location. When you lack lane priority, stay back and use your abilities to clear the wave.
varus-laning-safety.text: Varus has low movement speed, no mobility ability, and relatively low armor growth, so one positioning mistake can erase the advantage gained through his range. Step past the wave to aim Q only after checking both the opponent’s engage abilities and the enemy jungler’s location. Without lane priority, stay back and use your abilities only to clear the wave.

varus-laning-trade.basis: In lane, stack Blight on the opposing marksman with basic attacks, then detonate it with E. In lane, stack Blight on the opposing marksman with basic attacks, then detonate it with Q. Detonate Blight from basic attacks with an ability before it expires.
varus-laning-trade.text: In lane, build Blight stacks on the opposing marksman with basic attacks, then detonate them with E or Q. Letting the stacks expire leaves you with nothing, while using an ability first means there are no stacks to detonate and halves your damage. Following that order is itself a way to gain a lane advantage.

varus-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, use the bonus damage from W’s passive to poke and hold on. Once you learn E, you can clear waves and pressure opponents with its ground effect. Once you learn R at level 6, you can start fights yourself. Varus grows stronger as he gets items, but positioning remains important even late in the game.
varus-phase.text: At levels 1–2, poke and hold on with the bonus damage from W Blighted Quiver’s passive. Learning E gives you both wave clear and pressure from its ground effect; at level 6, R lets you initiate a fight yourself for the first time. Varus grows stronger with items, but he never gains a mobility ability, so his late game strength depends on positioning rather than damage alone.

varus-situational-antiheal.basis: Because E reduces healing, antiheal items are a lower priority even against healing focused opponents. If the opponents have several sources of healing or heal beyond E’s reach, choose Mortal Reminder instead of an armor penetration item.
varus-situational-antiheal.text: Even against healing focused opponents, antiheal items are a lower priority for Varus than for other marksmen because E Hail of Arrows already reduces healing on its contaminated ground. Choose Mortal Reminder in place of an armor penetration item only when the opposing team has several sources of healing or heals beyond E’s reach.

varus-situational-cc.basis: If the opponents have a lot of crowd control that prevents movement, buy Mercurial Scimitar earlier. If Varus is hit by crowd control that prevents movement, he cannot escape with an ability and struggles to regain distance afterward.
varus-situational-cc.text: Buy Mercurial Scimitar earlier when the opposing team has a lot of crowd control that prevents movement. Varus has no ability to escape once caught, so a single such effect can lead directly to his death; his low movement speed also makes it hard to regain distance afterward.

varus-skill-e.basis: Along with damage and a slow, E leaves contaminated ground that reduces healing. Place E where a healing focused enemy wants to stand or must pass through.
varus-skill-e.text: E Hail of Arrows deals damage, slows, and leaves contaminated ground that reduces healing. Place it where a healing focused enemy wants to stand or must pass, such as in front of Dragon or Baron or at a brush entrance, to shut down their healing. Since Varus has no mobility ability, also save E to place defensively along an approaching enemy’s path.

varus-skill-passive.basis: A kill or assist makes his passive increase attack speed, attack damage, and ability power. On a champion takedown, the passive’s bonuses are much larger and can exceed the attack speed cap. Varus is especially strong for a few seconds after a champion takedown. After the first kill in a teamfight, keep attacking the next target.
varus-skill-passive.text: A kill or assist triggers P Living Vengeance, briefly increasing Varus’s attack speed, attack damage, and ability power. The bonuses are much larger on a champion takedown and can exceed the attack speed cap, making the next few seconds his strongest. Once your team gets the first kill in a teamfight, keep attacking the next target instead of retreating.

varus-skill-r.basis: R spreads from the first champion it hits to nearby champions it has not infected. R is most effective when opponents are grouped. Since Varus has no dash, decide whether to use R to start a fight or defend against an assassin.
varus-skill-r.text: R Chain of Corruption spreads from the first champion it hits to nearby champions it has not infected. It is most effective against grouped opponents; firing it at someone isolated spends it on a single root. Because Varus has no mobility ability, decide whether to use R to start a fight or hold it to stop an assassin closing in on him.

varus-skill-w-active.basis: W’s active strengthens the next Q and has a long cooldown. Activate W when the opponent is tied to the wave or in a narrow path, where you can reliably land Q.
varus-skill-w-active.text: W Blighted Quiver’s active empowers your next Q Piercing Arrow and has a long cooldown. Save it for a Q you can reliably land, such as when an opponent is tied to the wave or has little room to dodge along a narrow path.

varus-skill-w-cooldown.basis: Detonating Blight on a champion or epic monster reduces the cooldowns of basic abilities. When attacking Dragon or Baron, stack Blight with basic attacks and detonate it with an ability.
varus-skill-w-cooldown.text: Detonating Blight on a champion or epic monster reduces the cooldowns of Varus’s basic abilities. Managing stacks well brings Q and E back noticeably faster, while using abilities only on minions slows that cycle down. The cooldown reduction also applies during objective fights, so weave basic attacks into your damage on Dragon or Baron to build stacks before using an ability.

varus-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, stay behind your frontline and disrupt the enemy formation with Q and E. Use R when opponents are clustered together. Wait until all opposing engage abilities are down before stepping forward to basic attack. Move forward right after a takedown activates your passive.
varus-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay behind your frontline and begin with Q and E to disrupt the enemy formation, using R only when opponents overlap. With no way to shake off someone who closes in, step forward for basic attacks only after all opposing engage abilities have been used. A takedown makes Varus sharply stronger through his passive, so advance immediately afterward.

vayne-combo-condemn.basis: Use Q to line up a wall behind the enemy, pin them against it with E, then build W stacks with basic attacks during the stun. E pushes the enemy away from the cast's origin. Q cannot cross walls. Distinguish between using Q to set up an angle and using it to disengage.
vayne-combo-condemn.text: Use Q to position yourself with a wall behind the enemy, then pin them against it with E and build W stacks with basic attacks during the stun. E pushes enemies away from where you cast it, so the wall must be behind them, not behind you. Q cannot cross walls; distinguish between using it to set up the angle and saving it to disengage.

vayne-combo-r.basis: Activate R, move in with Q's invisibility, then build W stacks with basic attacks. Q's cooldown is greatly reduced while R is active. Use Q sideways while R is active to make your reappearance position harder to predict.
vayne-combo-r.text: Activate R, move in with Q, and use its invisibility to hide your position while the enemy misses a targeted ability; then build W stacks with basic attacks. R greatly reduces Q’s cooldown, letting you use it repeatedly, so roll sideways instead of always moving in a straight line to make your reappearance harder to predict.

vayne-combo-w.basis: Time your trades around W procs. W triggers whenever attacks or abilities hit the same target a set number of times. Build W stacks with basic attacks, then use a Q-empowered basic attack for the final hit to deal both instances of damage together. Switching targets just before W triggers loses your accumulated stacks.
vayne-combo-w.text: Time trades around W: attacks and abilities both count toward its trigger when they hit the same target. Build the earlier stacks with basic attacks, then land a Q-empowered basic attack for the final hit to deal W’s maximum-health true damage and Q’s bonus damage together. Switching targets just before W triggers wastes the stacks you have built.

vayne-laning.basis: Vayne struggles against longer-ranged opponents because of her short basic attack range. Keep the wave near your turret and farm to reduce the risk of ganks. Vayne is weak in the early laning phase. Play to minimize losses early.
vayne-laning.text: Vayne’s low early health and armor and short basic attack range leave her vulnerable to longer-ranged opponents. Keep the wave near your turret and farm without forcing a push to reduce your exposure to ganks. Her CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute are among the lowest, so focus on minimizing losses during this early stretch.

vayne-laning-trade.basis: Only start a trade when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. Trigger W once in a short basic attack trade, then immediately retreat with Q. Avoid starting a trade if you cannot attack enough times to trigger W. Save E if the enemy does not have their back to a wall.
vayne-laning-trade.text: Start a trade only when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. Ideally, land enough basic attacks to trigger W once, then immediately retreat with Q; if you cannot trigger W, do not start the trade. Save E unless the enemy has their back to a wall.

vayne-phase.basis: Vayne is weakest at levels 1–2. Q's cooldown decreases significantly as its rank increases. Vayne becomes much stronger in the mid to late game once she has attack speed and penetration items. Avoid falling behind early and secure time to scale.
vayne-phase.text: Vayne is weakest at levels 1–2. Q (Tumble)’s cooldown drops sharply with each rank, letting her trade more often as she invests points in it; she then grows much stronger in the mid to late game as attack speed and penetration items come together. Her early game statistics are among the lowest, while the win rate for builds that complete three core items rises sharply. Avoid falling behind early and buy time to scale.

vayne-situational-antiheal.basis: If enemy healing offsets W's true damage, buy Executioner's Calling after one core item to reduce healing. Vayne's fighting pattern centers on attacking one target for an extended time. Vayne's sustained attacks on one target keep healing reduction items' effects active longer.
vayne-situational-antiheal.text: If enemy healing offsets W’s true damage, buy Executioner’s Calling after one core item. Vayne attacks one target for an extended time, allowing her to keep healing reduction active for longer.

vayne-situational-qss.basis: If the enemy has lingering crowd control that restricts movement, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items to break free. You cannot use Q while immobilized.
vayne-situational-qss.text: If the enemy has lasting crowd control that restricts movement, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. No matter how often Q (Tumble) is available, Vayne cannot use it while immobilized, so a way to break free when caught is more valuable than another damage item.

vayne-skill-e.basis: E stuns enemies if it pins them against a wall. E pushes away enemies who get close. Avoid spending E on simple poke in lane so you can respond to ganks. When trading with E, use it on an enemy with their back to a wall.
vayne-skill-e.text: E can finish a target by stunning them against a wall, and it is Vayne’s only defensive way to push away an enemy who gets close. Spending it on simple lane poke leaves you unable to respond to a gank. In open terrain, E can push the enemy out of range and end your own trade, so use it when the enemy has their back to a wall.

vayne-skill-passive.basis: P's movement speed bonus only applies when moving toward nearby enemy champions. P's movement speed bonus increases while R is active. Vayne is built to chase quickly but disengage slowly. Check your retreat path before closing in on the enemy.
vayne-skill-passive.text: P grants movement speed only when Vayne moves toward a nearby enemy champion, with a larger bonus during R; it does not help her escape. Because she chases quickly but retreats slowly, check your retreat path before closing in.

vayne-skill-q.basis: Q performs a short roll and grants an empowered basic attack. Vayne has relatively short basic attack range among ranged champions. Keep Q available to disengage instead of spending every use on closing in. Use Q immediately after a basic attack to cancel its recovery animation and reposition without losing damage. Q cannot cross walls.
vayne-skill-q.text: Q is a short roll followed by an empowered basic attack, making it both a movement tool and a damage boost. Vayne’s basic attack range is short even among ranged champions, but spending every Q to close the gap leaves you without a way to disengage. Use Q immediately after a basic attack to cancel its recovery animation and reposition without losing damage. Q cannot cross walls.

vayne-skill-r.basis: R increases Vayne's attack damage. R reduces Q's cooldown. Using Q while R is active makes you invisible. Takedowns extend R's duration, but it cannot exceed its original maximum. Use R after the fight starts and the enemy has used a targeted ability.
vayne-skill-r.text: R increases Vayne’s attack damage, reduces Q’s cooldown, and makes her invisible when she uses Q. Takedowns extend its duration, but never beyond its original maximum. Activating R well before entering a fight wastes that time; use it once the fight has started and the enemy has spent a targeted ability so you can benefit from the extension.

vayne-teamfight.basis: Avoid initiating teamfights. Enter after your allies start the fight and the enemy has used their engage abilities and targeted crowd control. Draw fights into narrow terrain near walls to set up wall stuns with E. After entering, focus W stacks on one enemy without switching targets.
vayne-teamfight.text: Let your allies start teamfights, then enter after the enemy has used their engage abilities and targeted crowd control. Draw fights toward narrow terrain near walls, where E can reliably stun a target. Once you enter, keep attacking one enemy to build W stacks instead of switching targets.

veigar-combo-basic.basis: For a kill, trap the target with E, land W and Q, then finish with R. W lands late, so time it to hit during E's stun. In a kill combo, don't cast W first without E.
veigar-combo-basic.text: For a kill, trap the target with E (Event Horizon), drop W (Dark Matter) where they are trapped, then use Q (Baleful Strike) and finish with R (Primordial Burst). W takes time to land and will rarely hit on its own, so keep this order to make it land during E’s stun. Casting W first without E is the most common reason Veigar fails to deal damage.

veigar-combo-e-placement.basis: E only stuns enemies who cross its edge. To stop an approaching enemy, place E on their path ahead of time.
veigar-combo-e-placement.text: E (Event Horizon) only stuns enemies who cross its edge. If you place it under an enemy, they can move and attack freely inside it. Place it behind them to block their escape route and force them to cross the edge to leave. Against an approaching enemy, set it on their path ahead of time, rather than on yourself.

veigar-combo-r.basis: R deals more damage the more health the target has lost. Use R after lowering the target's health with your W and Q. Use R after your allies deal damage.
veigar-combo-r.text: R (Primordial Burst) deals more damage based on how much health the target has lost, reaching its greatest effect when they are low. Use it at the end of a combo, after your allies have dealt damage or your W (Dark Matter) and Q (Baleful Strike) have landed. Casting it first on a full-health target gets only half the value from the same ability.

veigar-laning.basis: To prepare for ganks, keep the wave in the middle and don't push it all the way. When the wave is in the middle, poke from Q range and build stacks. Only step forward when you know where the enemy jungler is. Veigar relies heavily on mana and ability haste. When your mana drops below half, stop poking, farm, and wait to recover.
veigar-laning.text: Keep the wave near the middle instead of pushing it all the way out: without a mobility ability, E is Veigar’s only way out if he is ganked while pushed up. Build stacks by poking from Q range, and step forward only when you know where the enemy jungler is. Veigar relies heavily on mana and ability haste; when your mana falls below half, stop poking, farm, and wait for it to recover.

veigar-laning-roam.basis: After level 6, you can look for kills with E, W, Q, and R. Veigar has no mobility ability, so roaming out and back is slow. If there is no clear kill opportunity, manage the wave in mid and build stacks.
veigar-laning-roam.text: After level 6, you can look for a kill by trapping an opponent with E, landing W and Q, then finishing with R. Veigar has no mobility ability or exceptional movement speed, so roaming out and back is slow; without a clear kill opportunity, you gain more by managing the mid wave and building stacks.

veigar-phase.basis: Veigar is weakest at levels 1–5, when he has few stacks. Veigar's kill potential rises when he learns R at level 6. Veigar's stacks have no cap, so he grows stronger as the game goes on. Early on, aim to get through without losing ground rather than trying to win.
veigar-phase.text: Veigar is weakest at levels 1–5, when he has the lowest armor, no mobility ability, and few stacks. His kill potential rises when he learns R at level 6, and his uncapped stacks make him stronger as the game goes on. Early on, aim to get through lane without losing ground rather than trying to win it.

veigar-situational-zhonya.basis: If an assassin targets Veigar and closes in, buy Zhonya's Hourglass early. Get Zhonya's Hourglass to respond if an enemy engages after you use E.
veigar-situational-zhonya.text: If an assassin is targeting Veigar and closing in, move Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in your core build. Veigar is fragile and needs a defensive option for an engage after E has been used.

veigar-skill-e-defense.basis: Veigar has no mobility ability. Anticipate the opponent's approach and place E on their path ahead of time.
veigar-skill-e-defense.text: E (Event Horizon) is Veigar’s only survival tool as well as a way to start a fight. He has no mobility ability and has the lowest level-one armor of any champion, so using E only to attack can leave him dead when an enemy engages. If the opposing team has a champion who can close in, reserve E for defense at least half the time; anticipate their approach and place it on their path.

veigar-skill-passive.basis: Each time you hit an enemy champion with an ability, you gain Phenomenal Evil Power stacks. You gain more Phenomenal Evil Power stacks when you participate in a kill. In lane, hit opponents with Q when they enter range to increase your ability power.
veigar-skill-passive.text: Each ability hit on an enemy champion grants a Phenomenal Evil Power stack, and participating in a kill grants more. Hitting an opponent with Q in lane is permanent growth: farming without ever landing a spell on them costs Veigar that opportunity, while using Q whenever they enter range raises your ability power without spending gold.

veigar-skill-q.basis: Killing an enemy unit with Q grants a stack. Killing large minions and large monsters with Q grants many more stacks. Finish off cannon minions with Q. Line up two low-health minions and kill both with Q.
veigar-skill-q.text: Killing an enemy unit with Q grants a stack, and large minions and large monsters grant much more. Make a habit of finishing cannon minions with Q, and look to line up two low health minions for a single cast, since Q passes through only the first two units it hits.

veigar-skill-w.basis: W lands late, and opponents can see where it will land. Use W when an opponent is hit by immobilizing crowd control. Use W when an opponent is trapped by E. Use W when a narrow passage or minions make it hard for an opponent to dodge sideways. As you gain stacks, W's cooldown decreases, making it useful for farming too.
veigar-skill-w.text: W takes time to land, and opponents can see where it will fall, so cast it when they cannot move out of the way: during immobilizing crowd control, while trapped by E’s edge, in a narrow passage, or when minions block a sideways dodge. As you gain stacks, W’s cooldown falls enough to use it for farming too.

veigar-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, position behind your allies instead of standing on the front line. Use E to cut off the enemy’s approach or block their escape route behind them. When an opponent is trapped or hit by allied crowd control, land W and Q. Save R for an enemy you must kill, especially a damaged damage dealer.
veigar-teamfight.text: In teamfights, stay behind your allies and use E first to cut off an enemy approach or block their escape route. Land W and Q when an opponent is trapped or caught by allied crowd control, and save R for the one enemy you must kill, especially a damaged damage dealer.

veigar-teamfight-terrain.basis: If you can choose where to teamfight, choose a narrow area. At dragon or Baron pit entrances and jungle paths, E can easily block the enemy team's movement. Avoid teamfights in open areas where opponents can approach from all sides.
veigar-teamfight-terrain.text: If you can choose where to teamfight, choose a narrow area. Enemies can go around E in open space, but at a dragon or Baron pit entrance or on a jungle path, it can trap the whole team. Avoid open areas where opponents can approach Veigar from every side.

velkoz-combo-basic.basis: Knock the target up with E, cast W under them, then layer Q on top. Cast W the moment E knocks the target up so both W hits land during the knockup. Q takes longer to hit, so layer it in last. One E–W–Q combo completes the Organic Deconstruction stacks and triggers true damage.
velkoz-combo-basic.text: Knock the target up with E, cast W under their feet immediately so both its initial hit and delayed explosion land during the knockup, then layer Q on top because it takes longer to arrive. That E–W–Q sequence completes the Organic Deconstruction stacks and triggers true damage.

velkoz-combo-q-split.basis: You can recast Q to choose when it splits. Q's split beams travel to either side of its original path. When the target dodges sideways, recast Q just before it passes beside them. Against a target behind a wall or close to a brush, split Q in front of the wall to catch them from the side.
velkoz-combo-q-split.text: You can recast Q to choose when it splits into two beams that travel to either side of its original path. If you expect a sideways dodge, recast just before Q passes the target so the split beam catches them; against someone behind a wall or close to brush, split it in front of the wall to hit them from the side.

velkoz-combo-r-setup.basis: Build Organic Deconstruction stacks with Q or W, then cast R. R deals true damage that ignores magic resistance to targets recently damaged by Organic Deconstruction. Keep R on one target long enough to build stacks, and its damage turns into true damage midcast.
velkoz-combo-r-setup.text: Build Organic Deconstruction stacks with Q or W before casting R: targets recently damaged by Organic Deconstruction take true damage from R, bypassing magic resistance, so casting it without preparation produces a very different result. The beam also builds stacks periodically while it hits, and holding it on one target long enough turns its damage into true damage midcast.

velkoz-laning.basis: Vel'Koz support specializes in poke over protection or buffs. Keep hitting the enemy ADC with Q and W to complete Organic Deconstruction stacks. Use the moment the enemy loses health as your ally's signal to engage.
velkoz-laning.text: Vel'Koz support is a pure poke champion who cannot protect or buff his ADC. His job is to keep wearing down both opponents until they cannot stay in lane, repeatedly landing Q and W on the enemy ADC to complete Organic Deconstruction stacks. When an enemy's health drops, that is the signal for your ally to engage.

velkoz-laning-safety.basis: Vel'Koz has no mobility ability. Be especially careful when stepping forward to find a poke angle. Poke from behind or beside your ADC, using the edge of your range. Save E as your last safeguard when poking could put you in danger.
velkoz-laning-safety.text: Vel'Koz has no mobility ability and ranks near the bottom in both health and armor, making the moment he steps forward for a poke angle especially dangerous. Stand behind or beside your ADC rather than behind the minions, and cast only from the edge of your range. Against an engage composition, secure vision of the river and tri-brush before pushing the lane; keep E (Tectonic Disruption) as your last safeguard.

velkoz-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, you have few abilities and little mana, so your poke rotation is slow. Lane pressure grows once you have both Q and W and can complete Organic Deconstruction stacks in one rotation. Learning R at level 6 gives you chances to finish off enemies. As ability power builds, your true damage and late-game damage increase. Position farther back as your damage grows in the late game.
velkoz-phase.text: At levels 1–2, limited abilities and mana make your poke rotation slow. Lane pressure grows once you have both Q and W and can complete Organic Deconstruction stacks in one rotation, while learning R at level 6 creates chances to finish enemies. As ability power builds, your true damage and late-game damage keep rising, but Vel'Koz remains fragile, so position farther back as you grow stronger.

velkoz-situational-antiheal.basis: Against enemies with strong healing, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Vel'Koz can easily spread healing reduction by hitting several enemies with wide-ranging abilities.
velkoz-situational-antiheal.text: Against champions with strong healing, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Vel'Koz's wide-ranging abilities can hit several enemies, making it easy to spread healing reduction across the opposing team.

velkoz-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, get Zhonya's Hourglass so you can channel R to the end. When an assassin dives in, Vel'Koz has no mobility ability and relies on E to push them away.
velkoz-situational-zhonya.text: Get Zhonya's Hourglass if the enemy has an assassin who dives in. With no mobility ability, Vel'Koz otherwise has only E's pushback to survive the engage; you need a way to weather it if you want to channel R to the end.

velkoz-skill-e.basis: E is Vel'Koz's only reliable crowd control ability. Do not use E to clear waves or for simple poke. E pushes away enemies who are very close instead of knocking them up. In lane, when the enemy's engage ability is available, prioritize saving E for defense over starting a combo.
velkoz-skill-e.text: E is Vel'Koz's only reliable crowd control ability, so avoid spending it on wave clear or simple poke. It pushes very close enemies away instead of knocking them up, making it useful for peeling off an assassin who dives in. Since E both starts combos and protects you, prioritize defense in lane while the enemy's engage ability is available.

velkoz-skill-passive.basis: Landing different abilities together completes Organic Deconstruction stacks faster. Mix Q, W, and E hits to build Organic Deconstruction stacks quickly. Completing Organic Deconstruction stacks triggers true damage that ignores resistances. Basic attacks cannot add Organic Deconstruction stacks, but they extend their duration. If one stack remains, use a basic attack to buy time, then finish with an ability.
velkoz-skill-passive.text: Vel'Koz completes Organic Deconstruction faster by landing different abilities together, so mix Q, W, and E instead of repeating the same ability. Completing the stacks deals true damage that ignores resistances. Basic attacks do not add stacks, but they extend their duration; when one more stack is needed, use an attack to buy time before finishing with an ability.

velkoz-skill-q.basis: Q is Vel'Koz's main poke and his only slow. Q has long range and restores mana. Save Q for its slow when you need to keep a target in place. Q splits automatically at maximum range or on hit, even without a recast. When enemies are grouped, let Q travel its full range to hit several of them.
velkoz-skill-q.text: Q is Vel'Koz's main poke and his only slow. Its long range and mana recovery make it useful for constant lane pressure, but save it when you need the slow to keep a target in place. It splits automatically at maximum range or on hit even without a recast, so letting it travel its full range can hit more enemies when they are grouped.

velkoz-skill-r.basis: R is a channeled beam that follows the cursor. Vel'Koz is completely vulnerable while channeling R. Before casting R, check whether the enemy has used their engage ability. Before casting R, make sure you cannot be caught from behind. Use R's slow to keep hitting one target without changing the beam's angle much.
velkoz-skill-r.text: R is a channeled beam that follows your cursor, leaving Vel'Koz completely vulnerable while it fires. Before casting, check that the enemy has used their engage ability and cannot catch you from behind; then guide the beam slowly along the target's path instead of swinging it around. Its slow makes it easier to stay on one target, and holding the beam there without large angle changes deals more total damage.

velkoz-skill-w.basis: W has charges, so you can cast it twice in a row. W hits once, then erupts again after a delay. Even one W cast can reliably build Organic Deconstruction stacks. When clearing a wave, save at least one W charge for a fight.
velkoz-skill-w.text: W (Void Rift) holds charges, letting Vel'Koz cast it twice in a row, and each cast hits once before erupting again after a delay. That second hit makes even one cast a reliable way to build Organic Deconstruction stacks and a foundation for poke. W can also clear waves, but its mana cost is high; spending both charges on minions can cost you a chance to fight, so keep at least one available.

velkoz-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, fight from the back using your range. Before a fight, build Organic Deconstruction stacks on several enemies with Q and W. Cast R when an ally locks down the enemy. Move R's beam across the group your ally has locked down.
velkoz-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Vel'Koz fights from the back using his range. Before the fight starts, spread Organic Deconstruction stacks across several enemies with Q and W, then cast R when an ally locks them down and sweep the beam across the trapped group. Let the fight start before committing to R.

vex-combo-basic.basis: Land E's slow, then hit Q. The farther you throw E, the larger its area grows in flight, making it easier to land. Fire Q after E's slow takes effect.
vex-combo-basic.text: Start a basic trade with E (Looming Darkness) to slow the enemy, follow with Q (Mistral Bolt), then land a basic attack if a mark remains. E’s area grows as it travels, making long casts easier to land; cast too close, and its narrow area may miss. Fire Q after the slow takes effect so the target is easier to predict.

vex-combo-passive.basis: When Doom is ready, your next basic ability fears enemies. To land fear safely, lead with long-range Q or wide-area E. Use W to fear an enemy when they're already close. Clear minions while Doom is down so you don't waste it.
vex-combo-passive.text: When Doom is ready, your next basic ability applies fear, so the ability you use first determines who you fear. For a reliable hit, put it on long range Q or wide area E; use W only when an enemy is already close enough that it cannot miss. Clear minions while Doom is down so you do not waste it on the wave.

vex-combo-ult.basis: After the R projectile marks a target, recast R to dash to them. If a marked target damaged by R dies soon after, you can use R again. Land the first R on a target you can finish off. After landing from your R dash, use E to lock down nearby enemies and W for a shield.
vex-combo-ult.text: R has two stages: its projectile marks a target, then a recast dashes to them. If a marked champion dies soon after taking R damage, R becomes available again, so aim the first cast at someone you can finish off. Immediately after the dash lands, use E to lock down nearby enemies and W for a shield while you look for your next target.

vex-laning-vs-dash.basis: Hold Doom and wait for enemies who engage with a dash. As the enemy goes in, use a basic ability to interrupt their dash and fear them. If you spend Doom on the wave, retreat behind your minions.
vex-laning-vs-dash.text: Holding Doom makes the lane easier against enemies who dash in to trade. Use a basic ability as they engage to interrupt the dash, apply fear, and counterattack. If you spend Doom on the wave, retreat behind your minions while the enemy can close the gap freely.

vex-phase.basis: At levels 1–2, Q's long cooldown makes it slow to poke repeatedly. Once you learn E and can keep cycling Doom, you gain lane control. Learning R at level 6 lets you roam and force engages. Late game, Vex is strongest when kills reset R and let her chain engages. If enemies group up without giving you an R angle, your late-game impact drops sharply.
vex-phase.text: At levels 1–2, Q’s long cooldown makes repeated poke slow. Once you learn E and can keep cycling Doom, you gain lane control; R at level 6 lets you roam and force engages. Vex peaks late in the game when kills reset R and let her chain engages, but her impact drops sharply if enemies group up without giving her an R angle.

vex-skill-passive-antidash.basis: Nearby enemies gain a Gloom mark when they dash or blink. A basic ability used while Doom is ready interrupts enemy dashes and fears them. Against champions that engage, save Doom until they go in.
vex-skill-passive-antidash.text: Vex’s Doom 'n Gloom is a counter to champions with dashes: nearby enemies gain a Gloom mark whenever they dash or blink, and a basic ability used while Doom is ready interrupts a dash and applies fear. Against champions who engage, save Doom until the moment they go in.

vex-skill-passive-mark.basis: Consuming a Gloom mark with a basic attack reduces Doom's cooldown. Weave in one basic attack against a marked enemy, then back off. Killing an enemy with E also reduces Doom's cooldown.
vex-skill-passive-mark.text: Vex’s next basic attack consumes a Gloom mark and reduces Doom’s cooldown. Against a marked enemy, weave in one basic attack before backing off; casting abilities and retreating will not trigger that cooldown reduction. Killing an enemy with E (Looming Darkness) also reduces Doom’s cooldown, so clearing a wave can help cycle the passive.

vex-skill-q.basis: Q gets narrower and faster as it travels. Against close enemies, cast Q right in front of them. Against distant enemies, aim Q where they're moving.
vex-skill-q.text: Q (Mistral Bolt) gets narrower and faster as it travels. Up close, its hit area is wide, but it moves slowly enough to dodge on foot; at long range, it is fast but thin. Cast it directly in front of nearby enemies, and aim ahead of distant ones based on their movement.

vex-skill-r.basis: The R projectile marks the first enemy champion it hits. If the frontline is overlapping, shift your angle and fire R so it passes through only the backline. Before going in with R, check whether W and Flash are available.
vex-skill-r.text: The R projectile marks the first enemy champion it hits, so an overlapping frontline can cause it to mark the wrong target. Shift your angle so the projectile passes through only the backline. Once you dash in, you have no movement ability to get out, so check that W and Flash are available before committing.

vex-skill-w.basis: W gives you a shield and a close-range shockwave at the same time. Use W as the enemy's burst damage hits. Save W for an engage instead of using it early to poke.
vex-skill-w.text: W (Personal Space) grants a shield and releases a close-range shockwave at the same time, so the enemy must already be close to get both effects. Save it for an engage instead of spending it early to poke: it is Vex’s only survival tool, and you should activate it as the enemy’s burst damage hits.

vex-teamfight.basis: Don't go in first in teamfights. As the enemy engages, interrupt their dash with an ability empowered by Doom. After stopping the enemy engage, use E to lock down the backline. Use R once the enemy formation breaks and you can secure a kill.
vex-teamfight.text: Never engage first as Vex in a teamfight. Your first job is to interrupt the enemy’s dash with a basic ability empowered by Doom, then use E to lock down their backline. Cast R after their formation has broken and a kill is certain; a successful R that resets can let you clean up the rest of the fight yourself.

vi-combo-gank.basis: For a basic gank, charge Q and hit the target, then use an E-empowered basic attack, a basic attack, E, and a basic attack in that order. When Q hits a champion, Vi stops and knocks them backward. Approach from behind so Q knocks the target toward your allied laner.
vi-combo-gank.text: For a basic gank, charge Q, collide with the target to knock them back, then use an E-empowered basic attack, a basic attack, E, and another basic attack. Q stops Vi when it hits a champion, so approach from behind to knock the target toward your allied laner.

vi-combo-ult.basis: After knocking the target up with R, charge E while they land, then follow with a basic attack, E, a basic attack, and Q. R targets and chases its target, so use it to start the combo. Using Q first knocks the target away and breaks the follow-up.
vi-combo-ult.text: R targets and chases an enemy, so start the combo with it. After the knockup, charge E during the target’s landing, then follow with a basic attack, E, another basic attack, and Q as the knockup ends. Using Q first knocks the target away and breaks the follow-up.

vi-jungle-clear.basis: In the jungle, keep attacking one monster to activate W. Activate your passive shield before moving to the next camp to reduce health loss. Enemies other than champions are pulled toward Vi when Q hits them. Use Q to gather scattered monsters.
vi-jungle-clear.text: In the jungle, clearing is faster when you keep attacking one monster until W activates. Activate your passive shield before moving to the next camp to reduce health loss, and use Q to gather scattered monsters, since it pulls enemies other than champions toward Vi on hit.

vi-phase.basis: Start ganking at level 3, once you have your abilities. At level 6, learning R lets you reliably catch one target. Vi has low damage per minute early, so she has little impact if she only clears camps. As soon as you have your abilities, help a lane to gain an advantage. Later on, Vi's role shifts toward engaging and isolating targets rather than dealing damage.
vi-phase.text: Start ganking at level 3, once you have your abilities; learning R at level 6 lets you reliably catch one target. Vi’s early damage per minute is relatively low, so clearing camps alone gives her little impact: help a lane as soon as your abilities are available to gain an advantage. Later, her role shifts toward engaging and isolating targets rather than dealing damage.

vi-situational-cc.basis: If the enemy team can lock you down with crowd control after you engage with R and keep you from escaping, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. R itself cannot be interrupted, so prepare for being locked down after landing.
vi-situational-cc.text: If the enemy team can lock you down after an R engage and prevent your escape, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. R itself cannot be interrupted; the danger comes after landing, so use the item to help survive the aftermath.

vi-skill-e.basis: E turns your next basic attack into an area attack that passes through targets. If an enemy is behind a minion or jungle monster, hit the front unit with E to damage the enemy behind it. Use E's piercing attack to poke when helping a lane or to secure a last hit safely. E stores charges, so let them build up between camps.
vi-skill-e.text: E turns your next basic attack into a piercing area attack. If an enemy stands behind a minion or jungle monster, hitting the front unit deals full damage to the enemy behind it; use this to poke when helping a lane or to secure a last hit safely. E stores charges, so let them build up between camps.

vi-skill-passive.basis: Vi gains her passive shield when she hits an enemy or structure with an ability. Before a fight, hit a nearby minion or monster with an ability to activate your shield, then go in. Each time W activates, it reduces the cooldown of your passive shield.
vi-skill-passive.text: Vi’s passive shield activates when an ability hits an enemy or structure. Before a fight, hit a nearby minion or monster with an ability and enter with the shield up to absorb part of the opening combo. Each W activation also reduces the shield’s cooldown.

vi-skill-q-charge.basis: The longer you charge Q, the more damage it deals and the farther Vi dashes. Fully charge Q to catch or finish a fleeing enemy. If Q is interrupted while charging, you can use it again after a short wait.
vi-skill-q-charge.text: The longer you charge Q, the more damage it deals and the farther Vi dashes, so fully charge it to catch or finish a fleeing enemy. If the charge is interrupted, Q is available again after a short wait, making a brief charge a reasonable choice when you need to act quickly.

vi-skill-r.basis: R chases its chosen target to the end, so Flash cannot dodge it. Vi cannot be stopped during R, so she ignores enemy crowd control as she goes in. R fails if its target becomes untargetable. Other enemies in R's path are knocked aside and briefly stunned, but Vi keeps chasing her chosen target.
vi-skill-r.text: R chases its chosen target to the end, so Flash cannot dodge it, and Vi cannot be stopped during the cast, allowing her to ignore enemy crowd control as she goes in. It fails if the target becomes untargetable; enemies in its path are knocked aside and briefly stunned, but the chosen target does not change.

vi-skill-w.basis: W activates only when you hit the same target repeatedly. Keep attacking the target you have committed to so your W stacks stay on them. When W activates, it reduces the target's armor and increases Vi's attack speed. Vi gains more from staying on one target and attacking them longer.
vi-skill-w.text: W activates only when you hit the same target repeatedly. Switching targets spreads out the stacks, so once you commit to someone, keep attacking them. Each activation reduces their armor and increases Vi’s attack speed, making extended attacks on one target more rewarding.

vi-teamfight-engage.basis: Walk close enough for your team to follow, then engage with R. If you use R on a backline damage dealer too far ahead of your team, you will be left among the enemies without allied support.
vi-teamfight-engage.text: Do not engage with R so far ahead of your team that they cannot follow. Diving a backline damage dealer without allied support can leave you facing all five enemies alone, so walk close enough for your team to follow before using R.

vi-teamfight-focus.basis: In teamfights, pick off one key enemy damage dealer. Isolate the target with R, then attack only that target until W activates. Use Q to block the target's escape route or knock them toward your team. In teamfights, focus on one enemy instead of alternating between several.
vi-teamfight-focus.text: In teamfights, pick off one key enemy damage dealer. Isolate them with R and keep attacking only that target until W activates, using Q to block their escape route or knock them toward your team. If you switch between several enemies, you may catch none of them.

viego-combo-basic.basis: In a standard fight, approach with E, stun with W, then use Q. Your first basic attack against an enemy hit by an ability triggers an extra attack from Q's passive. After landing an ability, weave in basic attacks to deal damage.
viego-combo-basic.text: In a standard fight, approach with E, Harrowed Path, stun with W, Spectral Maw, then use Q, Blade of the Ruined King. Q’s passive adds an extra attack to your first basic attack against an enemy hit by an ability, so weave in a basic attack after landing an ability to deal full damage.

viego-combo-r-target.basis: R automatically attacks the nearby champion with the lowest percentage of remaining health. Before using R, check which champion it will target. R knocks back enemies other than its primary target. Use R to split the enemy team.
viego-combo-r-target.text: R, Heartbreaker, automatically strikes the nearby champion with the lowest percentage of remaining health. Check whom it will target before casting, since a more wounded enemy could draw you away from the one you intended to hit. R knocks back the other enemies, which can also split their formation.

viego-combo-w-charge.basis: The longer you charge W, the longer its stun lasts. Viego slows down while charging W. Interrupting Viego while he charges W cancels the charge. Against a fleeing enemy, charge W briefly to catch up. Charge W for a long time only when you are sure it will hit.
viego-combo-w-charge.text: Charging W, Spectral Maw, longer extends its stun, but Viego slows while charging and an interruption cancels it. Against a fleeing enemy, release it after a short charge to catch up; charge it fully only when you are sure it will hit.

viego-laning-gank.basis: Viego's only approach tools are W and E, so solo ganks have a low success rate. Prioritize ganking lanes where your ally has crowd control. If your ally has no crowd control, gank when the enemy pushes the lane near your ally's turret.
viego-laning-gank.text: W, Spectral Maw, and E, Harrowed Path, are Viego’s only ways to close the gap, so solo ganks have a low success rate. Prioritize lanes where an ally has crowd control; otherwise, gank only when the enemy has pushed near your ally’s turret.

viego-laning-objective.basis: Before an objective fight, use E to secure vision as you approach. Even if you lose the Smite fight, killing one enemy lets you heal through possession and look for a chance to reclaim the objective.
viego-laning-objective.text: Before an objective fight, approach with E, Harrowed Path, while securing vision. Even if you lose the Smite fight, do not retreat immediately: killing one enemy can let you heal through possession and reclaim the objective.

viego-phase.basis: Viego uses no resources, making his early jungle clear comfortable. A kill in a small fight near an objective can let Viego turn the fight through possession. Viego is strong in the mid game, when he has built his items. If Viego enters a late-game teamfight head-on first, he can easily die before creating a wraith to possess.
viego-phase.text: Viego uses no resources, making his early jungle clear comfortable. In a small fight near an objective, securing one kill can let him turn the fight through possession. He peaks in the mid game as he builds items, but entering a late game teamfight head on first can get him killed before he creates a wraith to possess.

viego-situational-antiheal.basis: If an enemy has strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Viego needs to kill an enemy to gain sustain through possession. If he does not kill a target, possession cannot begin.
viego-situational-antiheal.text: If an enemy has strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Viego gains sustain through possession only after a kill, so failing to finish a target means possession cannot begin.

viego-skill-e-approach.basis: E creates black mist along terrain. In E's mist, Viego is camouflaged and gains movement speed and attack speed. When ganking, cast E on a wall along your approach, then follow the mist in. Attacking or using an ability in the mist briefly reveals Viego. While approaching, stay camouflaged in the mist until just before using your first ability.
viego-skill-e-approach.text: E, Harrowed Path, spreads black mist along terrain, granting Viego camouflage, movement speed and attack speed inside it. For a gank, cast it on a wall along your approach and follow the mist so the enemy spots you later. Attacking or using an ability briefly reveals you, so stay camouflaged until just before your first ability.

viego-skill-passive-possession.basis: Enemy champions who fall near Viego remain as wraiths for a short time. Basic attack a wraith to begin possessing it. Possessing a target heals Viego based on the target's maximum health. While possessing a target, Viego can use its basic abilities and items.
viego-skill-passive-possession.text: Viego’s passive, Sovereign's Domination, is central to his playstyle. Enemy champions who fall near him briefly leave a wraith; basic attack it to begin possession. Possessing a target heals Viego based on its maximum health and lets him use its basic abilities and items, so start a teamfight by securing one kill.

viego-skill-possession-chain.basis: While possessing a target, Viego can use his own R once more at no cost instead of the target's ultimate. After using the abilities gained through possession, use R just before it ends to target the next enemy.
viego-skill-possession-chain.text: While possessing a target, Viego can use his own R, Heartbreaker, once more at no cost instead of the target’s ultimate. Use the abilities gained through possession, then cast R on the next target just before possession ends to chain kills. Retreating with possession time left wastes the opportunity.

viego-skill-possession-prep.basis: If you do not know the target's ability layout, you will be slow to react right after possessing it. Before a fight, check the basic ability layouts of all five enemies. Prioritize wraiths of enemies with dashes or shields.
viego-skill-possession-prep.text: If you do not know a target’s ability layout, you may hesitate as soon as you possess them. Before a fight, check which keys hold all five enemies’ basic abilities, then prioritize the wraiths of champions with dashes or shields.

viego-skill-q.basis: Q adds damage to basic attacks based on the target's current health. Q helps Viego damage high-health tanks and objectives. Q's damage speeds up jungle clearing and taking Dragon and Baron. Q's thrust pierces forward and can hit enemies behind minions.
viego-skill-q.text: Q, Blade of the Ruined King, adds damage to basic attacks based on the target’s current health, helping Viego damage high health tanks and objectives and clear the jungle or take Dragon and Baron quickly. Its thrust pierces forward, so it can also hit an enemy standing behind minions.

viego-teamfight.basis: Viego is not suited to starting teamfights. Enter after the enemy uses crowd control on your allied tank and a target you can kill appears. When you enter a teamfight, secure a wraith for your first possession. If you cannot create a wraith on your first entry, it is hard to keep fighting.
viego-teamfight.text: Viego should not start teamfights. Enter after the enemy has used crowd control on your allied tank and a killable target appears, then secure the first wraith. If you cannot create one on your first entry, the fight is already lost.

viego-teamfight-window.basis: Possession lasts only a short time, and the moment it ends is dangerous. Before possession ends, kill your next target or retreat to safety. If possession ends in the middle of the enemy team, Viego is easy to kill.
viego-teamfight-window.text: Possession lasts only a short time, and its end is the most dangerous moment. Watch the remaining time and either kill your next target or retreat to safety before it runs out; if you return to Viego’s body in the middle of the enemy team, you will be caught.

viktor-combo-q-aa.basis: Casting Q empowers your next basic attack. After using Q, follow up with the empowered basic attack. Use other abilities while your Q empowered basic attack is available.
viktor-combo-q-aa.text: Q empowers Viktor’s next basic attack, so using Q and backing away wastes much of its damage. Follow Q with the empowered attack, weaving in other abilities while the attack is available.

viktor-combo-trade.basis: Poke with E. If the enemy approaches, place W under them, then follow up with Q and the empowered basic attack. Use W after the enemy steps forward.
viktor-combo-trade.text: Poke with E, then, when the enemy steps forward, place W under them to slow them before using Q and its empowered basic attack. If you use W too early, they can simply walk out.

viktor-combo-ult.basis: Place R, then hold the enemy in it with W to deal R's damage over time. You can recast R to control it directly. Move R toward where you expect the enemy to retreat.
viktor-combo-ult.text: Place R, then use W to hold enemies in it for the full damage over time. Recast R to steer it toward their expected retreat path.

viktor-laning-safety.basis: Viktor has no dash to escape on his own. If you do not know where the enemy jungler is, do not move past the lane's midpoint. Keep W available to stop ganks and lane safely.
viktor-laning-safety.text: Viktor has low health and armor and no dash to escape on his own. If you do not know where the enemy jungler is, stay behind the lane’s midpoint and save W (Gravity Field) to stop a gank rather than use it for poke.

viktor-laning-wave.basis: Clearing a wave at once with E builds fragments quickly. After clearing a wave with E, you have time to roam or recall. Pushing the wave leaves you exposed to ganks. Get vision of the river before pushing the wave. When pushing the wave, keep your Q shield and W available in case of a gank.
viktor-laning-wave.text: Clearing a wave at once with E builds fragments quickly and creates time to roam or recall. Pushing also exposes you to ganks, so secure river vision first and keep your Q shield and W available.

viktor-phase-early.basis: Viktor ranks among the lowest mid champions in early kill participation. In lane, prioritize E poke and farming for augments over kills.
viktor-phase-early.text: Viktor has among the lowest early kill participation of mid champions but among the highest damage per minute. Treat lane as a chance to build augments through E poke and farming rather than chase kills.

viktor-phase-scaling.basis: Viktor peaks in the mid to late game with two or three augments and core items. Augments persist through death. Even if you fall behind in lane, keep farming to grow stronger.
viktor-phase-scaling.text: Viktor peaks in the mid to late game once he has two or three augments and core items. Augments persist through death, so even if you fall behind in lane, keep farming; time is on your side.

viktor-situational-zhonya.basis: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to deal with assassins who close in. Once placed, R keeps dealing damage even when Viktor stands still.
viktor-situational-zhonya.text: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against assassins who close in. Once placed, R keeps dealing damage even while Viktor is stationary, so buying time can turn a fight around.

viktor-skill-augment-order.basis: You cannot undo a chosen augment. Choose the augment with the effect you need most at that moment. If you urgently need poke and wave clear in lane, augment E first. If you need to withstand trades and stay close to the enemy, augment Q first. If you need to hold enemies in place during teamfights, augment W first.
viktor-skill-augment-order.text: Augments cannot be undone, so choose what you need most at the time: E if lane poke and wave clear are urgent, Q if you need to withstand trades while staying close, or W if you need to hold enemies in place during teamfights.

viktor-skill-e.basis: E hits in a straight line. You choose E's firing direction directly. Augmented E creates one more aftershock along its path. Augmenting E improves both wave clear and poke. Look for an angle to hit the wave and the enemy champion in one line with E.
viktor-skill-e.text: E fires in a straight line in the direction you choose. Once augmented, it triggers an additional aftershock along its path, improving both wave clear and poke, so look for an angle that catches the wave and the enemy champion in the same line.

viktor-skill-passive.basis: Viktor collects fragments to permanently augment his abilities. Killing minions grants fragments. Siege minions grant especially many fragments. Always last-hit siege minions yourself.
viktor-skill-passive.text: Viktor collects fragments from minion kills to permanently augment his abilities, with siege minions granting especially many. Farming drives his growth, so always last-hit siege minions yourself.

viktor-skill-q.basis: Q deals damage and grants a shield. Augmented Q also increases movement speed. When you need to take a trade, use Q for its shield before going in.
viktor-skill-q.text: Q deals damage and grants a shield; once augmented, it also gives movement speed. When you need to take a trade, use Q to shield yourself before going in.

viktor-skill-r.basis: R interrupts enemy channels when it appears. If an enemy has a channeled ultimate, save R to interrupt its cast.
viktor-skill-r.text: R interrupts channels as soon as it appears. If an enemy has a channeled ultimate, save R to interrupt it instead of using it early for damage.

viktor-skill-w.basis: W stuns only after the target stays in its area for a certain time. Place W on an escape route or in a narrow passage to set up a stun. Place W on an enemy who is already slowed or rooted to set up a stun.
viktor-skill-w.text: W stuns only after an enemy remains in its area for a while. Place it on an escape route, in a narrow passage, or under an enemy who is already slowed or rooted; otherwise, they can walk out.

viktor-teamfight.basis: Viktor is a champion who controls the battlefield. In narrow terrain, hold enemies in place with W and overlap R to deal damage over time. Viktor's short range forces him to stand a step forward. Viktor can die quickly if enemies engage on him. Stay just behind your frontline and focus on controlling R.
viktor-teamfight.text: Viktor controls fights by holding enemies with W in narrow terrain and placing R over them for its full damage over time. His short range requires him to stand a step forward, but he can die immediately if engaged on, so stay just behind your frontline and focus on steering R.

vladimir-combo-basic.basis: Prime Q on minions, then when the enemy enters range, charge E until it slows, fire it, and use empowered Q. Slow the enemy with E before using Q to hit them before they retreat out of range. If you use Q first and then charge E, the enemy may retreat and cause E to miss.
vladimir-combo-basic.text: Prime Q on minions, then charge E when the enemy enters range, fire it once it gains the slow, and follow with empowered Q. The slow helps Q land before the enemy retreats out of range; using Q first gives them time to back away while E charges, causing it to miss.

vladimir-combo-teamfight.basis: Hit multiple enemies with R, charge E as you move in, land empowered Q and E, then use W when they counterattack. You can use W while charging E. After casting R, coordinate your engage with your allies while its damage amplification is active.
vladimir-combo-teamfight.text: Hit multiple enemies with R, charge E as you move in, land empowered Q and E, then use W when they counterattack. W can be used without interrupting E’s charge, so you can enter and emerge from the pool while charging. Coordinate your engage with your allies after casting R so their damage benefits from its amplification.

vladimir-laning-health.basis: Farming carelessly with E costs health and gives the enemy a chance to engage. Pushing the wave with E is especially dangerous when you're below half health. When low on health, heal with Q before clearing the wave with E.
vladimir-laning-health.text: Careless farming with E steadily costs health and gives the enemy an opening to engage, especially if you push a wave with it below half health. Clear waves with E when you have health to spare; when low, heal with Q first.
