vladimir-laning-wave.basis: In patch 26.17 mid lane stats, Vladimir has very few deaths and damage per minute near the top, while his kill stats are in the lower middle. In lane, prioritize survival and growth over kills. Once you can clear waves quickly with E, push the lane and establish vision or join fights in other lanes.
vladimir-laning-wave.text: In patch 26.17 mid lane stats, Vladimir has very few deaths and damage per minute near the top, while his kill stats sit in the lower middle. Prioritize surviving and growing over getting lane kills. Once E can clear waves quickly, push the lane, then establish vision or join fights in other lanes.

vladimir-phase.basis: Vladimir is weakest at levels 1–5. Early on, W is either unavailable or on a long cooldown, making it hard to escape when caught. Once you learn R at level 6 and complete your first core item, your contribution to fights rises sharply. Because health and ability power increase each other, you grow stronger faster as you build items. Minimize losses early and aim to contribute to teamfights in the mid and late game.
vladimir-phase.text: Vladimir is weakest at levels 1–5: W is either unavailable or on a long cooldown, leaving him little chance to escape if caught, and his abilities still deal little damage. His contribution to fights rises sharply once he learns R at level 6 and completes his first core item. Health and ability power increase each other, so his strength grows faster as he builds items; minimize losses early and look to contribute in teamfights in the mid and late game.

vladimir-situational-antiheal.basis: If the enemy team also relies on healing to survive, buy Morellonomicon between core items. Repeated area damage lets you keep applying Grievous Wounds to multiple enemies.
vladimir-situational-antiheal.text: If the enemy team also relies on healing to survive, buy Morellonomicon between core items. Vladimir’s repeated area damage can keep Grievous Wounds applied to multiple enemies.

vladimir-situational-zhonya.basis: If the enemy has a burst champion that dives onto Vladimir, buy Zhonya's Hourglass early. Alternating W and Zhonya's Hourglass lets you survive two engages in one fight.
vladimir-situational-zhonya.text: If the enemy has a burst champion that dives onto Vladimir, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. W alone cannot cover the gaps between its cooldowns; alternating it with Zhonya’s Hourglass lets you survive two engages in one fight.

vladimir-skill-e.basis: E consumes health while charging and deals more damage the longer it charges. Charging E past a certain point adds a slow. Vladimir moves more slowly while charging E, and it fires automatically after a while. Choose where to aim when you start charging E. Enemy units in front block E, so don't fire it at an enemy champion through a minion wave.
vladimir-skill-e.text: E costs health to charge and deals more damage the longer Vladimir charges it, gaining a slow past a certain point. He moves more slowly during the charge, and E fires automatically after a while, so choose your target when you begin charging. Enemy units in front can block the wave; avoid firing through a minion wave at an enemy champion.

vladimir-skill-passive.basis: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into ability power and ability power into maximum health. Building health also increases your damage. W and E scale with health, so their area damage grows as you build health.
vladimir-skill-passive.text: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into ability power and ability power into maximum health, so building health also increases Vladimir’s damage. W and E scale with health, making their area damage grow as he builds it.

vladimir-skill-q-empower.basis: After two Q casts, a third Q used within a short time deals more damage and heals more. Use Q twice on minions to empower it, then use it on the enemy champion. Prime Q just before a fight so your first Q is empowered. Q deals damage before healing and costs no resources, making it reliable for last hits. If you need healing, use Q on an enemy champion instead of a minion, which gives reduced healing.
vladimir-skill-q-empower.text: After two Q casts, using a third within a short time greatly increases its damage and healing. Cast Q twice on minions, then use the empowered cast on the enemy champion; priming it just before a fight also lets you open with an empowered Q. Because Q deals damage before healing and costs no resources, it is reliable for last hits, but use it on an enemy champion when you need to heal, since it restores less health against minions.

vladimir-skill-r.basis: Enemies infected by R briefly take increased damage from all sources. R explodes after a delay and heals Vladimir based on the number of champions hit. R also amplifies allied damage, so use it early in a fight. Hit multiple enemies with R when they group up or right after an ally lands area crowd control.
vladimir-skill-r.text: Enemies infected by R briefly take increased damage from all sources. After a delay, it explodes and heals Vladimir based on the number of champions hit. Because it also amplifies allied damage, cast R early in a fight and aim to catch multiple enemies when they group up or just after an ally lands area crowd control.

vladimir-teamfight.basis: In teamfights, move between the front and back lines while dealing area damage. Without guaranteed crowd control, Vladimir struggles to start fights himself. Hit as many enemies as possible with R, then move in with your allies when they engage. Engage when W is ready and the enemy has used targeted crowd control on your team's initiator. Hitting more enemies increases your healing, so dive into grouped enemies instead of chasing one target.
vladimir-teamfight.text: In teamfights, Vladimir moves between the front and back lines while dealing area damage. He lacks guaranteed crowd control to start a fight himself, so hit as many enemies as possible with R and move in when your allies engage. Enter when W is ready and the enemy has already used targeted crowd control on your team’s initiator. Hitting several enemies increases his healing, so dive into grouped opponents instead of chasing one target.

volibear-combo-basic.basis: Activate Q and approach, stun with the empowered basic attack, then use W, a basic attack, and a second W in that order. Q's stun is delivered through an empowered basic attack. Approach with Q, then stun with a basic attack once you are in range. Aim to land W twice during the stun when trading.
volibear-combo-basic.text: For a basic engage, activate Q and close the gap, stun with its empowered basic attack, then use W, a basic attack, and W again. Q delivers its stun through the attack, so pressing the ability before you reach the target will not stun them; use its movement speed to get into range. Aim to land both W casts during the stun when trading.

volibear-combo-ult.basis: Leap in with R, then stun with Q after landing and use W and E. Start a turret dive by landing with R to disable the nearby turret briefly. Against mobile opponents, use R when they are immobilized or have no escape route. R grants bonus health, letting you keep fighting after you land.
volibear-combo-ult.text: For an R combo, leap in and land, stun with Q, then use W and E. Opening a turret dive with R briefly disables a turret near the landing point, while its bonus health lets you keep fighting. Because the leap is telegraphed and mobile opponents can evade it, use R when they are already immobilized or have no escape route.

volibear-combo-w-mark.basis: Using W again on a target hit by W deals more damage and restores health. Land a few basic attacks after the first W, then use the second W. If you expect to fight a champion, save your first W instead of using it on a minion.
volibear-combo-w-mark.text: W marks its target; casting it again on that target deals much more damage and restores health. Weave a few basic attacks between casts instead of using both back to back, and save the first W for the champion if a fight is coming rather than spending it on a minion and throwing off the second cast's timing.

volibear-laning.basis: Farm with W and manage your mana during lane. Trade when Q is available again. Trade when the enemy wave pushes toward your turret and you can catch the opponent nearby.
volibear-laning.text: Farm with W and manage your mana in lane, then trade only when Q is available. Without Q’s stun, the opponent can simply walk away while Volibear wastes mana. The best time to trade is when the enemy wave has pushed toward your turret and you can catch the opponent nearby.

volibear-laning-ranged.basis: Against ranged opponents, poke with E while securing CS. Approach with Q just after a ranged opponent uses a poke ability or steps forward from behind their minions. Early on, Volibear can usually win trades against ranged opponents if he closes the gap.
volibear-laning-ranged.text: Against ranged opponents, secure CS and poke with E instead of spending Q on an uncertain engage. Activate Q to close in just after they use a poke ability or step out from behind their minions. Volibear's relatively high level-one health and attack damage mean he can usually win the trade once he reaches them.

volibear-phase.basis: Volibear is strong in early melee trades. Before learning several abilities, he runs out of mana quickly. Your first power spikes come when W gains ranks and Q is available, and at level 6 when you learn R. Later on, enemy defensive items and healing reduction make it harder to survive on W's healing alone. Secure your lead in the mid game through dives and objectives.
volibear-phase.text: Volibear's relatively high level-one health and attack damage make him strong in early melee trades, though he runs out of mana quickly before learning several abilities. His first power spikes come as W gains ranks and Q comes back up, then at level 6 when he learns R. Later, defensive items and healing reduction make W's healing less reliable for survival, so use midgame dives and objectives to close out the game.

volibear-situational-antiheal.basis: Buy Executioner's Calling between core items against opponents with strong healing. Volibear can stay close and keep applying healing reduction with basic attacks and W.
volibear-situational-antiheal.text: Against champions with strong healing, fit Executioner's Calling between your core items. Volibear can stay close and keep applying healing reduction through basic attacks and W.

volibear-situational-mr.basis: If your lane opponent deals mostly magic damage, get magic resistance early. Choose Banshee's Veil if an opponent has a targeted ability that could be decisive. Choose Quicksilver Sash if guaranteed crowd control stops your engage.
volibear-situational-mr.text: If your lane opponent deals mostly magic damage, build magic resistance early. Choose Banshee's Veil against a potentially decisive targeted ability, or Quicksilver Sash if guaranteed crowd control keeps stopping your engage.

volibear-skill-e.basis: E is Volibear's only ranged ability, dealing damage based on maximum health and slowing enemies. Use E to poke opponents or clear waves when closing the gap is difficult. To hit a moving opponent with E, overlap it with Q's stun or an ally's immobilizing effect. E grants a shield only if Volibear is inside its blast area. E costs a lot of mana and has a long cooldown, so avoid using it out of habit before engaging.
volibear-skill-e.text: E is Volibear's only ranged ability, dealing damage based on maximum health and slowing enemies, so use it to poke or clear waves when you cannot close the gap. Its delayed strike is easy for moving opponents to dodge; place it over Q's stun or an ally's immobilizing effect. Volibear gains the shield only if he is inside the blast area, so even when using E to escape, place it underfoot as you move away. Its high mana cost and long cooldown also mean that using it out of habit can leave you without a shield for your next engage.

volibear-skill-passive.basis: Dealing damage with abilities and basic attacks builds passive attack speed stacks. At maximum passive stacks, your basic attacks also hit nearby enemies. Volibear's damage depends heavily on his passive stacks. Hit minions or jungle monsters just before a fight to build passive stacks.
volibear-skill-passive.text: Damaging enemies with abilities or basic attacks builds passive attack speed stacks; at maximum stacks, basic attacks also hit nearby enemies. Volibear's damage depends heavily on those stacks, so build them on minions or jungle monsters just before a fight. Engaging with no stacks can produce a very different result even with the same abilities.

volibear-skill-q.basis: Q's movement speed bonus doubles when you move toward an enemy champion. The movement speed bonus is smaller when fleeing, so use Q to close the gap. If you are immobilized before landing Q's stun, Q ends but its cooldown resets. Use Q first when trying to draw out the opponent's guaranteed crowd control.
volibear-skill-q.text: Q's movement speed bonus doubles only while moving toward an enemy champion, making it much less effective for escaping than for closing the gap. If you are immobilized before landing the stun, Q ends but its cooldown resets, so using it first to draw out an opponent's guaranteed crowd control carries little cost.

volibear-skill-r.basis: Turrets near R's landing point are briefly disabled. Dive with R when an opponent stays under turret for safety. Save R as a last resort for escaping.
volibear-skill-r.text: R deals damage and enables dives by briefly disabling turrets near its landing point, making the best time to use it when an opponent stays under turret for safety. Its bonus health can also help you escape, but doing so gives up its unique turret-disabling value, so save it for escapes only as a last resort.

volibear-skill-w.basis: W's short cooldown makes it central to farming and trading in lane. W heals more when you have more missing health.
volibear-skill-w.text: W provides both damage and sustain, and its short cooldown makes it central to farming and trading in lane. Because the heal scales with missing health, it restores far more after you’ve taken damage than when you’re at full health. Volibear is strongest when he’s around half health and closes in after the opponent backs away.

volibear-teamfight.basis: After an ally starts the fight and the opponents use their abilities, enter the backline with R. When you enter the backline with R, lock down an enemy damage dealer. Build passive stacks before entering a teamfight to damage nearby enemies too. If the enemy formation is not spread out, hold R, approach with Q, and hold the frontline.
volibear-teamfight.text: In a teamfight, wait for an ally to start the fight and for opponents to spend their abilities before using R to reach and lock down a backline damage dealer; going in first leaves you exposed to all their crowd control. Build passive stacks before entering so your attacks also damage nearby enemies. If the enemy formation is grouped together, hold R, approach with Q, and hold the frontline.

vs-aatrox-early.basis: Aatrox turns early advantages into much larger leads. Focus on securing CS without giving up kills early so the matchup improves as the game goes on.
vs-aatrox-early.text: Aatrox can turn an early advantage into a much larger lead. Secure CS without giving up early kills, and the matchup will improve as the game goes on.

vs-aatrox-passive.basis: Aatrox's empowered auto deals heavy damage early on. Try to trade right after Aatrox uses his empowered auto on a minion.
vs-aatrox-passive.text: Aatrox’s empowered auto deals heavy damage early, so trade right after he uses it on a minion.

vs-aatrox-q.basis: Aatrox relies on Q for most of his damage. Avoiding Q's sweet spot greatly reduces the damage you take. When you see Aatrox cast Q, move outside or inside the blade's tip area. Aatrox's attacks have pronounced windups, giving opponents time to react.
vs-aatrox-q.text: Aatrox relies on Q for most of his damage, so avoiding its sweet spot greatly reduces the damage you take. When you see him cast Q, move outside the blade’s tip area or step inside it; his pronounced windups give you time to react.

vs-aatrox-r.basis: Aatrox gains increased attack damage when he uses R. Aatrox gains increased self-healing when he uses R. R's duration can only be extended through takedowns. When Aatrox activates R, create distance to avoid taking a 1v1. Wait out Aatrox's R, then look to fight again.
vs-aatrox-r.text: R increases Aatrox’s attack damage and self-healing, which can reverse the outcome of a duel even at the same health. Its duration extends only through takedowns, so when he activates it, avoid the 1v1, create distance, and fight again after it expires.

vs-aatrox-w.basis: If W hits you, leave its area within the allotted time before it pulls you to the center. W's area is a circle centered where the chain hit you. Within W's area, the distance to get out is the same in any direction. If W hits you, walk out immediately instead of hesitating over which direction to take. Save your mobility ability to get out of W.
vs-aatrox-w.text: If W hits you, leave its area before the allotted time runs out or it will pull you to the center. The area is a circle centered where the chain hit you, so the distance to escape is the same in any direction: walk out immediately instead of hesitating, and save your mobility ability for this moment.

vs-ahri-e.basis: Standing behind minions lets them block Ahri's E. Ahri's damage potential drops sharply without Charm. During laning, keep the minion wave between you and Ahri.
vs-ahri-e.text: Stand behind minions to block Ahri’s E Charm. Her damage potential drops sharply without it, so keep the minion wave between you and Ahri throughout laning.

vs-ahri-fight.basis: Ahri is most vulnerable right after she uses E. Close in and attack as soon as you dodge Ahri's Charm. Ahri can create distance with an R dash. Ahri can create distance with W's movement speed boost.
vs-ahri-fight.text: Ahri has some of the lowest defensive stats among champions and is most vulnerable right after using E Charm. Close in and attack as soon as you dodge it; her remaining ways to create distance are an R Spirit Rush dash and W Fox-Fire’s movement speed boost.

vs-ahri-q.basis: Ahri's Q hits on both the outward and return paths. After dodging Q's first hit, keep moving out of its return path. Q's return damage is true damage, so magic resistance cannot reduce it.
vs-ahri-q.text: Ahri’s Q Orb of Deception hits on both its outward and return paths. After dodging the first hit, keep moving out of the orb’s path back to Ahri. The return hit deals true damage, so magic resistance cannot reduce it.

vs-ahri-ult.basis: Ahri has no mobility ability available when R is down. Track when Ahri's R will be available again. Time your ganks or engages for when Ahri's R is unavailable.
vs-ahri-ult.text: Ahri has no mobility ability when R Spirit Rush is down. Track its cooldown and time your ganks or engages for the window before it becomes available again.

vs-akali-e-mark.basis: If you are marked by E, Akali's second dash follows you wherever you run. Dodging the first E takes away one of Akali's ways to close in. Make dodging Akali's first E, a skillshot shuriken, your top priority.
vs-akali-e-mark.text: If Akali marks you with E, her second dash follows you wherever you run. Dodging the first E takes away one way she can close the gap, so make avoiding that skillshot shuriken your top priority.

vs-akali-early.basis: Akali is weak in close-range trades before level 6. Wait for Akali to leave the smoke and attack, then fight back. Build a health and CS lead while Akali's ultimate is unavailable.
vs-akali-early.text: Akali has some of the lowest armor, making her weak in close-range trades before level 6. Wait for her to leave the smoke and attack, then fight back; build a health and CS lead while her ultimate is unavailable.

vs-akali-r.basis: Akali's first cast of R is a targeted dash over an enemy champion. You can't dodge Akali's first cast of R by walking. Save your mobility or disengage tools while Akali is on you. When Akali engages with R, stop her with a mobility or disengage tool.
vs-akali-r.text: Akali’s first R is a targeted dash over an enemy champion, so you cannot dodge it by walking. Save your mobility or disengage tool while she is on you, then use it to interrupt her R engage.

vs-akali-shroud-entry.basis: Akali briefly appears when she enters the smoke. Cast skillshots during the brief moment Akali appears as she enters the smoke.
vs-akali-shroud-entry.text: Akali briefly appears when she enters her smoke. Throw a skillshot during that window to hit her inside it.

vs-akali-shroud-reveal.basis: Turrets and true sight reveal Akali inside the smoke. Place a Control Ward in the smoke to remove Akali's stealth advantage. Draw the fight near a turret to remove Akali's stealth advantage.
vs-akali-shroud-reveal.text: Turrets and true sight reveal Akali inside her smoke. Place a Control Ward in the smoke or draw the fight near a turret to remove her stealth advantage.

vs-akshan-camo.basis: W's camouflage lasts longer only near terrain and brush. Establish vision around river and jungle walls to track Akshan's roaming routes. In open areas, Akshan's W camouflage ends on its own. Stay grouped to stop Akshan from approaching under camouflage.
vs-akshan-camo.text: W (Going Rogue) camouflage lasts longer only near terrain and brush. Place vision around river and jungle walls to reveal Akshan's roaming route; his camouflage ends on its own in open areas. Entering an enemy champion's detection range also reveals him, so staying grouped can prevent a camouflaged approach.

vs-akshan-e.basis: Akshan must hook onto terrain to use E. Push Akshan into open areas to prevent him from engaging or escaping with E. Walk into the path of Akshan's E swing to interrupt his movement. A takedown resets Akshan's E cooldown.
vs-akshan-e.text: Akshan needs terrain to hook onto for E (Heroic Swing). Push him into an open area without walls to deny both his engage and escape, or walk into his swing path to end it immediately. A takedown resets E's cooldown, so denying him a kill also prevents that reset.

vs-akshan-early.basis: Akshan is weak in early basic attack fights. If you can pressure at close range, play aggressively at levels 1–2 to gain an advantage. After the early pressure, farm outside Akshan's Q poke range.
vs-akshan-early.text: Akshan's level 1 attack damage is among the lowest of all champions, leaving him weak in early basic attack fights. If your champion can pressure him at close range, push for an advantage at levels 1–2, then farm outside his Q (Avengerang) poke range.

vs-akshan-q.basis: Akshan's Q boomerang travels farther each time it hits an enemy. Do not stand behind the minion wave to dodge Q. Dodge both Q's outgoing and returning paths. If Akshan moves sideways, Q's return path shifts with him.
vs-akshan-q.text: Akshan's Q (Avengerang) travels farther each time it hits an enemy, making it dangerous to stand behind a minion wave. Dodge both its outgoing and returning paths, and account for the return path shifting if Akshan moves sideways after throwing it.

vs-akshan-r.basis: Akshan is rooted in place while aiming R. When Akshan aims R, an indicator appears on the target. If R targets you while you are low on health, move behind terrain. Someone in front can take Akshan's R bullets for you. Do not flee alone through an open area while Akshan is aiming R.
vs-akshan-r.text: Akshan is rooted while aiming R (Comeuppance), and an indicator appears on its target. If you are low on health, move behind terrain to block all the bullets, or stay grouped so someone in front can take them for you. Fleeing alone through an open area is the most dangerous option.

vs-akshan-w.basis: Killing one of Akshan's allies marks you as a Scoundrel. If Akshan kills you while you are marked as a Scoundrel, the enemies you killed are revived. While marked as a Scoundrel, avoid facing Akshan alone. If you are marked as a Scoundrel, fight outside Akshan's finishing range in teamfights.
vs-akshan-w.text: Killing one of Akshan's allies marks you as a Scoundrel. If Akshan kills you while you are marked, the allies of his whom you killed are revived. Until the mark is gone, avoid facing him alone and fight outside his finishing range in teamfights.

vs-alistar-cooldown.basis: Alistar's threat comes from his close-range Q and W. Counterattack right after Alistar uses Q and W. Push the lane or reposition while Alistar's Q and W are on cooldown.
vs-alistar-cooldown.text: Alistar’s threat comes from his close-range Q and W. Counterattack immediately after he uses both; while they are on cooldown, he can do little, so use that time to push the lane or reposition.

vs-alistar-r.basis: Alistar takes much less damage while his R is active. When Alistar activates R, back off and fight again after it expires.
vs-alistar-r.text: Alistar takes much less damage while R is active. When he uses it, avoid wasting abilities on him; back off, let it expire, then fight again.

vs-ambessa-e.basis: Ambessa’s E slow is strong enough to nearly stop you, but wears off quickly. Immediately after E hits you, use a mobility ability or cleanse to avoid the Q attack at the blade’s edge that follows.
vs-ambessa-e.text: Ambessa’s E applies a slow that nearly stops you but wears off quickly. Use a mobility ability or cleanse immediately after it hits to avoid the Q strike at the blade’s edge; waiting for the slow to end gives her time to finish the combo.

vs-ambessa-passive.basis: Ambessa can follow her abilities with short dashes. While she has stacks remaining, her basic attack range and attack speed increase. Step forward only while Ambessa’s abilities are on cooldown. Counterattack right after Ambessa has used all her abilities and spent her passive stacks.
vs-ambessa-passive.text: Ambessa can follow each ability with a short dash, and her remaining passive stacks increase basic attack range and attack speed. An ability can close a gap that looks safe, so step forward only while her abilities are on cooldown; counterattack right after she has used them all and spent her stacks.

vs-ambessa-phase.basis: Exploit Ambessa’s weakness at levels 1–2, when she has only one or two abilities. Exploit Ambessa’s weakness right after she uses all her abilities. Ambessa is strongest in the mid game as she builds core items. Avoid giving up kills early and keep up in levels. Once Ambessa learns R, its armor penetration and healing apply even when she does not use it.
vs-ambessa-phase.text: Ambessa is weakest at levels 1–2, when she has only one or two abilities, and immediately after using them all; she peaks in the mid game as core items come together. Avoid giving up early kills and keep up in levels to improve the matchup. Once she learns R, its armor penetration and healing remain active even while it is unused, so do not assume a one-on-one fight is safe just because she has cast it.

vs-ambessa-q.basis: Both of Ambessa’s Q strikes deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes; hits closer in deal half damage. If you cannot easily run far enough from Q, move close to Ambessa to reduce its damage. If you dodge the first Q, Cunning Sweep, completely, the second slam will not be readied.
vs-ambessa-q.text: Both strikes of Ambessa’s Q deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes and half damage closer in. If you cannot easily get out of range, move toward Ambessa to take less damage. Dodging the first strike, Cunning Sweep, completely prevents Sundering Slam from being readied.

vs-ambessa-r.basis: Ambessa’s R moves her to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line. Ambessa is unstoppable during R, so crowd control cannot interrupt it. During a standoff, position so Ambessa and your backline aren't in a straight line.
vs-ambessa-r.text: Ambessa’s R teleports her to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line. She is unstoppable during the cast, so crowd control cannot interrupt it; even if a tank stands in front, R will catch a backline champion farther along that line. During a standoff, avoid lining up your backline with Ambessa, and have backline champions use walls or allies to break her angle.

vs-ambessa-w.basis: When Ambessa gains a shield and briefly winds up, she has used W. Damaging Ambessa with an ability or basic attack during W’s windup greatly empowers its slam. When you see Ambessa wind up W, stop attacking and walk out of its range.
vs-ambessa-w.text: A shield followed by a brief windup signals Ambessa’s W (Repudiation). Abilities or basic attacks that damage her during that windup greatly empower its slam, so stop attacking and walk out of range.

vs-amumu-cleanse.basis: Make Amumu use R before starting a full fight. Once Amumu has used R, his teamfight threat drops sharply. A key damage dealer can neutralize Amumu's R with Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar.
vs-amumu-cleanse.text: Amumu poses little threat once R is down, so draw it out before committing to a full fight. Even one source of crowd control removal on your team can turn the teamfight, and a key damage dealer with Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar can negate an entire R.

vs-amumu-e.basis: Amumu's E passive reduces physical damage taken. The more auto attacks Amumu takes, the shorter E's cooldown becomes. If you deal physical damage against Amumu, build armor penetration. When attacking Amumu, combine your damage with your allies' magic damage.
vs-amumu-e.text: Amumu's E, Tantrum, passively reduces physical damage taken, and basic attacks against him shorten its cooldown. Trying to bring him down with physical damage alone takes time and lets him cast E repeatedly, so build armor penetration or attack alongside allies who deal magic damage.

vs-amumu-early.basis: Before level 6, Amumu is weak because his jungle clear is slow and costs a lot of health. Invade Amumu's jungle early to delay his level 6. Push lanes that offer early gank opportunities in advance to delay Amumu's level 6. Exploit Amumu's weak period before he gets R.
vs-amumu-early.text: Before level 6, Amumu is weak because his jungle clear is slow and costs a lot of health. Invade his jungle early or push lanes that offer gank opportunities in advance to delay his level 6. Exploit this window before he gets R, or he will keep dictating when fights begin afterward.

vs-amumu-q.basis: Amumu's Q is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Keep minions or jungle monsters between you and Amumu to block his Q engage. In lane, move unpredictably and stand behind minions to avoid Amumu's ganks.
vs-amumu-q.text: Amumu's Q, Bandage Toss, is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Keep a minion wave or jungle monsters between you and him to block his way in; in lane, moving unpredictably and staying behind minions greatly reduces his chance of a successful gank.

vs-amumu-r.basis: Amumu's R is an area stun around him. When Amumu has R available, don't stand close together with your allies. Against Amumu's R, fight in open areas rather than narrow passages. Keep your distance before Amumu gets close enough to use R.
vs-amumu-r.text: Amumu's R, Curse of the Sad Mummy, stuns an area around him. While he has it available, spread out from your allies and take fights in open terrain instead of narrow passages. Its short range means keeping your distance before Amumu gets close will largely neutralize it.

vs-amumu-w.basis: Amumu's W continually deals magic damage based on the maximum health of nearby enemies. Against Amumu, build magic resistance as well as health. Even as a frontliner, adjust your spacing so you don't stay beside Amumu for long.
vs-amumu-w.text: Amumu's W, Despair, continually deals nearby enemies magic damage based on their maximum health. Health alone is less effective against him, so include magic resistance in your defensive build. Even as a frontliner, keep adjusting your distance so you do not remain beside Amumu for long.

vs-anivia-e.basis: If Q hits you or you're chilled inside a fully grown R, E deals double damage to you. Right after Q hits you, watch out for the empowered E. If Q hits you, stop fighting and immediately leave R or use a mobility skill to dodge the next E.
vs-anivia-e.text: A Q hit or a fully grown Glacial Storm (R) chills you, causing the next Frostbite (E) to deal double damage. Anivia’s burst window comes immediately after Q lands, so stop fighting in place and immediately leave the storm or use a mobility ability to avoid the next E.

vs-anivia-early.basis: Anivia has no mobility skill. Before level 6, pressure Anivia with your jungler to force her egg or look for a kill. A lead gained before level 6 weakens Anivia's late-game terrain control.
vs-anivia-early.text: Anivia has some of the lowest movement speed and health in the game and no mobility ability. Pressure her with your jungler before level 6 to force Rebirth or kill her outright; a lead built then weakens her ability to control terrain later.

vs-anivia-egg.basis: When Anivia takes lethal damage, she becomes an egg and revives with full health. To make sure the egg is destroyed, attack it with your jungler or another ally. After Anivia revives, look for a kill while her passive is on cooldown.
vs-anivia-egg.text: When Anivia takes lethal damage, she turns into an egg and revives at full health. It is hard to destroy the egg alone, so attack with your jungler or another ally to make sure it breaks. Once she has revived, she is among the most fragile champions until Rebirth comes off cooldown; that is your chance to kill her.

vs-anivia-q.basis: Anivia can reactivate her straight-traveling Q to detonate it in place and stun. If you're a ranged champion, stay outside Anivia's Q range. If you're a melee champion, close in on Anivia and move past Q's explosion radius.
vs-anivia-q.text: Flash Frost (Q) travels in a straight line, then explodes and stuns where it is when Anivia reactivates it. Simply sidestepping its path can leave you caught by a predicted detonation. As a ranged champion, stay outside Q’s range; as a melee champion, move toward Anivia and past the explosion radius.

vs-anivia-wall.basis: Even a low-level W blocks a jungle path. Fight Anivia in a wide lane when possible so W cannot block your escape. When engaging, save Flash in case W separates you from your allies.
vs-anivia-wall.text: Crystallize (W) can block an entire jungle passage even at a low level. In narrow jungle or river paths, a single wall can cut off your escape from Anivia, so fight her in a wide part of the lane when possible. When engaging, save Flash in case the wall separates you from your allies.

vs-annie-mr.basis: All of Annie's damage is magic, and learning R also grants her magic penetration. Get enough magic resistance to survive one burst from Annie. Counterattack after surviving Annie's combo.
vs-annie-mr.text: All of Annie’s damage is magic, and learning R (Summon: Tibbers) grants her magic penetration. Build enough magic resistance to survive her burst, then counterattack after her combo.

vs-annie-no-mobility.basis: Annie has no mobility ability. Approach Annie when her stun is unavailable. If you have forced Annie to use Flash, look for a jungle gank.
vs-annie-no-mobility.text: Annie has no mobility ability, and her health and defenses are among the lowest. Close in when her stun is unavailable, leaving her few ways to respond; if you have forced her to use Flash, a jungle gank can secure the kill.

vs-annie-passive.basis: A white swirl around Annie means her stun is ready. Do not enter Annie's ability range while her stun indicator is visible. Pressure Annie right after she uses her stun, before she rebuilds the stacks.
vs-annie-passive.text: A white swirl around Annie means her stun is ready, so stay outside her ability range while it is visible. Once she uses the stun, pressure her before she can rebuild the stacks.

vs-annie-range.basis: Annie's ability range is relatively short for a mage. Poke Annie from long range. Look for the moment Annie pushes forward through your poke.
vs-annie-range.text: Annie’s abilities have relatively short range for a mage, so poke her from a distance. Against a longer range opponent, she must spend health and mana to move forward; look for that moment.

vs-annie-teamfight.basis: If Annie is out of sight or her stun is ready, don’t group up in twos or threes. Decide in advance who will take down Annie immediately when she moves forward with R.
vs-annie-teamfight.text: Most of Annie’s teamfight impact rests on a single area stun from Summon: Tibbers (R). If she is out of sight or her stun is ready, avoid standing together in groups of two or three. R has short range, so she must move forward to use it; decide in advance who will take her down immediately when she does.

vs-annie-tibbers.basis: Summoned Tibbers deals continuous damage to nearby enemies. Keep your distance from summoned Tibbers even after killing Annie. When Annie dies, Tibbers becomes enraged and moves faster. Summoned Tibbers can be killed with Smite.
vs-annie-tibbers.text: Summoned Tibbers continuously burns nearby enemies, so keep your distance even after killing Annie. Her death enrages him and makes him faster, and he can be dealt with using Smite.

vs-aphelios-calibrum.basis: If you are marked by Calibrum, you can be attacked once more from beyond Aphelios's normal range. If you are marked by Calibrum, retreat immediately to preserve your health.
vs-aphelios-calibrum.text: A Calibrum mark lets Aphelios hit you once more from beyond his normal range. Retreat as soon as you are marked and preserve your health; if you keep taking damage during the Calibrum phase, you may lack the health to withstand an all-in during the Infernum and Gravitum phase.

vs-aphelios-gravitum.basis: If Aphelios uses Q while you are slowed by Gravitum, you will be rooted. If a Gravitum basic attack slows you, immediately retreat out of range. Do not group with allies while slowed by Gravitum.
vs-aphelios-gravitum.text: Gravitum Q roots anyone slowed by that weapon. If a Gravitum basic attack slows you, immediately move out of range, and do not stand close to allies while the slow is active.

vs-aphelios-mobility.basis: Aphelios has very little mobility. When Aphelios does not have Severum, he has no way to escape other than Flash. Look for a chance to catch Aphelios when he does not have Severum.
vs-aphelios-mobility.text: Aphelios has very little mobility and, without Severum, has no escape other than Flash. Catch him during that window and you can take him out before a teamfight begins.

vs-aphelios-ult.basis: Aphelios's R must hit a champion to trigger. Every champion hit by R takes one additional attack from the main weapon. If Aphelios can use R, spread out from your allies before engaging.
vs-aphelios-ult.text: R Moonlight Vigil must hit a champion to trigger, and every champion it hits takes one additional attack from Aphelios’s main weapon. The more tightly you group, the greater the damage, so spread out before engaging when he can use R.

vs-aphelios-weapon-read.basis: You can see Aphelios's next weapon in his E slot. Trade with Aphelios when he has a weapon with low immediate damage.
vs-aphelios-weapon-read.text: Aphelios’s strength depends on the weapons he is holding. His E slot reveals the next weapon, so watch what is coming and trade when his current weapons have low immediate damage; you can win decisively even at the same level.

vs-ashe-mobility.basis: Ashe has virtually no mobility or defensive tools, leaving her vulnerable to enemies who get close. Focus your resources on creating chances to get close to Ashe in lane and teamfights.
vs-ashe-mobility.text: Ashe has virtually no mobility or defensive tools, making her vulnerable once an enemy gets close. In lane and teamfights, commit your resources to creating a way to reach her.

vs-ashe-q-window.basis: When Ashe builds stacks with basic attacks and activates Q, her damage rises sharply for a short time. Keep your distance while Ashe's Q is active. Move in after Ashe's Q ends.
vs-ashe-q-window.text: Once Ashe builds stacks with basic attacks and activates Q Ranger's Focus, her damage rises sharply for a short time. Keep your distance while it is active, then move in after it ends.

vs-ashe-r.basis: R travels in a straight line. When Ashe's R is ready, avoid initiating small skirmishes from outside vision.
vs-ashe-r.text: Ashe’s R, Enchanted Crystal Arrow, travels in a straight line, so running straight away will get you hit. Keep changing direction to make your movement harder to predict, and avoid starting small skirmishes from outside vision while her R is available.

vs-ashe-slow.basis: Frost Shot's slow refreshes with each of Ashe's basic attacks. Once slowed by Frost Shot, it's hard to create distance by walking. Don't stay within Ashe's basic attack range for long. When approaching Ashe, use a mobility ability to close the gap in one move.
vs-ashe-slow.text: P Frost Shot's slow refreshes with every basic attack, making it hard to escape by walking. Avoid staying within Ashe's basic attack range for long; when you approach, use a mobility ability to close the gap in one move.

vs-ashe-w.basis: Move sideways to dodge W's fan-shaped spread. Try to trade damage right after Ashe uses W.
vs-ashe-w.text: Ashe’s lane poke relies entirely on W Volley. Its fan-shaped spread can usually be dodged by stepping sideways, and the moment after she uses W is your chance to trade damage.

vs-asol-e.basis: Enemies below the health threshold are executed at E's center. If you are low on health, avoid even the edge of E. E pulls slowly, so you can walk out right after entering it. If you enter E, keep moving outward immediately.
vs-asol-e.text: E (Singularity) executes enemies at its center when their health is below the threshold. If you are low, avoid even its edge. The pull is slow enough to walk out immediately after entering, so keep moving outward if you get caught.

vs-asol-early.basis: Aurelion Sol is weak early, and W, his mobility tool, has a long cooldown. If your champion can close the gap, engage hard when his W is down. Stop Aurelion Sol from scaling before he stacks Stardust.
vs-asol-early.text: Aurelion Sol’s early health and armor are among the lowest, and his only mobility tool is W (Astral Flight), which has a long cooldown. If your champion can close the gap, engage hard when W is down to stop him from scaling before he stacks Stardust.

vs-asol-q.basis: Q deals full damage to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies. Q must stay on the same target for a while to trigger bonus damage and Stardust. Move out of Q's line of fire quickly.
vs-asol-q.text: Q (Breath of Light) deals full damage only to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies, so stand behind minions or an ally when he tries to poke. It must stay on the same target for a while to trigger bonus damage and Stardust; move out of its line of fire quickly to deny both.

vs-asol-r.basis: Once enough Stardust has stacked, R knocks enemies up and sends out an area shockwave instead of stunning. If several of you are grouped up when empowered R hits, you will be knocked up and slowed. Do not bunch up in narrow passages.
vs-asol-r.text: Once Aurelion Sol has enough Stardust, R changes from a stun into a knockup with an area shockwave and slow. If your team groups up late in the game, a single empowered R can knock everyone up and decide the fight. Spread out before he engages, especially in narrow passages.

vs-asol-stardust.basis: Aurelion Sol's strength scales with his Stardust count. Aurelion Sol does not lose stacked Stardust when he dies. Stay out of range to avoid unnecessary Q poke.
vs-asol-stardust.text: Aurelion Sol’s strength scales with Stardust, which stacks permanently when his abilities damage champions and remains even if he dies. Taking unnecessary Q (Breath of Light) poke helps him grow, so step out of range to avoid it.

vs-aurora-dive.basis: Once an opponent gets close to Aurora, her E hop is her only way to create distance. Engage once to draw out Aurora's E, then catch her with a second engage. After level 6, account for R when engaging on Aurora. If Aurora has used both E and W, look for a chance to catch her while she has trouble escaping.
vs-aurora-dive.text: Aurora has low armor growth, ordinary movement speed, and only E’s backward hop to create distance from an opponent who gets close. Engage once to draw out E, then catch her with a second engage. After level 6, account for R as well; when both E and W are down, she has few ways to escape.

vs-aurora-missing-hp.basis: Q's return damage increases with the target's missing health. If you're below half health, staying in range while cursed by Q can quickly put you within kill range. If your health is uncertain, back off before Q's curse returns.
vs-aurora-missing-hp.text: Q Twofold Hex deals more damage on its return based on the target’s missing health, so trades against Aurora become sharply worse as your health falls. Below half health, staying nearby while cursed can quickly put you within kill range. If your health is in doubt, back off before Q returns.

vs-aurora-q.basis: Q applies a curse on hit. You take return damage when Aurora recasts Q or its duration ends. If Q curses you, move off the straight line between you and Aurora to reduce the return damage.
vs-aurora-q.text: Q (Twofold Hex) curses you on hit, then deals damage again when Aurora recasts it or its duration ends. That return damage follows the path between you and Aurora, so move off the straight line or change your angle to her substantially after being cursed to reduce the second hit.

vs-aurora-r.basis: Enemies entering or leaving R's area are slowed. To leave without being slowed by R's area, retreat before the area appears. If you remain inside R's area, commit to fighting Aurora. Aurora can cross from one side of R's area to the opposite side.
vs-aurora-r.text: R (Between Worlds) slows enemies entering or leaving its zone. Retreat before the zone appears if you want to get out without taking that slow; if you stay inside, commit to fighting Aurora. She can cross from one side to the other, so chasing her directly may let her escape.

vs-aurora-w.basis: When Aurora suddenly disappears, it's W's brief stealth. When Aurora uses W's stealth, cast an area ability in advance where she might land. W's stealth is brief, so wait a moment for Aurora to reappear.
vs-aurora-w.text: If Aurora suddenly disappears, she has used the brief stealth from W (Across the Veil). Targeted abilities cannot hit her during it, so place an area ability where she may land instead of wasting a cast. Wait a moment and she will reappear.

vs-azir-burst.basis: Don't trade damage with Azir for long; concentrate your attacks in a short burst. When you catch Azir, don't let him go; kill him immediately.
vs-azir-burst.text: Azir grows stronger as time goes on but lacks burst damage. Avoid extended trades and overwhelm him in a short burst. He is fairly fragile, so finish him as soon as you catch him; if you let him go, he will keep wearing you down with his soldiers.

vs-azir-e.basis: Azir can escape by using E to dash to a soldier placed over a wall. If Azir places a soldier near a wall, block that escape route or engage before he uses E. Stand in the path Azir would take with E to stop his dash.
vs-azir-e.text: Azir escapes by using E to dash to a soldier placed beyond a wall. If he places one near a wall, block that route or engage before he can use it. E stops when it collides with an enemy champion, so standing in his intended path can interrupt the dash.

vs-azir-early.basis: Approach when his soldiers expire or Azir is low on mana. Azir cannot use R before level 6. Before level 6, pressure Azir with your jungler to slow his growth.
vs-azir-early.text: Azir aims to farm safely behind his soldiers during laning. Close in when they expire or he runs low on mana, when he has few ways to fight back. He also lacks R before level 6, so pressure him early with your jungler to slow his growth.

vs-azir-r.basis: Azir's R pushes enemies away and creates a soldier wall that remains briefly. Azir's allies can pass through the soldier wall created by R. When engaging Azir's team, spread out and approach from multiple directions in an open area.
vs-azir-r.text: R (Emperor's Divide) pushes enemies away and leaves a soldier wall briefly in place, which Azir’s allies can pass through. If you dive his team in a narrow passage, one R can push back everyone who went in and trap those following behind. Engage in an open area, approaching from multiple directions.

vs-azir-soldier-window.basis: Azir's damage depends on his sand soldiers. Avoid the line where a soldier stands, and approach Azir himself from behind or beside the soldier.
vs-azir-soldier-window.text: All of Azir’s damage comes from his sand soldiers, and Q has a cooldown after moving them. Approach while a soldier is stationary, avoiding the line it stands on; move around behind or beside it to close in on Azir himself.

vs-bard-mobility.basis: Bard's only escape tool is his E portal. After Bard uses his E portal, look for an opening to engage him again.
vs-bard-mobility.text: Bard’s E portal is his only escape tool. Make him use it, then look for another opening to close in and catch him.

vs-bard-portal.basis: The enemy team can also use Bard's E portals. If Bard opens an E portal to escape, follow him through and chase when it is safe. Bard can enter through an E portal, so do not leave your flank open.
vs-bard-portal.text: The opposing team can use Bard’s E portals too. If he opens one to escape, follow and chase when it’s safe; also keep your flank covered, since Bard can enter through a portal.

vs-bard-q.basis: Bard's Q must hit a wall or a second target to stun. When facing Bard, do not stand with your back to a wall. Position yourself so you do not line up with an ally or minion.
vs-bard-q.text: Bard’s Q needs a wall or a second target to stun. Don’t stand with your back to a wall or line up with an ally or minion, and you’ll only be slowed.

vs-bard-roam.basis: Bard often leaves lane to collect chimes. When Bard disappears from view, you can create a 2v1 in bot lane. When Bard disappears from view, signal on the minimap that he may appear in another lane.
vs-bard-roam.text: Bard often leaves lane to collect chimes. When he disappears from view, you have a chance to create a 2v1 in bot lane; signal on the minimap at the same time, since he may appear in another lane.

vs-bard-shrine.basis: Bard's W shrines disappear when stepped on. If you see a W shrine in lane, change your path if needed to step on it and remove it.
vs-bard-shrine.text: Bard’s W shrines disappear when an enemy steps on them. If you see one in lane, adjust your path to remove it rather than letting Bard or his allies use it for free.

vs-belveth-coral.basis: Bel'Veth needs a takedown on a champion or epic monster to get coral and transform. Giving Bel'Veth one kill makes the next fight much harder. If you lose an ally in a fight, retreat before Bel'Veth picks up the coral. Delay team fights while Bel'Veth is transformed.
vs-belveth-coral.text: Bel’Veth needs a champion or epic monster takedown to obtain Void Coral and transform, so giving her even one kill makes the next fight much harder. If an ally dies in a fight, retreat before she collects the coral rather than re-engaging there, and delay team fights while she is transformed.

vs-belveth-e.basis: Bel'Veth takes much less damage while casting E. Use burst abilities after Bel'Veth's E ends. Interrupt Bel'Veth's E with immobilizing crowd control.
vs-belveth-e.text: Bel’Veth takes much less damage while standing still and casting E, so using burst abilities into it wastes their damage. Wait until E ends before using them, or interrupt the cast with immobilizing crowd control.

vs-belveth-early.basis: Pressure Bel'Veth with jungle invades or early encounters at levels 1–3. Take large monsters and camps from Bel'Veth before she builds stacks to slow her growth.
vs-belveth-early.text: Bel’Veth has low health and attack damage at levels 1–3, making jungle invades and early encounters strong opportunities to pressure her. Take large monsters and camps before she builds stacks to slow her growth.

vs-belveth-q.basis: Bel'Veth's Q has a separate cooldown for each direction. Bel'Veth cannot immediately dash again in the direction she just used Q. When escaping or using a skillshot, use the line Bel'Veth just dashed along as your reference.
vs-belveth-q.text: Bel’Veth’s Q has a separate cooldown for each direction, so she cannot immediately dash again in the direction she just used. When escaping or aiming a skillshot, use the line she just dashed along as your reference.

vs-belveth-w.basis: W is Bel'Veth's only reliable crowd control. Dodging W prevents the Q reset and slows Bel'Veth's chase. When Bel'Veth closes in, sidestep to dodge W.
vs-belveth-w.text: W (Above and Below) is Bel'Veth's only guaranteed crowd control. Dodging it denies her Q reset and greatly slows her pursuit, leaving her only Q to stay close. When she reaches you, turn sideways to avoid W instead of running straight back.

vs-blitz-cooldown.basis: Q costs a lot of mana at level 1. Q has a long cooldown at level 1. Use the window immediately after a missed level 1 Q to pressure the lane or trade.
vs-blitz-cooldown.text: At level 1, Q costs a lot of mana and has a long cooldown. Immediately after Blitzcrank misses it, he poses no threat for a while, so use that window to push the lane or trade.

vs-blitz-mana.basis: Q costs a lot of mana. Watch Blitzcrank's mana bar to identify safe windows when he cannot use Q.
vs-blitz-mana.text: Q costs a lot of mana, so watch Blitzcrank’s mana bar: when he is out of mana and cannot grab, you have a safe window.

vs-blitz-minion.basis: Q pulls only the first target it hits along its path. Stand behind minions rather than beside them so they block Q.
vs-blitz-minion.text: Q pulls only the first target it hits along its path. Keep minions between you and Blitzcrank in lane by standing behind them, rather than beside them, to block the grab.

vs-blitz-peel.basis: Blitzcrank lacks the damage to finish off targets with crowd control alone. Bypass Blitzcrank and engage on his allies behind him. When enemies bypass Blitzcrank to attack his allies, his ability to protect only one ally becomes a limitation.
vs-blitz-peel.text: Blitzcrank lacks the damage to finish a target with crowd control alone. Bypass him and engage on his allies behind him; he can protect only one of them, giving your team the advantage.

vs-blitz-shield.basis: P creates a shield that scales with mana when health gets low. Account for P's shield, secure a way to finish the kill, then try to kill him in one go.
vs-blitz-shield.text: When Blitzcrank gets low on health, Mana Barrier (P) gives him a shield that scales with mana, making him harder to kill than he looks. Secure a way to finish him before committing to a kill in one burst.

vs-blitz-vision.basis: Giving up brush vision makes it harder to judge grab range. Use Control Wards to secure brush vision. Stay well away from brush when moving through areas without vision.
vs-blitz-vision.text: Without brush vision, you cannot see Blitzcrank’s grab range. Clear the brush with Control Wards, and keep well away from it when moving through areas without vision.

vs-brand-blaze.basis: Brand's threat comes from Blaze stacks more than individual abilities. Getting hit by consecutive abilities builds Blaze stacks until they explode. Dodge the first Q or W to break Brand's combo.
vs-brand-blaze.text: Brand’s threat comes from Blaze stacks rather than individual abilities: consecutive hits build toward an explosion. Dodging his first Q or W breaks the combo, so focus on avoiding that opening hit.

vs-brand-cluster.basis: Brand's E spreads twice as far around a burning target. Brand's R bounces between targets. Space out from your allies before engaging. Do not stand beside a burning ally.
vs-brand-cluster.text: Brand’s E spreads twice as far from a burning target, while R bounces between enemies. If you cluster together, a hit on one player can spread to everyone, so space out before engaging and stay away from any ally who is burning.

vs-brand-minions.basis: Brand uses E on burning minions to poke nearby enemies indirectly. Do not last-hit beside a burning minion. Where minion waves meet, step to the side before moving in.
vs-brand-minions.text: Brand can poke indirectly by applying Blaze to a minion wave and spreading it with E. Avoid last-hitting beside a burning minion, and step to the side before moving in where the waves meet.

vs-brand-punish.basis: Brand has very low health and no mobility abilities. Engage when Brand's W is on cooldown. Without Blaze, Brand cannot stun an enemy who gets close with Q.
vs-brand-punish.text: Brand has very low health and no mobility abilities, so engage as soon as he uses W if he remains in range. Once you get close, his only response is a Q stun, and he cannot land that stun unless you already have Blaze.

vs-brand-r.basis: Brand's R has a slow initial projectile, giving you time to spread out after you see him cast it. Move away from your allies when you see R cast. If you are on fire, move earlier to account for R's slow.
vs-brand-r.text: Brand’s R starts with a slow projectile, giving you time to spread out after you see the cast. Move away from allies immediately; if you are burning, move even earlier because R will also slow you.

vs-braum-damage.basis: Braum's own damage is very low. Target the ally Braum is protecting. Find another route past Braum to the backline.
vs-braum-damage.text: Braum deals very little damage himself. Instead of trying to kill him, target the ally he is protecting or find another route past him to the backline. If you pour damage into Braum, he has already done his job.

vs-braum-e.basis: Projectiles cannot get through from the direction Braum faces with E raised. Wait for the shield to drop before using projectiles. Move around Braum's side and look for an angle to attack from a direction his shield does not face.
vs-braum-e.text: Projectiles cannot get through E from the direction Braum faces. Wait for the shield to drop, or move around his side to attack from outside that direction. If your marksman keeps attacking from the front, Braum can shield his team from your team's damage.

vs-braum-q.basis: Braum must hit Q or a basic attack to apply the first Concussive Blows mark. Stand behind minions to block Braum's Q. Avoid lining up with Braum when a gap opens between minions.
vs-braum-q.text: Braum needs to land Q or a basic attack to apply the first Concussive Blows mark. Q stops at the first enemy it hits, so stand behind minions to block it and avoid lining up with Braum when a gap opens between them.

vs-braum-r.basis: Braum's R has a cast animation that gives you time to dodge. Dodge sideways out of R's straight-line fissure. Position early to avoid stepping into the slowing zone R leaves behind. If you are in the backline, stay out of R's straight path.
vs-braum-r.text: Braum's R has a long enough cast animation to react: dodge sideways out of its straight path and position early to avoid the slowing zone it leaves behind. The farther its first target is from Braum, the longer the knockup, so backline champions should be especially careful to stay off that line.

vs-braum-stacks.basis: Braum's stun triggers only after the mark gains multiple stacks. Once marked, move out of range before the remaining stacks build up.
vs-braum-stacks.text: Braum's stun requires several stacks. Once marked, move out of range before the remaining stacks build to avoid the stun entirely; standing still and taking more hits is the worst choice.

vs-briar-e.basis: Crowd controlling Briar while she charges E can stop her healing and wall stun. When Briar starts charging E, use a stun or knockup. Don't fight with your back to a wall, where Briar's fully charged E can stun you.
vs-briar-e.text: Crowd control during E’s (Chilling Scream) charge can stop both Briar’s healing and her wall stun. As soon as she begins charging the scream, use a stun or knockup, and avoid fighting with your back to a wall because a fully charged E can stun anyone it knocks into one.

vs-briar-r.basis: When Briar fires R, have your frontline stand in front to keep your backline carry from becoming the prey. If you become R's prey, Briar chases you with increased resistances and movement speed. If R marks you as its prey, move toward your allies and fight back together.
vs-briar-r.text: R’s (Certain Death) bloodstone makes the first champion it hits Briar’s prey, so keep your frontline ahead of your backline carry to block the shot. Once marked, you are hard to escape by running alone: Briar gains resistances and movement speed as she chases you to the end. Move toward your allies as soon as you become the prey and fight back together.

vs-caitlyn-e.basis: E is Caitlyn's only escape ability. E moves Caitlyn through recoil. Engage after Caitlyn uses E, when she has no way to create distance.
vs-caitlyn-e.text: Caitlyn's E, 90 Caliber Net, is her only escape and moves her through recoil. Engage after she uses it, when she has no way to create distance.

vs-caitlyn-phase.basis: Caitlyn is strongest during the laning phase and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid taking excessive risks early and giving Caitlyn kills.
vs-caitlyn-phase.text: Caitlyn is strongest in lane and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid taking unnecessary risks and giving her kills early; even farming CS under your turret will improve the matchup.

vs-caitlyn-q.basis: Caitlyn's Q passes through targets. Caitlyn's Q deals reduced damage to targets after the first. Stand behind allied minions when Caitlyn pokes with Q.
vs-caitlyn-q.text: Caitlyn's Q, Piltover Peacemaker, passes through targets but deals reduced damage after the first. When she uses it to poke, stand behind allied minions so they take the first hit.

vs-caitlyn-r.basis: R hits an allied champion of the target instead if they block its path. If an ally is targeted by R, step into the bullet's path to protect them.
vs-caitlyn-r.text: Caitlyn’s R, Ace in the Hole, hits another enemy champion instead if they stand in the bullet’s path. If an ally is targeted, step into its path to block the shot for them.

vs-caitlyn-rooted-cast.basis: Caitlyn stands still while casting Q. Caitlyn stands still while casting R. When you see Q or R's cast animation, close in or find an angle to attack. The moment after Caitlyn uses Q to clear the wave is the best time to engage.
vs-caitlyn-rooted-cast.text: Caitlyn stands still while casting Q or R. When you see either cast animation, close in or find an angle to attack; the best time to engage is just after she uses Q to clear the wave.

vs-caitlyn-trap.basis: Stepping on a W trap roots the target. Caitlyn's Headshot range increases against targets caught in a trap. Assume there are traps in bushes and narrow paths, and change your approach. Send minions ahead into bushes and narrow paths where you expect traps.
vs-caitlyn-trap.text: Stepping on a W trap roots you, extends Caitlyn's Headshot range against you, and exposes you to heavy damage. Assume traps are placed in brush and narrow passages; change your approach or send minions ahead.

vs-camille-e.basis: Camille’s engage relies on E latching its hook onto a wall. Against Camille, stay away from walls and position among minions. Because Camille can use W while traveling on her hook, count areas far from walls as within her threat range too.
vs-camille-e.text: Camille’s engage depends on E latching onto a wall. Against her in lane, stay away from walls, position among minions, and avoid being pushed toward a wall. She can cast W while traveling on the hook, so even positions a considerable distance from a wall can be within her threat range.

vs-camille-e-interrupt.basis: Knockbacks and pulls interrupt Camille’s E leap. If E’s leap is interrupted, Camille loses both the collision stun and the attack speed increase. Save knockbacks or pulls until Camille’s hook latches onto a wall.
vs-camille-e-interrupt.text: A knockback or pull can interrupt Camille’s E leap after her hook latches onto a wall. If interrupted, she loses both the collision stun and the attack speed increase, leaving her in melee range without her engage tool. Save your knockback or pull for the moment the hook catches the wall.

vs-camille-early.basis: Camille is at her weakest before completing her first core item. Camille clears waves slowly. Take lane control before Camille completes her first core item and deny her farm to delay it. Camille takes down turrets quickly from midgame onward. From midgame onward, defend the side lane to stop Camille from taking turrets.
vs-camille-early.text: Camille’s low early stats and slow wave clear leave her weakest before her first core item. Take lane control and deny farm before she completes it to keep delaying her items. From midgame onward, defend the side lane: left alone, she takes down turrets quickly.

vs-camille-passive.basis: Camille’s passive creates only a physical or magic shield, based on the enemy’s damage type. Since the shield blocks only one damage type, attack alongside an ally who deals a different type. Avoid trading right after Camille’s passive shield activates; approach once it has worn off.
vs-camille-passive.text: Camille’s passive creates either a physical or magic shield based on the enemy’s damage type. Since it blocks only one type, attack with an ally who deals the other type to bring her down faster. Avoid trading immediately after the shield activates and approach once it wears off.

vs-camille-q.basis: Camille relies heavily on Q-empowered auto attacks for damage. Armor does not reduce the true damage portion of her second Q. Use basic attack negation, a blind, or stealth to neutralize her Q-empowered auto attack. Create distance while Camille waits for her second Q to avoid the empowered auto attack.
vs-camille-q.text: Camille’s damage is concentrated in her Q-empowered auto attacks, and armor cannot reduce the true damage portion of her second Q. Attack negation, a blind, or stealth can deny that empowered attack. You can also create distance while she waits for the second Q, causing the attack to miss.

vs-camille-r.basis: A target trapped by R has virtually no way to leave its area. Camille becomes untargetable as she enters with R, allowing her to ignore crowd control. Don’t waste your counter ability as Camille enters with R; fight back after the area expires. Avoid the W slow or E stun that lets Camille get into R range. Use Flash to create distance before Camille reaches you, escaping R’s short cast range.
vs-camille-r.text: Once trapped inside The Hextech Ultimatum (R), you have virtually no way out. Camille is untargetable as she enters, so crowd control used at that moment will not stop her; save your counter ability, survive until the area expires, then fight back. R has a very short cast range, so Camille must first hold you in place with Tactical Sweep (W)’s slow or Hookshot (E)’s stun. Dodge that setup or Flash away before she gets close, and R will not reach you.

vs-cass-early.basis: Cassiopeia has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to early ganks. At levels 1–5, keep pressuring Cassiopeia with basic attacks and short trades. Build an early lead before Cassiopeia becomes strong in the mid to late game.
vs-cass-early.text: Cassiopeia has some of the lowest armor among champions and no mobility ability. Pressure her with basic attacks and short trades throughout levels 1–5 to win lane decisively; ganks are also more likely to succeed for the same reasons. If you fail to build a lead then, the mid to late game favors her.

vs-cass-r.basis: Cassiopeia's R stuns only enemies facing her. When you see R's cast animation, turn away to take the slow instead of the stun. When close to Cassiopeia, do not keep attacking while facing her R head-on.
vs-cass-r.text: Cassiopeia’s R stuns only enemies facing her. Turn away when you see its cast animation: taking the slow instead of the stun lets you escape rather than die on the spot. When close to her, the biggest mistake is continuing to deal damage while facing her head-on.

vs-cass-teamfight.basis: Late game, Cassiopeia can win teamfights with sustained damage as long as she is not caught. Establish vision to cut off Cassiopeia's path. Engage right after Cassiopeia uses W elsewhere. When you have an opening to engage, apply guaranteed crowd control before Cassiopeia gains movement speed.
vs-cass-teamfight.text: Late game, Cassiopeia can win teamfights through sustained damage if she is not caught. Instead of pushing straight at her, establish vision to cut off her route or engage just after she uses W elsewhere. Once you have an opening, apply guaranteed crowd control first and finish the fight before she gains movement speed.

vs-cass-w.basis: You cannot use movement abilities inside Cassiopeia's W poison cloud. If you are approaching with a dash, close the distance before W is placed. If W is already placed, take a route around the poison cloud.
vs-cass-w.text: You cannot use movement abilities inside Cassiopeia’s W poison cloud. If your champion engages with a dash, close the distance before W is placed; if it is already down, take a route that avoids the cloud. Cassiopeia is looking for the moment you try to dash while standing in it and nothing happens.

vs-chogath-e.basis: E's spikes deal damage based on the opponent's maximum health. E's spikes pierce enemies in a straight line in front of Cho'Gath. Standing behind minions in the path of E's spikes lets Cho'Gath poke you while clearing the wave. Stand away from the line of Cho'Gath's basic attacks.
vs-chogath-e.text: E's spikes scale with the target's maximum health and pierce everything in a straight line in front of Cho'Gath, so building only health makes them hurt even more. Standing in line behind minions lets him poke you while clearing the wave; move out of the line of his basic attacks.

vs-chogath-mobility.basis: Cho'Gath has no mobility abilities at all. During the laning phase, stay outside Q's range and poke Cho'Gath. Look for a gank right after Cho'Gath uses Q on the wave.
vs-chogath-mobility.text: Cho'Gath has no mobility abilities: keep your distance and he cannot close the gap, while a jungle gank leaves him with no way to escape. In lane, poke from outside Q's range and look for a gank just after he uses Q on the wave.

vs-chogath-q.basis: Q activates after a warning appears beneath your feet, giving you time to react. Move sideways immediately when you see Q's indicator. Save your mobility ability to dodge Q. Cho'Gath's combo depends on landing Q.
vs-chogath-q.text: Q activates after a warning appears beneath your feet, giving you time to react. Step sideways as soon as you see the indicator, and save your mobility ability for that moment. Cho'Gath needs Q to land to continue his combo, so dodging it makes his remaining abilities far less threatening.

vs-chogath-stacks.basis: Cho'Gath's late-game durability relies on Feast stacks. There is a cap on Feast stacks gained from minions and normal jungle monsters. When your health is uncertain, avoid giving Cho'Gath a kill to limit his Feast stack growth.
vs-chogath-stacks.text: Cho'Gath's late-game durability comes from Feast stacks rather than stat growth. Stacks from minions and normal jungle monsters have a cap, so beyond it his growth stops unless he gets champion kills. When your health is uncertain, simply avoiding death near him helps keep the enemy frontline smaller.

vs-chogath-w.basis: W silences enemies in a cone in front of Cho'Gath. If W silences you, you cannot escape with a mobility ability and may be hit by the follow-up Q. When trading with Cho'Gath, move around his side to avoid W's cone in front of him. Once silenced, walk out first instead of trying to use abilities.
vs-chogath-w.text: W silences enemies in a cone in front of Cho'Gath. If it hits you, you cannot use a mobility ability to escape and may take the follow-up Q. Avoid starting a trade directly in front of him; move to his side, and if silenced, walk out before trying to use an ability.

vs-corki-e.basis: Corki's E reduces both armor and magic resistance when it hits you. Move sideways out of the direction Corki aims E.
vs-corki-e.text: Corki’s E reduces both armor and magic resistance when it hits, increasing all damage that follows. It covers a cone, so move sideways instead of standing in front of it; that alone will get you out of most of its area.

vs-corki-mobility.basis: Corki is vulnerable to slows and targeted dashes. Corki is especially vulnerable to ganks. Pressure Corki during his weak first five levels to slow his growth.
vs-corki-mobility.text: Corki has one of the lowest movement speeds, making it easy to stick to him with slows or targeted dashes and leaving him especially vulnerable to ganks. His base stats are also low for the first five levels, so pressuring him then to slow his growth is most effective.

vs-corki-q.basis: Corki's Q reveals your position for a while if it hits you. If Q hits you while you are escaping, immediately use a mobility ability to create distance.
vs-corki-q.text: Corki’s Q reveals your position for a while when it hits. If it catches you during an escape, use a mobility ability immediately to create distance rather than assuming you are safe once you leave normal vision.

vs-corki-r.basis: Corki's R also damages enemies around the first target hit. Move out of Corki's R range instead of hiding behind minions. Corki's third missile deals heavy damage. Reposition to avoid being hit by consecutive missiles.
vs-corki-r.text: Corki’s R damages enemies around the first target it hits, so hiding behind minions will not protect you. Move out of missile range and reposition to avoid consecutive hits, especially from the much stronger third missile.

vs-corki-scaling.basis: Corki grows stronger as he gets more items. Use early lane pressure and ganks to disrupt Corki's farm.
vs-corki-scaling.text: Corki grows stronger as he gets more items. If early lane pressure and ganks don’t disrupt his farm, he can safely fire missiles from the back in the mid to late game and lock in a win. The key is to deny him time to farm comfortably.

vs-corki-w.basis: Engage right after Corki uses W. Corki can escape over terrain if W is available.
vs-corki-w.text: Engage Corki right after he uses W, when his mobility is down. If you try to close in while it’s available, he can escape over terrain.

vs-darius-e.basis: Poke Darius from outside his E range. Save mobility abilities and Flash to respond to Darius's E. Start a trade when Darius misses E or it is on cooldown.
vs-darius-e.text: All of Darius’s combos start with E Apprehend: if he pulls you in, his basic attack, W Crippling Strike, and Q Decimate are guaranteed to land. Poke only from outside E range, and save mobility abilities and Flash to respond to E rather than using them to escape. The only window to trade is when E misses or is on cooldown.

vs-darius-passive.basis: Darius's attack damage rises sharply when Hemorrhage reaches maximum stacks. Create distance from Darius if Hemorrhage stacks are building up. Hemorrhage stacks expire over time. Stay away from Darius until Hemorrhage stacks expire, then reengage.
vs-darius-passive.text: Darius’s attack damage rises sharply at maximum Hemorrhage stacks, so create distance whenever stacks are building; a fight you were winning can turn against you. Hemorrhage expires over time, so disengage briefly to let the stacks fall off, then reengage.

vs-darius-phase.basis: Repeat short, hit-and-run trades to deny Q healing and maximum Hemorrhage stacks. Darius relies on W's slow to disengage. Once you gain a favorable position against Darius, keep pressuring him, as he relies on W's slow to escape. Darius is strong in early skirmishes and dives. Watch out for skirmishes and dives when the enemy jungler joins Darius.
vs-darius-phase.text: Darius lacks mobility and sustain, but Q healing and maximum Hemorrhage stacks make extended fights dangerous. Repeat short hit and run trades instead, forcing him to recall to recover health. W’s slow is his only way to escape, so keep pressing once you have a favorable position. He is exceptionally strong in early skirmishes and dives, though, so watch for the enemy jungler joining him.

vs-darius-q.basis: Darius heals more based on the number of enemies hit by Q's blade. When you see Q being cast, move outside the blade's range to prevent damage and healing. When you see Q being cast, move close to Darius to get hit by the handle and reduce damage and healing. Poke Darius right after he uses Q to clear minions.
vs-darius-q.text: Darius’s Q Decimate heals him according to how many enemies its blade hits. When he starts casting, move beyond the blade’s range or get right next to him so the handle hits instead, reducing both damage and healing. Poke him right after he uses Q to clear minions.

vs-darius-r.basis: Darius's R deals true damage. Darius's R damage increases with the target's Hemorrhage stacks. If Darius gets a kill with R, its cooldown resets. If you have several Hemorrhage stacks and your health is dangerously low, move completely out of R range.
vs-darius-r.text: Darius’s R Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that increases with the target’s Hemorrhage stacks, and a kill resets its cooldown. If you have several stacks and low enough health to be at risk, leave R range completely rather than trying to survive with armor; your death could start a chain of kills against your team.

vs-diana-e.basis: If Diana enters with E without landing Q, she has no way back out. If Diana enters with E without landing Q, catch her with a slow or stun. If Q hits you, keep your distance from Diana because E will reset.
vs-diana-e.text: If Diana dives in with E without first landing Q, she has no way back out; catch her with a slow or stun. If Q has already hit you, E will reset, so give up on trapping her and create distance.

vs-diana-early.basis: Diana is weakest before level 6, when she has melee range and no finishing tool. Build a CS lead over Diana before level 6. As Diana reaches level 6, push the lane ahead of time or stay near your turret to weather her first all-in.
vs-diana-early.text: Diana is weakest before level 6, when her melee range and lack of a finishing tool limit her. Build a CS lead during that window, then push the lane ahead of her level 6 timing or stay near your turret to weather her first all-in.

vs-diana-q.basis: Diana's combo starts with Q. Dodge Diana's curving Q by sidestepping instead of moving straight back. If Q hits you and applies Moonlight, move away because E can hit you twice.
vs-diana-q.text: Diana's combos start with Q Crescent Strike. Because it curves, sidestep instead of retreating straight back. If it hits and applies Moonlight, move away: E can hit you twice.

vs-diana-r.basis: Diana's R deals more damage the more champions it pulls in. Establish vision to deny Diana an angle to enter from the side. In teamfights, spread out based on the angle Diana can enter from.
